Here, Sekkizhar Peruman mentions Thiru-Adigai, where ‘Seythava Maathavar’ (great ascetics who have performed penance) live.

Therefore, the word ‘Maathavar’ can also mean those who possess great penance. By splitting ‘Maathavar’ as ‘Maathu Avar,’ it can also specifically refer to Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar.

Thus, the inner meaning is that only great souls who have performed prior penance will be able to live in Thiru-Adigai. Even if they are Jivanmuktas, to prevent Prarabdha Karma from affecting them, Jivanmuktas also worship in temples. Not only that, but Jivanmuktas also reside in Thiru-Sthalams to guide others. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman reaches Thiru-Adigai Thiru-Sthalam, where such Jivanmuktas, the Maathavars, who worship in Thiru-Sthalams, reside. With the colic, which twists and burns in his stomach, continuing to accompany him, and with the great desire to go to Thiru-Adigai Veera-Ttaanam leading the way, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman reaches Thiru-Adigai Veera-Ttaanam. Sekkizhar Peruman sings that the ailment accompanies him only until he sets out for Thiru-Adigai Veera-Ttaanam.

All the harmful symbols of Jainism that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman had previously adopted, such as the mat, water pot, and peacock feather, remained in the Jains’ dwelling, and now Thiru-Navu- He comes to Thiru-Adigai Veera-Ttaanam with only the colic accompanying him.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, not in control of himself, arrives at Thiru-Adigai Veera-Ttaanam with only the colic, bestowed by the Lord as a form of grace, accompanying him. He cannot walk due to the colic, yet the great desire that arose in his mind pulls him forward. The colic accompanies him and drives him forward.

Thus, he reaches Thiru-Adigai Thiru-Sthalam. There, he sees the light of the sacred wall of the temple in Thiru-Adigai Thiru-Sthalam. The light of that wall seems to welcome him, calling him. Among the senses, the eye, my dear, It travels a long distance from its place to perceive objects far away.

Therefore, to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who comes with great desire, the light seen on the wall of Thiru-Adigai Veera-Ttaanam temple appears first. Light is a helper for those coming from darkness.

Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman has sung this to mean that one who was with the group of darkness is now entering the path of light. That is, Sekkizhar Peruman has sung this to convey that one who was in the group of darkness, the Jain religion, is now entering the path of light, the Shaiva religion. Having reached Thiru-Adigai Thiru-Sthalam in this manner, he reaches the sacred monastery where Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar resided. Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar resided. Why does Sekkizhar Peruman call this a sacred monastery and not a house where Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar resided? He refers to it as a sacred monastery because Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar is an ascetic performing penance as a service to Shiva.

Furthermore, she is also the Acharya who guided Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman.

Therefore, it is a place where such a revered person resided, and thus Sekkizhar Peruman refers to it as a sacred monastery here. That sacred monastery is currently said to be to the east of Thiru-Adigai Veera-Ttaanam temple. Sivakavimani Ayya notes that its commemorative marks are still present there.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman reaches the sacred monastery of Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar. Let us continue our reflection. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 292. Thiru-Nindra Charukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman comes to the sacred monastery of his elder sister, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar, and prostrates himself at her sacred feet. The next verse composed by Sekkizhar Peruman is as follows: “Having come and approached, he prostrated himself at Thilagavathiyar’s feet, saying, ‘You are the fruit of the good penance performed by our lineage.

“I have come, distressed by this body’s cruel colic.

“Now, without confusion, please tell me the path to attain peace and salvation.’” This is the sacred verse composed by Sekkizhar Peruman. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman comes here and prostrates himself at Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar’s sacred feet, He prostrates himself, his head touching her sacred feet. The arrogance that had previously held his head high now subsides with this act of reverence. One who stood with his head held high due to ego now becomes one who is humbled. Conversely, those who humbly prostrate themselves before elders and the Lord are elevated; this is a truth discovered by the wise.

“Accordingly, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman here prostrates himself, his head touching the sacred feet of Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar. After thus prostrating, he speaks to Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar as follows, making a supplication: He addresses Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar as one who is like the fruit of the good penance performed by their lineage.

“Here, ‘kulam’ (lineage) refers to the ancestors who came in our lineage.

“Thus, he says, ‘You are like the fruit of the penance performed by the ancestors who came in our lineage.’ The good penance performed by ancestors refers to the worship of Shiva Peruman, which is Shiva Puja. There are many types of penance, but the best among them is Shiva Puja.

“Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman addresses Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar, saying, ‘You are born in our lineage as the fruit of the penance performed by our ancestors.’ Furthermore, when he says ‘in our lineage,’ Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman includes himself in that lineage and speaks thus. The implicit meaning is that by being born in such a lineage, I too will now attain that benefit.

“Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman says, “You are like the fruit of the good penance performed by our lineage, and this body is suffering from cruel colic.” The colic has seized this body, but what is the reason for it? Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman realizes that it was his delusion and wandering into the wrong path of Jainism that caused the colic to seize his body. He thus understands the root of the disease. The root of this disease, this colic, is the delusion that led him to join the Jain religion.

“Therefore, only by removing the delusion, which is the root of the disease, will this disease, the colic, be cured.

“Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman supplicates to Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar, saying, “Please grant me the way to be freed from this delusion I have held, to find peace, and to attain salvation.” Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar, with great compassion, prayed to Shiva Peruman for her younger brother, Thiru-Navukkarasar, to return to the Shaiva faith. Shiva Peruman granted her wish. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman has now come to Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar.

“Therefore, he wishes to be freed from this colic, not only from the colic but also from the delusion that caused it, and asks for the way to escape from it. With the implication that she, as the divine, should grant him grace for that, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman makes his supplication to Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar. Seeing her younger brother, who has fallen at her feet and is suffering, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar remembers the divine grace of Shiva Peruman and worships with folded hands. She remembers Thiru-Veerattaaneswarar, the Lord who graciously took her and her younger brother into His fold, and worships, remembering His divine grace. Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar, remembering the Lord’s compassionate act of inflicting colic and bringing Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to her, meditates on it in her mind and offers worship with her hands, uniting her inner and outer being in reverence.

“Thus, to the Lord, Having worshipped, she then speaks to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman as follows: “You fell into the pit of other religions without a good purpose, and, not knowing the way to escape from it, you suffered in terrible distress.

“Now, arise!” Thus speaks Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who lay prostrate at her feet. She says, “You were immersed in the other religion, Jainism, which has no good principles, no good doctrine.” That is, she implies that all other religions that do not contemplate Shiva Peruman are religions without principles. She now tells Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, “Arise!” This implies, “Arise, freed from the colic!” And from the state of being fallen in delusion, There is also the implication here: “Arise, freed from that state!” And not only arising from the pit of other religions and the colic, but also remaining forever in the embrace of the Lord’s sacred feet—this is also the meaning conveyed by Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. Upon hearing these words from his elder sister, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who had been lying prostrate at her sacred feet, now, upon hearing his sister’s loving and gracious words, rises from his prostrate position on the ground and worships Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar. Even after rising, he continues to worship Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar.

“Then Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar says, “This is the divine grace of Shiva Peruman, who has matted locks.” Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar instructed Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, saying, “Worship and serve Shiva Peruman, who severs the attachments of those who attain His sacred feet.” This is a sacred verse composed by Sekkizhar Peruman: “Upon hearing her words, Marulneekiyar, trembling with his affliction, rose and worshipped. The great ascetic said, ‘This is the grace of the Lord with matted locks, who severs the attachments of those who attain His feet; worship and serve Him.’” In this passage, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar says, “This is the divine grace of Shiva Peruman.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman supplicates, “I am suffering greatly from colic.” Therefore, in response, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar imparts the truth to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, advising him to understand that the colic is not a bad disease but an act of Shiva Peruman’s divine grace.

“Now, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman had supplicated, “Please tell me the way to be freed without confusion and to attain salvation.” Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar responds to that supplication by saying, “Now, perform the service of the Lord.” Thus, she responds and guides Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. She commands him, “Now, perform service.” Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar commands him, “Worship and perform service to Shiva Peruman, who severs the attachments of those who attain His sacred feet.” The Lord’s The sacred feet are the pervasive grace. In the Kural, in the chapter on the praise of God, Thiruvalluvar Nayanar has composed most of the Kurals praising these sacred feet as ‘Thazh Adi’ (humble feet).

“Now, the next sacred verse: “And then, the female ascetic, who had accepted His grace and stood worshipping, remembering the pure Lord’s great grace, gave the sacred ash of the Lord of Thiru-Kailai mountain, chanting the five letters, for him to enter Thiru-Veerattam.” This is the sixty-sixth sacred verse, the one thousand three hundred and thirty-first sacred verse in the Periya Puranam, in the Puranam of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar, who had commanded him to perform the Lord’s service, and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, accepting her grace, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman now worships. Accepting the service mentioned by Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman now stands worshipping Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar as a sign of his consent.

“Thus, the female ascetic who accepted Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s worship, that is, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar, who stood seeking the upliftment of her younger brother, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar, the female ascetic who remained steadfast in the true path of Shaivism, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar, who was engaged in her sacred service, now, remembering the great grace of Shiva Peruman, bestows grace upon Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar had said, “Perform the Lord’s service,” and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman had consented.

“Therefore, now Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, He must go and worship the Lord enshrined in Thiru-Adigai Veera-Ttaanam. He must enter that Thiru-Veerattam temple.

“Thus, to make Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman worthy of entering that Thiru-Veerattam temple, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar, chanting the sacred five-letter mantra, the Sri Panchaksharam of Shiva Peruman, bestows the sacred ash of Shiva Peruman upon Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. When an Acharya performs a Diksha (initiation), specifically Kriyavati Diksha, when allowing the disciple (shishya) to enter the Diksha mandapam, the Acharya, remembering Shiva Peruman, The Acharya prays, “O Lord, this disciple is mature; he stands before me, seeking grace. I make him worthy to serve by remembering Your sacred feet. Please grant Your grace for this.” We must recall the Agamic rule for performing Diksha.

“Here, it is customary for the Acharya to proceed, not thinking, “I am purifying,” but rather, “I am doing this by the grace of the Lord.” Therefore, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar chanting the Sri Panchaksharam and offering sacred ash to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to enable him to enter the Thiru-Veerattam temple reminds us of this Shivagama rule, this Diksha rule. Naturally, Shiva Peruman, who is free from bonds and removes the impurities of those who approach Him, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar bestows the sacred ash, remembering the divine grace of Shiva Peruman.

“Therefore, it is certain that the divine grace of Shiva Peruman will help Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and lead him to salvation. The sacred five-letter mantra and the sacred ash are the means to make one worthy of entering the temple of Shiva Peruman. These are called Shiva Sadhanas.

“Thus, only those who embrace the sacred ash and the sacred five-letter mantra are worthy of entering the temple. It is the conviction of the wise and a rule of the true scriptures that those who do not embrace the sacred ash and the sacred five-letter mantra are unworthy of entering the temple of Shiva Peruman.

“Thus, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar bestows that sacred ash upon Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. Applying sacred ash, bathing in sacred ash, is referred to as Bhasma Snanam and Agneya Snanam in the Shiva Agamas. Through this, by applying sacred ash, it is a rule to purify the body and the soul.

“Thus, she bestows the sacred ash. In the Shaiva religion, the initiation into the faith is called Samaya Diksha. In this Samaya Diksha, the Shivagama rules state that the disciple is adorned with sacred ash accompanied by mantras, and then the sacred five-letter mantra is imparted. Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar performs the same procedure here. This sacred ash and the sacred five-letter mantra were given to our Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who was known as Dharmasenar in the Jain religion. The holy ash and the sacred five-syllable mantra became the means to purify Dharmasenar from the Samana religion and assist his entry into Shaivism.

“Therefore, for those who wish to truly understand Shaivism from other religions and enter it with truth and steadfastness, purification by a pure Acharya is necessary, as we observe here.

“Furthermore, this can be seen in detail in the initial rituals and the expiation chapters of the Shiva Agamas. Sivakavimani Aiya writes that Guru Diksha is performed by reciting the holy ash and the sacred five-syllable mantra and carrying out the aforementioned rituals.

“Let us proceed with our contemplation.

“Result” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 293. Thirunindrachcharukkam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar bestows the holy ash and the sacred five-syllable mantra upon Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, commanding him to perform Shiva-service and making him worthy to attain the holy feet of Shiva Peruman and enter the Thiru-Veerattanam temple. Sekkizhar Peruman continues to sing the 1332nd verse, the 67th verse in the Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam: “Thiruvalan Thiru-neeru Thilagavathiyar alippa Peru vazhvu vanthathu ena perunthagaiyar paninthu yetru angu uru aara aninthu thamakku utra vidathu uyu neri tharavaray tham munbu vanthar.” (When Thilagavathiyar bestowed the holy ash of Thiruvalan, the noble one humbly accepted it, saying great life had come, and adorned his body fully, becoming a guide to salvation in his time of distress, and came before her.)

Then he came. The holy verse: When Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar gave the holy ash of Thiruvalan, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, the noble one, accepted it humbly, saying, “Great life has come to me.” He then adorned his body fully with it, and Thilagavathiyar, who was born before him, became a guide to salvation in his time of distress. This is the meaning of that verse. “Thiruvalan Thiru-neeru Thilagavathiyar alippa” (When Thilagavathiyar bestowed the holy ash of Thiruvalan) is mentioned here. Thiruvalan means one who rules over the sacredness of liberation. Thiru refers to the nature of the Lord, which is called Aiswaryam, meaning one who is endowed with all Aiswaryam, as the Vedas praise Shiva Peruman.

The word Ishwaran refers exclusively to Shiva Peruman, not other deities, which is certain.

Therefore, Thilagavathiyar bestows the holy ash of such a Thiruvalan, Shiva Peruman. We have seen the greatness of this holy ash in many places before, and we will also see it in the Puranam of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, the child-saint. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, the noble one, humbly accepts this holy ash of Shiva Peruman, the Thiruvalan, saying that a great life has come to him. The method of accepting and wearing the holy ash when elders give it, by bowing with mind, speech, and body, is conveyed here. The rules for receiving the holy ash, the rules for revering the holy ash, and the rules for wearing the holy ash are many. All these rules are not practiced today and are disrespected, which is regrettable.

Therefore, Sivakavimani Aiya writes that devotees who receive the holy ash should know and follow these rules, as it will bring good.

Thus, when receiving the holy ash, one should sincerely praise and humbly accept it with both hands, believing that a great life has come through this holy ash. After receiving the holy ash with great humility, one should wear it according to the prescribed rules. Not even a small amount of holy ash should be spilled on the ground. When applying it to the forehead, one should stand upright to prevent it from falling. Applying holy ash in front of a Shiva shrine, sacred fire, or Guru’s presence, or in a pathway, or in an impure place, or standing while applying it, are all considered faults. These rules for wearing holy ash are extensively described in the Shiva Agamas, Upanishads, and other secondary texts.

We can find all of them.

Therefore, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman receives the holy ash, believing that a great life has come to him. He receives it, thinking that it will cure his colic disease in this worldly life and grant him the blissful life that cures the disease of birth. This is the state of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman’s mind and words when he received the holy ash. He humbly accepted and wore it, which was the action of his body. Having received and worn the holy ash, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman follows Thilagavathiyar, who was born before him. Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar goes ahead into the Thiru-Veerattanam temple, and Thirunavukkarasu Peruman follows her into the Thiru-Veerattanam temple.

Now, the next holy verse comes: “Neeru aninthar agathu irulum nirai kankul purathu irulum maara varum Thiruppalli Ezhuchiyinil maathavam sey seeradiyar Thiru alagum Thirumezhukkum thondiyum kondu aaru aninthar koyilin ul adainthavarai koduppukkar.” (Those who wore the holy ash, their inner darkness and the outer darkness of the full night, changed. In the Thiruppalli Ezhuchi, the great ascetics, with holy brooms and holy plaster, entered the temple, bringing those who had adorned themselves with the holy ash.) Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having worn the holy ash, follows Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar. Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar enters the Thiru-Veerattanam temple. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman also enters the temple behind her. The time when both of them entered was the period of Thiruppalli Ezhuchi. It is the dawn, between the fading of darkness and the birth of day.

During this Thiruppalli Ezhuchi period, the sun rises, dispelling the darkness of the outer world.

Similarly, this Thiruppalli Ezhuchi period now becomes the time when the inner darkness of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman is dispelled. The inner darkness in the heart of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman was the delusion he experienced while being part of the Samana religion. Emerging from that delusion, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman enters the temple during the Thiruppalli Ezhuchi period, so that his inner darkness may be dispelled. This Thiruppalli Ezhuchi period is the last quarter of the night before sunrise, lasting about three and three-quarter naligai. Before this Thiruppalli Ezhuchi period, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar daily goes to the temple and performs the service of cleaning the temple with a holy broom and plastering it. These are the services and devotional acts performed by the Ammaiyar in the path of Chariya.

Therefore, during the Thiruppalli Ezhuchi period, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar, who performs great penance, takes the necessary tools for sweeping and plastering, and enters the Thiru-Veerattaneswarar temple. The Nayanar follows her. Manikkavasagar Peruman has beautifully described this Thiruppalli Ezhuchi period in the Thiruppalli Ezhuchi section of his Thiruvasagam. Thiruppalli Ezhuchi is a prayer requesting Shiva Peruman to rise from his sacred sleep. There is a hymn called Thiruppalli Ezhuchi in Thiruvasagam. The title given to this section by elders is Thirodhana Sutthi.

Thirodhana means concealment, and Sutthi means purification.

Therefore, the purpose of the Thiruppalli Ezhuchi period is to remove Thirodhana and purify souls. The Thirodhana Sakthi performed the act of concealment for souls and prepared them to experience the fruits of their actions. The purpose of this Thiruppalli Ezhuchi is to sing to the Lord, requesting Him to rise from His sleep, so that the Thirodhana Sakthi may manifest as the Sakthi of Grace.

Therefore, generally, the Thiruppalli Ezhuchi period is the time when the inner darkness of souls is dispelled, and they are ready to unite with the grace of Shiva Peruman. This is the meaning of Thiruppalli Ezhuchi. Manikkavasaga Swamigal, also known as Thiru-Vathavooradigal, composed this Thiruppalli Ezhuchi hymn when he was residing in Thiru-Perunthurai.

One day, at dawn, he saw and heard these scenes, and to dispel his inner darkness and attain the light of true knowledge, he prayed to Thiru-Perunthurai Peruman, his soul’s Lord, to rise from his sacred sleep. That is the Thiruvasagam Thiruppalli Ezhuchi. During this special Thiruppalli Ezhuchi period, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman goes to the temple with his elder sister, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar. Manikkavasagar sings about the greatness of this Thiruppalli Ezhuchi period. Sivakavimani Aiya quotes the first three verses from this Thiruppalli Ezhuchi hymn here. In the first verse, he sings about the Thiruppalli Ezhuchi period, saying, “Chetrithazh kamalangal malarum” (The lotus flowers with muddy petals bloom).

The verse is as follows: “Potri en vazh muthal aagiya porule pularnthathu poongazharku inai thunai malarkon Yetri nin thirumugathu emakku arul malarum ezhil nagai kondu nin thiruvadi thozhugum chetrithazh kamalangal malarum than vayalchoozh Thiru-Perunthuraiyurai Sivaperumane yetruyar kodiyudayay enaivudayay Emperuman palli ezhuntharulay.” This is the first verse. As the second verse, Sivakavimani Aiya quotes the following verse: “Arunan Indiran thisai anuginan irul poy aganthathu udaya nin malar thirumugathin karunaiyin suriyan ezha ezha nayana kadimalar malaramatralam kannam niral nirai arupatha mural vana ivaiyor Thiru-Perunthuraiyurai Sivaperumane arulnithi tharavarum ananthamalaiye alaikadale palli ezhuntharulay.” In this, he sings that Arunan, the charioteer of the sun, comes in the direction of Indra, which is the east. In the third verse, he sings that cuckoos, roosters, and other birds crow, and conches blare. The verse is: “Koovina poonguyil koovina kozhi kurugugal iyampina iyampina sangam ovina tharagay oli oli udayathu oru padugindrathu viruppodu namakku devanar cherigazhal thal inai kattay Thiru-Perunthurai.” During such a special Thiruppalli Ezhuchi period, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar and Thirunavukkarasu Peruman enter the Thiru-Veerattanam temple. Sekkizhar Peruman sings here, “adainthu avarai kodu pukkar” (having reached, he brought them in). The action of an Acharya is to perform initiation for the disciple, purify the disciple, make him worthy of Shiva’s grace, and unite him with Shiva Peruman.

This is the action of an Acharya.

Therefore, we can see that Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar performs this action here.

Now, after this, the Nayanar attains the grace of Shiva Peruman and is saved.

At that time, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar, seeing that her desire was fulfilled and she had received the boon, wonders who else has received such a boon and prays to the Lord. We will see that story a little later.

Therefore, Thus, seeing Thirunavukkarasu Peruman saved by the grace of Shiva Peruman and immersed in Shiva-Ananda, Sekkizhar Peruman concludes the history of Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar there. We will see that later.

Therefore, at this point, Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar, acting as an Acharya, bestows the holy ash and the sacred five-syllable mantra upon Thirunavukkarasu Peruman and unites him with Shiva Peruman residing in Thiru-Athigai Veerattanam. Let us go on contemplating. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 294. Thirunindrachcharukkam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thilagavathiyar Ammaiyar unites Thirunavukkarasu Peruman with Shiva Peruman inside the Thiru-Veerattanam temple. The 1334th verse, the 69th verse in the Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam, composed by Sekkizhar Peruman, is as follows: “Thirai kedila veerattanathu iruntha chenkanaga varai silaiyar perumkoyil thozhuthu valam kondu irainji tharaithalathin misai veezhnthu thambiran thiruvarulal uraitha thamizh malaigal saathum unarvu pera unarnthu uraippar.” This is the holy verse.

What is its direct meaning? The river Kedila, with its waves, is the holy river Kedila. On the banks of this holy river Kedila is Thiru-Athigai Veerattanam. In Thiru-Athigai Veerattanam, Shiva Peruman, who once bent Mount Meru as a bow, resides in a great temple. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman worships such a great temple. He circumambulates it reverently and prostrates himself on the ground in Ashtanga Namaskaram.

At that time, the grace of Shiva Peruman fills Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, and he gains the understanding to compose Tamil garlands of praise for Shiva Peruman. Sekkizhar Peruman states this in this verse. The name of the temple in the holy place of Thiru-Athigai is Veerattanam. This Veerattanam holy place is situated on the banks of the Kedila river, on its northern bank.

The Lord residing in Thiru-Athigai Thiru-Veerattanam is Veerattaneswarar Peruman. He is the one who bent the golden mountain, Mahameru, as a bow. When did this happen? During the Tripura Samharam, when he burned the three cities, the Lord bore Mount Meru. Sekkizhar Peruman sings that such an Ishwara resides in the temple, because, as we have already seen, this Thiru-Athigai holy place is one of the places revered as sites where Shiva Peruman’s eight heroic deeds occurred, and it is the holy place where the Tripura Samharam took place.

Thus, when singing about the Lord in this holy place where the Tripura Samharam occurred, Sekkizhar Peruman sings that it is the temple where Shiva Peruman, who wielded Mount Meru as a bow, resides, reminding us of the event of the Tripura Samharam. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman reaches such a glorious temple. As soon as he sees the temple, he worships it.

After that, he circumambulates it. Even after completing the circumambulation, he continues to worship and prostrate himself. He prostrates himself with all eight limbs and five limbs touching the ground. These are all rules for temple darshan. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman demonstrates this to us here, and Sekkizhar Peruman graciously tells us. For those who wish to have Shiva darshan, the first rule in Shiva temple darshan is to bathe according to the rules in the Shiva Theertham near the Shiva temple and then begin the Shiva temple darshan.

Therefore, reflecting this, Sekkizhar Peruman sings about the Kedila river here, saying it is the Thiru-Veerattaneswarar temple on the banks of the Kedila river.

Now, upon approaching the Shiva temple, one should worship the Gopuram, which is the Sthoola Lingam. One should enter with hands clasped above the head, as per the temple darshan rules.

Accordingly, Sekkizhar Peruman sings about Thirunavukkarasu Peruman’s action: “thozhuthu koyil thozhuthu valam kondu irainji” (worshipped the temple, circumambulated, and prayed).

Therefore, it is understood that Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, upon approaching the temple, worshipped the Gopuram, which is the Sthoola Lingam, and entered with his hands clasped above his head, praying.

Furthermore, there is a rule that one should circumambulate the temple before entering. Accordingly, Sekkizhar Peruman sings that Thirunavukkarasu Peruman circumambulated and prayed.

Now, Sekkizhar Peruman sings, “tharaithalathin misai veezhnthu” (falling upon the ground). Sekkizhar Peruman sings that Thirunavukkarasu Peruman prostrated himself on the ground while worshipping. Sivakavimani Aiya writes that Thirunavukkarasu Peruman worshipped with Ashtanga and Panchanga Namaskarams. Generally, the methods of prostrating in a temple are first, Ashtanga. One should prostrate first with eight limbs (Ashtanga Namaskaram) and then with five limbs (Panchanga Namaskaram). We have seen that even Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, when he went to worship Thyagaraja Peruman and Putridam Kondanathar in Thiruvarur, prostrated with Ashtanga and Panchanga Namaskaram.

Similarly, here too, our Thirunavukkarasu Peruman prostrates with Ashtanga and Panchanga Namaskaram and enters the temple. Ashtanga Namaskaram means bowing with eight limbs touching the ground: head, two hands, two ears, two jaws, and two shoulders. Panchanga Namaskaram means bowing with five limbs touching the ground: head, two hands, and two knees. These are the prescribed methods of prostration in the rules for temple worship, generally. It is a general rule that men should perform Ashtanga Namaskaram and women should perform Panchanga Namaskaram. Thrayanga Namaskaram is common to both.

Thrayanga Namaskaram means bowing with both hands cupped over the head. These prostrations should be performed three, five, seven, nine, or twelve times. Performing it once or twice is considered an offense. When prostrating, one should extend their legs towards the west or south. One should not extend their legs towards the east or north. These are the rules for prostration to be observed in a temple.

Furthermore, How to prostrate before a shrine facing east, south, west, or north has been described in great detail. Sekkizhar Peruman mentions Thirunavukkarasu Peruman prostrating in this manner and also circumambulating. Circumambulation is called Pradakshinam. There are also rules for performing Pradakshinam. As mentioned above, one should prostrate according to the rules, then rise, bow, and perform Pradakshinam.

At that time, one should perform Pradakshinam with a mind that never forgets Lord Shiva, either by holding a rosary and chanting the Panchakshara mantra, or by cupping both hands over the heart. When performing Pradakshinam around Lord Shiva’s temple in this manner, One should perform Pradakshinam very slowly. How slowly? As slowly as a heavily pregnant woman walks.

Furthermore, if a pregnant woman is told to walk with a pot full of oil on her head without spilling any, she would walk very slowly; we should walk that slowly around the temple. One should walk slowly, looking at the ground with a melting heart, fearing that even tiny dust particles on the earth might be hurt. One should perform Pradakshinam around Lord Shiva’s shrine at least three times, or five, seven, nine, fifteen, or twenty-one times.

Furthermore, during the time of Abhishekam, one should not perform Pradakshinam or Namaskaram inside the inner prakaram. Brahmacharis should circumambulate clockwise. Householders and Vanaprasthas can circumambulate both clockwise and anti-clockwise. Sanyasis should circumambulate anti-clockwise, meaning they should perform Apradakshinam. When circumambulating clockwise (Pradakshinam), one attains worldly pleasures (Bhogam), and when circumambulating anti-clockwise (Apradakshinam), one attains both worldly pleasures and liberation (Moksham). This is a rule of temple worship, as stated in the Shivagamas.

Jaffna Sri Arumuga Navalar has explained this in detail in his Saiva Vinavidai, under the rules for temple worship.

Therefore, the message we receive here is that Thirunavukkarasu Peruman performs worship exactly according to the rules of temple worship. To Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, who is thus performing worship, By the grace of Lord Shiva, the inspiration to offer a garland of Tamil hymns praising Lord Shiva comes to him. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman enters the temple with the thought that Lord Shiva, who resides as Thiru Adhigai Veerattaneeswarar in that temple, is the Lord for himself and for his elder sister who guided him.

At that moment, divine grace from within inspires his consciousness. As divine grace thus inspires him from within, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman receives the inspiration to compose the Thevarams, the garland of Tamil hymns praising Lord Shiva. “Who can see if He does not show? Who can see if He does not show Himself as the eye?” This is a sacred saying of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman. Regarding this, It is thus established. As the divine grace of Lord Shiva inspired him from within, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman received the inspiration to sing the Thevarams, the hymns praising Lord Shiva.

Therefore, the Thevarams, the sacred utterances of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, are divinely inspired sacred utterances, realized through the inspiration of Lord Shiva. As this inspiration to sing Thevaram came to Thirunavukkarasu Peruman through divine grace, Sekkizhar Peruman now explains the sacred event of his singing the first Thiru-Pathikam. Let us also continue to contemplate. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 295. Thirunindra Charukkam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman enters the Thiru Adhigai Veerattaneeswarar Temple. The next verse, the 1335th verse, the 70th verse in Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam, is as follows: “With a body full of sacred ash, with a mind filled with love, with increasing affection, the Brahmin who destroyed the cities of the enemies, to remove the delusion, the disease, and the maya, he sang the flawless Thiru-Pathikam, ‘Kootraayina Vaaru Vilakkagileer,’ so that the sorrows of the seven worlds would depart.”

“...so that the sorrows of the seven worlds would depart, he stood before and declared.” This is that sacred verse. This is a wonderful verse composed by Sekkizhar Peruman, describing the situation in which Thirunavukkarasu Peruman sang his first Thevaram Thiru-Pathikam, “Kootraayina Vaaru Vilakkagileer.” The meaning of this verse is as follows: Thirunavukkarasu Peruman enters the Thiru Adhigai Veerattanam Temple. He enters with a body full of sacred ash. He enters after smearing sacred ash all over his body. The affection in his heart, filled with abundant love, increases. His affection for Lord Shiva increases.

Therefore, the Lord Shiva enshrined in Thiru Adhigai, Lord Shiva, who is the Veerattaneeswarar, the Brahmin who burned the cities of His enemies, to remove the deluding disease of colic and Maya, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman composed the lengthy and flawless Thiru-Pathikam beginning with “Kootraayina Vaaru Vilakkagileer.” Because Thirunavukkarasu Peruman composed this Pathikam, the sufferings that come in all seven births in this world are removed.

Thus, to remove the sufferings that come in all seven births, he stood before the shrine of the Lord inside the Thiru Adhigai Veerattanam Temple and sang that flawless Thiru-Pathikam, “Kootraayina Vaaru Vilakkagileer.” This is the meaning of that verse. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman enters the temple, having smeared sacred ash all over his body. That sacred ash was the sacred ash given by Thilagavathi Ammaiyar after chanting the sacred five letters. He enters, wearing such sacred ash all over his body.

Therefore, until now, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman’s body, which was lacking without sacred ash, is now complete, its deficiency removed by the application of sacred ash. With such a complete body, a body made complete by sacred ash, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman enters the temple. In his mind, a great desire, a great love, This love, which was abundant, increased more and more, and with immense love and affection, he proceeds towards the Lord’s shrine.

There, Lord Shiva, who is seated in the shrine inside the Thiru Adhigai temple, is referred to here by Sekkizhar Peruman as the ‘Vethiyar who destroyed the cities of the enemies.’ He is Veerattaneeswarar, who burned the three cities. The three cities are the three impurities (mummalakariyam), as stated in Thirumoolar’s Thirumandiram.

Therefore, the Lord burning the three cities is a symbol of His removing the three impurities.

Thus, the Veerattaneeswarar residing in the Thiru Adhigai temple is capable of removing disease and Maya, which is the implication here. Such a Lord, who destroyed the cities of the enemies, is a Vethiyar. ‘Vethiyar’ here means, Here, it means one who expounded the Vedas, one who is the essence of the Vedas, one who shines in the Vedas. Such a Lord removes the disease and Maya of Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar.

Here, ‘disease’ refers to the transformation of the Lord’s grace, which was in the form of Tirodhana Shakti until now, into Arul Shakti (graceful power). This is what is called ‘disease’ here.

Here, ‘Maya’ refers to the transformation of what was previously darkness into light. This is what is meant by ‘removing Maya.’ Therefore, ‘removing disease’ means that the Lord’s Tirodhana Shakti transforms into Arul Shakti, and ‘removing Maya’ means transforming what was previously darkness into light. Maya here, It has come here in the sense of the disease of birth.

Therefore, the Thiru Veerattaneeswarar Peruman here removes the disease of birth.

Thus, the Veerattaneeswarar Peruman, who removed the disease and Maya of Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, bestows grace upon Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar. We have already seen that the inspiration to sing Thevaram, the garland of Tamil hymns, for the Lord had already come and filled Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar by the grace of the Lord. While this inspiration to sing Thevaram, the garland of Tamil hymns, was happening within him by the grace of the Lord, at the same time, the Peruman in Thiru Veerattanam, as mentioned here, removes the deluding disease and Maya.

Therefore, now Thiru Navu- Karasu Nayanar, by the grace of the Lord, sings the first Thiru-Pathikam, “Kootraayina Vaaru Vilakkagileer,” so that all the sorrows that come in these seven worlds may depart. Sekkizhar Peruman refers to this Thiru-Pathikam as a “lengthy and flawless Thiru-Pathikam.” “Needitthal” means to remain imperishable and eternal. “Kothil” means without blemish; “Kothu” means fault. “Kothil” means a Thiru-Pathikam that makes all faults cease to exist. “Thiru” refers to liberation.

Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman states that this Thiru-Pathikam, “Kootraayina Vaaru Vilakkagileer,” is an imperishable and eternal Thiru-Pathikam, a Thiru-Pathikam that makes all our faults cease to exist, and a Thiru-Pathikam that bestows upon us the blessing of liberation.

Furthermore, the “lengthy and flawless Thiru- Pathikam” that appears, if “neediya” is taken as an adjective for “kothu,” it would mean “lengthy fault.” That refers to the strength of the Moolamalam (primal impurity) that has eternally clung to souls.

Therefore, it also implies a Thiru-Pathikam that is structured to nullify the strength of that Moolamalam, which has eternally clung to souls.

Furthermore, since “kothil” here means a Thiru-Pathikam that makes our faults—the three impurities of Anavam, Kanmam, and Mayai—cease to exist, “kothil” here signifies the removal of bonds (Pasa Neekam). Since “Thiru-Pathikam” appears, “Thiru” refers to the attainment of Shiva.

Therefore, for the souls, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman bestows this Thiru-Pathikam, “Kootraayina Vaaru Vilakkagileer,” as a Thiru-Pathikam that removes the bonds of souls and grants the attainment of Shiva. By his bestowing it thus, the sufferings that come in the seven types of births of souls are removed from them. Sekkizhar Peruman mentions this in the sacred verse as “the sorrow that comes in the seven worlds.” Here, “seven” refers to the seven types of births that come to souls, and also to the births taken by souls in the seven worlds.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar bestows this Thiru-Pathikam so that the sufferings that come in the seven types of births of souls are removed from those souls.

Therefore, the fruit of this Thiru-Pathikam is to remove the suffering of worldly beings, to effect the removal of bonds, And to grant the attainment of Shiva. This is the fruit of this Thiru-Pathikam.

Thus, as Veerattaneeswarar Peruman Himself inspired Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar from within, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar composed such a great Thiru-Pathikam, the lengthy and flawless Thiru-Pathikam, beginning with “Kootraayina Vaaru Vilakkagileer,” as his first Pathikam.

Here, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar not only sang it for himself but also, by the inspiration of Lord Shiva from within, composed it so that all who praise and sing this Thiru-Pathikam would also attain this removal of suffering and the attainment of Shiva. He presents this Thiru-Pathikam standing directly before the shrine inside the temple.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu- Nayanar composed his first Thevaram Thiru-Pathikam, “Kootraayina Vaaru Vilakkagileer,” at the sacred site of Thiru Adhigai Veerattanam.

Now, that Thiru-Pathikam. Pan: Kolli. Thalam: Thiru Adhigai Veerattanam.

“Kootraayina Vaaru Vilakkagileer, kodumai pala seythana naan ariyaen. Ettraay adikkae iravum pagalum piriyathu vananguvan eppozhudhum. Thotraathenpin agampadiyae kudarodu thudakki mudakki,” “Keezh aatraen adiyaen Adhigai Kedila Veerattana Thurai Ammane. Nenjam umakkae idamaga vaithaen ninaiyaathoru podhum irunthariyaen.

Vanjam ithu oppathu kandariyaen vayitrodu thudakki mudakkiyida. Nanjaagi vanthanai nalivathanai nanugaamal thurandhu karunthum ideer. Anjaelum eneer Adhigai Kedila Veera- ”...ttana Thurai Ammane. Paninthaaran paavangal paatra vallir. Padu vendalaiyil bali konduzhalveer. Thuninthe umakkaatseythu vaazhalutraal.

Sudugindrathu soolai thavirtharuleer. Pininthar podi kondumai poosa vallir. Pettram ettrugantheer suttrum vendalai kondu anintheer adikeel Adhigai Kedila Veerattana Thurai Ammane. Mun- “...nam adiyaen ariyaamaiyinaal muninthennai nalindhu mudakkiyida. Pinnai adiyaen umakkaazhum pattaen. Sudugindrathu soolai thavirtharuleer.

Thannai adainthaar vinai theerppathanro. Thalaiyaayavar tham kadan aavathuthaan. Anna nadaiyaar Adhigai Kedila Veerattana Thurai Ammane. Kaathaazh pavar kaaval igazhnthamaiyaal karai nindravar kandu kol,” “...endru solli neethaaya kayam puga nokkiyida. Nilai kollum vazhi thurai ondru ariyaen.

Vaarthai ithu oppathu kettariyaen vayitrodu thudakki mudakkiyida. Aarthaar punalaar Adhigai Kedila Veerattana Thurai Ammane. Salampoodu thooppam maranthariyaen. Thamizhodisai paadal maranthariyaen. Nalam theengilum unnai maranthariyaen. Un- ”...en naavil maranthariyaen.

Ulanthaar thalaiyil bali konduzhalvaay. Udal ullur soolai thavirtharulaay. Alanthaen adiyaen Adhigai Kedila Veerattana Thurai Ammane. Uyarnthaen manai vaazhkaiyum onporulum oruvar thalai kaavalaal. Vayanthaen umakkaatsu vaazhalutraal valikkindrathu soolai thavirtharuleer. Payanthaen enpin“

Akampadiye pariththu puratti aruththeertthidanaan ayarndhen adiyen Athikai Kedila Veerattaanaththurai ammanae valiththen manai vaazhkai makizhnthadiyen vanjam manam onrum illamayinaal saliththaal oruvar thunai yaarum illai sanga ven kuzhai kaathudai emperumaan kaliththeyan vayitrin akampadiye kalakki malakkittu kavarnthu thinna azhuththen. I am weary, O Lord of Thiru-Athikai Thiru-Kedila Veerattanam, for I have been plundered, overturned, and cut off. I have endured the joy of domestic life, and I, your servant, have no deceit in my heart. If I falter, there is no one to help me, O my Lord with the conch-white ear-ring. I have been pressed to eat, having been stirred and churned within my stomach by this affliction. Adiyen Athikai Kedila Veerattaanaththurai ammanae ponpolamizhavathore meniyineer poripun sadaiyeer meliyum piraiyeer thunbe kapalai piniyanrivatrai nanukaamal thuranthu karanthum ideer en polikal ummai ini theliyaar adiyaarpaduvathithuveyakil anbe amaiyum Athikai Kedila Veerattaanaththurai ammanae.

O Lord of Thiru-Athikai Thiru-Kedila Veerattanam, your form is like melting gold, your matted locks are adorned with sparks, and you bear the crescent moon. You do not approach or hide from suffering, disease, or the skull. If this is what your devotees endure, then those like me will not understand you. Love alone suffices, O Lord of Thiru-Athikai Thiru-Kedila Veerattanam. Poortthaay angor aanaiyin eeruri thol purangaadaranga nadamaadavallaay aartthaan arakanthanai maalvarai keezh adartthittarul seytha athu karuthaay veertthum poorandum vizhunthum ezunthaal en vedanaiyaana vilakkiyeedaay aartthaar punal soozh Athikai Kedila Veerattaanaththurai ammanae.

Ithuve antha kootraayinaavaaru vilakkakileer enru Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar. You covered yourself with the fresh hide of an elephant, and you are skilled in dancing in the cremation ground. Consider how you crushed the mighty mountain beneath the demon’s arm and bestowed your grace. My pain, which makes me sweat, stumble, fall, and rise, please remove it, O Lord of Thiru-Athikai Thiru-Kedila Veerattanam, surrounded by roaring waters.

This is the Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar’s Thiru-Pathikam beginning with “Kootraayinaavaaru vilakkakileer.” The first Thiru-Pathikam sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, the Thiru-Thevaram, was a prayer to the Peruman to cure his colic and to cut off the cycle of birth, which is called Maya. This Thiru-Pathikam was revealed by the grace of the Lord from within. Not only that, but it also contains a prayer for the removal of the sorrows that come from the seven worlds, as indicated by Sekkizhar Peruman.

Therefore, the benefit of reciting this Thiru-Pathikam and offering it as a prayer to the Lord is the same, according to our elders. We will continue to contemplate in detail the meaning of the ten Thiru-Padal-s in this Thiru-Pathikam.

Let us resume our contemplation.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 296, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We contemplated the history of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar singing the first Thiru-Pathikam, which begins with “Kootraayinaavaaru vilakkakileer.” Now we must contemplate the meaning of that Thiru-Pathikam. This Thiru-Pathikam was composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar at Thiru-Athikai Veerattanam. It is the first Thiru-Thevaram Thiru-Pathikam, offered as a prayer to the Lord to alleviate his colic.

Therefore, in each verse of this Thiru-Pathikam, he expresses his suffering from colic and requests liberation from it, offering his plea to the Lord residing in Veerattanam in each verse. We observed that this Thiru-Pathikam contains a total of ten Thiru-Padal-s.

Therefore, let us now contemplate the meaning of the first Thiru-Padal. “Kootraayinaavaaru vilakkakileer kodumai pala seythana naan ariyēn ēttraay adikke iravum pakalum piriyathu vananguvan eppozhuthum thōtraathu en vayitrin akampadiye kudarodu thudakki mudakkiyida aatrēn adiyēn Athikai Kedila Veerattaana thurai ammanae.” This is the first Thiru-Padal. Its meaning is as follows: O Shiva-Peruman, who is enshrined in the Thiru-Veerattanam temple in Thiru-Athikai, which shines to the north of the Thiru-Kedila river! The disease of delusion, like a Yama, afflicts me, your servant. Will you not explain such a colic? This disease has come upon me.

Therefore, I do not know what cruelties I have committed before this. So, O Shiva-Peruman, who comes on the bull, I will worship your holy feet day and night, always without separation. I am suffering, unable to bear this colic that has entangled my intestines and crippled me from within my stomach, without diminishing. Remove this suffering and take me into your grace. This is the meaning of the first Thiru-Padal that begins with “Kootraayinaavaaru.” This verse begins with “Kootraayinaavaaru.” This should be separated as “Kootru aayina aaru.” Sivakavimani Aiyavargal provides two types of explanations for this. He writes in the commentary on the Thiru-Pathikam verse.

If “Kootraayinaavaaru” is separated as “Kootru aayina aaru,” then “Kootru” here means Yama. In Tamil, Yama is also called “Kootruvan” and “Kootru” because he divides. “Kootru” means to separate. He is called “Kootruvan” because he performs this act of separation. We saw that “Kootru” means separation. Yama separates from the body, so he is called “Kootru” and “Kootruvan.” The colic that came to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman came like Yama.

It caused him such suffering.

Therefore, he begins in this way: “This suffering, like Yama, afflicts me.” He begins by saying, “This suffering, like Yama, afflicts me.” Now, “Kootru” also has another meaning: “word.” The second meaning is that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings, realizing that this suffering has come upon him due to the fault of his words, the sin committed through his speech, in his previous births. Sivakavimani Aiya mentions two incidents regarding what fault Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman committed through his words, through his speech, in his previous births.

Once, Ravana, out of arrogance, tried to uproot Mount Kailash. When he tried to do so, the Lord pressed it slightly with one of his big toes.

At that time, Ravana was trapped beneath Mount Kailash. He suffered and wept for a long time. To this suffering Ravana, Shankaran, who is fond of Sama-Gana, revealed a way to escape his suffering, saying that he could please Shiva-Peruman with music. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who was known as Vakeesar in his previous birth, gave this advice to Ravana when he was Vakeesar.

Next, on another occasion, during a discussion about religious truths on the banks of the Godavari, when sages questioned him about religious truths, he argued that Jainism was superior and that the Jain religion was the highest. This historical account also exists.

Therefore, due to these two transgressions, Thiru-Navukkarasu In this birth, he joined the Jain religion, and through that, he suffered from colic and thus laments.

Therefore, for “Kootru aayina aaru,” Sivakavimani Aiya writes in his commentary that there are two meanings for the phrase “Kootraayinaavaaru”: one, this disease caused by words, and two, this disease that afflicts like Yama.

Therefore, Navukkarasar sings, “Kootraayinaavaaru vilakkakileer.” Next comes, “Kodumai pala seythana naan ariyēn.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman tells the Lord, “This disease afflicts me like Yama.

“Therefore, I must have committed many cruelties before this, and as a result of that, This colic must have come.

“Therefore, I do not know what cruelties I have committed before this; I do not remember.

“Moreover, I did not do all these knowingly; I have committed many cruelties unknowingly. Even if I have committed many cruelties unknowingly, I will always worship your holy feet day and night, without ever separating from you.” Although Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman says he might have committed cruelties, in the scriptures, this is called “Abhukti Purva Vinai” (karma that has not yet borne fruit). Even if he has committed many cruelties, he says he will always worship you day and night without forgetting you. I am engaged in the sacred service of worshipping your holy feet. Is it proper for that karma to afflict me, who has surrendered to your feet? It is not proper.

“Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings, “Release me from this suffering.” That is the meaning of the line, “Ettraay adikke iravum pakalum piriyathu vananguvan eppozhuthum.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings to the Lord, “I will always worship you day and night without separation.” Now, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman has come into the Shaiva religion. So, if he sings this now, it is correct.

“But before this, he was in the Jain religion. In that case, when he sings, “I will always worship you day and night without separation,” does it not seem contradictory? It is not so. That is not the case. It is true that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sang that he would worship Paramasivan day and night, even during the entire period he was in a different religion, Jainism. How so?

“Now Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman has joined the Shaiva religion and attained Shaiva wisdom.

“Therefore, now, by the grace of Shiva-Peruman, with his help, he realized that all the religions here are included as parts within the Shaiva religion.

“Therefore, he later composed the Thevaram, “Yathoru Devar enappaduvaarkkellam Maadevan allaal Devar matraye” (All those who are called gods are none other than Mahadeva). Not only that, but in Sivagnana Siddhiyar, it is stated, “Yathoru Deivam kondir aththeivamaaki aange Maathoru Paakanartham varuvaar.” He now understands this truth after joining the Shaiva religion. All the worship offered by anyone to any deity reaches Shiva-Peruman.

“Therefore, Shiva-Peruman grants the benefits of worship according to the extent to which each person worships their respective deity. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman now understands this.

“Therefore, after joining the Shaiva religion, which encompasses all religions as its parts and is the supreme religion, all the worship performed by people in all paths ultimately reaches Shiva-Peruman. And after realizing the truth that Shiva-Peruman grants the fruits of all those worships, he sings, “I will always worship you day and night without separation.” Therefore, there is not even a slight contradiction in this. That is why later, in the sixth Thiru-Padal, he sings, “Salam poovodu thooppam maranthu ariyēn” (I have never forgotten water, flowers, and incense).

“Therefore, the Shaiva religion’s harmony is that all religions, placed in their proper order and at their respective levels, lead to the Lord, Shiva-Peruman, and the worship performed by adherents of those religions at those levels reaches the Lord. Religions that deny the existence of God, religions that consider souls, which are like cattle, as God, religions that deny the existence of souls, Religions that do not see the bonds that bind souls, religions that deny the existence of this world, religions that affirm the existence of God and see Him as one among souls – all these various religions differ and contradict each other, depending on the maturity levels of souls. All these truths are shown in the Sivagnana Siddhiyar and other gnana texts in the sections on Svapaksham and Parapaksham.

“Thus, all religions are arranged in hierarchical levels, and beyond all these religions, Shaiva Siddhanta shines as the supreme. And even the worship performed by souls in those religions at those hierarchical levels reaches Shiva-Peruman, as explained in the gnana texts. Thayumanavar Swami Even Thayumanavar Swami has uttered many words of wisdom, saying that the Sopana Paksham (staircase path) is shown, and that Vaidika Shaivism is established as the royal path, and that all these will stand together in one place by justice.

“Therefore, even when he was in the Jain religion, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman now understands the truth that he was truly worshipping Shiva-Peruman. So, he sings with his sacred words, “I will always worship you.” This is the meaning of the second line of the first verse, “Ettraay adikke iravum pakalum piriyathu vananguvan eppozhuthum.” Now Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings, “Thōtraathu en vayitrin akampadiye kudarodu thudakki mudakkiyida aatrēn adiyēn.” This stomach pain, this colic, without diminishing, remains within my stomach, entangling my intestines and causing me suffering. It cripples me.

“Therefore, I cannot bear this pain. I am suffering, unable to bear this pain. O Shiva-Peruman, who resides in Thiru-Veerattanam, which shines to the north of the Kedila river in Thiru-Athikai city! I am suffering, unable to bear the pain of this colic.

“Therefore, you are the Lord, and I am your servant. It is your duty to protect and bless this servant.

“Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman makes a plea to the Lord. This is the meaning of the first Thiru-Padal of this Thiru-Pathikam, which begins with “Kootraayinaavaaru vilakkakileer.” Now, the second verse begins with “Nenjam umakke idamaka vaiththen.”

“We will continue to contemplate its meaning.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 297, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We contemplated the meaning of the first verse of the first Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, which begins with “Kootraayinaavaaru.” Now, the second verse: “Nenjam umakke idamaka vaiththen ninaiyaathu orupothum irunthariyēn vanjam ithu oppathu kandariyēn vayitrodu thudakki mudakkiyida nanjaaki vanthu ennai nalivathanai nanukaamal thuranthu karanthum ideer anjēlum ennīr Athikai Kedila Veerattaanaththurai ammanae.” This is the second verse. Its meaning is as follows: O Lord enshrined in Thiru-Veerattanam in Thiru-Athikai on the banks of the Thiru-Kedila river! I have prepared my heart as a dwelling place for you alone. Not even for a moment I have never been without remembering you.

I have never before experienced such a cruel disease as this colic. I have not experienced it before. It comes like poison, entangling my stomach and crippling me, causing me suffering. You must drive away and hide that colic, so it no longer afflicts me. You must grant me refuge, saying, “Fear not.” This is the meaning of the verse.

Now, the third Thiru-Padal: “Paninthaarana paavangal paatravalleer padu vendalaiyil pali kondu uzhalveer thunithe umakku aatseythu vaazhalutraal sudhukindrathu soolai thavirththaruleer pininthaar podi kondu mey poosavalla.” Petram yetru ukanthīr sutrum vendalai kondu aninthīr adikeel Athikai Kedila Veerattaanaththurai ammanae. This is the third Thiru-Padal. Its meaning is as follows: O Shiva-Peruman, who smears the ashes of the deceased on your sacred body! O Shiva-Peruman, who delights in riding the bull! O Shiva-Peruman, who is adorned with a garland of skulls around your head!

O Shiva-Peruman, who is enshrined in Thiru-Veerattanam, which shines to the north of the Kedila river in Thiru-Athikai! You are capable of destroying the evil karmas of those who bow to you. Yet, you wander, begging for alms with a Brahma’s skull. My desire, looking at your omnipotence, It is understood from this that you are capable of removing the sins of those who worship you.

Therefore, you who are capable of removing the sins of those who worship you, please remove my colic disease, for I am your servant. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings, ‘Henceforth, I shall live as your servant.’ This is the meaning of the third Thiru-padal.

Now, the fourth Thiru-padal: ‘In my former ignorance, I was afflicted and crippled; later, I became your servant. Do not remove the burning colic. Is it not the duty of the foremost to remove the karma of those who seek refuge in them? O Lord of Thiru-Adhigai, Thiru-Veerattanam on the banks of the Kedila, where women of swan-like gait reside.’ The meaning of this verse is as follows: In the city of Thiru-Adhigai, where women of swan-like gait reside, O Shiva Peruman, enshrined in Thiru-Veerattanam, north of the Kedila River, I have already been your servant. I was your servant. In between, I joined another religion, Jainism.

Now I am your servant again.

Therefore, because I joined Jainism due to ignorance, you have hated me and given me this colic disease. That colic disease afflicts and cripples me. I became your servant, leaving that.

Now, even after becoming your servant, the colic burns me.

Therefore, please cure it. What is the duty of a leader? Is it not to remove the karma of those who seek refuge in them?

Therefore, I am your servant, and you are my leader. You have ruled over me, so It is your duty to remove my karma, who has sought refuge in you.

Therefore, please cure this colic disease, O Lord. This is the meaning of the fourth Thiru-padal.

Now, the fifth Thiru-padal: ‘Because the guardian of the deep pool neglected his duty, those on the bank said, “See for yourselves,” and pushed me into the deep pool. I know no way to stand firm. I have never heard such a word. The colic afflicts and cripples my stomach. O Lord of Thiru-Adhigai, Thiru-Veerattanam on the banks of the Kedila, where the waters roar.’ This is the fifth verse. Its meaning is: O Shiva Peruman, enshrined in the Thiru-Veerattanam temple, north of the Kedila River, in the great city of Thiru-Adhigai, where floods flow abundantly, he sings, starting with ‘Because the guardian of the deep pool neglected his duty,’ a story about There is a pond.

There is a guardian who guards that pond. A person who does not know where the deep parts of the pond are, what troubles are there, or where the landing places are, attempts to enter the pond.

At that time, the guardian of the pond’s bank prevents the person attempting to enter, warning them that the pond is very dangerous and that if they enter, they will not be able to swim out. Disregarding all these warnings, the person enters the pond.

Afterwards, they are trapped inside the pond, struggling to swim out and reach the bank. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings this Thiru-padal, placing this situation within it. He says, ‘When I joined Jainism, you did not protect me from it, but instead, You gave me colic disease and afflicted me. Even if one makes a mistake, it is the duty of great people to protect. Is it proper for you to afflict me in this way? This colic disease is in my stomach and causes me suffering.

Therefore, protect me from it,’ he sings in this fifth verse. Many religions serve as different paths for souls, according to their varying levels of maturity. These paths are all unstable, broken, ruined, slippery, and contain dangerous creatures like crocodiles.

Thus, there are many kinds of paths that cause souls to fall. However, the path free from all these defects is the Shaivite path, which has come down through the Vedic tradition. This is the essence of this song, as Thiru-Navukkarasu Arasu Peruman has sung.

Now, the sixth Thiru-padal: ‘I have never forgotten to offer water, flowers, and incense. I have never forgotten the musical songs in Tamil. I have never forgotten you in good times or bad. I have never forgotten your name on my tongue. You wander, begging for alms with a skull. Remove the colic within my body.

I am weary, your servant, O Lord of Thiru-Adhigai, Thiru-Veerattanam on the banks of the Kedila.’ Its meaning is as follows: O Lord of Thiru-Adhigai, Thiru-Veerattanam on the banks of the Kedila, I have never forgotten to worship you with water, flowers, and incense. I have never forgotten to sing musical praises of your glory in the Tamil language. I have never forgotten you, even in good times or bad. I have never forgotten to utter your sacred name on my tongue. O you who wander, begging for alms with Brahma’s skull, Please remove the colic disease that afflicts my body. I am suffering from that colic disease,’ he sings.

Now, the seventh Thiru-padal: ‘I renounced the exalted householder’s life and its possessions, for there was no one to guard me. When I resolved to live serving you, the colic pains me. Please remove it. I am afraid, my stomach is being torn, twisted, and cut. I am exhausted, your servant, O Lord of Thiru-Adhigai, Thiru-Veerattanam on the banks of the Kedila.’ The meaning of this verse is as follows: O Shiva Peruman, my Lord, who protects me, there is no one else to guard me but you. There is no one else to protect me but you.

Therefore, I have departed from the householder’s life and from the pursuit of wealth in a righteous way. By the grace of my past deeds, I now live as your servant. While I live thus, you still allow this colic disease to torment me without curing it. Please save me from this colic disease and rule over me. The colic disease is tearing, twisting, and cutting my intestines deep within my stomach.

Therefore, I am afraid and exhausted. So, please protect me from this colic disease, O Lord, enshrined in Thiru-Veerattanam, north of the Kedila River in Thiru-Adhigai.

Now, the eighth Thiru-padal: ‘I considered the householder’s life to be strong, and I rejoiced in it, for there was no deceit in my mind. If I falter, there is no one to help me, O my Lord, who wears the white conch shell as an earring. The colic within my stomach has stirred, It has churned, twisted, and seized me. I am exhausted, your servant, O Lord of Thiru-Adhigai, Thiru-Veerattanam on the banks of the Kedila.’ The meaning of this is as follows: O Lord, enshrined in Thiru-Veerattanam, north of the Kedila River in the great city of Thiru-Adhigai, O great Lord who wears an earring made of a white conch shell! There is no deceit in my mind, your servant.

Therefore, I considered the householder’s life, in which I rejoiced, to be superior. The colic disease is stirring within my servant’s stomach, confusing the parts of the stomach and seizing them, causing pain.

Therefore, I have grown weary of living. When I suffer like this, there is no one to help your servant but you.

Therefore, protect your servant from this disease. This is the meaning of the eighth Thiru-padal.

Now, the ninth Thiru-padal: ‘O you whose body shines like gold, O you with matted, reddish hair, O you with the crescent moon! If you would banish and conceal from me sorrow, anxiety, and disease, then those like me would clearly understand you as the Lord who removes suffering. If it is only love that remains, O Lord of Thiru-Adhigai, Thiru-Veerattanam on the banks of the Kedila.’ The meaning of this is: O Lord, enshrined in Thiru-Veerattanam, north of the Kedila River in the city of Thiru-Adhigai! O you whose sacred body is like gold! O you with matted, reddish hair! O you with the crescent moon!

If you would banish and conceal from me sorrow, anxiety, and disease, then those like me would clearly understand you as the Lord who removes suffering.

Therefore, your love alone will wipe away our sorrow and bring us peace.

Therefore, please remove my suffering.

Now, the tenth Thiru-padal: ‘You wore the skin of an elephant as a covering. You are skilled in dancing in the cremation ground. You crushed the roaring rakshasa Ravana under the great mountain and then bestowed grace upon him. Remember that. When I sweat, roll, fall, and rise, do not remove my suffering. O Lord of Thiru-Adhigai, Thiru-Veerattanam on the banks of the Kedila, surrounded by roaring waters.’ The meaning of this is as follows: O our Lord, who resides in Thiru-Veerattanam, situated on the banks of the Kedila River, which has roaring waters!

You once flayed the skin of an elephant and wore it as a covering. You are skilled in performing the dance, making the cremation ground your stage. You crushed Ravana, the roaring rakshasa who attempted to lift Mount Kailash, under that great mountain, And then you bestowed grace upon him.

Similarly, please remove these sufferings that I, your servant, am experiencing due to colic disease, as I sweat, roll, fall, and rise. This is the meaning of the tenth Thiru-padal.

Thus, we have briefly contemplated the meanings of the ten verses of the Thiru-padigam beginning with ‘Kootraayina Vaaru.’ Now, let us continue to contemplate the history of how the Lord accepted this Thiru-padigam, offered by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, and bestowed His grace upon him. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part Two Hundred and Ninety-Eight. Thiru-Nindra Charukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We contemplated the history of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman singing the first Thevaram Thiru-padigam, which begins with ‘Kootraayina Vaaru.’ As soon as Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar sang the first Thiru-padigam, the colic disease he had disappeared instantly. It vanished.

The colic disease that came to him was a disease caused by the Lord’s grace of mercy. It has now vanished. It has left Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar. Immediately, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar praises and worships Shiva Param-Porul, saying, ‘The Lord has given me my life and also His divine grace.’ Shiva Peruman returned Thiru-Navukkarasu Karasu Nayanar’s life. Not only that, but He also bestowed His divine grace. By removing the colic disease, Shiva Peruman gave life to Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar.

If the colic disease had not been removed, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar’s life would have ended.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman praises Shiva Peruman, saying that by removing the colic disease, He gave him life. Not only that, but Shiva Peruman also removed Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar from delusion and bestowed His divine grace. If He had only removed the colic disease and given life, without bestowing divine grace, that empty life would have been a useless life.

Therefore, Shiva Peruman, along with life, He also bestowed His divine grace upon Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman praises such a Shiva Peruman as ‘Sen-nindra Param-Porul.’ Its meaning is ‘the Supreme Being who stands in righteousness.’ Param-Porul means the Supreme Being, superior to this world. Senmai means ‘true essence.’ True essence refers to the nature of Shiva.

Therefore, ‘Sen-nindra Param-Porul’ means the Supreme Being who stands specially in the hearts of those who have love, and also the Supreme Being who stands above all else.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, praising Shiva Peruman, who gave him life and divine grace, as Param-Porul, plunged into the ocean of the Lord’s grace, which is the compassion of Shiva Peruman, the foremost, due to his spiritual ecstasy. He remained immersed. The spiritual ecstasy he experienced was a state of mind where, due to the excess of bliss, nothing else appeared. This state of knowledge is referred to here as delusion, confusion, spiritual delusion, or spiritual confusion by Sekkizhar Peruman. Even when one is in an advaitic union with anava (ego), delusion can arise.

But this delusion is not that delusion. This is the blissful delusion of being in an advaitic state with Shiva Peruman. In such a state of spiritual ecstasy, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar immerses himself and revels in the ocean of the Lord’s grace.

At that time, all the hairs on Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar’s body stood on end. This is called Pulakangitham. Generally, in moments of great fear or intense love, the hairs stand on end in this manner.

Now, due to the intensity of love, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar’s hairs stood on end, and goosebumps appeared. He experienced Pulakangitham. Tears of joy flowed incessantly from his eyes. Great souls would shed tears whenever they thought of the Lord’s immense grace and the great mistakes they had made towards Him.

Thus, with his hairs standing on end and tears of joy flowing from his eyes, he fell to the ground, rolled, and became exhausted. These are all physical manifestations that occur due to an excess of bliss, an abundance of joy. The fullness of Shiva Peruman’s grace Because it could not be contained within, these actions of falling, rolling, and becoming exhausted occurred. Thiru-Navukkarasar thinks, ‘I have committed a great sin. Even upon me, who has committed such a sin, you have showered such great grace. Am I worthy of all this?’ Thinking that he is not worthy of all this, he falls to the ground, rolls, and becomes exhausted, with his hairs standing on end and tears of joy flowing from his eyes. ‘I was lying in the deep pit of the external religion, Jainism.

You showed mercy on me to climb from that deep pit to the high ground of Shaivism, which is a great elevation.

Therefore, into that deep pit of Jainism where I lay, You poured your great flood. In that great flood, I floated and escaped from that deep pit and climbed onto the high ground of Shaivism. For that, you poured your mountain of great grace, which is a great flood,’ he sings.

Furthermore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman says, ‘I, who, due to delusion, did evil deeds, not knowing the way to rise from the deep pit of the external religion of the impatient Jains, who are base people, who multiplied falsehood as truth, what is the favor I can do in return for this colic disease, which has brought me the great blessing of reaching the lotus-like feet of Shiva Peruman, the husband of Parvati Ammaiyar, who has abundant fragrant hair?’ What favor can I do? He points to the colic disease and worships it.

Here, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman refers to the Jains as those who follow false speech. False speech means untruth. The mantra of the Jains is ‘asti nāsti,’ ‘is and is not,’ consisting of two words, ‘false’ and ‘true.’ Without that, when questioning objects in philosophical inquiry, their tradition is to state seven types: ‘is,’ ‘is not,’ ‘is and is not,’ and by adding ‘is not that’ and keeping it separate.

Furthermore, he refers to the Jains as impatient Jains. Impatience means It means tolerating other religions. Jains are those who have the intention of destroying other religions, differing from them. One of the religious tenets of Jains is to destroy and eliminate other religions.

Therefore, it is understood from this that they believe no other religions should exist besides their own, and that Jains are such intolerant people. As evidence for this, we can find these truths in the later events in the history of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, and in the Puranas of Thiru-Gnana Sambandha Peruman, Thandiyadigal, and others, as well as in religious polemical texts like Neelakesi. Jains, who claim to uphold non-violence, are those who incite murder. I was fallen into such a pit, without the knowledge to discern good from evil, I committed evil deeds due to delusion. Even though I did not do all these myself, but rather because of the place I was in, it is still a punishable offense. For example, even the Devas who went to Daksha’s Yaga were punished, weren’t they?

Similarly, I too am worthy of punishment. Nevertheless, you showed mercy on me and ruled over me by giving me colic disease.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasar, who praised the Lord, worships the colic disease that was instrumental in his return from the pit to the Shaivite religion. He asks, ‘What return can I make for this colic disease? What favor can I do?’ He points to the colic disease and worships it. That colic He expresses gratitude for the disease because it was instrumental in his union with the Lord.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman praises the Lord. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman praises and worships the Lord, contemplating the Lord’s immense grace at Thiru-Adhigai Thiru-Veerattanam.

Let us continue to contemplate the history of how the Lord continued to bestow His grace upon Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar within the Thiru-Veerattanam temple at Thiru-Adhigai. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part Two Hundred Ninety-Nine, Thirunindracharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Within the Thiru-Athikai Veerattanam temple, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sang the Thiru-Pathikam “Kootraayina Vaaru.” Immediately after singing that pathikam, his colic disease was cured.

Thereafter, he praised and glorified the Lord.

At that time, the Lord, as an ethereal voice, declared, “From today, the name Thiru-Navukkarasu shall be fitting for you.” Marul Neekkiyar was Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s childhood name. When he joined the Jain faith, his name was Dharma Senar. When he suffered from colic disease and came here, after his colic disease was cured, the name Dharma Sena which our Nayanar had been bearing, was replaced by the name Thiru-Navukkarasu bestowed by Lord Shiva. The Lord, as an ethereal voice, granted this name. Sekkizhar Peruman mentions this in the following verse: “Mevutra ivvelaiyil neediya seer veerattam amarnda piraan arulaal paavutru alar sen tamilin sol vala pathikodai paadiya paanmaiyinaal naavukkarasu endru ulagu ezhum naamam nayappura navarkkum viyappura manju urai vaanidaiye oru vaaimai ezhundathuve.” This verse was sung by Sekkizhar Peruman. The meaning of this verse is as follows: Thus, immediately after Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s colic disease was cured, as he was praising and glorifying the Lord, an ethereal voice arose through the grace of Thiru-Veerattaneswarar.

A voice from the cloud-laden sky arose, and that voice spoke as follows: “By virtue of having sung the Thiru-Pathikam, rich in sweet Tamil words, which blossomed in harmony with song, your auspicious name, Thiru-Navukkarasu, shall be fittingly known throughout the seven worlds.” This ethereal voice arose. After our Nayanar, suffering from colic disease, sang the Thiru-Pathikam “Kootraayina Vaaru,” and his colic disease was cured, the Nayanar, in the compassion of the Lord, was moved. It was declared that it would be fitting throughout the worlds. What kind of Thiru-Navukkarasu did that voice speak of? It said, “Because you have sung the Thiru-Pathikam, rich in sweet words, your auspicious name, Thiru-Navukkarasu, shall be fitting throughout the seven worlds.” Sekkizhar Peruman sings in the verse, “Paavutru alar sen thamil pathikodai paadiyinaal.” Sekkizhar Peruman sings these many attributes as a prefix to the first Thiru-Pathikam, “Kootraayina Vaaru,” sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, as if spoken by an ethereal voice. The Thiru-Pathikam beginning with “Kootraayina Vaaru” is a pathikam that embodies all these qualities: being poetic, blossoming, being pure Tamil, having sweet words, possessing strength, and being a garland of verses.

The term “pathikam” means a collection of ten songs. It is our tradition to name a collection of ten songs as a pathikam.

Therefore, this is a traditional name. Generally, even if there are eleven or twelve or more verses in some pathikams, they are still called pathikams by the rules of exception. The Thevara pathikams of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman usually consist of eleven verses. Some pathikams consist of twelve verses.

Similarly, some pathikams, such as the Vaalkozhiputhur Pathikam composed by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, contain twelve verses.

Likewise, the Thiru-Aiyyatru Thiruvarutha Pathikam, “Sindhippariyana,” composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, contains twenty verses. The Siththathokai and Thiru-Kurunthokai contain thirty verses. Despite all this, since the majority of them contain ten verses, it is our tradition to generally refer to them as “pathikam.” Furthermore, “pathikam” also has another meaning: to compile and state various meanings.

Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman here names the collection of ten songs beginning with “Kootraayina Vaaru,” composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, as a pathikam. As an attribute to that pathikam, the ethereal voice is said to have declared all these attributes.
