Besides that, the following books are associated with this Thiru-sthalam: Periyanayaki Amman Pathigam composed by Kumaradevar, Kshetra Kovai sung by Guru Namasivaya Adigal, Pazhamalai Andhadhi composed by Sivaprakasa Adigal, Periyanayaki Ammai Viruttham, Periyanayaki Ammai Kattalai Kazhithurai, Bhikshadana Navamani Malai, and Periyanayakiyamai Pillai-th-thamil composed by Sokkalinga Adigal. All these are facts found in the Sthala Purana, the history of the Thiru-mudukundra Thiru-sthalam. The Phalastuthi (fruit of praise) of this Sthala Purana states that those who learn and listen to this Sthala Purana will attain Sivagathi (liberation). ‘No need to perform any penance, no need to perform charities, by merely understanding the Virudhagiri Purana of Bhuvanesan, sorrow will be dispelled.’ Learned ones and listeners will attain liberation; it is Shiva’s command, Shiva’s command, it is the truth,’ thus states the Virudhagiri Sthala Purana Phalastuthi.

Continuing with the history of Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar, let us contemplate the Thiru-pathigam that Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar blessed this Thiru-sthalam with. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 352, Thiru-nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar, having worshipped the Lord in Thiru-mudukundram, also known as Virudhachalam, blessed it with a Thiru-thandagam. This is compiled as the sixty-eighth Thiru-pathigam in the Sixth Thiru-murai.

Now, let us briefly contemplate the verses of this Thiru-pathigam and their concise meanings.

First verse: Karumaniyai Kanagathin Kundrappanai Karuthuvaarkku Aatra Eliyaan Thannai Gurumaniyai Kolaravu Ondru Aattuvaanai Kolvengai Adalaanai Kovananai Arumaniyai Adainthavarkku Amuthu Oppaanai Aananjum Aadiyai Naan Abayampukka Thiru-maniyai Thiru-mudukundru Udaiyaan Thannai Thiru- The meaning of this is: ‘Like the pupil of the eye, he is precious; like a golden mountain, he is; for those who meditate, he is very simple; a good-colored ruby; one who makes a fierce snake dance; one who wears the skin of a fierce tiger; one who wears a loincloth; a rare gem; like nectar to those who seek refuge in him; one who bathes in the five products of the cow; the precious gem that grants liberation to me who sought refuge; the Lord who resides in Thiru-mudukundram—I, who am full of evil deeds, have been bewildered until now, not knowing him.’ Now, the second sacred verse: ‘Kaarozhiya Kandaththu Em Kadavul Thannai Kaapaali Kattanga Mentinaanai Paarozhiyai Vinnoliyai Paathaalanaip Paal Mathiyam Soodi Or’ The meaning of this is: ‘My Lord, whose throat is dark like a cloud, who is Kapali, who holds the Kattanga weapon, who is the light of the earth, the light of the sky, and the light of the netherworld, who wears the crescent moon, a virtuous one, a great light, one who has the female part (Parvati) in his body, one who removes the karmas of those who desire him, the glorious light, the Lord who resides in Thiru-mudukundram—I, who am full of evil deeds, have been bewildered until now, not knowing him.’ Now, verse number three: ‘Eththisaiyum Vaanavargal Thozha Nindraanai Yerurnda Pemmanai’ The meaning of this is: ‘He who stands to be worshipped by celestials in all directions, the Lord who rides the bull, to whom I, a devotee, bowed down saying ‘my Lord,’ and who trained me to sing garlands of verses for many days; he who is like a pearl, my gem, a ruby, like a sprouting red coral shoot, the enlightened one, the Lord who resides in Thiru-mudukundram—I, who am full of evil deeds, have been bewildered until now, not knowing him.’ Now, verse number four: ‘Oon Karuvin Ulnindra Jothiyaanai Utthamanai Patthar Manam Kodikondaanai Kaan Thirindhu Kaandheepam Enthi’ The meaning of this is: ‘He who is the light within the life that is conceived in the body, the perfect one, who resides in the hearts of devotees, who roamed the forest as a hunter, holding the Gandiva bow for Arjuna, whose throat is like a dark cloud, who is fire and wind, who, having considered, took me as his servant and placed his sacred feet on my head, the sweet sugarcane, the Lord who resides in Thiru-mudukundram—I, who am full of evil deeds, have been bewildered until now, not knowing him.’ Now, verse number five: ‘Thakkanathu Peruvelvi Thagarththaanaagi Thaam’ The meaning of this is: ‘He who destroyed Daksha’s great sacrifice, who himself is Brahma residing in the lotus, who is the great fire, water, and sky, who is beyond the upper worlds and also in this world, who adorns conch shells and pearls, and who, for his devotees, according to their maturity, became the six different religions, the direction, my Lord who resides in Thiru-mudukundram—I, who am full of evil deeds, have been bewildered until now, not knowing him.’ Now, verse number six: ‘Pugazholiyai Purameriththa Punithan Thannai Pon Pothintha Meniyanai Pura’ The meaning of this is: ‘He who is the light of fame, the pure one who burned the three cities, whose body is adorned with gold, the ancient one, who became the sound of wisdom and the sound of blossoming, the unique one who resides in Venkadu, who, with the sound of his anklets and the jingle of his bangles, goes from door to door for alms, the shining light, the Lord who resides in Thiru-mudukundram—I, who am full of evil deeds, have been bewildered until now, not knowing him.’ Now, Verse number seven: ‘Porththaanaiyin Uri Thol Pongap Ponga Puli Ethale Udaiyaaga Thirivaan Thannai Kaaththaanai Aim Pulanum Purangal Moondrum Kaalanaiyum Kurai Kadalaal Kaaynthaan Thannai Maaththaadi Pattharaay Vanangum Thondar Valvinai Verarum Vannam Marunthumaagi Theerththaanai Thiru-mudukundru Udaiyaan Thannai Theevinaiyen Ariyaathu Thigaiththavaare.’ The meaning of this is: ‘He who wears the skin of an elephant, and whose body shines brightly as he roams wearing a tiger skin, who controlled the five senses, who destroyed the three cities, who kicked Yama with his sacred foot, who performs the supreme dance, who becomes the medicine to eradicate the strong karmas and the diseases arising from them for devotees who worship him, and who thus removes all those, the Lord who resides in Thiru-mudukundram—I, who am full of evil deeds, have been bewildered until now, not knowing him.’ The Peruman residing in Thiru-Mudukunram, I, a person of evil deeds, have been deluded and ignorant until now.

Now, in verse number eight: “Thuravaadhe yaakkai thurandhaan thannai sodhi muzhu mudhalaay nindraan thannai piravaadhe evvuyirkkum thaaneyaagi penninodu aanuruvaay nindraan thannai maravaadhe than thirame vaazhthum thondar manathagathe anavaratham manni nindra thiralaanai thirumudukunru udaiyaan thannai theevinaiyen ariyaadhe thigaiththavaare.” Its meaning is: He who is naturally free from bonds, who is in the form of light, who never takes birth but is the benefactor of all living beings who take birth, who is in the form of both woman and man, who is always present in the hearts of devotees who praise His attributes without forgetting Him, the Peruman of Thiru-Mudukunram, I, a person of evil deeds, have been deluded and ignorant until now. He who is always present in the hearts of devotees, the Peruman residing in Thiru-Mudukunram, I, a person of evil deeds, have been deluded and ignorant until now.

Now, in verse number nine: “Pottrunai pulaal naaru kabaalamendhi puvalogam ellaam muzhi thandhaanaai muttraadha ven thingal kanniyaanai muzhu mudhalaay moovulagum mudivu ondru illaa katrunai kaalaththi malaiyaan thannai karudhaadhaar puramoonrum eriya ambaal settraanai thirumudukunru udaiyaan thannai theevinaiyen ariyaadhe thigaiththavaare.” Its meaning is: He who is like a golden pillar, who carries a skull reeking of flesh and wanders all over the upper worlds, who wears the crescent moon, who is the primordial God, who pervades all worlds and supports them like an endless stone pillar, He who resides in Kaalaththi Malai, who destroyed the three cities of His enemies with an arrow, the Peruman residing in Thiru-Mudukunram, I, a person of evil deeds, have been deluded and ignorant until now.

Now, in verse number ten: “Ighazhdhaanai irubadhu thol neriyavur undri ezhu narambin isaippaada inidhu kettru pugazhdhaanai poondhuruththi meyaan thannai punniyanai vinnnavargal nidhiyam thannai magizhdhaanai malai magalvor paagam vaiththu valar madhiyam sadai vaiththu maalor paagam thigazhdhaanai thirumudukunru udaiyaan thannai theevinaiyen ariyaadhe thigaiththavaare.” Its meaning is: He who, when Ravana, who scorned Shiva, shook Mount Kailash, pressed His finger so that Ravana’s twenty shoulders were crushed, and then, hearing his music played on seven strings, praised him as a musician, He who resides in the sacred place of Poondhuruththi as a virtuous one, who is the treasure of the celestials, who rejoices with Parvati as one half of His body, who wears the crescent moon in His matted locks, and who shines with Thirumal as the other half of His body, the Peruman residing in Thiru-Mudukunram, I, a person of evil deeds, have been deluded and ignorant until now.

This is the Thevara Thiruththandaga Thiruppathigam sung by Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar on the Lord of Thiru-Mudukunram, also known as Virudhachalam, along with its ten verses and their brief meaning.

Next, we will contemplate the sacred history of Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part Three Hundred and Fifty-Three, Thirunindrachcharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We saw that Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar had a vision of the Lord in Thiru-Mudukunram, also known as Virudhachalam, and sang a Thiruppathigam. Sekkizhar Peruman sings that Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar continues to visit many sacred places: “Vandhamizh men maa malar maalai punaindharuli marungulla thandhurai neerpadhigalum thanividaiyaaar mevi idam kondarulum thaanangal kumbittu gunadhisai mel pundarigath thadam soozhndha nivaakkaraiye podhuvaar.” Sekkizhar Peruman sings that after singing Thevarams, which are like soft flower garlands made of rich Tamil, he departed from Virudhachalam, He visits and worships many water-filled sacred places nearby. Sekkizhar Peruman sings that Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar worships the unique Shiva Peruman and the sacred places where He resides. Sekkizhar Peruman refers to the Thiruppathigams composed by Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar in Thiruvaraththurai and Thiru-Mudukunram as “van thamizh men malar maalai” (strong Tamil soft flower garlands).

In this way, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar visits many places and composes many Tamil garlands. He visits many temples in those places. He visits the temples where the Lord is manifest and seated. “Neyam malindhavar vedamum aalayam thaanum arananaththozhume” is The twelfth sutra of Sivagnana Botham. For this, Sivagnana Munivar, who gave the Sivagnana Maapadiyam, states the reason that He stands brightly in other places and unbrightly in places other than those. That is, even though the Lord is omnipresent, He is manifest like ghee in curd only in two places: the sacred form inside the temple and His devotees.

In all other places, He stands unmanifest like ghee in milk.

Therefore, it is said here to worship only in these two places. That is why, even those who are Jivanmuktas, it is said in the Saiva tradition that they should worship the form of Shiva’s devotees and The temples where Shiva Peruman is enshrined. For those with true knowledge, Parameswaran is present everywhere without distinction. Is it not appropriate to see such a Parameswaran?

Furthermore, in Nindra Thiruththandagam and Sri Rudram, it is explained how the Lord is present everywhere, in animate and inanimate objects. Do not Sri Rudram and Nindra Thiruththandagam describe and prescribe worship for all these places where the Lord is present? When the Lord is omnipresent in all places, is it not appropriate to see Parameswaran in all these places? The question may arise within us: Is it not appropriate to see the Lord in all places when He is omnipresent? If the question is asked why, even though the Lord Shiva is omnipresent, it is stated in this twelfth sutra that one should see and worship Parameswaran in the sacred form of Shiva’s devotees and in the Shiva Linga forms in temples, it is because Shiva Peruman, though omnipresent, will manifest brightly like ghee in curd in the sacred form of Shiva’s devotees and in the sacred forms in temples. In all other places, He stands unmanifest like ghee in milk.

Therefore, the sacred form of the devotee and This twelfth sutra states that one should worship the Shiva temple as Parameswaran.

Therefore, Sri Rudram and Nindra Thiruththandagam state that the Lord is present in all things. But the twelfth sutra of Sivagnana Botham states that He is manifest in the two places mentioned above and unmanifest in other places.

Therefore, according to the rule that even Jivanmuktas should worship the sacred form and the temple, our Nayanmars and Samayacharyas, who were Jivanmuktas, went to temples and worshipped the Lord.

Therefore, as mentioned in Sekkizhar Peruman’s song, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar went to many sacred places and worshipped Shiva Peruman there. Having worshipped thus, he comes eastward along the banks of the Niva River. The Swetha River, also known as Vellaru, which flows near the town of Bhuvanagiri, north of Thillai, is called the Niva River. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar comes along the banks of this Niva River.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar travels and approaches the sacred city of Thiruchitrambalam. Desiring to worship the sacred feet of the Lord who performs the dance of grace in Thillai Ambalam and to attain the benefit of both body and soul, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar approaches Thiruppuliyur, also known as Thiruchitrambalam. This Thiruchitrambalam is a city of never-ending glory. Other While other sacred places are spoken of in the Mahapuranas and other Upapuranas, this sacred place of Thiruchitrambalam, unlike them, is a sacred city praised by the Vedas, which are the word of the Lord, such as the Pundarika and Mandukya Upanishads.

Thiruchitrambalam is also eternally glorious, spoken of in the Tamil Vedas such as Thevaram and Thiruvasagam, which are the sacred words of the Acharyas who stood in the service of the Lord, becoming one with Him. It is said that Thiruchitrambalam is where the special people who perform the five sacrifices (Panchayagna) live, where wealth always increases, and where food is always served. These are the general characteristics for all three periods of time. The never-ending glory of this Thiruchitrambalam, also known as Thillaivanam, is the result of the Tamil Vedas describing these glories in the present tense. It is also the glory of this place that gave us our Periya Puranam. “Aanaadha seer thillai ambalaththae aadugindra aanaaru pudai parakkum malarchchadaiyaar adi vanangi oonaalum uyiraalum ulla payan kola ninaindhu thenaaru malarchcholai thiruppuliyoor marungu anaindhaar” is the sacred verse of Sekkizhar Swamigal.

Here, Sekkizhar Peruman states in the introduction to the Puranam that to worship the golden feet of the Lord who dances in Thiruchitrambalam, the birth of a body that has attained flesh is to attain the certainty of its purpose. Accordingly, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar comes to Thiruchitrambalam, desiring to attain the benefit of both the body and the soul. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar comes to Thiruchitrambalam, desiring to attain the benefit of both the body and the soul. Without the body, the soul cannot benefit, and without the soul, the body cannot benefit.

Therefore, Sekkizhar Swamigal says here, “the benefit of both the body and the soul.” Here, “oon” refers to the body, but more specifically, it refers to the human body. It indicates that humans have a very special body compared to other births. Even plants like trees and shrubs have bodies and births, but those bodies are not bodies that have attained flesh. Other living beings like sheep and cattle also have bodies that have attained flesh. Among them, the human body is the body that has attained flesh, which is the abode of superior knowledge, having come up through virtuous deeds.

Therefore, in the second verse of the Periya Puranam, it is sung: “Oon adaindha udambin piraviye thaan adaindha urudhiyai saarumal then adaindha malarpozhil thillaiyul maanadam sey varadhar pottral thozha.” The purpose of human birth and intelligence is to worship the feet of the Lord. Even though the body follows the soul’s direction, acts like pilgrimage and sacred service can only be performed by the soul using the body.

At the same time, seeing Shiva Peruman and attaining supreme bliss upon seeing Him can only be done by the soul. It cannot be done by the body.

Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman differentiated here by saying “by body and by soul.” Thirumooladeva Nayanar also said, “I nurtured the body, I nurtured the soul.” And Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, regarding reaching the sacred place of Thiruchitrambalam, said, “If I can see the raised golden foot, I desire human birth on this great earth.” Thiruppuliyur, another name for Thiruchitrambalam, is mentioned here. In this verse, Puliyur means the place where the tiger-footed sage Vyagrapada Munivar worshipped and attained fame.

Hence, it is named Puliyur. As soon as he reached the sacred boundary of Thiruchitrambalam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar prostrated himself on the ground. The sacred boundary of Thiruchitrambalam is a structure one kadam (about 10 miles) in all four directions from the city of Thillai. Upon reaching this boundary of Thillai, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar prostrates himself on the ground. As he approaches Thillai, the desire to see the Lord dancing in bliss within it grows stronger and stronger in Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar.

Therefore, he continues his journey. He travels through the fertile plains. The fertile plains of Thiruchitrambalam’s sacred boundary are filled with groves, peacocks, lotus ponds, and fields. In the Saiva tradition, reaching Thillai is of unique significance.

Therefore, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar travels from the boundary of Thillai, crossing the fields, towards the city of Thiruchitrambalam.

Next, we will contemplate the history of Appar Peruman’s vision of Thiruchitrambalam. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part Three Hundred and Fifty-Four, Thirunindrachcharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, having visited many sacred places, reached the boundary of Thillai and continued his journey towards Thillai. Sekkizhar Peruman, with his Shiva-vision, observes and describes the natural beauty of Thillai to us. We saw that when Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar traveled from the boundary of Thiruchitrambalam, he saw many water bodies in the outer region.

Next, we will see that there are agricultural fields. Beautiful lotus flowers have bloomed in these water bodies. Lotus flowers with fragrant petals are densely bloomed in the water bodies. Buffaloes are creatures of dull intellect. Even such dull-witted buffaloes, knowing the fragrance and quality, eagerly graze on the fresh lotus flowers. This shows us that even among dull-witted buffaloes, there are creatures with a more developed intellect, shining with special intelligence.

The new flowers are abundant enough for the buffaloes to graze and fill their stomachs. This indicates the richness of that land. Sugarcane grows beside these water bodies. These sugarcane stalks have grown densely and tall like bamboo. From the nodes of these thick sugarcane stalks, pearls emerge as the nodes burst. We have already seen that there are twenty places where pearls are born, and sugarcane is one of them.

We have already seen that pearls can also emerge from sugarcane.

Thus, the nodes of the sugarcane growing here burst and pearls emerge from them. Sekkizhar Peruman sings that this is like the sugarcane shedding tears upon seeing the sacred form of the great Thirunavukkarasu Peruman and melting with emotion. Seeing the sacred form of great Shiva devotees, Shedding tears of emotion is a characteristic of love. “Neyam malindhavar vedamum aranenath thozhume” is the twelfth sutra of Sivagnana Botham. According to this, when one sees the sacred form of devotees, one should worship with love and a melting heart, seeing them as Parameswaran. The methods of worshipping Shiva Peruman are also applicable to the sacred form of devotees.

Here, the sacred form of Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar is one that inspires love in those who see it.

Therefore, it is as if pearls are falling from the nodes of the sugarcane, like tears shed upon seeing that sacred form. Whenever Sekkizhar Peruman describes natural resources, he connects them with Shiva. This is a characteristic we see throughout the Periya Puranam. To Sekkizhar Peruman’s Shiva-eyes, Shiva and His devotees appear everywhere, in plants and all other places, due to his loving nature. Because of this, wherever he looks, Shiva and His devotees appear. He describes this to us in his sacred verses.

As the Lord has indicated, the sugarcane here has grown well, and it is implied that the paddy fields have also grown well. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar continues his journey. As he travels, he passes the paddy fields and moves forward, approaching Thiruchitrambalam. As seen in the previous verse, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, who is seen by others, The great one, who possessed a melting holy form, was not only that but also great in wisdom.

Here, wisdom refers to Shiva-gnanam. As he walks, the paddy fields recede behind him, and he proceeds forward. In front, Nandavanams (flower gardens) appear. In those Nandavanams, cuckoos are present.

There, the cuckoos call out. From the branches of the trees in the Nandavanams, the cuckoos call out. How do the cuckoos call out? “Viduvir iruvinai perugi thodar piniyuru paasam parivutridu anaiyumin” (Abandon the two karmas that proliferate and the binding attachment that causes suffering; come here). Sekkizhar Peruman sings that the cuckoos on the tree branches in the Nandavanams call out thus. On the path of Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, there are two On both sides, the cuckoos in the Nandavanams call out in this manner.

The cuckoos call out, “Abandon!” They call out, “O those who wish to abandon the sinful paths of birth! Abandon the paths that lead to hostile births!” They also call out, “Come here so that the two karmas that proliferate and the binding attachment may cease!” The cuckoos call out, “Iruvinai perugi thodar piniyuru paasam” (The two karmas proliferate and the binding attachment continues). As the two karmas proliferate, the attachment that binds you grows stronger and stronger. The cuckoos call out, “Come to Thillai so that this attachment may be uprooted and cease.” The cuckoos call out, “Come to Thiruchitrambalam!” In this song, it is stated that due to this birth, the two karmas proliferate.

Here, “birth” refers to the body, and it signifies the Maya-malas (impurity of illusion), because the Lord creates the body, instruments, worlds, and experiences from Maya.

Therefore, mentioning the body is mentioning the Maya-malas. It is stated that due to this birth, the two karmas proliferate. By mentioning these “two karmas,” Karma-malas (impurity of action) are indicated here. In this birth, the two karmas proliferate.

Therefore, the attachment that binds you grows stronger and stronger, it is stated next. The “paasam” (attachment) mentioned here refers to Anava-malas (impurity of ego). The two karmas, good karma and bad karma, Both become causes for birth.

Therefore, this attachment binds you more and more, making you stronger. So that it does not gain such strength, so that it is uprooted, so that this attachment diminishes and wears away, the cuckoos call out from the Thiru-Nandavanams on both sides, “Join the path of Shiva!” Therefore, it is stated here that joining the path of Shiva is the only way for attachment to wear away. Birth and karma bind souls only through Anava (ego).

Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman connects “pava neri piravi pava neri” (the path of birth, the path of birth) and “iruvinai perugi thodar paasam” (attachment that proliferates and continues due to two karmas) with attachment. Why do the cuckoos call out to us in this manner? Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar is walking along that path to Thillai, approaching Thillai. Seeing this, the cuckoos in Thillai call out in this manner. Because the great one in Shiva-gnanam is now approaching.

Therefore, this is a good time. So, all of you, come here! By seeing Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar and through the good fruit of that darshan, you will see the Lord of the Sacred Dance of Thiruchitrambalam and make a way for birth to cease, the cuckoos call out to the people of this world. At the time when Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar is approaching Thillai, these cuckoos call out in this manner. Manikkavasagar Peruman has composed “Kuyil Pathu” (Ten Verses on the Cuckoo) in Thiruvachagam. Are not these cuckoos in Thillai now the cuckoos that have descended in that lineage, having heard the teachings of Manikkavasagar Peruman in that “Kuyil Pathu”?

Therefore, seeing Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar approaching, those cuckoos call out to the people of the world. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar sees such Thiru-Nandavanams (sacred gardens) in front of him. Sekkizhar Peruman, who sang that the paddy fields quickly receded behind, sings that Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar saw the Thiru-Nandavanam in front of him. All along the path that Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar travels, even though there are many things, only Shiva and things related to Shiva are visible to the eyes of great ones. In accordance with this truth, for Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, for his Shiva-punyam (merit), Thiru-Nandavanams that are useful appear before him. Just as darkness does not shine before the sun, and unreality does not shine before reality, and just as the wise see only the Supreme and not material things, this is also the meaning of the truths of Gnana Sastras.

In those Thiru-Nandavanams, there are many flowering trees planted for cut flowers. We have seen these types of trees earlier at the beginning of Periya Puranam. Planting trees that yield cut flowers in Nandavanams brings great and lasting benefits.

Therefore, the author praises them greatly. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar is one who performs Thiru-Thondu (sacred service) without ceasing, rather than just manual service, as in “pitharku patharagi arumbu nan malargal kondu” (being devoted to the mad one, with budding good flowers) and “poomalai punainthethi” (adorning with flower garlands and praising). He is one who performs Thiru-Thondu (sacred service).

Therefore, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar sees those Thiru-Nandavanams related to that Thiru-Thondu with great fondness. Since cut flowers are mentioned in this song, we should also include other types of flowers such as climbing flowers, water flowers, and ground flowers, by extension.

Let us resume our reflection. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 355. Thirunindrachcharukkam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We saw that Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, on his way to Thillai, reverently bowed to all the Nandavanams on its border. Upon seeing the Thiru-Nandavanams, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar bowed and worshipped them, and then approached them.

Bowing and worshipping the Thiru-Nandavanams means worshipping with three limbs, five limbs, or eight limbs.

Similarly, we have seen earlier that Sundaramurthy Swamigal also bowed to all these Thiru-Nandavanams on his way to Thillai. The pure, mature souls that possess tender leaves, flowers, unripe fruits, ripe fruits, roots, etc., which are offered to Lord Shiva, Are present in the Thiru-Nandavanams as trees, plants, and creepers.

Therefore, bowing to all of these as we go is the path shown to us by our ancestors. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar performed penance in all his previous births. Because of that, he attained the state of a Thondar (devotee) in this birth. He remains steadfast in that state. He is also a Tamil king. Seeing Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, who stands firm in the state of a Thondar and excels in that sacred service, the small parrots called Sirupuvai, the Myna birds, and other birds in the Thiru-Nandavanams, upon seeing Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar approaching, are filled with pride and They are filled with joy and pride, thinking that they have been blessed with the fortune of seeing Thirunavukkarasar, this holy devotee with such a sacred form.

They exclaim, “This is a wonder!” and praise Shiva with “Hara Hara!” “Atthan aandu than adiyarin kootiya athisayam kandame” (We have seen the wonder of the Lord gathering His devotees) is the Athichayappathu (Ten Verses on Wonder) composed by Manikkavasagar Peruman. According to that, all these birds saw wonder, experienced joy, and felt pride. These birds come before our Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar and speak the words “Hara Hara.” These birds are from the Nandavanams of Thillai.

Therefore, having lived in the Nandavanams of Thillai for many years, they have the habit of saying “Hara Hara” to the Shiva devotees who come to Thillai. These parrots and birds already possess that habit of speaking.

Therefore, now, upon seeing the holy form of Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, they have come, saying “Hara Hara,” worshipped, rejoiced, and felt proud. Those parrots are capable of reciting the Vedas and Thiru-Pathigams (sacred hymns), beginning with “Hara Hara.” “Parisaiyum pandithargal pannalum payindru odum osai kettu verimali pozhir kilai vedangal porutkollum mizhalaiyame” (Hearing the sound of scholars reciting the Vedas with melody, the branches of the fragrant groves understand the Vedas; this is Mizhalai) is the sacred utterance of Aludaiya Pillaiyar. We can also recall here the meaning of Aludaiya Pillaiyar’s Thevaram, “Siraiyarum madakiliye” (O parrot with beautiful wings).

Thus, not only do these parrots and Myna birds and other birds speak “Hara Hara” upon seeing Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, but they also recite the Vedas and Thiru-Pathigams. Even though it is only parrots and small Puvai birds that speak in this manner, since they speak the words of Shiva, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar considers them to be Shiva’s devotees and bows to all these birds. Would Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, who even bowed to the plants in the Thiru-Nandavanams that provide materials for Shiva Puja, pass by without bowing to these birds that speak the words of Shiva?

Therefore, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar proceeds, bowing even to these birds. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar considers these parrots, Puvai birds, etc., to be exalted beings who, due to the special karma of previous births, were born, lived, saw, heard, spoke, and wandered in this sacred place, thereby attaining great merit. Not only that, but it is Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar’s nature to bow immediately upon hearing the words of Shiva, isn’t it?

Therefore, he bows according to that nature. Devotees with a compassionate heart, who already possess grace, melt in their hearts and bow when they hear the words of Shiva. Rejoicing, melting of the heart, and overflowing love upon merely hearing the name of the Lord are the characteristics of an excellent heroine. We can recall here the meaning of Aludaiya Pillaiyar’s Thiru-Thonipuram Thevaram, where the heroine asks the parrot, “Ilam piraiyalan thirunamam enakku oru kal pesaye” (O young parrot, please speak the sacred name of the crescent-moon-crowned Lord to me just once). “Erar ilam kiliye engal perunthuraikkon seer ar thirunamam thernthu urayay” (O beautiful young parrot, please choose and speak the glorious sacred name of our Lord of Perunthurai) is from Thiruvachagam, Thiru-Thasangam. Such a state occurs only to souls that have matured through penance performed in many previous births.

For our Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, the grace that had already sharpened within his heart, upon hearing those parrots and small Puvai birds speak the words of Shiva, that hearing produced joy, love, and an even greater, more complete love. All these are states of mind with different emotional experiences. These were all states of mind that Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar already possessed.

Here, the parrots and Puvai birds speaking those words further aided this. Due to the love that arose in this way, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar’s speech falters. This is one of the expressions that arise from intense love.

Similarly, shedding tears, sobbing, Goosebumps, etc., are also expressions of love.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar reaches the border of Thillai. Thillai is a sacred place where Brahmins who speak eloquent sacred words reside. Thirugnanasambandha Peruman refers to the Thillai Vazh Andanars (Brahmins of Thillai) as those who “kattraangu eri ombi kaliyai varame settar” (protected the fire as they learned and prevented the Kali Yuga from coming) and as “andanar piriyatha thillai” (Thillai from which Brahmins do not depart) and as “seelathar” (those of good conduct). Sundaramurthy Swamigal has sung in Thiru-Thondu Thogai, “Thillai vazh andanartham adiyarkkum adiyen” (I am a servant to the servants of the Thillai Vazh Andanars). Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar reaches the border of that sacred city of Thillai, where such esteemed Thillai Vazh Andanars reside.

There, to the west, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar reaches the western gate. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar set out from Thiru-Muthukundram, visited Thiru-Koodalai, Attur, and other sacred places along the way, and then came from the west along the Niva river bank towards Thiru-Puliyur.

Therefore, he reaches the border of Thillai city through the western gate.

Similarly, we saw that Sundaramurthy Swamigal came through the northern gate of Thillai.

Likewise, in the Puranam of Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, whom we are about to see, Thirugnanasambandha Peruman comes from Sirkazhi to Thillai.

Therefore, he reaches Thillai through the southern sacred gate. Manikkavasagar Peruman, another Samayacharyar, reaches Thillai through the eastern gate.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Arasu Nayanar reaches the city of Thillai through the western gate. Let us continue to reflect on Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar’s darshan of Thillai. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 356. Thirunindrachcharukkam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal enters the city of Thillai through its northern gate.

There, devotees who consider Shiva’s penance as their primary goal welcome Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar. Devotees of Shiva, who consider penance as their primary goal. “Primary” here means capital. The meaning of the word “Thapothanar” is also the same.

Thus, these Shiva devotees, who consider penance as their capital, welcome Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar. The penance performed by these devotees is a penance that bestows grace to remove suffering and birth. That is, the penance performed by the devotees is Shiva Puja itself. Although this birth may seem like pleasure to us, in the end, it brings suffering.

However, it is Shiva Puja that removes such suffering and brings joy.

Thus, Shiva devotees are those who consider Shiva Puja, which is the penance that removes this suffering-inducing birth, as their capital and primary goal. Such Shiva devotees welcome Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar. In Thillai, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar is preeminent through penance.

Thus, Shiva devotees, who consider Shiva’s penance as their primary goal, welcome Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, who is preeminent through penance. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, having entered the city of Thillai in this manner, bows to the sacred streets of Thillai. The sacred streets of Thillai are streets where the essence of Shiva prevails and flourishes. The sacred streets of Thillai are streets with good mansions filled with the Thillai Vazh Andanars, who are wealthy families that cherish the holy feet of the Lord of the Dance, who owns everyone as His servants. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar bows to and approaches such a sacred street where the essence of Shiva prevails. In this sacred street, there are good sacred mansions filled with Thillai Vazh Andanars.

These Thillai Vazh Andanars are those who have mastered many branches of learning, beginning with the great Vedas. Learning is a vast ocean. “Kalvi ennum palkadal pizhaithum” (Having crossed the many oceans of learning) is from Thiruvachagam. The Thillai Vazh Andanars are those who have mastered such learning. That is, the Thillai Vazh Andanars are those who have fully mastered all branches of knowledge, understood their ultimate conclusion, and become clear, and at the same time, without getting entangled and confused within these branches of knowledge, thinking them to be the ultimate truth, they aspire for Shiva-gnanam, which lies beyond them. The Thillai Vazh Andanars are those who aspire for Shiva-gnanam, which is beyond artistic knowledge and is attained through such artistic knowledge.

Therefore, they are devotees who cherish the anklets of the Lord of the Dance. These Thillai Vazh Andanars are those who have mastered many branches of learning, beginning with the great Vedas.

Therefore, they are those who consider themselves, as souls, to be possessions, and the Lord to be their master who owns them, and serving such a Lord always and cherishing His anklets to be the means of salvation for the soul. The Thillai Vazh Andanars are those who, having learned and understood, acted accordingly and fully attained the undiminished wealth of Shiva. The street of Thillai city is a street with many mansions where such Thillai Vazh Andanars reside. The street of Thillai city grows and extends amidst the mansions of these Thillai Vazh Andanars. This sacred street of Thillai city is a sacred street where Shiva Himself prevails. This sacred street of Thillai city is a sacred street that bestows Shiva to those who approach and bow to it.

Sekkizhar Peruman sings in the Thirugnanasambandar Puranam, “Madhavangal nalkum thiruveethi nankum thozhuthu” (Bowing to the four sacred streets that bestow great penances). It is for this reason that this street possesses the unique and supreme distinction of having the Lord of the Sacred Dance, Ponnambalavanar, gracing the Thiru-chariot and uplifting all souls.

Thus, Sekkizhar Swamigal extols this sacred street of Thillai Thiru-nagaram. All our revered preceptors have traversed these sacred streets with reverence.

Therefore, as we circumambulate these sacred streets, we must proceed with devotion. To walk with head held high without venerating these streets is an offense.

Furthermore, Sekkizhar Peruman continues to sing the praises of this sacred street. Devas are beings who reside in the higher worlds; each Deva is preeminent in a particular cosmic sphere or world.

Thus, these respective Devas govern their own worlds. All the directional deities have assembled in Thillai to witness the Sacred Dance.

At that time, they established and worshipped Shiva Lingams in their respective directions, as is the sacred history of Thillai. Such is the glory of the streets of Thillai.

Furthermore, these Devas are those who, having performed sacrifices and other rituals, were granted the enjoyment of celestial pleasures such as Svarga by Shiva Peruman. These Devas, immersed in such pleasures, forgot Shiva Peruman for a long time, and as a result, they were tormented by Asuras. Subsequently, to alleviate their suffering and attain liberation through performing Shiva Punya, they came to this earthly realm. With various intentions, all the Devas converge upon these sacred streets of Thillai Thiru-nagaram. As many Devas thus gather closely in these sacred streets to worship the sacred feet of Shiva Peruman, their jeweled crowns clash against each other, scattering gems. All these scattered gems lie in the sacred street of Thillai.

However, Vayu Devan, considering these gems to be unsuitable objects for the sacred street of Thillai, removes them from the street with the wind, performing the sacred sweeping service. When Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar was performing service in Thirupugalur, specifically the Uzhavaara service, gold and nine precious gems appeared throughout those streets. He removed all of them with his Uzhavaara implement and deposited them in a pond. That is a history yet to unfold.

Similarly, here in the street of Thillai Thiru-nagaram, Vayu Devan removes all the gems from the scattered jeweled crowns of the Devas, performing the sacred sweeping service. These gems, having been used and scattered by the Devas, became impure.

Furthermore, they are products of Maya.

Therefore, these gems would obstruct the devotees walking in the sacred street of Thillai Thiru-nagaram.

Thus, it becomes Vayu Devan’s sacred duty to sweep them away. So, Vayu Devan removes all these gems and performs the sacred sweeping service.

After this, Varuna Devan cleanses these sacred streets with water, purifying them. These Devas are worshipped by lesser beings according to their respective abilities and positions.

However, Shiva’s devotees are worshipped by all, including the Devas.

Therefore, considering the gems scattered from the jeweled crowns of the Devas who worship Shiva’s devotees to be impure, and believing they would obstruct Shiva’s devotees walking in that sacred street, Vayu Devan and Varuna perform this sacred service. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, revering these sacred streets with their high-flying banners and sacred mansions, approaches the seven-tiered western gopuram entrance. He bows and worships the gopuram. The three thousand of Thillai, Patanjali, Vyagrapada, Jaimini, Vyasa, Sukar, Sutar, and other sages, their sounds of praise are eternally heard as Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar approaches that western gopuram.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar worships the western gopuram and enters through its passage into the sacred temple. There, he beholds the golden-adorned sacred mansion. This sacred mansion, known as Thirumaligai Paththi, is a structure within the temple, adjacent to the sacred wall in Thillai. It is referred to as the golden-adorned sacred mansion. This Thirumaligai Paththi is a row of sacred mansions adorned with gold by King Anapaya Chozha and his predecessors. The term Thirumaligai also means sacred temple.

Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar circumambulates this sacred mansion. His ardent desire to worship the Lord who performs the dance of grace within the Thillai sacred temple and to venerate His sacred feet overflows. With a body filled with the ocean of love, his hair stands on end. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar reaches the Thiru-anukkan Thiru-vaayil Gopuram, which is the sacred golden gopuram. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, who entered Thillai through the western gate, worshipped the sacred streets, entered the western gopuram, circumambulated the Thirumaligai Paththi, and then entered the second gopuram on the eastern side, now stands before the Thiru-anukkan Thiru-vaayil Gopuram and worships that gopuram. Entering through the Thiru-anukkan Thiru-vaayil, he then directly beholds the Kanaka Podhu.

Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar beholds the Lord in the golden hall, the space where the Lord performs His dance. This Thiru-ambalam, the sacred hall where the Lord performs His sacred dance, is a Thiru-ambalam filled with the ever-increasing light of wisdom, manifesting with the enduring grace of liberation. The light of wisdom refers to the light of wisdom that is self-luminous, giving light to all luminous objects. Manikkavachaka Perumanar states in Thiruvasagam, in Neethal Vinnappam, “The beautiful feet from which all true light emanates.” That light here refers to the light of wisdom.

Thus, in that Thiru-ambalam, in the Thiruchitrambalam, which stands as the light of wisdom, he beholds and worships the sacred feet of the dancing Lord. Sekkizhar Peruman thus sings of the vision experienced by Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar: “With enduring grace, the overflowing light fills the hall, and with love that directly unites, he attains the state where the three qualities are experienced. Brahma, Vishnu, and the Devas, and all other beings, seek to understand the unique, dancing, ankleted, ambrosial sacred dance, and worship it in six ways.” The phrase “nanaivura” (to remember) appears, indicating the function of the mind among the four inner instruments. The phrase “nerae koodumbadi” (to unite directly) appears in this verse, indicating the function of the eye among the five external senses. The phrase “anbaal inporu gunamum” (with love, the quality of bliss) appears here. This refers to the state of sattva within the sattva guna among the three gunas.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar attains this rare state. This state is described by Sundaramurthy Swamigal in his verse when he beheld the Lord of the Dance in Thillai: “The five senses become eyes, the immeasurable four inner instruments become the mind, and the three gunas become pure sattva.” Sekkizhar Peruman seems to summarize that very idea here in this verse. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar beholds the sacred feet of the Lord performing the dance of grace in Thillai. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar’s entire mind becomes the Thiru-ambalam, shining brightly, filled with meditation. In his sacred mind, the Thiru-ambalam thus stands as the ultimate fulfillment.

Therefore, even the external world, visible to the eye, becomes the Thiru-ambalam. Due to the fullness of love, it entirely becomes bliss, and the sattva guna prevails. This is how Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar experiences the divine vision.

Therefore, the meaning is that the three gunas became pure sattva, and as a result, the Thiru-ambalam filled his agitated mind everywhere, and through that, the external vision occurred.

Thus, the vision seen by Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar is a divine vision that cannot be comprehended by the individual consciousness of beings born in various forms, whether they be Devas or others.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar beholds the ambrosial sacred dance of the ankleted feet. That sacred dance removes death, makes birth non-existent, and bestows the bliss of liberation. “Seek the lotus feet that grant liberation” is the scripture. He worships and experiences this divine vision in six ways. That experienced bliss continues to endure. Sekkizhar Peruman continues to sing of this enduring experience of Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar.

Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar’s hands are clasped in anjali above his head. His sacred eyes shed tears like an incessant rain. His inner instruments are also filled with melting love. His blessed body rises even before it falls to the ground.

Thus, the sacred dance of the Lord who dances, the overflowing devotion of Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar as he worships, is immeasurable. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar’s instruments and senses perform their respective functions, that is, the act of worship, without any conscious effort. His sacred body falls to the ground, then rises, and bows. He continues to do this.

Thus, due to his boundless devotion to the Lord, all these expressions of emotion occur in Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar. Sekkizhar Peruman then continues to explain the Thevara Thirumozhis sung by Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar as he beholds the Lord’s sacred dance.

Let us go on contemplating. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part Three Hundred and Fifty-Seven, Thirunindra Charukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We have been observing how Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar witnessed the dance of grace of Koothapiran in the Thillai Podhu. At this juncture, Sekkizhar Peruman mentions that Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar composed three Thirupathigams. We saw how Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar stood worshipping Koothapiran. He worshipped and rose many times.

At that moment, Koothapiran, addressing Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, indicated his divine intention, saying, “When did you come?” Koothapiran thus showed his divine intention to Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar.

Thus, with this divine indication, the Lord who dances in the Thiru-ambalam, through His grace-filled compassion, composed the Thiruviruththa Thirumozhi in a song of true bliss, receiving that grace.

Then, with an abundance of love that grew and overflowed within his mind, he composed the blissful Thirunerisai Thirupathigam. Koothapiran, addressing Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, welcomed him with a smiling face, saying, “When did you come? Welcome!” He showed this indication to Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar. This is the divine facial expression of the Lord as perceived by Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar. It is the welcoming sign that appeared on His face. This is the indication that Koothapiran welcomed the one who came to Him with a smiling face, saying, “When did you come?

“Welcome!” Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar sings of this in Thevaram, saying, “It is the divine indication of my Lord who said, ‘When did you come?’” Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar perceives such an indication on the divine face of Nataraja Peruman.

“Similarly, when Sundaramurthy Swamigal incarnated in this world, and after many days of separation from the Lord, came on the white elephant and reached Thiru-Kailai, the Lord accepted Sundaramurthy Swamigal.

“At that time, the Lord addressed Sundaramurthy Swamigal, saying, “O native, you have come!” We shall see this in the Vellanai Charukkam.

“Thus, the Lord will manifest indications according to the worthiness of those who behold the forms of the deities. If we make ourselves worthy of seeing those indications, they will also become clear to us.

“Thus, to receive the grace of compassion that bestows divine grace, he composed the Thirunerisai Thiruviruththa Thirumozhis in a song of true bliss. Divine grace is Shiva Peruman’s boundless compassion that desires the salvation of all living beings. Compassion refers to the state where that compassion turns towards the faces of living beings. The phrase “to receive the grace of that compassion” appears in this verse. In that state, that is, when Shiva Peruman’s unique compassion turns towards living beings, the extent of the blessing received is evident from “to receive the grace of this compassion.” The state of bliss, the true nature of bliss, is the inner experience filled with truth that arises from that blessing. The state in which Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar stood here is the state of realizing the Lord’s nature, the nature of Sat-Chit-Ananda, by standing as one and serving the Lord.

“Thus, in that state of realizing the Sat-Chit-Ananda nature, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar sings the Thiruviruththam. He sings that Thirupathigam composed in the poetic form of Thirunerisai. Nataraja Peruman gives the indication, “When did you come?” The Nayanar sings of this indication that he perceived in the Thevara Thirupathigam he has now sung. It appears in the second verse of this Thirupathigam.

“Therefore, the Thirupathigam sung by Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar at this time is the Thirupathigam that begins with “Karunatta Kandanae.” This Thirupathigam belongs to the Thillai Sthalam, which is called Koyil. It is compiled as the eighty-first Thirupathigam in the Fourth Thirumurai. Its melody is Thiruviruththam.

“Now, let us contemplate that Thirupathigam briefly.

“First verse: “I praise the Lord with the dark throat, the head of the universe, the wish-fulfilling tree, who could shoot the three strong, fortified cities, who danced the sacred dance with the red fire blazing, the Lord of Thillai, who performed the great dance in Thiruchitrambalam, as the Lord of the Devas.” Its meaning: “I praise as the Lord of the Devas, the one with the dark throat, the Lord of the worlds, who grants the wishes of devotees like a wish-fulfilling tree, who could destroy the three cities, who danced the beautiful dance with the red fire blazing in his palm, the Lord of Thillai city, who performed the great dance in Thiruchitrambalam.” Here, “the sacred dance with the fire blazing” and “danced” appear. This is the Agni Thandavam performed at the end of the cosmic dissolution. “The great dance in Thiruchitrambalam” appears. This is the five-fold dance that the Lord eternally performs.

“Now, the second sacred verse: “Unite and meditate, there is no harm for you. Go and worship the feet of the Lord who kicked the angry Yama for his devotees, who dances in Thiruchitrambalam in Thillai, the Lord who said, ‘When did you come?’” Its meaning: “Shiva Peruman kicked Yama, the angry god of death, with his sacred feet for the sake of his devotee, Markandeya. Such a Shiva Peruman is dancing in Thiruchitrambalam in Thillai city.” He is performing the sacred dance with a raised hand, indicating to us, that is, to the devotee who came to behold Him, “When did you come?” Go and worship Him. Meditate on that dance with a focused mind. Birth and death will no longer come to you,” sings Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar.

“Unite and meditate,” he advises us. This means the unification of all inner and outer instruments. “To be” (iruththal) is the state of remaining unwavering after such unification. “To meditate” (ninaithal) is the state of being absorbed in that experience, the state of meditation, the state of meditating as one.

“Thus, by being in this state, behold that sacred dance. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar sings, “Neither birth nor death will come to you.” Now, the third sacred verse: “O people with stony hearts, what is the use of speaking and showing your fleeting desires? Behold the dance in Thiruchitrambalam in Thillai, where good people reside. My mind has entered and settled firmly, like a silver mountain on a golden mountain, and there is no trace of its departure.” Its meaning: “O worldly people with hearts as hard as stone, your minds constantly generate desires. You ask the Lord to fulfill all those desires and make requests. Behold the dance performed by the Lord in Thiruchitrambalam in Thillai city.

“This alone will bring true benefit to the soul.” Apart from this, there is no benefit in desiring small, fleeting benefits in this earthly life. In Thillai Thiruchitrambalam, Koothapiran grants His vision like a silver mountain on a golden mountain. Such a Koothapiran has firmly settled in my mind, without any trace of His coming or going,” he sings.

“Now, the third sacred verse: “If one can behold the arched eyebrow, the budding smile on the coral-red lips, the matted locks moistened by Ganga, the milk-white sacred ash on the coral-like body, and the lifted golden foot that bestows sweetness, then even this precious human birth is desirable in this great world.” In this sacred verse, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar sings of what we can see in the Lord’s sacred form. These are the eyebrow, the Lord’s smile, the matted locks, the sacred body, the sacred ash, and the foot. He sings of the “arched eyebrow,” meaning the Lord’s curved eyebrows. He sings of the Lord’s curved eyebrows, the budding smile on His coral-like red lips, His matted locks moistened by the Ganga, the milk-white sacred ash smeared on His coral-like red body, and His lifted sacred feet that bestow supreme bliss. If a soul can attain the opportunity to behold these, if we can attain it in this birth, then for that very reason, one can take human birth in this world. Even this birth, which is not desired by the wise, becomes very special; we can desire and obtain it.

“For what? To behold the Lord’s divine form and His sacred dance.

“Now, the fifth sacred verse. Vāyttatu nam tamakku ītor piṟavi matittiṭumīṉ pārttaṟku pācupatam aruḷ ceytavaṉ pattaruḷḷīr kōttaṉṟu muppuṟam tī vaḷaittāṉ tillai ampalattu kūttaṉukku āṭpaṭṭu iruppatu aṉṟō nam tam kūḷaimaiyē. This human birth, which has been granted to us, is indeed a precious gift. Reflect upon it, for it is our servitude to the Dancer of Thillai’s Amphitheatre, He who granted the Pasupata to Arjuna, and who once encircled the three cities with fire. In the previous verse, even human birth, which was scorned by the wise, was desired for the sake of witnessing the sacred dance of the Lord in Thillai’s Thiruchitrambalam.

“Following that, the poet sings here, “Vāyttatu nam tamakku ītor piṟavi” (This human birth has been granted to us). O devotees of Lord Shiva, through our good karma, this incomparable human birth has been bestowed upon us. Value this human birth and act accordingly.

“Lord Shiva is the one who bestowed the Pasupatastra upon Arjuna. He is the one who created the three cities and consumed them with fire. He is the one who performs the dance in Thillai’s Amphitheatre. To be a servant to such a Lord is our servitude.

“Now, the sixth sacred verse: Pūttaṉa poṟcaṭai poṉpōl miḷirap puri kaṇaṅkaḷ ārttaṉa koṭṭi arittaṉa pal kural pūta kaṇam tēttaṉa veṇṭicai vaṇṭukaḷ pāṭu ciṟṟampalattu kūttaṉil kūttu vallār aruḷarō eṉ taṉ kōlvaḷaikkē. This verse is a sacred poem expressed by a mother with great joy. A mother says, “Are there others who can captivate my daughter’s heart with their dance? Only the Lord of Thillai’s Thiruchitrambalam can captivate my daughter’s heart with His dance.” This poem is set in the Akam genre, where a mother joyfully declares that only the Lord can captivate her daughter’s heart with His dance. His red matted locks possess a blossoming radiance, for the Lord wears the Konrai flower in them, shining like gold.

“The throngs of devotees rejoice with shouts of joy. The hosts of Bhoothas play musical instruments, and the bees hum.

“Thus, Lord Shiva, who performs the dance in Thiruchitrambalam in the city of Thillai, is the only one who can captivate her daughter’s heart with His dance, sings the mother.

“Now, the seventh sacred verse: Muṭikoṇṭa mattamum mukkaṇṇiṉ nōkkum muruvalippum tuṭikoṇṭa kaiyum tutainta viṇṇīrum curikuḻalāl paṭikoṇṭa pākamum pāypuli tōlum eṉ pāvi neñcil kūṭa Kuṭikoṇṭavā tillai ampala kūttaṉ kuṟaikkaḻalē. In this verse, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar describes the divine form of the Lord residing in his heart. He enumerates the Lord’s anklets, the Mattam flower worn by the Lord, the Lord’s divine gaze, the Lord’s gentle smile, the Lord’s sacred hands, the sacred ash worn by the Lord, Uma Devi who is part of the Lord’s form, and the tiger skin worn by the Lord. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar reveals to us the wonder of the Lord’s divine form enshrined in his heart through this verse. In this verse, the Lord who performs the dance in Thiruchitrambalam in the city of Thillai, with His ringing anklets, the Umathai flower adorning His head, the gaze of His three sacred eyes, His gentle smile, His sacred hands that play the Udukkai, and the sacred ash smeared all over His body, His right side, which holds Parvati as His left, and the tiger skin that covers His waist, have permanently taken residence in my sinful heart. These worldly objects, which have only brought me evil, have now been replaced by the Lord in this sinful heart of mine, where He has permanently taken residence, sings the Nayanar.

“Now, the eighth sacred verse: Paṭaikkalamāka uṉ nāmattu eḻuttu añcu eṉ nāvil koṇṭēṉ iṭaikkalamallēṉ eḻupiṟappum uṉakku āṭcaiceykiṉṟēṉ tuṭaikkiṉum pōkēṉ toḻutu vaṇaṅki tū nīru aṇintu uṉ aṭaikkalam kaṇṭāy aṇi tillaic ciṟṟampalattu araṇēṉ. O Lord of the beautiful Thiruchitrambalam! I hold the sacred five letters of Your name on my tongue as a weapon to protect me from the evils that the poor may inflict. I have never ceased my service to You, and I continue to serve You. In all seven types of births, I serve You according to the birth I take. Even if You cast me away, I will not leave You.

“I will always worship You with my mind, bow to You with my body, wear sacred ash, and remain as one who needs to be protected by You, sings the Nayanar.

“Now, the ninth sacred verse: Poṉṉotta mēṉimēl veṇṇīru aṇintu puri caṭaikaḷ miṉṉottu ilaṅka pali tērntu uḻalum viṭaṅkavēṭac ciṉṉattiṉāṉ mali tillaiyuḷ ciṟṟampalattu naṭṭam eṉ attaṉ āṭal kaṇṭu iṉpuṟṟatāl ivviru nilamē. Its meaning: The Lord, whose body is like gold, wears white sacred ash, and whose twisted red matted locks shine like lightning, wanders seeking alms. He is naturally adorned with the sacred marks of Shiva. This world rejoices upon witnessing the sacred dance of my Lord, who resides in the abundant Thillai city’s Thiruchitrambalam.

“Now, the tenth sacred verse: Cāṭa eṭuttatu takkaṉ taṉ vēḷviyil cantiraṉai vīṭa eṭuttatu kālaṉai nāraṇaṉ nāṉmukaṉum tēṭa eṭuttatu tillaiyuḷ ciṟṟampalattu naṭṭam āṭa eṭutta pātaṉṟō nammai āṭkoṇṭatē. Its meaning: The Lord’s sacred feet were raised to crush the moon, who participated in Daksha’s sacrifice to receive his share of the oblation. The Lord’s sacred feet were raised to destroy Yama. The Lord’s sacred feet grew downwards into the netherworld, making it impossible for Vishnu and Brahma to find them. Such sacred feet of the Lord were raised to dance in Thillai’s Thiruchitrambalam. Was it not such a left foot of Lord Shiva that enslaved us? sings the Nayanar.

“This is the first Thiru-Pathikam, beginning with “Karunatta Kandanai,” which Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar sang before the Dancing Lord in Thillai.

“Now, let us continue to contemplate the second and third Thiru-Pathikams.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 358. Thiru-Nindra Charukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We saw that Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar sang three Thiru-Pathikams before the Dancing Lord in Thillai. We contemplated the first Thiru-Pathikam.

Now, the second Thiru-Pathikam.

The Lord of the Kulams sings, beginning with “Paththanai Paadamaatten” (I will not sing as a devotee) and ending with “Aththa un aadal kaanbaan adiyen vanthavaaru” (O Lord, Your dance, to see it, Your servant has come). It is said that Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, with a desire to perform manual service, bowed down after singing this sweet Tamil garland of verses. The phrase “Thiru-Nerisai-kku-uriya antha pan poruntha” (suitable for the Thiru-Nerisai melody) indicates that the melody should be taken as Kolli-pen. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar sings this Thiru-Pathikam with an abundance of love. Having sung thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar’s mind was not at peace, and a desire to perform manual service arose in him. Previously, his mind and speech had served.

Now, it is the Saivite tradition to believe that this body too should serve and benefit. In the rules of Shiva Puja, after completing the inner worship (Aga Puja), when entering into the outer worship (Pura Puja), one thinks, “O Lord, until now I have performed inner worship. Through it, my inner faculties have been purified, and my mind is at peace.

“Now, I enter into outer worship so that my outer instruments may be purified and become useful.” This is the Saivite tradition. Accordingly, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, who had served until now with his mind and speech, now begins to perform manual service, specifically the Uzhavara service. The verses he sang now is the Pathikam that begins with “Paththanai Paadamaatten” (I will not sing as a devotee). The meaning of this Thiru-Pathikam is: “I will not sing as a devotee, but still, O my Lord, what is the way I have come to see Your sacred dance? Purify my mind and make me remember You, and grant me the grace to serve You.” This Thiru-Pathikam is compiled as the twenty-third Thiru-Pathikam in the fourth Thiru-Murai, as a temple Thiru-Pathikam.

“Now, that Thiru-Pathikam, Thiruchitrambalam, verse number one: Paththanai Paadamaatten Paramane Paramayogi Eththinaal Bhakthi seykēn eṉṉai nī igaḻa vēṇṭā Mutthane muthalvā tillai ampalattu āṭukiṉṟa Aththā uṉ āṭal kāṇpāṉ aṭiyeṉ vaṉtavārē. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar sings, “I will not sing to You with devotion, with the fullness of love, yet I have come to see Your sacred dance. What is my ignorance? What qualification do I have to see Your sacred dance?” He sings with melting devotion. “O Shiva, You who are free from beginningless karma, You who are the foremost of all, O Lord who dances in Thillai’s Amphitheatre, O exalted one, O supreme Yogi! I am incapable of singing as a devotee.

“Therefore, with what shall I perform devotion? Do not scorn me. Your servant has come to Thillai to see Your dance.” Now, the second sacred verse: Karutthanāyp pāṭamāṭṭēṉ kāmpaṉa tōḻi paṅkā Oruttharāl aṟiyavoṉṉā tiru uru uṭaiya jōti Thirutthamaam tillai taṉṉuḷ tikaḻnta ciṟṟampalattē Niruttham nāṉ kāṇa vēṇṭi nērpaṭa vaṉtavārē. O Lord, whose consort has bamboo-like shoulders, O Lord, whose consort has bamboo-like shoulders, O beautiful luminous form, unknowable by anyone! I, your servant, who cannot sing with a focused mind, having enshrined You in my heart, have come to witness Your sacred dance in the pure Thiruchitrambalam, which shines in Thillai. Verse number three: Kēṭṭilēṉ kiḷai periyēṉ kēṭkumā kēṭṭiyākil Nāṭṭiṉēṉ niṉṟaṉ pātam naṭupaṭa neñciṉ uḷḷē Māṭṭiṉīr vāḻaippāyum malku tirucciṟṟampalattai Kūṭṭamāṅkuvi mulaiyāl kūṭa nī āṭumāṟē.

“Its meaning: “I have not truly heard of Your greatness before. If You would allow me to hear it, without separating from Your assembly of devotees, then I will firmly establish Your sacred feet in the center of my heart,” he sings. I have not truly heard of Your greatness before. If You would allow me to hear it, without separating from Your assembly of devotees, then I will firmly establish Your sacred feet in the center of my heart,” he sings. He sings, “In Thiruchitrambalam, rich with water bodies where plantain fish leap, through the grace of Your sacred dance with Parvati, whose breasts are gathered, I will firmly establish Your sacred feet in the center of my heart.” Verse number four: Cintaiyai tigaippiyātē ceṟivuṭai aṭimai ceyya Entai nī aruḷic ceyyāy yātu nāṉ ceyvatheṉṉē Centiyār vēḷvivōvā tillai ciṟṟampalattē Antiyum pakalum āṭa aṭiyiṉai alacum kollō. In Thillai, the sacred city where the sacrificial rituals of the Brahmins who tend the red fire never cease, You perform Your dance day and night in Thiruchitrambalam.

“Will Your sacred feet not tire from this? You have not yet granted me the grace to free my heart from worldly attachments and approach You to perform Your service. What shall I do now? He sings, “You have not yet granted me the grace to free my heart from worldly attachments and approach You to perform Your service. What shall I do now?” Verse number five: Kaṇṭavā tirintu nāḷum karuttiṉāl niṉṟaṉ pātam Koṇṭiruntu āṭi pāṭi kūṭuvaṉ kuṟippiṉālē Vaṇṭu paṇpāṭum cōlai mala ciṟṟampalattē Eṉ ticaiyōrum ētta iṟaivaṉī āṭumāṟē. “As I have experienced, I will wander daily, contrary to worldly ways, with Your sacred feet firmly in my heart, dancing and singing, and by Your divine grace, I will come to witness Your dance in Thillai’s Thiruchitrambalam, where bees hum in the groves, and where You, as the Lord, dance to be praised by all eight directions.” Verse number six: Pārttiruntu aṭiyēṉ nāṉ paravuvaṉ pāṭi āṭi Mūrttiyē eṉpaṉ uṉṉai mūvaril mutalvaṉ eṉpaṉ Ēttuvār iṭarkaḷ tīrppāy tillai ciṟṟampalattu Kūttā uṉ kūttuk kāṇpāṉ kūṭa nāṉ vaṉtavārē.

“O Dancer of Thillai’s Thiruchitrambalam, You who remove the sufferings of those who praise You! I, Your servant, will watch Your dance and praise You, dancing and singing, calling You the Supreme Being, the foremost of the three. I have come with Your devotees to witness Your dance.

“Now, verse number seven: Poyyiṉai tavaṟaviṭṭu puṟamalā aṭimai ceyya Ayyaṉi aruḷic ceyyāy ādiyē ātimūrtti Vaiyakam taṉṉil mikka malku ciṟṟampalattē Paiyaṉi āṭal kāṇpāṉ paramaṉāṉ vaṉtavārē. O my Lord, grant me the grace to abandon attachment to perishable things and perform true service. O Primeval Being, O Primal Form! I have come to this world, to the abundant Thiruchitrambalam, to slowly witness Your dance. O my Lord, grant me the grace to abandon attachment to perishable things and perform true service. O Primeval Being, O Primal Form!

“I have come to this world, to the abundant Thiruchitrambalam, to slowly witness Your dance. Verse number eight: Maṉattiṉār tigaitthu nāḷum māṇpalā neṟikaḷ mēlē Kaṉaipparāl eṉ ceykēṉō karaiyaṇi kaṇṭattāṉē Tiṉaittaṉai vētam kuṉṟā tillai ciṟṟampalattē Aṉaittu niṉ nilaiyam kāṇpāṉ aṭiyeṉ vaṉtavārē. O Lord with the blue throat adorned with poison! My mind, bewildered, wanders daily on paths that bring no glory but only insignificance. What shall I do? I have come to Thillai’s Thiruchitrambalam, where the Vedas never diminish even by a tiny measure, to behold Your abode, Your servant.

“I will come. Verse number nine: Neñciṉai tūymai ceytu niṉaikkumā niṉaippiyātē Vañcamē ceytiyālō vāṉavar talaiyavaṉē nī Mañcaṭai cōlai tillai malku ciṟṟampalattē Añcolāḷ kāṇaṉiṉṟu aḻaga nī āṭumāṟē. O Lord of the Devas! You deceive me by not purifying my heart and making me always remember You. In Thillai’s Thiruchitrambalam, with its groves where clouds gather, You dance beautifully for Parvati, who speaks sweet words, to behold. What a wonder!

“Verse number ten: Maṇṇuṇṭa mālavaṉum malarmicai maṇṇiṉāṉum Viṇṇuṇṭa tiru uruvam virumpiṉār kāṇamāṭṭār Tiṉṉuṇṭa tiruvē mikka tillai ciṟṟampalattē Paṇṇuṇṭa pāṭalōṭum paramaṇi āṭumāṟē. Even Vishnu, who swallowed the earth, and Brahma, who resides on the lotus, desired to see Your luminous form that pervades the sky, but they could not. Yet, in the supremely sacred Thillai Thiruchitrambalam, You, the Supreme Being, openly dance amidst songs set to melody. Who can comprehend its greatness? sings the Nayanar.

“These are the ten sacred verses of the Thiru-Pathikam that begins with “Paththanai Paadamaatten” and their meanings.

“We will continue to contemplate them.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 359. Thiru-Nindra Charukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We have contemplated the two Thiru-Pathikams sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar in Thillai Thiruchitrambalam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar performs Uzhavara service in the sacred streets of Thillai.

He performs sacred service in the temple courtyards of the Lord of the Amphitheatre. He performs Uzhavara sacred service. He performs Uzhavara service in the sacred streets of Thillai, which are praised as streets adorned with high flags, streets where the Lord’s chariot runs, and beautiful streets. He performs sacred service, bows down, and sings. With abundant divine joy, he sings the Thiru-Kurunthogai beginning with “Annam Palikkum” and performs the Thiru-Uzhavaram with great love. Perunthiruthondu ceythu viruppuṟu mēṉi kaṇṇīr veṇṇīṟṟu vaṇṭalāṭa eṉṟu cēkkuḷar perumāṉ itaṉai pāṭukiṉṟār.

Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar sings this, saying, “With abundant divine joy, he performs great sacred service, and tears flow from his beloved body, mixing with the sacred white ash to form a muddy paste.” Here it is mentioned that Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar sings the Thiru-Kurunthogai beginning with “Annam Palikkum” with abundant divine joy. The great joy arising from receiving the Lord’s grace overflows, and with that rising love, he performs great sacred service. Tears flow from his beloved body, and these tears, mixing with the sacred white ash worn by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, form a muddy paste, and that appearance, that sacred form, shines. The Thiru-Pathikam beginning with “Annam Palikkum,” which was just sung, is a Thiru-Pathikam recited daily by Saivite devotees. The food offered by the Lord in Thillai Thiruchitrambalam is not like other food; it is food that bestows the Lord’s grace, removes the impurities of living beings, and brings about Shiva’s bliss.

Thus, he sings the Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam beginning with “Annam Palikkum.” Kurunthogai is a type of Tamil poetic meter. Like Thandagam and Thiru-Viruttham, Thiru-Kurunthogai is also a type of poetic meter. If each verse within a Pathikam is a Kurunthogai verse, it is called a Thiru-Kurunthogai Pathikam. Of the Kurunthogai Pathikams sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar for Thillai, we have Only two Thiru-Pathikams are available. The first one sung is this Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam beginning with “Annam Palikkum.” Here it is mentioned that he performs the Thiru-Uzhavara service while singing this Thiru-Pathikam. We can understand from this that the joy of immersing oneself in singing the Thiru-Pathikam, and the great love for this sacred service, arose in the Nayanar, and Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar considered it a great service.

Now, let us contemplate the Thiru-Pathikam beginning with “Annam Palikkum Thillai Thiruchitrambalam” and its verses and meanings. This Pathikam is a Pathikam sung in the joy of receiving the Lord’s grace. Thillai Thiruchitrambalam bestows food, gold, and everything else. What else is needed in this birth?

Therefore, reach Thillai Thiruchitrambalam and be saved. What can sorrow, ignorance, or ancient karma do to me, who has attained this and embraced servitude? Yama, the god of death, will not approach the devotees who draw near Thillai. The feet of Ambalavanar reside within my heart; even Brahma knows this. Can one find Him by searching and reforming? This hymn’s note states, “Thillai Thiruchitrambalam, which bestows food.” As a result of the Nayanar’s true sacred utterance, even today, all who approach the sacred presence of Thillai Koothan receive food, and the tradition of offering rice flourishes.

We can still witness this in Thillai.

Furthermore, the daily six-time worship of Thiru Ambalamudaiyar includes Annabhishekam (rice anointing) and many Thiruppavadai offerings, which are unique glories of this sacred place. The temple there ...is also one of the Annamaya Koshas, and we can interpret the philosophical principle as being indicated here. With such special significance, this sacred hymn, “Annam Palikkum Thillai Thiruchitrambalam,” is customarily recited during Maheswara Puja when chanting Thevaram among Shaivite devotees. Sivakavimani writes that this entire hymn is worthy of memorization and recitation. This sacred hymn, beginning with “Annam Palikkum,” is compiled as the first hymn in the Fifth Thirumurai, a Thirukkurunthogai Thiruppathigam.

Now, that sacred hymn: Thiruchitrambalam. “Annam palikkum Thillai Thiruchitrambalam, Ponnam palikkum melum ippoomisai, Ennam palikkum aaru kandu inburra, Innam palikkumo ippiraviyee.” “Palikkum” means “will bestow.” Thillai Thiruchitrambalam ...bestows the abode of supreme bliss and the life of the golden world. The Nayanar sings, “Will my Primal Lord grant me this good human birth again, so that I may behold such a Thiruchitrambalam, where my love on this earth may grow, and I may easily attain the state of supreme liberation and bliss?” The phrase “Annam Palikkum Thillai Thiruchitrambalam” appears, and the word “annam” here refers to the bliss of liberation. “Soru” (rice) is a term that signifies liberation. “Pathagame soru pattinava thonokkam” is from Thiruvachagam. In this Thiruvachagam, “soru” is used in the sense of supreme bliss by Manickavasagar Swamigal.

It is our tradition to refer to God as “annam” (food) and “amudham” (nectar). Even today, there are Pavadai offerings in Thillai. In earlier days, this might have occurred on a much grander scale.

Therefore, the Nayanar sings, “Annam Palikkum Thillai Thiruchitrambalam.” Thus, “Annam Palikkum Thillai Thiruchitrambalam” means “Thillai Thiruchitrambalam, which bestows liberation, the abode of supreme bliss.” Now, the second verse: “Arumbattappada aay malar kondu neer, Surumbattappada thoovi thozhumino, Karumbattach silai kaamanai kaaindhavan, Perumbattap puliyoor emperaanaiyee.” When gathering flowers for the worship of the Lord, the rule is to remove the buds and pluck only the blossoms.

In this manner, one should offer those carefully selected flowers, after removing the buds, at the Lord’s sacred feet and perform sacred worship. He sings, “Worship Perumbattap Puliyoor Emperuman, who burned Manmatha, the god of love, who wielded a sugarcane bow.” Thus, you ...should worship, he sings. Verse number three: “Arichutra vinaiyaal adar pundu neer, Erichutraku idandhaar endru ayalavar, Sirichutra pala pesappadamunam, Thiruchitrambalam sendradaindhu uyminee.” He sings, “Before others laugh and speak many things, saying that you are afflicted by troublesome karma and lie surrounded by fire in the cremation ground, you should all go and attain Thiruchitrambalam and find salvation.” Now, the fourth verse: “Allal en seyyum aruvinai en seyyum, Thollai valvinai thondhanthaan en seyyum, Thillai maanagar chithrambalavanaarkku, Ellaiyillathathor adimai poondenukke.” The meaning of this is: What can sorrow, which is the result of future actions (agamiyam), do? What can the difficult karma (prarabdha vinai) that can only be resolved through experience do? What can the ancient, powerful karma (sanchita vinai), referred to as “thollai valvinai thondham,” do? These sorrows, spoken of as pairs like good deeds and bad deeds, dharma and adharma, pleasure and pain—what can these dualistic sufferings, which are called “dvandvam” in Sanskrit, do to us?

To us, who have embraced boundless servitude to Thiruchitrambalavanar, who performs the sacred dance in the great city of Thillai, these karmas will cause no suffering. So he sings.

Now, verse number five: “Oonil aavi uyirkkum pozhudhellaam, Naanilaavi iruppan en naadhanai.” “Thenilaaviya Chithrambalavanar, Vaanilaavi irukkavum vaippare.” The meaning of this is: As long as life breathes within the body, I will worship Thiruchitrambalavanar, who is my Lord. That Thiruchitrambalavanar, who is filled with the honey of bliss, will keep me established in the abode of supreme bliss. Verse number six: “Chittrar vaanavar sendru varam kollum, Sirar vaazh Thillai Chithrambalaththurai, Siran sevadi kaithozha sellum, Achchirpaal anugaan serukaalane.” The meaning of this is: Thillai Thiruchitrambalam is a place of distinction where sages and gods go to receive boons. It is a dwelling place for distinguished Brahmins. Yama, the god of death, will not approach those true sages, those distinguished ones, who go to worship with folded hands the sacred feet of the Gnanamurthy (Lord Shiva) who performs the sacred dance in that Thillai Thiruchitrambalam, just as he would approach others.

Yama, the god of death, will not approach them.

Now, verse number seven: “Oruthanar ulagangatku oru sudar, Thiruththanar Thillai Chithrambalavanar, Viruththanar ilaiyaar vidam unda em, Aruththanar adiyaarai arivare.” The meaning of this is: The unique primal being, the one light for all worlds, is Lord Shiva. He is the perfect one who performs the sacred dance in Thiruchitrambalam. He is ancient, yet youthful. He is our wealthy Lord who consumed poison. He knows His devotees well.

Now, verse number eight: “Vinniraindhadhor vevvazhalin oru, Enniraindha iruvarkku arivonaa, Kanniraindha kadi pozhil Ambalaththu, Ul niraindhu nindru aadum oruvane.” The meaning of this is: The one who stands and dances, filling the sacred Ambalam, surrounded by beautiful, fragrant groves, is the unique one, the primal Lord, who was an immeasurable pillar of fire, incomprehensible to the two who were filled with pride, Brahma and Vishnu, who searched ...He was an immeasurable pillar of fire, incomprehensible to the two who were filled with pride, Brahma and Vishnu. He is the peerless great Lord, who stands and performs the Panchakritya dance, filling the Thiruchitrambalam in Thillai, surrounded by fragrant, delightful groves. That primal Lord, unknown to Brahma and Vishnu, revealed Himself to the sages Vyagrapada and Patanjali, who worshipped Him with love, made His nature known, and bestowed supreme bliss.

Now, verse number nine: “Villai vattappada vaangi avunartham, Vallai vatta ammadhil moondrudan maayththavan, Thillai vatta thisai kaithozhuvaar vinai, Ollai vattam kadandhoduthal unmaiyee.” Lord Shiva, who bent Mount Meru as His bow and destroyed the three fortresses of the Asuras of the three cities, is the one. Those who fold their hands and worship the direction of Thillai, where He is enshrined ...all their accumulated karmas will flee from them. This is the truth.
