O one who smears sacred ash on his body, who holds a shining axe, O Lord of Kodikka!” “Eru ugandhu erinane irungadal amudhu oppane Arumor nangu vedam aram uraitthu arulinane Koorumor penninane Kodikkavudaiya Kove Kalanai kalal settru andru arul puri karunaiyane Neelamarkandathane neenmudiyamarakove Gnalamam perumaiyane nalir ilam thingal soodum Kolamar sadaiyinane Kodikkavudaiya Kove Poon aravu arathone puli uri araiyinane Kaanil ven kopanamum kaiyil or kapalam yendhi Oonumoor pichaiyane umaiyor bhagathane Konal venpiraiyinane Kodikkavudaiya Kove Kezhal venkompu poonda kilaruli marbinane Ezhaiyen ezhaiyen nan en seigeyan endhai pemman Mazhaiyon kanninargal valaithanil mayangugindren Koozhaiyerudaiya selva” Gloss: “O one who delights in riding the bull, who is like the nectar from the great ocean, who graciously taught the six and four Vedas, who has a woman as part of himself, O Lord of Kodikka!

“O compassionate one who once crushed Yama with his foot and bestowed grace, O blue-throated one, king of the long-crowned celestials, O glorious one of the world, who wears the cool young moon in his beautiful matted hair, O Lord of Kodikka! O one adorned with a snake, who wears a tiger skin around his waist, who, when seen, wears a white loincloth and holds a skull in his hand, who begs for food, who has Uma as a part of himself, who wears the crescent moon, O Lord of Kodikka! O one with a shining chest adorned with the white tusk of a boar, I am a poor wretch, what shall I do, my Lord? I am entangled in the net of women with dark eyes, O wealthy one with a bull!” Gloss: “Kodikkavudaiya Kove Azhal umizh angaiyane arivaiyor bhagathane Thazhal umizh aravam aarthu thalai thanil palikolvone Nizhal umizh solai soozha neelvari vandinangal Kuzhal umizh geetham padum Kodikkavudaiya Kove Evadu silaiyinale puram avai eriseythane Mavadu vagirkol kannal malaimagal bhagathane Avadu thuraiyulane aivaral attappatten Kovadu kutram theerai Kodikkavudaiya Kove Yetra neer gangaiyane irunilam thavinanum Natramamalar mel yerum nanmugan ivargal koodi Atralal alakkalutrarkku azhaluru ayinane Kootrukkum kootrathanaai Kodikkavudaiya Kove Pazhagan an adimai seiven pasupathi pavanaasa Mazhaga” Gloss: “O Lord of Kodikka, whose hand emits fire, who has wisdom as a part of himself, who wears a fiery serpent and receives alms on his head, O Lord of Kodikka, where long-striped bees sing flute-like melodies amidst the shade-giving groves!

“O one who burned the cities with a bow and arrow, who has the mountain maiden with mango-slice-like eyes as a part of himself, O resident of Avaduthurai, I am tormented by the five senses, remove my sins, O Lord of Kodikka! O one who bears the Ganga water, when Vishnu who measured the vast earth, and Brahma who rides on the fragrant lotus, came together and tried to measure your power, you became a fiery form, O Lord of Kodikka, who is death to death itself! I, the ancient one, will serve you, O Pasupathi, purifier of sins, O beautiful one!” “Azhali yanaiyin thol malaimagal veruva portha azhagane Arakkan thin thol aruvarai neriy oorndrum kuzhagane Kolamarpa Kodikkavudaiya Kove Thiruchitrambalam.” The next Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal for this sthalam is the Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathigam, compiled as the seventy-eighth Thiru-Pathigam in the fifth Thirumurai.

“Now, that Thiru-Pathigam.

““Sangula mun kai thaiyalor bhagathin vengula madha velam vegundavan Kongulam pozhil Kodikkavaana engilathathor inbam vandhu eydhume Vadi vazhvadhennavathu madharpal Odi vazhvinai ulkinir nalthorum Kodikkavanai koorirel koorinen Padi kavalil pattu kazhudire Mullai nanmuruvallamai panganar Thillai” Gloss: “O Lord, who is part of the maiden with conch-like forearms, who was enraged by the fierce elephant, O Lord of Kodikka, surrounded by fragrant groves, an incomparable joy will come! What is the use of living in sorrow? You who daily seek life by running after women, if you do not speak of the Lord of Kodikka, I tell you, you will perish in the prison of singing! The Lord, who is part of the beautiful smiling Mullai, the wealthy one who resides in Thillai’s temple, who rides the bull, if you say ‘Kodikkava!’ there, no harm will come to those who praise him quickly!” “Ambalathil urai selvanar Kollai yetrinar Kodikkavaana endru angu ollai yetthuvarkku oonam ondriyillaiye Navalm perumaru manan nannuthal Amalan solli anbu seiyinallal Komalan sadai Kodikkavavena Evazhindranai yesum avvelaiye Viruthan peruvaar silar agilum Naru poongonrai than miga nalkanel Kooruven Kodikkavulayi endrumal Yeruvain nummal yesappaduvano Nadi naranan nanmugan vanavar Thedi yesaravum theriyathathor Kodikkavanai kooratha nalellam Padikkavalil pattu kazhiyume.” In this Thiru-Pathigam, the seventh, eighth, and ninth verses are not available to us.

“Now, the tenth verse: “Varangalal varai eduthan thanai” Gloss: “The wealthy one who resides in the temple, who rides the bull, if you say ‘Kodikkava!’ there, no harm will come to those who praise him quickly! If you do not approach the Lord with a beautiful mind and speak of him with love, saying ‘Kodikkava!’ to the Lord with beautiful matted hair, then at that very moment, you will be reviled! Even if some attain greatness, if he does not bestow the fragrant Konrai, I will say, ‘O Lord of Kodikka!’ and will I be reviled by you forever? Narayanan and Brahma, the celestials, searched and could not know him, all the days I do not speak of the Lord of Kodikka, I will spend in the prison of singing.” “Aranga oondri arul seytha appanur Kurangu ser pozhil Kodikkavaavena Iranguven manathu ethangal theerave Thiruchitrambalam.” Now, the third Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal for this sthalam is the eighty-first Thiru-Pathigam in the sixth Thirumurai, a Thiru-Thandaga Thiru-Pathigam.

““Kandalanjer netriyilam kalai kandai Kanmadhil soozh kandama thanathan kandai Mandalanjer mayakkarukkum marundhu kandai Madhirkachi ekamba meyan kandai Vindalanjer vilakkozhiyay nindran kandai Miyachoor piriyatha vikirthan kandai Kondalanjer kandathu enguththan kandai Kodikka amarndhuraiyum kuzhagan thane Vandadu poonguzhalal bhagan kandai Maraikattu uraiyum manalan kandai Pandadu” Gloss: “O Lord, you are the young bull with a forehead adorned with Kandal flowers, you are the Lord of Kandamathanan surrounded by strong walls, you are the medicine that removes worldly delusions, you are the one who resides in Kachi Ekambam, you are the light that shines in the sky, you are the unique one who never leaves Miyachoor, you are our Koothan with a cloud-like throat, you are the beautiful one who resides in Kodikka! You are the one with the maiden with bee-humming flower-adorned hair as a part, you are the groom who resides in Maraikadu, you are the one who cures ancient karmic diseases, you are the supreme one who shows the path to the higher world, you are the one who destroyed the cities of the Asuras with a ball, you are the one who resides in Thiruvarur Thirumoolathanam, you are the one who dwells in the hearts of worshipping devotees, you are the beautiful one who resides in Kodikka! You are the one with the Ganga water in his matted hair, you are the sweet nectar for devotees, you are the one with the mountain maiden as a part, you are the one who stands as the crown jewel for the celestials, you are the one with the leaf-adorned trident weapon, you are our Father who stands as the seven worlds, you are the one who wore the skin of the murderous elephant, you are the beautiful one who resides in Kodikka! You are the one who has no equal, you are the one who delights in Mayiladuthurai as his abode, you are the pure one who adorns himself with snakes from the anthill, you are the one who stands as the truthful one in Poonthuruthi, you are the one who is for those who have nothing, Gloss: “You are the one who is for those who have nothing, you are the Lord who never leaves Aiyaru, you are the Koothan who resides in Kutralam, you are the beautiful one who resides in Kodikka!

“You are the one with the maiden with a breast-band as a part, you are the one who delights in wearing the snake on his chest, you are the one who rides the great bull of battle, you are the pure one who never leaves Pugazhur, you are the one with the flowing matted hair, you are the one who lightens the burden of karma for those who meditate on him, you are the one with the three-pronged spear weapon, you are the beautiful one who resides in Kodikka! You are the one with matted hair adorned with fragrant Konrai flowers, you are the one who granted Kannappa’s request, you are the one who cuts off countless births, you are the one who is the support for those who have no attachments, you are the one whose anklets jingle as he dances, you are the Lord worshipped by the hosts of celestials, you are the one with the banner-adorned walls of Thillai!” Kootthan Kandaay Kodikkaa Amarndhuraiyum Kuzhaganthaane Uliyaadu Karathalam Ondru Udaiyaan Kandaay Ottriyur Ottriya Udaiyaan Kandaay Kalaiyaadu Kazhukkundram Amarndhaan Kandaay Kaalaththik Karpagamaay Nindraan Kandaay Izhaiaadum En Puyaththa Iraivan Kandaay En Nenjaththul Neengaay Emmaan Kandaay Kuzhaiaada Nadamaadum Kootthan Kandaay Kodikkaa Amarndhuraiyum Kuzhaganthaane Padamaadu Pannakku Asaiththaan Kandaay Paraiththuraiyum Paasurum Meyaan Kandaay Nadamaadi Ezhulagum Thiruvaan Kandaay Naan Maraiyin Porul Kandaay Naathan Kandaay Kadamaadu Kaliru Uriththa Kandan Kandaay Kayilaayam Meviyirundhaan Kandaay Kudamaadi Idamagaak Kondaan Kandaay Kodikkaa Amarndhuraiyum Kuzhaganthaane. The ninth and tenth verses of this Thiru-pathigam are not available to us.

“These three Thiru-pathigams are the sacred hymns bestowed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal upon the Thiru-sthalam of Thiru-Kodikka.

“We shall continue to contemplate them.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 381. Thiru-Nindra Sarukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Sekkizhar Peruman sings that Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, after worshipping Thiru-Kodikka, proceeded to Aavaduthurai. The Thiru-sthalam referred to by Sekkizhar Peruman as Aavaduthurai here is the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Aavaduthurai. It is the thirty-sixth sthalam on the south bank of the Kaveri.

As mentioned by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal in the Thiru-pathigam he bestowed upon this sthalam, Sekkizhar Peruman also refers to Aavaduthurai in this verse. The coolness of Aavaduthurai, the nature of its presence, is the coolness of the water enriched by the Kaveri. Not only that, but it also signifies the coolness of the shade of the sacred feet that alleviates the heat of birth for the souls who arrive here. It also signifies the coolness of the shade of the sacred feet that alleviates the heat of birth for the souls who arrive here. If Aavaduthurai is split as ‘Aa Adu Thurai’, ‘Aa’ means cow-nature, and ‘Adu’ means to remove.

Therefore, there is also a reference here to a sacred sthalam that removes the cow-nature of living beings. This is the sthalam where Ambikai, having come in the form of a cow, regained her true form after her cow-form was removed. There are two Sthala Vinayagars in this sthalam. The first is Thunaivandha Vinayagar, who accompanied Ambikai when she came in the form of a cow. He is enshrined south of the temple gopuram entrance. The second is Azhagiya Vinayagar, who imparted the Panchakshara Upadesam to Agasthya Muni.

He is located east of Dakshinamurthy. The sacred names of the Lord in this sthalam are Sri Swayam Vyakteswarar, Prakashamani Nadhar, Masilamani Eesar, Gomuktheesar, Gokkali Nadhar, Anaiththezhundha Nayagar, Pookailaseswarar, Putthira Thiyagar, Bodhivana Nadhar, Bodhi Ambalavanar, Mahathandaveswarar, Arthathiyagar, Mukthi Thiyagar, Sivaloka Nayagar. The sacred names of the Goddess are Athulyakujanayaki, Oppila Mulaiyammai. This sthalam has various sacred names: Thiru-Aavaduthurai, Gomukthi, Gokkali, Pookailasam, Nandinagar, Thiyagapuram, Bodhivanam, Arasavanam, Mahathandavapuram, Vedapuram, Sithapuram, Navakodisithapuram, Mukthikshethram, Sivapuram. There are three sacred tanks: Mukthi Theertham or Gomukthi Theertham, which is in front of the Thiru-Koyil. The second is Kaivalya Theertham, which is in the Thiru-Kaveri.

The third is Padma Theertham, located beside the Sri Konganeswarar Temple. The Sthala Vruksham here is the sacred fig tree (Arasu), which spreads widely, hence it is known as ‘Padarndha Arasugal’ (Spreading Figs) and ‘Nila Arasugal’ (Ground Figs). The Sabha here is Bodhi Ambalam or Arasa Ambalam. Nandi is Dharma Nandi Devar. The special events performed by Lord Shiva in this sthalam are as follows: He removed the cow-form, which was a divine play, from Uma Devi and stood as Anaiththezhundhu, revealing this sthalam as Kailasagiri. According to Lord Shiva’s command, the Devas appeared as spreading fig trees, and Lord Shiva was enshrined in their shade.

To Musukunda Chakravarthi, who sought progeny, Lord Shiva revealed this sthalam as Thiruvarur and Himself as Thiyagesar, granting him offspring. It was in this sthalam that Lord Shiva accepted Dharma Devata, who praised Him, as His Rishabha Vahanam. Not only that, but He also granted Dharma Devata the boon to be enshrined in the shade of the fig tree. Responding to the prayers of the Devas and Munis, Lord Shiva performed the Maha Thandavam in the Ambalam situated in the shade of the fig tree. It was in this sthalam that He intervened and saved Thirumoolanayanar, bestowing His grace to reveal the Thirumandiram, the essence of the Agamas. It was here that the Lord granted the golden purse to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman.

He bestowed Shiva Gnana Upadesam upon some Munis. He recited the Vedas to some Brahmins. To Bogar and other Siddhas, and to the Navakodi Siddhas, He granted the Ashtama Siddhis and other boons as they desired. In this sthalam, Lord Shiva, due to these Due to these historical events of the sthalam, various sacred names are attributed to the Lord of this sthalam, as we have seen. The Thevara Thiru-pathigams associated with this sthalam include one Thiru-pathigam composed by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, five Thiru-pathigams composed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, and two Thiru-pathigams composed by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, totaling eight Thevara Thiru-pathigams.

Additionally, there is one Thiru-visaippa pathigam composed by Sendhanar.

Furthermore, a Thiru-Aavaduthurai Puranam, comprising two thousand six hundred verses, composed by Sri Sasthiram Saminatha Munivar, a disciple of Sri Velappadesika Moorthigal, the tenth Guru Maha Sannidhanam of the Thiru-Kailaya Paramparai Thiru-Aavaduthurai Adheenam, is also associated with this sthalam. Thottikkalai Sri, one of the disciples of Sri Madhava Sivagnana Yogigal, the Dravida Maappadiyakkarar, Thiru-Aavaduthurai Kovai composed by Subramaniya Munivar, Thurai Sai Yamaga Anthathi composed by Mahavidwan Thirusirapuram Sri Meenakshi Sundarampillai, and Thurai Sai Silaiyadai Venba composed by Rayasam Sri Ponnuchamy Chettiyar are also present. Thiru-Aavaduthurai is located within the Uyyakkondar Valanadu, a region situated between the Kaveri and Arisilaru rivers. Thiru-Aavaduthurai falls under Thenkarai Thiraimoor Nadu, one of the divisions of Uyyakkondar Valanadu.

Now, regarding the festivals of this sthalam: In this Thiru-Koyil, a seven-day festival used to be held in the month of Purattasi. It was customary to hoist the flag on Moola Nakshatram and perform Theerthavari on Poorattathi Nakshatram. It is known that on the concluding day of this festival, Purattasi Poorattathi, Thirumoolanayanar’s drama and the seven acts of Aariya Koothu were performed. Thillai It is known from Sendhanar’s Thiru-visaippa that there are a thousand ‘Saandhai Meippugazhalar’ and ‘Poosurar Meyye Thiruppani Seivor’ (those who truly perform sacred service), similar to the three thousand Brahmins of Thillai, the five hundred of Mizhalai, and the three hundred of Thiru-Perundurai. Saandhai is Saathanur, a place near this sthalam. Musukunda Chakravarthi performed the Thai festival for Draviya Thiyagesar.

A ten-day festival is also held for Sastha, Durga, and others who guard Thiru-Aavaduthurai, and for Vinayagar and Muruga. In the month of Thai, on the day before Ratha Sapthami, a flag is hoisted for the procession of Thiyagarajar, after crowning him with Chandrasekara Pattabhishekam. During the four-day festival, he appears with Uma Devi in various vehicles: palanquin, Bootha Vahanam, Kailaya Vahanam, and Vimanam. On the fifth day, he ascends the Dharma Vidai under the shade of the Arasu tree, Ascending the Dharma Vidai under the shade of the Arasu tree, He proceeds in procession with the Goddess through the streets, entering the temple through the gopuram, passing the inner gate, and performing the dance in the Arasa Vanam and the Navanidhi Ambalam.

Afterwards, seated on the throne with the Goddess, He receives worship and other services, then enters the temple. On the ninth day, after the chariot festival in Thurai Sai street, He returns to the temple and appears as Anaiththezhundha Nayagar from Masilamani Eesar. On Ratha Sapthami day, at dawn during Uttarayana, for the purpose of bestowing Theertham, He ascends the Rishabha Vahanam and appears with Uma Devi in the form of Anaiththezhundha Kolam. The Lord, with the Goddess, bestows Theertham and returns to the temple. In the evening, to be seen by devotees, He grants the Pandal காட்சி (Pandal Darshan) and enters the Thiru-Koyil with the Goddess. This is customary during this festival.

The Devas celebrate the Chithirai festival in this stalam. In the month of Chithirai, during the Suklapaksha, before Chithra Pournami, a five-day festival is held for Saathar, five days for Veeramakaali, five days for Vinayaka Kadavul, and five days for Muruga Kadavul.

Afterwards, a ten-day festival begins for Masilamani Eesar and Oppila Mulai Ammaiyar, with the hoisting of the Rishabha flag, known as Dhvaja Arohanam. On the first day of the festival, the golden palanquin, on the second day the Bootha Vahanam, on the third day the Anna Vahanam, on the fourth day the Kailaya Vahanam and Simha Vahanam, and on the fifth day the Rishabha Vahanam are used for the procession of Masilamani Eesar with the Goddess, allowing everyone to witness. On the sixth day, the Karpaga Vruksham, on the seventh day, the Goddess’s Manjal Neer Kuzhi (turmeric water ritual). After Sapthami, on the night of Uthira Nakshatram, the sacred marriage of Oppila Mulai Ammaiyar is celebrated. On the ninth day, there is the Thiru-Ther Ula Kaatchi (chariot procession), and on the tenth day, the festival with the Goddess, including the bestowal of Theertham, takes place. In the month of Chithirai, a marriage festival, and in the month of Vaikasi, a Vasantha festival were held.

In the month of Aani, on Uthira Nakshatram, at dawn, the Maha Thandava Utsavam was held in the Arasampalam, also known as Bodhi Ambalam. The Aadi Pooram festival for Athulya Kujambikai lasts for ten days. All these festivals are extensively described in the Sthala Puranam. It is believed that the Thiru-sthalam referred to as Gokkali in Manikkavasagar Peruman’s Thiruvasagam is Thiru-Aavaduthurai. The Sthala Puranam states, “Because the Goddess, whose words are like honey, shed her cow-form, the name Gokkali was given to the city of Gomukthi.” The Sthala Puranam explains the reason for the name Gokkali.

In the Sivapuranam of Thiruvasagam, composed by Sri Manikkavasagar Swamigal, the term ‘Gokkazhiyaanda Gurumani Than Thazh Vazhga’ (Long live the Guru-gem who ruled Gokkazhi) is interpreted as referring to both Thiru-Aavaduthurai and Thiru-Perundurai. The Thiru-Aavaduthurai Adheenam, established by Sri Panchakshara Paramacharya Swamigal, is located here. In the lineage of the external Santhana Gurus of the Saiva faith, Sri Meykanda Deva Nayanar, Arulnandi Sivachariyar, Sri Maraignana Sambandha Peruman, and his disciple Umapathi Sivachariyar form the external Santhana Guru Paramparai. The disciple of Sri Umapathi Siva Sivachariyar is Sri Arul Namasivayar, whose disciple is Siddhar Sivaprakasar, and his disciple is Sri Panchakshara Paramacharya Swamigal, the founder of the Thiru-Aavaduthurai Adheenam.

Therefore, the Thiru-Aavaduthurai tradition, which began with the Deva Paramparai and Bootha Paramparai, continues to this day as the Abhisheka Paramparai. We can learn about the history of the Thiru-Aavaduthurai Adheenam in great detail from the book ‘Thiru-Aavaduthurai Adheenam Varalaru’. All these are the Puranic accounts and special features of the Thiru-Aavaduthurai sthalam. Sekkizhar Peruman elaborates on Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal’s visit and worship here in the following verse: “Having reached the Lord of Aavaduthurai, I was saved,” thus he began with the Thiru-Thandagam, and then composed the beautiful Thiru-Kurunthogai, Nerisai, and Santhaviruththams. With various other poets, he adorned the Lord with many garlands of exquisite Tamil verses, and with overflowing devotion, he stayed for many days, praised by the people of the world, Sekkizhar Peruman sings, “He performed the sacred service of Ulavara Pani with his hands, continuously remembering the Lord.” Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal composed the Thiru-Thandagam, expressing the sentiment, “Having reached the Lord enshrined in the cool Aavaduthurai, I was saved.” Following this, he composed various other pathigams, including Thiru-Kurunthogai, Thiru-Nerisai, and Santhaviruththams. He sang these pathigams, which are like garlands of exquisite Tamil verses, and with ever-increasing love, he stayed for many days in Thiru-Aavaduthurai, praised by the world, continuously performing the sacred service of Ulavara Pani with his hands.

Although Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal composed a total of five pathigams for this sthalam, Sivakavimani now refers to four pathigams composed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal at this time. Sivakavimani Aiya, the commentator of Periyapuranam, notes that the Thiru-pathigam ‘Maayiru Gnalamellam’ for this sthalam was composed later.

We will now continue to contemplate the four Thiru-pathigams composed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal for Thiru-Aavaduthurai. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 382. Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal composed four Thiru-pathigams for Thiru-Aavaduthurai at this time. The first of these Thiru-pathigams is the Thiru-Thandaga Thiru-pathigam beginning with ‘Nambanai Naalvedam’. It is compiled as the forty-sixth Thiru-pathigam in the sixth Thiru-Murai.

Now, that Thiru-pathigam: Thiruchitrambalam. Kaiyaanaai Kaaman Udal Vevakkaayndha Kannaanai Kan Moondru Udaiyaan Thannai Paiyaadaravam Mathiyudanai Vaiththa Sadaiyaanai Paaypuliththol Udaiyaan Thannai Aiyaanai Aavaduthan Thuraiyulmeya Aranadiye Adinaayen Adaindhu Uyndhene Vendaamai Venduvadhum Illaan Thannai Visaiyanai Munnasaiviththa Vedan Thannai Thoondaamai Sudarvidu Narsothithannai Soolappadaiyanai Kaalan Vaazhnaal Maandoda Udhai Seydha Maindhan Thannai Mannavarum Vinnavarum Vanangiyeththum Andaanaai Aavaduthan Thuraiyulmeya Aranadiye Adinaayen Adaindhu Uyndhene Pandhanavu Melviralaal Paagan Thannai Paadalodu Aadal Payindran Thannai Konthanavu Narungondrai Maalaiyanai Kolama Neela Midatran Thannai Senthamizhodu Aariyanai Seeriyanai Thiru Maarbil Puri Vennool Thigazhap Poonda Andhananai Aavaduthan Thuraiyul Meya Aran Adiye Adinaayen Adaindhu Uyndhene Thariththaanai Than Kadal Nanjundaan Thannai Thakkan Than Peru Velvi Thagarththaan Thannai Piriththaanai Piraiththaval Senjadaiyinaanaai Peruvaliyaal Malai Eduththa Arakkan Thannai Neriththaanai Nerizhaiyaal Paagaththaanai Neesanaen Udal Uru Noyana Theera Ariththaanai Aavaduthan Thuraiyulmeya Aranadiye Adinaayen Adaindhu Uyndhene Thiruchitrambalam. This is the first Thiru-pathigam composed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal.

Now, the second Thiru-pathigam. This is a Thiru-Thandaga Thiru-pathigam, compiled as the forty-seventh Thiru-pathigam in the sixth Thiru-Murai.

Now, that Thiru-pathigam: Thiruchitrambalam. Thiruve En Selvamay Thenay Vaanor Sezhunjudaray Sezhunjudar Narsothimikka Uruve En Urave En Oonay Oonin Ullamay Ullaththin Ullay Nindra Karuve En Karpagamay Kannay Kannil Karumaniyay Maniyaadu Paavaay Kaavaay Aruvaaya Valvinai Noy Adaiyaavannam Aavaduthan Thurai Urayum Amarar Eray Maatraen Ezhuthanjum Endra Naavin Maravaen Thiruvarulgal Vanja Nenjin Etraen Pira Deyvam Enna Na My dog-like self, if I do not contemplate Thiru-Erumaan’s holy feet, and seeing the deeds you perform, I give way to suffering day after day, I cannot bear it. Do not say, “Fear not,” to this servant, O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! O partner of the slender-waisted maiden, O Lord of the Ganga, O Lord with matted locks, if I were to die without uttering your name, what would it matter if I were afflicted by any terrible disease? To the devotees who, melting with thought, with overflowing tears, lovingly praise your ocean-like self, do not say, “Fear not,” to this servant, O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! O Lord who bent the bow to burn the three cities, making Uma Devi fear, and who, joyfully placing his hand on the great elephant, flayed it, O Kankala, our King!

The people of this earth will not bear it day after day. O Lord who protects life, I am not pressing you. Do not say, “Fear not,” to this servant, O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! Having plucked fresh flowers, bathed in water, and praised and glorified your feet daily, I have cast off sorrows that cannot be cast off. What if the karma of the world comes upon me? O Lord who, becoming a kinsman, drank the poison from the roaring ocean to save the celestials, do not say, “Fear not,” to this servant, O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai!

O Lord who, taking the form of Narayana, held his head in his hand, covered himself with the skin of a dead elephant, and wandered everywhere as a Kankala hunter! Who am I to you, a destroyer of karma? You are the origin of all good and bad deeds. Do not say, “Fear not,” to this servant, O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! O Lord who flayed the skin O Lord whose garment is the flayed skin! O Lord of Uma Devi!

O Lord of the celestials! O Lord of Kailasa, who drank the poison from the dark ocean! It is your duty, O Great One, to forgive the faults of your devotees. Is not great compassion yours? O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai, where peacocks dance in the groves! O Beloved One who captivates the hearts of those who love you, O Lord who wanders, begging for alms from the celestials, holding a skull in your hand!

O Lord with the dancing hand! Alas, truly, I have wandered day after day, immersed in the delusion of birth, a body filled with impurities. Do not say, “Fear not,” to this servant, O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! O Lord who holds many white skulls in his hand, who rides a bull, and begs for alms from town to town! O Lord of the stony mountain You and all will depart. If you do not consider those who dance in the cremation ground, everyone will surely despise me.

I have abandoned the ignorant Jains and Buddhists. Do not say, “Fear not,” to this servant, O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! I have not walked the pure path of the renunciates, nor am I pure enough to offer garlands. All the days I have not spoken of your holy grace are days I have not been born. I know all the deeds you performed when you crushed the king of Lanka, whose city was fortified. Do not say, “Fear not,” to this servant, O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai!

This is the third of the four Thiru-Pathikams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasar Swamigal for Thiru-Aavaduthurai, that is, the third of the four Thiru-Pathikams composed at this time. The Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam is the twenty-ninth Thiru-Pathikam in the fifth Thiru-Murai.

Now, that Thiru-Pathikam.

“Niraikka vaaliyal allalin nerizhai maraikkavaaliyal allali maadharaal piraikkavaala perumpunal aavaduthurai kavaaliyodaadiya sunname thavalamaadhi saayaloor chandiran pilavusoodiya pingyagan emmirai alavukandila aavaduthurai kalavu kandanal otthanal kanniye paadhi pennoru paagaththin panmarai odhi en nuzham kondavan on porul aadhi aavaduthurai meviya sodhiye sudare” — She is not able to fill, nor is she able to conceal her distress, the maiden. The great flood of Thiru-Aavaduthurai, where the Lord danced with the skull, is like the white moon. He wears the crescent moon, a fiery one, our Lord. She has not seen the measure of Thiru-Aavaduthurai. She has seen the theft, as if she were a virgin.

He who holds half a woman in his body, who recites many Vedas, who has taken my soul, the unique primal being, the light that resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai, the flame, she says. He whose throat is like a dark cloud, she is filled with pride, thinking of him, the one with the Konrai flower, Thiru-Aavaduthurai. She stands for him, and her feet are not seen. He whose throat is dark, whose light is like the fierce sun, he is like the nectar of milk. She went near him and cried, “O Lord of Thiru-Aavaduthurai, my only Lord!” He who holds the flute, the Konrai, the skull, and the maiden as part of his body. “Is he not the beautiful one of Thiru-Aavaduthurai?” she says, her bangles slipping from her hands.

She, with her soft feet like cotton, who has him as her refuge, is not afraid of anyone. This is the madness she has with the Lord of Thiru-Aavaduthurai. He who wears the crescent moon, who is both male and female, who has a full heart and purity.

The Lord of Thiru-Aavaduthurai, with its fragrant groves, my Lord, he thinks of me. He who measured the earth and Brahma, when they sought to see the truth, became a pillar of fire. O Lord of Thiru-Aavaduthurai, my Lord, the white bangles on my hand are slipping off. He who begs for alms while ghosts sing, he who destroyed the strength of the mighty Ravana. See him, the naked one, who wears bones, in Thiru-Aavaduthurai, the shameless one!

This Thiru-Pathikam is presented as the words of a mother describing the state of her daughter, who, having seen the Lord, is infatuated and has lost her self-control. This Thiru-Pathikam is set in the Akapporul (love poetry) genre. If we remember that the essence of this site is the removal of the animalistic nature of souls, and contemplate this Thiru-Pathikam, we can attain great bliss.

Next, the fourth Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasar Swamigal. The fourth Thiru-Pathikam, Thiru-Ner-Isai Thiru-Pathikam, is the fifty-seventh Thiru-Pathikam in the fourth Thiru-Murai.

“Manjanai maniyum aanai maragatha thirulumaanai nenjule pugundhu nindru ninai tharu nigazhvinaanai thunjumbodhaaga vandhu thunaiyanakku aagi nindru anjal endru arula vendum aavaduthuraiyulane” — You are the dark one, the jewel, the emerald cluster. You entered my heart and stood there, becoming the one who brings forth thoughts. When I am about to die, please come and be my companion, stand by me, and say, “Fear not,” O Lord who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! “Naan ugandhu unnai naalum nanuguma karuthiyeyum oon ugandhu oombum naayen ullura aivar nindrar thaan ugandhe yugandha thagavilaa thondane naan aan ugandhu eruvaane aavaduthuraiyulane” — Even though I desire to approach you daily, I am a dog-like being who cherishes the flesh, and five senses reside within me. I am an unworthy servant who loves what you love.

O Lord who rides the bull, who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! “Kattame vinaigalaana kaaththivai nokki aalaai ottave otti naalum unnai ul vaikkamaatten pattavaan thalai kaiyendhi pazhi thirindhu oorgalthorum attamaa uruvinaanai aavaduthuraiyula” — My karmas are a burden. I cannot keep you in my heart daily, even if I try to embrace you. O Lord who holds a skull in his hand, who wanders from town to town, who has eight forms, who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! I cannot speak of the greatness of Thillai. I cannot ascend to heaven by contemplating you with a single mind.

I am cleansing the body that has been darkened. O Lord who drank the rare poison, who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! I am a wicked one, caught in the whirlpool of karma. Protect me from the five senses that come to disturb me. O Lord who joyfully holds the fragrant garlanded maiden in one part of his body, who wears the eight great serpents, who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! O Lord whose throat is like dark fire, who burned the three fortresses with a single fiery arrow, who has fire in his matted locks, you remove the karmas of those who remember you.

O Lord who dances holding the six fires, who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! I am not firm in my mind, I cannot perceive the holy feet of Shiva. I have no goal, no good qualities, I cannot speak of them. I have no righteous path, I cannot think of you. I am ignorant, I have forgotten. O Lord who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai!

I cannot understand the beautiful form you took with the beautiful maiden. My deeds have covered me. Grant me that I may not suffer in this great world. O Lord who drank the poison from the great banyan tree, who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! The tall one and Brahma searched on both sides, but they could not speak of the form you took, a fierce form, a pillar of fire. O Lord who resides in my heart, who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai!

When the demon went to the mountain, Uma Devi feared. He lifted it with his hands above his head. You pressed him with your immeasurable toe and granted him boons. O Lord who wears the agitated great Ganga, who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai!

These four Thiru-Pathikams were composed by Thiru-Navukkarasar Swamigal. These are the Thiru-Pathikams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasar Swamigal after reaching Thiru-Aavaduthurai and worshipping the Lord. Sivakavimani Ayya writes that the fifth Thiru-Pathikam for this site, the Thiru-Ner-Isai Thiru-Pathikam called “Mayooru Gnanam,” was composed later.

Let us resume our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 383, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped at Thiru-Aavaduthurai, continues his pilgrimage to the Ponni Nadu Thiru-Thalaiyathirai.

The Lord sings as follows in his Thiru-Thalaiyathirai: “Eri punal pon mani sidharum thirai neer ponni idai maruthai sendru eythi anbinodu mari viravu karaththaarai vanangi vaiki van tamil paamaalai pala magizhchchaaththi poriyaravam punaindhaarai thiru naagechuraththu potri arunthamil maalai punaindhu poandhu serivirai nan malarcholai pazhaiyaaru eythi thiru chaththi muttraththai sendru serndhaar” — Having reached Thiru-Idai-Maruthu, where the waves of the Ponni scatter fire, gold, and jewels, and having worshipped with love the Lord who holds a deer in his hand, he stayed there and joyfully offered many garlands of rich Tamil verses. Having praised the Lord who wears a serpent in Thiru-Nageswaram and offered a garland of rare Tamil verses, he proceeded to Pazhaiyaru, a grove of fragrant flowers, and reached Thiru-Chaththi-Mutram.

Thus sings Sekkizhar Peruman. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped at Thiru-Aavaduthurai He goes to the holy site of Thiru-Idai-Maruthur and worships there.

After that, he reaches the holy site of Thiru-Nageswaram, sings Thiru-Pathikams there, then goes to the holy site of Pazhaiyaru, sings Thiru-Pathikams there, and then reaches the holy site of Thiru-Chaththi-Mutram. Sekkizhar Peruman sings this in one verse. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman goes to the holy site of Thiru-Idai-Maruthur. In the holy site of Thiru-Idai-Maruthur, the Lord’s holy name is Maruthavanar Mahalingeswarar. The Goddess’s holy name is Pirakat Sundara Kujambikai Perunala Mulai Ammai. The Sthala Vriksham is the Marutha tree.

In this holy site, eleven Rudras, on the night of the great dissolution when all living beings merged, came and worshipped and attained Shiva-Peru.

Furthermore, the Mahalinga Peruman resides in this holy site. The Vinayagar of this holy site resides in Thiru-Valanchuzhi, Muruga-Kadavul in Swamimalai, Chandikeswara Nayanar in Thiru-Vaipadi, Surya and other Navagrahas in Suryanar Koil, Nataraja Peruman in Thiruchitrambalam, Bhairava-Kadavul in Sirkazhi, Nandi Devar in Thiru-Aavaduthurai, Somasakandar in Thiruvarur, and Dakshinamurthy in Thiru-Alangudi and Thiru-Irumpoolai temples. The Mahalinga Peruman in Thiru-Idai-Maruthur, like a central jewel in the sanctum sanctorum, is surrounded by these subsidiary temples.

Therefore, this is a very great holy site. Shiva Peruman showed the sages in this town the greatness of Uma Devi meditating on the Lord in her heart-lotus. Shiva Peruman appeared and gave darshan to the sages in the midst of a grove of Marutha trees to bless the sage Romasa, according to the Puranic history. This holy site has twelve holy names: Shanpakaranayam, Sakthipuram, Vilvavanam, Thapovanam, Jothipuram, Sarvatheerthapuram, Selva Viruththipuram, Dharma Viruththipuram, Mukthipuram, Idaimaruthu, Veeracholapuram, and Pooloka Sivalokam. The Puranic history states that Veeracholan reached this holy site, worshipped, cleared the forests, cultivated the land, and performed many temple renovations.

Therefore, this holy site is called Veeracholapuram. The Veeracholan river flowing north of this holy site confirms this. Ancient texts such as Kanda Puranam, Linga Puranam, Brahma Kaivartha Puranam, and Sivaragasyam have glorified this holy site of Thiru-Idai-Maruthur. They speak. If we consider Manikkavasagar’s words in Thiruvasagam, “Ananda Thenirundha Pondhai” (the pot containing the honey of bliss) in reference to the Lord of Idaimaruthu, the antiquity of this site will be well understood. The great sages, by the command of Agastya Muni, began to meditate on Uma.

They obtained the knowledge of the Vedas and Agamas and the materials for Shiva worship through the grace of Namagal and Thirumagal, and began to strive for their primary goal of spiritual progress. Just as a child comes to know the father through the mother, the sages also began to meditate, seeking the grace of Shakti. Shakti is very fond of groves filled with Champaka flowers. Knowing this, the sages began to meditate in a Champaka grove here. They began to meditate there.

The Lord has the nature of quickly reaching the heart-lotus of those who remember Him with love. The Goddess also has this nature.

Therefore, the Goddess appeared and blessed the great sages. The great sages prayed to the Goddess, saying, “Mother, we desire to attain the Father.” Immediately, the Goddess, contemplating the Lord in her heart-lotus, performed Shiva Yoga in a state of silence. The great sages served the Goddess and performed penance. In this state, as the Goddess had wished in her heart, the Lord appeared as a luminous form, as Mahalinga Murthy, as Jyotir Mahalinga, and blessed the sages with His vision. All the sages, unable to behold the luminous Lord, were bewildered, but by the grace of the Goddess, they beheld Him and attained great bliss. In the state where the Lord appeared and blessed the great sages, He became Ekanayagan.

He manifested. Not only that, but in the very state in which He appeared, He Himself explained to souls the method of performing Shiva Puja and the benefits attained by those who worship. This holy site is bounded by Panapuram to the east, Thiru-Neelakudi to the south, Thiru-Bhuvanam to the west, and the Kaveri River to the north. The holy waters located in this site are as follows: Karunyamirtha Theertham, which is the most excellent of all holy waters. By bathing in it during the auspicious time of Chithirai Vishu, one can attain great merit. Next is Pana Theertham, located in Panapuram, which forms the eastern boundary of this site.

This is a holy water created by Sri Rama. Bathing in it during Vaikasi Pournami is considered special. Next is Parasara Theertham. This holy water is believed to be the Pidari Kulam located at the intersection of the north and east streets. Bathing in it during the month of Margazhi is special. The Sthala Puranam states that Parasara Muni, following the advice of Romasa Muni, bathed in this Theertham and was cleansed of the impurity of having been with Machagandhi.

Next is Soma Theertham, which is located to the east of Karunyamirtha Theertham. Bathing in it on Somavaram (Monday) is special. It was created by Chandra (the moon god) and removes the five great sins. It is currently known as Ayyanar Kulam. Next is Rudra Theertham. Next are Padma Theertham, Pandava Theerthams, Indana Theertham, Vayu Theertham, Kubera Theertham, Isana Theertham, Kanaka Theertham, Ganga Kupam, Garuda Theertham, Vasu Theertham, Surya Theertham, Maruthukkal Theertham, Narasinga Theertham, Nandi Theertham, Drona Theertham, Ragava Kupam, Sura Theertham, Muni Theertham, Kachapa Theertham, Gautama Theertham, Kalvi There are thirty-two Theerthams in this site, including Kalyana Theertham.

The other temples located around this site are Theradi Pillaiyar Koil, Viswanathar Koil, Kumarak Koil, Rishipuriswarar Koil, Melamariamman Koil, Perumal Koil, Aghoraveerabhadrar Koil, Sokkanathar Koil, Keelamariamman Koil, Ulagatchi Koil, and Atmanathar Koil. This site is a Panchalinga Sthalam. Viswanathar shines in the east, Rishipuriswarar in the west, Sokkanathar in the north, and Atmanathar in the south, with Sri Mahalinga Peruman seated as the central deity. The temple stands majestically in the center of the town. The outer circumambulatory path of this temple is called Ashwamedha Pradakshina Prakaram. Those who circumambulate this path will receive the benefit of having performed the Ashwamedha sacrifice.

The next circumambulatory path is called Kodumudi. It is called Prakaram. Those who circumambulate this Prakaram will receive the benefit of having circumambulated Thiru-Kailasa.

Next, the Prakaram located adjacent to the sanctum sanctorum is the Pranava Prakaram.

Thus, this temple shines. Other deities in the temple include Padithurai Vinayagar and Anda Vinayagar. There is a Mookambikai shrine in this site. The Goddess is in a meditative posture. Inscriptions refer to this Ambikai as Pidari Yogirundha Parameswari. The sanctum sanctorum of this temple is built in the North Indian style.

Next, the deities of Vempadi Kumarar Koil and Sokkanathar Koil are located. There are many mandapams, including Kalyana Mandapam and Natiya Mandapam. The Thevara Thiru-Pathikams sung by the Samayacharyas, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, and Sundaramurthy Swamigal, are available for this site. There are a total of eleven Thevara Thiru-Pathikams for this site. Manikkavasagar Swamigal has also sung about this site in Thiruvasagam. Pattinaththu Swamigal has composed a work called Thiru-Idai-Maruthur Mummani Kovai.

This work is in the eleventh Thiru-Murai. Bhadragiriyar has worshipped at this site. Sivakozhundhu Desikar has translated the Sthala Puranam of this site from Sanskrit into Tamil. Six daily pujas, starting from Thiru-Ananthal, are performed in this temple. During the second period, a special puja is performed exclusively for Ekanayagar. The Thai Poosam festival and the Vaikasi Vasantha festival are celebrated grandly in this temple.

In addition to these, festivals such as Thiru-Athirai Oonjal festival, Panguni Theertham, Chithirai Vishu Punyakalam, and Shivaratri festival are also celebrated grandly. This temple is under the administration of the Thiru-Kailaya Paramparai Thiru-Aavaduthurai Adheenam. Three special sites are mentioned as having the Marutha tree, also known as the Arjuna tree, as their Sthala Vriksham. The first holy site is Thiru-Paruppatham, known as Srisailam.

There, the Lord is enshrined by the name Mallikarjuneswarar, and therefore it is called Mallikarjunam. In the south, in the Pandya country, in the Tirunelveli region, there is a holy site called Thiru-Pudai-Maruthur. Here too, the Marutha tree, called the Arjuna tree, is the Sthala Vriksham. This is called Pudharjunam. Between these two sites, this site, Thiru-Idai-Maruthur, is located as Madhyarjunam. This holy site is where Varaguna Pandiyan’s Brahmagathi Dosham was removed.

Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman There are six Thiru-Pathikams sung by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, five Thiru-Pathikams sung by Appar Swamigal, and one Thiru-Pathikam by Sundaramurthy Swamigal for this site. Karuvur Devar has sung about this site in Thiru-Isaippa. As we have already seen, Pattinaththu Pillaiyar has composed the Prabandham called Thiru-Idai-Maruthur Mummani Kovai. Not only that, but Appar Swamigal and Sundaramurthy Swamigal have also mentioned Thiru-Idai-Maruthur in other Thiru-Pathikams. Manikkavasagar Swamigal has also sung about Thiru-Idai-Maruthur in six places in Thiruvasagam. In the seventy-fifth line of Keerththi Thiru-Agaval, he has sung, “Idaimaruthu athanil eenda irundhu” (residing there in Idaimaruthu).

In the one hundred and forty-fifth line of Potri Thiru-Agaval, he has sung, “Idaimaruthu uraiyum enthaay potri” (Praise to my Lord who resides in Idaimaruthu). In the Thiru-Poovalli Thiru-Pathikam of Thiru-Vasagam, the second verse, which begins with “Entha Enthai Sutram Mattumellam Ennudaiya Bandham Aruthu Ena Aandu Konda Pandi-Piran Antha Idaimaruthil Aanandha Thenirundha Pondhai Paravinam Poovalli Koyyamo,” praises the Lord of Thiru-Idaimaruthur as the abode of joyful honey. In the second verse of the Thiru-Poonnusal Thiru-Pathikam, it is sung, “Oon Thangi Nindru Urukkum Uthirakosamangai Kon Thangu Idaimaruthu Paadi.” In the ninth verse of the Thiru-Vesaravu Thiru-Pathikam, it is sung, “Arul Enakku Ingu Idaimaruthe Idam Konda Ammane.” In Thiru-Kovaiyar, in the song beginning “Kundram Kidaikkum Kadandhu Umar,” Thiru-Idaimaruthur is mentioned as “Idaimaruthu Ekambam Vanjiyam.” Parana Deva Nayanar has sung about Thiru-Idaimaruthur in the Thiru-Andhadhi of Lord Shiva. Literary works such as Maruthavana Puranam, Thiru-Idaimaruthur Ula, Thiru-Idaimaruthur Kalambagam, Thiru-Idaimaruthur Patirruppathandhadhi, and Thiru-Idaimaruthur Nondi Nadagam also elucidate the glory of this sacred sthalam. We have seen that Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, who visited this sthalam, composed five Thiru-Pathikams.

Now, let us consider those Thiru-Pathikams. The first Thiru-Pathikam is the thirty-fifth Thiru-Pathikam in the fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Nerisai Thiru-Pathikam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 384, Thiru-Nindratcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We have seen the first of the five Thiru-Pathikams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar for the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Idaimaruthur.

Now, the second Thiru-Pathikam, compiled as the fourteenth Thiru-Pathikam in the fifth Thiru-Murai, is a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam.

Regarding the numbers in the sixth verse, Sivakavimani notes that “Aiyirandum Aarondrum” refers to sixteen, representing the sixteen Kala Prasadha Mantras, and “Arumoonru” refers to eighteen, representing the eighteen Puranas, and “Naanmoonru” refers to twelve, representing the Moola Mantra along with the Samhita Mantras.

At the same time, regarding the difficult meaning of the seventh verse, Sivakavimani Ayya writes that this song is one of those whose meaning is not easily understood.

We shall continue our contemplation of this. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 385, Thiru-Nindratcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. After worshipping Thiru-Idaimaruthur, singing Thevarams, and devoutly worshipping Lord Shiva, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar stayed there, performed sacred service, and then reached the sthalam called Thiru-Nageswaram. Thiru-Nageswaram is a sacred sthalam very close to Kumbakonam. The Lord’s sacred names are Nageswarar, Naganathar, Shanbagaranyeswarar. The Goddess’s sacred names are Girikujambigai, Kundrumamulai Ammai.

The Sthala Vriksham is the Shanbaga tree. The Theerthams are Surya Theertham, Yama Theertham, Brahma Theertham, Chandra Theertham, Agni Theertham, Durga Theertham, Gautama Theertham, Parasara Theertham, Indra Theertham, Bhrigu Theertham, Kanva Theertham, Vasishtha Theertham. This sthalam is where the Naga Rajas, namely Adiseshan, Dakshan, and Karkotakan, worshipped Lord Shiva.

Hence, this sthalam is named Thiru-Nageswaram. This sthalam is renowned because the Naga Raja worshipped in the first yama at Kudanthai Keezhkottam, which is a Bilva forest, in the second yama at Thiru-Nageswaram, which is a Shanbaga forest, in the third yama at Thiru-Pambaram, which is a Vanni forest, and in the fourth yama at Nagai Karonam, which is a Punnai forest, during one Shivaratri. These four sthalams are known by the name of the Naga Raja. Enraged by Bhringi Muni, who worshipped only Lord Shiva, Goddess Parvati performed severe penance under the Shanbaga tree at this sthalam, desiring the Ardhanareeswara form of Lord Shiva. Not only Adiseshan, Dakshan, and Karkotakan, but also Gautama, Nandi, Nalan, Parasara, Bhagiratha, and others have worshipped here and attained blessings. Surya worshipped here.

Ganesha worshipped here and became the lord of the Ganas. Gautama worshipped and attained Ahalya. Nalan worshipped here and regained his lost wife. Parasara Muni worshipped and was freed from sin. The Pandavas worshipped and regained their lost wealth, and also conducted the Karthigai month festival for this Lord. Vasishtha Muni worshipped.

Indra, Brahma, and Bhagiratha also worshipped. A king named Chitrasenan conducted a festival in Vaikasi and was blessed with a good son. Shaunaka Muni performed penance for infatuation here. A muni named Narkunan lit lamps and observed fasts on Karthigai Somavaram after being bitten by a snake. Many devotees in this sthalam have been blessed and freed from diseases such as Rakshasa, Paisacha, and Vetala, and have had their dead children brought back to life. This sthalam has been sung by the three great saints: Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, Thiru-Navukkarasar Swamigal, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal.

Sekkizhar Peruman undertook sacred service here, and Thiru-Nageswarathu Peruman is Sekkizhar’s spiritual deity. Due to his affection for this sthalam, Sekkizhar Peruman built a temple with the same name in his hometown of Kundrathur, which is known as Vadathiru-Nageswaram. The sthalam’s Vinayagar is Shanbhaga Vinayagar. This temple is also known as Shanbhaga Vanam and Girikannigai Vanam. It is customary to worship at Kudanthai Keezhkottu Thiru-Nageswaram in the morning, Thiru-Nageswaram at noon, and Thiru-Pambaram in the evening, all on the same day. The idols of Sekkizhar Peruman, his mother, and his younger brother Balaravayan are present in the temple.

Here, Girikujambigai, Lakshmi, and Saraswati are seen in a single sanctum. The sanctum sanctorum of this sacred temple is built according to the Ardhanareeswara principle. The Moolavar, Naganatha Swami, has his sanctum facing south, and the sthalam’s Ambal, Piraiyani Amman, has her sanctum facing north. Both sanctums face east. Instead of separate circumambulatory paths for each sanctum, there is a single path encompassing both, reflecting the Ardhanareeswara concept. The wall on the north side of the Swami’s sanctum and the wall on the south side of the Ambal’s Ardha Mandapam are conjoined, making it impossible to circumambulate the Lord and Goddess separately.

The Lord, who manifests as Ardhanareeswara, bestows His grace here in that very principle. To the east of the Thiruchitrambalamudaiyan Mandapam, facing north, is a seated sculpture of Sekkizhar Peruman, the author of Periya Puranam. To Sekkizhar’s right is a standing sculpture of his mother, Azhagambigai. To Sekkizhar’s left is a seated sculpture of his brother, Balaravayar. These three sacred forms are arranged facing the dancing Nataraja Peruman in the Nataraja Mandapam, which faces south, with their hands clasped in worship. There are two Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman for this sthalam, and Thiru-Navukkarasar Swamigal composed three Thiru-Pathigams, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal composed one Thiru-Pathigam.

Thiru-Navukkarasar Swamigal visited this sthalam and composed three Thiru-Pathigams. The first Thiru-Pathigam is the sixty-sixth Thiru-Pathigam in the fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Nerishai Thiru-Pathigam.
