Swamigal’s three Thiru-Pathigams for Thiru-Nageswaram.

We shall proceed with our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 386. Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped at Thiru-Nageswaram and sung Thiru-Pathigams there, then proceeds to the sacred sthalam of Pazhaiyarai. This sthalam is also known as Pazhaiyarai.

It is the birthplace of Amarneethi Nayanar. We have contemplated the special features of this sthalam in the Puranam of Amarneethi Nayanar. The Thiru-Pathigam sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal at this sthalam is not available to us. The Thiru-Pathigam ‘Thalaiyellam Parikkum Saman Kaiyar’, sung at Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, is a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathigam, which Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar composed later when he visited and worshipped at Pazhaiyarai Vadathali. We shall see that sacred history later in the Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Having worshipped at Pazhaiyarai, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal then reached the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Sakthimuttram.

Thiru-Sakthimuttram is located very close to Thiru-Pattiswaram, near Kumbakonam. Thiru-Pattiswaram is the twenty-second sthalam among the Cauvery South Bank sthalams, and Thiru-Sakthimuttram is the twenty-third. The south street of Thiru-Sakthimuttram is the north street of Thiru-Pattiswaram. These two sthalams are thus interconnected. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar arrives at Thiru-Sakthimuttram.

Here, the Lord’s sacred name is Sivakkozhundeesar, and the Goddess’s sacred name is Periya Nayaki. The sthalam’s sacred tree is Vilvam, and its sacred water is Soola Theertham. In this sthalam, Thiru-Sakthimuttram, in this temple, Uma Devi worshipped Lord Shiva and embraced and kissed Him, which is why this sacred sthalam is known by the sacred name Thiru-Sakthi Muttram. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal praised this in his Thevara Pathigam, saying, “Mattar Kuzhali Malaimagal poojai magizhtharulum Sitta Thiru-Sakthi Muttram uraiyum Sivakkozhundhe.” This sthalam is now known as Sakthi Muttram. The history of this sthalam states that the Goddess desired to worship the Lord and behold His sacred form, and a light appeared from the Shiva Lingam, at which point the Goddess embraced the Lord. The sacred marks corresponding to this event are visible on the Moolalingam Peruman in this temple.

Next to the Moolasthanam, we can behold the sacred form of the Goddess embracing and kissing the Shiva Lingam. The temple is a large structure facing east, situated amidst four sacred streets. At the entrance, Vallabhai Ganapathi is present. The Vasantha Mandapam at the temple entrance is a grand hall. There are two circumambulatory paths. The Rajagopuram has five tiers.

The outer circumambulatory path is very large. The Yagasalai is in the northeast direction, and the Pakasalai (kitchen) is in the southeast. In front of the sanctum, there is a flagstaff, Nandi, and Balipeetams. Beyond that is the front mandapam. Upon entering past the mandapam, one finds the second gopuram entrance with Vinayagar and Murugan. To the right, the Ambal temple faces south.

Beyond the second gopuram, there is a Maha Mandapam with a Nataraja Sabha. Opposite it is the Nalvar Sannidhi. At the entrance of the Swami Sannidhi, to the south is Somaskandar, and to the north is the traditional deity depicting Sakthi Muttram. Behind this traditional sculpture, there is also a scene of the Ambal performing penance standing on one leg. In the inner circumambulatory path, to the southwest are the sthalam’s Vinayagar, followed by Somaskandar, Arumugar, and Gajalakshmi. In the sanctum’s niches, to the south are Vinayagar, Natarajar, a sage, and Dakshinamurthy; to the west is Lingothbhavar; and to the north are Brahma and Durga.

In the northern circumambulatory path, there is a separate Chandeesar temple. He can be worshipped from the Swami Sannidhi itself. Next to the Natarajar Sabha is the old Ambal idol. Upon entering further, one reaches the Ardha Mandapam. Beyond that, one can worship Vinayagar and the Dvarapalakas. The Swami Sannidhi is very special.

When Appar Swamigal requested to receive Thiru-Adi Deekshai, this deity granted him grace, saying, “Come to Nallur.” The Ambal temple is in the first circumambulatory path. This is the sthalam where the Ambikai performed penance, hence this sanctum is very special. Appar Swamigal mentions the name of the Lord of this sthalam, Sivakkozhundeesar, in every verse of the Thiru-Pathigam he composed. The Thazhuva Kulantha Nathar idol in this sthalam is very beautiful. The sacred water outside the temple is known as Soola Theertham and Surya Theertham. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal comes to Thiru-Sakthi Muttram for darshan.

He worships Sivakkozhundeesar, who is enshrined in Thiru-Sakthi Muttram, and performs his characteristic sacred service of Ulavaara Thiru-Pani. He also offers garlands of Thevaram to the Lord.

At that time, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal sings the Thevara Thiru-Pathigam beginning with ‘Kovay Mudugi’. In this Thiru-Pathigam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman makes a request to Sivakkozhundeesar, the Lord of this sthalam. He requests, “Before Yama comes and takes my life, please imprint the mark of your flower-like sacred feet upon my head.” In this Thiru-Pathigam, he refers to the Lord’s feet as ‘poovar thiruvadigal’ (flower-like sacred feet), feet adorned with flowers offered by Ambikai and devotees. He prays, “Please imprint the mark of those sacred feet upon my head.” ‘Poriththu vaiththal’ means to engrave it permanently, so that the mark of the sacred feet never changes. The meaning is that devotees should always remain under the shade of the Lord’s sacred feet, never going anywhere else. The meaning is that devotees should always remain under the shade of the Lord’s sacred feet, never going anywhere else.

Thus, with the request that the Lord’s sacred feet should be on his head, he prays, “Please place your sacred feet upon my head.” ‘Thadalai Karalai’ are symbolic expressions belonging to the Saivite tradition. ‘Thazh Thalai’.

Thus, he sings that Thiru-Pathigam, which is the Thiru-Pathigam ‘Kovay Mudugi’. This is the ninety-sixth Thiru-Pathigam in the fourth Thiru-Murai.

Now, that Thiru-Pathigam.

Kovay mudugi aduththal kootram kumaippathan mun Poovar adichchuvadu enmel poriththu vai pogavidil Moova muzhappazhi moodum kanday Muzhangum thalal kai Deva Thiru-Saththi Muttram uraiyum Sivakkozhundhe Kaynthay anangan udalam podipadak kalanai mun Paynthay uyir segap patham panivar tham palpiravi Aynthaynthu aruppay adiyerkku arulay un anbar sinthai Serththay Thiru-Saththi Muttram uraiyum Sivakkozhundhe Poththar kurambai pugunthu aivar nalum pugazh azhippar Matthar thayirpol marugum en sinthai marukkozivi Aththa adiyen adaikkalam kanday amarargal tham Siththa Thiru-Saththi Muttram uraiyum Sivakkozhundhe Nilla kurambai nilaiya karuthi innee nilaththu Onralla kuzhi veezhnthu ayarvuruvayenai vanthu andu kondaiy Viller puruvaththu umaiyal kanava vidil keduven Selva Thiru-Saththi Muttram uraiyum Sivakkozhundhe Karuvutru irunthu un kalale ninainthan karuppuviyil Theruvil pugunthan thigaiththu adiyenai thigaippu olivi Uruvil thigazhum umaiyal kanava vidil keduven Thiruvil polichchaththi Muttram uraiyum Sivakkozhundhe Vemmai naman thamar mikku viravi vizhuppathan mun Immai un thazh en nenjaththu ezhuthivai eengu igazhil Ammai adiyerkku aruluthi enbathu ingu ararivar Semmai tharu Sakthimuttram uraiyum Sivakkozhundhe Vittar purangal oru nodi vevavor venganiyal Suttay en pasathth thodarbu aruththu andukol thumbi pambum Mattarkuzhali malaimagal poosai magizhtharulum Sitta Thiru-Saththi Muttram uraiyum O Thiru-Sivakkozhundhu, residing in Thiru-Sathimuttam, who, when the scornful Daksha performed his sacrifice, and the celestials implored, on that very day, you, the blue-throated one, took victory! Grant me, your praising devotee, release from my sins. O Thiru-Sivakkozhundhu, residing in Thiru-Sathimuttam, I, having attained the worthy, and overcome by sorrow, have sought refuge at your feet. What love, what benefit, do I possess other than your grace? O Thiru-Sivakkozhundhu, residing in Thiru-Sathimuttam, who is greatly desired by those in Thillai, and who is the direction of the great north!

When the chariot-borne demon, Ravana, who had taken up the burden, had his golden crown crushed and his skin torn, you pressed a single toe, causing him to wail and descend, and then you granted him grace. O Thiru-Sivakkozhundhu, residing in Thiru-Sathimuttam, you destroyed the disease of the cruel deeds I committed.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, at Thiru-Sathimuttam, petitions Thiru-Sivakkozhundhu Eesar that the sacred footprints of the Lord be imprinted upon his head. Immediately after he sang this Pathikam, Thiru-Sivakkozhundhu Eesar at Thiru-Sathimuttam graciously commands Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, saying, “Come to Nallur!” Nallur is a sacred sthalam known as Thiru-Nallur. This sacred sthalam is very close to Thiru-Sathimuttam. We know that Thiru-Nallur is the sthalam where the history of Amarneethi Nayanar, ascending the balance and reaching Kailash, occurred, as recounted in the Puranas of Amarneethi Nayanar.

The Lord graciously commands him to come to that Thiru-Nallur.

Thus, guided by divine grace, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar ...the sacred devotee, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, reverently and joyfully arrives at Thiru-Nallur. Upon arriving at Thiru-Nallur and worshipping the Peruman there, as he rises, Lord Shiva graciously declares, “We shall fulfill your desire,” and places His lotus feet upon the head of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar. Sekkizhar Swamigal sings this history as follows: “Kovai mudigi” (When the Lord, as death, comes to torment before the flowery feet are placed upon my head, as I pleaded, ‘Place them upon my head,’ and sang the Pathikam with my tongue, the Lord Himself, saying, ‘Come to Nallur,’ bestowed His grace. The devotee, Vaageesar, reverently and joyfully, following the path of great goodness, arrived at Thiru-Nallur and remained there.) When he worshipped and rose joyfully, Lord Shiva placed His lotus feet upon his head, saying, “We shall fulfill your desire.” This is what Sekkizhar Peruman states in these two sacred verses.

The Lord Shiva graciously says, “Come to Nallur,” at Thiru-Sathimuttam. The repetition of “Come” twice here signifies the abundance and certainty of His grace.

Similarly, in the sacred history of Sundaramurthi Swamigal, in the Purana of Thaduthatkonda, when Sundaramurthi Swamigal was worshipping Nataraja Peruman in Thillai, Lord Shiva called him to come to Thiruvarur.

Likewise, He graciously commanded Manikkavasagar Swamigal to come to Thillai.

Similarly, here at Thiru-Sathimuttam, Lord Shiva calls Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, who had petitioned for the sacred lotus feet of Lord Shiva to be placed upon his head, saying, “Come to Nallur!” Lord Shiva, a supreme divine flame transcending time and space, is present everywhere, shining in Thiru-Sathimuttam and Thiru-Nallur. When such a Lord Shiva graciously commanded, “Come to Nallur!”, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar came to Thiru-Nallur, worshipped the Peruman, and as he rose, the Lord graciously placed His sacred lotus feet upon the head of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, saying, “We shall fulfill your desire.” Placing the lotus feet upon the head is a form of initiation (Thiruvadi Deekshai). This is performed after Gnana Deekshai and is also known as Sambhavi Deekshai. “Sevadi Kanam Sen...” ...“Manni Thigazhume” is from Thiruvasagam. Just as the Lord, in the form of a Guru, came and bestowed grace upon Manikkavasagar Peruman, the sage of Thiru-Vathavur, similarly, the Lord, who came as a Guru, placed His sacred feet upon the head of Manikkavasagar Swamigal.

In accordance with the manner in which Sundaramurthi Swamigal was forcefully taken into service, when Sundaramurthi Swamigal was staying in the Siddhavadam Matham, the Lord Himself came and performed the Thiruvadi Deekshai for Sundaramurthi Swamigal. In this sacred verse, Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal as “Mannu Thiruthondar” (the steadfast sacred devotee). “Mannum Thiru” are epithets that signify the greatness and imperishability of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar’s devotion to Shiva and his greatness as Vaageesar. Previously, he was a Gnana Thiru-Munivar ...who performed penance as Vaageesa Munivar. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, later, came here as Thiru-Navukkarasar and served for many days by singing garlands of sacred verses.

After this, finally, becoming the very form of pure Shivanantha Gnana, he continues to perform sacred service even while seated beneath the sacred feet of Lord Shiva. Because this sacred service is blessed in all three times (past, present, and future), Sekkizhar Peruman uses the epithet “Mannu” (steadfast). And because the sacred service he performed leads to liberation, he uses the epithet “Thiru” (sacred).

Thus, Lord Shiva, in Thiru-Nallur, places His grace upon the head of Thiru-Navukkarasar. “He placed His sacred feet, which were wet, upon my head,” thus, the holy one, praising with the composed Thiru-Thandagam, and remembering His grace ...and melting with devotion, falling and rising, filled with joy, and like one who has received immense, inexhaustible wealth, his heart blossomed,“ sings Sekkizhar Peruman. “He placed His sacred feet, which were wet, upon my head,” thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar now composes the Thiru-Thandagam Pathikam and praises the Lord. Remembering the immense grace bestowed upon him by Lord Shiva, the holy one, he melts with devotion, falls to the ground, then rises, filled with contentment and inner joy, and his heart blossoms. Just as a poor person would rejoice upon receiving inexhaustible wealth, so too does his heart blossom. In this verse, Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Lord Shiva as “Punithar” (the Holy One).

“Punithar” means one who is naturally free from attachments. “Punithar” also means one who purifies. One who possesses natural purity also possesses the power to purify. This is its meaning.

Thus, due to the history of Lord Shiva placing His sacred feet upon the head of Thiru-Navukkarasar in Thiru-Nallur, even today, in the Thiru-Nallur temple, the custom of placing the Lord’s sacred feet upon the heads of devotees continues.

Now, at this time, the Thiru-Pathikam sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar about the Peruman of Thiru-Nallur is the Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathikam. It is compiled as the fourteenth Thiru-Pathikam in the Sixth Thiru-Murai.

Now, that Thiru-Pathikam: Thiruchitrambalam. “He made the devotees who remember and melt with devotion to suffer (in separation), He made evil deeds disappear without remaining, He covered Himself with the skin of an enraged elephant, He placed the crescent moon, He placed the celestial beings, searching for gems and crowns...” ...He placed the flowers, blooming with honey, upon my head, those sacred feet, wet with nectar, are those of our Lord of Nallur, how good He is! He placed the golden, fragrant Konrai on His matted locks, He placed the tiger skin, He placed the water, He placed the battle-axe on His strong shoulders, He placed the earrings in His long ears, He placed the moon, He placed the part of the slender-waisted one, He placed the quiver of the god of love, He placed the sacred thread, He placed the sacred feet, full of goodness, upon my head, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is! He placed the blooming Konrai flowers on His matted locks, He placed the dense garland, He made the waves crash, He placed the cool Datura flower, He placed the snake, He placed the eye on His sacred forehead, He placed the bow, He placed the daughter of the mountain, He placed the sacred feet, known throughout the land, upon my head ...He placed them, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is! He graciously placed the bow, He placed the part of the one who was burned, He placed the waterfall on His matted locks, He placed the mountain as a bow, He placed Kailash, the mountain of the gods, He placed the gods, He graciously taught the four sages the Dharma, He placed the ashes of the burning ground, He placed the ascetics, He graciously placed His sacred feet upon my head, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is!

He made the three cities burn in the sky, He made the deeds of those who worshipped disappear, He placed the ascetics, He burned Kama with His eye, He placed the fragrant lotus flower, He placed Kailash, He placed the fierce path and the cool water together, He made the celestials, who worshipped the directions, shine and praise, He graciously placed His sacred feet upon my head, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is! He placed the seven worlds of suffering and disease, He placed life, He placed the path that life takes ...He placed the multitude of other celestials, He placed the Vedas of the celestials, He made the waning moon grow, He placed the path that does not allow anger, desire, and greed to flourish, He placed the ascetics, He placed the sacred feet of the good ascetics upon my head, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is! He made the opposing Vedas burn, He placed them on His jeweled crown, He made the beautiful body, filled with water, dance, He placed the eye on His forehead, He placed the abode, He made the waves of the river burn, He made the celestials worship His feet with devotion, He placed the fragrant lotus feet upon my head, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is! He placed the worlds with many oceans, He placed the small jewels, He placed the form, He placed the top of the serpent, He drank the poison, He placed the eight shoulders, He placed the water and fire in the earth ...He placed the wind, He placed them in the high sky, He placed them in the minds of those who thought, He graciously placed His sacred feet, full of goodness, upon my head, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is! He placed the two suns and moons in the sky, He placed the ten directions firmly on the earth, He stood and made the celestials worship His feet, He made the full and hidden meaning shine, He killed and made the cruel Yama tremble and flee, He placed His sacred feet, which are the refuge, He placed the bull, He graciously placed His sacred feet upon my head, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is! He placed the snake, the moon, and the waves in His matted locks, He placed the grace for all those who serve Him, He placed the ashes of the burning ground, He placed beauty, He made the powerful karmic disease disappear, He placed Uma on one side, He placed His sacred feet, which the celestials praise with joy, upon my head, our Lord of Nallur ...how good He is!

He placed the seven oceans with their rising waves, He placed the mountain with small jewels, He pressed a single toe upon the head of the one who lifted the mountain with his hand, causing him pain, and when he cried out, “O Lord!”, He graciously placed the sword and fame, He graciously placed His sacred feet, full of goodness, upon my head, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is!

In this Thiru-Pathikam of eleven sacred verses, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, remembering the grace of Lord Shiva in many ways, and melting with devotion, with a blossoming heart, has graciously composed this Thiru-Pathikam, saying, “By His good grace, the Lord of Nallur placed His sacred feet upon my head so that I might attain goodness.” We shall proceed with our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 387, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Having stayed in Thiru-Nallur for a long time, he performs many heartfelt Thiru-Thondus (sacred services) with his hands. He composes many garlands of Thevaram Tamil verses for the Lord.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar performs these sacred services, focusing not on living beings and the world, but on Lord Shiva, the God of gods. While he is doing so, he visits and worships the sthalams where Lord Shiva, the God with an eye on His forehead, resides, such as Thiru-Karugavur, Thiru-Avur, Thiru-Palaithurai, and others, sings Thevaram Pathikams there, and then returns to Thiru-Nallur. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, Karuga ...Sekkizhar Peruman sings that Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, having visited Thiru-Karugavur, Thiru-Avur, Thiru-Palaithurai, and other places where the Lord with the eye on His forehead resides, and having worshipped there, performs abundant and ardent sacred service, and serves with a melting heart, never leaving Thiru-Nallur for a moment.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar departs from Thiru-Nallur, reaches the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Karugavur, and there praises the Lord and sings a Thiru-Pathikam. Thiru-Karugavur sthalam is located south of Thiru-Nallur, on the south bank of the Vettaru, a river that flows like a canal. This sacred sthalam is known by names such as Mullai Vanam, Madhavi Vanam, Karugavur, and Karppapuri. This sthalam is the eighteenth sthalam on the south bank of the Cauvery. The sacred name of the Lord of Thiru-Karugavur is Karppapureeswarar, Mullaivananathar, Madhavi Vaneswarar. The sacred name of the Goddess is ...Karumbanaiyal Ammai, Karpparakshambikai, Karukkakkum Nayaki.

The sacred waters are Brahma Theertham, Ksheerakundam, Sathyakoopam, Vriddha Cauvery, etc. The sthala tree is the Mullai creeper. This sthalam is named Karugavur because the Goddess here medically protected the fetus of a helpless woman. Many women who suffer from frequent miscarriages and are distressed by childlessness come to this sthalam, worship the Lord and Goddess, fulfill their vows, and attain the blessing of good children. This is a notable miraculous event of this sthalam. Among the Pancha Aranya Sthalams, which are sacred sthalams on the south bank of the Cauvery, Thiru-Karugavur (Mullai Vanam), Avalivanallur (Padiri Vanam), Arathai Perumpali (Vanni Vanam), Thiru-Irumboolai (Poolai Vanam), and Thiru-Kollamboodur (Vilva Vanam) are the five sthalams.

These are called the Pancha Aranya Sthalams. Thiru-Karugavur, also known as Mullai Vanam, is one of them. It is said that those who worship these sthalams at dawn, noon, evening, and midnight, respectively, will attain all good things. The greatness of Thiru-Karugavur is described in the Sanatkumara Samhita of the Kshetra Vaibhava Kanda in the Skanda Purana, as narrated by Sanatkumara to Narada Muni. The sthala Purana states that if one, no matter where they are, desires to go to this sthalam, named Madhavi Vanam, and takes three steps, then with the first step, all their sins will be removed. With the second step, the celestial world will become theirs.

With the third step, they are assured of attaining Shiva Sayujyam. The sthala Purana states that if one merely thinks of Thiru-Karugavur, speaks of it, resides there, or sees it, or hears of its greatness, or passes through it to other towns, all evils will be removed, they will attain various enjoyments, and finally, it is certain that they will merge with the Lord’s sacred feet. The Karppaga Vinayagar and Nandhi Devar of this sthalam are self-manifested deities. In the Somaskanda arrangement, the Lord’s shrine is on the right, the Goddess’s shrine is on the left, and Murugan’s shrine is in the middle. Brahma, Gargya, Gautama, Gujathvajan, Sangakarnan, Nithruvar, Bheemasenan, Punyathvajan, Chandra, and others have worshipped here and received blessings.

The Lord residing in this sthalam is a Swayambhu Murthy. Appar Adigal praised Him as “the eye that appears before the world as a fetus.” Thiru-Gnanasambandar, in every verse, connects the greatness of this sthalam, named Mullai Vanam, and the glory of the Lord adorned with Mullai flowers, to the Mullai. The Goddess residing in this sthalam ...protected the fetus of Vedikai, the wife of Nithruvar, from a miscarriage caused by the curse of Urthuvapatha Maharishi, and gave form to the fetus.

Hence, she is known as Sri Karpparakshaki and Karpparakshambikai. It is said that those who have lived or worshipped in this sthalam from time immemorial do not experience premature births or labor pains. It is also said that no mothers have died with their fetuses in this sthalam. The Lord’s Lingam is made of earth (Prithvi). Only civet paste is applied to it. A scar from a Mullai creeper wrapped around it is visible on the Lord’s sacred body.

Abhishekam is performed only for the Avudaiyar. Mullai flowers are offered to the Lord daily. The sthala Purana states that those who come to this sthalam, bathe in the sacred waters, and worship will attain all good things. Thiru-Gnanasambandar ...Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal each sang one Thiru-Pathikam, so there are two Thiru-Pathikams for this sthalam. The name of this sthalam is mentioned in the Thiru-Pathikam verse of Oorthogai composed by Sundarar. The temple, with a beautiful appearance, faces east and is located in the middle of the village on the south bank of the Vettaru.

There are four streets surrounding the temple. Opposite the temple is a large sacred tank called Thiru-Parkulam. A Raja Gopuram with five tiers adds beauty to the temple. Sri Sarvasiddhi Vinayagar is present at the right entrance of the temple. After passing through the Raja Gopuram entrance, one can reach the first outer prakaram. To the south of the Gopuram entrance is the Thiru-Nandavanam (sacred garden), and to the north is the Vasantha Mandapam.

After passing through the second Gopuram entrance, one can reach the first prakaram. At the entrance, there are Vinayagar, the flagstaff, twin Nandis, and Balipeedams. To the south are the sixty-three Nayanmars and the nine Thogaiyadiyars. Next to them are the Santhanacharyars and Samayacharyars. In the southwest corner is Vinayagar. To the west, between the Lord’s shrine and the Goddess’s shrine, in a Somaskanda arrangement, is the shrine of Arumuga Kadavul, and next to it is the Mahalakshmi shrine.

To the north is the Chandeesar shrine. In the Garbhagriha Koshtams, to the south are Vinayagar and Dakshinamurthy, to the west is Ardhanareeswarar, and to the north are Brahma and Durga. The sthala tree, Mullai, is in the northern prakaram. In the northeast direction are the Yagasalai and the Sabha Mandapam in the form of a chariot for horse racing. In this mandapam are the Shiva Lingams worshipped by Nithruvar, Gargya, and Sangukarnan. We circumambulate, worship Vinayagar at the sacred entrance, and enter the temple.

In the Maha Mandapam are the Navagrahas, arranged according to Agamic rules, and the Nataraja Sabha. To the right of the temple is a separate Somaskanda Mandapam. Inscriptions of the sthala Thiru-Pathikams are installed. After worshipping Karppaga Vinayagar, upon entering the Ardha Mandapam, the Panchamurthies are present. With the Dvarapalakas guarding the entrance, Sri Mullai Vana Nathar resides in the Garbhagriha and bestows grace.

The Lord shines with a tall Lingam made of earth (Prithvi) and a scar from a Mullai creeper wrapped around it. Abhishekam is performed only for the Avudaiyar. Upon worshipping and coming out, in the first prakaram, on the way to the Ambal shrine, there is a sacred water body called Sathyakoopam and the Gautameswarar temple. Opposite, facing east, the Ambal temple shines as a separate temple with its own prakaram. Karukkatha Nayaki, as the mother who binds our thoughts, bestows grace. The historical painting of the sthalam is inscribed at the entrance.

Now, the Puranic story of this sthalam ...is as follows: Brahma Devar developed the ego of “I.” As a result, the act of creation did not succeed. In this sthalam, Brahma created a sacred water body in his name, bathed in it, worshipped Mullai Vana Nathar, regained the power of creation, and attained Sathya Lokam. The sage Gargya, who caused a merchant named Swarnadharan, who had wandered in the form of a ghost for twenty-one yugas for having cheated a Brahmin of his entrusted wealth, to bathe in the Ganges and other sacred waters, and finally in the Brahma Theertham of this sthalam, thereby enabling him to attain Devalokam. This same sage performed many renovation works in this temple. The history of the sage Nithruvar is the reason why the Goddess is named Karukkatha Nayaki. The sage Nithruvar lived a married life in this sthalam with a woman named Vedikai.

When the sage had gone to another town to perform a sacrifice, Urthuvadhava The sage Nithruvar came to the ashram. Vedikai, being heavily pregnant, was unable to rise and offer alms. Urdhvapathar, angered, cursed Vedikai, the heavily pregnant woman, with the disease of Rajayatchu. Due to the power of this curse, the woman’s fetus slipped and fell. Vedikai, in a swoon of sorrow, prayed to Mullai Vananathar.

The Lord filled the fetus in the Goddess’s ambrosial pot and commanded Kamadhenu to nurture the child.

The Lord said that if Vedikai bathed in Brahmateertham for one year and worshipped Him with red lotus flowers, the curse would be lifted. Nithruvar prayed to the Goddess for the boon that those living in this sthalam would not suffer from pregnancy pains, and received it.

From then on, those who worship in this sthalam do not experience miscarriage. The Goddess is known as Karukka tha Nayaki. As we have already seen, this sthalam has one Thiru-pathigam sung by Thiru-gnanasambandhar Peruman and one Thiru-pathigam sung by Appar Swamigal, making a total of two Thevara Thiru-pathigams.

Additionally, this sthalam has sthala puranam, Pathittruppattu Andhadhi, Irattai Manimalai, Nan Manimalai, and other literary works.

Now, the Thiru-pathigam sung by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, who visited this sthalam, is compiled as the fifteenth Thiru-pathigam in the sixth Thirumurai.

Now, that Thiru-pathigam: Thiruchitrambalam. “Kurugam vairamam kooru naalang kollum kizhamaiyang kole thanam, Baruga amudhamam paalin neyyam pazhathin radhamam paattir pannam, Oru kaal umaiyaalor paaganumam ul nindra naavir kuraiyaadiyang karuvaai ulagukku munne thondrum kannang karugavoor” Enthai thane vitham mulaiyagum vere thanam vendum uruvamam virumbi nindra patham adiyarkor pangunam paal niramam paramjothi thanam thotham amararganam soozhndhu potra thondradhu en ullathin ulle nindra katham adiyerku kaanagattum kannang karugavoor enthai thane poothanam poovin nirathanamam pookuzhal vasamam manni nindra kothanam kolvalaiyal kooranagum konda samayathar devanagi ethathatharku endrum idare thunbam eevanam en nenjathu ulle nindru kaathanam kaalan adaiyavannam kannang karugavoor enthai thane iravanam elli nadamadiyam en thisai kunthevanam enuzhanam aravanam allal aruppanumam akasa moorthiyam aaneru erum kuravanam kootrai udhaithan thanam kooratha vanja kuyalarkku endrum karavanam katchikku ezhiyanumam kannang karuvoor enthai thane padaithanam paarai idanthanamum parisu ondru ariyama nindran thanam udaithanam onnar purangal moonrum ol azhalal mootti orukki nindru adaithanam soolam mazhuvor nagam asaithanam aaneru ondru oornthanamum kadaithanam kallam arivar nenjil kannang karugavoor enthai thane moolanam moorthiyam munne thanam moovatha meni mukkinanam Seelanar sernthar idargal theerkkum selvanar senjudarkor sothithanam malanam mangaiyor baganamam mandradiyam vanorthangarkellam kalanam kalanai kaynthanagum kannang karugavoor enthai thane araiser aravanam alathanam adhirai nalanam andavanor thiraiser thirumudi thingalanam theevinai nasan en sinthaiyanam uraiser ulagathar ullanumam umaiyalorbaganam velik karaiser kadal nanjai undanagum kannang karugavoor enthai thane thudiyan thodiyin muzhakkathana sollvar sollallam sothippanam padi thanam pavam aruppanamum paal neetranam paramjothi thanam kodiyan nang kootrai udhaithanagum kooratha vanjak paani payindran thanam etturuvam moorthiyam en tholanam ennuchi melanam embiranam katturuvam kadiyanai kaynthanagum kannang karugavoor enthai thane poruthirundha pullurvan ullanagi ulliruthangu ulnoi
