This is the Thiru-thandagam Thiru-pathigam bestowed by Appar Swamigal upon the Thiru-karugavoor sthalam.

We shall continue our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part Three Hundred Eighty-Eight. Thirunindrachcharukkam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped at Thiru-karugavoor and bestowed the Thiru-thandagam Thiru-pathigam, reaches the sthalam known as Thiru-avoor Pasupatheeswaram. Avoor is the name of this village, and Pasupatheeswaram is the name of the holy temple.

This holy place shines as a Maadakkoil (temple built on an elevated platform). It is the sthalam where the divine cow Kamadhenu worshipped, hence the name A-voor (cow’s village). This village also bears the sacred name Ashwathavanam. The vimanam (tower above the sanctum) where the Lord resides is called Manikkoodam because it has a beautiful mountain peak. It is said that Govandakkudi, near this village, is the place where Kamadhenu came to this earthly world from Thiru-kailayamalai. It is said that one of the two mountain fragments brought by Vayu Devan from Thiru-Kailayamalai settled in Nalloor and the other in this village.

The Vinayagar located in the southwest direction of this sthalam is called Niruthi Vinayagar. Murugan appears here as a spear-wielding warrior. The Lord’s name here is Pasupatheeswarar, a Swayambhu Murthy. He is the leader of Kamadhenu, the cow, and all living beings, hence He is called Pasupatheeswarar.

The Lord is also known by the sacred names Ashwatha Vananathar, Avoor Udaiyar, and Pasupatheeswara Udaiyar. There are two Amman shrines in this temple. One is the shrine of Arulmigu Mangalambikai. It is said through oral tradition that this deity was taken from the holy tank and consecrated. The other is the shrine of Pangajavalli, which is the ancient Amman shrine. Pangajavalli Pangaiya Mangai Virumbum Avoor (Avoor desired by the lotus maiden) is how this Amman is referred to in Thevaram.

The sthala tree is the Arasamaram (peepal tree). The thirthams are Brahmateertham, Kamadhenu Theertham, Chandra Pushkarani, Agni Theertham, and Poigaiyaru, a branch of the Kudamurutti river. There is a Thevara Thiru-pathigam for this sthalam, sung and worshipped by Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman. There is a sthala history written by Panchanatham Pillai.

Now, the puranic story of this sthalam is as follows: Once upon a time, Sage Vasishta performed a Vajapeyam yagna. For this, he collected materials and invited many sages and Brahmins. He intended to invite Kamadhenu to provide milk for the yagna.

However, Kamadhenu was in Brahmalokam with the Devas and could not come. Vasishta became angry. The sage cursed Kamadhenu. Knowing this, Sage Narada came to Vasishta and spoke of Kamadhenu’s greatness and the sin Vasishta incurred by cursing Kamadhenu. He told the sage that his sin would be absolved if he went to Thiru-vayaaru, bathed in Surya Pushkarani, and worshipped Jappeswarar. Kamadhenu, in the form of a cow, came to this village, Ashwathavanam, worshipped, and after her curse was lifted, provided the necessary assistance to Vasishta.

Kamadhenu, having come from Brahmalokam, took the form of a cow, came to this sthalam, Ashwathavanam, bathed in Brahmateertham, offered milk to the Lord for abhishekam, removed impurities with her tongue, and worshipped in various ways. She created and worshipped a separate Lingam and Theertham. The Lord, accompanied by Mangalavalli, appeared in a divine vision on a Rishabha Vahanam on the Chithirai Amavasai day.

Thus, because Kamadhenu worshipped here, this sthalam came to be known as Avoor Pasupatheeswaram. Dasaratha has visited this sthalam, worshipped, and performed renovations.

King Dharmadhwajan’s leprosy was cured at this site.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman visited Avoor Pasupatheeswaram, which possesses many such glories, worshipped, and bestowed Thiru-pathigams. However, due to our lack of merit, those Thiru-pathigams are not available to us now. Having worshipped Avoor Pasupatheeswaram in this manner, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar reached the sthalam called Thiru-palai-thurai and worshipped the Lord there. The holy sthalam of Thiru-palai-thurai is also nearby. It received this name because it was formerly a desert. The history of this sthalam is that Lord Shiva killed a tiger, flayed its skin, and wore it.

This sthalam is located between Kumbakonam and Thanjavur, This sthalam is the nineteenth sthalam among the Kaveri South Bank sthalams. It is located on the banks of the Kudamurutti river, with the palm tree as its sthala tree. That is also why it is called Palai-thurai. The temple faces east. In front of the temple, on the south side, there is a holy tank. The ancient temple has a five-tiered Rajagopuram, followed by an outer prakaram.

Near the gopuram entrance, there is a granary for storing paddy for the temple. This massive granary, built of brick, capable of storing eleven thousand kalams of paddy, is awe-inspiring. It indicates that at one time, this temple had such a large income.

However, today it is not in use. In the northeast corner is the yagasalai, and in the southeast corner, are the Thirumadaippalli (temple kitchen). In this sthalam, the Lord and Goddess appear in their wedding attire. The Goddess is on the right side. In the outer prakaram, there is a separate shrine for the Goddess. The Nandi and Balipitam are here.

To the north of this is the Vasantha Mandapam. Vinayagar is at the gopuram entrance. Upon entering, one finds the Mahamandapam. In the northern part of this mandapam, Lord Nataraja faces south. Opposite, on the south side, are the four Samayacharyas. In the western prakaram, there is a very beautiful stone mandapam.

There are mandapams where deities such as Vinayagar, Somaskandar, Murugan, Vasishta Lingam, and Mahalakshmi reside. In the northern prakaram, sixty-three Nayanmars are enshrined. In the garbhagriha koshtams are Nardana Vinayagar, Oordhuva Thandavar, Dakshinamurthy, and on the west, in the place of Lingodbhavar, is Ardhanareeswarar. In the northern prakaram are Brahma, Durga, and Chandeswarar. One can circumambulate and reach the Ardhamandapam. With two guards, Dvarapalakas, on either side, Palai Vananathar shines.

One can worship Him and then come to the outer prakaram and reach the Amman temple to worship. The Lord’s sacred name here is Palai Vananathar. The Goddess’s sacred name is Thavalaven Nagaiyal, meaning ‘she with white teeth’. The local people call the Amman Thavalambal. Theerthams include Vasishta Theertham, Indra Theertham, Yama Theertham, and Kaveri. The sthala tree is the Palai tree.

This holy sthalam is mentioned as one of the seven Sapthasthanams belonging to Thiru-nalloor. Thirumal, Brahma, the Ashta Dikpalakas, and others have worshipped this sthalam. The Thiru-pathigam composed by Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman is not available to us, though he worshipped this sthalam and left. During their exile, the Pandavas, on the advice of Sage Dhaumya, worshipped the Lord of this sthalam, understood the intricacies of archery, went to the netherworld, married Princess Ulupi there, and returned. This is the puranic history. The sages of Tharukavanam, disregarding Lord Shiva, performed a malevolent yagna to destroy Him, creating a tiger and sending it against Lord Shiva.

The Lord flayed the skin of that tiger at this sthalam and wore it. In the Kritha Yuga, unable to bear the cruelty of Bandasuran, the Devas performed a great yagna at this sthalam. The Mother appeared and destroyed Bandasuran.

The Lord pacified the heat of the sacrificial fire created by the Devas with the waters of the Ganga. The sacrificial pit itself became a Theertham. In the Dvapara Yuga, this sthalam was known as Punnagavanam. The mountain The sage Kala, having been insulted, became a bear. Following the command of Sage Agasthya, he came to this sthalam, bathed in the Kaveri, regained his true form, celebrated the Lord’s wedding festival with joy, and then went to Madurai. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar came to this sthalam and bestowed the Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathigam.

In the Thiruvasagam Keerthi Thiru Agaval, Manikkavasaga Swamigal sang, “Andharathu ezhindhu vandha azhagamar palaiyul sundaraththanmaiyodu thuthaindhu irundhu aruliyum” (Having risen in the sky, in the beautiful Palai, with beautiful nature, having been immersed and bestowed grace). There is one Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathigam bestowed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal upon this sthalam. It is a very special Thiru-pathigam. This Thiru-pathigam proves that the Thirumurais bestowed by the three (Sambandhar, Appar, Sundarar) are the Tamil Vedas. It is customary to refer to the Vedas as Thrayi, and that Thrayi The Panchaksharam shines as the central jewel in the Yajur Veda, which is in the middle of the Vedas called Thrayi. We know that the Panchaksharam shines in the middle of Sri Rudram.

Similarly, the Thevarams of the three, namely Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, and Sundaramurthy Swamigal, are called Tamil Vedas. Just as the Panchaksharam shines in the middle of the three Vedas - Rig, Yajur, and Sama - similarly, the Panchaksharam shines as the central jewel in the Thirumurais bestowed by the three great ones. The Thevarams sung by the three - Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, and Sundaramurthy Swamigal - are compiled as seven Thirumurais, namely one, two, three, four, five, six, and seven respectively. Among them, the central jewel is the fourth, fifth, and sixth Thirumurais bestowed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal. Among these three Thirumurais, the central jewel is the fifth Thirumurai. In this fifth Thirumurai, one hundred and one Thiru-pathigams shine.

Among these one hundred and one Thiru-pathigams bestowed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, the central Thiru-pathigam, shining as the fifty-first Thiru-pathigam, is the Thiru-palai-thurai Thiru-pathigam. Mostly, Appar Swamigal’s pathigams have ten verses, but this Thiru-pathigam has eleven verses.

Therefore, in the verse that shines as the central jewel among these eleven verses, that is, in the sixth verse, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal has sung the pure Panchaksharam. In the sixth verse, which shines as the central jewel, there are four lines, and in the second line, at the end, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal has placed that pure Panchaksharam.

Therefore, this Thiru-pathigam serves to prove that the Thirumurais bestowed by the three are the Tamil Vedas.

Now, that Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathigam is as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. “Neelamaamani kandaththar neezh sadai kolama madhi gangaiyum koottinaar soolamaan mazhu endhi sudar mudi paal nei aaduvar palaiththuraiyare kavalamam kazhitrin uri porththavar thavalavennagai mangaiyor panginar thivalavaanavar potri thisai thozhum pavalameyniyar palaiththuraiyare minnin nun nidai kanniyar mikku engum ponni neer moozhgi potri adithozha manni naanmaraaiyodu palkeedhamum panninaar avar palaiththuraiyare needu kaadu idamai nindra pey ganang koodu bhootha” kuzhumi nindrarkave aadinar azhagagiya naanmarai paadinar avar palaiththuraiyare siddhar kanniyar devargal thanavar piththar naanmarai vedhiyar peniya aththane namai aaludaiyay enum paththarkku anbar palaiththuraiyare. Next is the sixth Thiru-padal: “Venninar panindheththa viyappurum manninarr maravathu sivaya endru enninarkku idama ezhil vanagam panninar avar palaiththuraiyare.” As we have already seen, in this central Thiru-padal, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar has sung the pure Panchaksharam ‘Sivaya’. Just as the Vedas, called Thrayi, honor the name of Shiva in their heart, so too, in the Thevaram of Nayanar Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, which is central among the Thevarams of the three, and which is central to In this Thirumurai, which is central, in this fifty-first Thirupathigam, which is central, in this Thirupadal, which is central, we can see the divine arrangement where the Shiva Moolamantra ‘Sivaya’ shines as the central jewel in the second and third lines. Continuing the Thirupathigam: “Kuravanar kodu kottaiyum kokkarai viravinar pan kezhumiya veenaiyum maruvu naan malar malligai senbagam paravu neer ponni palai thuraiyare thodarum thondarai thukkam thodarnthu vandhu adarum potharu aranai arul seybavar kadalin nanjani kandavar kadipunar padarum senjadai palai thuraiyare megam thoybirai sooduvar megala nagam thoyndha arayinar nalliyal bogam thoyndha punarmulai mangaiyor bagam thoyndhavar palai thuraiyare vengaan vazhara vaatti veruttuvar anganar adiyarkku arul na nalkuvar sengaanmalayan thedarkku ariyavar paingannetrinar palai thuraiyare uraththinaal arakkan uyar maamalai nerukkinanai neriththu avan paadalum irakkama arul seytha palai thurai karaththinaal thozhuvar vinai oyume Thiruchitrambalam. This is the Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathigam, special for having the Sundarapanchaksharam at its center, bestowed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman upon the Thiru-palai-thurai sthalam.

“Our contemplation shall continue.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 389, Thirunindra Charukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, having departed from Thirunallur, visited Thiru Karugavur, Thiru Avur, Thiruppalaithurai, and other holy places, and then returned to Thirunallur. Sekkizhar Peruman sings, “Having worshipped Karugavur and other places where the Lord with the eye on His forehead resides, and having performed great Thiru-thondus with overflowing devotion, he returns to Thirunallur, never parting from it, and worships with an inner melting heart.” He sings that Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, having visited and served all the previously mentioned holy places, also worships Thirunallur without ever parting from it. The three holy places mentioned earlier, and others, are located within a few hours’ travel from Thirunallur. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, who regularly worships these places, would stay in Thirunallur, perform his services, visit these places, and then return to Thirunallur to worship the Lord there.

This is understood to be his practice of Thiru-thondar. Even if he visited and worshipped other places, he never forgot the great grace of the Lord of Thirunallur, who placed His holy feet on Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar’s head, always keeping it in his mind and worshipping with devotion. Earlier, when he visited Thiruchitrambalam, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal worshipped Thiru Vetkalam, Thiru Kal- Palai and other holy places, and then, remembering the Lord of the Dance whose temple is the mind of those who remember Him, he sang, “Will I ever forget Him for even a moment and be saved?” and returned to Thillai to worship.

Similarly, here, having departed from Thirunallur, he visited all the nearby holy places and then returned to Thirunallur to worship. Having served for a long time in this manner, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, having received the grace of the Lord who owns him, departs from Thirunallur and goes to the holy place called Thiruppazhanam. Sekkizhar Swamigal’s Thiru-padal states, “Having received the grace of his Lord, he departed and reached Thiruppazhanam, where there are banana groves and water-filled fields, and he was blessed to worship the feet of the Lord with the dark throat, adorned with ornaments, who dances in the long night.”

Here, the holy place Thiruppazhanam is described as “Vazhaipai Punar Pazhana Thiruppazhanam” (Thiruppazhanam with banana groves and water-filled fields). This description clarifies the meaning of the place name “Pazhanam.” This reminds us of Sekkizhar Peruman’s earlier singing about Thiru Amur, where Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar incarnated, as “Thiru Amur, Thiru Amur.” It also reminds us of his singing “Selva Needur, Thiru Needur.” Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, with a melting heart, worships the incomparable temples where Lord Shiva joyfully resides in the holy places surrounding Thiruppazhanam. The holy places surrounding Thiruppazhanam include Thiruppullamangai, Thiruchakkarappalli, and other holy places.

However, for these places, Thiru-Nava- The Thiru-pathigams sung by him are not available. We can consider the special features of these places later.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, who had clearly understood the true essence, arrives at Thingalur, the village of Apputhi Adigal, who possessed indescribable glories. Sekkizhar Peruman sings, “The King of Tongues, who sought the true essence, arrived at Thingalur, the village of Apputhi Adigal, who possessed indescribable glories, and worshipped with a melting heart in the incomparable places where righteousness rejoices in the holy places surrounding that village.” In this Thiru-padal, Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar as “the King of Tongues who sought the true essence.” “Meypporul Ther” means knowing and experiencing Lord Shiva, who is the true essence. This signifies a state of being. Jivanmuktas always look at the Supreme Being; they do not look at material things. Jivanmuktas see only Shiva, as stated in Sivagnana Siddhiyar.

Accordingly, the state of knowing and experiencing Lord Shiva, who is the true essence, is the state of Jivanmuktas. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman is such a great being who seeks the true essence. Even such Jivanmuktas worship Shiva temples as Shiva Himself. Why do Jivanmuktas, who have cleansed themselves of the anava mala, worship in this manner? It is to remove the vasana mala and to guide other souls.

Thus, Jivanmuktas see temples as a fortress and worship them. They live in this world with an uninterrupted awareness of Shiva’s meditation.

Thus, the phrase “meypporul ther” (seeker of the true essence) contains profound philosophical meanings. Sekkizhar Peruman uses this phrase here to describe Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, the king of tongues. Apputhi Adigal Nayanar is a devotee who lives by worshipping the holy name of Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, the king of tongues, as a mantra, and performs charities and worship in that name, the name of Thirunavukkarasar. He is one who has given the holy name of Thirunavukkarasar to all his children and everything else.

Thus, to indicate the name Thirunavukkarasar, which Apputhi Adigal embraced, Sekkizhar Peruman in this song refers to him as “Navinukku Ve-” In this song, Sekkizhar Peruman refers to him as “Navinukku Ve-” (King of Tongues). Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar arrives at Thingalur, the village where Apputhi Adigal, of indescribable glory, lives. Sundaramurthy Swamigal, in his Thiruthonda Thogai, in this very Thirunindra Charukkam, has sung about Apputhi Adigal, saying, “A Nambi, I am a servant of Apputhi Adigal.” In accordance with Sundaramurthy Swamigal’s statement, “A Nambi, Apputhi,” Sekkizhar Peruman here refers to him as “Apputhi Adigal of indescribable glory.” Sundaramurthy Swamigal sang, “A Nambi, Apputhi.” Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar sang about Apputhi Adigal in his Thevaram. Sekkizhar Peruman also sang the holy history of Apputhi Adigal as the Apputhi Adigal Nayanar Puranam.

Thus, the depth of Apputhi Adigal’s love and his glories are indescribable, and therefore Sekkizhar Peruman sings of him as “Apputhi Adigal of indescribable glory.” Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, having departed from Thiruppazhanam, arrives at Thingalur, where such an Apputhi Adigal Nayanar lives. Thingalur is one of the Thevaram Vaipu Sthalams, a village very close to Thiruppazhanam. The Lord’s name here is Kailasanathar, and the Goddess’s name is Periya Nayaki. The Vilva tree is the Sthala Vriksham, and Chandra Pushkarani is the Theertham. It is here that Apputhi Adigal Nayanar, with great devotion to Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, performs many charitable works in the name of Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar. In the Puranam of Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, at this point, that is, from the 201st Thiru-padal Up to the 210th Thiru-padal, in ten Thiru-padals, Sekkizhar Peruman sings in the Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam about Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar going to Apputhi Adigal’s house, and while he was there to partake of the holy food, Apputhi Adigal’s son was bitten by a snake.

Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar then laid Apputhi Adigal’s son, who had been bitten by the snake, in front of the Thingalur temple and sang Thevaram, and Apputhi Adigal’s son came back to life. Sekkizhar Peruman sings this history in these ten songs. Sekkizhar Peruman sings this history in detail in forty-five songs in Apputhi Adigal’s Puranam. In this Thirunindra Charukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Sekkizhar Peruman sings.

Here, when this part of Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar’s history comes, Sekkizhar Peruman sings it briefly in ten songs. What was sung briefly in this Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam is expanded upon in the Apputhi Adigal Nayanar Puranam, and parts that were sung briefly in the Apputhi Adigal Nayanar Puranam are expanded upon in the Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. This is a unique characteristic of Sekkizhar Peruman, to shorten and expand the same story in different places as needed.

We will continue to contemplate the history of Apputhi Adigal in the history of Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 390, Thirunindra Charukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. In Thingalur, Apputhi Adigal Nayanar, along with his son, establishes many charities such as roads, wells, ponds, and water-sheds, all in the holy name of Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, who is called “Andavar Arasu” (the Lord King), and performs holy service there. Sekkizhar Peruman sings, “The exalted Brahmin Apputhi Adigal, with his son, established many charities such as roads, wells, ponds, and water-sheds in the name of Andavar Arasu, and when Vakkisar (Thirunavukkarasu) heard of this and arrived, he entered their good home.” Sekkizhar Peruman praises Apputhi Adigal Nayanar as “the exalted Brahmin Apputhi Adigal.” The word “Andanar” means one who reaches the end. Just as it is stated in the twelfth sutra of Sivagnana Bodham, “Shiva is the end,” “Andanar” means one who reaches the end.

“Antam” is Vedanta, and “Antatara” is Siddhanta.

Therefore, in this context, “Andanar” refers to one who reaches the end, signifying the Saiva Siddhanta, which is the clear Vedanta. What does it mean to reach the end? It means to attain the perfection of wisdom and the descent of divine power, which are the ultimate states of Saiva Siddhanta. Even while bearing the body as long as the Prarabdha karma lasts, and living in the world until then, it means to consider the holy form and the Shiva temple as the ultimate reality, worship them, and live immersed in them.

Here, “exalted Brahmin” The meaning is that Apputhi Adigal Nayanar is one who has matured and stands firm in that understanding. We can learn this from the subsequent songs composed by Sekkizhar Peruman, such as “You are the form of overflowing compassion” and “You spoke thus with the auspicious holy form.” Furthermore, here, “Andanar” not only means one who reaches the end but also, by implication, refers to the first varna, the Brahmin.

Therefore, we also learn that Apputhi Adigal Nayanar belonged to the Brahmin varna, the first varna. Apputhi Adigal performs holy services with his sons. “Tanaiyar” means children. Apputhi Adigal Nayanar is one who has named his children Thirunavukkarasu and lives accordingly. What holy services did he perform with his sons? He built roads, planted shade-giving trees on both sides of the roads for the benefit of travelers, made the roads even, and provided many other facilities.

He established many charitable institutions and performed services. He built wells, which are small bodies of water from which water can be drawn.

Similarly, he created ponds and performed holy services. A pond is a large body of water where one can directly descend and draw water. This pond benefits not only people but also other creatures. If “kulam” (pond) is taken to mean “vellam” (flood), then “kulantharu thanneer” (water from the pond)

Here, it means water mixed with floodwater, and he distributes panakam (a sweet drink). In the water-sheds, he distributes panakam along with water to the people. He has wells and ponds where people can go and draw water.

But in the water-sheds, he brings water for the people and distributes it there. Not only that, since it is a cool water-shed, there are facilities for those who need rest on their journey to stay there for a while. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, the Vakkisar, sees all these charitable works when he comes to Thingalur. Not only that, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar also hears about Apputhi Adigal Nayanar’s other charitable deeds from everyone else. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar thus learns about them. When Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar arrived at Thingalur, Apputhi Adigal Nayanar, with great joy, came with his wife, children, and large retinue, met Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, worshipped him, rose, circumambulated him, and bowed.

He requested Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar to partake of food in his holy home. Sekkizhar Peruman, who briefly sang these events in the Thirunavukkarasu Peruman Puranam, sings in detail about Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar’s arrival in Thingalur and his visit to Apputhi Adigal Nayanar’s holy home in ten songs, from the ninth to the eighteenth, in the Apputhi Adigal Nayanar Puranam. Since he sang in detail there, he sings briefly here. Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal approaches Apputhi Adigal’s holy When Apputhi Adigal heard that a devotee had arrived, he came out and worshipped.

Then Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal asked why he performed charitable deeds in the water-sheds and other charitable institutions without writing his own great name, but instead used another name, namely Thirunavukkarasu. Apputhi Adigal then became angry and asked, “You call the holy name of Thirunavukkarasu, which is a sacred and pure name, another name? Who are you who do not know his greatness, the greatness of Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar?” To this, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal replied, “I am a humble one, devoid of understanding, who was taken into service by the Lord through the crucible of suffering.” Then Apputhi Adigal, filled with great joy, called his wife, children, relatives, and everyone else from inside, He worshipped and rose before the Nayanar. Sekkizhar Peruman has described all these events in great detail in the Apputhi Adigal Nayanar Puranam. Apputhi Adigal considered Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar as his object of meditation and his Guru. As a result of worshipping him as his object of meditation and Guru, he was greatly delighted to see Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal himself come to his holy home.

Apputhi Adigal Nayanar was enslaved by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman’s acts of grace, but he had not yet had the opportunity to see Thirunavukkarasu Peruman. That is why, when Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar came and asked, he thought he was another devotee and replied thus.

Now, hearing that the one who had come was indeed Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, he was greatly delighted and requested him to come to his holy home and partake of food.

Thus, when Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar arrived at Apputhi Adigal Nayanar’s holy home, Apputhi Nayanar, with great love, arranged for holy food and various kinds of curries, whatever was needed, with great affection and desire. He arranged for various kinds of curries, differing in taste and type. In accordance with the saying, “food in four ways, with six tastes,” he arranged the food items. He arranged the holy food to be suitable for Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, the Lord King, his Guru, to partake of, making it a pure and loving offering to the Guru. Apputhi Adigal Nayanar has sons, and he has named all of them He had named all of them after Thirunavukkarasu Peruman. While Apputhi Adigal was arranging the holy food for Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, Apputhi Adigal Nayanar called his eldest son, who was named after Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, to bring a banana leaf for Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar to partake of the holy food.

He called his eldest son, the elder Thirunavukkarasu, and instructed him to go to their home garden and cut a young banana shoot from a flourishing banana tree. He told him to cut a large banana leaf from a banana tree to serve the holy food to Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal. In this song, Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Apputhi Adigal Nayanar as “Anbutharu Gnana Thirumaraiyor” (the wise Brahmin who bestows love). Love here refers to love for God, love for Lord Shiva. If one has love for Lord Shiva, that love will manifest as devotion to Shiva’s devotees.

Thus, when Lord Shiva appears as the Guru, wisdom is realized through that Guru’s grace. This is Saiva Siddhanta. The wisdom mentioned here refers to Shiva-gnanam (divine wisdom). It is the fruit obtained through Sanmarga (the good path). In his commentary on the eighth sutra of Sivagnana Bodham, “My first Guru, who enlightened me through penance,” the teacher Meykandar Devar states that the primary purpose is to explain the method of realizing wisdom. We can reflect on these words here.

Apputhi Adigal Nayanar, the wise Brahmin, possessed such greatness. He was skilled in the Vedas, which are general scriptures, and also especially skilled in the Agamas.

Therefore, he was a great person who had attained the fourth stage of wisdom, which is known through the Agamas. And such a great person calls his eldest son, the elder Thirunavukkarasu, and tells him to bring a banana leaf. He tells him to bring a leaf from a flourishing banana tree. Although flourishing is a common characteristic of all banana trees, in the history of Apputhi Adigal Nayanar, this banana tree plays a role in the divine event that is about to occur, so it is specifically referred to here as “Vankathali” (strong banana). He tells him to pluck it. This means a young banana leaf that has not yet matured.

As soon as he said this, Apputhi Adigal Nayanar’s eldest son, the elder Thirunavukkarasu, goes quickly without delay. In Shiva’s holy service, Apputhi Adigal Nayanar Similarly, the eagerness of his elder son, Thiru-Navukkarasu, is mentioned here. It is stated that he went quickly and with great zeal. As the elder Thiru-Navukkarasu thus swiftly went to cut the beautiful tender banana shoot, a snake bit him. A snake bite means the snake’s fangs penetrate the body, injecting venom and causing harm. Due to this, harm befell the elder Thiru-Navukkarasu.

Before the severity of the poison ascended to his head and caused him to fall, the elder Thiru-Navukkarasu rushed back, eager to deliver the banana shoot. He entered the house and approached his mother.

At that moment, the virulent poison ascended to his head, and he fainted. He handed the fresh banana shoot he had brought to his mother’s hand, then weakened and fell. He fell without even mentioning that a snake had bitten him. Seeing the elder Thiru-Navukkarasu fall thus, his mother and father were greatly distressed and grieved. Why were they distressed? Why did they tremble?

Because they feared that this incident would hinder the sacred Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal from partaking of the sacred meal, and thus they were agitated. Concealing their son’s corpse, and without any mental agitation due to what had occurred, Appoothiadigal Nayanar Peruman and his wife came before Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar and stood in supplication, requesting, “Our Peruman, please partake of the sacred meal.” Their son had fallen and departed life. The news and the corpse of their son, which would convey it, were concealed.

Then, without mental agitation, they came before Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar and made their request to partake of the sacred meal. At that moment, by the divine grace of Lord Shiva, a perturbation arose in the pure sacred heart of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, the sacred devotee of Lord Shiva, the God of gods. What kind of person was Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar? He was one who possessed the steadfastness not to waver even if the sky were to fall, as he declared, “I shall not waver.” He was one who stood firm, stating, “There is nothing to fear, nor anything to cause fear.” Such was the pure sacred heart of the Nayanar. In that sacred heart, by the divine grace of Lord Shiva, a perturbation arose. Such a perturbation arising in great ascetics is the way the Lord enlightens them from within.

This is the method of enlightenment. As this perturbation arose, Appoothiadigal Nayanar then invited Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to partake of the sacred meal. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar asked for the elder son to be called to apply sacred ash to Appoothiadigal and his children. To this, Appoothiadigal replied, “He is not available here now.” Hearing Appoothiadigal say this, a perturbation entered the Nayanar’s pure sacred heart. When asked to speak the truth, Appoothiadigal narrated what had happened. Hearing this, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal said, “Well done, what you have done,” and bestowed immense compassion upon Appoothiadigal and his wife for their act of love in concealing their son’s corpse.

He then had the corpse brought before the sacred temple of Lord Shiva, who wears a fragrant matted lock adorned with a Konrai garland. He then sang the sacred Thiru-Pathigam beginning with “Ondru Kolam.” The fact that the son had fallen due to poison evoked immense compassion in Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s heart towards Appoothiadigal. More than that, their act of concealing it caused immeasurable compassion to blossom in the Nayanar’s sacred heart towards them. This compassion overflowed not for the son, nor for Appoothiar who had lost him, because these are all very natural occurrences in the world. In this world, death is natural for living beings; losing a son is also natural. All these are the Lord’s decree.

Therefore, a good teacher, a good Acharya, would not say, “I will try to revive all the dead,” or “I will prevent anyone from dying hereafter.” To attempt such would be the act of those ignorant of the Lord’s decree.

However, here, compassion greatly increased in the heart of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman; it was intensified and brought forth by the act of Appoothiadigal and his wife in concealing this matter. This was done out of their immense love for the devotees of Shiva.

Therefore, that act caused compassion to arise in the heart of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar. Even then, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman could have sung the Pathigam from Appoothiadigal Nayanar’s sacred home, and the Lord would have bestowed grace.

But he brought the body of the elder Thiru-Navukkarasu before the sacred temple. This is because that act was to make the world know that it occurred by the divine grace that bestows upon devotees the nature of the Lord’s own actions. It is to make the world know that it happens by the divine grace that bestows upon devotees the nature of the Lord’s own actions.

Therefore, he had the body brought before the sacred temple, outside the sacred walls, and there he sang the sacred Thiru-Pathigam beginning with “Ondru Kolam.” That sacred Thiru-Pathigam, starting with “Ondru Kolam,” proceeds through “Irandu Kolam,” “Moondru Kolam,” and so on, up to “Pathu Kolam,” being expounded in forty ways. As Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman thus bestowed the venom-curing sacred Thiru-Pathigam, “Ondru Kolam,” the elder Thiru-Navukkarasu, son of Appoothiadigal, arose as if waking from sleep. The risen elder Thiru-Navukkarasu bowed at the sacred feet of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and received and adorned himself with the sacred ash bestowed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar. The elder Thiru-Navukkarasu, having risen cured of the poison, first worshipped Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, not his own parents. This is because, when his life departed earlier, it was with the thought of serving Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and bringing banana leaves.

Now, upon rising, cured of the poison, as a continuation of that sacred devotion, he first bowed before Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman.

Thus, the truth is revealed to us here that, like Appoothiadigal Nayanar, his son also clung to the sacred feet of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. Sekkizhar Peruman Nayanar narrates the history of how he sang the hymn, saying, “Looking at the lifeless corpse, he sang the hymn with melodious verses, bestowing grace.” Even after witnessing their beloved son regain his life and rise, the minds of Appoothiadigal Nayanar and his wife were not relieved of their distress. For now, they were distressed and grieved that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman was delayed in partaking of the sacred meal.

Therefore, to alleviate their mental distress, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, the sacred sage Vageesar, went to Appoothiadigal’s sacred home, partook of the feast lovingly offered by them, and graciously blessed them there with pleasure. Let us go on contemplating. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 391. Thiru-Nindra Sarukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Due to the devotion of Appoothiadigal, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar stayed with him for some time in Thingu-Lur and then proceeded to the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Pazhanam, dedicated to Lord Shiva. Appoothiadigal also accompanied him up to Thiru-Pazhanam.

Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar greatly praised the exalted conduct of Appoothiadigal Nayanar. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having thus come from Thingu-Lur to Thiru-Pazhanam, sang the sacred Thiru-Pathigam of Thevaram, a garland of words, there. Thiru-Pazhanam is a sacred sthalam very close to Thingu-Lur. We saw that Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar had visited Thiru-Pazhanam before coming to Thingu-Lur.

Now, again, from Thingu-Lur, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar has set out and arrived at Thiru-Pazhanam. Sekkizhar Peruman states that he now sings the sacred Thiru-Pathigam, a garland of words. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman bestows the sacred Thiru-Pathigam beginning with “Sonmalai payilkindra kuyilinangal” at this sthalam. He describes it thus. Thiru-Pazhanam is one of the Sapthasthana sthalams of Thiru-Vaiyaaru. It is located on the way from Thiru-Vaiyaaru to Kumbakonam, on the northern bank of the Kaveri.

This sacred sthalam has been sung by Appar Swamigal and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. Five sacred Thiru-Pathigams sung by Appar Swamigal and one sacred Thiru-Pathigam sung by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, making a total of six sacred Thiru-Pathigams, are dedicated to this sthalam. The Lord’s name here is Aabathsahayar, and the Goddess’s name is Brihannayaki, also known as Periya Nayaki. It is a village surrounded by fields where sugarcane and paddy intertwine. It is a village surrounded by fields where sugarcane and paddy intertwine, hence it is named Pazhanam. This is the fiftieth sthalam on the northern bank of the Kaveri.

Vageesa Peruman has sung about these in Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar’s general Thiru-Thandagam. Vageesa Peruman visited this sthalam twice, before and after his visit to Thingu-Lur. In the Pathigam sung during his second visit, he has specially praised the devotion of Appoothi Nayanar. Sekkizhar Peruman also mentions that he sang a sacred Thiru-Pathigam here, praising Appoothiadigal. In this sacred Thiru-Pathigam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar has also glorified Appoothiadigal by singing about the Lord as “Anjippoi kali meliya azhal vombum Appoothi Kunjipoo-vai nindra sevadiyai.” The Thiru-Pazhanam Thiru-Pathigam is the twelfth Pathigam in the fourth Thiru-Murai.

Now, that Sacred Thiru-Pathigam.

“O cuckoos that practice garlands of words, tell me! He of Pazhanam, where many garlands of humming bees sing melodies, whose head is adorned with a crescent moon, whose chest bears a golden garland, will he not appear before me, my new beauty? O thorns, O lotuses, O screw-pines, O water-lilies! He of Pazhanam, whose dance is eternal, whose songs never cease, will he not know my tender hue, having taken it after I bathed in the pond where bees hum, and will he not heed me? O young heron of the riverbank, have you forgotten?

“He of Pazhanam, who wore the elephant’s hide, whom many sing of, will you not convey all my thoughts, O buzzing bee? Will she, with lotus-like eyes, not speak and languish?” “O new one, O sweet one, O fragrant breeze, is this not his abode, the cremation ground, he of Pazhanam, whom many sing of? He who honored the sacrifice of those who disrespected him, he who bears the Ganga, the one of destiny, has he ceased his sport upon my life? He who is the ultimate refuge for those who live on earth, for the great Brahmin ascetics, and for the gods in heaven, will I abandon him, the father of Pazhanam, who sings melodious songs, even when my eyes are closed? O red-legged white heron, that seeks food by going back and forth in the unagitated great ocean, I know not what to do.

“Will he, who stole my beautiful bangles, he of Pazhanam surrounded by beautiful groves, not bestow his beautiful, fragrant Konrai garland? O foolish heron, that embraces its mate and reaches the shore, he of Pazhanam, whose songs never cease, who wears the palm-leaf ornament, he whose chest is adorned with a pair of arrows that turned the mighty fortresses in the sky to dust, will he not appear before me, my beauty?” “O river Kaveri, that flows with pearls and gems, O Pazhanam, where the beautiful maiden’s mouth shines with pearls as she bathes!

“The Lord of the mountain daughter with coral lips, whose banner bears the bull, O parrot, O sweet-voiced one, is there no time left? He who bears the spotted deer and the speckled serpent, he of Pazhanam, where the Lord of the serpent couch is worshipped and praised, the world says he removes the karma of those who contemplate him. O foolish me, how can I abandon him, my husband? He who deceived and stole my bangles, will he not come? Even so, he of Pazhanam, where the cotton-footed cranes fly and cry out.” “He who protects the fire, so that Kali’s influence weakens and flees in fear, Appoothi, whose sacred feet are like a flower on the head, O Lord of Kodi!

“This sacred Thiru-Pathigam is composed in the Akapporul genre. It is structured as the lament of the heroine, remembering the hero with whom she united and then separated. Thiru-Pazhanam is a sacred sthalam filled with paddy fields.

“Accordingly, this entire Pathigam contains the inner meaning of ‘oodal’ (lovers’ quarrel), which is the proper theme for the Marutham landscape. The ‘karupporul’ (native elements) such as swans, cuckoos, herons, etc., are also present in this Pathigam. The heroine addresses them as ‘O cuckoo,’ ‘O young heron,’ ‘O fragrant breeze,’ ‘O heron,’ and so on, saying, ‘My Lord, Shiva, the Lord of Pazhanam, who once sported with my life and ruled me, has now separated from me! Has he abandoned me? Will Shiva, adorned with the Konrai garland, bestow his grace to console me, or will he not?’ Thus, the song is structured as the heroine’s lament. Cuckoos, fragrant breezes, herons, swans, etc., were all objects that aided in bringing joy when the hero and heroine were united.

“Therefore, the heroine addresses them, expressing both the sentiment of ‘oodal’ and ‘irangal’ (lamentation) in this sacred Thiru-Pathigam. We can also consider the references to the Thiru-Thonipuram Pazhanthakkaraga Pathigam, ‘Siraiyaru madakkiliye,’ here. In the first verse, he addresses the cuckoo, singing, ‘Sonmalai payilkindra kuyilinangal.’ This reminds us of the Thiru-Vasagam ‘Kuyil Pathu,’ ‘Geetham iniya kuyile.’” This reminds us of the Thiru-Vasagam ‘Kuyil Pathu,’ ‘Geetham iniya kuyile.’ Thus are the thematic notes of this sacred Thiru-Pathigam.

“We shall continue our contemplation.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 392. Thiru-Nindra Sarukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having worshipped Lord Shiva in Thiru-Pazhanam and sung sacred Thiru-Pathigams, then proceeded to Thiru-Sotrutthurai, a sacred sthalam, with the intention of performing the sacred service of worshipping all the sthalams where the Lord resides. Thiru-Sotrutthurai is the third sthalam among the Sapthasthana sthalams of Thiru-Vaiyaaru.

It is very close to Thiru-Pazhanam. Thiru-Sotrutthurai is the thirteenth sthalam among those on the southern bank of the Kaveri. This sacred sthalam has the glory of being sung by the three great saints. It is also known as Gautama Ashramam. History states that this sthalam protected all Shiva devotees who arrived during times of famine. It is said that the Lord bestowed an inexhaustible Akshaya Patra upon a saint here.

The sthala purana states that the Lord bestowed an inexhaustible Akshaya Patra upon a saint here. This sacred sthalam was worshipped by Indra, Surya, and others. The Lord’s names here are Othavaneswarar, Sotrutthurainathar, and Tholaiyachelvanathar. The Goddess’s names are Annapoorani and Tholaiyachelvi. The sthala tree is the Panneer tree. The sacred waters are the Kaveri Theertham and Surya Theertham.

Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, who visited this sthalam, has bestowed four sacred Thiru-Pathigams here. The first of these is the forty-first sacred Thiru-Pathigam in the fourth Thiru-Murai, composed as a Thiru-Nerisaithiru-Pathigam.

“I spent my time considering this body, filled with falsehoods, as real. I am not one whose mind is filled with truth, O Vedhiya, O Vedhana! I became weary, possessing this body tormented by the five senses. He is the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, whose righteousness is praised by the carp in the fields.” “Do not waste your time standing as bound ones.

“He who dances at night, swinging his eight arms, worship him with eight kinds of flowers. He who performs the five sacred dances, he is the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, who bestows grace as a perfect one. Those who lovingly praise the Lord, who shot three cities with a single arrow, day and night in solitude, those wealthy ones who wander with a skull in their hand, they are the good meaning of words, they are the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai. He who is the shore, he who has an eye on his forehead, he who has a woman as half of his body, he who is the Lord, he who is sweet, he who is unique, he who bears the cool white crescent moon, he who is the source of all deeds, he who is glorious, he who is the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, free from decay, entered and saw the weariness in my heart and bestowed his grace. I spent my time thinking of this body as real and enduring it.” “O my Father, O Unique Form, I cannot stand and praise you.

“He who is both bondage and liberation, he who is the Supreme, he who is like honey in the mind, he is the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai. Proclaim so that you may not be born again, the glory of the Lord who has a foolish woman as part of him, who bestowed grace upon Arjuna, the Pasupatha. He who received the Ganga, which descends with a roar, and made it a sacred water, he is the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai. Alas, I spent my time speaking of women with fragrant tresses, without praising the Lord who stands as my Father and my Master, the Primeval Being who keeps the beautiful-hipped one with him, he is the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, surrounded by red pollen. Do not consider the sun as the Lord. Prepare yourselves to follow the path of the fierce sun.

“The Primeval Being who keeps the sun with him, he is the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, whom the red sun worships.” “O people of the world, you spend your time reciting, but you do not contemplate the One with righteousness, nor do you call him the Pure One. He who is the Light that Brahma and Vishnu could not see, he who is the Effulgence, he is the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai. If you wish to spend your next life without attachment to other things, then proclaim the Lord by the means you have received. He who became angry and bestowed grace when the learned Ravana tried to lift this Mount Kailash, he is the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai.

“The thematic note of this sacred Thiru-Pathigam is as follows: ‘I spent my time considering this body, filled with falsehoods, as real, and speaking of women with fragrant tresses. I became weary.

“The Lord of Sotrutthurai saw the weariness in my heart and bestowed his grace. O people of the world, you stand as bound ones.’” } Do not waste time as I do, speaking of this and that, forgetting the Lord. If you still desire freedom from rebirth, if you wish to escape the cycle of existence, then day and night, in solitude, praise and worship the Lord. Adore Thiru-Sotrutthurai Peruman, thus sings Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman in the second Thiru-Pathigam for Thiru-Sotrutthurai, the eighty-fifth Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Viruttha Thiru-Pathigam.

““Rising in the morning, bringing fresh, pure flowers, the place desired by the celestial beings above, fragrant with groves, Thiru-Sotrutthurai, upon the matted locks of the Resident Lord, is not the crescent moon beautiful to our Peruman?” “The garland of bees, the Konrai, the Vanni, the Datura, and the living serpent.” Adorned and mounted upon the bull, the Lord with matted locks, to His feet, the devotees, having danced, reside in Thiru-Sotrutthurai. Upon His matted locks, is not the garland of white skulls beautiful to our Peruman? To measure the path, for the devotees who contemplate within their hearts, He illuminates, removes the karma of His devotees, the Lord of the celestials. Upon the matted locks of the Resident Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, adorned with swaying earrings, is not the dancing moon beautiful to our Peruman?

“With a serpent in His hand, mounted on a great bull, He dances among humans everywhere, with matted locks. Upon the matted locks of the Resident Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, adorned with fresh, great flowers, is not the upraised trident and axe beautiful to our Peruman? Having overcome Yama, having bound the fierce serpent, smeared with sacred ash, His wandering form, we do not know. Lying in the river, entangled and tossed, it seems to be. Upon the matted locks of the Resident Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, is not that pure moon beautiful? Those who speak with power, standing firm, even if fierce Asuras kill and crush, the celestials come and worship.

“The Resident Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, who speaks and practices, is not His stance, having wielded the bow, beautiful to our Peruman? We do not know His ancient form. He, who drew the bow of Kama, the destroyer of fortresses, and shot, the pure one with sacred ash, the Resident Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai. Upon His matted locks, is not the surging, white-foamed Ganga beautiful to our Peruman? The poison that arose when the celestials churned the ocean, He consumed and subdued it, the Lord of the mighty celestials. Upon the matted locks of the Resident Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, who practices devotion, is not the garland of the moon beautiful to our Peruman?

“The Lord of the ocean-hued Vishnu and the four-faced Brahma, whom they do not know, He with the blue throat, He is my Lord. Upon the matted locks of the Resident Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, who dances adorned with light, is not the hooded serpent beautiful to our Peruman?

“The Lord of Lanka, with twenty shoulders and heads, He pressed with His toe, causing him to tremble and lose his might. He with the shining axe, the Resident Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai. Upon His matted locks, is not the radiant moon beautiful to our Peruman?

“The sacred grove, desired by the celestials, fragrant with flowers, the Lord Shiva, who resides in Thiru-Sotrutthurai, is the king of the celestials who removes karma. He is smeared with sacred ash, capable of consuming and subduing poison, and holds an axe, thus this Thiru-Pathigam describes my Lord, Shiva, as having the beautiful crescent moon, the garland of white skulls, the upraised trident, the surging Ganga, the hooded serpent, and the stance of wielding the bow.

“Now, the third Thiru-Pathigam bestowed upon this sacred place, a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathigam, is found as the thirty-third Thiru-Pathigam in the Fifth Thiru-Murai.

““They who ride the bull, they who wear the fierce serpent, the Lord who resides in Thillai-Chitrambalam, the ancient Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, O foolish heart, serve Him with diligence!” “You have not performed any penance for liberation, you have not given anything to the devotees out of compassion. To the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, where flowers bloom in clusters, O foolish heart, serve Him with devotion!” “The clinging bodily ailments, the karmic bonds, the accumulated past deeds, may they all depart. To the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, who stands close, O foolish heart, serve Him with diligence!” “He is the beginning, He bestows grace upon the celestial beings, He is justice, He is ever pure, He is light. To the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, who is the beginning, O foolish heart, serve Him!” “You made me dance, You drove away my karma, You wear a young white earring in one ear. To the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, O foolish heart, serve Him with extended devotion!” “The poison of the ocean that surged and rose, tell me, is there any other deity who consumed it and kept it?

“To the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, O foolish heart, serve Him by clinging to Him!” “You are strong like a nail, see! Like a ladder, rising and sighing, to the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, who is a boat, O foolish heart, serve Him as an ornament!” “He rides the bull, what if ghosts dance? What if He wears a serpent in a anthill? To the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, O foolish heart, serve Him by clinging to Him!” “He who is the five-headed serpent, the one whom Brahma and Vishnu do not know, tell all these things. To the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, O foolish heart, serve Him by embracing Him!” “Having abandoned the quarrelsome and the powerless, the ignorant, to escape and attain salvation, having performed devotion. To the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, O foolish heart, serve Him by partaking!” “He who lived, He who pressed his toe, causing the mighty Ravana to cry out in pain.

“To the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, surrounded by the Bhootha Ganas, O foolish heart, serve Him by bowing down!” The essence of this Thiru-Pathigam is: “O foolish heart, always serve the Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai!” Now, the Thiru-Sotrutthurai The fourth Thiru-Pathigam bestowed upon the sacred place by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, the forty-fourth Thiru-Pathigam of the Sixth Thiru-Murai, is a Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathigam.

““He who is the eldest, prior to the world, He who creates all things in order, He who is praised, He who became the seven worlds, He who is bliss, He who removes sorrows, He who protects, He who sees all things, He who removes my severe karma, O Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, O radiant light, Shiva, I seek refuge in You!” “He who is the leader, the unique one for the world, He who is the truth, He who is sweet nectar to those who seek Him, He who is eternal, He who has no equal, He who, angered, attacked Yama who did not understand, He who killed, He who wore the skin of the fierce elephant, He who shot the three strong fortresses with His bow, O Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, O radiant light, Shiva, I seek refuge in You!” “He who wears the unripe crescent moon, He who is like the sprouting Kalpaka creeper, He who has no relatives, He who is the radiant light worshipped by the world, He who learned the Vedas, He who removed the disease of my unlearned karma, O Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, O radiant light, Shiva, I seek refuge in You!” “He who is the eye, He who protects all worlds, He who witnesses the ages and epochs, He who is the celestial, He who bestows grace upon the celestials, He who is Brahma, He who expounded the Vedas, He who is the thought, He who, before the three cities of the enemies could blink, looked with fiery eyes and laughed, O steadfast Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, O radiant light, Shiva, I seek refuge in You!” “He who is the beloved, He who became the four Vedas, He who is skilled in dancing, He who is the dance of wisdom, He who is the pillar, He who resides in the great city of Kanchi, He who shot the strong fortresses three into dust with His arrow, He who is of immeasurable greatness, He who is sweet nectar to His devotees, He who rides the bull, O golden Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, O radiant light, Shiva, I seek refuge in You!” “He who is filled, You who became all worlds, He who is established, He who is of immeasurable greatness, He who is keen, He who is the dancer of Thiru-Kutralam, He who holds the three-pronged trident, He who fought, He who is the Peruman of all deluges, He who always resides in the heart that speaks of Him, O Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, O radiant light, Shiva, I seek refuge in You!” “He who is the celestial, He who has a generous heart, You who are the Lord of the celestials adorned with great jewels, He who is the boar, He who followed the boar, He who destroyed the three fierce fortresses, He who is the self, He who resides on His Kailash, He who is ever sweet to the Goddess who has no equal, O Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, O radiant light, Shiva, I seek refuge in You!” “He who is His own, He who became all worlds Himself, He who is the truth, He who is sweet nectar to those who seek Him, He who is mine, He who resides in my heart, O Lord, He who removes the bonds of karma, O King, He who holds the mountain maiden as a part of Himself, O Lord of the Ponni, worshipped by the celestials, O Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, O radiant light, Shiva, I seek refuge in You!” “He who burned, He who is the eye for all eight directions, He who stood before all seven worlds, He who, unknown to the two who sought Him, became the beginning and the end and separated there, unknown to anyone else, He who always resides in the heart that praises Him as Peruman, O Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, O radiant light, Shiva, I seek refuge in You!” “He with the throat like ink, He with the trident in His hand, whose form was unknown to Vishnu and the other celestials, He who, with His toe, on that day, the Lord of fierce Lanka, He who destroyed his trembling crown and shoulders, O true one, He who bestows what His devotees desire, O celestial, He who grants when petitioned, O red one, O Lord of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, O radiant light, Shiva, I seek refuge in You!” These are the four Thiru-Pathigams bestowed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman upon the sacred place of Thiru-Sotrutthurai.

“Our contemplation shall continue.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 393. Thiru-Nindrachcharakkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped and prostrated at the sacred place of Thiru-Sotrutthurai, visited and worshipped the Lord in many nearby sacred places. These sacred places include Thiru-Kandiyur, Thiru-Vethikudi, Pasupathi Kovil, Thiru-Chakkarappalli, Thiru-Alandurai, and other temples.

Having worshipped thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal resided in Thiru-Pazhanam for many days, performing sacred service. Before going to Thingu-Lur, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped Thiru-Pazhanam, worshipped Thiru-Pazhanam again after returning from Thingu-Lur.

Thereafter, he stayed there with Appoothi Adigal, worshipping many places including Thiru-Sotrutthurai, and then came to Thiru-Pazhanam and stayed there for many days. All these were due to Appoothi Adigal’s profound devotion. While staying in Thiru-Pazhanam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal remembered the Lord of Thiru-Nallur, who had initiated him with the sacred feet and taken him as His own.

Therefore, he again went to Thiru-Nallur to worship there. It is not recorded in the history of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar that he revisited Thiru-Vathigai, the place where the Lord had afflicted him with colic and taken him as His own.

However, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar repeatedly remembered and came to worship the sacred place of Thiru-Nallur, which demonstrates to us the profound benefit of the sacred foot initiation. Thiru-Pazhanam is a sacred place on the north bank of the Kaveri. Thiru-Nallur is a sacred place on the south bank.

Therefore, from Thiru-Pazhanam, just as he had come to Thiru-Pazhanam from Thiru-Nallur before, in the same way, he crossed the Kaveri and the Kudamurutti river again by the path he had come, and reached Thiru-Nallur on the south bank of the Kaveri. He reached Thiru-Nallur, which is a Maadakkovil. Having gone to Thiru-Nallur, he worshipped the sacred feet of his Lord there, and with overflowing love, attained bliss, praised Shiva, and performed sacred service. The Nayanar stayed in Thiru-Nallur for many days, singing many garlands of Tamil verses and performing sacred service. Among the many Pathigams he sang, as mentioned by Sekkizhar Peruman, only the Thiru-Pathigam beginning with “Attumin Ilpali” is currently available to us, among the many Pathigams sung with overflowing love and praise. The other Pathigams are not available to us, which is due to our lack of merit.

This Thiru-Pathigam, beginning with “Attumin Ilpali” and “Agamkaindhorum Vandhu,” is a Thiru-Nallur Thiru-Pathigam. It describes the state of a heroine who, having been separated from her beloved for many days, sees him in a dream, and then, having lost the dream, laments to her friend. This Thiru-Pathigam, with the inner meaning of lamenting after losing a dream, is found as the ninety-seventh Thiru-Pathigam in the Fourth Thiru-Murai. It is a Thiru-Viruttha Thiru-Pathigam.

“Attumin Ilpali” (Offer the household alms) - those who churned their hearts and came, the women with fragrant hair, how did they take away the bangles? The Lord, who danced with His foot raised, beating the rhythm, with the fierce serpent, resides in Thiru-Nallur. “The women, with good resolve, not as before, who wander for alms, came with good resolve and entered the house in Thiru-Nallur. The singers and dancers, looking intently with their eyes, went away. There is a reason, they found the shore.” “O beautiful maiden with a serpent-like waist, in broad daylight, someone, like one who takes alms, entered the house and walked.

“Are they the dancers whose feet are accustomed to dancing? The northern Kailash and the southern Thiru-Nallur are their dwelling places.” “The red-glowing coral-like cluster of pearls, the Lord with the poison-adorned throat, the beloved who resides in Thiru-Nallur, I saw Him once in a dream, and worshipped Him in my dream. He has not left my heart for many ages, He has remained there.” “He who stands radiant, wearing the white moon, worshipped by the celestials, in Thiru-Nallur, where songs never cease, He stands firm, He who shot the three cities. His sacred feet are in my eyes and heart.” “If Shiva resides in Thiru-Nallur, clearly, the devotees who do not go and see Him, due to their foolish minds, are like those who lose something in the river and search for it in the pond, wandering all over the world in a frenzy, seeking to see Him.” “In Thiru-Nallur, surrounded by lotus ponds, He who said, ‘Give me a loincloth,’ and caused the mountain to fall, He who took the merchant with his wife, with sword-like eyes, as His own, does not this wide world speak of that story? In this song, the phrase “took the merchant with his wife as His own” refers to Amarneethi Nayanar. This is the place where the Lord took Amarneethi Nayanar as His own, and Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar sings about it.

“He who wears the anklets on His feet, He who has a garland of white Konrai flowers on His beautiful matted locks, in Thiru-Nallur, He became a singer and dancer, and bestowed grace, He with the crescent moon on His red matted locks, dancing, He is the Pinakan.” “The permanent great Brahmins, rejoicing and praising, the gathered devotees, singing sweet melodies and worshipping, the maidens of Thiru-Nallur, in their dreams, their beloved, the one who is not a stranger, the Lord, bestows grace, they say.” “The lotus where Lakshmi resides, the beautiful red water lily, the blue water lily, the Kuruva flower, the Kongu, the Kura, the Magizh, the Shanbagam, the Konrai, the Vanni, the fragrant long creeper, the mansions, the many Brahmins, in Thiru-Nallur, we contemplate the Lord who has Uma as a part of His form.” “The Lord with the bull banner, Shiva’s great temple, Shiva’s city, I am skilled in entering, the king of Lanka, surrounded by walls, He who crushed his unlearned crowns and shoulders with His foot, is not the Lord who resides in Thiru-Nallur, the one who rules us?”

“Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, having sung Pathigams in Thiru-Nallur, worshipped the Lord and performed sacred service, remembered and desired to go and worship Thiru-Arur, where Shiva resides.

“Therefore, he now set out from Thiru-Nallur, visited all the sacred places on the way, and went to Thiru-Arur. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, having received gracious permission from the Lord in Thiru-Nallur, worshipped Shiva in Pazhaiyarai. There are three Shiva temples: Arai Arai Vadathali, Arai Mertrali. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, having worshipped all these places, sang Thevaram Thiru-Pathigams. Without the Nayanar’s effort, by divine grace, the sacred words flowed forth. He sang such rich Thiru-Pathigams from the tongue of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman.

“Thus, having worshipped Pazhaiyarai, he then worshipped Thiru-Valanjuzhi. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped Thiru-Valanjuzhi, bestowed three Thiru-Pathigams. Two of them are for the sacred place of Thiru-Valanjuzhi, and the third Thiru-Pathigam is a Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathigam that combines Thiru-Valanjuzhi and Thiru-Kottaiyur Kodicharam. Thiru-Valanjuzhi is the twenty-fifth sacred place on the south bank of the Kaveri. It is named Thiru-Valanjuzhi because the Kaveri takes a right turn here. The Kaveri that flows here is called Melai Kaveri.

“It is said that Adisesha, from the netherworld, came through a hole on a Shivaratri and worshipped in four places during the four yamas, and this is one of those four places. The other three sacred places are Thiru-Nageswaram, Thiru-Pambaram, and Thiru-Nagai Karonam. When Adisesha came through the hole and the Kaveri went down into it, the Chola king, seeing this, prayed to the Lord, and the Lord, acceding to his request, descended and bestowed grace. At the place where the Kaveri descended, the Lord announced through an ethereal voice that if one offered a matted lock or a head, the Kaveri would emerge.

“Therefore, when Eranda Munivar, who was performing penance in Kottaiyur, descended into the hole, the Kaveri emerged, turned right, and flowed abundantly. This is the history of this sacred place. In the temple, in the Biladvara, Trinavardeswarar and Eranda Munivar are seated nearby. This place is also known as Trinavardam and Dakshinavardam. When the celestials churned the ocean for nectar, Indra installed and worshipped the white Pillaiyar (Svetavinayagar) here, who was worshipped to gather the nectar. That Svetavinayagar, the white Pillaiyar, is seated prominently in front of this temple.

“This is the place worshipped by Indra.

“Here, the Lord’s name is Kapardeeswarar, Garbhaganatheswarar, Valanjuzhinathar. The Goddess’s name is Piraganayaki, also known as Periya Nayaki. The Sthala Vinayagar, as we have already seen, is Svetavinayagar. The sacred waters are Kaveri, Arisol Nadi (Arasalaru), Jatta Tirtham, which is an ancient pond inside, next to the gopuram. The Sthala Vriksham is the Vilva tree.

“We have already seen the reason for the name of this place.

“In addition, because the Svetavinayagar here is a right-turning deity, this place came to be known as Thiru-Valanjuzhi. It also has another name, Sagathivanam. Those who received grace here include the Chola king, Eranda Munivar, Adisesha, Parasakthi, Thiru-Gnanasambandhar, Thiru-Navukkarasar, Brahma, Indra, and a serpent. There are four prakarams, including the Rathaveethi. There are five mandapams and a five-tiered Rajagopuram. This temple, which is a pinnacle of sculpture, contains many ancient stone sculptures.

“The name of the Goddess is Piraganayaki, also known as Periya Nayaki. The Sthala Vinayagar, as we have already seen, is Svetavinayagar. The sacred waters are Kaveri, Arisol Nadi (Arasalaru), Jatta Tirtham, which is an ancient pond inside, next to the gopuram. The Sthala Vriksham is the Vilva tree. We have already seen the reason for the name of this place.

“In addition, because the Svetavinayagar here is a right-turning deity, this place came to be known as Thiru-Valanjuzhi. It also has another name, Sagathivanam. Those who received grace here include the Chola king, Eranda Munivar, Adisesha, Parasakthi, Thiru-Gnanasambandhar, Thiru-Navukkarasar, Brahma, Indra, and a serpent. There are four prakarams, including the Rathaveethi. There are five mandapams and a five-tiered Rajagopuram. This temple, which is a pinnacle of sculpture, contains many ancient stone sculptures.

“The mandapam of Swetha Vinayagar, with its painted pillars, entirely made of black granite, and its balcony, resembling a chariot with wheels, captivates the eyes and minds of onlookers. Thiruvalanchuzhi Sthalam is located very close to Kumbakonam, and very close to Swamimalai. The Rajagopuram faces east. Inside the temple, there are three prakarams, and outside, there is a street. Adjacent to the front gopuram are the sacred tank and the mandapam temple. Inside the next entrance are the flagstaff, the Nandi mandapam, and the shrine of Swetha Vinayagar.

“To the north is the ornamental mandapam. Next to it, in the surrounding area, is the Niraippani mandapam. To the south are the kitchen and to the north are the Utsava mandapam. In the inner prakaram, on the south side, are many Linga-murthis and Navasakthi-murthis. To the west are the Sthala Vinayagar, Valanchuzhi Vinayagar, and next to them, Somaskandar and Shanmuga Subramaniar. Lakshmi and other deities, and on the north side, many Linga-murthis worshipped by various devotees.

“On the south side, in the garbha-griha koshtam, are Dakshinamurthy, Picchadana, and other idols. On the north side is the shrine of Chandesar, and next to it, Sani is present alone. On the north side of the main shrine are the Utsava-murthis, and the principal Sri Nataraja-murthy is an ancient, large idol. Inside the Maha-mandapam, on the north side, is Eranda Maharishi. In the third outer prakaram, on the south side, Ambikai Periyanayagiyar is enshrined, facing east. Inside the Amman temple, on the south side, Ashtabhuja Kali is seated.

“This Sthalam was once a Bhairavar Sthalam. Adjacent to the Rajagopuram, on the south side, there is a separate temple dedicated to Bhairavar.

“Here, a nine-day Indra Puja festival is held. The Swetha Vinayagar, a sea foam deity, was created by Indra from the foam that arose from the ocean of milk.

“Therefore, no ablutions other than sprinkling green camphor are performed for this Vinayagar. Vinayagar, accompanied by Vani Kamalambal, celebrates a nine-day Brahmotsavam during Avani Chathurthi.

“The Lord of this temple is Kapardeeswarar, a Swayambhu Murthy. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, in his Thevaram, praises the Lord of this Sthalam very beautifully, asking, “What good deeds have you done, O mind?” Ambikai appears majestically with four arms.

“Once, due to Adiseshan emerging from the netherworld, a great chasm, a pit as deep as the netherworld, was formed. The Kaveri river flowed down into that chasm. The Chola king, seeing this, was greatly distressed.

“At that time, Shiva Peruman spoke an ethereal voice. Shiva Peruman graciously said that if a king or a great sage descended into the netherworld and offered themselves as a sacrifice, the chasm would close. The king was distraught. Eranda Muni, who was performing penance here, consoled the king and descended himself. The chasm closed, and the Kaveri flowed normally.

“Therefore, the image of Eranda Maharishi is in the temple. In this Sthalam, Parasakthi also incarnated as the daughter of a sage, worshipped the Lord of this Sthalam, and married Shiva Peruman.

“Hence, this Sthalam is also known as Sakthi Vanam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar came here and composed two Thiru-pathigams for Thiruvalanchuzhi. In the third Thiru-pathigam, he sang connecting Thiruvalanchuzhi and Thirukottaiyur Kodicharam.

“We will continue to contemplate those Thiru-pathigams.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 394, Thirunindrachcharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman came to Thiruvalanchuzhi and composed three Thiru-pathigams. The first of these Thiru-pathigams is Thirukkurunthogai Thiru-pathigam, which is the sixty-sixth Thiru-pathigam in the fifth Thirumurai.

Othamar kadalin vidam undavan Boothanayagan porkkailaikku irai Mathurbagan Valanchuzhi Eesanai Padham etha paraiyunam pavame Kailainathan karuthavar muppuram Eyilgal theeyazha velvala vithagan Mayilgalalum Valanchuzhi Eesanai Payilkilarsilar pavithozhumbare Ilaiya kalam emmanai adaikila Thulaiyila sevi thondargalal num udal Valaiyum kalam Valanchuzhi Eesanai Kalaiganaga karuthi Neer uymine Naraigul poompunal kondu ezhu Manikkay Kuraivila kodungootru udhaithithavan Maraigul navan Valanchuzhi meviya Iraivanai ini endru kolkanbathe Vindavar puram moonrum erigola Thin thiral silaiyal eri seithavan Vandu panmurulum than Valanchuzhi Andanukku adimai thirathavane Padankol pampodu panmathiyanjadai Adanga vazha vallan umbar thambiran Madanthai bhagan Valanchuzhiyan adi Adainthavarkku adaimai thirathavane Nakkondu paravum adiyar vinai Pokkavalla purisadai punniyan Makol solai Valanchuzhi Eesanthann Ekola puram moonru eriyanave Theduvar Biraman Thirumal avar A Padupatham avarum arugilar Madaveethi Valanchuzhi Eesanai Theduvan urugindrathu en sinthaiye Kan panikkum kaikoopum kan moonru udai Nanbanukku ena nan koduppen enum Van ponni then Valanchuzhi meviya Panbaniponai seitha parisu ithe Ilangaivendan irupathu thol ira Nalankol padhathu oru viral oondrinan Malangu pay vayal soozhntha Valanchuzhi Valangolvar adi en thalaimelave Thiruchitrambalam. The meaning of this Thiru-pathigam is that by praising Valanchuzhi Eesan, sins will vanish, and one will become his servant. Some foolish devotees do not worship him. The feet of those who circumambulate Valanchuzhi are upon my head.

Now, the second Thiru-pathigam sung by Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar for this Sthalam is the Thiruthandaga Thiru-pathigam. The seventy-second Thiru-pathigam in the sixth Thirumurai. Alaiyar punar Gangai nangai kana Ambalathil aru nattamadi vedam Tholaiyatha vendriyar nindriyurum Nedunkalamum mevi vidaiyai melkondu Ilaiyar padai kaiyil endhi engum Imiyaverum umaiyavalum irainji etha Malaiyar thiral aruvi ponni soozhntha Valanchuzhiye pukkidama maruvinare Thiruchitrambalam. Only one verse from this Thiru-pathigam is available to us. The other verses are not available due to our lack of merit.

Now, the third Thiru-pathigam composed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman for this Sthalam is the Thiru-pathigam that connects Thiruvalanchuzhi and Thirukottaiyur Kodicharam. Thirukottaiyur is another Sthalam. Thirukottaiyur is the name of the Sthalam, and Kodicharam is the name of the temple. As mentioned in the history of this Sthalam, the name Valanchuzhi came to this Sthalam because Eranda Muni, who was performing penance in Kottaiyur, came here and descended into the chasm, and the Kaveri emerged from the chasm.

Therefore, this Thiruvalanchuzhi Sthalam is related to Thirukottaiyur Sthalam. Hence, Thirunavukkarasu Swami sang connecting Thiruvalanchuzhi and Thirukottaiyur.

Now, that Thiru-pathigam.

varathan kanday Kurumani pol azhamarum Kottaiyuril Kodichcharathu uraiyum Koman thane Kalaikandru thangu karathan kanday kalai Payilvor gnana kan anan kanday Alaikangai senjadai mel etran kanday
