Thakkanathu peruvellvith thagarthan kanday Sadhasivankan salantharanai pilanthan kanday Mai kon mayithalai kondu varu neer ponni Valanchuzhiyan kanday Mazhuvan kanday Kokkamarum vayal pudaisoozh Kottaiyuril Kodichcharathu uraiyum Koman thane Sandanai nal andar thozhacheythan kanday Sadhasivan kanday Sankaranthan kanday Thondar palar thozhuthu etham kadalan kanday Sudar oliyay thodarvarithay nindran kanday Mandu punal ponni valam suzhiyan kanday Mamunivar thammudaiya marunthu kanday Kondal thaval kodimada Kottaiyuril Kodichcharathu uraiyum Koman thane Anavarian kanday amalan kanday Avinasi kanday Andathan kanday Panmani ma nagamudaiyan kanday Pandarangan kanday Bhagavan kanday Manalvaru neer ponni valam suzhiyan kanday Madhavarkkum nanmugarkkum varathan kanday Gunamudai nal adiyar vazh Kottaiyuril Kodichcharathu uraiyum Koman thane Viraigamalun malarkkondrai tharan kanday Vedangal thozhanindra nathan kanday Araiyathanil pulli athaludaiyan kanday Azhaladi kanday azhagan kanday Varuthirai neer ponni Valanchuzhiyan kanday Vanja manathavarkku ariya mainthan kanday Kuravamarum pozhil pudaisoozh Kottaiyuril Kodichcharathu uraiyum Koman thane Thalangilarum thamarai athanathan kanday Dasarathan than magan Asaivu thavirthan kanday Ilamberaiyum muthir sadai mel vaithan kanday Ettettu irunkalaiyum anan kanday Valangilar neerponni valam suzhiyan kanday Mamunigal thozhuthazhu porkalalan kanday Kulangulir senguvalai kizhar Kottaiyuril Kodichcharathu uraiyum Koman thane Vindar puram moonru erithan kanday Vilangalil val arakkann udal adarthan kanday Thandamaraianum malum theda Thalar pilambay neenda kalalan kanday Vandar pooncholai Valanchuzhiyan kanday Mahadevan kanday Maraiyodu angangondu adu vedhiyar vazh Kottaiyuril Kodichcharathu uraiyum Koman thane Thiruchitrambalam. These are the Thiru-pathigams composed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman for Thiruvalanchuzhi. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, having worshipped and praised Thiruvalanchuzhi from Thirunallur and Pazhaiyarai, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, who worshipped and praised Thiruvalanchuzhi, continues his journey, visiting Thiru-sthalams such as Thirukudamookku, also known as Kumbakonam, Kudanthai Keezhkottam, Thirunalur, Thirucherai, Thirukudavayil, and Thirunaraiyur.

We will continue to contemplate that history. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 395, Thirunindrachcharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped Thiruvalanchuzhi, arrives at the Thiru-stalam of Kumbakonam, also known as Thirukudamookku. Kumbakonam is a very famous and special place, to the extent that there is no one who does not know about it. The Adi Kumbeswarar Mangalanayagi Temple in Kumbakonam is one of the temples on the southern bank of the Kaveri. The temple’s Vinayagar is Thirukudamookku Vinayagar, Adi Vinayagar.

The Lord’s name is Adi Kumbeswarar. The Goddess is Mangalambikai. The sacred tank is Mahamaham. The Kaveri is the Sthala Vriksham, the Vanni tree. This temple is prominently located in the center of Kumbakonam city. During the time of the deluge, when the pot filled with ambrosia floated, Shiva Peruman, in the form of a Kiratha form, a hunter’s form, used an arrow to spread the ambrosia in all directions through the mouth of the pot, hence the name Kudamookku.

It is also known as Kudanthai and Kumbakonam. In this city of Kumbakonam, besides the Adi Kumbeswarar Temple, which is praised in Thevaram, there are also Shiva Sthalams like Kudanthai Keezhkottam and Kudanthai Karonam.

Furthermore, there are various other Shiva Thiru-sthalams and Shiva temples here. There are also monasteries belonging to various paths of Sanatana Dharma. The Kumbeswarar temple, the central jewel of Kumbakonam city, faces east. In front of the temple, a nine-tiered Rajagopuram stands as a Sthula Lingam. Inside the temple, there are three prakarams. In the first prakaram, located inside the Kailasa Gopuram, In the eastern row are the sixty-three Utsava-murthis and the Stanikar’s room.

In the southern row are the four Saiva Samayacharyars, the sixty-three, the Sapta Kanniyar, and others. In the western row are the shrines of Vinayagar, Bhikshadana, Subramaniar, Karthikeyar, Lakshmi, and others. In the northern row are the Palliyarai, the Kattalai rooms, and the Kirathamurthy shrine. In the center of the mandapam are Adi Kumbeswarar, and to the south, Somaskanda Murthy, and to the north, Mangalambikai Amman, enshrined in separate mandapams. In the second prakaram, to the southeast is the kitchen, and to the northeast are the Yagasalai and the Sri Lakshmi Narayana Perumal shrine. In the third prakaram, within the great gopuram, to the southwest is Adi Vinayagar, and to the northwest is a Shiva Lingam.

In the center of the Kumarakkottam is Dandapani Murthy. To the north are the Thirukalyana Mandapam, the elephant stable, the Sattanathar temple, and the sacred tank. To the south, the Vanni tree, the Vinayagar temple, and the Nanda Vanam are located. The Thirukalyana festival is held in the Kalyana Mandapam. The fourth prakaram of this temple is the street where the chariot runs. Except for the south entrance, the other three entrances have gopurams.

We saw that the Vinayagar of this Sthalam is Adi Vinayagar. Knowing that the Lord and Goddess were coming to this Sthalam, Vinayagar also arrived at this Sthalam in the beginning and created a great sense of devotion, thus earning the name Adi Vinayagar. The Moolavar is known by the names Adi Kumbeswarar, Amudakumbesar, and Amudesar. He is called Adi Kumbeswarar because the Parapara, the primordial cause of the world, appeared in the pot. He is called Amudakumbesar because he appeared in the pot of ambrosia. He is called Amudesar because he arose from the ambrosia of abundant taste.

Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, in his Thiru-pathigam, refers to the Lord as Kuzhagan. In the Amudakumbam, As the source for the emergence of various other Lingams, that pot is called Kshetra Beeja Kumbam.

Here, the Goddess is known by the names Mangalambikai and Mangalanayagi. She is called Mangalanayagi because of her greatness in bestowing divine auspiciousness upon those who worship her with love.

Furthermore, the Goddess is also known by the name ‘Pazha Noyarukkum Parai’ (one who cures many diseases) because she cures many diseases of those who worship her. Shiva Peruman, appearing in the form of a hunter, shot an arrow at the pot of ambrosia, thus earning the name Kirathamurthy. The Kumbeswarar temple, also known as Kudamookku, was established because the ambrosia flowed through the mouth of the pot of ambrosia that floated during the deluge. The items that adorned the pot of ambrosia, such as mango leaves, darbha grass, uriy, bilva, coconut, sacred thread, etc., were scattered by the wind, and wherever they fell, they appeared as individual Lingams. All of them are enshrined as separate temples here in Kumbakonam. The first of these temples is the Nageswarar temple.

The bilva leaf that adorned the pot of ambrosia fell to the southeast of the Kumbeswarar temple. Hence, it is known as Bilva Vanesar. It is also called Nageswarar because he blessed Adiseshan, the king of serpents, and Pathalalingesar because it is in the netherworld. For three days a year, the sun’s rays fall on the Moolalingam. It is also known as Bhaskara Kshetram. The Goddess is Periyanayagi.

The sacred tank is Naga Theertham. Next is the Someswarar temple, located to the east of the Potramarai Kulam. This is the place where the uriy, which supported the pot of ambrosia, rested.

Hence, it is called Sikkam. Sikkam means uriy. Since the uriy that supported the pot rested here, it is called Sikkam. The great Lord is known by the name Sikkam. He is called Someswarar and Ezha Somanathar because he blessed Chandra (the moon), and the Goddess is named Somasundari. He is also known as Vyazha Somesar because Jupiter worshipped him.

There is a sacred tank called Soma Theertham, also known as Chandra Pushkarani. Next is the Abhimukeswarar temple, located on the eastern bank of the Mahamaham Kulam. This is the place where the Nalikera, or coconut, that adorned the pot of ambrosia fell. A Shiva Lingam appeared at this spot.

Hence, this Sthalam is known as Nalikera Eswaram.

The Lord is named Nalikera Eswarar. The name Abhimukeswarar came about because the Lord appeared facing west (abhimukham) to the nine rivers, including the Ganga, who came to bathe in the Mahamaham Theertham. The Goddess here is Amirthavalli. To the Brahmin woman suffering from leprosy and a mute prince, the Lord showed his grace and cured their diseases and muteness. Next in this temple is the Gautameswarar temple, located in the southwest corner of the Mahamaham Kulam. This is the place where the sacred thread that adorned the pot of ambrosia fell.

A Lingam appeared at that spot, and thus the Lord was named Yagnopaviteswarar. He is also known as Gautameswarar because he blessed Gautama Muni. There is a sacred tank called Gautama Theertham. The Goddess is named Soundarya Nayagi. Next is the Kasi Viswanathar temple, located on the northern bank of the Mahamaham Kulam. At the request of the Nava Kannikas, including Ganga, the Lord came here with them from Kasi and resided.

The Nava Kannikas are also seated in this Sthalam. When Rama Peruman came to this Sthalam to destroy Ravana and others and sought the Lord’s grace, the Lord entered Rama’s body, thus earning the name Kayarohanar. The Goddess is named Kasi Visalakshi. Next is the Banapureeswarar temple. This is Banapuresam, or Banathurai, the place where Shiva Peruman, in the form of a hunter, stood and shot an arrow at the pot of ambrosia that floated during the deluge.

Banam means arrow. Because he shot an arrow, the Swami was named Banapureeswarar. The idol of Kirathamurthy, in the form of a hunter, is in the Kumbeswarar temple. To commemorate this, the Goddess here is named Somakalambal. In this Sthalam, Vyasa, Surasena’s wife Gandhimati, and others have worshipped and gained fame.

Thus, many Shiva temples related to the history of Kumbakonam are located here. Not only these, but in this city, there are also Kailasanathar temple, Kampatta Viswanathar temple, Kalatheeswarar temple, Ekambareswarar temple, Viswar The temples of Natha Temple, Brahma Temple, Karumbayira Vinayagar Temple, and others are located here and there. The Pancha Krosha Sthalams are situated here. It is said that due to the grace of Lord Shiva, the ambrosia-filled hall was destroyed, and the ambrosia spread in all four directions, extending up to five kroshas and enriching the land, thus earning the name Pancha Krosha Sthalams. These include Thiruvidaimaruthur, Thirunageswaram, Tharadareeswaram (i.e., Tharasuram), Thiruveragam (Swamimalai), and Thirupadalavanam (Karuppur). One krosha is said to be a distance of two and a half naligai (a unit of time, approximately one hour).

The pilgrimage rule for those traveling to Kumbakonam is that they must visit these Pancha Krosha Sthalams, bathe according to the rituals, have darshan, and stay for one day at each place before proceeding to Kumbakonam. Just as many texts serve as auxiliary parts to the Vedas, these five places serve as auxiliary parts to Kumbakonam. are situated. The learned praise Kumbakonam and those who appreciate it should undertake the five-krosha pilgrimage. The wise say that visiting each of the five sacred places for one day will yield great merit. This is according to the Thirukudanthai Puranam. The sacred waters (theerthams) in this holy city include the Mahamaham Theertham, which is a central and captivating feature of the city, surrounded by many mandapams, and is a crucial part of the Mahamaham festival.

A portion of the ambrosia that overflowed from the Amrita Kumbha settled in the southeast direction, and that spot is the Mahamaham Theertham.

Furthermore, the Navakannikas, the goddesses of the rivers Ganga, Yamuna, Godavari, Narmada, Saraswati, Kaveri, Kumari, Payodini, Sarayu, and others, come to Kumbakonam once every twelve years on the Mahamaham day to cleanse themselves of the sins accumulated from the countless people who bathe in their rivers. On the Mahamaham day, when Jupiter is in the sign of Leo and the Moon is in the sign of Aquarius, which is the full moon day of Masi Maham, the local purana states that they come to Kumbakonam and bathe in the Mahamaham tank.

Therefore, it is believed that on that day, rivers like the Ganga join the Mahamaham tank. “Thavi muthal Kaveri nal Yamunai Gangai Saraswati Potramarai Putkarani thenneer Goviyodu Kumari varu theertham soozhntha Kudanthai Keezhkottathu em Koothanare” is from Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar’s Thevaram. “Boomaruvum Gangai muthal punithamaam peruntheertham Maamagandhaan aadutharku vandhu vazhi padungoyil” is from Periya Puranam. This tank is also known by names such as Amudavavi, Amudha Theertham, Kanniyar Theertham, and Pavanasam Theertham. Currently, it is colloquially called Mamangam Kulam. Sri Rama, Chandi, and Sulochana, wife of Hemavagu, among others, are said to have bathed here and attained blessings.

The Purana states that if one bathes and worships in this Theertham on the Mahamaham day coinciding with a full moon, it will bring merit to seven generations: one’s own lineage, son-in-law’s lineage, grandfather’s lineage, maternal aunt’s lineage, sister’s lineage, paternal uncle’s lineage, and maternal uncle’s lineage. Accordingly, people from various parts of the country, with faith, come to this place, bathe in the Theerthams, and worship the Lord. During the grand festival for Adi Kumbeswarar in the month of Masi, on the tenth day, which is Maham, the Lord, along with the Panchamoorthies, proceeds to this tank, performs Theertham, and bestows blessings. In the month of Panguni, the Theppam festival (float festival) takes place. The deity of Sri Nageswarar Temple also comes and stays in a mandapam in this tank to perform Theertham. The auspicious times for bathing here include Amavasai (new moon), Pournami (full moon), month beginnings, the two Ayana periods, Sukravaram (Friday), Mahavyapatham, Karthigai, Shivaratri, and other special days.

There are sixteen mandapams surrounding this tank. These are known as Sodasa Linga Mandapams. It is said that Govinda Dikshitar, a minister to Achyutappa Nayakar who ruled Thanjavur, built these sixteen mandapams with the king’s support.

Furthermore, it is said that he also built Pushpa Mandapams in Thiruvaiyaru, Kumbakonam, Thiruvidaimaruthur, and Thiruvalanjuzhi. His statue and his wife’s statue are in the Kumbeswarar Temple. The names of the deities in these sixteen mandapams are as follows: Brahma Theertheswarar, Mukundeswarar, Thaneswarar, Rishabheswarar, Bharanesvarar, Koneswarar, Bhaktikeswarar, Bhairaveswarar, Agastheeswarar, Vyaseswarar, Umaibhageswarar, Nairutheeswarar, Brahmeswarar, Gangadhareswarar, Muktatheertheswarar, Kshethrapaleswarar, and others. Among these sixteen mandapams, the first one on the northern bank, Brahma Theertheswarar, has a Thulabharam painting.

Hence, it is also called Thulabharam Mandapam. There are many Theerthams within the Mahamaham tank. Specifically, there are eighteen Theerthams inside the Mahamaham tank, and a nineteenth, the sixty-six crore Theertham. Their details are as follows: Brahma Theertham (1), the Theerthams of the Dikpalakas (8), which are Indra Theertham, Agni Theertham, Yama Theertham, Niruthi Theertham, Varuna Theertham, Vayu Theertham, Kubera Theertham, and Isana Theertham. Next are the Theerthams of the nine rivers (9), which are Ganga, Yamuna, Godavari, Narmada, Saraswati, Kaveri, Kumari, Payodini, and Sarayu. This totals eighteen Theerthams.

In addition to these, there is the nineteenth, the sixty-six crore Theertham. By bathing in the Mahamaham tank, which contains all these Theerthams, on the Masi Maham day and worshipping deities like Kumbeswarar, one can attain benefits in this life and the next. is Kashyapa Theertham. Kashyapa Theertham, located in Kumbakonam, is where Sage Kashyapa came, bathed in the Kaveri river, and worshipped Kumbeswarar. The place where he bathed is known as Kashyapa Theertham. During festival days, Kumbeswarar also comes to this spot to perform Theertham.

Hence, it is also called Thirumanjana Padithurai.

Thirdly, Kamadhenu Theertham. To the north of Kumbeswarar Temple, the divine cow Kamadhenu created a Theertham and worshipped the Lord. That is Kamadhenu Theertham.

Next, Kandakoopam. Lord Muruga, to achieve victory in his battle against Surapadman and others, found a Theertham in the northeast of the temple and worshipped the Lord with it.

Hence, it was named Kandakoopam. Mangala Koopam, also known as Mangala Sivagangai, is now referred to as Thirukulam. Besides these, there are various other Theerthams belonging to other temples in Kumbakonam. The glories of this sacred place cannot be easily described. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman sings, “If you say Kudamookke, Kudamookke, your evil deeds will cease, and you will reach the Lord.” This holy place, Thirukudamookku, is indestructible even during the time of dissolution. The Kaveri river flows here under the name Kumaradharai.

According to the Sthala Purana, Chandi, Krithavanman, Sudhanman, Veeravanman, Sulochana, Kashyapan, Gnanavan, Suvarnaroman, Karmasanman, and others worshipped here and attained blessings. Indra and other deities also worshipped and received blessings. The sage Bhagavar performed penance and attained liberation. A bathing ghat in the Kaveri is named Bhagavar Padithurai after him. The Adi Kumbeswarar Temple celebrates the Sapthasthanam festival, where the Lord, with his consort, proceeds in a palanquin to seven places and circumambulates them. In this temple, daily, six-time ablutions and worship ceremonies are performed.

The pujas take place at Ushathkalam (dawn), Kalaichandi (morning), Uchchikalam (noon), Sayarakshai (evening), Iramam (second period), and Arthajamam (midnight). Annually, the grand Masi Maham festival is celebrated for ten days in the month of Masi. On the first day, coinciding with the Ashvathi star, the flag is hoisted. On the eighth day, Vennai Thali (butter offering) is performed, and on the ninth day, the chariot procession takes place. On the tenth day, the auspicious full moon day coinciding with Maham, the Panchamoorthies, riding on vehicles such as the mouse, peacock, and bull, proceed to the Mahamaham tank to perform Theertham. This event and the Mahamaham grand festival, which occurs once every twelve years, are celebrated by this temple.

In the month of Panguni, the Theppam festival (float festival) is held in the Mahamaham tank, and in the month of Chithirai, the Sapthasthanam festival takes place. On the day of the Sapthasthanam festival, Adi Kumbeswarar, along with Mangalanayaki, adorned in a wonderfully decorated palanquin, proceeds to seven places: Sakkottai, Thiru- Kalaiyanallur, Tharasuram, Thiruvalanjuzhi, Swamimalai, Kottaiyur, and Melakaveri, grants darshan, and returns. In the month of Vaikasi, the sacred marriage of Sri Mangalambikai and Kumbeswarar takes place. Other festivals such as Aani Thirumanjanam, Dakshinayanam, Pathinettam Perukku, Aadi Pooram, Pavithra Vizha, Avani Moolam, Vinayaka Chathurthi, Navaratri, Kanda Shashti, Kadaimugam, Karthigai Somavaram, Karthigai Deepam, Margazhi Thiruvathirai, Mahavyathipatham, Sankaranthi, Shivaratri, and Amudhu Padaiyal are celebrated at their respective times. The five seasonal festivals of Pradosham, Karthigai, Friday, Amavasai, and Thiruvathirai are also celebrated at their respective times. The history of this place is mentioned in Sanskrit Puranas such as Bhavishya Purana, Brahmanda Purana, and Skanda Purana.

The Thirukudanthai Puranam, authored by the great scholar Meenakshi Sundaram Pillai, is available in Tamil. It comprises seventy chapters and two thousand three hundred and eighty-four verses. The history of Adi Kumbha is as follows: Once, Brahma went to Lord Shiva, who was seated on Mount Kailash, and presented his grievance. He said, “Lord, a deluge that will destroy all worlds is approaching. The Vedas and other things will be destroyed. If the seed of creation (Srushti Beejam) is also destroyed, how will I perform the act of creation?

“You must tell me a solution.” The Lord said to Brahma, “Mix ambrosia and earth, fashion a mystical pot, fill it with ambrosia, and place within it the seed of creation that I give you. It has the power to create all things. Adorn the pot with mango leaves, bilva leaves, coconut, sacred thread, and other items, sprinkle it with ambrosia, place the pot in a sling, and set it on a peak of Mount Meru. During the deluge, the pot will float and move towards the south.

“Then, I will come and do what is necessary.” Thus spoke Lord Shiva. This is the history that unfolded as per his grace, the history of Kumbakonam, as we have already seen.

“Later, Lord Shiva appears to Brahma along with Ambika. This is the sacred history of the Adi Kumbeswarar Mangalanayaki Temple, known as Thirukudamookku. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman arrives here.

“Let us go on reflecting.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 396, Thirunindracharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman worships Thiruvalanjuzhi and arrives at Kumbakonam, also known as Thirukudamookku. He worships Adi Kumbeswarar, accompanied by Mangalambikai, and sings a Thirupathigam. That Thirupathigam is the twenty-second Thirupathigam in the fifth Thirumurai. This is a Thirukurunthogai Thirupathigam.

Now, that Thirupathigam.

Poovanathan punniyan nanniyang kaavanaththudaiyaan adiyaargalai theevanath thiruneeru meyppoosiyor kovanaaththudaiyaan kuda mookkile pooththaadik kazhiyaadhe neer poomiyir theeththaadi thiram sindhaiyul vaimino verththaadung kaali than visai theerkendru kooththaadi uraiyum kuda mookkile. (Gloss: He who is the lord of the sacred grove, the virtuous one, the one with the loincloth, who smears sacred ash on his devotees, resides in Kudamookku. Do not waste your time in worldly pleasures, O people of the earth, but keep in your mind the power of the sacred fire. He who dances to remove the frenzy of Kali, who dances with sweat, resides in Kudamookku.) (Gloss: If you speak of the power of the unlearned tongue, it will be sweet. The place where the Lord, who rides the bull, resides, is where the Yamuna and Godavari rivers flow, in Kudamookku.) Nakkaraiyanai naalthorum nannenchche Vakkaraiyurai vaane vanangu nee Akkaraiyodu aravarai aarththavan Kokkaraiyudaiyaan Kudamookkile. (Gloss: O good heart, worship the Lord daily.

Worship the one who resides in Vakkarai. He who tied the serpent to his waist, the one with the skull, resides in Kudamookku.) Thuravi nenjinaraagiya thondargal Piravi neenga piththaraay Maravanaayp paarththan mel kanai thotta em Kuravanaar uraiyum Kudamookkile. (Gloss: O devotees with ascetic hearts, become mad to escape rebirth. Our Lord, who shot arrows at Arjuna as a hunter, resides in Kudamookku.) Thondaraagith thozhuthu panimino Pandai valvinai pattraara venduveer Vindavar puram moonroru maaththirai Kondavan uraiyum Kuda- Mookkile. (Gloss: Become devotees, worship and serve, if you wish to be free from ancient strong karma. He who destroyed the three cities of the enemies in a moment resides in Kudamookku.) Kaamiyanjcheythu kaalang kazhiyaadhe Omiyamjcheythu angu ullaththu unarmino Saamiyodu Saraswathi aval Komiyum uraiyum Kudamookkile. (Gloss: Do not waste time in worldly desires; perform sacrifices and realize within your heart. The Lord, along with Saraswati, resides in Kudamookku.) Siramanjcheythu Sivanukku paththaraay Paramanai palnaalum payitrumin Piraman maalodu mattrozhingaarkkellaam Kuravanaar uraiyum Kudamookkile. (Gloss: Perform penance and be devoted to Shiva; worship the Supreme Lord daily. The Lord, who is the guru to Brahma, Vishnu, and all others, resides in Kudamookku.) Andruthaan arakkan Kailayaththaich Chenruthaan edukka Umai anjchalum Nandruthaan nakku nalviral oondri pin Kondru geetham kettan Kudamookkile. (Gloss: That day, when the demon went to lift Kailash and Uma was frightened, he laughed well, pressed his good toe, then killed him and heard his song, in Kudamookku.)

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped at Kudamookku, reached Kudanthai Keezhkottam and worshipped the Lord there. This is the Nageswarar Swamy Temple in Kumbakonam, which, as we saw in the historical account, is another temple located on the banks of the Mahamaham tank. It is a place where the Sun worshipped. In this holy temple, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal worshipped the Lord Madanthaibagar and sang a Thirupathigam. The Thirukudanthai Keezhkottam Thirupathigam is a Thiruthandagam Thirupathigam. It is the seventy-fifth Thirupathigam in the sixth Thirumurai.

He is like the Lord who is neither male, female, nor neuter. He is like the one whose color is difficult to comprehend, like blue, diamond, emerald, and red gold. He is our Koothanar in Kudanthai Keezhkottam, where the beautiful, gem-like Ponni river flows.) Mudikonda valarmathiyum moonraayth thondrum Mulai nyaayiru anna malar kangal moonrum Adikonda silamboliyum arulaar sothi Ani muruval sevvaayum azhagaayth thondra Thudikonda idaimadavaal paagam kondu Sudar sothikkadi sempon malai polinaal Kudikondu en manaththagaththai pugunthaar polum Kudanthai Keezhkottaththu em Koothanare. (Gloss: He is like the one who entered my heart and made it his abode, with the growing moon on his head, three eyes appearing like the rising sun, the sound of anklets on his feet, a graceful radiance, and a beautiful red mouth with a gentle smile, taking the slender-waisted maiden as his part, shining like a mountain of pure gold. He is our Koothanar in Kudanthai Keezhkottam.) Kaarilangu thiruvuruvath thavarkkum mattra Kamalaththil kaaranarkkum kaatchiyonraa Seerilangu thalar pilambil sivanthaar polum Silai valaiviththu avunar puram siththaar polum Paarilangu punal anal kaal paramaakaasam Parithimathi suruthiyumaayp paranthaar polum Koorilangu vel kumaran thaathai polum Kudanthai Keezhkottaththu em Koothanare. (Gloss: He is like the one whose sacred form is not visible to those with dark bodies and to Brahma, the creator. He is like the one who became red in the glorious, trembling chasm. He is like the one who bent the bow and destroyed the cities of the demons.

He is like the one who spread as earth, water, fire, air, ether, sun, moon, and Vedas. He is like the father of the sharp-speared Kumaran. He is our Koothanar in Kudanthai Keezhkottam.) Poochchoozhntha pozhil thazhuvugalur uLLaar Purampayaththaar arampurip poonthuruththi pukku Maachchoozhntha pazhanaththaar naithaanaththaar Maathavaththu valarchchottruththuraiyaar nalla Theechchoozhththa thigiri Thirumaalukku eendhu Thiruvanaikkaavil or silanthikku annaal Kochchozhar kulaththarasu koduththaar polum Kudanthai Keezhkottaththu em Koothanare. (Gloss: He is like our Koothanar in Kudanthai Keezhkottam, who resides in the flower-encircled groves of Thazhuvugalur, who entered the sacred Thoonthuruththi of Purampayaththar, who resides in the vast fields, who is in Naithaanam, who is in the growing penance of Valarchchottruththurai, who gave the fire-encircled discus to Thirumal, and who, on that day, gave the kingdom of the Chola dynasty to a spider in Thiruvanaikkaavu.) Pongaravar puliththolar puraanar maarbil Porikizhar ven poonool punithar polum Sangaravak kadanmugadu thatta vittu Sathura nadam aattugantha Saivar polum Angarava thiruvadikkaa pizhaiththa thanthai Anthananai ara erinthaarkku arulappothe Kongaravachchadai kondrai koduththaar polum Kudanthai Keezhkottaththu em Koothanare. (Gloss: He is like the ancient one with a roaring serpent, tiger skin, and a sacred white thread on his chest. He is like the Saiva who loved to perform the graceful dance, striking the top of the ocean. He is like the one who, at that moment, bestowed grace upon the Brahmin father who cut off the leg of his son, who had erred at the sacred feet of the serpent. He is like the one who gave the Konrai flower to his fragrant matted locks.

He is our Koothanar in Kudanthai Keezhkottam.) Eviyidar kadalidaip pattu izhakkindrenai Ippiravi aruttheera vaangi aange Koovi amarulagu anaiththu muruvi poga Kuriyilaru gunaththaandu kondar polum Thaavi muthal Kaavirinal Yamunai Gangai Saraswathi potramarai putkarani thenneer Koviyadu Kumari varu theertham soozhntha Kudanthai Keezhkottaththu em Koothanare. (Gloss: He is like the one who, having called me who was suffering in the sea of troubles, took me to cut off this birth and made me cross over to the world of gods, ruling me with his six qualities. He is our Koothanar in Kudanthai Keezhkottam, surrounded by the leaping Kaveri, the good Yamuna, Ganga, Saraswati, the golden lotus, the Pushkarani, the clear waters, the Goviyadu, and the Kumari rivers.) Serikonda sinthai athanul thelinthu theri Thiththikkum Sivabhuvanaththu amuthampolum Nerikonda kuzhaliyumai paagamaga Nirainthamarar ganam vananga nindraar polum Marikonda karathalaththu em mainthar polum Mathil Ilangai kon malanga varai keezhittu Kurikonda innisai kettuganthaar polum Kudanthai Keezhkottaththu em Koothanare. (Gloss: He is like the ambrosia of Sivabhuvanam, sweetening the mind that has become clear and understood. He is like the one who stands with the beautiful-haired Uma as his part, worshipped by the host of gods. He is like our Lord with the deer in his hand. He is like the one who, when the king of Lanka was confused, pressed the mountain down and was pleased to hear the sweet music. He is our Koothanar in Kudanthai Keezhkottam.)

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped Thirukudanthai Keezhkottam, reached the sacred place called Thirukudanthai Karonam and sang praises to the Lord there. The pathigam sung by Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar for Thirukudanthai Karonam is not available to us due to our lack of merit. The Sthala Purana of this place can be found in the Purana of Aludaiya Pillaiyar.

Following this, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal reaches the sacred place called Thirunalur. The Thirupathigam sung by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal for this Thirunalur sacred place is not available to us. This place’s many special features will be discussed later when this Thirupathigam appears elsewhere.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped Thirunalur, reaches the sacred place called Thirucherai. We shall proceed with our reflection. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 397, Thirunindracharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped the sacred places of Thiruvalanjuzhi, Adi Kumbeswarar Temple in Thirukudamookku, Thirukudanthai Keezhkottam, Thirukudanthai Karonam, and Thirunalur, reaches the sacred place called Thirucherai. This is the ninety-fifth sthalam among the sacred places on the southern bank of the Kaveri in the Chola country. It is located near Nachiyar Koil, close to Kumbakonam. Arisilkkarai Puthur, Thirunaraiyur, Nalur Mayanam, and Kudavayil are nearby sacred places.

This village, like Aattur and Aarai, is colloquially known as Cherai, a corruption of Saettrur. In Thevaram hymns, this place is referred to as “Sennellar Vayal Cherai” and a prosperous city surrounded by fields. Sage Markandeya and Sage Dhaumya Muni The sacred place worshipped by this Peruman is Thiru-Chenneriyappar, and the Goddess’s name is Gnana-Valli. It is also known as Udaiyar Kovil. The shrine faces east. Opposite the temple is a sacred tank called Gnana-Vavi.

After passing through the short gopuram entrance, there is an outer prakaram with a flagstaff, Nandi, and balipeetams. To the right is an ornamental mandapam where the Panchamurtis are enshrined. After circumambulating and passing through the second gopuram entrance with three tiers, upon entering the temple and circumambulating the first prakaram, one can worship Vinayagar in the Kanni-Moolai. In the adjacent mandapam, there is a Shiva Lingam worshipped by Markandeyar and idols of Ambal. In the next mandapam, there are the Sapta Matrikas and the Samaya Kuravargal.

Next, Murugapperuman appears as Bala-Subramaniar. Following that are Gaja-Lakshmi and Jyeshta-Devi. A small mandapam continuously surrounds the Garbhagriham. In the niches, to the south is Vinayagar. Natarajar, Rishabharudar, Dakshinamurthy, and to the north, Kala-Bhairavar and three Durgas are present. In the Ishana direction are Natarajar, and to the east are Suryan and Sanibhagavan.

The Peruman’s temple comprises an Asthana Mandapam, Maha Mandapam, Snapana Mandapam, Ardha Mandapam, and Garbhagriham. At the entrance of the Snapana Mandapam are Dvarapalakas and Dvara-Vinayagar. Opposite the Peruman are Nandi and balipeetams. Thiru-Chenneriyappar is manifest in a beautiful circular avudaiyar. The banam is large, a divine form with the power to attract our hearts. After worshipping the Peruman, one can reach the Ambal shrine.

The Ambal temple is in the outer prakaram to the left of the Peruman’s temple. The shrine faces east and is adorned with a beautiful front mandapam. Arulmigu Gnana-Valliyammai grants darshan. This sacred temple also bears the name Saraparameswarar for the Peruman. The Sthala Vriksham is the Mango tree. The sacred tank is Markanda Tirtham.

For this sacred Thiru-Sthalam, there is one Thiru-Padigam composed by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and two Thiru-Padigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, totaling three Thiru-Padigams. The Thiru-Padigam composed by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman for this Thiru-Sthalam is called Vali Mozhi Thiru-Viragam. This is a metrical Thiru-Padigam sung with a predominance of short vowels. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, who visited this sacred Thiru-Sthalam, composed two Thiru-Padigams. The first of these Thiru-Padigams is the seventy-third Thiru-Padigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Ner-Isai Thiru-Padigam.

Perunthiru Himavan petra penkodi pirintha pinnai varunthuvan thangal seyya ma manam punarnthu mannum arunthiru meni than pal angoru pakamaka thirunthida vaithar Serai Chenneri Selvanare. Orthulavaru nokki unmaiyai unara kundar. Varthaiyai meyyendru enni mayakkil veezhnthu azhunthuvayenai porthanai alakondu piravivan pinikalellam theertharul seithar Serai Chenneri Selvanare. Ondriya thavaththu manni udaiyan ulappil kalam nindru thang kadalgal eththu neezh silai visaiyanukku vendrigol vedanaki virumbi veng kanagaththu sendru arul seithar Serai Chenneri Selvanare. Anjaiyum adakki atral udaiyanay anek kalam vanjamiravath thunindru manniya bhagiratharkku venjina mugangalaki visaiyodu payum Gangai senjadaiyettar Serai Chenneri Selvanare.

Niraintha ma manalaik kuppi nesamodu avin palai karanthu kondattak kandu karuthathan thathai thalai erintha manikku appothe ezhilkol Chandeesan ena sirantha peyaralithar Serai Chenneri Selvanare. Viriththapal kathirgal soolam vedipadu thamarugangai thariththathor kola kala Bhairavanaki velam uriththu umai anjak kandu onthiru manivay villach chiriththarul seithar Serai Chenneri Selvanare. Sutrumun imaiyor nindru thozhuthu thu malargal thuvi matramai uyakkol ena mannuvan purangal moonrum utroru nodiyin munnam ol azhal vayil veezhach chetrorul seithar Serai Chenneri Selvanare. Munthiya ivvulagamellam padaithavan malinodum enthaninathanenru irainji nindru etthal seyya anthamil sothithannai adimudi ariyavannam senthazhal anar Serai Chenneri Selvanare. Oruvaru nikarilatha onthiral arakkanodi perumvarai eduththa thinthol pirangiya mudigalitru mariviyam Peruman enna malaradi mella vangi thiruvaru. Seithar Serai Chenneri Selvanare.

Now, the second Thiru-Padigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Cherai Thiru-Sthalam is the Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Padigam. It is compiled as the seventy-seventh Thiru-Padigam in the Fifth Thiru-Murai.

Puriyavarum punniyam poikedum koorithaya arivu kai koodidum seeriyarpayil Seraiyul Chenneri Naribaganthannamam navilave. Ennamathavam seithanai nenjame minnu varsadai veda vizhupporul chennalar vayal Seraiyul Chenneri mannu sothi nambal vandhu vaigave. Pirappu mooppum perum pasi van pini irappu neengi ingu inbam vandhu eithidum sirappar Seraiyul Chenneriyan kalal marappathindri manathinul vaikkave. Madu thedi mayakkil veezhnthu neer odi eithum payanilai oomarkal. Sedervaal Serai Chenneri mevya adalan than adaiyadaithu uyminne.

Enninnalum eriyiyal kootruvan thun en thondril thurakkum vazhikanden thinnanjerai Thiruchenneriyurai annalar ular anjuvathu ennukke. Thappi vanam tharani kambikkilen oppil venthar orungudan seeril en seppaman Serai Chenneri mevya appanar ular anjuvathu ennukke. Vaithamadu madanthai nallarkalum oththavathavuttarkalum en seivar siththar Serai Thiruchenneriyurai aththartham ular anjuvathu ennukke. Kulangal en seiva kutrangalen seiva thulangini nindru sornthidal nenjame ilangku Seraiyil Chenneri mevya alanganar ular anjuvathu ennukke. Pazhaginal varum pandula sutram. Mum vilavidavidil vendiya eithona thigazhkol Seraiyil Chenneri mevya azhaganaru ular anjuvathu ennukke.

Porundhu neenmalaiyai pidithu enthinan varuntha oondri malaradi vanginan thirundhu Seraiyil Chenneri mevayirundha sothi enbarkku idar illaiye.

These are the two Thiru-Padigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for Thiru-Cherai Thiru-Sthalam. Sekkizhar Peruman mentions that Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal visited the sacred Thiru-Sthalams of Nalur, Cherai, Kudavayil, and Naraiyur. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar must have gone from Nalur in a northwesterly direction to reach Thiru-Cherai, then returned along the same path to the southeast to reach Kudavayil, and then proceeded north along that path to reach Naraiyur.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, after worshipping Thiru-Cherai, visited Thiru-Kudavayil Thiru-Sthalam. This is the ninety-fourth Thiru-Sthalam on the southern bank of the Kaveri. The Thiru-Padigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar for this Thiru-Sthalam is not available to us.

Next, he proceeds to the sacred Thiru-Sthalam called Thiru-Naraiyur. This Thiru-Sthalam is the sixty-fifth Thiru-Sthalam on the southern bank of the Kaveri. Siddheeswaram is the name of the temple in this sacred Thiru-Sthalam. The Thiru-Padigam sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for this Thiru-Sthalam is also not available to us. Sekkizhar Peruman sings that Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having thus worshipped, proceeds to many more sacred Thiru-Sthalams. The sacred Thiru-Sthalams indicated as “Idambala” must be Peenu Perunthurai, Nalur Mayanam, and other such places.

Having thus worshipped, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal reaches the sacred Thiru-Sthalam called Thiru-Vanchiyam. There, he sings a Thiru-Padigam.

Let us go on contemplating. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 398. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal arrives at Thiru-Vanchiyam Thiru-Sthalam, also known as Sri Vanchiyam. This is the sacred place where Maha Vishnu, desiring Sri, meaning Lakshmi, worshipped the Lord.

Hence, it is called Sri Vanchiyam. It is the seventieth Thiru-Sthalam on the southern bank of the Kaveri. The Peruman’s sacred name is Vanchiyanathar. Ambal is Mangala Nayaki, also known as Vazhavandha Nayaki. The sacred tank is Gupta Gangai. The sacred tree is the Sandalwood tree.

This Thiru-Sthalam called Sri Vanchiyam is near the town of Nannilam in Tamil Nadu. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, from Thiru-Naraiyur Siddheeswaram, traveled south along the southern bank of the Thirumalarajan River on the way to Nannilam, came to Sri Vanchiyam, and worshipped the Lord here. All the glories of this Thiru-Sthalam are praised in the Puranas such as Skandam, Brahmandam, and Agneyam. In the book Shiva Bhoga Saram, it is mentioned that Sri Vanchiyam is one of the sacred places equal to Kasi. This sacred place has the holy names Bhu Kailasam, Narayana Ashramam, Gandharanyam, and Sri Vanchiyam. Sri Vanchiyam is called Thiru-Vilayur in Tamil.

As we have already seen, since Thirumal desired, longed for, and attained Lakshmi in this sacred place, it is named Thiru-Vilayur. Since Vishnu worshipped Shiva Peruman here and resided here, this sacred place has the holy name Narayana Ashramam. As this sacred place possesses fragrant sandalwood trees, it is named Gandharanyam. Name. Various deities, including Brahma, Gautama, Jamadagni, Kashyapa, Atri, Vishwamitra, Bharadvaja, Vasishtha, Parashara, Valmiki, King Magudavarthana, the Chola king Veerathanusu, Krishna, Lakshmi, Indra, Vikukshi, and his wife Charumati, worshipped the Lord in this sacred place and attained their desires, rejoicing.

Here, there is a sacred tank called Punya Pushkarani. In Kali Yuga, it is known as Muni Tirtham. In previous Yugas, this same Tirtham was known as Thuya Pushkarani, Atri Tirtham, and Parashara Tirtham, respectively. Sages like Kashyapa, fearing the evils of Kali, came to this sacred place, bathed in this Tirtham, and performed severe penance.

King Magudavarthana Chola, when threatened by enemies, bathed in this Tirtham according to Parashara’s command, defeated his enemies, and attained glory. A Kshatriya named Mahathanusu bathed in this Tirtham, was freed from his demonic form, and attained bliss. Charumati, afflicted with leprosy due to a curse, came and bathed in this Tirtham and was cured of her disease. A Vaishya named Dharmadhvajan, upon bathing in this Tirtham and departing his life, ascended to Kailasam in a golden vimanam. Ganga, by the command of Easwara, immersed herself in this water and reduced her sins.

Hence, this Tirtham is called Gupta Ganga. Surrounding this Tirtham are many other Tirthams, such as Brahma Tirtham and Narada Tirtham. The demon Veera Nakthanjan, who approached Agastya Muni with the intention of devouring him, was kicked by Agastya and, by the merit of his good deeds, fell into this Tirtham, was freed from sin, and ascended to Svargam. Surya This Tirtham absolved Surya of the sin of Shiva-droha. This Tirtham removed the Brahmahatya dosha of the Brahmin named Paripadran.

Thus, it is understood that this Pushkarani has the power to remove even the five great sins. Those who bathe in this Tirtham on Sundays attain a higher state. Especially, those who bathe in this Tirtham on Sundays in the month of Karthigai are purified from sin, become pure, and attain their desired boons. The Peruman of this sacred place is Sarvalokadhipathi, the all-powerful. The Peruman’s sacred name is Thiru-Vanchinathar. Since he was worshipped by Brahma Devar, he bears the sacred name Nalinasanar.

By the request of Agastya Muni, the Peruman also has the name Agastheeswarar. He also bears the sacred name Prakrutheeswarar. One of the By removing the sin of murder, the Peruman also bears the sacred name Punaruknesar. As he suppressed Kali, he also bears the sacred name Kali Nigrakar. Since he is seated amidst sandalwood trees, the Peruman is also known by the sacred name Sri Gandharanyar. In Tamil, the Peruman is called Sandanavananathar.

This Bhu Kailasanathar, at the request of Yama, granted him dominion and accepted him as his mount.

Therefore, in this sacred place, the Peruman is praised as Yamavahanan. In this sacred place, the Peruman appeared as a gem in Kritha Yuga, as gold in Treta Yuga, and as silver in Dvapara Yuga. The Sthala Ithiham states that the kalas of all the Lingams in all sacred places come and merge into this Shiva Lingam at midnight every day. The Sthala Ithiham also states that at dawn, all those kalas return to their respective Lingams in those sacred places. During the time of Pralaya, this Lingam shines as a fiery, luminous form.

Furthermore, the Peruman here appears as a Svayambhu Murthi, a self-manifested Lingam that emerged from the netherworld for the welfare of the world. The sacred name of the Ambigai in this sacred place is Vazhavandha Nayaki. She also has the sacred name Mangala Nayaki. Since Ambal came from her sacred hand to this sacred place to receive blessings, she is also called Bhagya Nayaki. What is special about this sacred place is the shrine of Yama. Yama, who takes all lives, was freed from that sin by worshipping the Lord here.

He also received the boon of being the Lord’s mount in this sacred place.

Therefore, Yama himself is the Kshetrapalaka here. Regular daily pujas and monthly festivals are conducted in this sacred place. In the month of Masi, a Brahmotsavam is held for Somaskanda Murthi. The Brahmotsavam begins on Ashvathi Nakshatram and concludes with the Yama Tirtham and Theerthavari on Bharani and Magam. Since Yama is the Lord’s mount and Kshetrapalaka here, and since the Lord grants Yama Tirtham on Bharani in the month of Masi during the Brahmotsavam, those who live and die in this sacred place are not subjected to Yama’s torment. So says the Sthala Puranam.

The Sthala Puranam states that the Lord whispers the Panchaksharam into the right ear of those who die in this sacred place and unites them with Shiva Lokam. As we have already seen, the Lord grants Tirtham in this sacred tank, known as Gupta Ganga, on Sundays in the month of Karthigai. Ganga always resides in this Tirtham, the Gupta Ganga. The Sthala Puranam states that Ganga, leaving only one of her kalas in Kasi, resides here in Sri Vanchiyam in Gupta Ganga with nine hundred and ninety-nine kalas. That is why this Tirtham is named Gupta Ganga. It is in this Tirtham that the Lord grants Tirtham on Sundays in the month of Karthigai.

At that time, people bathe in the Gupta Ganga, perform ablutions, and seek liberation. This sacred place has the distinction of being sung by the Three. There is one Thiru-Padigam each sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, and Sundaramurthi Swamigal for this sacred place.

Thus, there are three Thevara Padigams for this sacred place. Arunagirinathar has composed two Thiru-Pugazhs for Murugan of this sacred place. There is a Sthala Puranam in Sanskrit for this sacred place and a Sthala Puranam in Tamil composed by Kalandai Kumaran. Manikkavasagar has sung about this sacred place in Thiruvasagam, in Keerthi Thiru Agaval, saying “Thiru-Vanchiyathil Seerpera Irundhum.” He has also mentioned this sacred place in Thiru-Kovaiyar. In such a special sacred place, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman has composed the Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Padigam. Five The Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Padigam is arranged as the sixty-seventh Thiru-Padigam in the Thiru-Murai.

Padaiyum boothamum pambum pulvay adaiyum thangiya utthamanarku idam pudai nilaviya poompozhil Vanchiyam adaiyavallu allal onrillaiye. Parappaiyum pasuvum paduthu pala thiraththavum udaiyor thigazhum pathi karaippiraichchadai kannuthal ser tharu sirappudai Thiru-Vanchiyam sermine. Putril adaravodu punal mathi thetru senjadai thevar piranpathi sutru madangal soozh Thiru-Vanchiyam patti paduvarkku pavam illaiye. Angam arum arumarai nankudan thangum velviyartham payilum nagar sengannmalidamar Thiru-Vanchiyam thangkuvar nam. Amararkku amarare neeru poosi nimir sadaimel pirai arusuudum adigal uraipathi maruthan orungum vayal Vanchiyam theri vazhbavarkku selvam agume.

Atru patrindri yaraiyum illavarkku utra natrunai avan uraipathi thetrumadangal soozh Thiru-Vanchiyam katru serpavarkkum karuthavathe. The seventh, eighth, and ninth Thiru-Padalgal of this Thiru-Padigam are not available to us.

Now, the tenth song: Arukkan angi yamanadu thevargal thiruththum sevadiyan thigazhum nagar oruththi pakam ugandhavan Vanchiyam aruthiyall adaiwarkku illai allale.

Those who are able to reach Thiru-Vanchiyam will have no suffering, no sin, and will attain wealth. He will be the Lord of all immortals. These are the notes of this Padigam. According to the Sthala Puranam, in this sacred place, the deities such as Arukkan (Surya), Angi (Agni Bhagavan), Yama, and other deities worshipped the Lord of this sacred place and received blessings. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal sings about this Sthala history in the tenth Thiru-Padal.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, who set out with the desire to reach Thiruvarur, visits various sacred places along the way, sings Thiru-Padigams, and continues his journey towards Thiruvarur, visiting sacred places such as Thiru-Peruvelur, Thiru-Vilamar, and Thiru-Karaveeram. However, the Padigams sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for these sacred places are not available to us.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal reaches Thiruvarur. Peruvacha Malar Sekkizhar Peruman sings that after worshipping Peruvelur, he praised the Lord of the fragrant Konrai flowers and other sacred places, went with Thiruvarur Vilamar, worshipped, and then Vakkisar, who burned the three cities, reached Thiruvarur.

The devotees residing in Thiruvarur are those who have received the abundant grace of the Lord. They are worthy of liberation by virtue of being born in Thiruvarur. “I am a servant to all” is the sacred saying of Sundaramurthi Swamigal. Hearing the blessed news that Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, who is of such greatness, has arrived in Thiruvarur, all the devotees residing in Thiruvarur decorate the houses, mansions, and streets of Thiruvarur with auspiciousness.

Thus, the beauty of Thiruvarur shone even more brightly. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is the great one who overcame the illusion of the Jains and crossed the ocean using a stone as a raft. All the Shiva devotees of Thiruvarur rejoice that such a great Peruman, who has received such divine grace, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, has arrived in their Thiruvarur. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s act of transforming a stone into a raft and floating on it was an extraordinary feat. Even greater was his overcoming the illusion of the Jains. The Thiruvarur Thiru-Thondars praise and admire Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, extolling these great acts of divine grace.

The Nayanar of immeasurable greatness.

Thus, the devotees of Shiva residing in Thiruvarur joyfully welcome, greet, and worship Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar. The Shiva devotees of Thiruvarur thus welcome and worship Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar worships and praises those Thiru-Thondars of Thiruvarur, for the Shiva devotees of Thiruvarur are the Thondars of Vanmeeganathar, who is enshrined in an anthill. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman worships the devotees of Thiruvarur, thinking that he has been blessed with the merit of being a Thondar to those Thondars. He considers himself a humble one who has come here to be saved from the great sinners, the Jains, and to be cured of his illness. He wonders if he is worthy of such a great blessing.

Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, contemplating whether he is worthy of such a blessing, enters the sacred streets of Thiruvarur, devoid of self-consciousness.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman worships and approaches the Thiru-Thondars of Thiruvarur and the sacred streets of Thiruvarur. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar’s recovery from the colic disease and his arrival at Thiru-Adigai was an act of divine grace. The trident and bull symbols were branded on Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s shoulder at Thiru-Thungaanai Maadam. This was a boon he received by praying to the Lord. He had prayed that he would not live with the body that had been associated with the Jains and the evil that came from being with them. In accordance with that prayer, at Thiru-Thunga- The trident and bull symbols were branded on his sacred shoulder at Anai Maadam.

Here, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman prays to the Lord in Thiruvarur for bodily purification, for the ever-increasing experience of Shiva-ananda, and for the blessing of being with the devotees of Thiruvarur, which is also the companionship of devotees. The twelfth sutra of Sivagnanabodham speaks of the principle that one should worship the guise of those who have attained and the Shiva temple as a refuge. In accordance with this, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman here worships the devotees of Thiruvarur and Thiruvarur, praying for the ever-increasing experience of Shiva-ananda. “Having escaped the illness that afflicted me due to the great sinners, the Jains, who had no attachment, I came to be saved.” “I have been blessed with the merit of being a Thondar to the Lord who resides in the anthill.” With this feeling, he entered the sacred streets of Thiruvarur, as described in the sacred verse composed by Sekkizhar Peruman.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, contemplating whether he is worthy of the merit of being a Thondar to the Thondars of the Lord who resides in the anthill, melts in devotion and enters the sacred streets of Thiruvarur. Accordingly, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal sings in each verse of the Thiruviruttam he composed, “The merit of being a Thondar to the Thondars.” That sacred hymn, which begins with “Kulambalam Paavaru,” is referred to by Sekkizhar Swamigal in his own verse. Appar Swamigal has composed twenty-one sacred hymns for the sacred sthalam of Thiruvarur. Among them, this The sacred hymn composed at this time, when he entered the sacred streets of Thiruvarur, is the 101st sacred hymn of the Fourth Thirumurai, the Thiruviruttam. This sacred hymn was sung by Appar Swamigal in the sacred streets of Thiruvarur with the feeling that he had been blessed with the merit of being a Thondar to the Thondars of Thirumoolattanathar.

“Kulambalam Paavaru Kundar Munne Namakku Undu Kolo Alambalam Paavaru Than Punal Aroor Avirchadaiyan Silambalam Paavaru Sevadiyan Thirumoolattanam Pulambalam Paavaru Thondarkku Thondaram Punniyame.” “Is there any merit for us, who have left our homes and renounced all other places, to be a Thondar to the Thondars of the Lord who resides in the anthill, who became a hunter and bought a place with Vijayan?” “Is there any merit for us, who stand without form before the Kundars, to be a Thondar to the Thondars of the Lord who destroyed the three cities with his fierce bow, who is the Lord of Thiruvarur, Thirumoolattanam, the Lord with the red-eyed bull?” “Is there any merit for us, who have left the Jains with their impure bodies and cruel hearts, and who remember and praise the Lord, to be a Thondar to the Thondars of the Lord of Thiruvarur, Thirumoolattanam, who is worshipped by the Brahmins?” “Is there any merit for us, who have left the Jains who do not speak while eating, and who have come to remember and praise the Lord, to be a Thondar to the Thondars of the Lord of Thiruvarur, Thirumoolattanam, who has a strong fort and who is worshipped by the ascetics?” “The swollen shoulders and feet,” “Is there any merit for us, who eat like mutes before the foolish ones, to be a Thondar to the Thondars of the Lord of Thiruvarur, Thirumoolattanam, who has beautiful lotus feet and who resides in the fragrant groves?” “Is there any merit for us, who have left the Jains who speak of the scriptures and who have attained the grace of the Lord, to be a Thondar to the Thondars of the Lord of Thiruvarur, Thirumoolattanam, who has a strong fort and who is our benefactor?” “Is there any merit for us, who have left the Jains who say that shaving the head is happiness, and who have come here to be saved, to be a Thondar to the Thondars of the Lord of Thiruvarur, Thirumoolattanam, who is the Lord of Thirukailai and who is worshipped by his beloved devotees?” “Is there any merit for us, who have left the Jains who eat standing with food in their hands, and who have found the path to salvation and come here to be saved?” “Is there any merit for us, to be a Thondar to the Thondars of the Lord of Thiruvarur, Thirumoolattanam, who has beautiful fields, and who has true love?” “Is there any merit for us, who have left the sinful Jains and who have come to perform good deeds and be saved, to be a Thondar to the Thondars of the Lord with the golden anklets, who crushed the strength of Ravana with his mighty shoulders?”

Let us continue to contemplate Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s darshan of Thiruvarur. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 399. Thirunindrachcharukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, accompanied by the Shiva devotees of Thiruvarur, proceeds through the sacred streets of Thiruvarur and reaches the sacred entrance of the temple in Thiruvarur, where archways shine.

There, he comes before the Devasiriyamandapam and worships. The Devasiriyamandapam is a sacred hall where many great souls, filled with the grace of the Lord, are eternally seated. It is a hall where gods and others always wait outside to receive the grace of those sacred souls. It is a hall where gods always seek refuge. Sekkizhar Peruman has sung about the Devasiriyamandapam in 130 verses at the beginning of the Periya Puranam.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped the Devasiriyamandapam, enters the temple through the sacred entrances of the great temple, which resembles the Chakravazha mountain. In the Thiruvarur Thiru-Poongoyil, in the Thiruvarur temple, after passing the first gopuram entrance, the Devasiriyamandapam is the first thing in the outer courtyard. After worshipping it, there is the first entrance to the sacred mansion. This is the entrance where Thiyagaraja Peruman appeared to Sundaramurthy Swamigal and commanded him to sing the Thiru-Thonda Thogai, and also gave him the first line, “Adiyarkkum Adiyen” (I am a servant to the servants of the Thillai Vazh Andanars). Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman worships this entrance and enters. He passes through many sacred entrances and reaches the sanctum of Thirumoolattanathar.

Sekkizhar sings: “Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, with the surrounding sacred devotees, reached the archway, bowed before the glorious, tall Devasiriyan, entered the sacred mansion’s entrance, and directly beheld the Lord who resides in the anthill, shining like a great jewel.” The Lord who resides in the anthill is known by various names such as Vanmeeganathar and Putridam Kondanathar, and is enshrined as Thirumoolattanathar. There, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman beheld the Lord, manifesting fully in his entire consciousness. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, seeing the Lord, was immersed in the resulting bliss. He saw, worshipped, and fell prostrate, his hands and feet and other limbs He worshipped with goosebumps on his limbs. As his love overflowed, tears streamed from his eyes like rain.

Then, praising the lotus-like feet of Thirumoolattanathar, he composed the Thiruthandagam hymn, “Kandale Karuthai Ninaithu” (Contemplating only seeing). Sekkizhar Peruman describes this in two sacred verses: “Standing before the self-luminous light, like an unextinguished lamp, the Lord who resides in the anthill, he praised and melted in devotion. With a heart full of love, he circumambulated the beautiful temple and worshipped, then exited through the long sacred entrance.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman beholds the Lord who resides in the anthill. He worships. He falls prostrate on the ground. His hands, feet, and other limbs are covered in goosebumps.

He worships. As love overflows, tears stream from his eyes like rain.

At that time, praising and extolling the lotus-like feet of Thirumoolattanathar, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman composes the Thiruthandagam hymn. This is the Potri Thiruthandagam dedicated to Thiruvarur Thirumoolattanam, composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. This is the second sacred hymn composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar in Thiruvarur. Because the words “Potri, Potri” (Praise, Praise) appear in this Thiruthandagam, it is called Potri Thiruthandagam. It is the 32nd sacred hymn in the Sixth Thirumurai.

“Katravar Unnum Kaniye Potri, Kazhaladainthar Sellum Gathiye Potri, Atravarukku Aaramudham Aanai Potri, Allal Aruthu Adiyenai Aan” “Undai Potri, Matroruvar Oppilla Maintha Potri, Vaanavargal Potrum Marundhe Potri, Settravartham Purameritha Sivane Potri, Thirumoolattanane Potri Potri. Vangamali Kadal Nanjam Undai Potri, Madaiyanai Eerurivai Porthai Potri, Kongalarum Narungondrai Thaarai Potri, Kolpuli Thol Aadai Kuzhaga Potri. Malaiyan Madanthai Manala Potri, Mazhavidaiyai Nin Paatham Potri Potri.

“Nilaiyaga En Nenjil Nindrai Potri, Netrimel Otrai Kan Udaiyai Potri, Ilaiyar” “Moovilai Vel Enthi Potri, Ezh Kadalum Ezh Pozhilum Aanai Potri, Silaiyal Eyil Eritha Sivane Potri, Thirumoolattanane Potri Potri. Ponniyalum Meniyane Potri Potri, Boothappadai Udaiyai Potri Potri, Manniyasir Marai Nankum Aanai Potri, Mariyenthu Kaiyane Potri Potri. “Thiru Meikkanintha Sothi Potri, Senchadaiyai Nin Paatham Potri Potri, Thirumoolattanane Potri Potri. Sankarane Nin Paatham Potri Potri, Sadhasivane Nin Paatham Potri Potri, Pongarava Nin Paatham Potri Potri, Punniyane Nin Paatham Potri Potri. Angamal Thayanodu Maalum Kanaa Analuruvai Nin Paatham Potri Potri, Sengamal Thiruppaatham Potri Potri, Thirumoolattanan Potri Potri. Vambalavu Kondrai Sadaiyai Potri, Vaanpiraiyum Vazharavum Vaithai Potri, Kombanai Nunniyadiyal Koorai Potri, Kuraikazhalal Kootruthaitha Kove Potri. Nambum Avarkku Arumporule Potri Potri, Naalvedham Aarankam Aanai Potri, Semponne Maragathame Maniye Potri, Thiru” “Moolattanane Potri Potri.

“Ullamai Ullathe Nindrai Potri, Ugappar Manathu Endrum Neengai Potri, Vallale Potri Manala Potri, Vaanavarkon Thol Thunitha Maintha Potri, Vellai Eru Erum Vigirtha Potri, Melorkkum Melorkkum Melai Potri, Thelluneer Gangai Sadaiyai Potri, Thirumoolattanane Potri Potri. Poovarntha Senni Punitha Potri, Puththeli Potrum Porule Potri, Thevaarntha Devarkkum Deve Potri, Thirumalukku Aali Azhithai Potri, Saavame Kaathennai Aandai Potri, Sangoththa Neetru En Sathura Potri, Sevaarntha Velkodiyai Potri Potri, Thirumoolattanane Potri Potri. Piraman Than Siram Arintha Periyoi Potri,” “Pennuruvodu Aanuruvai Nindrai Potri, Kara Nankum Mukkanum Udaiyai Potri, Kaathalipparkku Atra Eliyai Potri, Arumantha Devarkku Arase Potri, Andarakan Ainanku Tholum Thaalum Siraneritha Sevadiyai Potri Potri, Thirumoolattanane Potri Potri.

“” The glories of the Lord are praised in many ways in this sacred hymn. The word “Potri” (Praise) is used 108 times in these sacred hymns. This is a unique feature of this sacred hymn.

“Similarly, the hymns of Thiru-Adigai Potri Thiruthandagam and Thirukailaya Potri Thiruthandagam are also worshipped by devotees as hymns of adoration to the Lord.

“Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having sung the Potri Thiruthandagam, Sekkizhar Peruman sings that Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, who sang the hymn beginning with “Kandale Karuthai Ninaithu” (Contemplating only seeing), stands before the Lord who resides in the anthill, who is a self-luminous light like an unextinguished lamp, and praises Him. This sacred hymn begins with “Kandale Karuthai Ninaithu.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, who was in Thirunallur, desired to worship Thiruvarur. He visited various sthalams and came to Thiruvarur, did he not? He desired to worship Thiruvarur. This sacred hymn begins by explaining that he contemplated only worshipping Thiruvarur. This is the twentieth sacred hymn in the Fourth Thirumurai.

“Sekkizhar Peruman refers to this sacred hymn as Kalaippathigam (Hymn of Arts). The sacred hymns that are a place for many arts and sciences to flourish What is it?

“Therefore, it is called the hymn of arts and sciences. This sacred hymn is set in the Seegamarappann.

““Kandale Karuthai Ninaithirunthen Manam Pugunthai Kazhaladi Poondhu Kondu Olinthen Puramboyinal Arayo Eendu Maadangal Neenda Maaligai Mel Ezhu Kodi Vaan Ilam Mathi Theendi Vanthu Ulavum Thiruvarur Ammanae. Kadambada Nadamaadinai Kalaigan Inakkoru Kaathal Seithadi Odungi Vanthu Adaindhen Ozhippai Pizhaippavellam Mudangiran Muthuneer Malangizha Vaazhai Sengayal Sel Varaal Kaliru Adaintha Than Kalani Ani Aroor Ammanae. Arumani Thadamboo Mulai Arambaiyarudu Arulipaadiyar Urimaiyil Thozhuvaar” “Rudhra Palkanaththar Virisadai Virathigal Andhanar Saivar Pasupathar Kapaaligal Theruvinil Poliyum Thiruvarur Ammanae. Poongazhal Thozhuthum Paraviyum Punniya Punitha Un Porkazhal Eengirukka Pettren Enna Kuraiyudaiyen Ongu Thengilaiyar Kamugu Ilam Vaazhai Maavodu Maathulam Pala Theengani Sitharum Thiruvarur Ammanae.

Pirathalum Piranthal Pinipadavainthu Asainthu Udalam Pugunthu Nindru Irakumaaru Ulathae Izhiththen Pirappinai Naan Arathaiye Purintha Manathanai Aarvachchetra Kurotha Neekki Un Thirathanai Olinthen Thiruvarur Ammanae. Naadinar Kamalam Malar Ayanodu Araniya Naagam Keendavan Naadi Kaana Maattaaththalalai Nambanai Paaduvaar Panivaar Pallandu Isaikkooru Paththargal Siththaththul Pukku Thedi Kandu Kondhen Thiruvarur Ammanae.

“” The summary of this sacred hymn is as follows: “O Lord of Thiruvarur! For many days, I only thought of seeing and worshipping you. That too happened because you entered my mind and graced me. Today, I have come and seen you directly and worshipped your sacred feet. You are my only support and refuge.” “I have come and surrendered to you.

“Please forgive all my mistakes and remove all my faults. Now I have no shortcomings. I have despised this birth, which involves being born and then dying.

“Therefore, I have come and joined you. You reside in my mind. How can you leave me now? I will not leave you anymore. I have embraced you in my heart. Just as I have seen you directly manifest here in Thiruvarur, I have searched and found you within my consciousness.

“I will always be your refuge.” This is how Sivakavimani Ayyavargal writes the summary of this sacred hymn. Let us press on with our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part Four Hundred, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, having worshipped Putridam Konda Nathar at Thiruvarur Poongkoil, sang Thevaram Thiru-Pathigams and returned to the Devasiriya Mandapam.

There, he sang a Thevaram Thiru-Pathigam with the sentiment, “I am a thief who, seeing the cuckoo singing in the flower garden and peacocks dancing in Thiruvarur, did not worship it with my hands, but instead of the ripe fruit, seized the unripe one.” This Thiru-Pathigam by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal is known as the Pazhamozhi Thiru-Pathigam (Proverb Thiru-Pathigam). It is the fifth Thiru-Pathigam in the Fourth Thiru-Murai, set to the Gandhara Pann. In all ten verses of this Thiru-Pathigam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman has sung, placing a proverb at the end of each verse.

Therefore, this Thiru-Pathigam is called the Pazhamozhi Thiru-Pathigam. Sekkizhar Peruman states that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sang a Thiru-Pathigam with such a sentiment, based on the inner meaning of this Thiru-Pathigam, “Koyyula Malarcholai Kuyil Koova.” This sentiment appears in the second part of the first verse of this Thiru-Pathigam: “Koyyula Malarcholai Kuyil Koova Mayilum Arurarai Kaiyinal Thozhadhu Ozhindhu Kaniyirukka Kaikavar Kalvanene.” Sekkizhar Peruman, in his own verse, describes that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sang a Thiru-Pathigam with such a sentiment. “Kaniyiruppa Kaikari” To err is a proverb. The proverb means, “When ripe fruits are available, would anyone prefer to eat unripe ones?” That is, when beneficial things that yield good results are available, would anyone abandon them and pursue things that yield no benefit? No, they would not.

The beneficial thing is to attain the Lord of Thiruvarur. The useless harm is to abandon the path of Shiva and stand in other false paths.

Here, when Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings, the meaning is that he is singing about his association with the harmful and useless Jain religion.

The Lord of Thiruvarur, who gave us this life for our well-being, instead of using it to praise and glorify the Lord of Thiruvarur, he used it in the harmful path, having associated with the Jain religion.

Therefore, when there was a way to attain the Lord of Thiruvarur, who is like a ripe fruit, I joined the Jain association, which is like an unripe fruit.

Thus, the Lord sings, “I am a thief who, when there was fruit, seized the unripe one.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman refers to himself as “Kaniyiruppa Kai Kavarndha Kalvan” (a thief who, when there was fruit, seized the unripe one). The meaning of “kallaththanmai” (thievish nature) is theft, or misappropriating something entrusted. God has given us this life for our well-being.

Therefore, using this life in a bad way is called thievish nature, theft. It means misappropriating this life, which God has entrusted to us, and using it for a different purpose. When Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sang this song, when he sang this Thiru-Pathigam, the state of mental anguish he was in is clearly conveyed to us by this Thiru-Pathigam. Sekkizhar Peruman refers to this as “Eydhariya Kaiyaravu.” “Kaiyaravu” means sorrow. This is because Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman was born into a family with Shaivite leanings. Even though he was born into such a Shaivite family, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman himself willingly went and spent many days in the Jain religion, spending a large part of his life there.

Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sang this Thiru-Pathigam with great regret about this. This is the state of mind Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman was in when he sang this Thiru-Pathigam. Sekkizhar Peruman mentions this.

Thus, this state of mind is expressed in all ten verses, using ten proverbs as similes for his actions, and he sings this Thiru-Pathigam with regret.

Therefore, the summary of this Thiru-Pathigam is that even though Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman had the good fortune to embrace Shaivism, he did not worship the Lord of Thiruvarur, but instead willingly joined the Jain religion and spent a long time there, performing such actions. He sings with regret, using proverbs like “Kaniyirundha Kaikavar Kallam” (the theft of seizing unripe fruit when ripe fruit was available), that all these actions were futile.

Now, this Thiru-Pathigam, Thiruchitrambalam. “Meyyellam Venniru Sannitha Meniyan” Thazhthozhadhe uyalam endru enni uri thookki uli thandhu en ullam vittu Koyyula malarcholai kuyil koova mayil alum Arurarai Kaiyinal thozhadhu ozhindhu kaniyirukka kaikavarndha kazhvanene Enbiruthi narambu thol pugappeidittu ennai or uruvamakki Inbiruthi munbirundha vinai thirthittu en ullam koyilakki Anbiruthi adiyenai koolatkondu arul seytha Arurtham Munbirukkum vidhiyindri muyalvittu kakkai pinponavare Peruguvithu en pavathai pandalam kundargal tham solle kettu Uruguvithu en ullathin ullirundha kallathai thalli pokki Aruguvithu pinikatti atkondu pini thirtha Arurtham Arugi Irukkum vidhiyindri aram irukka maram vilaikku kondavare Kundanai thalai parithu kuvimulaiyar nagai nanadhu olitharvenai Pandama paduthennai paralaiyil thelithu than padam katti Thondalam isaippada thoomuruval arul seyyum Arurarai Pandalam ariyadhe pani niral pavai seyya pavithene Thunnagath thenagi thursanavar sorkettu thuvarvaikkondu Ennagath thirindhu ingu irukai yetridam unda ezhaiye nan Ponnagath thadiyenai pugappeidhu porutpadutha Arurarai En agaththu iruthadhe ethan porkku adhanai agappattene Pappodhi pavanai parithoru thalaiyode thiridharvenai Oppoda odhuvithu en ullathin ullirundhu angu uruthi katti Appodhaikku appodhum adiyavarkku ar amudham Arurarai Eppodhu ninaiyadhe iruttaraiyin maladhu karandhu eythavare Gathiyendrum ariyadhe kan azhalath thalai parithu kaiyilvundu Pathiyondru nedhuveedhi palarkana nagainanadhu olitharverku Mathi thandha Aruril var thenai vaymaduthu parugi uyyum vidhiyindri Mathiyiliyen vilakku irukka minmini thee kayndhavare Poovaiyai thalai parithu poriyatrra saman neesar solle kettu Kavisar kan madavar kandu odi kadhavu adaikkum kalvanen than Avaiyai pogame thavirthu ennai atkondu Arurarai Paviyen ariyadhe paluril payakkambu keythavare Ottadha vazh avunar puram mundru or ambin vayil vizha Kattanai kamanaiyum kalanaiyum kanninodu kalin vizha Attanai Aruril ammanai arvasettrra krodham Thattanai saradhe thavam irukka avam seythu tharukkinene Maruthan or vallakkan irayandhu mudiyinodu tholum thalum Iruthanai ezhil mulari thavisinmisai iruthan than thalaiyil ondrai Aruthanai Aruril ammanai alalam undu kandam Karuthanai karuthadhe karumbu irukka irumbu kadithu eythavare Thiruchitrambalam. This is the Pazhamozhi Thiru-Pathigam. The proverbs in the ten verses of this Thiru-Pathigam are as follows: In the first verse, the proverb “Kani irukka Kai Kavardhal” (seizing unripe fruit when ripe fruit is available) appears. It means, “I wasted my time without worshipping the Lord who graciously resides in Thiruvarur.

“When there were sweet, delicious fruits, I became a thief who desired tasteless unripe fruits instead of savoring them.” This is the meaning of the proverb in the first verse. The proverb in the second verse is “Muyal vittu Kakkai pin ponavare” (leaving the rabbit and following the crow). That is, it is easy to run after a rabbit, but following a crow, or flying after a crow, is a very difficult, arduous, and impossible task. The rabbit is a simile for the Shaiva religion. The crow is a simile for the Jain religion.

“Therefore, to go Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings that he left the easy path of the Shaiva religion, which is like a rabbit, and followed the Jain religion, which is like a crow. This is used as a simile for abandoning the path of grace and following the path of delusion. Generally, all the proverbs here are used in this sense by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman.

“Now, the proverb in the third verse is “Aram irukka Maram Vilaikku Kondavare” (buying a tree when righteousness is available). That is, dharma, righteousness, is something that cannot be obtained even by paying a high price. We can easily obtain that Shiva dharma by being near the Lord of Arur without paying a price.

“But, abandoning that, I became an ignorant person who bought a tree, which is a hateful sin, even though it was obtained for free and without cost. I have used the proverb here. The proverb in the fourth verse is “Pani Neeral Pavai Seythal” (making a doll with dew water). That is, “Pani Neer” means cold water, and “Pavai” means doll. Can a doll be made with cold water? No, it cannot.

“But like one who tries to make a doll with cold water, I engaged in actions contrary to true knowledge, says Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, using this proverb in the fourth verse.

“Now, in the fifth verse, the proverb is “Ethan Porkku Adhan Agappattathu Pol Anen” (I became like one caught in another’s fight). That is, in a fight started by one person, another person who has no connection to that fight gets caught and suffers.

“Similarly, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who was a hereditary servant, was caught by the Jains and suffered for many years. He sings about this through this proverb. The proverb in the sixth verse is “Iruttu Araiyin Maladu Karandhu Eythal” (milking a barren cow in a dark room). That is, like one who tries to milk a barren cow in a dark room, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings, “I spent the first part of my life with the Jains!” and “Without thinking of Thiruvarur Thiyagaraja Peruman, who is like nectar, I spent most of my life with the Jains!” The proverb in the seventh verse is “Vilakku Irukka Minminiyin Theeyinai Payanpaduthuvathu Pola” (like using the light of a firefly when a lamp is available). The Lord, who is like abundant honey in Arur, is present. Without getting the opportunity to taste that honey and attain salvation, I, a humble servant, instead of using the beneficial thing, used the useless thing, like using the light of a firefly to warm myself when a lamp is available, and thus wasted my life, he sings with regret in this seventh verse through the proverb “Minmini Thee Kayndhavare.” Next, the proverb in the eighth verse is “Pazhuril Paikkambu Eythavare” (like one who goes to a ruined village to beg).

“That is, like one who goes to a ruined village to beg, a village that is already ruined and in poverty, and goes there to beg.

“Similarly, I went on the path of the Jains and spent my life there, without joining the Lord of Arur, who is the life of all, I spent it in the Jain religion, he sings with regret.

“Now, the proverb in the ninth verse is “Thavam Irukka Avam Seythu Tharukkinene” (when penance was available, I did evil and became arrogant). That is, if one joins Lord Shiva, who is the leader in Arur, evil qualities like attachment, enmity, and anger will not approach us.

“But without approaching such a Lord, without performing the actions suitable for penance, I joined the Jain religion, performed useless actions, and wandered with arrogance, he sings. The proverb in the tenth verse is “Karumbu Irukka Irumbinai Kadithu Eythavare” (when sugarcane was available, I bit iron and became weary).

“The Lord of Arur is like very sweet sugarcane. Abandoning that sugarcane, without tasting that sugarcane, like biting tasteless iron that cannot be bitten, I joined the Jain religion and wasted the first part of my life, he sings.

“Thus, in all ten verses, using ten proverbs, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings that he wasted the first part of his life by joining the Jain religion, which is the path of delusion, instead of the Shaiva religion, which is the path of grace. Generally, the sentiment in this Thiru-Pathigam is that when good things were available, I did not obtain them, but instead used bad things. Anapaya Chozhan was wasting his time reading Seevaga Sinthamani instead of studying Shaiva scriptures. Sekkizhar Peruman, who was the Prime Minister of Anapaya Chozhan, Sekkizhar Peruman went to Anapaya Chozhan and explained, “Is it appropriate for you to read such a useless story as Sinthamani when there are exalted Shiva stories?” and he preached the exalted Shiva stories, the sacred histories of the Nayanmars, to Anapaya Chozhan. Umaapathi Sivachariyar, who sings about this incident, has used some of these proverbs in the history of Thiru-Thondar Puranam. The Thirukkural, “Iniya Ulavaaga Innaadha Koorall Kaniyiruppa Kai Kavar” (speaking harsh words when pleasant ones are available, like seizing unripe fruit when ripe fruit is available), was also composed using this proverb, “Kaniyiruppa Kai Kavarndhal.” Let us persist in our reflection.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part Four Hundred and One, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having worshipped and prostrated at Thiruvarur Thiru-Koil, prostrated in the streets of Thiruvarur, performed Uzhavaara service there, praised the Lord, and sang Thiru-Pathigams. Sekkizhar Peruman explains this through a beautiful verse. In this verse, Sekkizhar Peruman vividly portrays the sacred form of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. The 1490th verse in Periya Puranam, the 225th verse in Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam: “Marbara pozhi kannir mazhaivarum thiruvadivum Madhuravakkil Servagum thiruvayil thendhamizhin malaigalum sempotrale Sar”

Vaana thirumanamum uzhavara thanippadaiyum thamumagi Parvazha thiruveedhi pani seythu panindhu ethi paravi selvar. This is the sacred verse. Sekkizhar Peruman sings how the sacred form of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman shines. This sacred verse has the greatness of being like an excellent painting that completely depicts the sacred form of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, his sacred words, and the state of his sacred heart.

Similarly, earlier, in the 1405th verse, it was sung: “Thooya venniru thuthaindha pon meniyum thazhvadavum Nayagan sevadi thaivaru sindhaiyum nainthurugi Paivadhu pol anbu nirpozhi kannum pathigisjol Meya sevvaayum udaiyar pugundhanar veedhiyulle.” And there, this sacred verse is composed in the same way. How does the sacred form of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman shine? Rain-like tears are flowing from the sacred eyes of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. They flow down to the sacred chest of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. The heart of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is always melted in remembrance of the Lord.

Therefore, due to that thought, tears continuously flow from his sacred eyes, drenching his chest. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman thinks. He thinks of the smallness of the mistake he made by joining the Jain religion. He also thinks of the incomparable greatness of the Lord who pardoned that mistake and took him into His service.
