As he thinks and melts thus, due to the abundance of love, tears flow from his eyes.

Therefore, this rain of tears shows us the state of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar melting with love.

Now, Sekkizhar Peruman sings, “Madhuravakkil thendhamizhin malaigal servagum thiruvayum” (and his sacred mouth, from which garlands of sweet Tamil words emerge). Sweet Tamil hymns continuously emerge from the sweet words of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. The form of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is a sacred form, his mind is a sacred mind, and similarly, his mouth becomes a sacred mouth. His words are sweet words, words full of poetic beauty. From them come Thevarams, which are garlands of sweet Tamil. His sacred mind is attached to the golden feet of the Lord.

His mind is like a heroine gently caressing the feet of her hero. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is always contemplating the sacred feet of Lord Shiva.

Therefore, the mind of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar is always contemplating the sacred feet of Lord Shiva. The state in which Lord Shiva manifests in the knowledge of great souls who have transcended these worlds, which are tattvas and tattvatvas, and attained Shivattva, is such a high state. In that state, the senses of these great souls, like grass thrown into a salt pan, lose their individual consciousness and manifest as Shiva-consciousness.

Thus, the knowledge of these transformed great souls, to realize themselves, He gives His own form and places it within them to realize themselves. The twelfth sutra of Sivagnanabodham states, “The devotee realizes himself through the contemplation of ‘Sivoham’.” According to this commentary, the state of those great ones who become one with the Lord, devoted to His service, and deeply absorbed in His benevolence, is such. This was the state of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman.

Therefore, his mind is a sacred mind. This is what the Peruman sings in the verse, “The mind that caresses the sacred feet of the Lord.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, being in this state, holds the sacred Ulavaram (hoe) in his sacred hand. The Ulavaram is a tool that severs the bonds of illusion, which is the implication here. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar embodies such a form. For the welfare of this world, he performs sacred service in the streets of Thiruvarur and sings Thevaram Thiru-Pathigams. The benefit of the sacred service, the Shiva service, performed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar in the streets of Thiruvarur through mind, word, and deed, is for the people of this world to know and benefit from it, and to live by it.

It is for the people of this world to live in the path of Shiva.

Therefore, it implies that Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar did nothing for his own benefit. The 1405th Thiru-Pattu, “Thuya Venniru Thuthaintha Ponmeniyum” (Pure white ash-smeared golden body), refers to Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, upon being released from the prison of the Samanas by the Lord, remembering that great grace and returning to Thiru-Athigai. When he entered the sacred street of Thiru-Athigai, the form that appeared to the devotees was that form, which Sekkizhar depicted in the 1405th verse, beginning with “Thuya Vennitru Thuthaintha Ponmeni” (Pure white ash-smeared golden body).

Similarly, in the 270th verse of the Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman Puranam, there is the Thiru-Pattu “Sinthai Idaiyara Anbum” (Unceasing love in the mind). With that love further overflowing, when Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar entered the sacred street of Seerkazhi with the desire to see Aludaiya Pillaiyar, the sacred form that appeared to Aludaiya Pillaiyar’s gracious sight was that sacred form, explained in the verse “Sinthai Idaiyara Anbum.” Here, in this sacred verse, remembering the great grace of Thiruvarur Peruman, who bestowed the ability to be a servant to servants upon the devotees, Thiruvarur Thiru- When Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar entered the street, with that love further overflowing, his form is depicted by Sekkizhar Peruman in this sacred verse. These three sacred verses, namely the 1405th verse, the 270th verse in the Thiru-Gnana Sambandha Peruman Puranam, and the 1490th verse which we have just seen, are verses bestowed by Sekkizhar Peruman for us to directly perceive, meditate upon, and worship Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar in our minds and attain salvation. Sekkizhar Peruman has composed and bestowed the growing, maturing, and overflowing state of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar’s love in the first verse as a five-footed Kalithurai, the second verse as a larger six-footed Kalinedil Virutham, and the third verse as an even larger We can discern this through the excellence of the six-footed Kalinedil Virutham composed by Sekkizhar Peruman, and we can enjoy that divine poetic beauty. Madhava Sivagnana Munivar has composed a hymn in praise of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar in the Kanchi Puranam, based on the ideas of these three verses. That verse is as follows: “Idaiyara Peranbu Mazhai Vaarum Iru Vizhiyum Ulavara Thin Padaiyara Thirukkaramum Sivaperuman Thiruvadikke Pathitha Nenju Nadaiyara Perunthuravum Vageesa Perunthagai Than Gnana Paadal Thodaiyara Sevvayum Sivaveda Polivazhagum Thuthithu Vazhvam” (May we live praising the unceending great love, the two eyes that rain tears, the strong sacred hands that hold the hoe, the mind fixed on the sacred feet of Sivaperuman, the unwavering great asceticism, the sacred mouth that composes the songs of wisdom of Vageesa Perunthagai, and the beautiful splendor of the Shiva attire).

This is the sacred verse composed by Madhava Sivagnana Munivar in the Kanchi Puranam in praise of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, highlighting his greatness. The meaning of the verse sung by Madhava Sivagnana Munivar is that we shall always praise and live joyfully, celebrating the unchanging devotion of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, who possessed noble qualities, his sacred eyes that shed tears of joy like rain, his strong sacred hands holding the Ulavaram, his sacred heart firmly fixed on the sacred feet of Sivaperuman, his great ascetic state free from any deviation in good conduct, his sacred mouth that unceasingly composes Thevaram Thiru-Pathigams, which are songs of Shiva wisdom, and the supreme beauty of his Saivite attire.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s state of love grew immensely in Thiruvarur. He attained the grace of the Lord in Thiruvarur, becoming a servant to servants, and a servant to the Lord. Remembering that grace, this state of love further increased.

Here, we can also recall the theme of the Pathigam, “Thondarkku Thondaram Ponniyame” (Being a servant to servants is golden).

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, residing in Thiruvarur, daily worships and bows to the Lord who dwells in the anthill at various times, and sings many Thiru-Pathigams. The Peruman mentions that he sang many, including the Pathigam beginning with “Paadilam Boothathinaal.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings many Thevaram Thiru-Pathigams, including the Pathigam “Paadilam,” in Thiruvarur. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman daily worships during each period, from Thiru-Palli Ezhuchi (waking hymn) to Arthajamam (midnight worship). Sekkizhar Peruman states that he thus bowed and worshipped as prescribed by the Agamas, and sang many sacred hymns, starting with the hymn “Paadilam Boothathinaan.” Among the many hymns thus sung, those currently available are one hymn, “Soolappadaiyanai,” from the Seegamarappam Pathigam; two Kurunthogai Pathigams, “Eppothum Iraiyum Kokkarai Kuzhal”; two Thiru-Nerisai Pathigams, “Paduguzhi Pavvam Kuzhal Valam Konda”; and seven Thiru-Thandaga Pathigams, “Uyir Aavanam Irunthu Paathithan Thiru-Uru Thiruneetrinaiyum Netrimel Thirumaniyai Empantha Valvinai Idaru Kedumaaru Oruvanai Ulagu Etha.” Thus, twelve sacred hymns can be placed and examined here. Sivakavimani Ayya writes that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman composed these twelve sacred hymns.

Therefore, let us contemplate each of these sacred hymns. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 402, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. The next sacred hymn among those composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman in the sacred shrine of Thiruvarur is the fourth sacred hymn in the fourth Thiru-Murai, composed in the Gandhara Pann.

Paadilam Boothathinaanum Pavala Sevvai Vannathaanum Koodilam Menmulaiyaalai Koodiya Kolathinaanun Odilam Venpiraiyaanum Olithigal Soolathinaanun Aadilam Paambasaithaanum Aarur Amarntha Ammaane Nariyai Kuthirai Seivaanum Naragarai Thevu Seivaanum Viratham Kondu Aaduvallaanum Vichinri Naaru Seivaanum Murasu Athirnthaanai Mun Noda Mun Paninthu Anbargal Etha Aravari Saathi Nindraanum Aaru Amarntha Ammaane. (He who is the Lord of the Boothas, with coral-red lips, united with the slender-breasted one, wearing a white crescent moon, holding a shining trident, and adorned with a dancing serpent, is the Lord who resides in Aarur. He who turns foxes into horses, makes the wicked divine, can dance with vows, and makes seeds sprout without sowing, and who stands adorned with a garland of bones while the drum resounds and devotees bow and praise Him, is the Lord who resides in Aarur.) Neerum Mey Poosavallaanum Ninaippavar Nenjaththulaanum Erugandhu Eravallaanum Eripurai Meniyinaanun Naaru Karanthaiyinaanun Naanmarai Kandaththinaanun Aaru Sadaikkarandhaanun Aarur Amarntha Ammaane Kombunal Venillavanai Kuzhaiya Muruval Seithaanum Sempunal Kondu Eyil Moonrum Theeyezha Kan Sivanthaanum Vambunarkondraiyinaanun Vaatkanni Vaattamatha Eytha Ambar Eeruriyanaanum Aarur Amarntha Ammaane Oozhi Alakkavallaanum Ugappavar Uchiyullaanum Thaazh Ilanjensadaiyanaanum Thannamar Thinkodiyanaanum Thozhiyar Thuthidaiyaada Thozhuthu Adiyaargal Vananga Aazhivalai Kaiyinaanun Aarur Amarntha Ammaane. (He who can smear water on his body, who is in the hearts of those who remember Him, who can ride the bull with joy, whose body is like fire, who wears fragrant Karanthai, whose throat holds the four Vedas, who concealed the river in his matted locks, is the Lord who resides in Aarur. He who smiled gently at the beautiful woman with a bow, whose eye reddened with fire to burn the three cities with red water, who wears fresh Konrai, who shot the arrow at the beautiful-eyed one, who wears the skin of an elephant, is the Lord who resides in Aarur. He who can measure the eons, who is in the minds of those who love Him, who has long, young, red matted locks, who has a strong banner of his own, whose hand holds the ocean’s net, while maidens send messages and devotees bow and worship Him, is the Lord who resides in Aarur.)

Oorthirai Velaiyullaanum Ulagiranthon Porulaanum Seertharu Paadalullaanum Sengan Vidai Kodiyanaanum Vaartharu Poonguzhalaalai Maruviyudan Vaiththavanum Aarthirai Naalugandhaanun Aarur Amarntha Ammaane Thozhar Gangai Thunnin Nindrarkku Thondri Arulavallaanum Kalar Gangai Panmalar Kondu Kaathal Kanatra Nindranaanum Kular Gangaiyaalai Ul Vaiththuk Kolach Sadai Karandhaanum Azhal Gangai Enthavallaanum Aarur Amarntha Ammaane Aayiram Thaamarai Polum Aayiram Sevadiyaanum Aayiram Pon Varai Polum Aayiram Tholudaiyaanum Aayira Njaayiru Polum Aayiram Neenmudiyanaanum Aayiram Perugandhaanun Aarur Amarntha Ammaane. (He who is in the surging waves of the sea, who is the one substance that begged the world, who is in the glorious songs, who has a red-eyed bull on his banner, who embraced and kept the woman with fragrant hair, who loved the day of Arudra, is the Lord who resides in Aarur. He who can appear and bestow grace upon those who stood firm in the Ganges, who stood with many flowers from the Ganges to ignite love, who concealed the cool Ganges within his beautiful matted locks, who can hold the fiery Ganges, is the Lord who resides in Aarur. He who has a thousand sacred feet like a thousand lotuses, who has a thousand shoulders like a thousand golden mountains, who has a thousand long crowns like a thousand suns, who loved a thousand names, is the Lord who resides in Aarur.) Veedaranga Niruvaanum Visumbinai Vethi Thodara Odarangaaga Vaiththaanum Ongi Or Oozhiyullaanum Kaadu Aranga Magizhnthaanum Kaarigaiyaargal Manaththul Aadu Arangaththidaiyaanum Aarur Amarntha Ammaane Paiyanjudar Vidu Naagap Palli Kolvaan Ullaththaanum Kaiyanju Naangu Udaiyaanai Kaal Viralal Adarththaanum Poyyanji Vaaymaigal Pesi Pugazh Purinthaarkkarul Seyyum Aiyanjin Appuraththaanum Aarur Amarntha Ammaane Thiruchitrambalam. The theme of this hymn is as follows: The Lord praised by attributes such as “Aarur Amarntha Ammaane” (The Lord residing in Aarur), “Paadilam Boothathinaan” (He who is the Lord of the Boothas), “Nariyai Kuthirai Seyvaan” (He who turns foxes into horses), “Naragarai Thervu Seyvaan” (He who makes the wicked divine), “Vichinri Naaru Seyvaan” (He who makes seeds sprout without sowing), “Ninaippavar Nenjaththullaan” (He who is in the hearts of those who remember Him), “Aathirai Naal Ugandhaan” (He who loved the day of Arudra), “Aayiram Sevadi Aay” (He who has a thousand sacred feet), He who has a thousand shoulders, a thousand long crowns, and a thousand names, is the Lord of Thiruvarur. This is the theme of the hymn.

In the second verse of this hymn, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings, “Nariyai Kuthirai Seyvaan” (He who turns foxes into horses). This refers to the divine sport performed by the Lord in Madurai for Manikkavasagar Swamigal, where He turned foxes into horses. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings about this here. There are those who interpret this to mean that it signifies the all-powerful nature of the Lord.

Now, the next sacred hymn sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for the sacred shrine of Thiruvarur is the nineteenth sacred hymn in the fourth Thiru-Murai, composed in the Seegamaram Pann.

Soolappadaiyanai Soolaga Veezharuvi Kolaththot Kungumanjer Kundru Ettudaiyaanai Paalaththa Men Mozhiyaal Panganai Paangaaya Aalaththin Keezhaanai Naan Kandathu Aarure Pakkame Paaridangal Soola Padu Thalaiyil Pukka Ur Pichaiyetru Undu Polivudaitthaay Kokkiragin Thuval Kodiyeduththa Kobanaththu Odu Akku Anintha Ammaanai Naan Kandathu Aarure Seyya Ulagamum Sel Saarvum Aanaanai Maayappor Vallaanai Maalai Thaazh Maarbanai Veyoththa Thozhiyartham Menmulaimeel Than Saanthin Aayaththidaiyaanai Naan Kandathu Aarure Eretra Maaveri Enkanamum Pinpadara Maaretrar Vallanam Seeri Mayaanaththin Neeretra Meniyanay Neelsadaimel Neer Thathumba Aaretru Anthananai Naan Kandathu Aarure Thaango Pola Vellilumbu Poonduththam Eru Eri Paangaana Urkkellaam Sellum Paramanaar Thengaavi Naarum Thiruvarur Thon Nagaril Poongoyilul Magizhnthu Pogaathu Irunthaare Empattam Pattum Udaiyaanai Ermathiyin Numpattam Serntha Nuthalaanai Anthivaay Sempattuduththuch Sirumaan Uri Aadai Ambattasaithaanai Naan Kandathu Aarure Poloththa Venmathiyam Soodi Polinthilangu Velaththu Uri Porththaan Velvalaiyaal Thaan Veruva Uzhiththeeyaanai Ongoli Maa Poondaththor Aazhithther Viththaganai Naan Kandathu Aarure Vanjanaiyaar Yaarppaadum Saaraatha Mainthanai Thunjirul Aadal Ugandhaanai Than Thondar Nenjirul Koorum Pozhuthu Nilaappaari Thanjudaray Nindraanai. I saw the Lord in Aarur, who is the one with the trident, who has a beautiful shoulder adorned with kumkum, who has eight mountains, who is the partner of the soft-spoken woman, who sits under the banyan tree. I saw the Lord in Aarur, who is surrounded by ghosts, who enters the skull, who eats alms and is glorious, who holds the banner of the crane’s feather, and who wears bones. I saw the Lord in Aarur, who is the red world and its support, who is skilled in illusory warfare, who has a chest adorned with garlands, and who is among the women with bamboo-like shoulders, adorned with sandalwood paste on their soft breasts. I saw the Lord in Aarur, who rides the bull, followed by the eight ganas, who is angry at his opponents, who has a body smeared with ash from the cremation ground, with water overflowing from his long matted locks, and who is the Brahmin who accepted the river.

I saw the Lord in Aarur, who wears white bones like a garland, who rides his bull and goes to all the beautiful towns, who is the supreme Lord, who joyfully resides in the beautiful temple of ancient Thiruvarur, which smells of fresh water lilies, and does not leave. I saw the Lord in Aarur, who wears a beautiful garment, who has a forehead adorned with the crescent moon, who wears a red silk garment at dusk, who wears the skin of a small deer, and who is adorned with a serpent. I saw the Lord in Aarur, who wears the crescent moon like a flower, who is resplendent, who wears the skin of an elephant, who made the white bangles tremble, who is the fire of the deluge, who is the master of the great chariot with a shining wheel. I saw the Lord in Aarur, who is the strong one, untouched by deceitful people, who loves to dance in the deep darkness, and who stands as a bright light when his devotees’ minds are clouded by darkness. I saw the Lord in Aarur, whose broad chest is adorned with fragrant Konrai flowers and cool water, who drank the great poison from the ocean to save those who drank the nectar, and who became the nectar itself. I saw the Lord in Aarur, who has hands that embrace, sacred feet like a lotus, who has a unique form, who wears a sacred thread, who has anklets of dancing serpents, who is the Lord, and who is the dancing fire-dancer.

I saw the Lord in Aarur, who pressed down the mountain with his beautiful finger, who made the unceasing warrior Ravana’s eyes bleed, who adorned his chest with red sandalwood paste, and who smeared his chest with pure white ash.

Soolappadaiyan In this hymn, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman states that the Lord, known by attributes such as “Akku Anintha Ammaan” (The Lord adorned with bones), “Aazhithther Viththagan” (The master of the chariot with a wheel), and “Aadum Theekkooththan” (The dancing fire-dancer), is the Lord whom he saw in Thiruvarur.

Now, the next sacred hymn is the sixth sacred hymn in the fifth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Kurunthogai hymn.

Eppothum Iraiyum Maravaathu Neer Muppothum Piraman Thozha Nindravan Seppothum Ponin Meni Sivan Avan Appothaikku Anjal Ennum Aarurane Sadaiyin Melumor Thaiyalai Vaiththavar Adagilaa Aravai Arai Aarththavar Padaiyin Nerththat Kannumai Paagamaa Adaivar Pol Idagaadar Aarure Vindavindalaye Kalanaagave Konda Kambali Ther Kuzhaganar Thunda Venpirai Vaiththa Iraiyavar Andavanaarkku Arulum Aarure Vidaiyum Eruvar Venthalaiyil Pali Kadaigal Thorum Thiriyum Eng Kannuthal Udaiyum Seerai Uraivathu Kaattidai Adaivar Pol Arangaaga Aarure Thulaikkai Velaththu Uriyudal Porththavar Valaikkaiyaalaiyor Paagam Magizhveiththi Thilaikkum Thingal Sadaimudiyil Thisai Muzhuthu Alakkum Sinthaiyar Polum Aarure Pannin Inmozhiyaalaiyor Paagamaa Vinninaar Vilangum Mathi Soodiye Sunna Neeru Meyppoosi Sudalaiyin Anniyaaduvar Polum Aarure Mattuvaar Kuzhalaalodu Maalvidai Ittamaa Ugandhu Eruum Iraivanaar Kattuvaanga Kanal Mazhumaan Thanodu Attamaam Puyam Aagum Aarure. (The Lord of Aarur, whom you should never forget, who stands to be worshipped by Brahma three times a day, who is Shiva with a body like red gold, who says “Fear not” at that moment. He who placed a woman on his matted locks, who tied a serpent around his waist that cannot be contained, who has Uma as a part of his eye, who is like a resident of the cremation ground, is the Lord of Aarur. He who holds a skull as a begging bowl, who is the beautiful one with a blanket, who wears a crescent moon, who bestows grace upon the celestials, is the Lord of Aarur. He who rides a bull, who wanders through streets begging for alms in a white skull, whose eye is on us, who wears a garment and resides in the forest, who is like a stage, is the Lord of Aarur. He who wears the skin of an elephant with a trunk, who joyfully holds the woman with bangles as a part of himself, who has the moon shining in his matted locks, whose thoughts encompass all directions, is the Lord of Aarur.

He who has the sweet-voiced woman as a part of himself, who wears the shining moon in the sky, who smears white ash on his body, who dances near the cremation ground, is the Lord of Aarur. He who joyfully rides the great bull with the fragrant-haired woman, who holds the Khatvanga, the fiery axe, and the deer, who has eight arms, is the Lord of Aarur.) They are the Lord of Aarur, whose matted locks are adorned with the waning moon, who holds fire and dances in the night, whose eye burned Kama, who recites the well-researched four Vedas. They are the Lord of Aarur, who consumed poison and held it in his throat, who has a unique nature with a red matted lock, who wears a loincloth, and who is worshipped by the celestials with keen intellect. They are the Lord of Aarur, whom Vishnu and Brahma could not reach, who overcame Yama, who holds a trident, a deer, and an axe in his hands, and who is the beautiful one who consumed poison.

Now, the next sacred hymn composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for this sacred shrine is the seventh sacred hymn in the fifth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Kurunthogai hymn.

Kokkarai Kuzhal Veenai Kodukotti Pakkame Paguvayana Boothangal Okka Aadal Ugandhuudan Kooththa Tharaay Akkinodu Aravu Aarppar Aarure Entha Maathavam Seithanai Nenjame Pantham Veedu Avayaaya Paraaparan Anthamil Pugazh Aarur Araneri Sinthaiyullum Siraththullum Thangave Vandulaamalar Kondu Valarsadaikku Indai Maalai Punainthum Iraappagal Thondaraagi Thodarnthu Vidaathavarkku Andammaalavum Vaippar Aarure Thunpalaam Ara Neengi Subaththaraay Enpalaam Nekki Iraappagal Eththi Nindru Inbaraay Ninainthu Endrum Idaiyara Anbaraam Avarkku Anbar Aarure Muruttu Meththaiyil Mun Kidaththaamunam Arattar Aivarai Aasaruththu Ittu Neer Murattadiththavaththakkan Than Velviyai Arattadakki Athann Aarur Adai. (The Lord of Aarur, who dances with the Kokkarai, flute, veena, and Kodukotti, accompanied by the split-mouthed Boothas, who dances with fire and serpents. O heart, what great penance have you performed that the Supreme Being, who is both bondage and liberation, the Lord of Aarur, whose fame is endless, the path of righteousness, resides in your mind and head?

The Lord of Aarur, who wears garlands of flowers on his growing matted locks, who is worshipped day and night by devotees who never leave him, will also keep them in the heavens.

The Lord of Aarur is a lover to those who are free from all suffering, who are auspicious, who melt their bones, who praise him day and night, who are joyful, who always remember him, and who have unceasing love. Before lying on the rough bed, you should conquer the five unruly senses and suppress the sacrifice of the stubborn Daksha, and then reach Aarur.) Emmai Yaarilai Yaanum Ulen Alen Emmai Yaarum Ithu Seyya Vallare Ammai Yaar Enakku Endru Endru Arattrinaerkku Ammaiyaarai Thanthaar Aarur Aiyare Thanda Aazhiyai Thakkan Than Velviyai Sendrathaadiya Thevaragandanai Kandu Kandu Ival Kaathaliththu Anpathaay Kondiyaayinavaaru En Than Kothaiye Ival Namai Pala Pesath Thodanginaal Aval Nam Andru Enil Aarur Aran Enum Pavani Veethi Vidanganai Kandu Ival Thavaniyaayinavaaru Enthan Thaiyale Neerai Senjadai Vaiththa Nimalanaar Kaaroththamidatra Kanal Vaayara Aarththar Uraiyum Ani Aarurai Thooraththe Thozhuvaar Vinai Thooliye. (Who am I? I am not even myself. Who else can do this to me? To me, who cried out, “Who is my mother?” the Lord of Aarur gave a mother.

My dear girl, seeing the Lord who destroyed Daksha’s sacrifice and the wheel, she fell in love and became devoted. If she starts to say many things about us, and if she is not ours, then, my dear girl, seeing the beautiful Lord of Aarur, who is called Aran, in the processional streets, she has become devoted. The sins of those who worship from afar the beautiful Aarur, where the pure Lord with water in his red matted locks, whose throat is like a cloud, and whose mouth is fire, resides, will turn to dust.) Ullame Ondru Uruthi Urappen Naan Vellanthangu Virisadai Vediyan Allal Neer Vayal Aarur Amarntha Em Vallal Sevadi Vaazhththi Vanangide Vindamaamalar Melurai Vaanodum Kondal Vannanum Koodi Arugilaa Andavaanthan Aarur Adithozha Pandai Valvinai Nillaa Paraiyume Maiyulaaviya Kandaththan Andaththan Kaiyulaaviya Soolaththan Kannuthal Aiyan Aarur Adithozhuvaarkkellaam Uyalaam Allal Ondrilai Kaanmine Thiruchitrambalam Thodarnthu Sinthippom Thiruchitrambalam. (O heart, I will tell you one truth: praise and worship the sacred feet of our generous Lord, the Vedic scholar with flowing matted locks, who resides in Aarur, a land of fertile fields with abundant water. When the Lord of the universe, who resides on the great lotus flower, and Vishnu, whose color is like a cloud, come together and worship the feet of Aarur, ancient strong karma will not stand and will vanish. For all those who worship the feet of the Lord of Aarur, who has a dark throat, who is the universe, who holds a trident in his hand, and who has an eye on his forehead, there is no suffering; they can attain salvation.

See!) Let us proceed with our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 403. Thirunindrachcharukkam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. The ninth Thiru-Pathikam sung by Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar in Thiruvarur, beginning with “Padukozhi Pavvathannu.” This is the fifty-second Thiru-Pathikam in the Fourth Thirumurai, a Thiru-Nerisaith Thiru-Pathikam.

“Padukuzhi pavvathanna pandiyai peythavaatral Keduvathu immanithar vaazhkai kaandorungedukindren Muduguvar irunthul aivar moorkare ivarkalodum Adiyanen vaazhamaatten Aarur Moolatta Neere.” “Pazhupeitha pandithannai puramoru tholaal moodi Ozhukkaraa onpathu vaay ottumai ondrum illai Sazhakkudai ithanul aivar sangadam palavum seyya Azhippanaay vaazhamaatten Aarur Moolatta Neere.” “Panchin mel” “Adiyaargal paangaray avarkal nindru Nenjil noy palavum seythu ninaiyinum ninaiya ottar Nanjani midatrinane nathane nambane naan Anjinerkku anjal ennnir Aarur Moolatta Neere.” “Kendaiyan thadangan nallar thammaiye kezhuma vendi Kundaraayth thirinthu aivar kulaithu idarkuzhiyil nokka Kandu naan tharukkillen kaathukkol karaiser kanda Anda vaanvarkal potrum Aarur Moolatta Neere.” “Thaazh kuzhal insol nallar thangalai thanjamendru Ezhaiyenagi naalum en seyken enthai pemman Vaazhvathael arithu polum vaikalum aivar vandhu Aazhkuzhi padukkavaatren Aarur Moolatta Neere.” “Maatramondrarulakillir mathiyilen vithiyilamai Seetramum theerthal seyyir sikkan udaiyaragi Kootram pol” “Aivar vandhu kulaithittu koguseyya Aatravum killen nayen Aarur Moolatta Neere.” “Uyirnilai udambe kaalaa ullame thaaliyaaga Thuyarameyetramaaga thunbakkol athanai patri Payirthanai suzhiyavittu paalku neer iraithu mikka Ayarvinaal aivarkku aatren Aarur Moolatta Neere.” “Katrathel ondrumillai karikaiyarodu aadi Petrathel perithum thunbam pethaiyen pizhaippinale Mutrinaal aivar vandhu muraimurai thuyaram seyya Atru naan alandhu ponen Aarur Moolatta Neere.” “Pathanaay vaazhamaatten paviyen paravi vandhu Sithathul aivar theeya seyvinai palavum seyya Mathoru thayire pola marugum en ullamthaanum Athane amarakove Aarur Moolatta Neere.” “Thadakkai naalainthum kondu thadavarai thannai” “Patri eduthavan peyarkka odi erinthanar poothamellam Mudithalai pathum tholum murithara iraiye oondri Adarthu arul seythathu enne Aarur Moolatta Neere.” In this Thiru-Pathikam, praising Thiruvarur Thiru-Moolattanaththu Peruman, the five senses within this body delude us, cause many troubles, and push us into a pit of distress.

Due to the mischief of these five senses, our heart is distressed and churns like curd stirred by a churner.

Therefore, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, as if praying for us, asks Thiruvarur Thiru-Moolattanaththu Peruman to protect us.

Now, the next Thiru-Pathikam, the tenth Thiru-Pathikam, begins with “Kuzhal Valam Konda.” The note for this Thiru-Pathikam states that those who were born into this world were born to worship Thiruvarur. That is, the purpose of being born into this world is solely to go to Thiruvarur and worship Aarur Emman. Those who see and worship Aarur Peruman are truly called those who are born into this world. Aarur Peruman entered the hearts of devotees who possessed devotion and remained there. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman sings of all the qualities of Peruman in this Thiru-Pathikam, stating that He is the one who wears the moon, and so on.

This Thiru-Pathikam is compiled as the fifty-third Thiru-Pathikam in the Fourth Thirumurai, set to the tune of Thiru-Nerisaith.

“Kuzhal valam konda sollaal kolaveer kanni than” “Kazhal valam kondu neenga ganangal ganangal Azhal valam konda kaiyaan arutkathir erikkum Aarur Thozhal valam kondal seyvaan thondrinaar thondrinaare.” “Naagaththai nangai anja nangaiyai mangai endru Vedaththai thavira naagam velaththin urivai porthu Paagaththin nimirthal seyyaa thingalai minnendru anji Aagaththil kidantha naagam adangum Aaruranaarke.” “Thozhuthu agam kuzhaiyamevi thottimai udaiya thondar Azhuthu agam pugundhu nindraar avaravar polum Aarurar Ezhilaga naduvenmuththam andriyum merkol veli Pozhilagam vilangu thingal puthumukil soodinaare.” “Nanjirun manigal kandar nagaiyirul eemakkangul Venchudar vilakkaththa” “Aadi vilanginaar polum moova Venchudar mugadu theendi velli naarasamanna Anjudar ani ven thingal aniyum Aaruranaare.” “Enthazhir neermai kola meniyendru imaiyor etha Painthazhi kombar anna padarkodi payilappattu Thanjadai thothinaalum thammador neermaiyalum Anthazhi raagam polum vadivar Aaruranaare.” “Vaanagam vilanga malgum valankezhu mathiyam soodi Thaanagam azhiya vandhu thaam pali thervarpolum Oonagam kazhintha ottil unpathu olikona aanagaththanjum aadum adigal Aaruranaare.” “Anjanai kanaiyinaanai azhalura andru nokki Anjanai kuzhalinaalai amuthama anainthu nakku Anjanai anjum aadi aadaravaattuvaarthaam Anjanai veli aa” “Arur aathariththu idam kondaare.” “Vanangi mun amarar etha valvinaiyaana theer Pinangudai sadaiyil vaiththa piraiyudai perumai annal Manam kamal othi paagar mathinilaa vattathaadi Anangodi maadavithi Aaruriyam adigale.” “Nagalidam pirarkkaaga naanmaraivorkal thangal Pugalidamaagi vaazhum pugazhili iruvar koodi Igalidamaaga neendang eendazhil azhalathaagi Agalidam paraviyetha adigal Aaruranaare.” “Aayiram thingal moyththa alaikadal amutham vaangi Aayiram asurar vaazhum animathil moonrum veva Aayiram tholum mattith thaadiya asaivu theera Aayiram adiyum vaiththa adigal Aaruranaare.”

Now, the eleventh Thiru-Pathikam, a Thiru-Thandakam, composed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal for Thiruvarur, begins with “Uyiraavanam irundhu utru nokki.” The Pathikam is the twenty-fifth Thiru-Pathikam in the Sixth Thirumurai. The note for this Thiru-Pathikam is as follows: Thiruvarur Peruman is one who lives in complete union with those who have realized themselves through the path of Shiva Yoga. That Peruman is present here, being worshipped by all the Devas. Peruman, having manifested in many Thiru-Sthalams, has entered and become established in Thiruvarur. It is the nature of mature souls to hear the name of Aarur Peruman, then His form, then the place where He resides, and then to become His servant, forgetting the world and themselves, and to surrender at His sacred feet.

Thus, this Thiru-Pathikam contains many profound Shaiva Siddhanta concepts in its many verses. These Siddhanta concepts should be clarified by seeking out suitable Gnana-Acharyas and receiving their instructions.

Now, that Thiru-Pathikam.

“Uyiraavanmirundhu utru nokki ullum kiliyin uru ezhuthi Uyiraavanam seythittu un kai thanthaal unarappaduvaarodu otti vaazhthi Airaavanam eraathu aaneru eri amarar naadu aalaathe Aarur aanda Airaavaname en ammane nin arutkannal nokkaathaar allaathaare.” “Ezhuthu kodiyidaiyaar ezhaimen thol ilaiyarkal nammai ikazhaa munnam Pazhuthu padaninaiyel paavi nenje panduthaan ennodu pagaithaan undo Muzhuthu ulagil vaanvarkal mutrum koodi mudiyaluravanangi mutra” “Patri azhuthu thiruvadikke poosai seyya irukkiraan oorpolum Aarurthaane.” “Theruraar maavuraar thingalurar thigazh pun sadai mudimel thingal soodi Karuraa nindra kazhanichchaayal kannaarntha nedumaadam kalandhu thondrum Oruraa ulagelam oppakkoodi umaiyaal manavaazhaa endru vaazhththi Aaruraa Aaruraa enkindraarkal amararkal thampemane engutraaye.” “Kovanamam tholaa udaiyaavathu kollero velamo oorvathuthaan Poovanamo purambayamo andraayiththaan porunthaathathaar vaazhkai Thirunthaamaiyo thivanaththa senjadai mel thingal soodi thisai naankum vaiththugandha sentheevannar Aavanamo otriyo ammanaraam ariyien matroor aamaaraarurthaane.” “Enthu mazhuvaalar innambaraar erippava” “Avalavannaar kudamookkilaar vaaintha valaikkaiyaal paagamaaga Vaarsadaiyaar vandhu valanjoliyar ponthaar adigal purambayaththai pugazhurkke poyinaar porereri Aainthe iruppaar poy Aarurppukkaar annalaar seykindra kan maayame.” “Karuvagik kuzhambirundhu kazhiththu moolai karu narambum vellelumbum serndhu ondraagi Uruvaagi purappattu ingoruththi thannaal valarkkappattu uyiraarum kadai pogaaraal Maruvaagi ninnadiye maraven amman mariththorukaal pirappundel maravavannam Thiruvarur manavaazhaa thiruthenguraay sempon ekambane thikaiththittene.” “Munnam avanudaiya naamam kettaal murththi avanirukkum vannam kettaal Pinnai avanudaiya Aarur kettaal peyarthum avanukke pichchiyaanaal” “Annaiyaiyum aththanaiyum andre neeththaal agandraal agalidaththaar aacharam thai Thannai maranthaal thannaamam kettaal thalaippattaal nangai thalaivan thaale.” “Aaduvaay neettam alavil kundraa aviyaduvaar arumaraiyor arinthen unnai Paaduvaar thumbaruvaum naarathaathi paravuvaar amararkalum amararkonum Theduvaar thirumaalum naanmuganum theenduvaar malaimagalum gangaiyaalum Koodume nayadiyen sey kutreval kuraiyundo thiruvarur kudikondirke.” “Neerurum senjadaiyaay netrikkannay nilaththingal thundaththaay ninnaith thedi Orurum ozhiyaame ottriththu engum ulagelam thirithandhu ninnaik kaanbaan Therurum neduvithi patri nindru thirumaalum naanmuganum thernthu kaanaathu Aaruraa Aaruraa enkindraarkal amarar” “Tham perumane Aaruraaye.” “Nallure nandraga nattamittu naraiyetraip pazhaiyare paaya eri Pallurum pazhithirindhu setrur methe palarkana thalaiyalattinudhe Illarntha peruvellurththaliye peni ira patteechcharangadandhu manarkal pukku Ellarum thalichchaththangudiyil kaana iraippozhuthil thiruvarurppukkaar thaame.” “Karutthuththik kathanagam kaiyil enthi karuvarai pol kaliyanai katharak kaiyaal Uriththeduththu sivandhathan thol porundha moodi umaiyavalai achchurutthum oli kolmeni Thiruththuruththi thiruppazhanam thiruneyththaanam thiruvaiyaaru idam konda selvar innaal Aripperuththa velletrrai adarayeri appanaar ipparuvam Aaruraare.”

Now, Thiruvarur. The twelfth Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, beginning with “Paathiththan Thiruvuruvil,” is the twenty-sixth Thiru-Pathikam in the Sixth Thirumurai, a Thiru-Thandakam.

“Paathiththan thiruvuruvil penkondaanaip pandorukaal thasamuganai azhuviththaanai Vaathiththu thadamalaraan siram kondaanaip vankaruppu silaikkaman udal attaanai Sothi chandiran meni maru seythaanai sudarangi thevanaiyor kai kondaanaai Aathiththan parkkonda amman thannai Aaruril kandu adiyen ayarthavaare.” “Verpuruththa thiruvadiyaal kootrattanaai vilakkinvoli minnin oli muththin sothi Oppuruththa thiruvuruvath thoruvanaith thannai othaathe vedam unarnthaan thannai Appuruththa kadal nanjam undaan thannai amuthundaar ulanthaalum ulavaathaanai ap” “Appuruththa neeragaththai azhalaanaanaai Aaruril kandadiyen ayarthavaare.” “Oru kaalath thoruthevar kankondaanaai oozhithorum oozhi uyarnthaan thannai Varukaalam selkaalam aayinaanaai vankaruppu silaikkaman udal attaanai Poru vela kazhichchurivai porvaiyaanaai pullaraiyan udal thannai podi seythaanai Aruvelvi thagarththu echchan thalai kondaanaai Aaruril kandadiyen ayarthavaare.” “Meyppaal venniru anintha meniyaanaai venpazhungin utpathiththa sothiyaanaai Oppaanai oppilaa oruvan thannai uththamanai niththilaththai ulagelam Vaippaanaik kalaippaanai varuvippaanai valvinaiyen manaththagaththai manninanaai Appaalai kappaalai kappaalaanaai Aaruril kandadiyen ayarthavaare.” “Pindaththil piranthathoru porulai matrai pindaththai padaiththathanai periya veda thundaththin” “Thuni porulai sudi theeyaagi suzhal kaalaay neeraagi paaraayitrai Kandaththil theethin nanju amuthu seythu kanmoonru padaiththoru karumbai paalai Andaththukku appuraththaar thamakku viththai Aaruril kandadiyen ayarthavaare.” “Nithiyaay nilanaagi neruppaay neeraay nirai kaalaay ivaiyitrin niyamamaagi Paathiyaay ondraagi irandaay moondraay paramaanuvaay pazhuththa pankalaagi Sothiyaay irulaagi suvaikalaagi suvai kalantha appaalaay veedaay veettin Aathiyaay anthamaay nindraan thannai Aaruril kandadiyen ayarthavaare.” We have seen six Thiru-Paadalgal in this Thiru-Pathikam. Thiru-Paadalgal seven, eight, nine, and ten are not available to us.

We will continue to contemplate the Thiruvarur Thiru-Pathikams. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 404. Thirunindrachcharukkam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. The thirteenth Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman in Thiruvarur, beginning with “Neetrinaiyum Netrimel Ittaarpolum.” This is a Thiru-Thandakam, the twenty-eighth Thiru-Pathikam in the Sixth Thirumurai.

“Neetrinaiyum netrimel ittaarpolum neengaame vellelumbu poondaarpolum Kaatrinaiyum kadithaaga nadanthaarpolum kannin mel kannondru udaiyaarpolum Kootrinaiyum kurai kazhalaal uthaiththaarpolum kol puliththol aadai kuzhagarpolum Aatrinaiyum senjadai mel vaiththaarpolum ani Aarur Thiru-Moolattanaare.” “Pariyathor paambarai mel aarththaarpolum paasupatham paarththarkku aliththaarpolum Kariyathor kalichchurivaip porththaarpolum” “Kaapaalam kattanga kodiyaarpolum Periyathor malaivillaa eythaarpolum per Nandi ennum peyaraarpolum Ariyathor aranangal attaarpolum ani Aarur Thiru-Moolattanaare.” “Thuniyudaiyar tholudaiyar enbaarpolum thooya thirumeni selvarpolum Piniyudaiya adiyaarai theerppaarpolum pesuvaarkkellam periyaarpolum Maniyudaiya maanaaga maarpaarpolum vaasuki maa naanaaga vaiththaarpolum Aniyudaiya neduvithi nadappaarpolum ani Aarur Thiru-Moolattanaare.” “Ottagaththai oonaaga ugandaarpolum oruuruvaay thondri uyarnthaarpolum Naattagaththai nadai palavum navindraarpolum gnana perungadarkkor naatharpolum Kaattagaththai aadal udaiyaarpolum kaamarangal paadi thirivaarpolum Aattagaththil aanainthu ugandaarpolum ani Aarur Thiru-Moolat” “Tanaare.” “Enaththu ila maruppu poondaarpolum imaiyavarkal etha irundhaarpolum Kaanakkallaal keezh nizhalaarpolum kadal nanjam undu irunda kandarpolum Vaanaththil ila mathiser sadaiyaarpolum vaankaiyilai verpin magizhnthaarpolum Aanaththu mun ezhuththaay nindraarpolum ani Aarur Thiru-Moolattanaare.” “Kaamanaiyum kariyaagak kaainthaarpolum kadal nanjam undu irunda kandarpolum Somanaiyum senjadai mel vaiththaarpolum sollaagi sorporulaay nindraarpolum Naamanaiyum vedaththaar thaamepolum nangaiyorpaal magizhntha nambarpolum Aamanaiyum thirumudiyar thaamepolum ani Aarur Thiru-Moolattanaare.” “Mudiyaar mathiyaravam vaiththaarpolum moovulagum thaameyaay nindraarpolum Sediyar thalai pali kondu uzhalaarpolum selgathithaan kanda si” “Ivanaarpolum Kadiyaar nanjundu irunda kandarpolum kangaala veda karuththarpolum Adiyaar adimai ugappaarpolum ani Aarur Thiru-Moolattanaare.” “Indiraththai inithaaga eenthaarpolum imaiyavarkal vandhu irainjum iraivarpolum Sundaraththa podithannai thuthainthaarpolum thoothuya thirumeni thondarpolum Mandiraththai manaththulle vaiththaarpolum maanaagam naanaaga valaiththaarpolum Anthiraththai aniyaa nanjundaarpolum ani Aarur Thiru-Moolattanaare.” “Pindaththai kaakkum pranaarpolum piravi iravi izhaathaarpolum Mundaththu mukkan udaiyaarpolum muzhuneer poosum muthalvarpolum Kandaththu iraiye karuththarpolum kaalaththi kaaronam meyaarpolum Andaththukku appuramaay nindraarpolum ani Aarur Thiru-Moolattanaare.” “Oru kaalaththu ondraagi nindraarpolum oozhi pala kandu irundhaarpol” “Polum Perugaame vellan thavirththaarpolum pirappu idumbai saakkaadu ondru illaarpalum Urugaathaar ullaththu nillaarpalum ugappaar manaththu endrum neengaarpalum Arugaaga vandhennai anjel enbaar ani Aarur Thiru-Moolattanaare.” “Nandraga nadai palavum navindraarpolum gnana perungadarkkor naatharpolum Kondraagi kondrathu ondru undaarpolum kol arakkar kon thalaigal kuraiththaarpolum Sendraar thiripurangal eythaarpolum thisaiyanai anaiththum aanaarpolum Andraagil aayiram peraarpolum ani Aarur Thiru-Moolattanaare.”

Now, the fourteenth Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman for Thiruvarur, beginning with “Thirumaniyai,” is a Thiru-Thandakam, the twenty-ninth Thiru-Pathikam in the Sixth Thirumurai.

“Thirumaniyai” “Thikkum thenai paalai theengarumabin insuvaiyai thelintheerar kurumanaiyai Kuzhal monthai thaalam veenai kokkaraiyin sachchariyin paaniyaanai Parumaniyai pavalaththai pasum pon muththai paruppathaththil arunkalaththai paavam theerkkum Arumaniyai Aaruril amman thannai ariyaathu adinaayen ayarthavaare.” “Ponpol thirumeni udaiyaan thannai pongu ven noolaanai punithan thannai Minnaanai minnidaiyaal paagan thannai velaththin uri virumbi porththaan thannai Thannaanai thannoppar illathaanaith thaththuvanaith uththamanai thazhal pol meni Annaanai Aaruril amman thannai ariyaathu adinaayen ayarthavaare.” “Ettranaai ezhu ulagum aanaan thannai ezhu kadalum ezhu malaiyum aanaan thannai Kootranaai kootram uthaiththaan thannai kodumazhuvandathor kaiyaan thannai Kaatranaai theeyaanai neerumaaga” “Kadigamizhum punjadai mel gangai vella aatranaai Aaruril amman thannai ariyaathu adinaayen ayarthavaare.” “Munthiya valvinaigal theerppaan thannai moovaatha meni mukkaninanaai Chandiranum venkathirum aayinaanaith sangaranai sangak kuzhaiyaan thannai Mandiramum maraiporulumaayinaanaai marumaiyum immaiyum aanaan thannai Anthiranai Aaruril amman thannai ariyaathu adinaayen ayarthavaare.” “Piraneriyay peedaagi pingaganumaay piththanaayppar manaththin ulle Ura neriyay omamaay eemakkaatti ori pala vida nattamaadinaanai Thura neriyay thoobamaay thotramaagi naatramaay nanmalar mel uraiya nindra Araneriyaai Aaruril amman thannai ariyaathu adinaayen ayarthavaare.” “Pazhagiya valvinaigal paatruvaanai pasupathiyai paavaganai paavam theerkkum Kuzhaganai kolaravu ondru aa” The One who dances with the Kodukotti, the One who holds it in His hand, the One who is worshipped by all, the One who resides in Thiru-Veerattam, the One desired by the celestials, the beautiful One, the Lord of Thiru-Aroor – how did this lowly dog-like servant forget Him without knowing? The One with a crown adorned with a radiant jewel, the One who is the effulgence adorned with sacred ash, the One who wears a fierce serpent, the One who wears a tiger skin as garment, the One who is always in the hearts of devotees, the trustworthy One, the naked One, the three-eyed One, the deep One, the Lord of Thiru-Aroor – how did this lowly dog-like servant forget Him without knowing?

The pearl, the gem, the ruby, the unfading sprout of the wish-fulfilling tree, the cluster of diamonds, the One who rides a bull, the One who controls a fierce serpent, the devotee, the One who is in the hearts of devotees, the One with a body like the sun, the Father, the Lord of Thiru-Aroor – how did this lowly dog-like servant forget Him without knowing? The One who holds a fierce serpent in His hand, the One with a body like the sun, adorned with sacred ash, the One who is butter The pure One with a dancing body, the One who has a third eye on His forehead, the red One, the One like a cluster of rich coral, the One who placed the white crescent moon on His red matted hair, the One who resides in Thiru-Aiyaaru, the Lord of Thiru-Aroor – how did this lowly dog-like servant forget Him without knowing? The One with a glorious crown of ten heads, the One who destroyed the beauty of the god of love with His sacred toe, the One who bestowed great glory, the One who is both female and male, the One who burned the three cities of the enemies, the holy One adorned with sacred ash, the One who is the river, the Lord of Thiru-Aroor – how did this lowly dog-like servant forget Him without knowing?

The fifteenth Thiru-Pathigam bestowed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to Thiru-Aroor Thiru-Sthalam, beginning with “Embandha Valvinai Noi,” is the thirtieth Thiru-Pathigam in the Sixth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Thandaka Thiru-Pathigam.

He is the One who cured our binding strong karmic disease, He is the seven seas and the seven He is the worlds. He is the garland of fragrant Konrai flowers. He is the One with a crescent moon in His hair. He is the One who burned the three cities with a single arrow when the celestials pleaded. He is the One who dances with fire and performs the Ananda Thandavam.

He is our Lord in Thiru-Aroor, in the Thiru-Moolattanam with its golden jeweled mansions. He is the One who wears a garland of bones. He is the nectar for His devotees. He is the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaatru. He is the One with matted hair adorned with peacock feathers, Konrai garland, cool moon, and water. He is the pure path that devotees follow.

He is our Lord in Thiru-Aroor, in the Thiru-Moolattanam, whose fame fills all directions, praised by the celestials. He is the pure One with water in His matted hair. He is the One with a single eye on His forehead. He is the One who shares half His body with the beautiful-breasted Goddess. He is the One with a crescent moon He is the One with matted hair. He is the Great God.

He is the One with a throat like a dark cloud. He is the One who taught the dharma under the Banyan tree. He is our Lord in Thiru-Aroor, in the Thiru-Moolattanam with its glorious jeweled mansions. He is the One who wears an elephant hide. He is the wish-fulfilling tree. He is the One who kicked Yama.

He is the One who receives alms in a skull. He is the perfect One. He is the One who resides in Thiru-Ottrriyur. He is the Lord who rides a bull. He is the ancient One who caused the sun to lose its teeth. He is our Lord in Thiru-Aroor, in the Thiru-Moolattanam, with its honey-filled flower gardens.

He is the One who has no birth or death. He is the One who is both female and male. He is the One who removed the delusion from my mind. He is the One who showed a path unknown even to the celestials. He is the One who receives fragrant flowers, incense, lamps, and good fragrant sandalwood, worshipped daily by the celestials with great reverence, our Lord in Thiru-Aroor, in the Thiru-Moolattanam. He is Shankara.

He is the One who bestowed the discus upon Vishnu. He is the One with the crescent moon on His head. He is the Lord. He is the One who cut off one of the five heads of Brahma. He is the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaatru, surrounded by beautiful groves. He is our Lord.

He is the God who removes my sufferings. He is the One praised by the celestials. He is our Lord in Thiru-Aroor, in the Thiru-Moolattanam, surrounded by fields of red lotuses. He is our trustworthy Lord who bestows good and removes evil. He is the One who is the four Vedas and the six Angas. He is the effulgent light.

He is the ancient One. He is the One with the bull as His banner. He is the Lord of Thiru-Kachchi Ekambam, surrounded by dense groves. He is the Lord of Thiru-Sottrutthurai. He is the One in Thiru- Thiru-Aroor, in the Thiru-Moolattanam, where the fragrant breeze from the south blows. He is the One with matted hair adorned with golden Konrai flowers.

He is the One who resides in Thiru-Pugalur and Thiru-Poovanam. He is the One who shares half His body with the slender-waisted Goddess. He is the Vedic scholar. He is the One with the sacred thread on His chest. He is the One who holds the three-pronged spear. He is the One with a beautiful body adorned with sacred ash.

He is the One in Thiru-Aroor, in the Thiru-Moolattanam, surrounded by fertile fields. He is the One who burned the three cities of the enemies. He is the One with a dark throat from swallowing the ocean poison. He is the One who shines with increasing light in the world. He is the Lord of Thiru-Vaimoor and Thiru-Marai-Kadu. He is the ancient One whom even Vishnu with lotus eyes and Brahma on the lotus could not find.

He is the One in Thiru-Aroor, in the Thiru-Moolattanam, surrounded by fields with southern waves. He is the One who rides a small red-eyed bull. He is the Lord of Thiru-Nannai-Kavan. He is the One who burned the three cities of the enemies who opposed Him and fell into the fire. He is the mighty One whom deceit cannot approach. He is the One who crushed the ten heads and twenty shoulders of Ravana, who lifted Mount Kailash, with His sacred toe.

He is our Lord in Thiru-Aroor, in the Thiru-Moolattanam.

The sixteenth Thiru-Pathigam bestowed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar to Thiru-Aroor Thiru-Sthalam, beginning with “Idarkedumaaru Ennudhiye Nenje Nee Vaa,” is a Thiru-Thandaka Thiru-Pathigam, the thirty-first Thiru-Pathigam in the Sixth Thiru-Murai.

If you wish to be rid of suffering, O mind, come! He is the One with Ganga in His matted hair, always shining. He is the effulgent light within, never fading. He is the One with shoulders adorned with sacred ash. He is the One with a dark throat from swallowing the ocean poison.

He is the One with a deer in His hand. He is the One with a deer in His hand. He is the mighty bull, the sweet nectar, the primordial One. If you do not cry out “Thiru-Aroora!” again and again, how will the sins that grow like weeds be removed? O mind, think steadfastly of Him! He is the One with a body adorned with sacred ash.

He is the pure One who tore off the skin of the elephant demon. He is the One who made me His servant. He is my Lord, my King of Thiru-Aroor. He is the Lord of Thiru-Kachchi Ekambam, surrounded by fragrant groves. He is the wish-fulfilling tree. If you do not cry out “Karpagame!” again and again, how will you attain stability?

O mind, come! Enter the temple of our Lord daily before dawn, sweep and clean, adorn with flower garlands, praise and sing, prostrate with your head, dance, and cry out “Shankara, hail! Hail!” and “Our primordial Lord with Ganga in His red matted hair!” and “Thiru-Aroora!” again and again. If you do not cry out “Thiru-Aroora!” again and again, how will you attain merit and the good path? O mind, listen carefully to this! He is the One with a chest adorned with the subtle sacred thread.

He is the unfading effulgent light. Daily, the celestials, the four Vedas, Brahma on the fragrant lotus, and Vishnu, all together, praise Him with countless sacred names. If you do not praise Him as “Thiru-Aroora!” again and again, how will you cross the boundary of allotted days? Day and night, praise and worship Him! He is the great One who forgives all mistakes. He is the golden One.

He is the One with a dark throat. I cry out to Him, “O Lord, I have found Your refuge!” He is the beautiful One who resides in Thiru-Aroor. O mind, speak of Him as “Our Lord with matted hair!” There is no fault in me for speaking thus. I thought of the way to remove countless births. O mind, I thought of the way to remove countless births, steadfastly. He is the One with the bull banner that never leaves.

He is Shiva, who bestowed the path to Shiva-Loka. Brahma, who never leaves the lotus, and Vishnu with lotus eyes, praised Him. He is the One who stood as a pillar of fire. O mind, think of Him as “Thiru-Aroora, rich in wealth!” If you wish to remove the sins that cling to you, if you wish for a way to attain the higher realm, if you wish for the surrounding karmas to fall away, listen, O mind, I will tell you! Without slumber, say, “You are my kin and my support! I worship no other deity but You!” He is the pure One who wears a serpent as a belt.

O mind, praise Him as “Thiru-Aroora!” again and again! O mind, this is the way to salvation for all celestials. He is the Lord, the sweet nectar, the primordial One. O mind, praise Him as “My Lord, my Master of Thiru-Aroor!” again and again, with devotion and offering flowers, and circumambulating, singing praises, “O Lord with the radiant moon in Your hair, O Destroyer of Yama, O wish-fulfilling tree!” If you do not cry out “Karpagame!” again and again, how will you break the bonds of attachment, O mind? He is the supreme light, the One with sacred ash, the destroyer of illusion. He is the light of the world, the God of gods.

He is our Lord in Thiru-Aroor, in the Thiru-Moolattanam. If you do not increase your love, stand before Him, contemplate Him daily, fall at His feet, and praise Him as “O Lord of the celestials, our Lord!” again and again, how will you attain salvation? O mind, do not waste your time being driven by the five senses and wandering aimlessly! Come! He is the Lord with matted hair adorned with Ganga. He is the One who destroyed Daksha’s great sacrifice.

He is the Lord who crushed the heads of the King of Lanka. He is my Father who resides in Thiru-Aroor. He is the One who placed His auspicious feet on my head. O mind, praise Him daily, and you will attain goodness.

We will continue to contemplate the Thiru-Pathigams of Thiru-Aroor. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 405. Thiru-Nindra-Charukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. The seventeenth Thiru-Pathigam bestowed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal at Thiru-Aroor Thiru-Sthalam, beginning with “Oruvanai Ulagatthe Nindra Naalo,” is compiled as the thirty-fourth Thiru-Pathigam in the Sixth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Thandaka Thiru-Pathigam. This Thiru-Pathigam is structured as Appar Swamigal wondering about the day when Peruman enshrined Himself in Thiru-Aroor.

Was it the day when He stood alone, praised by the world? Was it the day when one form became three forms? Was it the day when He burned Yama? Was it the day when He opened His eye of fire on Kama? Was it the day when He created the earth and sky without blemish?

Was it before or after the Goddess with the deer in her hand, the consort of the Lord, Was it before or after the Goddess, the consort of the Lord, came to reside in Thiru-Aroor? Was it the day when He rejoiced with the golden mountain-like Goddess? Was it the day when He fed the celestials the powerful nectar and established their permanence? Was it the day when He stood as an unfathomable pillar of fire? Was it before or after He swallowed the poison from the turbulent ocean? Was it the day when He sat surrounded by the host of celestials?

Was it before or after He burned the three cities with His bow? Was it the day when He enshrined Himself in Thiru-Aroor? Was it the day when He, along with the Goddess with soft feet adorned with anklets, went to witness Arjuna’s prowess, and became a hunter, wielding a bow and arrow? Was it the day when He stood as the eye for the celestials? Was it before or after He entered the jeweled hall of Thillai, filled with mansions and palaces, to perform the dance? Was it the day when He enshrined Himself in beautiful Thiru-Aroor?

Was it the day when He stood tall and mighty? Was it the day when one aeon became seven aeons? Was it the day when He destroyed the great sacrifice of Daksha, performed by the celestials with great pride? Was it before or after Brahma on the lotus and Vishnu, who could not find Him, praised Him as “Our Lord!” and placed Him in their minds? Was it the day when He enshrined Himself in prosperous Thiru-Aroor? He is the One who did not grow as a child.

He is the refuge for those who worship Him. He is the eight-shouldered One with a blue gem-like throat. He is yesterday, today, and tomorrow. His nature is the path to Shiva-Loka. His greatness is sharpness, His quality is goodness. Was it before or after He assumed His beautiful form?

Was it the day when He enshrined Himself in cool Thiru-Aroor? Was it the day when He showed many paths and actions, and stood as both small and great? Was it the day when He removed the delusion of those with many trees and bestowed grace upon the great sages? Was it the day when He wandered, begging for alms with the skull of Brahma? Was it before or after He expounded many dharmas? Was it the day when He enshrined Himself in beautiful Thiru-Aroor?

Was it the day when He became a tall form on earth? Was it the day when He became all that stands and moves, and stood as a wish-fulfilling tree to explain? Was it before or after He created Vishnu for a reason, and to make the powerful Asuras perish by reducing their strength, and to save the celestials by making Vasuki vomit poison, and to kill Jalandhara? Was it the day when He enshrined Himself in Thiru-Aroor? Was it the day when He protected Muyalakan with His foot and stood as the supreme light on earth? Was it the day when He bestowed the imperishable celestial world upon His devotees who sing His praises?

Was it before or after the pure One, the Lord of the Bhootas, who never speaks falsehoods, the four Vedas, for the celestials, Was it before or after the pure One, the Lord of the Bhootas, who never speaks falsehoods, the four Vedas, for the celestials, expounded the Vedas? Was it the day when He enshrined Himself in glorious Thiru-Aroor? Was it the day when the eight smokes, the eight paths, the eight senses, the eight worlds, the eight groves, the eight arts, the eight protections, the eight visions, and the eight arts of those who reached His sacred feet, the eight smiles, the eight days, the eight good things, and the eight flowers in the hearts of the virtuous, were revealed? Was it before or after He revealed the eight directions? Was it the day when He enshrined Himself in Thiru-Aroor? Was it the day when He became the Lord and the seven worlds became mountains, and He destroyed Ravana?

Was it the day when He became the fragrant breeze of the flower-filled groves? Was it the day when He rejoiced wearing the elephant hide? Was it the day when He gave the pollen-filled flower to Chandi? Was it the day when He brought the Sagarars back to life and made them His own? Was it before or after the world knew Him? Was it the day when He enshrined Himself in Thiru-Aroor?

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings Thiru-Pathigams for Thiru-Aroor Sthalam. Sekkizhar Peruman continues to say that the Lord bestowed His grace upon Naminandhi Adigal, did He not? Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings about the greatness of Naminandhi Adigal’s Thiru-Thondu in his Thiru-Pathigam. Sekkizhar Peruman sings that the greatness of Naminandhi Adigal is spoken of in the four Vedas and other scriptures. The greatness of Naminandhi Adigal’s Thiru-Thondu. Because of the excellence of Naminandhi Adigal’s Thiru-Thondu, which was excellent in truthfulness, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal has sung about Naminandhi Adigal in his Thiru-Pathigam.

If Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, who only sings about Parameshwara, has sung about Naminandhi Adigal in his Thiru-Pathigam, then we can understand the greatness of Naminandhi Adigal’s Thiru-Thondu, which was excellent in truthfulness.

In addition, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings Thiru-Pathigams praising the glory of Shiva, who wears a garland of honey-filled Konrai flowers, and who is enshrined in the Thiru-Aroor Araneri temple. The Thiru-Sthalam where Naminandhi Adigal performed the Thiru-Thondu of lighting lamps with water is the Aroor Araneri temple, which is inside the Thiru-Aroor temple.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, who sings about Aroor Araneri, also sings about the greatness of Naminandhi Adigal’s Thiru-Thondu. To enable the people of the world to understand and benefit from the greatness of the devotees, Shiva Himself orchestrated the Thiru-Thonda Thogai Thiru-Pathigam through Nambiyaroorar in Thiru-Aroor. In that Thiru-Thonda Thogai, in the Thiru-Nindra Charukkam that we are currently examining, Naminandhi Adigal is spoken of as the last devotee.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal sings, “Arunambi Naminandhi Adiyaarkkum Adiyen” (I am a servant to the devotees, even to Arunambi Naminandhi). In the Thiru-Aroor Araneri temple, Naminandhi Adigal performs the Thiru-Thondu of lighting lamps with water. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal praises this event in the Thiru-Pathigam beginning with “Vempinai Pesi.” Therefore, Naminandhi Adigal is blessed to have his name appear in the Thevaram Thiru-Pathigam. Sekkizhar Peruman has also recorded this event in the thirty-first verse of Naminandhi Adigal Puranam.

Thus, the Thevaram that praised Naminandhi Adigal, sung by Thiru-Navukkarasar, The Thiru-Pathigam that begins with “Vempinai Pesi” is a Thiru-Aroor Thiru-Pathigam, the 102nd Thiru-Pathigam in the Fourth Thiru-Murai, composed in Thiru-Virutham Pann.

O devotees, you who speak of the neem, cherish the flesh, increase karma, block the passage, and consider relatives as support, come! Under the shade of the feet of the Lord who resides in Thiru-Aroor, with its beautiful lotus ponds, smear yourselves with sacred ash, and without deceit, serve and be saved! He who carefully selected and kept the foremost devotees, the golden ones, in Thiru-Aroor, He who performed the Paaroor Parippatham and Panguni Uthiram festivals, the Lord of fragrant flowers in Naaroor, His devotee Nambi Nandhi, the world knows how he lit lamps with water. Whether it is a beautiful vessel or a golden vessel, if the Lord who sweetly resides in Thiru-Aroor desires a vessel, we will make a vessel of Tamil garlands and worship Him, O foolish mind! He who wears a trembling moon, adorned with a coiled serpent, and whose devotees, the sages, serve Him, and not only that, but also those devotees who smear themselves with sacred ash, Nandi, the foremost devotee, is there for the nectar of Thiru-Aroor.

Those who held sugarcane were wounded by an axe. Those who held iron were made happy. Let them be.

The Lord who resides in beautiful Thiru-Aroor, surrounded by blossoming groves, I desire nothing from You, O mind that loves Him! Those who attain great wealth, such as banners, fly-whisks, drums, conches, and hand-lamps, even if they are flawless devotees and are within the six Even if they are flawless devotees and are within the six, for those who adorn themselves with that sacred ash, darkness is like Nandi, if he does not go out. In this Thiru-Pathigam, the seventh, eighth, and ninth verses are not available to us.

Now, the tenth verse: Let the conch shells sound in the early morning, let the incense of frankincense be offered in the blazing fire, He who placed the twenty skins, He who placed the red blood and the finger, His lotus feet have enslaved me.

In the second verse of this Thiru-Pathigam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings about the greatness of Naminandhi Adigal. He sings about Naminandhi Adigal lighting lamps with water. Naminandhi Adigal lighting lamps with water was in the Thiru-Aroor Araneri temple, which is a temple located within the Thiru-Aroor temple. This Thiru- Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal has bestowed a separate Thiru-Pathigam for the Thiru-Aroor Araneri temple.

In addition, he has bestowed a Thiru-Thandaka Pathigam connecting the two Sthalams, Thiru-Aroor Thiru-Moolattanam and Araneri. This glorious Aroor Araneri temple is located on the south side within the Thiru-Aroor temple. This temple is called Achaleshwaram. The sacred name of the Lord of Thiru-Aroor Araneri is Achaleshwarar. The sacred name of the Goddess is Vandaarkuzhali.

Here, the shrine of Lord Nataraja is very splendidly arranged. It is in this Thiru-Sthalam, the Thiru-Aroor Araneri Thiru-Sthalam, that Naminandhi Adigal performs the Thiru-Thondu of lighting lamps. During these days, at one time, due to the cruelty of the Jains, the conspiracy made by the Jains Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal has bestowed a separate Thiru-Pathigam for the Thiru-Aroor Araneri temple.

In addition, he has bestowed a Thiru-Thandaka Pathigam connecting the two Sthalams, Thiru-Aroor Thiru-Moolattanam and Araneri. This glorious Aroor Araneri temple is located on the south side within the Thiru-Aroor temple. This temple is called Achaleshwaram. The sacred name of the Lord of Thiru-Aroor Araneri is Achaleshwarar. The sacred name of the Goddess is Vandaarkuzhali.

Here, the shrine of Lord Nataraja is very splendidly arranged. It is in this Thiru-Sthalam, the Thiru-Aroor Araneri Thiru-Sthalam, that Naminandhi Adigal performs the Thiru-Thondu of lighting lamps. During these days, at one time, due to the cruelty of the Jains, the conspiracy made by the Jains Naminandi Adigal could not obtain oil to light the sacred lamps.

Therefore, lacking oil, Naminandi Adigal took water from the Deva Theertham in Thiruvarur and lit the sacred lamps, performing service. Near this spot is a mandapam called Thiruppani Kattum Mandapam. This mandapam is associated with the sacred histories of Kalarchinga Nayanar and Seruthunai Nayanar, which we will see in their respective Puranas. This Thiruvarur Araneri temple is referred to as Achalesam in the Thiruvarur Sthala Purana. A king named Samarkaran performed severe penance for four hundred years and was granted a vision of Lord Shiva. When Lord Shiva appeared, He asked, “What do you desire?” To this, King Samarkaran replied, “The Linga image that I have established and worship in this sacred place ...may you forever reside within it.” Thus, because the Lord resides immovably in this Linga image, this place is called Achalesam.

Worshipping here during Shivaratri yields great benefits. This Shivalinga possesses a unique glory: the shadow of Achaleshwar falls only to the east; it does not fall in other directions—that is its unique feature.

Furthermore, it is said that those who come to this place and behold this Shivalinga will not see its shadow if they are to die within six months. The Thiruvarur Purana states these truths: “That auspicious shadow of the Linga does not appear in any direction other than the east.” The Sthala Purana ...further states that if one who is to die within six months looks upon it, that peerless shadow will not be seen, as recounted in the Thiruvarur Purana. Such is the glory of the Thiruvarur Araneri temple, also known as Achaleswaram, located within the Thiruvarur temple complex. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman has bestowed a separate Thiru-pathikam upon this sacred place.

Additionally, he has bestowed a second pathikam, combining Thiruvarur Thirumoolattanam and Araneri. Those two pathikams are as follows: Araneri Thiru-pathikam, the fourth, seventeenth Thiru-pathikam. “This Thiruchitrambalam, whatever fire may enter, no harm comes to us. They will hide within us, murmuring ‘thethe.’ Holding a three-pronged spear that attains liberation, of that fiery hue ...Araneriyaare, they bear valor and wounds. They bear the burden of those who love them, like the wife of Vijayan. They bear the burden of the good, with bright green eyes, and wear garlands.

“Araneriyaare, they are of golden hue, with matted locks. They are of a deceptive hue, with the bee-laden tresses of the lady. They are of a sleeping hue, yet their eyes are sleepless, worshipped by the five-hued ones. Araneriyaare, they revealed Kama, causing him to fall. They destroyed the Ganga from the sky. They cleansed sins.

“They destroyed the three fortresses surrounded by stones. Araneriyaare of Thiruvarur. They are those who wear a coiled loincloth of white skull. They are those who have shed all their karmas. Those who reached out to worship Araneri of Thiruvarur attained light. They are those with coiled serpents, with jingling anklets.

“They are those who are eternally righteous, before whom the garland ...in the midst of darkness, the righteous ones, with five-hooded serpents spreading their hoods, the righteous ones of Araneri. They are skilled in union, with Uma in their thoughts. They are skilled in singing, practicing dawn and dusk. They are skilled in dancing, those who seek Araneri of Thiruvarur, they are skilled in dispelling karma.

“The Lord of Araneri of Thiruvarur, whose sacred feet are adorned with a garland of cool white moon and green konrai, and a garland of flowers, whose mind is a temple for those who worship Him morning and evening.

“The Lord of Araneri of Thiruvarur, whose crown is the color of the sky, whose chest is adorned with sacred ash, whose vehicle is glorious, whose form is the color of the ocean, whose feet are the color of the red sun.

“The Lord of Araneri of Thiruvarur, whose feet are the shade of the golden-haired one, who bestows sweet grace, who is worshipped day and night by kings, kinnaras, and celestials.

“The Lord of Araneri of Thiruvarur, who, regarding the king, took the Pushpaka, and regarding the deluded king ...bestowed with a sword, whose throat became dark from the poison he drank, the gracious Lord of Araneri of Thiruvarur.

“Now, let us contemplate the Purana of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, continuing with the Thiru-pathikam sung by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, combining Thiruvarur Thirumoolattanam and Thiruvarur Araneri. This is the thirty-third Thiru-pathikam of the sixth Thirumurai, a Thiruthandaka Thiru-pathikam.

“The Lord who wears the hide of a rutting elephant, who resides in Poovanam and Valanjuzhi, who is the nectar and honey of sugarcane, the brilliant light difficult to perceive, the golden mountain.

“The Lord who graciously resides in the Thiruvarur Moolattanam with its great golden ramparts, worshipped by the celestials, the ascetic. By reaching the Father in Araneri, I, your servant, have cut off the disease of karma. He who became the Kalpaka tree and the two luminaries, who resides in Kalatthi and on Mount Kailash. He who opened his eye to destroy Kama, who stood as a hunter for Vijayan. ...The Lord who resides in the beautiful groves of Thiruvarur Moolattanam, the wondrous one in the hearts of those who do not oppose Him. By reaching the Father in Araneri, I, your servant, have cut off the disease of karma.

“He who has a woman as half of his body, and the Ganga on his head, who resides in Paasoor and Parankundram. The Vedic scholar, who is easily accessible to his devotees, the light of true knowledge, whose fragrance is like a flower.

“The Lord who resides in the Thiruvarur Moolattanam, with its beautiful groves, who took residence in an anthill, worshipped by those who are. By reaching the Father in Araneri, I, your servant, have cut off the disease of karma.

“The Lord who accepts the service of Nandi, who made Nageswaram his abode. The true essence worshipped by celestials who offer fresh flowers, who bestowed the discus upon Markandeya.

“The Lord who took residence in the Thiruvarur Moolattanam, with its groves where the moon enters, the Brahmin worshipped by celestials. By reaching the Father in Araneri, I, your servant, have cut off the disease of karma. ...The Lord with a coral-like sacred body adorned with white ash, the Jyotirlinga, the Lord of Thungaanai Maadatthu. He who has the cremation ground as his abode, who is capable of burning the great sacrifice.

“The Lord who resides in the Thiruvarur Moolattanam, with its groves of palm trees, who crushed the sacrifice of the ignorant. By reaching the Father in Araneri, I, your servant, have cut off the disease of karma.

“The Lord who is the mother of all beings, the peerless one, the leader who performs the dance of dignity. He who, when Vishnu and Brahma and the celestials praised him, drank the poison of the churning ocean and rejoiced.

“The Lord who resides in the Thiruvarur Moolattanam, with its beautiful groves, the Lord who desired. By reaching the Father in Araneri, I, your servant, have cut off the disease of karma. He who became the good, meaningful words, who resides in Pukaloor and Purambayam. He who is the medicine for those with deluded minds, who made Marakaadu and Saikkaadu his abode. ...The Lord who joyfully resides in the Thiruvarur Moolattanam, with its dark, good groves, worshipped by celestials. The gracious one.

“By reaching the Father in Araneri, I, your servant, have cut off the disease of karma.

“The Lord who kicked Yama with his foot, who resides in Kaaronam and Kazhippalai. He who bestowed the ocean upon the child. He who is dear to his devotees who love to serve him.

“The Lord who resides in the Thiruvarur Moolattanam, with its fields where fish leap, the Lord who gave birth to coral. By reaching the Father in Araneri, I, your servant, have cut off the disease of karma. The peerless one, who has no equal, who resides in Oothoor and Uraiyoor. He who is the treasure, the ruby light, who became the wind, fire, water, and earth. The true essence, who resides within my heart, the one free from karma, the golden one who resides in Thirumoolattanam. By reaching the Father in Araneri, I, your servant, have cut off the disease of karma.

“He who knocked out the teeth of the sun god ...the one who was praised by the serpent, who made Painili his abode. He who troubled Ravana, the enemy, who is the darkness in the hearts of those who do not worship him.

“The Lord who resides in the glorious groves of Thiruvarur Moolattanam, the one who is not in the hearts of those who do not praise him. By reaching the Father in Araneri, I, your servant, have cut off the disease of karma.

“Let us continue to contemplate the Purana of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 406, Thirunindracharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having worshipped in Thiruvarur and sung many Thiru-pathikams, visits some temples near Thiruvarur and then returns to Thiruvarur. During his stay in Thiruvarur, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, using that town as a base, visited and worshipped in other sacred places such as Thirukkandrappur, Keezhvelur, and Thiruvalivalam. Sekkizhar Peruman sings: “He went, remembering Thiruvalivalam, where the Lord with matted locks and the moon resides. He worshipped the feet of the Lord, the partner of Uma, the lady with full breasts, and sang with joy.

“He sang, visiting Keezhvelur and Kandrappur, where the Lord with a dark throat resides. With insatiable love, he returned to Thiruvarur that very day.” Even after visiting Thiruvalivalam, Kandrappur, Keezhvelur, and other places and singing praises to the Lord, he returns to Thiruvarur and worships there due to his unceasing love for Thiruvarur. Sekkizhar Peruman mentions that Thirunavukkarasu Peruman visited three temples at this time, and by the grace of Lord Shiva, we now have a Thiru-pathikam for each of these three temples. The first of these temples is Kandrappur, which is now known as Koyil Kannappur. This Kandrappur temple is one of the temples on the southern bank of the Kaveri.

“This sacred place, Kandrappur, has received the prefix ‘Koyil’ and is known as Koyil Kandrappur. Kandrappur is located near Thiruvarur. Since the Pandavaaru and Vellaiyaru rivers flow near this place ...Kandrappur is rich in land and water resources. The Lord’s sacred names here are Vasthathampureeswarar, Naduthariyappar, Nadutharinathar. The Goddess’s sacred name is Srivallinayaki, Maathu Uma Ammai. The Sthala Vriksham is Kalpanai, a type of palm tree.

“The sacred waters of this place are Gnana Koopam, a well located inside the temple.

“Once, a merchant bathed in this sacred water, worshipped Nadutharinathar, and was cured of his eye disease. Next is Gnanamirtha Theertham, a well located amidst the fields near the Amman shrine. In ancient times, the Theerthavari ceremony was held in this sacred water during the Vaikasi festival. Next is Sivagangai, this sacred tank is to the east of the temple. Those who bathe in it will be saved from many diseases such as leprosy, epilepsy, tumors, colic, rheumatism, tuberculosis, eye ...diseases, headaches, fever, hiccups, and glandular diseases. Next is Karunamirtha Theertham, which is located to the west of the temple.

“The Nadutharinathar temple in Kandrappur is situated facing east, amidst groves and fields. This temple has only one Rajagopuram. There are four streets surrounding the temple. Inside the temple, there are two circumambulatory paths. The outer walls of the first circumambulatory path are small, and the walls of the inner circumambulatory path are new and tall. If one circumambulates the first circuit after passing the Rajagopuram, the kitchen is on the south side.

“Nearby is the Mani Mandapam. Opposite it, Rishabhadevar is seen with the Balipeetam. The sanctum sanctorum where Nadutharinathar resides, followed by the Ardha Mandapam, Maha Mandapam, the sanctum sanctorum of Maathumai Nayaki, and the stone mandapam are arranged. In the temple ...in the Maha Mandapam in front of Nadutharinathar, there are processional images of Somaskandar, Vinayagar, Subramaniyar, Chandeswarar, Natarajar, Sivakamiyammai, Chandrasekar, and others. Nearby, there are also processional deities such as Mariyamman, Manikkavasagar, Sundarar, Adippoor Amman, Pradosha Nayagar, and Asthradevar. In the circumambulatory path on the west, in the Thirumaligai pathi, there are images of Nirthana Vinayagar, Sundareswarar, Sundara Vinayagar, Siddhi Vinayagar, Sakthi Vinayagar, Mukthi Vinayagar, Narthana Vinayagar, and Bala Vinayagar.

“The Balasubramaniyar temple is separately located in the middle. Deities bearing images of Pidari, Jeshtadevi, Ayyanaar, Karpaganathar, and others are also seen. In the northern circumambulatory path, the Chandikeswarar temple is located. It is said that the Sthala Vriksham was a Kalpanai tree.

“However, that Sthala Vriksham is no longer there. Just as there is a stone banyan tree, Kalpanai must have been a type of palm tree.

“Now, let us see the reason for the name Kandrappur and the history of Nadutharinathar. Kandrappur means ‘calf’ (kandru) and ‘post’ (aappu), referring to the small post to which a calf is tied. Naduthari means ‘planted post.’ Once, Lord Shiva was seated on Mount Kailash with Goddess Uma.

“At that time, a Vidyadhara woman named Sudhavalli, assuming the form of Goddess Uma, danced before the Lord. She brought joy to the Lord by taking the form of Goddess Uma. Seeing this, Goddess Uma became angry with Sudhavalli, who had assumed her form, and ...cursed her to be born on earth. Sudhavalli, hearing Goddess Uma’s curse, shed tears and panicked, asking what she should do.

“Then the Goddess blessed her, saying, “You will reach the earth, worship Shiva, and attain us.” As commanded by Goddess Uma, Sudhavalli reached the southern Tamil country and was born in this sacred place, south of Devur, into a lineage of Saiva Vellala, full of Shiva-gnana, and grew up with the sacred name Kamalavalli. Kamalavalli lived always contemplating Lord Shiva. She grew up following the Saiva path. Due to her past karma, she performed Shiva Puja. She also reached marriageable age. Her parents, after considering her lineage and family, married Kamalavalli to a man they deemed suitable.

“Kamalavalli lived her married life in a separate house in that village. Kamalavalli, like Karaikkal Ammaiyar, was devoted to her husband, yet she had immense love for Lord Shiva, who is the life of all beings, and lived performing many acts of charity. She worshipped Lord Shiva incessantly. Her husband, not realizing Kamalavalli’s greatness, disliked her worship of Shiva and threw the Shivalinga into a well without her knowledge. Kamalavalli realized this and wondered whether to worship Shiva against her husband’s wishes or to abandon Shiva Puja. She decided to perform Shiva Puja secretly, without her husband’s knowledge.

“Therefore, she wished to perform Shiva Puja without her husband or anyone else knowing. There was a post in her house where a calf was tied. She worshipped that very post as a Shivalinga.

“At this time, Kamalavalli’s husband discovered this. He became angry when he realized that Kamalavalli was worshipping the post to which the calf was tied, considering it a Shivalinga, contrary to his wishes. He struck that calf-tying post, which Kamalavalli considered a Shivalinga, with an axe.

“At that moment, blood gushed out.

“Therefore, to make Kamalavalli’s devotion known to the world and to her husband, the Lord appeared there in the form of a Linga in that tying post. Kamalavalli and her husband attained Shivlokam.

“Thus, because the post to which the calf was tied transformed into a Linga, this place came to be known as Kandrappur.
