Although this Shivalinga image appeared as a Swayambhu Murthy, because it emerged from the post, people began to worship the Lord by the name Nadutharinathar. The place where that calf-tying post stood is now known as the Nadutharinathar temple. Even today, we can see the axe mark on the top of Nadutharinathar. To convey this great truth to the world, Appar Swamigal, in each verse of the pathikam he sang for this temple, concludes by singing, “One can see the Naduthari of Kandrappur.” This is the Sthala Purana of Kandrappur.

“Similarly, Kandrappur is a place associated with the Mahabharata story. Kandrappur is a place associated with the Mahabharata story. When the Pancha Pandavas were in exile in the forest, they came to the south and visited Kandrappur. As a sign of this, a river flowing near this village is named Pandavaaru. In the history of the Mahabharata, the name of a person called Idumban appears. Two histories concerning this Idumban are connected with Kandrappur.

“Because Idumban performed worship, a Shiva temple located a short distance from Kandrappur is still called Idumbavanam. According to the advice of Sage Parasara, Idumban came to Kandrappur in the south with his wife, bathed in the Sivagangai Theertham there, worshipped Nadutharinathar, and was blessed with a child. Idumban, who lived during the time of the Pancha Pandavas, following the instructions of the sages, came to Kandrappur, bathed in the Sivagangai, worshipped Nadutharinathar, and was cured of his eye disease. Daily rituals are regularly performed in this temple. The Vaikasi Visakam festival is celebrated annually as a three-day event. In this temple, the processional deity Mariyamman, also known as Seethalambikai, has a grand ten-day festival celebrated annually in the month of Chithirai.

“These are the Sthala Puranas and information about Kandrappur. As we have already seen, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, who set out from Thiruvarur, came to Kandrappur, worshipped Nadutharinathar, and sang a Thiru-pathikam there. This Thiru-pathikam is compiled as the sixty-first Thiru-pathikam in the sixth Thirumurai, a Thiruthandaka Thiru-pathikam.

““O Lord, who delights in having a woman as half of your body, who has the sacred Vedas as your tongue, who wears the moon, the Lord of all celestials ...daily praising and melting with devotion, free from deceit and full of love, with the power of penance, offering water and flowers thrice a day, never forgetting to praise and worship. In the hearts of devotees who worship with such love, one can see the Naduthari of Kandrappur. As soon as dawn breaks, smearing white ash on their bodies, wearing a white loincloth, saying, ‘You are the one who cures the disease of strong karma, you are Shiva who shows the path to liberation,’ saying, ‘You are the partner of the lady with a slender waist like a drum,’ saying, ‘You are the light who dances in the cremation ground,’ offering fresh flowers and worshipping. In the hearts of such devotees, one can see the Naduthari of Kandrappur. If anyone, by chance, sees sacred ash and sacred symbols, they will not despise them.

“When they see such people, they will rejoice and remember their service, and then ...looking at them, they will not say, ‘This is their god, that is their god,’ and avoid duality, but will cherish the Lord’s power. In the hearts of such devotees who worship without covetousness, one can see the Naduthari of Kandrappur. In their hearts, they will not think, ‘Youth will not last,’ but will give alms to everyone, and without shining, they will stand on the path, with abundant wisdom, making truth abundant and removing falsehood. Protecting the celestials who do not shine, keeping their minds fixed on the feet of the Lord who drank poison. In the hearts of such devotees who worship without wavering, one can see the Naduthari of Kandrappur. “O ancient one, whose throat drank the poison of the ocean, who wears the white moon on your matted locks, O unique one, O husband of Uma, O Lord of the world, O subtle, brilliant light, O beloved of your devotees!” Even if they lament thus, restraining the five senses within, and looking inward with lamentation.

“In the hearts of such devotees who worship with their minds, one can see the Naduthari of Kandrappur. Mesiyinal midaithu puzhu pothintha porvai pollatha pulaal udambai nilasumendru pasiyinal meethoorappattE eetti palarkku udaval athu ozhinthu pavalavayar vasiyinal agappattu veezha munnam vanavarkon thirunamam anjum solli kasivinal thozhum adiyar nenjin ullE kantrappur naduththariyai kaanalame Aiyinal midaru adaippu undu aakkai vittu aaviyar povathume agaththarkoodi maiyinal kannazhuthi malai sootti mayanaththil iduvathan mun mathiyam soodum aiyanarkku aalagi anbu mikku agam kuzhainthu mey arumbi adigal patham kaiyinal thozhum adiyar nenjin ullE kantrappur naduththariyai kaanalame thiruththimaiyal aivaraiyum kaval Evi thigaiyathe sivayanama ennum sinthai suruthitha thuyakkaruththu thunba vellak kadal neenthik karaiyerum karuththai mikku paruthithanai parpariththa pavanasa paramchudare endrendru paravinallum karuthi miga thozhum adiyar nenjin ullE kantrappur naduththariyai kaanalame Iththiruppathigaththil onpathavathu seyyul namakku kidaikkapperavillai ini paththavathu thiruppadal kunintha silaiyal puram moondru eriththay endrum kootruthaiththa kurai kalar sevadiya endrum thananjaiyarkku pasupatham eenthay endrum thasakkirivan malai adukka viralal oondri muninthavan than siram paththum thallum thollum muran azhiththittu arul koduththa murththi endrum kaninthu miga thozhum adiyar nenjin ullE kantrappurai kaanalame Thiruchitrambalam ivvaru kantrappur vanthu thiruppathigam padiyathirunavukkarasu peruman keezh Thiru-Velur, a sacred sthalam, where he worships the Lord.

“Let us go on contemplating.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 407, Thiru-nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped at Thiru-Kandrappur, reached the sacred sthalam of Keezh-Velur and sang a Thiru-pathigam there. Keezh-Velur is located near Nagapattinam in Tamil Nadu. The Lord’s sacred names are Akshaya Lingeswarar, Kediliyappar. The Goddess’s sacred names are Vanmulai Nayaki, Sundara Kujambal.

The sthala-vriksham is the Ilandai tree. The Thirtham is Saravana Poigai, Saravana Thirtham. Since Vel, or Lord Muruga, worshipped the Lord here, this sthalam is named Velur. To prevent any hindrance to Lord Muruga’s Shiva Puja, the Goddess, as an aspect of Durga, guarded it.

Here, that Goddess is known as Anju-vattathu Ammai. It stands as the eighty-fourth sthalam among the sacred sthalams sung on the southern bank of the Cauvery. It is one of the Maada temples built by Kochengat Chozhan. This sacred temple shines with nine thirthams, chariot-moving streets, four-sided walls, gopuram entrances, mathavilagam, Shanbagavanam, and other features. Originally, when the Devas and Asuras churned the sacred Milk Ocean, a drop of Amrita that arose scattered into two, with one part falling in the northern part of Bharatham and the other part of that drop falling in the southern part of Bharatham. The drop that fell in North Bharatham became an Ilandai tree, then a forest, and was called Vadapathrikasiramam.

The other part of that Amrita drop fell here in Keezh-Velur, becoming an Ilandai forest, and was called Thenpath Pathrikaranayam.

Therefore, the Ilandai tree became the sthala-vriksham in this sthalam. This is the sthalam where Lord Muruga performed puja to Lord Shiva to remove the dosha of Veeragathi.

Hence, it is known as Bhoosaranayapuram. Just as the celestial realm where Lord Muruga resides is called Mel-Velur, this place where Lord Muruga stayed and performed puja on this earth is called Keezh-Velur.

After the Samharam (destruction) was completed, Lord Muruga, who performed Shiva puja in Thiru-Chendur, came to this sacred sthalam, revered as Then Ilandai Vanam, by the divine command of Lord Shiva, and performed Shiva puja to remove the sin of killing. As Lord Shiva commanded, here Lord Muruga established five Lingams and performed Nava-Lingam Lord Muruga performed the puja. For this, the Thirtham created by Lord Muruga is called Pathala Gangai. To the east of this sthalam, Lord Muruga consecrated and worshipped Kailasanathar and Soundarya Nayaki.

Therefore, this sacred sthalam is called Kovil Kadambanur. To its east, the place where Chaturveda Murthy established and worshipped Tharunasoriyai is called Azhiyur. To its east, since Soundarya Nayaki consecrated and worshipped Sundareswarar, that sthalam is called Ilam Kadambanur. To the northeast of this sthalam, Sundarakesi consecrated Somanatha Peruman, and Lord Muruga worshipped him. That village is called Perunkadambanur.

After this, to the northeast, in Kadambara Vazhkai, Lokambal Lord Muruga consecrated and worshipped Sakalanathar with Lokambal, thus completing the Pancha-linga puja.

Similarly, Lord Muruga also performed the Nava-linga puja in this sthalam. All the sthalams where the Nava-linga puja was performed are located near this sthalam. Lord Muruga created the Thirtham called Athibhavanam and performs the Nava-linga puja. The place where Lord Muruga established and worshipped Narmadeswari Narmadeswarar is called Vallamangalam.

Then, to the south, in Pattumangalam, he consecrated Visalakshi with Viswanathar and performed Shiva puja.

Then, in Sottal Vannam, he consecrated and worshipped Maheswari Poosesarar.

Then, in Devur, known as Kadalivanam, he praised Devapureeswarar.

Then, to its west, he came to Madhuvana and O In Podhiyathur, he worshipped and praised Thulainayaki with Thulaisar, completing the Nava-linga puja. Lord Muruga worshipped the self-manifested Shiva Lingam, which shone as a form of light beneath the ancient Ilandai tree, and established a Vimanam named Pushkalam.

Then, at the eastern gopuram entrance, in the Agni corner, he created the sacred tank to be known as Saravana Thirtham.

First, he bathed in it, and then made the nine Veerars, one hundred and eight Senathipathis, and two thousand Vellam Bhoothapadais bathe. In this sacred tank, Lord Muruga performed Shiva puja to remove the sin of killing and the Veeragathi. The Veeragathis caused hindrances to the Shiva puja he performed.

Therefore, thinking that the Shiva puja performed for the father should be completed, he called the Mother. The six-faced Kumaran. The Mother immediately arose as Durga and circled in the four directions and in the sky, protecting and blessing the Shiva puja performed by Lord Muruga, so that no hindrance occurred.

Therefore, this Mother is known by the sacred name Anju-vattathu Amman. Brahma came here and created Brahma Thirtham and worshipped Lord Shiva. Indra lost all his wealth because he did not worship Vasishta, the Guru of the Devas. Knowing the way to regain it, Indra came to this sthalam on a new moon day in the month of Margazhi, created the Indra Thirtham tank in the Niruthi corner, bathed in it, celebrated a festival in the month of Chithirai, and regained his freedom from the curse and his wealth.

Once, the Maruts, in a yagna, received the Havis with disgust.

Therefore, they suffered from a stomach ailment. To cure this ailment, they came to this sacred sthalam, created Agni Thirtham, worshipped Shiva, and were relieved of their illness. Yama, wishing to atone for all the evil deeds he had committed against Shiva’s devotees, came to this sacred sthalam, which is a forest of sacred trees, created Yama Thirtham in the southwest corner, bathed in it, worshipped Kediliyappar according to the rules, and became pure.

Thus, the two thirthams, Agni Thirtham and Yama Thirtham, are now combined and known as Arasanaikulam. On a Chaturthi day in the month of Aani, Chandra mocked Lord Ganesha’s pot-belly.

Then Ganesha cursed Chandra. As a result, Chandra’s phases began to wane. Chandra, who came to this sacred sthalam, created Chandra Thirtham in the northeast direction, bathed in it, worshipped Lord Shiva three times a day, and regained his waxing phases. Adiseshan once conquered Vayu, and thus became arrogant. Due to this arrogance, Adiseshan’s strength began to diminish. Realizing this, Adiseshan came to this sthalam, created a tank in the west named Sesha Thirtham after himself, bathed in it, brought a Banalingam from the banks of the Narmada, placed it in the western part of this tank, named it Anantheswarar, and worshipped Lord Shiva for a long time, regaining his former strength.

Adiseshan.

The Lord of this sthalam showed his right foot to Agathiyar.

Furthermore, those who received grace in this sthalam are as follows: Markandeyar. A man named Thunmathi attained liberation here. Chandraguptan, a Vaishya, regained all his lost wealth. Savveeran was freed from his curse in this sthalam. Even a monkey and a cat worshipped the Lord here and received divine grace. Dharmagnyan received the power of penance here.

A Brahmin woman named Utpalangi received the Lord’s grace here.

The Lord rendered justice to an Adisaiva woman here.

Thus, many have worshipped the Lord of this sthalam and received grace. There is one Thevaram Thiru-pathigam by Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and one Thevaram Thiru-pathigam by Appar Swamigal for this sthalam. The Thiru-pathigam sung by Appar Swamigal is the sixty-seventh Thiru-pathigam in the sixth Thiru-murai, a Thiru-thandaga Thiru-pathigam.

Alana adiyavarkku anban thannai ananjum adiyai naan abayampukka thalanai thannoppar illathanai santhanamum kungumamum santhum thoyntha tholanai tholatha muththoppanai thu veluththa kovanamathai araiyil arththa keezhanai keezhvelur aalum kovai kediliyai nadum avar kedu ilare sorpavam porul therinthu thuymai nokki thungaththar manaththirulai vangathanai narpannmai ariyatha nayinenai nannarikkE selum vannam nalkinanai parpavam vayara padiyadi paninthelunthu kurainthu adainthar pavam pokkirpanai keezhvelur aalum kovai kediliyai nadumavar kedilare alaivayil aravasaiththa azhagan thannai atharikum adiyavarkatku anbe endrum vilaivanai meignana porul He is the beloved of those who have become His devotees, He who bathed in the five sacred substances, I sought refuge in His feet, He who has no equal, He whose shoulders are smeared with sandalwood, saffron, and paste, He who is like an unpierced pearl, He who wears a pure white loincloth around His waist, He is the Lord who rules Keezh-Velur, those who seek Kedili will have no harm. He who, understanding the meaning of words, looking for purity, does not remove the darkness from the minds of those who do not sleep, He who granted me, a dog who knows no goodness, the path to righteousness, He who removes the sins of those who sing with their mouths full of words, worship, rise, and surrender, He is the Lord who rules Keezh-Velur, those who seek Kedili will have no harm. He who is the beautiful one who tied the snake to the waves, He who is always love for the devotees who cherish Him, He who is the essence of true knowledge, He who is within, the master, He who destroys the devotion of even the Buddhas, He who does not soften for those who are not His, He who is endless, He who entered within me and stirred the impurity in my mind, He is the Lord who rules Keezh-Velur, those who seek Kedili will have no harm. He who shines in the lotus flowers, He who cut off a head and observed the great vow, He who became the day of the fierce battle, He who will save me from the pit of terrible hell, I, who am full of evil deeds, He who is the father of Vishnu, He who is the Brahmin, He who listens to the Veena that holds the meaning of the Vedas, He is the Lord who rules Keezh-Velur, those who seek Kedili will have no harm. He who is good, He who rides a white bull, He who is the word that the four Vedas and their six angas cannot approach, He who became the three lights, He who is close to those who serve as devotees, He who is the archer, He who has a gentle woman as a part of Him, He who cannot remove the sins of those who do not think of Him as true, He is the Lord who rules Keezh-Velur, those who seek Kedili will have no harm.

He who twisted the Ganga, the flower, the Vanni, the Konrai, the pure Dhatura, and the living snake, He who destroyed the three cities by fire, He who consumed the deadly poison for the sake of all, He who opened His eye and made Kama’s body turn to dust, He who desired the gentle woman as a part of Him, He who tore apart, He is the Lord who rules Keezh-Velur, those who seek Kedili will have no harm. He who is the inner light, He who is the inner meaning of Omkara residing within the heart, He who is the light that emits, He who is the two lights and the one, He who became the sky and the earth, He who is the growing light, He who is of the form of emerald, He whom the celestials always praise, He who is the ancient light, He is the Lord who rules Keezh-Velur, those who seek Kedili will have no harm. He who stopped Yama with His foot, He who bestowed grace upon the young boy who sought refuge in Him, He who wore the tiger skin and the bones and the snake, He who is within the hearts of those who contemplate Him, He who held the terrible poison in His throat, He who destroyed the sacrifice of Daksha when the celestials gathered, He is the Lord who rules Keezh-Velur, those who seek Kedili will have no harm. He who wears the bones of the dead, He who is the dancer in the cremation ground, He who wears the snake and bones, He who dances in the cremation ground, He who entered my heart and took residence, ruling me, He who is of unknowable thought, He who removed all the doubts of the celestials, He is the Lord who rules Keezh-Velur, those who seek Kedili will have no harm. He who broke the mountain with harsh words, He who sang by plucking the nerves of his arm before his old age, He who extended his small knife, He who imprinted His sacred feet in my sinful heart, He who burned the three cities, He who, by deceiving the liars, He who makes them waste their time, He is the Lord who rules Keezh-Velur, those who seek Kedili will have no harm.

Let us resume our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 408, Thiru-nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped at Thiru-Kandrappur and Keezh-Velur, reaches the sacred temple of Thiru-Valivalam. Thiru-Valivalam is a sacred sthalam located on the Thiru-varur Thiru-thuraipoondi road. The Lord’s sacred names here are Hrudaya Kamalanatheswarar, Manathunai Nathar. The Goddess’s sacred names are Vazhaiyanganni, Angaiyarkanni.

The sthala-vriksham is the Punnai tree. The Thirtham is Karanar Gangai, Sankara Thirtham. Since the sparrow, called Valiyan, worshipped here, this sthalam is named Valivalam. Surya and Karanama Munivar worshipped here and gained fame. The Thevaram Thiru-pathigams of Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, Thiru-navukkarasu Swamigal, and Sundaramurthy Nayanar are found here for this stalam. The sacred names of this sthalam include Vilvavanam, Ekachakrapuram, and Munnurru Mangalam.

This is a Maada temple built by Kochengat Chozhan. The sacred verse beginning ‘Pidiyathan uruvumai kola’ belongs to this sthalam. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, who came to this sthalam, composed a Thiru-thandaga Thiru-pathigam. This is the forty-eighth Thiru-pathigam in the sixth Thiru-murai.

Nallan kan nan maraigal ayinan kan namban kan nanugathar puram moondru eytha villan kan vinnvarkkum melankan melliyalal pangkan kan veda velvi sollan kan sudar moondrum ayinan kan thondagi panivarkku tholvan eeya vallan kan vanavargal vanangiyethum Valivalathan kan avan en manaththane. He is the good one, He is the four Vedas, He is the trustworthy one, He is the archer who shot the three cities of those who did not approach Him, He is superior to the celestials, He has a gentle woman as a part of Him, He is the word of the Vedic sacrifice, He is the three lights, He is capable of granting ancient liberation to those who serve as devotees, He is Valivalathan whom the celestials worship and praise, He is in my heart. He is the flesh, He is the life for the body, He is the existent, He is the non-existent, He is the honey for Uma, He is the sacred, He is the direction, He is the sacred water, He is the one who saw Parthan’s service, He is the forest, He is the ocean, He is the mountain, He is the celestial who covered the elephant’s skin with joy, He is Valivalathan whom the celestials worship and praise, He is in my heart. He is the one who is, He is the natural one for all, He is joy, He is free from sorrow, He is the mother, He is the unique tattva for the world, He is the supreme, He is everywhere, He is beyond the universe, He is the mouth of those who melt in heart, with goosebumps, and weep, He is Valivalathan whom the celestials worship and praise, He is in my heart. He is the one who sustained, He is the life for the body, He is the one in Omkara, He is the seed for all the worlds, He is the rain that pours from the sky, He is the fruit, He is the one who always deceived the hearts of those who did not desire Him, He is the one who bore the seven worlds, He is the one who placed the water, the growing moon, and the snake on His head, He is Valivalathan whom the celestials worship and praise, He is in my heart.

He is Yama, He is virtue, He is the mark, He is all faults, He is the beautiful ash, He is the shadow, He is the fire, He is the one who received the water-filled Ganga on His matted hair, He is the seven worlds, He is the one who changed Kama into dust in an instant, He is Valivalathan whom the celestials worship and praise, He is in my heart. He is the permanent, He is the creator, He is the Lord, He is the water, He is the rock, He is the archer who shot the three cities, He is the one who added the honey-tongued woman with red lips and dark hair to one side, He is the art, He is the wind, He is the one who caused Yama to fall, He is the divine mountain called Kailash, He is Valivalathan whom the celestials worship and praise, He is in my heart. He is the woman, He is the man, He is always great for the great, He is the rare one, He is Brahma, He is the number, He is the letter, He is the joyful music, He is the nature, He is the eye that sees all, He is the thought, He is the past word and the path, He is the moon, He is the king surrounded by the seven seas, He is Valivalathan whom the celestials worship and praise, He is in my heart. He is the first one. He is the one behind, He is the primeval one with an ageless form, He is the one with the crown, He is the one with three lights. He is near to His devotees and to the worlds, He is far, He is the immeasurable light.

He is the lightning, He is the thunder, He desired a part of Thirumal. He is the eternal lord of the Ganga here, He is the Lord of Thiruvalivalam whom the celestials worship and praise. He is in my heart. He is the treasure for all, He is the justice that none can conceive, He is the Veda, He is the refuge for those who contemplate Him. He is the cloud, He became fire, He is the Lord, He is the ancient one, He is the one who holds the moon with the snake. He is the Lord of Thiruvalivalam whom the celestials worship and praise.

He is in my heart. He is the one whom Brahma on the lotus and Vishnu who measured the world as a child could not find by praising. He is the fire that cannot be measured by those with hands on their heads. The king of Lanka, surrounded by the roaring sea, with his fragrant locks. He is the beautiful one who pressed the crowned head with his finger. He is the Lord of Thiruvalivalam whom the celestials praise.

He is in my heart.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped Thiruvalivalam, returns to Thiruvarur. During these days when Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman resided in Thiruvarur, the day of Thiruvathirai arrives. On that auspicious day of Thiruvathirai, the Lord proceeds in a procession, and a grand procession is witnessed. In that procession on the day of Thiruvathirai, celestials and sages gather in crowds and worship Lord Thiyagaraja. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman goes before them and serves, joining with the Shiva devotees. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman will now sing about the glories of this Thiruvathirai day in the Thiru-Pathikam that begins with “Muthuvithanam.”

Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is about to sing about all the glories of this Thiruvathirai day in the Thiru-Pathikam.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who was delighted by the darshan in Thiruvarur, feels a desire in his heart, by the grace of God, to worship the sacred feet of Lord Shiva residing in Thiruppukalur. The yearning to worship Thiruppukalur arises in the heart of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman by the grace of God. This is because Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar goes to Thiruppukalur and worships the Lord there.

There, the presence of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman occurs. Consequently, and as a continuation, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, these two great personalities, travel together for a long time, showing the path of devotion to this world. They show the path of devotion to the world. In Thiru-Vizhimilalai, they protect the Shiva devotees by feeding them. Both then go to Thiru-Maraikkadu and make the Lord appear before them through Tamil Vedas.

Then, from there, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman proceeds to the Pandya country to fulfill his divine mission of refuting other religions and explaining the greatness of the sacred ash.

After that, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s pilgrimage to Thiru-Kailash takes place.

Thus, there are many continuous events that are yet to happen. For all these to happen, the divine grace of the Lord, sensing from within Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, makes him yearn to go to Thiruppukalur and serve the Lord there. Unwilling to part from the Lord of Thiruvarur, he leaves Thiruvarur and reaches Thiruppukalur. He visits many sacred places on his way. These sacred places include Thiruppalliyin Mukkoodal, Thiru-Virukudi, Thiruppanaiyur, and other holy sites. Among these, we have received one Thiru-Thandagam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for the holy site of Thiruppalliyin Mukkoodal.

Thiruppalliyin Mukkoodal is also known as Kuruvirameswaram. The Lord’s name is Mukkonanathar, Thrineethraswami, Mukkoodalnathar. The Goddess’s name is Anjanakshi, Maimevu Kanniy. The sacred tree is Vilvam, and the sacred water is Mukkoodal Theertham. In the ancient Sivathala Manjari text, this place is referred to as Ariyanpalli. Jatayu performed penance to the Lord and asked when his end would come.

The Lord told Jatayu that when Ravana abducts Sita, he would obstruct him, and then his wings would be cut, and he would fall and die. Jatayu, upon hearing this, said, “Oh Lord, then I will not be able to bathe in the sacred waters of Kasi, Ganga, Rameswaram, Sethu, etc., and attain their benefits. What shall I do?” The Lord then created the Mukkoodal Theertham and commanded him to bathe in it. Jatayu bathed there and received the benefits. Based on this history, people colloquially call this area Kuruvirameswaram. This sacred water is considered equal to Thiruveni Sangamam.

It is said to bestow sixteen times the benefit of bathing in the Ganga, Sethu, and other sacred waters.

Therefore, it is called this sacred water. This holy site is near Thiruvarur. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped this site, has composed a Thiru-Thandaga Thiru-Pathikam, which is the sixty-ninth Thiru-Pathikam in the sixth Thiru-Murai. It is predominantly structured.

“Aaratha Innamuthai Ammaan Thannai Ayanodu Maal Ariyaatha Aathiyaanai Thaaraarum Malarkondrai Chadaiyaan Thannai Sangaranai Thannoppar Illaathaanai Neeraanai Kaatraanai Thee Aanaanai Neelvishumbaay Aazhkadalgal Ezhum Soozhntha Paaraanai Palliyin Mukkoodalaanai Payilaathe Paazhenaana Uzhantravaare.” (He is the insatiable nectar, He is the Lord, He is the beginning whom Brahma and Vishnu do not know. He is the one with a matted lock adorned with fragrant Konrai flowers, He is Shankara, He has no equal. He is water, He is air, He is fire, He is the vast sky, He is the earth surrounded by the seven deep seas. He is the Lord of Palliyin Mukkoodal. I, a fool, wandered without knowing Him.) “Vidaiyaanai Vinnnavargal Ennathaanaai Vedhiyanai Venthingal Soodum Sennichchadaiyaanai Saamam Pol Kandaththaanai Thaththuvanaithannoppar Illaathaanai Adaiyaathaar Mummathilum Theeyil Moozhga Aduganai Koththaanai Ayilkol Soola Padaiyaanai Palliyin Mukkoodalaanai Payilaathe Paazhenaana Uzhantravaare.” (He is the bull-rider, He is the thought of the celestials, He is the Veda, He is the one with a matted lock adorned with the white moon on His head, He is the one with a throat like the Sama Veda, He is the truth, He has no equal.

He is the one who shot the arrow so that the three forts of those who did not reach Him were immersed in fire. He is the one with a sharp trident as a weapon. He is the Lord of Palliyin Mukkoodal. I, a fool, wandered without knowing Him.) “Poodhiyanai Ponvaraiye Polvaan Thannai Purichchadai Mel Punal Karantha Punithan Thannai Vedhiyanai Venkaadu Meyaan Thannai Vellertrin Melaanai Vin. He is the one who is like a golden mountain, He is the holy one who hid the water in His matted locks. He is the Veda, He is the one who resides in Venkadu, He is the one who rides the white bull, He is the sky.

“He is the origin of all these, He is the Lord, He is the one whose half is the dark-eyed Goddess. He is the Lord of Palliyin Mukkoodal. I, a fool, wandered without knowing Him. He is the one who wore the tiger skin, He is the holy one who shot the arrow so that the three cities were reduced to dust. He is the one whose half is the woman with firm breasts, He is the one who drank the poison from the roaring sea and removed the fear of the celestials. He is the one who looked at Kama, who went to the south, and reduced his body to dust.

“He is the Lord of Palliyin Mukkoodal. I, a fool, wandered without knowing Him. He is the one who removed the sins, sufferings, diseases, evil deeds, and poverty of those who sought refuge in Him. He is the one with a throat like a dark cloud, He is the one who cut the body of the fierce one with the discus. He is the one who has no equal, He is the truth, He is the perfect one, He is the one who resides in the hearts of those who remember Him. He is the Lord of Palliyin Mukkoodal.

“I, a fool, wandered without knowing Him. He is the one who hid the Ganga flood in His red matted locks. He is the one with the sacred body that dances with fire, He is the one with the lotus-like hand, He is the God of gods, He is the radiant light, He is the one who protects His devotees from suffering. He is the one who spread as earth, sky, roaring sea, vast firmament, and all else. He is the Lord of Palliyin Mukkoodal. I, a fool, wandered without knowing Him.

“He is the one with the river in His matted locks, He is the Lord of Nallur, He is the one who resides in Nallatru, He is the Lord of Nallathaanam. He is the Lord of Vaimoor, surrounded by honey-laden groves, He is the one who resides in Maraikkadu, He is the Lord of Akkur. He is the friend of the treasurer, He is the Lord of Needur, He is the one who resides in Neythanam, He is the Lord of Aaroor. He is the Lord of Palliyin Mukkoodal. I, a fool, wandered without knowing Him. He is the good ascetic, He is the one who became the four Vedas, He is the good one, He is the one who destroyed the three forts of those who did not approach Him.

“He is the victorious one who resides in Thirumoolathanam of Thiruvarur, adorned with the moon on His red matted locks, He is the one who wore the fierce snake, He is the one who approached Him humbly. He is the refuge for those who have taken refuge in His power. He is the Lord of Palliyin Mukkoodal. I, a fool, wandered without knowing Him. He is the flesh, He is the body, He is the life, He is the one who became the seven worlds, He is the Lord of the celestials, He is the celestial one, He is the one with the moon, He is the wealthy one, He is the one who went behind the boar before the mountain daughter. He is the one who is seen, He is the one who is in Mount Kailash, He is the one who melts and resides in the hearts of those who are devoted to Him.

“He is the Lord of Palliyin Mukkoodal. I, a fool, wandered without knowing Him. He is the one who stopped, He is the one who, in anger, clapped His hands and lifted the great mountain with His twenty shoulders and heads. He is the one who pressed with His sacred toe and sweetly listened to the musical song of the seven strings, and gave him the name and the sharp sword. He is the one who killed Yama with His broken anklet. He is the Lord of Palliyin Mukkoodal.

“I, a fool, wandered without knowing Him.

“Thus, Thiruppalliyin Mukkoodal. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having worshipped the Lord at the sacred site and composed a Thiru-Pathikam, visits the sacred sites of Thiru-Virukudi, Thiruppanaiyur, and others, and then reaches Thiruppukalur.

“At the same time, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, having set out from Sirkazhi, visits many sacred sites where Lord Shiva manifested, and then arrives at Thiruppukalur, also known as Poombukalur, and resides in the sacred math of Muruga Nayanar.

“At the same time, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman arrives at Thiruppukalur.

“Therefore, the second meeting of the great Acharyas, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, is about to take place. We shall continue our reflection.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 409, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having departed from Thiruvarur and visited many holy sites, arrives at Thiruppukalur, also known as Poombukalur. Pugalur is a place called Saranyapuri, a place where souls, fearing the heat of birth, surrender to the Lord.

Therefore, it is called Saranyapuri, a place where one takes refuge in the Lord, hence called Pugalur. It is referred to as Poombukalur in the Thiru-Muraigal. The word ‘Poo’ means beauty, a place for both worldly pleasures and liberation.

Furthermore, this town has many ponds and many lotuses, and the temple shines like another lotus amidst these lotuses. This place is called Poombukalur. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman mentions “Poombukalur Meviya Punniyane” in a Thiru-Thandagam. Such a Pugalur, Thiruppukalur, is of great significance. It is the place where Muruga Nayanar was born and performed the sacred service of Thiruppalliththamam. In the Puranam of Muruga Nayanar, we extensively discussed his sacred history and the sacred services he rendered with the garlands of flowers he made.

Thus, Muruga Nayanar was special in adorning the Lord with different garlands of flowers according to the seasons and delighting in His divine will.

Moreover, Muruga Nayanar had the unique distinction of having both the great spiritual leaders, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, the child-saint, and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, the king-saint, residing in his sacred math at the same time and worshipping them. Muruga Nayanar also had the unique distinction of attending the wedding of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and attaining liberation there. Thiruppukalur is the town where such a great Muruga Nayanar lived. In such a Thiruppukalur, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman is already residing in Muruga Nayanar’s sacred math. At this same time, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having completed his darshan in Thiruvarur and visited many places on the way, is heading towards Thiruppukalur. As soon as Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, who is residing in Muruga Nayanar’s sacred math, hears the news that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is coming to Thiruppukalur, he desires to go and meet Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar.

Therefore, surrounded by his retinue of devotees, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman goes to meet and welcome Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman goes to meet and welcome Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman.

At this point, Sekkizhar Peruman sings that Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar returned to Thiruppukalur. “Mezhuthal” means to come. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar came to Thiruvarur by worshipping the temples from the north, such as Thiru-Peruvelur and Thiru-Vilamar. From Thiruvarur, if one turns east, one can reach temples like Thiru-Keezhvelur, Thiru-Sikkal, Thiru-Nagai Karoanam, etc.

But instead of going there, he returns directly north towards Thiruppukalur by the same path he came.

Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman mentions here that he “returned.” Thus, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman comes to welcome Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, hearing of the loving welcome from Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, comes with a joyful heart. Devotees also accompany these two great personalities. Shiva devotees gather there eagerly to witness the sacred event of these two great personalities meeting. The meeting of devotees from both sides was like the joining of two oceans of moonlight, as Peruman sings. He sings that it was like the meeting of great oceans of light.

The light of the moon is white.

Here, the devotees coming from both sides are those who have smeared sacred ash.

Therefore, as white light emanated from both sides and the two sacred groups joined. Sekkizhar Peruman compares it to two oceans of moonlight merging. “Karandhamali Thadam Poigai Kaaliyar Kōn Ethir Anaiyum Kaathal Kettu Varanthu Mani Punal Pugalur Nōkki Varum Vaakeesar Magizhndhu Vanthaar Thiranda Perum Thiruneetru Thondar Kuzhaam Iru Thiramum Serntha Pōthil Irandu Nilavin Kadalgal Onraagi Anainthana Pōl Isaintha Anre” (Hearing of the love of Kaaliyar Kōn coming to meet him at the pond full of water, Vaakeesar, who was coming towards Pugalur with its clear waters, came joyfully. When the large gathering of devotees smeared with sacred ash from both sides met, it was as if two oceans of moonlight merged into one.) Sekkizhar Peruman sings that it was like two oceans of moonlight merging into one. The phrase “merged into one” indicates that the gathering of devotees smeared with sacred ash from both sides mingling with each other is a symbolic representation of the non-dual union of Shiva’s bliss. Thiru-Navukkarasar went forward to worship.

Thiru-Gnanasambandha Pillaiyar, the divine truth of Sirapuram, bowed in return and said, “Appare, when you come, please describe the greatness of Thiruvarur.” Peruman composes the next verse, stating that he, whose truth is practiced in the five sacred letters, also replied in return. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, with a great desire to see and worship each other, come together and worship each other. Even though Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman came to meet him, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, with the intention of going to meet and worship him first, worshipped Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman also worshipped Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar in return and welcomed him. He welcomes Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman as “Arunaamathu Anjezhuthum Payil Vaimaiyavar,” meaning the Nayanar whose truth is well-versed in the rare five sacred letters, which are the names of Shiva.

This means that Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, even when tied to a stone in the middle of the sea, or when thrown into the sea with a stone, was saved by the truth of chanting “Namasivaya.” He is the one who used the Namasivaya mantra as a weapon, saying, “I have taken the five letters of Your name on my tongue as a weapon.” He composed the Thevaram Thiru-Pathikam called “Nappinai Thazhuviya Namasivaya Pathu.” Therefore, the sacred words of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. The sacred words of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman always speak of the sacred name of Shiva, which is his glory and nature.

Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman refers to him as “Arunaamathu Anjezhuthum Payil Vaimaiyavar” in this verse.

At the same time, in this verse, he refers to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman as “Deiva Vaimai” (divine truth).

Therefore, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman is the lord of Sirapuram with divine truth, while Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is one whose truth is practiced in the five sacred letters.

Thus, Sekkizhar Peruman praises these two great personalities in this verse through their truth.

Thus, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, who welcomed Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, asks Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, “Appare, you have come from Thiruvarur.

“Therefore, please tell us about the greatness that takes place in Thiruvarur.” When great devotees meet each other, What one asks of the other is the glory of Shiva. What one tells the other is the glory of Shiva.

“Therefore, it is understood here that when devotees meet, they spend their time discussing the divine grace of Lord Shiva and the greatness of the devotees.

“Similarly, in the Puranam of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, when he was in Madurai, also known as Thiru-Alavai, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman asked his father, Sivapada Hrudayar, who had come to see him, “Did the great one who took me in my ignorant age remain with the Goddess?” We can recall Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman’s act of inquiring about the well-being of the Lord of Sirkazhi here.

“Therefore, we, as Shiva devotees, when we meet our loved ones, instead of wasting time discussing perishable worldly matters and worldly affairs, It is beneficial to live a great life by discussing the attributes of God and the glories of God’s devotees. This is the message we receive here. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman has come here with the intention of worshipping Thiruppukalur from Thiruvarur.

“Therefore, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman asks Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar about the glories that take place in Aaroor. To this, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman says, “How can I describe the nature of the Thiruvathirai festival of Lord Thiruneelakandar, who rules the southern city of Thiruvarur?” and then composes the Thiru-Pathikam that begins with “Muthuvithanam Mani Porkavari.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman witnessed and experienced the Thiruvathirai festival in Thiruvarur and then came to Thiruppukalur.

“Therefore, he has now composed a separate Thiru-Pathikam specifically for the Thiruvathirai festival that takes place in Thiruvarur. He composes this Thiru-Pathikam at the request of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman says that even though he has come to Thiruppukalur, his mind is still absorbed in the Thiruvathirai day in Thiruvarur. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman asks, “When you come, please tell us about the greatness that took place in Thiruvarur.” Therefore, that greatness, the greatness that took place there, is the Thiruvathirai festival.

“So, he says, “How can I describe the glory of the Thiruvathirai festival? It is so glorious that it cannot be described.” Even though it is indescribable, he says, “Since you asked, I will tell you.” And thus, he begins the Thiru-Pathikam with “Muthuvithanam.” This Thiru-Pathikam is arranged as the twenty-first Thiru-Pathikam in the fourth Thiru-Murai. It is a Thiru-Pathikam set in the Kurinji Pann.

““Muthuvithanam Mani Porkavari Muraiyaalai Bhakthargalodu Paavaiyar Soozha Balippinne Vithagakkola Vendalai Maalai Virathigal Atthan Aaroor Aathirai Naalaal Athu Vannam Naniyar Seyar Nallar Theeyar Naadorum Pinithaan Theerum Endru Pizhangik Kidappaarum Maniye Ponne Maintha Manaala Enbarkku Aniyan Aaroor Aathirai Naalaal Athu Vannam Veethigal Thoroom Venkodiyodu Vithanangal Sothigal Vittu Sudar Ma Manigal Oli Thondra Sathigalay Paval.” Thiru-Aroor’s Thiru-Adhirai festival is a wondrous sight. Devotees, like madmen, speak of its qualities, gather, sing, and argue among themselves. The celestials, bowing, come daily. Thiru-Aroor’s Thiru-Adhirai festival is a wondrous sight.

“With the sound of white conches and drums, many cannot stand still. The bells tied to their feet fly everywhere, and thinking it to be the sound of thunder, peacocks dance. Thiru-Aroor’s Thiru-Adhirai festival is a wondrous sight. They sigh, tremble, their eyes do not clear, they are bewildered. They are not aware of their own selves, they hit their heads. They say, “Our Lord, our Master, our Father.” Thiru-Aroor’s Thiru-Adhirai festival is a wondrous sight.

“Maidens with red lips contemplate the Lord’s sacred feet. Men and women gather and become ecstatic. Indra and other celestials. The Siddhas praise Thiru-Aroor’s Thiru-Adhirai festival, a wondrous sight. With bowed heads, the ageless ones walk in front. Behind them, maidens with beautiful bamboo-like shoulders walk, filling the sky.

“Devotees, smeared with sacred ash, sing and surround the Lord. Thiru-Aroor’s Thiru-Adhirai festival is a wondrous sight. Some say, “Days without worshipping the subtle truth are days of sorrow.” Others say, “Days of praising the subtle truth are days of joy.” Still others say, “Allow us to enter your subtle presence.” Thiru-Aroor’s Thiru-Adhirai festival, a wondrous sight, is for the beloved.

“The devotees worship the Lord of the earth and the ocean, praising him. The songs and dances of glory never cease, filling them with pride. Without exception, the whole world praises Thiru-Aroor’s Thiru-Adhirai festival.

“Let us continue to contemplate Thiruchitrambalam.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 410. Thiru-Nindra Charukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman bestows a Pathigam (hymn) about the glory of the Thiru-Adhirai festival that takes place in Thiru-Aroor. He bestows this Thiru-Pathigam for Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman to hear.

Among the Thevara Thiru-Pathigams, only the Thiru-Aroor Thiru-Adhirai festival has a unique Thiru-Pathigam dedicated solely to a festival. This Thiru-Pathigam is so special. On Thiru-Adhirai in Thiru-Aroor, Thiyagaraja Peruman bestows the darshan of his left foot. For ten days in the month of Margazhi, Manikkavasagar Swamigal, seated in the Rajanarayana Mandapam, offers Thiru-Vembavai in the shrines of Araneriyaar, Neelothpalambal, and Vanmeeganathar. For Arudra Darshanam, with the Ajapa dance, he proceeds to the Rajanarayana Mandapam.

There, for Kamala Vasantha Thiyagaraja Peruman, a Musukunda Sahasranama Archana is performed. At midnight, Thiyagaraja Peruman receives a Maha Abhishekam. From early morning, he bestows the darshan of his sacred feet. Patanjali Munivar and Vyagrapada Munivar come to Thiru-Aroor from Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, near Thiru-Aroor, to witness the darshan of the sacred feet.

Therefore, on Thiru-Adhirai in Margazhi, for that one day, we can see the darshan of Thiyagaraja Peruman’s left foot throughout the day. In this Thiru-Pathigam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman highlights the glory of Thiru-Aroor Peruman’s Thiru-Adhirai festival, the manner in which devotees worship the Lord there, and other such glories. The glory of the Lord’s festival and this Thiru-Pathigam has the unique distinction of clearly describing its special qualities. Not only that, but this Thiru-Pathigam was also bestowed by one Acharya of the Saiva Samayam (Shaivite tradition) when another Acharya requested it. Upon hearing this Thiru-Pathigam, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman’s desire to have darshan of the Lord of Thiru-Aroor intensified, and he proceeded to Thiru-Aroor. Even if he could not witness the festival, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman wished to see Thiyagaraja Peruman.

Such is its greatness. “The great benefit of being born on earth is to feed the devotees of the Lord who wears the crescent moon, and to behold the splendor of their good festival with one’s eyes,” thus Thiru-Gnana- Sambandha Peruman’s Puranam states that the purpose of souls being born on this earth is to witness the splendor of the festivals held in Shiva Peruman’s temples and to feed the devotees. Sekkizhar Peruman says that these are the two greatest benefits that souls born into this world to experience karma receive. In this entire Thiru-Adhirai Thiru-Pathigam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman highlights one of these two great benefits: “beholding the splendor of His Lord’s good festival and finding solace.” We have seen the ten verses of this Thiru-Pathigam.

Now let us look at their brief meaning. Behind the offerings carried for our Lord during the festival, devout men and women and great ascetics follow in an orderly manner. Thiyagaraja Peruman, the Lord of Thiru-Aroor, presents a beautiful sight on the day of Thiru-Adhirai.

At that time, the Lord is seated under a canopy adorned with pearls, and he is fanned with golden-handled whisks. When such a Thiru-Adhirai festival takes place, Shiva devotees come from far and wide to witness it.

Therefore, even from a distance, all Shiva devotees come to be very close to Thiru-Aroor, very close to the Lord. Even those who are in Thiru-Aroor but do not witness this festival are considered to be very far away.

Thus, various devotees come and worship Thiru-Aroor Thiyagaraja Peruman. They worship, calling out, “O Lord!” They cry out, wail, weep, dance, and sing.

The devotees act in this manner upon seeing the Lord of Aroor seated in his sacred form on Thiru-Adhirai day. In the minds of these devotees, the sacred form of Thiru-Aroor Thiyagaraja Peruman on Thiru-Adhirai always remains a steadfast image. In the streets of Thiru-Aroor, white flags are hoisted, canopies are erected, and garlands of corals and pearls adorn the place. The great beauty of Arooran’s Thiru-Adhirai festival, for he is the first among all things, is always remembered by his devotees. Thiru-Aroor Devas come daily to worship Thiyagaraja Peruman and have his darshan. All the Shiva devotees who have come to witness the Thiru-Aroor Thiru-Adhirai festival speak of the many qualities, heroic deeds, and divine sports of the Lord, the divine leader.

They all gather together, sing his praises, and, competing with each other in serving the Lord, they roam about like madmen in the streets of Thiru-Aroor. They blow white conches, like the moon, and sound drums.

The devotees perform ecstatic dances.

Therefore, the sounds of the anklets and other ornaments tied to their feet are always heard. These sounds are louder than the sound of the clouds.

Therefore, thinking it to be the sound of thunder from the clouds, male peacocks spread their tails and beautifully dance, swirling around. Such is the glory of the Thiru-Aroor Thiru-Adhirai festival. All the devotees remember the Lord and sigh. They speak with trembling lips and wide eyes. They sing the praises of the Lord with full voice. Who are these devotees?

They are those who do not claim any good deeds or virtues for themselves, but believe that everything is the Lord’s doing. They joyfully hit their heads, proclaiming, “Our Lord, our ruler, our master!” Thus, they stand as devotees who praise Thiyagaraja Peruman. In this Thiru-Adhirai festival of Thiru-Aroor Peruman, men and women gather and contemplate the sacred feet of Shiva Peruman. The Devas bow their heads and go first, and behind these Devas, the women of the celestial world follow. In front of them, devotees smeared with sacred ash stand surrounding on all four sides, and our Lord bestows his sacred vision at the Thiru-Adhirai festival in Thiru-Aroor. At such a festival, all the devotees make a request to the Lord of Thiru-Aroor.

“O Lord, at the Thiru-Adhirai festival, we are your servants. The days we do not worship you are days of sorrow for us. The days we worship you are days of joy for us.

“Therefore, engage us in the service of your sacred feet, so that we, your servants, may always come before you.” This scene of making a request to the Lord is seen there. Like an ocean, devotees gather together, worship, and praise. Songs praising the Lord’s glory are always heard. All those from the surrounding villages come and extol the praises of our Lord. Such is the great beauty, glory, and special nature of Aroor Peruman’s Thiru-Adhirai festival. That day is a sacred day that will forever remain in the hearts of devotees.

“Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sang the Thiru-Adhirai Thiru-Pathigam with this meaning. Hearing it, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, even though he did not get the opportunity to witness this festival, had a great desire to have darshan of the Lord of Thiru-Aroor. He set out for Thiru-Aroor from Thiru-Pugalur. Before Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman departed for Thiru-Aroor, he said to Appar Swamigal, “I will go to Southern Thiru-Aroor, worship, and then return here to Thiru-Pugalur to join you. Until then, please remain here.” Having said this, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman proceeds towards Thiru-Aroor from the border of Thiru-Pugalur.

“As soon as Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman goes to Thiru-Aroor, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who was at the border of Thiru-Pugalur, enters Thiru-Pugalur. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is to attain the sacred feet of the Lord in Thiru-Pugalur at the end of this birth, and here he will become a form of Shiva-Ananda Gnana (blissful knowledge of Shiva) in the shade of the Lord’s sacred feet. Remembering this, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman now enters Thiru-Pugalur at this time, as if to enter that state. His heart is filled with overflowing love for the Lord, and that flood, unable to be contained, flows as tears from his eyes, like a stream. “Is there a bolt to contain love? The tears of the ardent will proclaim it,” says the Thirukkural.

“Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman has darshan of the Lord of Lords, the leader of all Devas, who is like honey, residing in the beautiful Pugalur. He sings Thevara Pathigams, which are garlands of pure Tamil. From Thiru-Palli Ezhuchi (waking up the Lord) to Ardha Jamam (midnight worship), he worships without fail at every time of puja. Those who are deeply immersed in the love of the Lord worship the Lord at all these times. In temples, at other times, they perform other services necessary for the Lord. Appar Swamigal has bestowed five Thiru-Pathigams for the Thiru-Pugalur shrine.

“Among them, the Thiru-Pathigam beginning with “Pagaithittar” Purangal” and the Thiru-Pathigam beginning with “Seyya Vennoolar” are the two Thiru-Pathigams that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman bestowed at this time, as mentioned by Sivakavimani Ayya. The sacred name of the Lord of Thiru-Pugalur is Agneeswarar, Saranyapureeswarar, Konappiran. The sacred name of the Goddess is Karuntharkuzhali, Choolikambal. The Sthala Viruksham (sacred tree) is the Punnai tree. The Theertham (sacred water) is Agni Theertham, Bana Theertham.

“We have extensively discussed the glories and special features of this Thiru-Pugalur shrine in the Thiru-Puranam of Muruga Nayanar.

“Therefore, at this time, let us contemplate the two Thiru-Pathigams bestowed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. The first Thiru-Pathigam is the 54th Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Nerisaith Thiru-Pathigam.

““Pagaithittar The Lord of the Devas, who burned the three cities of the enemies into ashes, I am without senses, trapped in this body, and the five senses torment me daily. I am bewildered, what can I do, O Lord of Thiru-Pugalur? Caught in the net of maidens with dark, beautiful eyes, I cannot remember the Lord who holds the trident. When the soul is trapped in the throat, I know not what to do, O Lord of Thiru-Pugalur? This body, a hut of thirty-six elements, and the five senses come like a father and demand, ‘Give it, leave it.’ When they torment me thus, I know not how to survive, O Lord of Thiru-Pugalur, whose body shines with righteousness?

“Cherishing this body, which is without senses and full of impurities, thinking falsehood to be truth, I went on paths that were not righteous. I am a wretch, without any knowledge of justice, O Lord of the celestials, who places nectar on the sand. I am without steadfastness, what can I do, O Lord of Thiru-Pugalur? To those women with flowing hair, I became devoted. I am without clarity, my heart is without virtue, never remembering the Lord of Veerattam, whose songs are endless, whose feet are adorned. What can I do, O Lord of Thiru-Pugalur?

“With young women, I lived in harmony, thinking many days would pass. I am a wretch, I did not contemplate you, the primordial one, nor did I praise your feet with knowledge. I am without means, what can I do, O Lord of Thiru-Pugalur? I did not protect the two and three, nor did I have education. I was not truthful in my service, nor was I pure. O Supreme Being, who bestowed grace upon Arjuna, O Lord of Thiru-Pugalur, where sacred ponds shine, what can I do?

“Becoming water and fire, earth and sky, and the glorious rays, the celestials worship you, who are difficult to comprehend, and dance everywhere. You are the God of Gods, O Lord of Thiru- Pugalur. Lighting a lamp within my body, and raising it as high as desired, I seek a way to salvation, but you have placed the five senses within me, and they are very powerful. I know not what to do, O Lord of Thiru-Pugalur? He who bore the six, and he who is the origin of the Vedas, neither of them could know the Lord. When the king of Lanka, Ravana, tried to lift Mount Kailash, blood flowed from his eyes, and the Lord pressed him with his sacred toe.

“O Lord of Thiru-Pugalur.

“Now, the second Thiru-Pathigam bestowed upon Thiru-Pugalur, the sixteenth Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai, composed in Indalappann.

““Seyyar Vennoolar Karumaan Marithollum Kaiyar Kanaikazhal Kattiy Kaalinar Meyyar Meynindravarkku Allathavarkkendrum Poyyar Pugalur Porisadaiyare Meganal Oorthiyar Minpol Milirsadai Paagamathinuthalaalai” One part of the moon-browed lady, with a shining matted lock like lightning, riding a good cloud, wearing snake bracelets and snake garments, a renunciate, is the Lord of Pugalur with matted locks. He wears the crescent moon on his great matted hair, and with the dark-haired lady, he is united. He is never associated with those of impure minds, the Lord of Pugalur with matted locks. He wears a garland of beads on his chest, and snakes.

“He is naked, wearing the young crescent moon. Daily, he takes skulls and eats the offerings. He enters Pugalur, the Lord with matted locks. He destroyed the life of Yama, the god of death, and tore his body. He covered himself with the hide of the fierce elephant that attacked the beautiful lady with the crescent moon on her forehead. He is the Lord of Pugalur with matted locks.

“He is the three-eyed one who burned Kama, who had a banner with a fish, with his fierce bow. He is the path of salvation, wearing sacred garments. He is the Lord of Pugalur with matted locks. He kicked Yama, the god of death, with his foot, and destroyed the sacrifice performed by the shining Daksha. He covered the eye of the fierce sun with his hand and head. He is the Lord of Pugalur with matted locks.

“He is the one with burnt heads, who burned the three strong cities with his arrows, and whose matted locks spread out with the flowing Ganga. He is the Lord of Pugalur with matted locks. When the two, Brahma and Vishnu, could not find his beginning or end, he stood as a pillar of fire. He wore the bones of the dead and a garland of Konrai flowers. He is the Lord of Pugalur with matted locks. He has a dark throat, and he pressed his toe down, severing the ten heads of the king of Lanka.

“He controlled the five senses and bore the part of the beautiful lady. He is the Lord of Pugalur with matted locks.

“Let us continue to contemplate Thiruchitrambalam.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 411. Thiru-Nindra Charukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having worshipped the Lord in Thiru-Pugalur, visits the nearby shrines of Thiru-Sengattangudi, Thiru-Nallaru, Thiru-Saathamangai, and Thiru-Marugal.

There, he sings Thevara Thiru-Pathigams. Sekkizhar Peruman states this: “He went with abundant love and rejoiced, worshipping Thiru-Sengattangudi, which bestows glory, Thiru-Nallaru, which has many groves, Thiru-Saathai Ayavanthi, and Thiru-Marugal, where the Lord has a part of the soft-breasted lady.” Here, Sekkizhar Peruman uses the epithet “Seertharu Sengattangudi” for the shrine of Thiru-Sengattangudi. “Seertharu” means that Thiru-Sengattangudi bestows glory upon all who come and seek refuge there.

Here, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman has sung, indicating that the great glory of Siruthonda Nayanar is about to be revealed. The Thevara reference sung by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman for that shrine is, “He resided as a strong city to bestow grace upon Siruthondar.” The shrine of Thiru-Sengattangudi is located in the Thanjavur region, near Nannilam, on the Thiru-Aroor-Mayuram route. Nearby are the shrines of Thiru-Pugalur and Thiru-Kannapuram. This shrine has been sung about in Thevaram by both Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar. Thiru-Sengattangudi is the name of this village. The name of the temple here is Ganapatheeswaram.

It is the place where Ganapati worshipped Shiva Peruman, hence the temple is named Ganapatheeswaram. The Sthala Vinayagar (presiding Ganesha) here is Vaathapi Ganapati. The Moolavar (main deity) is Sri Ganapatheeswarar, also known as Sri Uttarapatheeswarar. The sacred name of the Goddess is Vaithathirukkuzhali, Choolikambal. The Theerthams (sacred waters) include Sathya Theertham and Surya Theertham. The sacred tree is the Aathi tree.

This shrine is the seventy-ninth among the Thevaram-sung shrines located on the south bank of the Kaveri River. To the north of this shrine flows the Mudikondan River, and to the south, the Puthaaru River. When Vinayagar killed Gajamukhasura, the demon’s blood flowed, turning the forest red. As it appeared as a red forest, this Thiru-sthalam is named Thiru-sengattangudi, as we have already seen. Since Ganapathi worshipped Lord Shiva in this Thiru-sthalam, this Thiru-koil is named Ganapatheeswaram. This Thiru-sthalam has various sacred names such as Manthirapuri, Senkadu, Sathyapuri, Brahmapuri, Aathivanam, Bhaskarapuri, Samudrapuri, Indrapuri, etc.

Since Lord Shiva bestowed the seven crore great mantras upon the Devas and Munis in this Thiru-sthalam, it is called Manthirapuri. When Sage Sathyasada performed penance for Lord Shiva, and Lord Shiva slew the Asuras Rathanamukhi and Rathabeejan who sought to destroy his penance, their blood stained the earth, giving this Thiru-sthalam the name Senkadu. Since Sage Sathyasada worshipped and performed pooja here, this Thiru-sthalam is called Sathyapuri. And since Brahma worshipped here, it is called Brahmapuri. Because the Thazhambu flower lied for Brahma, who went in the form of a swan searching for Lord Shiva’s sacred crown, and to atone for that sin, the Thazhambu sprouted as an Aathi tree and performed penance here, this Thiru-sthalam is also known as Aathivanam. Since the Sun worshipped and performed pooja during the Maha Shivaratri period, it is called Bhaskarapuri.

Since Samudrarajan installed a Shiva Lingam and worshipped here, it is called Samudrapuri. And since Indra worshipped here, it is called Indrapuri. Surrounding this Thiru-sthalam are other Thiru-sthalams such as Thiru-marugal, Thiru-ramanatheeswaram, Thiru-kannapuram, and Thiru-pugaloor. The temple faces east. Groves and ponds surround the temple. In front of the temple, there is a five-tiered gopuram.

Processions take place through the gate next to it. To the south, there is a gate, and to the west, a gopuram. Beyond the gopuram, there is a kitchen and a yagasalai (sacrificial hall). In the front mandapam, there is Nandi and a flagstaff. Nearby, there is an ornamental mandapam and a south-facing Amman temple. Close by, Samudra Rajalingam stands as a separate shrine.

On both sides, there are standing forms of Dvarapalakas. Beyond the inner gate, in the prakaram (circumambulatory path), on the eastern side, there are sacred forms of Siruthondar, Thiru-venkattu Nangai, Seeralan, Santhana Nangai, Bhairavar, and Suryan. To the south, there are sacred forms of the Sixty-Three Nayanmars, Brahma, Ardhanareeswarar, the Four Saints, Sanghanidhi, Padumanidhi, etc. To the west, there are shrines for Vaathapi Ganapathi, Sambandhar, Sathyasada Lingam, Murugan, Lakshmi, etc. To the north, there are the Vasantha Mandapam, Kalanjiyam (storehouse), Navathandava Mandapam, Vahana Mandapam, etc., and Nataraja Rajar and the Navagrahas are also installed. In the inner mandapam, there is an Aathi tree.

The Moolavar (presiding deity) shrine and the Uttharapatheeswarar shrine face east. Next to Uttharapathiyar, a Maragatha Lingam is housed in a silver casket. Inside the temple, there are two prakarams and an outer street, making a total of three prakarams. Outside the temple, there are the Sathya Pushkarani and the Vendum Vinayagar temple. In the southwest, there are the Surya Pushkarani and the Siruthondar temple. Above the entrance of the Siruthondar temple, there are sacred images of Uttharapathiyar, Siruthondar, and others.

Inside, Uttharapathiyar bestows grace in a seated posture. Thiru-venkattu Nangai appears with a bowl and ladle, in the act of serving food. On the other side, the sacred image of Aiyadigal Kadavar Kon is installed. In the western street, there is a cow shed, and in the Agni corner, a Nandavanam (flower garden). Just as Vinayagar destroyed Gajamukhasura with his single tusk, he now appears holding a single tusk in his hand. The Vinayagar of this Thiru-sthalam is called Vendum Vinayagar.

This name came about because Siruthondar made a request. Another Vinayagar, Vaathapi Ganapathi, was brought from the city of Vaathapi. The Moolavar is known by the name Ganapatheeswarar. This name is bestowed upon the Lord here because he was installed by Ganapathi. In inscriptions, the Lord’s sacred names are also given as Ganapatheeswaramudaiya Nayanar, Ganapatheeswaramudaiya Mahadevar, Parameswaramudaiya Mahadevar, Ganapatheeswaramudaiyar, Thiru-valangadudaiya Nayanar, Seeraladevar, etc.

The Lord who came in the guise of Bhairava is called Peruman is called Uttharapatheeswarar. This name arose because he came from Uttharapathi in the northern country. The sacred name of the Goddess here is Vaitha Thiru-kuzhali Nangai. In Sanskrit, it is Sulikambal. In Thiru-ambar, the Goddess’s name is Vamba Vanakkuzhali, in Thiru-pugaloor, Karunthar Kuzhali, in Ramanatheeswaram, Sariyarkuzhali, and in Thiru-marugal, Vandarkuzhali. It is truly astonishing that the names of the Goddess are consistently similar in all the nearby Thiru-sthalams.

The wild Aathi tree is the Sthala Vriksham (sacred tree) here. It is directly opposite the Uttharapatheeswarar shrine. The trunk of this tree is very low and has grown in such a way that it does not obstruct the Lord’s shrine.

Now, let us consider this Thiru-sthalam’s Thirthams.

First, the Sathya Thirtham. It is also called Soola Thirtham because Lord Shiva created it by piercing the earth with his trident. It is located in the Agni corner of the temple. Next is the Surya Thirtham, named after the Sun. It is in the southwest of the temple. Bathing in it and worshipping on Sundays in the month of Karthigai will cure all diseases.

Besides these, there is the Indra Thirtham in the east, Yama Thirtham in the south, Agni Thirtham in the southeast, Varuna Thirtham in the west, Vayu Thirtham in the northwest, and Chandra Pushkarani Thirtham. In Thiru-marugal, behind the place where Seeralan received education, there is a Thirtham called Seeralan Kulam. Those who bathe in this Thirtham on special days like Chithirai Bharani and worship the Lord will be freed from sins and attain merit and all siddhis. This Thiru-sthalam is a very ancient Thiru-sthalam, distinguished by its Moorthy (deity), Sthalam (place), and Thirtham (sacred water). The Moola Lingam is situated very deep. This sacred Thiru-sthalam is where Lord Shiva, along with the Goddess and Lord Muruga, appeared and bestowed grace upon Siruthondar, who offered his own sacred son to the Lord’s devotee.

We will see the sacred history of Siruthondar Nayanar in his Thiru-puranam. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman has enshrined and sung the greatness of Siruthondar in his Pathigam. This sacred temple is the Thiru-sthalam where Uttharapathiyar, who appeared as Bhairava from the north of Siruthondar’s house, is enshrined. In this sacred temple, the deities are arranged in the forms of Guru, Lingam, and Sangamam. Sri Dakshinamurthy bestows grace here as the Guru form, the Moolavar as the Lingam, and Uttharapathiyar as the Jangamam. True to the name of this Thiru-sthalam, there are many Ganapathi images in the town and the sacred temple.

This is the Thiru-sthalam where Uttharapathiyar, having asked for food on Aippasi Bharani day, set out to receive food on Chithirai Bharani day and gave darshan. It is said that in this sacred Thiru-sthalam, Aiyadigal Kadavar Kon first, and then Kulothunga Chola, carried out temple renovations. Very beautifully carved sculptures are found in this sacred temple. In the Navathandava Mandapam of this sacred temple, the forms of the nine Thandava Moorthies, namely Bhujangalalithar, Gajasamharar, Oorthuva Thandavar, Kalasamharar, Kangalar, Tharukavana Bhikshadanar, Thripura Samaharar, and Bhairavar, who are the Moolavar Uttharapathiyar, are very beautifully arranged. Uttharapathiyar, the Peruman, is the principal deity here. The sacred form of Lord Shiva, who came in the guise of Bhairava to bestow grace upon Siruthondar, is the Uttharapathiyar Thiru-kolam.

The appearance of Uttharapatheeswarar is one that captivates and enraptures those who behold it. With a Damarukam in his right hand, a Kapalam (skull) in his left hand, a three-pronged trident on his shoulder, a benevolent smile on his face, his waist bent, and both feet planted on the earth, he bestows grace in the form of a Samapada dance. This is the sacred form of Uttharapatheeswarar. In this sacred form, the five cosmic functions (Panchakrithyam) are included. Creation is represented by the Damarukam (drum), destruction by the slaying of Seeralan, preservation by bringing him back to life, concealment by his disappearance from Siruthondar and others, and finally, bestowing grace upon them. These are all contained within the sacred form of Uttharapatheeswarar.

The procession of Uttharapathiyar takes place three times a year. In this sacred temple, daily rituals (kala pooja) are regularly performed. Milk offerings are made daily to Uttharapatheeswarar.

At that time, the Suddha Mathalam and Chinnam are played. Ten ablutions are performed for Uttharapathiyar in a year. These take place on days such as Aippasi Bharani, Chithirai Bharani, the beginning of the month of Chithirai, the beginning of the month of Aadi, the beginning of the month of Aippasi, and the beginning of the month of Thai. On Thiru-vonam day, a darshan is granted to Aiyadigal Kadavarkon. On every Bharani star day of each month, ablutions and Kulithaligai Aradhanas are performed for Vidangar. On Fridays, the Goddess’s procession takes place, and on Karthigai days, ablutions and processions are held for Lord Muruga.

Annually, in the month of Chithirai, the Brahmotsavam takes place. The festival begins with flag hoisting on Sathayam day and continues for ten days. On the second day, there is a flower palanquin procession; on the third day, a Bhutha Vahanam (demon vehicle); on the fourth day, an elephant vehicle; on the fifth day, the deities are seated on a Rishabha Vahanam (bull vehicle) and give darshan. On the sixth day, Bharani, the Bhikshadana Utsavam (begging festival) and Amudhu Padaiyal Vizha (food offering festival) take place.

At that time, in the morning, Uttharapatheeswarar sets out from Kailash, the northern abode, adorned with a Kanjukam (garment), Soolam (trident), Kapalam (skull), Damarukam (drum), Pokkanam (bag), Manikka Kanthai (jeweled cloth), Vattavar Sadai (circular matted locks), and wearing white, he proceeds.

At that time, Nattumuttu Silambu musical instruments are played. In the daytime, Uttharapathiyar proceeds to Siruthondar’s house to ask for sacred food, and then sits under the sacred Aathi tree. At night, he again proceeds to Siruthondar’s sacred house to partake of the sacred food.

At that time, Uttharapathiyar disappears and then, mounted on a Rishabha Vahanam, bestows grace upon Siruthondar and others, and takes them with him to the world of liberation. This festival is the main festival celebrated in Thiru-sengattangudi.

Then, on the seventh day, the Lord gives darshan seated in a Pushpa Vimanam (flower chariot), and on the eighth day, on a horse vehicle. On the ninth day, there is a chariot procession (Therottam), and on the tenth day, Theerthavari (sacred bath). On the eleventh day, the Chandikeswarar festival takes place, and on the following day, the Vidayathi Utsavam. On Thiru-vonam night, the Shanbhaga festival, where darshan is given to Kadavar Maharaja, takes place. In Aani, there are ablutions for Nataraja; in Aadi, the Poora festival; in Aavani Moolam, the Pittu festival; in Purattasi, the Navaratri festival; and on Vijayadasami, the Ambu Poduthal (arrow-shooting) ceremony. On Aippasi Bharani day, Uttharapathiyar proceeds and gives darshan.

On Karthigai Sundays, Chandrasekarar’s procession and on Somavarams, Deepam (lamps), and on Karthigai day, a Sudalai (funeral pyre) made of palm leaves are observed. In the month of Margazhi, on the day of Poorvapaksham Sathayam and Sashti, the festival where Ganapathi worships Lord Shiva takes place.

Furthermore, in the month of Margazhi, Dhanur Pooja and Maha Vyathipatha Aradhana, and on Thiru-vathirai day, ablutions and processions for Nataraja take place. In the month of Thai, on Thai Pongal day, Somaskandar’s procession, and on Maattu Pongal day, Subramaniyar’s procession on a horse vehicle and the Vedupari Utsavam take place. In the month of Maasi, on Shivaratri day, ablutions and aradhanas are performed during all four periods of the night. On Panguni Bharani day, ablutions and worship take place. “The great benefit of being born on earth is to feed the devotees of the Lord who wears the moon, and to find solace by seeing the splendor of their good festivals with one’s eyes.” This is a sacred verse from the Periya Puranam. According to that, all those born as humans must witness and benefit from the festivals held in Thiru-sengattangudi.

Feeding the devotees who come there is also a great Shiva-punyam (meritorious act). There is a Sthala Puranam (local legend) that elaborately describes the glories of this Thiru-sthalam. It contains one thousand and fifty-four verses in twenty-two sections, from the introduction to the Abhisheka Sarukkam.

However, the author of this work is unknown. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, having set out from Thiru-pugaloor, came to this sacred Thiru-sthalam of Thiru-sengattangudi, bowed and worshipped the Lord, and composed a Thiru-thandagam. It is found as the eighty-fourth Thiru-pathigam in the sixth Thiru-murai.

The great one, the rare ruby, who resides in the hearts of those who remember and praise him, the radiant lamp, who was seated on the lotus flower, the Lord who performs the great dance with eight arms, the golden mountain of light, who, under the banyan tree, bestowed the meaning of the sacred Vedas upon the four sages, him I saw in Thiru-sengattangudi. Not by sharp claws alone, nor by the destruction of the mighty Hiranyan, but by the golden Lord Vishnu and Brahma, who searched for the six-fold fire, and by the medicine that caused Ananga’s body to turn to dust, by the golden mountain of Kailash, by the Lord who stands firm, by the golden-bodied one, my Lord, him I saw in Thiru-sengattangudi. The honey that flows for the devotees with melting hearts, the jewel on the crown of the celestials, the knowledge of those who stand firm in truth, the meaning of the Vedas for the devoted Brahmins, and furthermore, the support of the true ascetics, the source of all, for those who wander among fragrant flowers, the Lord who shares a part with Thiru-kuzhal Uma Nangai, him I saw in Thiru-sengattangudi. The one with matted locks adorned with fragrant Kondrai flowers, the radiant jewel, the golden light, the one who shares a part with the beautiful flower-like maiden, the mother of all moving and unmoving beings, who freed me, a dog, from bondage and made me his servant, and then made me sing Tamil garlands of well-composed verses, the one whose sacred grace removed the confusion from my mind, him I saw in Thiru-sengattangudi.

The Lord with the poisoned throat, the one with an eye that blazed with fierce fire to destroy the flower-arrowed god of love, the one who resides in Thiru-venkedil Veeratttam, the Lord who dwells in Thiru-varoor, with its tall mansions and streets shaded by dense groves, the one with the fierce trident weapon, him I saw in Thiru-sengattangudi. The one who concealed the Ganga in one of his matted locks, the one who dwells in Thiru-kadavoor Veeratttam, our pure Lord of Thiru-aiyaru surrounded by the Ponni river, the one who resides in Thiru-poonduruthi and Neydhanam, the one whose nature is to expound the well-composed four Vedas, the one whom the Devas lovingly worship and praise as the Supreme Lord, the one whose sacred feet are adorned with the crown of their heads, him I saw in Thiru-sengattangudi.

The Lord who stands in all directions, the one who resides in Ekambam, the one who saved me from falling into the false path of the Samanars who pluck their hair and worship non-existent deities, by showing me the path of devotion and removing my sins, and by removing all the effects of past karma, the honey that flows sweetly in the mind, him I saw in Thiru-sengattangudi. The God who does not approach the minds of the unlearned, the beloved of the learned and the close ones, the one who shot the fierce arrow that day to make the three cities of those who followed evil paths fall and perish, the one who, to remove the entanglement of this impermanent body of flesh, bestowed upon me, his servant, abundant penance, and who leads me to the eternal good path, him I saw in Thiru-sengattangudi. The one who stands as the knowable truth, the one with the dark throat who consumed the poison from the churning ocean, the one with the red eye, the radiant jewel, the one who appears as a great light, the one who bestows all the worlds upon his devotees who perform various rightful deeds, the one who has taken a maiden as a part of himself, him I saw in Thiru-sengattangudi. The one who rides a great bull, the one who is the Lord of the one who is the Lord of Purambayam and Pugaloor, the one who kept the cool crescent moon on his red matted locks, the pure one, the one with the victorious anklet that crushed the heads of the Rakshasas who wore large serpents as ornaments, my Lord, him I saw in Thiru-sengattangudi.

Thus, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, having worshipped Thiru-sengattangudi, proceeds to the Thiru-sthalam of Thiru-nallar. We shall continue our reflection on this. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 412. Thiru-nindracharukkam. Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Sekkizhar Peruman sings that Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman reaches Thiru-needu Nallaru. The epithet given by Sekkizhar Peruman to the Thiru-sthalam of Thiru-nallar is Thiru-needu Nallaru.

Its meaning is that Thiru-nallar is a sacred place that remains eternally in the minds of devotees. In the Thiru-sthalam of Thiru-nallar, the sacred name of the Lord is Dharbaranyeswarar, Thiru-nallatru Eesar. The sacred name of the Goddess is Pranaambikai, Bhogamartha Poonmulaiyal. The Sthala Vriksham (sacred tree) is Dharbai grass and the Vilva tree. The Thirthams are Nala Thirtham and Sivaganga Thirtham. This is a Thiru-sthalam where the three great saints, Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, Thiru-navukkarasu Swamigal, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, received Thevaram hymns.
