Thiru-nallar is also a Thiru-sthalam praised by Nambiandar Nambi and Sekkizhar Peruman. This is a Thiru-sthalam worshipped by Thiru-mal, Brahma, Indra, Agasthiyar, Pulastiyar, Arjuna, Nala Chakravarti, the Dikpalakas, the Vasus, Bhojan, and Muchukunda Chakravarti. Since Nalan worshipped in this sacred temple, it is called Nallaru. By the grace of the Lord, Nalan was freed from the affliction of Saturn. During the Anarvatham (fire debate) conducted by Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman with the Samanars in Thiru-alavai (Madurai), when the Pathigam of this Thiru-sthalam, “Bhogamartha Poonmulaiyal,” was placed in the fire, it did not burn but remained fresh and green. It became known as the “Green Pathigam” and established Saivism.

For this Thiru-sthalam, Thiru-gnana Sambandha Peruman composed four Thiru-pathigams, Appar Swamigal composed two Thiru-pathigams, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal composed one Thiru-pathigam. This is one of the Saptha Vidanga Sthalams established by Muchukunda Chakravarti. The Thiyagaraja Peruman here is called Nagavidangar. This Thiru-sthalam is special because people come here to worship Lord Shiva to alleviate the ill effects of Saturn, as the Lord here performs Unmatha Natanam (frenzied dance). After worshipping Lord Shiva here, one must proceed to the shrine where Saturn is located. This temple is under the administration of the Dharumai Adheenam.

This Thiru-nallar Thiru-sthalam is located near Karaikal in the Union Territory of Puducherry. It is the fifty-second Thiru-sthalam among the sacred places on the southern bank of the Kaveri River. Adhipuri, Dharbaranyam, Vidangapuram, Naleswaram—these four sacred names have been given to this Thiru-sthalam in the four Yugas. This sacred Thiru-sthalam is where a Brahmin was freed from the sin of cow slaughter and a Kalinga king was freed from the curse of a Brahmin.

The Lord is Dharbaranyeswarar, and therefore, there are marks resembling Dharbai grass sprouts on the Lord’s sacred form. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, who came and worshipped this sacred Thiru-sthalam, composed two Thiru-pathigams for this Thiru-sthalam. The first of these Thiru-pathigams is the sixty-eighth Thiru-pathigam in the fifth Thiru-murai, a Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathigam.

Ullarathathore pundarikath thiral thellaraa siva sothith thiralinai kallaratha porkondrai kamal sadai nallaraa ena nam vinai nasame. (The cluster of lotuses within, the clear cluster of Shiva’s light, the good serpent on the matted locks adorned with unplucked golden Kondrai flowers, thus our karma is destroyed.) He is the Lord of grace, the essence of the Vedas, the bridegroom clad in elephant hide. He is the good one whom Narayana approaches and praises, the God of causal knowledge and wisdom. He is the good one who, with a cloud-clad Meru, shot the three cities, causing sorrow and tears to flow. He is the good one who dances with a serpent, sharing a part with the great Vishnu and Brahma.

He is the holy one who holds the beautiful Ganga in his matted locks, adorned with a flourishing red serpent, and who rejoices greatly, seeing the strength of the good ones who crushed the crushing Yama. He is the one who fills the heart with coolness as a kinsman, who stands as the Lord, immeasurable. He is the good one of Thiru-Nallaru, surrounded by groves, the illusion of going after a boar as a hunter. He is the Lord of the red-hued, radiant light, the naked one. He is the good one who holds the discus, who granted the discus to the Mayas who seized the lives of the crooked. He is the one with a throat adorned with deceitful poison, the king of the goddess of wealth and knowledge.

He is the good one who does not give way to those with deceitful hearts, who shows grace to those with poisonous hearts. He is the radiant one who, when not, becomes a blooming flower, who is called a blacksmith, the one who is capable, and the wealthy. He is the good one to the good, standing well. He is the good one whom we worship and praise, whose feet are beyond measure, whom the supreme one reclining on a serpent and the ancient one shining on a lotus both worship. He is the good one who placed his finger on the great mountain, causing the twenty shoulders of the Lankan king to wither, the one adorned with sacred ash, whom we worship daily. All karmas will vanish.

This is the second Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for this sacred sthalam, the twentieth Thiru-Pathigam in the sixth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Thandaka Thiru-Pathigam.

He is the one who, when Brahma spoke an untruth from his face, cut off his head with his hand, and showed the good path to Shiva’s abode. He is the one who became one half with the beautiful Uma, the Lord whom Brahma on the lotus and Vishnu could not find. He is the trustworthy one, the good one, whom I, your servant, have come to think of and am relieved. He is the one with a host of weapons, the one in the guise of Pasupatha, the one who looked at the ancient Kama, the one who protects from all sins, the rare medicine for his devotees, the one who says ‘Ah, Ah’ and bestows grace. He is the one with matted locks, who wears the moon, the trustworthy one who rides the white bull with a bell.

He is the good one whom I, your servant, have come to think of and am relieved. He is the Supreme Being who tied a serpent around his waist, who resides in the beautiful parrot. He is the one who churned the ocean with a fierce serpent and consumed the poison as nectar, the primordial one. He is the one adorned with the beautiful Konrai flower, the great jewel, the one who made Yama, the lord of death, tremble. He is the good one whom I, your servant, have come to think of and am relieved. He is the one who holds a battle-axe in his hand, wears bracelets and earrings, smears himself with cremation ash, and is beautiful, holding a trident.

He is the one who wears a garland of skulls, who dances in the forest with his many ganas, the good one whom I, your servant, have come to think of and am relieved. He is the one who, with his body, roams the entire world in a moment, the God of gods who bestowed endless wealth upon the spider, the Shiva of Thiru-Chirappalli. He is the one who, with his mind, is always in love with the sky, the Ekambara of Kanchi, the trustworthy one adorned with fragrant Konrai flowers, the good one whom I, your servant, have come to think of and am saved. He is the one who can remove evil by giving a trident, the one who has the daughter of the mountain king on his left side. He is the Vedic scholar who removed impurities and bathed in the great sacred water, the one with the crescent moon in his red matted locks. He is the trustworthy one who removes obstacles and bestows good upon those who follow the path of the fundamental principle of compassion, the good one whom I, your servant, have come to think of and am saved.

He is the one with matted locks adorned with blooming Konrai flowers, our Lord of Purambayam, the one of Pukalur. He is the mighty one who flayed the elephant, the one who resides in Maraikkadu and Valivalam. He is the one who destroyed all the sacrifices of the shining Daksha, the one who took his head after kicking him. He is the one whose mouth utters the Vedas. He is the good one whom I, your servant, have come to think of and am saved. He is the one who is the word, the radiant coral light, the archer who burned the three cities of the ancient demons.

He is the one who is supreme over all, the one who shares his body with the gentle lady. He is the one who taught dharma under the shade of the Banyan tree, the one of Kalatthi, the good one residing in Kailash, the trustworthy one, the good one whom I, your servant, have come to think of and am saved. He is the one who, to remove the curse of the great sage, crushed Yama in the ocean. He is the one who, to burn the three cities of the demons, made the fish-mouthed arrow pierce. He is the one who grants whatever is desired, the trustworthy one who is always good to those who say ‘Shiva is our Lord,’ the good one whom I, your servant, have come to think of and am saved. I have reached the limit without begging.

Thus, he is the one who, by pressing down the twenty shoulders of the mighty Ravana, became his kinsman, listened to his sweet music, and then returned, capable of curing his illness. He is the one who always resides in the thoughts of those who do not forget him, the one with fragrant red matted locks adorned with the great moon, Konrai, and Datura, the good one whom I, your servant, have come to think of and am relieved.

These two Thiru-Pathigams were sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman in praise of the Lord of Thiru-Nallaru. After worshipping Thiru-Nallaru, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal reaches the sacred sthalam of Saththamangai. Saththamangai is the name of that village. The temple there is called Ayavanthi. This sthalam has several names such as Thiru-Saththamangai and Seeyaththamangai.

Here, the Lord’s name is Aya- Vanthi-Eswarar, Brahmapuriswarar. The name of the Goddess is Ubaya Pushpa Vilochanai, Irumalkann Ammai. The Sthala Vriksham is the Konrai tree. The Theertham is Arputha Theertham, Kaveri Theertham. A Theertham inside the temple, its upper half is called Chandra Theertham and its lower half is called Surya Theertham. There is a Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman for this sacred sthalam.

Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman has now come and worshipped this sacred sthalam, as Sekkizhar Peruman sings. When singing about Thiru-Neelanakka Nayanar in the Thiru-Thondar Thogai, he sang about this sacred sthalam as ‘Saththamangai surrounded by flowing water.’ This sacred sthalam is Thiru-Neela- Nakka Nayanar’s birthplace. The idols of Thiru-Neelanakka Nayanar and his wife are in this temple. The name of Thiru-Neelanakka Nayanar’s wife is commonly known as Mangaiyarkarasi here. Thiru-Neelanakka Nayanar attained liberation with Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman at Thiru-Aachchalpuram, also known as Nallur Perumanam, on Vaikasi Moolam. It is said that daily pujas are performed according to the Rudra Vyamala Tantra Agama method.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, after worshipping Thiru-Saththamangai, reaches the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Murugal. There, he sings a Thiru-Pathigam. In the sthalam of Thiru-Murugal, the Lord’s name is Manikka Vannar, Ratnagireeswarar. The name of the Goddess is Vandarkuzhali, Amodhalaka Nayaki. The Sthala Vriksham is a type of banana tree called Marugal. The Theerthams are Lakshmi Theertham and Manikka Theertham.

Thiru-Pathigams sung by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Appar Swamigal are available for this sacred sthalam. This is the sacred sthalam where the miracle performed by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman took place, where he heard the lament of a woman grieving for her lover who died from a snakebite, saw her sorrow, and brought the dead man back to life.

Afterwards, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman arranged their marriage.

Therefore, it is believed that by worshipping the Lord of this sthalam, delayed marriages will be successfully concluded by the grace of the Lord. It is believed that by reciting the Thiru-Pathigam sung by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, ‘Sadaiya Enumal,’ delayed marriages will be successfully concluded. This temple is one of the Maadakkoils built by Kochengat Chola Nayanar. It is one of the Maadakkoils built by Kochengat Chola Nayanar. This sacred sthalam is located between Mayiladuthurai and Peralam in Tamil Nadu. On the south street, opposite the south gopuram entrance, there is the temple of Visham Theertha Vinayagar.

He is the Sthala Vinayagar. It is a very ancient temple with an east-facing sanctum and a five-tiered Raja Gopuram. After passing through the Raja Gopuram, there is the Kodinilai Mandapam, followed by the Amman temple, the Maha Mandapam, and then the temple where Manikka Vannar is enshrined. The Lord’s abode is built like an artificial mountain. Since it is a Maadakkoil built by Kochengat Chola Nayanar, the Manikka Vannar sanctum is located high up on an artificial mountain. In the inner prakaram of the temple, along the northern wall, there is the Sthala Vriksham.

The banana tree is there. Because of this, this sthalam is called Kadalivana Kshetram.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal has also sung, “Marugal Nadu Marugale, where bananas bear fruit.” In the eastern outer prakaram, there is a Vanni tree. It serves as a great testament to the marriage of the Chetti girl, which is the reason for the special significance of this sthalam. The Moolavar, Manikka Vannar, is a Swayambhu Murthy. To the right of Manikka Vannar’s sanctum, there are idols of Somaskandar, Vinayagar, Ayyanaar, and other deities. In this sthalam, there are also idols of the Chetti boy and the Chetti girl. Ananda Koothar is seated facing south.

The idol of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman is in the form of Koothadum Pillaiyar. The idols of the sixty-three Nayanmars are located in the southern inner prakaram. After descending from the mountain, The Amman temple is there. The Amman faces south and bestows grace. The idol of the Amman is large and exquisitely beautiful. The name of the Amman is Vanduvar Kuzhali, and in Sanskrit, Amodhalaka Nayaki.

In the outer circumambulatory path, on the south side, there is the Suram Theertha Vinayagar temple. In the northern prakaram, there is Santhana Vinayagar. The Theerthams here are Lakshmi Theertham. The pond in front of the temple is called Lakshmi Theertham. It is a custom among the people of this region that if one observes the Varalakshmi Nombu with discipline, bathes, and then bathes again the next day, worships Manikka Vannar, and performs Parana, then debt troubles will be removed and wealth will increase. There is a Theertham called Seeralan Kulam.

This was formerly an educational institution. It is believed that Seeralan, the son of the illustrious Siruthondar, came here to study. This sacred sthalam is mentioned in the sacred verses of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. Two Thiru-Pathigams sung by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and one Thiru-Pathigam sung by Appar Peruman are available for this sacred sthalam. We will see the miracle performed by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman in this sacred sthalam described in detail in the Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman Puranam. There is a Sthala Puranam in Sanskrit for this sacred sthalam.

Festivals are celebrated grandly here. Brahmotsavam is held in the month of Chithirai. The flag is hoisted on the Shashti of Suklapaksha. A ten-day festival is held. On the seventh day of the festival, the Chetti girl’s wedding festival is celebrated. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, who came to this sthalam from Seeyaththamangai, has composed a Thiru-Pathigam.

It is the eighty-eighth Thiru-Pathigam in the fifth Thiru-Murai. This is a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathigam.

“Great penance can be attained, ignorance can be dispelled, twisted thoughts can be straightened. One can drink the supreme bliss by praising and worshipping the feet of Marugal. Those who have learned the art of singing and gone to other lands, you who are like a blacksmith’s anvil, if you worship the Lord of Marugal, surrounded by mansions, liberation will be easy. All actions born of anger will cease, and with great love, for those who remember the Lord of Marugal in their minds, there is no earthly life. To the parrot, feeding it nine kinds of nectar, protecting it, and teaching it many things, the lady will begin to send it as a messenger to the Lord of Marugal.”

“I do not know what it is, but my bangles slip, and tears well up in my eyes. My heart melts for the Lord of Marugal, the Lord of the fertile South. My bangles slip, and my clothes loosen. The maiden approaches the street where the Lord of Marugal comes. O maidens, what shall I do for this? Even if I do not see him daily, my love for him increases, knowing no return.

“My maiden, who is greatly devoted to the Lord of Marugal, will have much humility. Her heart remembers him, and tears well up. She will draw a Koodal, saying, ‘If the Lord of Marugal comes, you will join him.’ The maiden with fragrant, braided hair, at dusk, with the bull, will be confused, thinking, ‘Come, Lord of Marugal,’ and will be bewildered.” “He is the one who, when the great mountain was lifted, said ‘Jyothi’ and bestowed ancient grace. Those who praise and live by the grace of the Lord of Marugal are superior to the celestials.”

“Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, after worshipping the sacred sthalams of Thiru-Chenkattangudi, Thiru-Nallaru, Thiru-Saththamangai, and Thiru-Murugal, returns to Thiru-Pukalur. Our reflection now resumes.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 413, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, having worshipped Thiru-Murugal, returned to Thiru-Pukalur.

There, he performed sacred service, worshipped the Lord, and praised him with garlands of hymns. At this same time, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, who had gone to Thiruvarur, the one who had attained true knowledge, our Gnanasambandha Peruman, the one with the golden sacred thread from Venupuram, after completing his darshan in Thiruvarur, arrived in Thiru-Pukalur. Earlier, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman had taken leave of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, saying, “I will go to Thiruvarur, have darshan, and then return to join you here. Until then, please stay here.” Accordingly, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman The Lord, Thiru-Navukkarasu, remained in Thiru-Pukalur, visited sacred places like Thiru-Chenkattangudi, Thiru-Nallaru, Thiru-Murugal, and Seeyaththamangai, and then returned to stay in Thiru-Pukalur.

At this time, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman also came from Thiruvarur to Thiru-Pukalur and joined Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar at Thiru-Muruga Nayanar’s math. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman welcomed Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, and they stayed together in Thiru-Pukalur, immersed in Shiva-Ananda.

At that time, Thiru-Neelanakka Nayanar also arrived. Thiru-Muruga Nayanar was residing in his math.

Now, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is also there. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman has also returned here from Thiruvarur. Thiru-Neelakanda Yazhpanar is always with Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. Siruthonda Nayanar and Thiru-Neelanakka Nayanar join them. This place, where six Nayanmars stayed together at the same time in the math of Thiru-Muruga Nayanar, immersed in Shiva-Ananda, is a very significant place in the Periya Puranam. Sekkizhar Peruman states this, saying, “When Pillaiyar arrived, the heart of Vakkisar rejoiced with great desire, and he welcomed him.

“During their stay together, when Vallalar Siruthondar and others arrived, everyone else also arrived.” The phrase “stay together” here implies that all the devotees are together, united. This place serves as an excellent illustration of the truth of the twelfth Sutra of Sivagnana Bodham, “Marry with love.” This place serves as an excellent illustration of that truth for the twelfth Sutra. In this sacred verse, Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Siruthonda Nayanar as Vallalar Siruthondar. This is the first mention of Siruthonda Nayanar in the Periya Puranam.

“Therefore, he extols the Nayanar as Vallalar Siruthondar. The specialty of Siruthonda Nayanar is that he was willing to give a great gift to a devotee of Shiva, a gift that no one else could give.

“Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman refers to him as Vallalar.

“At the same time, when referring to Thiru-Neelanakka Nayanar, he mentions him as “Ellarum Seer Neelanakkar” (all are glorious Neelanakkar). Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman mentions Thiru-Neelanakka Nayanar in his Thiru-Pathigam.

“Thus, Thiru-Neelanakka Nayanar is one who is glorified in Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman’s Thiru-Pathigam.

“Therefore, Sekkizhar Swamigal states that he is a Nayanar of flawless glory. Hearing of the special occasion where Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal were together in Thiru-Muruga Nayanar’s math in Thiru-Pukalur, these two Nayanmars came here to see and worship Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal and to live in their company. This is the nature of devotees. The second sacred verse for the twelfth Sutra of Sivagnana Siddhiyar states: “With desire, approach the devotees of the Lord, make their work your work, speak with humility and grace, stand in the mark of knowledge, worship, clap, and dance.” This is the sacred verse. Just as these two Nayanmars arrived, many other devotees of Shiva also arrived and stayed together here, as we note.

“Thus, all the devotees stayed together in Thiru-Pukalur for a long time.

“At that time, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal sang Thiru-Pathigams about Shiva, the virtuous one who resided in Pukalur. The beautiful Tamil words of their Devara Thiru-Pathigams and the Shiva-Ananda meaning derived from them shone brightly there. Many devotees gathered there regularly studied and recited the Thiru-Pathigams of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. Hearing this, even the Nagana birds, that is, the Indian Myna birds and other birds, Even these birds sing these Pathigams in their sweet voices.

“Thus, the Thiru-Pathigam sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman at this time is the Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathigam beginning with “Thunnakkovana Sunnavenniranai,” the forty-sixth Thiru-Pathigam in the fifth Thiru-Murai.

““The Lord of Pukalur, adorned with a loincloth and white ash, with golden eyes and matted locks, keeps the shining moon and serpent together in his mind.” “The serpent that hisses, the moon that burns, the foaming Ganga, and the subtle red matted locks. How can I describe the Lord of Pukalur, who is flawless and beautiful, when my bangles slip? My waist, which is like a swing, my hair, which is like a rope, has brought me blame and taken away my beauty. O daughter, how can I complain and lament?”

“The Lord of Thiru-Pukalur, whose consort is the lightning-waisted Uma, who has no equal, who resides in the groves of Punna trees, I shall keep Him in my thoughts and be joyful. Where can I see the anklets of the King who wears the moon, by meditating on Him, chanting His names, and reciting the five letters? In the sacred Thiru-Pukalur and in my heart. He who consumed poison for the sake of the celestials, who sang the ancient four Vedas, those who worship Him as devotees are in the lotus of Thiru-Pukalur. No one has found the essence of truth; those who have found the essence have not seen it. He is not the essence for those who do not stand firm in the essence, but He is the Lord of Thiru-Pukalur.

“He who wore the skin of a fierce elephant that came to destroy, a black elephant with a large trunk, He is the Lord of Thiru-Pukalur. May my suffering cease by meditating on the Lord of Thiru-Pukalur, whose color is like gold, whose color is like the surging ocean, and who resides in the groves of Punna trees. He who, in his madness, did not regard the mountain, but praised it with his strong, crowned head, and then pressed it with his finger, worship the Lord of Thiru-Pukalur.

“In those days, as Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman resided in Thiru-Pukalur, a desire arose in both these great souls to visit and worship the sacred places where Lord Shiva is enshrined. These two great souls sing praises to the Lord and demonstrate the path of Chariya and Kriya, etc., to guide the people of this world. It is also noteworthy that during this pilgrimage, the refutation of other religions and the establishment of the Shaiva religion are to take place. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, who began his pilgrimage from here, visited many sacred places and was residing in Thiru-Maraikkadu when the Queen of Pandya and Kulachirai Nayanar explained the state of Jainism and Shaivism in the Pandya country to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and invited him to visit the Pandya country.

“There, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman set out for the Pandya country, refuted Jainism, and established the Shaiva religion. This pilgrimage, in which such acts of grace are to occur, is now about to be undertaken by these two great souls.

“Therefore, these two great souls intend to undertake a pilgrimage. So, there, at once, Thiru-Neelanakka Nayanar and Siruthondar Nayanar take their leave and depart. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, after praising Lord Shiva residing in Thiru-Pukalur and taking their leave, set out on their pilgrimage from Thiru-Muruga Nayanar’s hermitage. Muruga Nayanar also bids farewell to these two great souls. From here, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal both reached the sacred place called Thiru-Ambar and worshipped the Lord there. Thiru-Ambar and Ambar Mahanaam are separate temples.

“Both of these are the fifty-fourth and fifty-fifth sacred places on the south bank of the Cauvery. This sacred place is called Thiru-Ambar Perunthirukkoil. This sacred place, which Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman reached, Here, the Lord’s sacred name is Brahmapureeswarar, Brahmapurinathar. The Goddess’s sacred name is Poonguzhal Nayaki, Suganthakundalambikai. The Sthala Vriksham (sacred tree) is the Punna tree and the Marutha tree. The Theertham (sacred water) is Brahma Theertham, Arisilaru, Annamaam Poigai, Indra Theertham, Soola Theertham.

“Inside this sacred temple, there is a well called Annamaam Poigai. The Sthala Purana (temple history) states that Brahma bathed in the water of this well, worshipped a Shiva Lingam near the well, and was freed from the curse of having an Anna (swan) form. The demons Amban and Ambaran, born to Durvasa Muni and the celestial maiden Madalola, reached Punnakavanam, performed penance, and received the boon of conquering everyone. The atrocities of these two, who had received the boon, increased. The Devas (celestials) feared these two. Vishnu and other Devas appealed to Lord Shiva to protect everyone.

“At that time, Lord Shiva, He smiles slightly at the Goddess who was on His left side. The Goddess, understanding Lord Shiva’s intention, summons Kali there. She commanded Kali, who had arrived there, to destroy those two demons. Kali, in the form of a beautiful maiden, and Vishnu, as an old Brahmin, set out from there and reached the palace of these two demons. The two demons, Ambaran and Amban, captivated by the beauty of Kali, who had taken the form of a beautiful woman, competed with each other to marry her.

“At that time, Vishnu, who had come as an old man, says that the woman will marry whoever is stronger among the two of you.

“The old man Vishnu says that the woman is his daughter. Immediately, a fight broke out between Amban and Ambaran. who won there, went to the woman saying, “I will marry her, I will take her as my wife.” At that moment, the maiden, assuming a gigantic form that terrified everyone, kicked Ambaran in the chest. Kali destroyed Ambaran there; she annihilated him. The place where Ambaran was killed is called Ambakarathur. To remove the sin caused by killing the demon there, Kali worshipped Lord Shiva in Ambar Mahanaam and received His grace. This sacred place is where Bhairava destroyed the demon Samahara Seelan.

“This sacred place is where Vimalan, a Brahmin from Kasi, received grace. Manmathan worshipped here. This sacred place removed the Brahmahathi dosha of Nandan, the king of Kambhoja Desam. This sacred place is where the Brahmin Somasi Mara Nayanar, who was born in Ambar, lived. We will see his sacred history separately in the Purana of Somasi Mara Nayanar. This sacred temple is a Maadakkoil built by Kochchengan Chola Nayanar.

“A festival is held in this sacred temple on the auspicious day of Masi Magam. Ambar is known by the names Makkalapuram, Magalipuram, Punnakavanam, Brahmapuri, Nandarajapuram, Sampakaranyam, and Marapuri. This temple is located on the north bank of the Arisilaru river, facing east. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, who set out from Thiru-Pukalur and arrived here, praise and worship the Lord and sing hymns. The hymn sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar is not available to us. One Thiru-Padigam (hymn) composed by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman for this sacred place is currently available.

“Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu, Arasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman depart from there and arrive at the sacred place of Thiru-Kadhavoor. They worship and praise the golden feet of the Lord who kicked Yama. They arrive at Thiru-Kadhavoor and reside in the hermitage of Kungiliya Kalaya Nayanar. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar. We have already discussed this in the Purana of Kungiliya Kalaya Nayanar of Thiru-Kadhavoor.

“Thus, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, who are residing in the hermitage of Kungiliya Kalaya Nayanar, partake of food in the hermitage. We have discussed all the details in the Purana of Kungiliya Kalaya Nayanar in songs eight hundred sixty-two and eight hundred sixty-three. The hermitage of Kungiliya Kalaya Nayanar is his house. It is to the east of the Thiru-Kadhavoor temple, We can understand that it is located in the north-eastern part of the present street. We have also discussed the Sthala Purana of Thiru-Kadhavoor in the Purana of Kungiliya Kalaya Nayanar. Thiru-Kadhavoor is a Thevara sacred place sung by the Three Saints.

“Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, who resided here, has composed one Thiru-Padigam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman has composed three Thiru-Padigams. There is one Thiru-Padigam sung by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal.

“Therefore, at this time, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman has composed three Thiru-Padigams for this sacred place. We will continue to discuss those hymns.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 414. Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal arrive at the sacred place of Thiru-Kadhavoor. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman bestows three Thiru-Padigams upon this sacred place.

The first Thiru-Padigam is the thirty-first Thiru-Padigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Nerisai Thiru-Padigam.

If you wish to dispel the flood of desire for the evil, decaying body, then desire to light a lamp and incense. Those who can understand by lighting a lamp of understanding in their hearts will surely cast off deceit, for they are the Lord of Kadavur Veerattanam. If you value this earthly body and become deluded, who will explain when the King of Death demands it? He is like the jewel in the eye for the devotees who sing and dance to the melodies, for He is the Lord of Kadavur Veerattanam. He is the Lord of Kadavur Veerattanam.

You, who lead a false life within this body, do not understand the One, and do not remove the wickedness from your hearts. Those who can torment the tormenting elephant will surely reside in His thoughts, for He is the Lord of Kadavur Veerattanam. Those who bathe in the great dawn, become devotees of the Madman, and with flowers and buds, keep devotion within their hearts, and can offer good lamps and incense according to the rules, for them He is like a lump of jaggery, for He is the Lord of Kadavur Veerattanam. I have lived a life of deceit, without any proper conduct, and because there is no one to explain, I am like a chicken that has been explained. When the messengers of Yama come to disturb my mind, I am disturbed, for You are the Lord of Kadavur Veerattanam. I cannot live on the path, pouring water into the barren field of this sinful body, nor can I understand illusion.

I am like a boat in the midst of joy, tossed about by the five senses in this perishable life. I am like a boat in the midst of joy, tossed about by the five senses in this perishable life, for You are the Lord of Kadavur Veerattanam. I cannot understand illusion, and with a deluded mind, I have become like a ghost, a screech owl, a Pinya. I cannot think of You with love, You are the just one, I am a wretch. I cannot cast off this body, for You are the Lord of Kadavur Veerattanam. I lived a life without attachment, and poured water into the barren field.

I am like the saying that only the wicked will not understand until they experience it. What shall I do? I have learned no knowledge from suffering, and I see no refuge, for You are the Lord of Kadavur Veerattanam. He who kicked Yama for Markandeya, who stood firm to avoid the illusion, by offering milk, good curd, ghee, and many other things to Shiva, leaving the ways of women with eyes like fish, He is the Lord of Kadavur Veerattanam. The two in the beginning, and the three who became, The six, along with Indra and the Devas, and the Rishis, to bring joy, He crushed the strength of the one who lifted the mountain with his twenty arms, and listened to the Gandharvas, He is the Lord of Kadavur Veerattanam.

Now, the second Thiru-Padigam bestowed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman upon the sacred place of Thiru-Kadhavoor, the one hundred and seventh Thiru-Padigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Virutham Thiru-Padigam.

For Markandeya, the boy who worshipped Him to dispel the sorrow of delusion, He is the Lord of Kadavur, the Supreme One, whose sacred foot kicked Yama, whose dark body, curved sword, and sharp teeth, whose tongue was rolled up, caused Yama to tremble. The five-letter mantra, recited with devotion, for the boy who was about to lose his life, He is the Lord of Kadavur, the Supreme One, whose sacred foot kicked Yama, causing blood to flow like a river from his eyes. He is the Lord of Kadavur, the Supreme One. He is difficult for those with deceitful minds to see. He is the one with eyes that spit fire at Kama, and with the Ganga and the surging river on His widespread red matted hair, He is the milk-colored one, the Lord of Kadavur, the Supreme One, whose sacred foot once kicked Yama.

He is the Lord of Kadavur, the Supreme One, whose sacred foot, with a trident in hand, made Yama, who came to take the life of the boy who had worshipped Him with joy, cry out in pain. He is the Lord of Kadavur, the Supreme One, whose sacred foot, with a trident in hand, made Yama, who came to take the life of the boy who had worshipped Him with joy, cry out in pain. He is the Lord of Kadavur, the Supreme One, whose sacred foot, with a trident in hand, made Yama, who came to take the life of the boy who had worshipped Him with joy, cry out in pain. He is the Lord of Kadavur, the Supreme One, who, for the sake of the child, once gave the ocean of milk and sat under the banyan tree, reciting the Vedas, He is the Lord of Kadavur, the Supreme One, who, for the sake of the six sages, became angry with Yama, who came with a trident and a noose to pursue and attack. He is the Lord of Kadavur, the Supreme One, whose matted hair is adorned with Konrai flowers and a serpent garland, who wears a rope as a waist-cord, whose body is adorned with skulls, who wanders for alms, whose sacred foot, with a trident, cut Yama into pieces. He is the Lord of Kadavur, the Supreme One, whose matted hair is adorned with a garland of white skulls and the Ganga, who is the great one, the Lord who dances with ghosts, whose forehead has an eye, who became angry with Yama, and who consumed the poison from the ocean.

He is the Lord of Kadavur, the Supreme One. He is the Lord of Kadavur, the Supreme One, who, when Vishnu and Brahma, who could not be seen, sought Him, became an immeasurable column of light, and who, for Vishnu, who offered his eye as a lotus, and for Brahma, who sought Him, kicked Yama and became the eternal one. He is the Lord of Kadavur, the Supreme One, whose sacred foot, adorned with honey-dripping Konrai flowers and a garland of Koozhil flowers on His sacred head, pressed down the ten heads of the crooked-toothed Ravana, who lifted the mountain, causing them to fall.

Now, the third Thiru-Padigam bestowed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman upon the sacred place of Thiru-Kadhavoor, the thirty-seventh Thiru-Padigam of the Fifth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Padigam.

My heart, which is entangled in the strong karma that confuses like a mountain elephant, will not remain stable. For He is the Lord of Kadavur, who kills even the elephant with a murderous trunk, He is the elephant of the arts. He is the Lord of Kadavur, who is like a silver mountain, who is within us as He truly is, who is the elephant in the temple that is like a treasury, He is the elephant of deceit. He is the Lord of Kadavur, who is the good knowledge, He is the Lord of Kadavur, who is the good knowledge, who melts the body to burn it, who skinned the elephant of desire and made Uma fear, He is the elephant that can be seen. He is the Lord of Kadavur, who is the beautiful elephant that drank poison, who is the elephant with a dark body and a long crystal, who is the elephant of the beautiful bright light, He is the elephant of time.

He is the Lord of Kadavur, who is the elephant that destroys and dances with the five, who is the elephant with a white long flag, who is the elephant that made the beautiful Kama rise, He is the elephant that has been cast off. He is the Lord of Kadavur, who is the elephant that sent the great mountain to the sky, who is the elephant of the pure great mountain, who is the elephant that became angry with the fierce Yama, He is the elephant that became angry. He is the Lord of Kadavur, who is the elephant that deludes those on earth, who is the elephant that many in thought praise, who is the elephant that many in heaven cannot reach, He is the elephant in the eye. He is the Lord of Kadavur, who is the elephant of the angry red coral, who is the elephant that removes the fragrant strong karma, He is the Lord of Kadavur, who is the elephant with a loving heart that embraces, He is the elephant that trumpets. He is the Lord of Kadavur, who is the elephant of the fiery light of the Vedas, who is the elephant of justice and righteousness, who is the elephant that understands by studying the ages, He is the elephant of love. He is the Lord of Kadavur, who is the elephant that Vishnu and Brahma, who sought to see Him, could not find, He is the elephant that became an immeasurable column of light.

He is the Lord of Kadavur, the elephant that can be seen.

In this hymn, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman refers to the entire hymn as “Aanaiyar.” “Aanaiyar” means “one who is like an elephant.” Therefore, he sings metaphorically as “one who is like an elephant.” Now, taking “Aanaiyar” to mean “Aanai” as a cow, “Aanaiyar” refers to “one who rides a cow,” which is Pasupathi.

Here, the meaning is that the heart, which is tormented by strong karmas that come like a mountain-dwelling elephant, will be protected and made joyful by the Lord, who is like an elephant, entering your heart and saving you from the egoistic elephant of madness.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, who worshipped Thiru-Kadhavoor, proceed to Thiru-Kadhavoor Mayanam, which is very close by. Thiru-Kadhavoor Mayanam is a sacred place very close to Thiru-Kadhavoor. There are Mayanam Sthalams such as Kachi Mayanam, Kali Mayanam, Veli Mayanam, Nalur Mayanam.

Therefore, to distinguish this place from other Mayanam Sthalams, it is called Thiru-Kadhavoor Thiru-Mayanam by adding Thiru-Kadhavoor in front. This sacred place, Thiru-Kadhavoor Mayanam, is a place sung by the Three Saints. It is the forty-eighth sacred place on the south bank of the Cauvery. The Lord’s sacred name here is Brahmapureeswarar. The Goddess’s sacred name is Malarkuzhal Minnamai. The Sthala Vriksham (sacred tree) is Vilvam.

The Theertham (sacred water) is Kashi Theertham. It is the place where Brahma was burnt in a Kalpa and then revived to regain his creative power, hence it is called Mayanam. Brahma worshipped here. Kashi Theertham is located very close to this sacred place. On the Aswini day in the month of Panguni, Amirthakadeswarar appears and gives Theertham. From this Kashi Theertham, the sacred bathing water is brought daily for Thiru-Kadhavoor Veerattaneswarar.

Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal have each composed one hymn. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Appar Swamigal, who came to this sacred place, worship the Lord residing here.

Now, the Thiru-Padigam bestowed by Appar Swamigal upon this sacred place is the thirty-eighth Thiru-Padigam in the Fifth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Padigam.

Those with matted hair, wearing a loincloth, who are the Lord of Kadavur Mayanam, they remove the sins and faults committed by their ancient devotees. The Lord’s feet.

The Lord of Kadavur Mayanam, whom the celestials think of and praise, He will not say “no” to those who worship Him. The Lord’s feet. He who holds a trident, wears a tiger skin, consumes poison and then tastes nectar, He is the Lord of Kadavur Mayanam, the Destroyer of Time, whose chest is adorned with garlands. The Lord’s feet.

The Lord of Kadavur Mayanam, whose sacred feet are worshipped by the celestials, who is the Lord of the trees, The Lord of Kadavur Mayanam, who is the righteous one, removes the birth cycle of His devotees. The Lord’s feet. He who calmed the raging Kali, He is the mad one, the Lord of Kadavur Mayanam, who wanders doing things that are both fitting and unfitting, He is a madman. The Lord’s feet. He who has a fiery body and wears the young moon, He is the dark one, the Lord of Kadavur Mayanam, who is rare for the celestials, and greater than Brahma and Vishnu. The Lord’s feet.

He who has Anangu as a part of Him, who is the four Vedas, who is the Lord of Kadavur Mayanam, where the Ganas gather, He removes the suffering of those who worship Him, He is the Lord of Kadavur Mayanam, the Lord of the cremation ground where corpses are found. The Lord’s feet. He who has a trident in hand, who is the ancient Purana, who is the Lord of Kadavur Mayanam, where trees are found, He removes the suffering of those who praise Him, He accepts their worship, He is the Lord of Kadavur Mayanam, the Lord even for Brahma. In this Thiru-Padigam, the ninth and tenth The sacred songs are not available to us.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, who worshipped Thiru-Kadhavoor Mayanam, reach the sacred place called Thiru-Akkur. There, they worship the Lord residing in the temple called Thanthondri Madam. Akkur is a sacred place near Mayiladuthurai, very close to Sembanar Koil. The name of the village is Thiru-Akkur, and the name of the temple is Thanthondri Madam. It is the forty-sixth sacred place among the sacred places on the south bank of the Cauvery. This sacred place has two Thiru-Padigams, one composed by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and one by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar.

In the eleventh Thiru-Murai, Kapila Deva Nayanar has sung about this place. Sirupuli Nayanar was born here and served by offering sacred food to all devotees. This sacred sthalam is renowned for its greatness. The sacred temple here is one of the Maadakkoils built by Kochchengan Chola Nayanar. The beautiful deity known as ‘Aayirathil Oruvar’ (One in a Thousand) in this sthalam is worthy of darshan. Facing east, the sacred temple has a sacred tank in front of it.

The Rajagopuram has three tiers, and at its entrance resides Vinayagar. After worshipping Him and entering, one reaches the second prakaram.

First, there is the Sabha Mandapam where Lord Nataraja is enshrined. In this prakaram, to the right of the Lord, the Ambikai temple faces east. This is one of the sacred sthalams where Lord Shiva granted His wedding vision to Agastya. Vinayagar is in the Kanni Moolai (southeast corner), and Murugapperuman is in the west. To the north is the Chandesar temple. Proceeding clockwise, we ascend the steps of the Maadakkoil to have darshan of the Lord.

The Maadakkoil stands five cubits high from the ground. Vinayagar is in front. After worshipping the Lord and ascending the steps, one can see the Nandi and Balipeedams. Beyond them is the Munmandapam, where the Panchamoorthigal and Navagrahangal are present. Following this are the Maha Mandapam and then the first prakaram. In the southern part of the first prakaram are Banalingam, Viswanathar, Visalakshi, Sirappuli Nayanar, and the Samayacharyargal.

To the west are Vinayagar, Murugan, and Gajalakshmi. To the north are Kailasanathar, Kamakshi, and many Lingamoorthigal.

Next, one can behold the Lord enshrined as ‘Aayirathul Oruvar’ in a separate vimanam. He is the special deity of this sthalam. In the Garbhagriha Koshtams, to the south are Agastya, Narthana Vinayagar, and Dakshinamurthy. To the west is Lingothbavar. To the north are Brahma, Durga, and Markandeyar. The Lord’s shrine is adorned with small Dvarapalakas.

The Thanthondreesar shrine radiates divine splendor, captivating our hearts. At the outer entrance are Surya and Bhairavar. The Ambikai temple is beautifully adorned with separate mandapams. In the Thevara Thiruppathigam for this sthalam, composed by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, the Shaivites residing in this town are specially praised. It is stated that the Brahmins and Vellalars living here are followers of the path of truth, free from falsehood, and worship the Lord by carrying flowers and water. They are also described as those who joyfully give to the needy, never saying ‘no’ to those who come to them in want.

The Brahmins are lauded as those who have mastered the six Angas, the rare Vedas, and the five Yagnas, and as those who uphold the four Vedas, the six Angas, and many arts. The Vellalars are praised as ‘Thaalalar’ (industrious ones) who are mighty in their prowess. Sekkizhar Peruman, when describing this sthalam in the Periya Puranam, explains the reason for the town’s name, stating that it is the town that creates prosperity, hence Thiru-Aakkoor. As previously observed, the name of this sacred temple is Thanthondri Maadam. Two sacred temples named ‘Maadam’ are mentioned in Thevaram. One of them is Thoongaanai Maadam in Pennagadam, and the other is Thanthondri Maadam.

Lord Shiva is known here by the sacred name ‘Aayirathil Oruvar’ (One in a Thousand). In this sthalam, a king, by divine command, fed a thousand Brahmins.

The Lord appeared as one of those thousand Brahmins, partook of the food, and blessed the king.

Therefore, the sacred image of the Lord, who came as one among a thousand, is present in the sacred temple. The Lord’s name here is Thanthondriyappar, or Swayambunathar. The sacred name of the Goddess is Thiru-Valnedungkan Ammai, which is Kadkanethri in Sanskrit. The Theertham is Kumudha Theertham, located behind the temple. All these are the special features of the Thiru-Aakkoor Thanthondri Maada sacred temple. These are the glories.

Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, who came here to worship, composed Thevara Thiruppathigams. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman composed one Thiruppathigam, which is a Thiruthandaga Thiruppathigam. It is the twenty-first Thiruppathigam in the Sixth Thirumurai.

He is like one who placed His feet on the lotus. He is Thanthondriyappar in Aakkoor. He is like the one who wears a five-headed serpent. He is Thanthondriyappar in Aakkoor. He is like the one whose feet are like a sea of red gold.

He is Thanthondriyappar in Aakkoor. He is like the one who became the vast sky, white ash, fire, moon, countless numbers, earth, and the sky itself. He is Thanthondriyappar in Aakkoor. He is like the one who is the ancient town, the ancient waves.

He is like the one without beginning or end. He is like the one who stands as good deeds, dispelling evil. He is like the wealthy one who is Himself the eight directions. He is like the one who resides as the star Aathirai. He is Thanthondriyappar in Aakkoor. He is like the Lord with a blue throat, who stood when Vishnu and Brahma searched for Him. He is like the one whose form is the color of fire, red gold, and whose color is that of the gem-hued Vishnu.

He is like the one who became the refuge of devotees. He is Thanthondriyappar in Aakkoor. Let us press on with our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part Four Hundred and Fifteen. Thiru-Nindra Charukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, after worshipping the Lord at Thiru-Aakkoor Thanthondri Maadam, continue their sacred pilgrimage to the sthalam of Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. Sekkizhar Swamigal sings that after worshipping at Thiru-Aakkoor Thanthondri Maadam and venerating many other sacred places, they reached Thiru-Vizhimizhalai.

In the same context, in the Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman Puranam, Sekkizhar Peruman sings that Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, after worshipping at Thiru-Aakkoor Thanthondri Maadam, visited sthalams like Thiru-Miyachur and Thiru-Paambaram, and then reached Thiru-Vizhimizhalai.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman must have worshipped at Thiru-Aakkoor, then visited sthalams like Thiru-Miyachur and Thiru-Paambaram, and subsequently reached Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. The sacred places on the way from Thiru-Aakkoor to Thiru-Miyachur are not mentioned here. The Nayanmars proceeded north from Thiru-Kadhavoor to Thiru-Aakkoor.

Therefore, they must have traveled west from there. If they had taken that route, they would have worshipped at Thiru-Chembanpalli, Thiru-Vizhanagar, Thiru-Mayiladuthurai, and then proceeded south to worship at Thiru-Vazhuvoor Veerattanam before arriving at Thiru-Miyachur.

Thus, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman must have reached Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. In this pilgrimage of these two great personages, Thiru- It was customary for Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to proceed first, followed by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman in a palanquin, reaching the sthalam. This can be seen in the Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman Puranam.

Thus, these two great personages arrive at the wondrous sacred sthalam of Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. Let us contemplate a little about the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. This sthalam, Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, is known by ten sacred names: Bhu Kailasam, Kalyana Puram, Panchakshara Puram, Dakshina Kasi, Shanmangala Sthalam, Swetha Kaananam, Akasha Nagaram, Panacharanyam, Netrappana Puram, and Thejini Vanam. This sacred sthalam, Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, is sung by all three Nayanmars: Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. It has twenty-three It possesses. The sacred sthalam of Thiru-Vizhimizhalai is the sixty-first sthalam among the Kaveri South Bank sthalams in the Chola country.

It is sung in Sendanar’s Thiruvisaippa. Arunagirinathar’s Thiruppugazh also pertains to this sthalam. This sacred sthalam is located a short distance west from Poonthottam, which is on the road from Mayiladuthurai to Thiruvarur. One can also reach Thiru-Vizhimizhalai from the cities of Thiruvarur and Kumbakonam. The sacred name of the Lord in this sthalam is Vizhi Azhagar. Netrappaneswarar and Vizhi Azhagisar are other sacred names.

The sacred name of the Goddess is Sundarakujambikai, or Azhagu Mulai Ammai. The sacred name of Vinayagar is Padikkasu Vinayagar. The Thiru-Ula Moorthy (processional deity) of this sthalam is Kalyana Sundarar. This sthalam has a total of twenty-three Thiruppathigams. exist. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman composed fourteen Thiruppathigams, Appar Peruman eight Thiruppathigams, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal one Thiruppathigam, totaling twenty-three Thiruppathigams for this sthalam. There is one Thiruvisaippa pathigam composed by Sendanar.

In the Thirumurais, the history of Thirumal receiving the Chakra in this sthalam is extensively mentioned. There is a Sthala Puranam for Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. Its author is Sri Meignana Munivar, who was a disciple of Sri Maraignana Desikar, the second Guru Moorthy of Thiru-Avaduthurai Adheenam. The total number of verses in this Puranam is six hundred and seventy-eight. This Sthala Puranam must have been composed approximately four hundred years ago. The sacred monasteries where Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal stayed and worshipped in this sthalam are located on the North Street here.

This temple contains many inscriptions. The mandapam known as Vavvalnathu or Vavval Netri in this temple is very famous. Sthapathis (temple architects) who undertake temple renovations usually have contracts for all renovations except for certain rare works in some sthalams. Among such exceptional works, the Vavvalnathu mandapam in this sthalam is one. Like the Thillai Moovayiravar and Perunthuvar, in Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, Lord Shiva is also one among five hundred Brahmins. Vizhi Sivagra Yogigal, the second Guru Moorthy of Thiru-Kailaya Paramparai Suryanar Koil Adheenam, attained Shiva Paripoornam in this sthalam.

Their Guru Moorthy monasteries are also here. In connection with this sthalam, there is also a prabandham called Azhagiya Mamulai Ammai Pillai Tamil. This sacred sthalam is under the spiritual administration of the Thiru-Kailaya Paramparai Thiru-Avaduthurai Adheenam. The sacred temple faces east. The shrines of the Lord and the Goddess face east. The Goddess’s temple is to the left of the Lord’s temple.

In front of this temple shines the Vishnu Theertham. Upon passing the Rajagopuram entrance, one finds the Thiru-Kalyana Mandapam, known as the Vavvalnathi Mandapam, which adds glory to this sacred temple. No one can help but marvel at the structure of this mandapam, which is wide and constructed with lime plaster without central pillars. The Kodungai in Avudaiyar Koil, the Vavvalnathi Mandapam in Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, and the Thiru-Mathil in Kadaram Kondan are considered excellent examples of architectural craftsmanship. It is said to be excellent. The Lord’s sacred wedding festival takes place in this mandapam during the month of Chithirai.

After passing the second gopuram, in the outer circumambulatory path, one can see to the east the Balipeedam where the Lord bestowed coins upon Thiru-Gnanasambandhar, and to the west the Balipeedam where coins were granted to Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal. Nearby, one can have darshan of Padikkasu Vinayagar and the sacred forms of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. After passing the third gopuram entrance, the first prakaram is found. The Vizhinathar sacred temple is built in the Maadakkoil style. In the southern prakaram are the Sthala Vinayagar, and to the west are Somaskandar, Murugan, Mahalakshmi, and other deities. In the northern prakaram, Chandeswarar is enshrined.

In the Sabha located in the northeast direction, Natarajar is enshrined. While circumambulating this prakaram, one can clearly see the Vinnizhi Vimanam, the Lord’s vimanam brought and installed by Thirumal from the divine world. This vimanam, adorned with copper plates and a golden kalasam, possesses a unique beauty and stands distinct from the vimanams of other temples. ‘Vinnizhi Vimanam udai Vinnvar Piran maruvu Vizhi Nagare’ is a Thevaram verse by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman about the vimanam of this sthalam. During the Maha Kumbabhishekam held approximately eight years ago, this vimanam was covered with Panchaloha plates. It is said that when Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman was staying and worshipping in this sthalam, he desired to see the Lord of Seerkazhi.

At that time, the Lord graciously revealed His form as seen in Seerkazhi in this sthalam. The Lord’s shrine is beautifully arranged with the Garbhagriham, Ardhamandapam, and Mahamandapam. In the sanctum sanctorum of the Vinnizhi Vimanam, the Moolalingam, Arulmigu Vizhinatheswarar is enshrined. Behind the Lord is the wedding posture of the Lord with Goddess Parvati. At the entrance are Dvarapalakas. In accordance with this being the sthalam where the Lord married Umaiyamai, there is a pillar called Arasani Kaal at the entrance of the Garbhagriham, and a pillar called Pandhal Kaal in the outer Mahamandapam.

In a separate mandapam within the Mahamandapam, the Kalyana Sundara Swamy, known as Mappillai Swamy, who is unique to this sthalam, is enshrined.

The Lord is seen as a bridegroom embracing Umaiyamai, near the Rishabam. At the Lord’s feet shines a lotus flower, which Thirumal offered by plucking one of His own eyes as a flower. Adjacent to this mandapam are Bhikshatanar, Kalasamharamurthy, and others. Near the Lord’s shrine, Thyagesar is enshrined with the Chakra weapon in hand. After worshipping Him, one can reach the Ambikai shrine through the entrance located in the northern prakaram. One can behold Arulmigu Sundara Kujambikai, who shines as a goddess whose beauty is unparalleled.

It was in this sacred sthalam that Thirumal received the Chakra he desired.

Once, when Lord Shiva was in His divine form with Uma Devi on Mount Kailash, Thirumal worshipped the Lord and made a request. He said, “My Chakra has become very weak.

“Therefore, Your Holiness should bestow upon me the Chakra with which you vanquished the demon Jalandhara.” Lord Shiva, in His compassion, blessed Mahavishnu, saying, “Go to the sthalam named Thejini Vanam, south of the Kaveri, and worship Me.” Mahavishnu took leave of the Lord and immediately came to this sacred sthalam. He worshipped the Lord and decided to create a lotus pond. He invoked the Kaveri River. The Kaveri River branched off west of Thiruvalanjuzhi, flowed as the Arisilaaru to the south of this Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, then turned north to merge with the Ksheera Nadi at the Lord’s shrine, and finally flowed east to join the sea. Vishnu created a pond here, named Padma Theertham, and cultivated red lotuses in it. He brought the Vinnilai Vimanam, supported by sixteen lions, and enshrined Lord Shiva in it.

“Daily, Mahavishnu bathed in the Theertha Pushkarani, adorned himself with Vibhuti and Rudraksha, and worshipped Lord Shiva according to scriptural injunctions with a thousand lotus flowers.

“Thus, daily, he offered a thousand lotus flowers for the thousand sacred names of Lord Shiva. He continued to perform the archana.

“One day, by the divine grace of Lord Shiva, one flower was missing from the thousand. Vishnu considered this to be the Lord’s divine will. Instead of the lotus flower, that is, since one flower was missing, he plucked his own right eye and offered it at the Lord’s sacred feet.

“At that moment, Lord Shiva, easily accessible through love, appeared before Vishnu. He bestowed upon Vishnu the Chakra weapon with which He had vanquished the demon Jalandhara.

“Afterwards, Vishnu stayed here for some time, worshipped, and created a theertham named Vishnu Theertham in his own name.

“Then he returned to his own world.

“Once before, Lord Brahma became infatuated with Tilottama, whom he had created. Lord Brahma absolved himself of that sin by worshipping Lord Shiva in this sacred sthalam. Kathyayanamuni, the foremost among sages, reached this sthalam, built an ashram on the bank of the Theertha Pushkarani, bathed daily in the Theertha Pushkarani, worshipped Azhagiya Mamulai Ammai and Vizhinathar, and performed severe penance with his wife in the Pannagasalai. He had no offspring, so he performed rare yagnas for this purpose.

“At that time, the Goddess appeared as Annapoorani, holding a vessel of food in her left hand and a ladle for serving food in her right hand, and asked the great ascetic, “What boon do you desire?” To this, Kathyayanamuni replied, “Mother, you yourself should come as my daughter.” The Goddess granted this boon to the sage. The Goddess took leave of the Supreme Lord and appeared in the form of a beautiful female child in a magnificent blue lotus flower in the Theertha Pushkarani near the Pannagasalai where the sage was performing penance. The sage’s wife, named Thumangalai, saw her, was filled with joy, took the child, embraced her to her chest, and gave her to Kathyayanamuni. They named the child Kathyayini and raised her. When Kathyayini reached marriageable age, the sage performed severe penance to Lord Shiva. Lord Shiva, moved by the sage’s penance, appeared.

“The sage prostrated at the Lord’s sacred feet and prayed, “O Lord, You Yourself should come here in the guise of a bridegroom and marry this maiden.” Lord Shiva, pleased in His heart, blessed him, saying, “We shall marry on the Magam star day in the month of Chithirai.” As the Lord had promised the sage, on the Magam star day in the month of Chithirai, He departed from Sri Kailash, accompanied by Thirumal, Brahma, Nandi, and other ganas, adorned in all ornaments, and proceeded south to reach the place where Kathyayanamuni resided in Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. Kathyayanamuni welcomed the Lord, worshipped Him, and made arrangements for the wedding. With grand decorations and great splendor, the wedding ceremony of Sri Kailasapathi and Kathyayini Ambikai took place.

“Afterwards, the Lord and the Goddess went in procession through the sacred streets and entered the temple.

“At that time, Kathyayanamuni had a doubt: whether the one who came as the bridegroom was indeed Lord Shiva. Knowing this, the Lord, in order to dispel the sage’s doubt, appeared there in the form of the bridegroom, radiating light, with the lotus-eye that Thirumal had offered instead of a lotus flower, and the Vilanga fruit offered by the devotee Mizhalai Kurumbar.

“At that moment, the sage fell at the sacred feet of Lord Shiva and worshipped Him. His doubt dispelled, Kathyayanamuni danced in ecstasy.

“The Lord forever resides in this sthalam. As they wished, praying that He should be graciously seated, the Peruman is seated there even today in the same bridal form for many to see.

“Therefore, it is true that those who wish for an early marriage will achieve it quickly if they come to this sthalam and worship the Peruman in that manner. This Thiru-sthalam is where the history of Shvetaketu, similar to the sacred history of Maharishi Markandeya, took place. Emperor Sibi came to this sthalam, worshipped the Peruman, performed sacred services, and brought five hundred Brahmins, who were well-versed in the Vedas and Agamas, to Thiru-vizhimizhalai. He provided them with all their needs and made them reside there.

“At that time, Lord Shiva, in the guise of a Brahmin, also received alms as one of the five hundred.

“Then, Maharishi Narada pointed out to Emperor Sibi that Lord Shiva was receiving alms as one of the five hundred Brahmins.

“At that time, Lord Shiva, the king, was greatly pleased. Afterwards, Emperor Sibi, with the help of those five hundred Brahmins, conducted daily pujas and festivals for Lord Shiva with great splendor. He provided everything necessary for the temple, received many boons, returned to his city, and lived happily. The couple Pururavas and Bhadravalli came to this sthalam, performed sacred services, received boons, and rejoiced. Kamadhenu worshipped Lord Shiva. The milk with which Kamadhenu performed abhishekam overflowed, becoming known as ‘Arasil Nadhi,’ and merged with the river at the Swami Sannidhi.

“Manu worshipped Lord Shiva at this sthalam. This sthalam was a forest of Thejini, meaning a forest of Veeli plants.

“In addition, many other trees like sandalwood, champak, and jackfruit were dense in that forest.

“At that time, there was a hunter named Mizhalai Kurumbar. He saw Lord Shiva, was filled with joy, and worshipped Him with love, offering a Vilangkani fruit daily.

“The Lord appeared before him and blessed him. From then on, he adopted an ascetic form, performed great penances, and worshipped Lord Shiva. Through the power of his penance, he attained the eight great siddhis. The form of the Vilangkani fruit accepted by the Peruman is still visible at the sacred feet of Manavala Peruman. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and Appar Swamigal received gold coins here. We will discuss this in detail.

“There are five sacred places (Panchakrosalams) associated with this sthalam. They are Vasishteswaram, which is located in the northeast direction of this sthalam, in Vadugakkudi, on the east bank of the Kirthiman River, where only a Moolingam is visible. Vasishta Theertham and Theertham are in the form of a field.

“Secondly, Indireswaram is a temple in the nearby Kadkambadi.

“Thirdly, the Lingam worshipped by Manu, now known as Manu Thapacheri, is a temple. There is also Manu Theertham.

“Fourthly, Gautameswaram is in the southeast direction of this sthalam, in Sambandan Padi, where only a Lingam is visible in the field. The Theertham is a field.

“Fifthly, Kaleswaram is in the south, on the bank of Kallikulam. Currently, it is in Vishnupuram, on the bank of Dharmakulam, and is a temple. Next is Markandeswaram, which is a temple in the first tier. Next is Subeswaram, which is a temple in Sembankudi. Next is Abhimukteswaram, which is a temple on the west, on the bank of Thamaraikulam. Tenth is Bhadravallieswaram, which is a temple in the south.

“The eleventh is Svargavadhaneeswaram, which was near the Kathyayaniyamma temple. Currently, it is in the Bhadravallisar temple. In the northern street, there are separate temples in the sacred matham where Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-navukkarasu Swamigal resided. The deities are Thiru-moolattanam, Mayuranathar, Madhyarjunewarar, Annamalaiyar, Brahmalingam, Thyagarajar, and many other Lingams.

“Now, in this sthalam, there are many Utsava Moorthies (processional deities) such as Natarajar, Somaskandar, Chandrasekarar, Chakradhanar, Bhikshadanar, Kalasamharar, Svargavadhaneeswarar, Nayanmars, and others. The Sthala Vriksham (sacred tree) is different for each Yuga. In the first Yuga, the sandalwood tree was the Sthala Vriksham. In the second Yuga, the Champak tree. In the third Yuga, the Veeli plant. In the fourth Yuga, the Jackfruit tree were the Sthala Vrikshams.

“The Theerthams (sacred waters) in this sthalam are Pushkarani Theertham, Vishnu Theertham, Brahma Theertham, Thiru-veni Sangamam, Padma Theertham, Indra Theertham, Yama Theertham, Varuna Theertham, Kubera Theertham, Gautama Theertham, Markanda Theertham, Viswamitra Theertham, Gayatri Theertham, Savitri Theertham, Saraswati Theertham, Lakshmi Theertham, Bhoomi Devi Theertham, Rudra Theertham, Kapila Theertham, Bhadravalli Theertham, Parvati Theertham, Manu Theertham, Vasishta Theertham, Abhimukta Theertham, and Samudra Theertham, totaling twenty-five Theerthams. In this sthalam, the Brahmotsavam takes place in the month of Chithirai, with the Dhvajarohanam (flag hoisting) on the Mrigasirisha star, the Thiru-kalyanam (sacred marriage) on the Magam star, and the Theertham (sacred bath) on the Chithirai star. Besides these, the Sashti Utsavam, Thiru-vathirai Utsavam, and Navaratri Utsavam are also celebrated. One-day festivals like Avani Moolam are also held. All these are the news and special features of the Thiru-vizhimizhalai Sthala Puranam. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman arrive at this sthalam.

“Let us proceed with our contemplation.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 416. Thiru-nindra Sarukkam. Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman arrive at Thiru-vizhimizhalai. The sacred devotees (Thiru-thondar) and Brahmins of Lord Shiva residing in Thiru-vizhimizhalai come to the outskirts of Thiru-vizhimizhalai and greet and worship Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman.

Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman worship the devotees who came to greet them.

Thus, the devotees of Thiru-vizhimizhalai and the two great spiritual leaders mingle with each other. Those who were already united by love now meet directly. A large gathering of Thiru-vizhimizhalai’s devotees welcome the two great spiritual leaders. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, in his Thevaram, has sung about how the devotees of Thiru-vizhimizhalai came to greet him, saying, “Known devotees went in every direction, eagerly welcoming me to Vizhimizhalai.” This conveys to us the abundance of the devotees’ love. It is for this reason that the Lord of Mizhalai placed gold coins for both Nayanmars, for the devotees of Thiru-vizhimizhalai, and protected them from suffering throughout the famine, which is a significant point.

To welcome the two great spiritual leaders arriving at Thiru-vizhimizhalai, the Brahmins living in that city decorate the main streets of the sacred city. At the entrances of their mansions, they arrange rows of auspicious lamps, large banana trees, and areca nut trees. They welcome them, holding full golden pots. Accepting their welcome, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman comes to the sacred temple of Thiru-vizhimizhalai and arrives at the entrance of the temple, which has a celestial vimanam. Having arrived thus, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman enters the sacred temple, circumambulates the sacred temple of Lord Shiva, who graciously resides in Thiru-vizhimizhalai, bows in the sacred courtyard, falls at the sacred feet of the Peruman, rises, and is overwhelmed with emotion. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman joins his two hands above his head and worships the Lord’s sacred feet.

Love fills the heart of Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, and it overflows. His heart melts and dissolves. Tears flow like a waterfall on his sacred body. Having worshipped the Peruman in this manner, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman sings the Thiru-thandakam, which conveys the idea that those who do not join the Lord with the red matted hair will join the path of evil. “Those who do not join the Lord with the red matted hair will join the path of evil” is the central theme of the pathigam sung by Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman at Thiru-vizhimizhalai. In each verse of this pathigam, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman has used the refrain, “Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil.” Earlier, when worshipping the Lord of Thiru-nageswaram, Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar stated in a negative sense, “Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-nageswaram will not join the good path.”

Now, Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar, who had previously stated in a negative sense that those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-nageswaram will not join the good path, now affirms in a positive sense that if they do not join the good path, they will indeed join the evil path. Appar Swamigal has blessed this sthalam with eight Thiru-pathigams.

At this time, he blessed the Thiru-thandakam pathigam that begins with “Poranai Irurivai Porvaiyanai,” which is the fiftieth Thiru-pathigam in the sixth Thiru-murai. Let us now contemplate that Thiru-pathigam.

“Poranai Irurivai Porvaiyanai, Puliyathale Udai Aadai Potrinanai, Paranai Mathiyanai Pagalananai, Palluyirai Neduvelliyai Paranthu Nindra Neeranai Katranai Theeyananai Ninaiyathar Purameriya Ninaitha Theiva Theranai Thiru-vizhimizhalaiyanai Serathar Theenrikke Serkinrare Savantha” “He who wears the ashes and bones from the cremation ground, with a skull and hair-rope, He who is the Pasupatha in the form of a mendicant, He who consumed all the sacrifices offered by the ancient gods, He who is Ekamban of Kanchi, He who turned red when Yama, who had approached the ocean, fell, Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil. He who taught dharma under the banyan tree, He who loved Agastya, He who stood when Brahma and Vishnu searched, He who drank the poison from the ocean, He who conquered the five senses while united with the beautiful maiden, He who resided in Meeyachur, He who went to measure the penance of the slender maiden, Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil. He who is pure, He who is the radiant coral light, He who is the mother who stands as a support for all living beings, He who gave the discus to Markandeya,” “He who is Shankara, He whose mouth recites the Chandoga Sama, He who is in the hearts of those who meditate, He who is far from those who utter the five letters with deceit, Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil.

“He who is good among the fragrant ones, He who consumed the poison that came as evil, He who is immortal even if other gods perish, He who is a unique light that cannot be understood by those who know the past, present, and future, He who destroyed the three cities in the two skies, Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil. He who has a dark throat, He who has the moon on his matted hair like a lightning bolt in the sky, He who rains everywhere, He who performs the dance of a mendicant, He who holds the trident while the split ghosts roar, He who is truthful without falsehood, He who creates the life that encompasses the earth and the heavens,” “Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil. He who is great, He who is the Lord of those who seek refuge, He who became the six different religions, He who entered all things, He who is common to all, He who is worthy of all things praised by the inhabitants of the golden world, He who is the truth that is not other than Himself, He who made the great mountain the center, Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil. He who is the son who crushed the shoulders of the king of the celestials, He who resided in Valai Kulam and Marai Kadu, He who is the flesh, He who is the life, He who went to know the state of the great penance of Arjuna one day, He who is the eye, He who resided in Kailash, He who has the Ganga in his matted hair, He who is honey to those who mingle with Him, Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil. He who is pervasive, He who is many on this side, He who is Pasupathi, He who grants liberation to devotees,”

“He who is the boon, He who is in the hearts of those who worship, He who destroyed the three cities with the arrow of fire, He who is the arrow, He who is the ascetic who placed the arrow under your feet, He who has the green head adorned with a crown of matted hair, Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil. He who is the meaning, He who fearlessly cut off one of the five heads of Brahma, He who crushed the shoulders of the demon who lifted the mountain, He who listened to the music of the seven strings, He who crushed the moon, He who took the teeth of the sun, He who, at the request of the celestials for Bhagiratha, gathered the flowing waters of the Ganga like snow, Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil.”

“Thus, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, having worshipped the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai, blessed this Thiru-thandakam pathigam at this time. Although both great spiritual leaders, the Samayacharyas, visited the sacred temple together, even though they visited the sacred temple together, this is the Puranam of Thiru-navukkarasu, so it describes the worship methods and actions performed by Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman separately here. Sekkizhar Peruman, where necessary, brings them together and shows us their actions.

“Similarly, in the Puranam of Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, at this place, that is, where Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman visited Thiru-vizhimizhalai, Sekkizhar Peruman specifically sings about how the Brahmins greeted Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, how Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman entered the sacred temple and worshipped, and how he came out and resided in a sacred matham.

“Thus, after completing their worship, the two great personalities and the devotees resided in different sacred mathams for many days. Sambandha Peruman and Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman stayed in the sacred mathams in Thiru-vizhimizhalai for many days, performing darshan and singing sacred pathigams.

“In addition, other devotees also joined these two great personalities and worshipped the Lord. Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman as ‘Meimai Arunthavargal’ (those who performed true penance). The meaning of this is that just as the Lord’s form is truth, these two great personalities, by constantly clinging to the Lord, became of the very nature of the Lord. The meaning is that they were those who performed rare Shiva pujas that bestow the state of truth.

“Therefore, their sacred words became true sacred words and acted as the Lord’s own sacred words.

“Moreover, the other devotees who had the great fortune of sitting with these two great personalities are also considered worthy devotees who attained liberation. worthy devotees.

“Thus, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman stayed in Thiru-vizhimizhalai for a long time.

“At that time, there was a drought in Thiru-vizhimizhalai. Even the Kaveri, which always flowed without fail, changed its season of water flow. Water is essential for crops and living beings. At a time when water was needed for crops and living beings, the Kaveri did not provide water, and the season changed. The rain also decreased.

“Therefore, food items that depend on water became scarce. Consequently, all living beings that depend on food suffered. Poverty came there. It did not rain, and there was no water in the Kaveri.

“Therefore, paddy crops did not grow, and there was a shortage of food items. All living beings and people suffered. Poverty came, and there was a famine in the world.

“Consequently, the living beings of the world suffered from hunger.

“Thus, the devotees in Thiru-vizhimizhalai also suffered from hunger.

“At that time, Lord Shiva, the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai, appeared in the dreams of both Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman.

“Lord Shiva appeared separately in the dreams of both, with matted red hair, holding a deer and an axe, and blessed them. He said, “Due to this change in time, this period of famine, you will not be disheartened. You will not diminish in your state. Nevertheless, to give to the devotees who worship you, I will give you a gold coin daily.” Thus, Lord Shiva appeared in the dreams of Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and spoke. “When famine and poverty come to the world, and all people suffer from the disease of hunger, they are helpless.” Therefore, Lord Shiva, who appeared in their dreams, said, “Even though you will not suffer from this hunger or famine, to give to those who worship you, I will give you a gold coin.” He blesses, saying, “We are giving.” The implication here is that wealth is acquired only for the purpose of giving to those who need it in a good way.

“Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman were of the nature of those who have renounced everything. They would view running gold and red gold equally. They were of the nature that they desired nothing but to worship with increasing love.

“Therefore, even though they did not need all these things, the Lord, intending to protect the world through them and to manifest the greatness of Lord Shiva’s servitude, appeared in their dreams and blessed them, saying, “Even though you will not suffer from the disease of hunger, take the coin we give and feed the devotees.” It is certain that if the Peruman had not appeared in their dreams and blessed them in this manner, these two great individuals would not have expected coins. “My duty is to sustain my servant, and my duty is to serve and remain.” This is the mindset of the Nayanmars.

“Therefore, it became the Lord’s duty to protect the devotees who worshipped them, as they had completely surrendered themselves to the Lord.
