“Thus, to protect the devotees who worshipped Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, the Lord appeared in the dreams of these two great individuals and promised to give them a coin daily.

“Lord Shiva says, “I will give you a Padikkasu.” ‘Padi’ means a daily prescribed order.

“Therefore, Padikkasu means, “I will give you a coin daily without fail,” says Lord Shiva. To the east and west of the celestial vimanam of Thiru-vizhimizhalai, there are altars. On the altar to the east, the Lord grants one gold coin per day to Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, and on the altar to the west, to Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, as revealed by the Lord in their dreams. There are altars to the east and west of the sacred temple. The eastern altar is directly opposite the Swami Sannidhi.

“There, he grants one coin to Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman. On the western altar, he grants one coin to Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman. The western altar is directly behind the Swami Sannidhi.

“Thus, by the grace of Lord Shiva, a gold coin is received daily at the eastern and western altars. These two great individuals use those gold coins and feed the sacred devotees. They announce twice a day throughout the village, proclaiming, “All who are devotees of Lord Shiva, the primordial God, come and partake of food.” They used the coin granted by the Lord to provide food. Sekkizhar Peruman’s verse at this point is: “The gold coins received by the grace of the Lord of the dark-throated ones, the wealth that increased for many, the devotees of the Lord, all come and eat, thus proclaiming twice a day, they announced and provided food, dispelling poverty.” Sivakavimani says that this verse is of great significance and is recited during blessings during Maheswara Puja. The author notes that this sacred hymn is glorious in that it advises devotees to utilize the wealth bestowed by the Lord for the benefit of other devotees, thereby attaining good fortune. All wealthy devotees should follow this path and attain benefit, writes Sivakavimani.

“Thus, with the sacred coins granted by the Lord, Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman procured all necessary provisions for food, prepared meals, and fed all the devotees of Shiva, thereby alleviating and eradicating poverty. Let us resume our reflection.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 417. Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. When famine struck Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, the Lord granted a sacred coin daily to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman, one at the western and the other at the eastern pedestal. With these, they appeased the hunger of Shiva’s devotees and fed them.

Sekkizhar Peruman then sings: “The Lord of Mizhalai, from the Lord, received the sacred milk from the holy breast of the Daughter of the Himalayas, and as the great son, he received coins with ‘vasi’ (value). Due to his servitude of manual service, Vakkisar received coins without ‘vasi’.” Thus sings Sekkizhar Peruman. To these two great personages, Lord Shiva grants sacred coins daily. The sacred coin bestowed upon Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman at the eastern pedestal was a coin with ‘vasi’ (value). The sacred coin granted by Lord Shiva to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman at the western pedestal was a coin without ‘vasi’. If a coin has ‘vasi’, ‘vasi’ means a circle or mark, so exchanging that coin for food items was somewhat difficult.

Lord Shiva bestows such a coin with ‘vasi’ upon Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman. To Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, however, He grants a coin without ‘vasi’ at the western pedestal.

Therefore, with that coin, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman quickly obtained the necessary food items to feed the devotees in his sacred monastery and serves them food. Sekkizhar Peruman explains here why Lord Shiva gave coins in two different ways to the devotees. Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman is the sacred son of the Lord. Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman partook of the sacred milk from the Divine Mother. By this relationship, he is the son of Lord Shiva. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, however, serves as a devotee to the Lord, as a servant to the Lord.

Therefore, the coin he received, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, is a servant performing manual service to the Lord. Hence, the coin given to him was a coin without ‘vasi’.

The Lord did not give coins for the Nayanmars; He placed coins for the devotees who worship the Nayanmars. He placed coins to alleviate the hunger and suffering of those devotees.

Therefore, even though He placed coins for the devotees who worship the Nayanmars, He gives those coins to the devotees through the Nayanmars.

Thus, the Lord bestows coins in a manner appropriate to these two Nayanmars. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, as Vakkisar, serves the Lord in the capacity of a servant, performing vocal service and manual service. Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman, on the other hand, receives a golden cymbal from the Lord, receives a palanquin, and receives a pearl canopy.

Thus, receiving these, Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman is in a state of performing service without his sacred body experiencing any hardship. As the saying goes, “Labor brings wages,” Lord Shiva gives Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman a coin without ‘vasi’ for the manual service he performs. If Lord Shiva were to give Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman a coin with ‘vasi’, it would imply that the Lord, as a master, is extracting work without providing appropriate wages for the sacred service Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman performs.

Therefore, there is no fault even if the coin given to Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman, who is in the state of a son without physical hardship, has ‘vasi’. However, Lord Shiva thus ordains that a coin without ‘vasi’ must be granted to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who performs sacred service with his body, hands, and voice.

Thus, He gives Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman a coin with ‘vasi’.

Therefore, Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman sang a Thiru-Pathikam, requesting, “Grant me coins without ‘vasi’,” and received coins without ‘vasi’ from Lord Shiva. That sacred history we shall see in the sacred history of Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman.

Thus, as the Lord granted sacred coins daily to these two great personages, they, in their sacred monasteries, fed the devotees.

The devotees rejoiced and found happiness always. This act of placing sacred coins for the Nayanmars is attested as internal evidence in the Thevara Thiru-Pathikams, the sacred utterances of these two great spiritual leaders. The places where Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman resided were called sacred monasteries. These sacred monasteries are now established as separate temples in Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, bearing the names of these two, and worship is conducted there.

Thus, these two great personages have been performing this Shiva-service for a long time. It is mentioned here as “long time,” implying that they must have stayed in Thiru-Vizhimizhalai for at least a year, receiving sacred coins from the Lord, feeding the devotees, and alleviating the hunger caused by the famine. It is understood that during their stay and worship, these two great personages would have composed numerous Thevara Thiru-Pathikams. Among them, fourteen Thiru-Pathikams composed by Aludaiya Pillaiyar, Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman, are now available to us. Eight Thiru-Pathikams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman are available to us.

Thus, for a long time, both performed this sacred service.

After some time, rain fell again, the Kaveri river overflowed, paddy crops grew abundantly, and Thiru-Vizhimizhalai and the world prospered.

Now, in this period, we saw that eight Thiru-Pathikams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman are available to us. We have already reflected on the first Thiru-Pathikam.

Let us reflect on the other seven Thiru-Pathikams. The second Thiru-Pathikam, pertaining to Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, is the sixty-fourth Thiru-Pathikam in the Fourth Thiru-Murai. It is a Thiru-Nerisai Thiru-Pathikam.

“Poothathin padaiyar paambin pooninar poornanoolar Seethaththil pozhindha thingal kozhundhar nanjazhundhu kandar Geethaththil pozhindha osai kelviyar velviyalar Vedaththin porular” Vizhimizhalaiyul vigirthanare. “Kalaiyil kathirsai meni kangulil karuththa kandar Malaiyil mathiyam serntha magudaththar mathuvum paalum Alaiyil paagum pola anniththittiyarkku endrum Velaiyin amuthar Vizhimizhalaiyul vigirthanare.” “Varunthina nerunal endrai vazhangina nalar arkizh Irunthu nan porulgal nalvarkku iyambinar iruvarodum Porunthinar pirinthu thampaal poyyaram avarkkandrum Virunthinar thirunthu Vizhimizhalaiyul vigirthanare.” “Nilaiyila oor moondrondra nerupparikaattambaaga Silaiyu nanathuvu naagam kondavar devar thangal Thalaiyinaal thariththa enpum thalaimayir vadamum poonda Vilaiyilaavedar Vizhimizhalaiyul vigirthanare.” “Maraiyidai porular mottin malar” vazhi vasathenar Karavidai paalin neyyar karumbinil kattiyalar Piraiyidai paambu kondrai pinaiyal ser sadaiyul neerar Viragidai theeyar Vizhimizhalaiyul vigirthanare.“ “Ennagaththillai allar ularallar imavaan petra Pennagaththaraiyar kaatril peruvazhi iruvaraagi Mannagaththaivar neeril nalvar theeyathanil moovar Vinnagaththoruvar Vizhi Mizhalaiyul vigithanare.” “Santhani kongaiyalor panginar samavedar Enthaiyum enthai thanthai thanthaiyumaya eesar Anthiyodu udai anthanalar an neyyal vetkum venthazhal oruvar Vizhimizhalaiyul vigirthanare.” “Neetrinai niraiya poosi nitthal ayiram pookkondu Etruli orunaal ondru kuraiya kan niraiyavitta Aattralukku aazhi nalki avan konarnthu izhichchum koyil” Veetrirunthu alippar Vizhimizhalaiyul vigithanare.” “Siththi seybavarkkellaam servidam sendru kooda Paththi seybavargal paavam paraippavar irappilalar Mutthisai pavalameeni muthiroli neelakandar Vitthinil mulaiyar Vizhimizhalaiyul vigirthanare.” “Tharukkina arakkan therur sarathi thadainilathu Poruppinai eduththa thozhum ponmudi patthum punnay Nerippu unda angu alari meendu ninainthu adiparava tham vazh Viruppodungoduppar Vizhimizhalaiyul vigirthanare.”

Now, the third Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Vizhimizhalai is the ninety-fifth Thiru-Pathikam in the Fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Viruttha Thiru-Pathikam.

“Vaan sottachchotta nindrattum valarmathiyodaye Then sottachchotta nindrattum thirukkondrai sennivai theer maanpettai” nokki manaleer mani neer mizhalai ullir naan satta ummai marakkinum ennai kurikkonmine.“ “Anthamum aathiyum aagi nindru eerandam en thisaiyum Panthamum veedum parappukkinreer pasu etrukkanthir venthazhal ompu mizhalai ullir ennai thenthisaikke unthidum pothu marakkinum ennai kurikkonmine.” “Alaikkindra neer nilam kaatranal ambaramaagi nindreer Kalaikkandru serum karaththir kalaipporulaagi nindreer Vilakkinri nalkum mizhalaiyullir meyyil kaiyodu kaalkulaikkinru nummai marakkinum ennai kurikkonmine.” “Theeththozhilaan thalai theeyilittu seytha velvi setreer Peythozhilattiyai petrudaiyeer pidiththu thiriyum veyth thozhilalar mizhalaiyullir vikki anjaliththum otthozhinthu um” marakkinum ennai kurikkonmine.” “Thotpatta naagamum soolamum sutriyum putthimaiyan Merpatta anthanar veezhiyum ennaiyum verudaiyeer Natpatta vanthu piranthen irakka naman thamartham Kotpatttu nummai marakkinum ennai kuri konmine.” “Kandiyil patta kazhuththudaiyeer karikattilitta Pandiya parikalaththir pathiveezhik kondir Undiyar pattini noyill urakkaththil ummai avar Kondiyil pattu marakkinum ennai kuri konmine.” “Thotramkandan siramonru kondir thuyavellarithu ondru Etram kondir ezhil veezhi mizhalai irukkai kondir Seetram kondinmel sivanthatthor paasaththaal veesiya vengootram kandu ummai marakkinum ennai kurikkonmine.” “Suzhipatta gangaiyum thingalum soodi sokkam payintrir” Pazhipatta paambarai pattrudaiyeer padar theepparuga Vizhipatta kaamanai vitteer mizhalaiyullir piravi chollipattu nummai marakkinum ennai kurikkonmine.“ “Pillaiyirpatta pirai mudiyir maraiyothavalleer Vellaiyirpatthatthor neetrir virineer mizhalaiyullir Nallaiyirpattaivar nakkarai pikka naman thamar thang Kollaiyil pattu marakkinum ennai kurikkolmine.” “Karukkontharakkan kaiyilayai pattriya kaiyum meyyum Nerukkendrirachcha sevadiyal kootrai neeru seytheer Veri kondrai malai mudiyir virineer mizhalaiyullir Irakkinru nummai marakkinum ennai kurikkolmine.”

Now, the fourth Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar for Thiru-Vizhimizhalai is the twelfth Thiru-Pathikam in the Fifth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam.

Sambalam karainthu kaithozhuvaraiyum kaathalan Varainthu vaithozhuvaraiyum vaadalan niranthapaaridaththodavar Nitthalam virainthu povathum Vizhimizhalaiyeke.” “Etruvelkodi eesan than aathirai naatram Sooduvar nannarunthingalar neetruchchanthana vellai viravalar Vetru kolamkol Vizhimizhalaiye.” “Punaippor soolaththan porvidaiyoorthiyan vinaivel naagaththin venmazhu vazhinan Ninaiya nindravan eesanaiye enna vinaiyilar thozhum Vizhimizhalaiye.” “Maadaththaadu manaththudan vaiththavar kodaththar kurukketthiraththar palar Paadaththar pazhippar pazhippallaththor vedaththar thozhum Vizhimizhalaiye.” “Eduththa velkodi erudaiyan thamar udupparkovanam unpathu pichchaiye Keduppathavathu keezh nindra valvinai viduththu povathu Vizhimizhalaiyeke.” Kuzhalaiyazh mozhiyar isai vetkaiyal uzhalaiyakkaiyai oonum unarvileer Thalalai neermadi kollan min satrinom mizhalaiyan adi saara vinnazhvare.“ “Theeran thee thiralan sadai thangiya neeran aadiya neetran vanthar kondrai Tharan malaiyan thannarunkanniyan veeran Vizhimizhalai vigirthane.” “Eriyinar iraiyar idukattidai nariyinar pariya magizhkindrathor Periyanar tham pirappodu saathalai viriyinar thozhum Vizhimizhalaiye.” “Neenda soozh sadai melor nilamathi kaandusevadi melor kanai kazhal Venduvavar avar veethi pugunthilar meendum povathu Vizhimizhalaiyeke.” “Paalai yazhodu sevazhi pankola malai vanavar vanthu vazhipadum alaiyarazhal antha” Ahuthi velaiyar thozhum Vezhi Mizhalaiye.” “Mazhalai etru manalan thirumalai suzhala aarthethutthan mudi tholira Kazhalgol kaalin thiruviral oondralum mizhalaiyanadi vazhkana vittathe.”

Let us continue to reflect on the other Thiru-Pathikams pertaining to Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 418. Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Among the eight Thiru-Pathikams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, the fifth Thiru-Pathikam begins with “En ponne em imaiyor thozhu paingazhal.” It is a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam, the thirteenth Thiru-Pathikam in the Fifth Thiru-Murai.

“En ponne imaiyor thozhu paingazhal Nanponne nalan theengarri ondrillen Semponne Thiru-Velimizhalaiyul Anbane adiyenai kurikkole.” “Kanninaal kali koora kaiyaal thozhuthu Ennumaaru ariyathu izhaippen thannai Vinnullor thozhum Vizhimizhalaiyul Annale adiyenai kurikkole.” “Nalame visumbe” nalan theemaiye Kalame karutthe karutthaal thozhum seelame Thiru-Vizhimizhalaiyul Kolame adiyenai kurikkole.“ “Mutthane muthalva mugizhum mulai Otthane oruva uruvaagiya Siththane Thiru-Vizhimizhalaiyul Atthanae adiyenai kurikkole.” “Karuvane karuvaayth thelivaarkkellaam Oruvane uyirppaay unarvaay nindra Thiruvane Thiru-Vizhimizhalaiyul Guruvane adiyenai kurikkole.” “Kaaththane pozhil ezhaaiyum kaathalaal Aaththane amararkku ayanthan thalai Serththane Thiru-Vizhimizhalaiyul Kooththane adiyenai kurikkole.” “Neethivaanavar nitthal niyamam seyth Othivaanarum unaraathathor Vedhiyaa vithithaa Thiru-Vizhiyul Aathiye adiyenai kurikkole.” Pazhagi ninnadi soodiya paalanai Kazhagin mel vaiththa kaalanai saadiya Azhagane ani Vizhimizhalaiyul Kuzhagane adiyenai kurikkole.” “Andavaanavar koodik kadaintha nanj Undavaanavane unarvondrilen Vindavaan pozhil Vizhimizhalaiyul Kondane adiyenai kurikkole.” “Orutthan ongalai thaangalutran uram Varutthinaay vanjanen manam manniya Thirutthanae Thiru-Vizhimizhalaiyul Arutthanae adiyenai kurikkole.”

Now, the sixth Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Vizhimizhalai is a Thiru-Thandaka Thiru-Pathikam, the fifty-first Thiru-Pathikam in the Sixth Thiru-Murai.

“Kayilaya malaivullar karonaththar kanthamathanaththular kalaththiyar Mayiladu thuraiyullar” Magalaththar vakkaraiyar sakkaram maarkku eenthar vaayntha ayilvaay soolamum kapaalamum amarum thirukkaraththar aaneru eri veyilaya sothi vilangu neetrar Vizhimizhalaiye mevinare.“ “Poothiyani ponniraththar poonanoolar pongaravar sankarar venkuzhaiyor kaathar kethichcharam mevinar kedaraththar kedila vada athigai veerattaththar maathuyaram theerththu ennai uyya kondar mazhapaadimeya mazhuvaazhanar vedikudiyullar meeyachchurar Vizhimizhalaiye mevinare.” “Annamalaiye amarnthar arur ullar alappoorar anthanargal maadakkoyil unnaligaiyar umayalodum imaiyor perumanar otriyurar pennakadaththu perunthunganai maadaththar koodaththar” Peravurar vinnorgalellaam virumbiyeththa Vizhimizhalaiye mevinare.” “Venkatthar sengattangudiyar venni nannagarar vetkalaththar vedanavar pankattum vandar pazhanaththullar parayththuraiyar sirappalliyullar pandor venkottuk karungazhitrai pizhapattri uriththu urivai porththa vidalai vedam vinkattum pirainuthali anja katti Vizhimizhalaiye mevinare.” “Pudaichoozhndha poothangal vedampaada puliyur sittrambalaththai nadamaaduvar udaichoozhndha puliththozhar kalikachchi mel thazhiyullar kulirsolai ekampaththar kadaisoozhndhu palitherum kankalanar kazhumalaththar sezhimalaththar kuzhaliyooodum vidaichoozhndha velkodiyar malku selva Vizhimizhalaiye mevinare perum puliyur virumbi” The Perumpazhiyar, the Perumparra Puliyur Mulattanattar, the Irumbuthalar, the Irumbuli Yerar, the Innambarar, the Ingoymalaiyar, the sweet-worded Karumbanaiyal with Uma, the Karugavoorar, the Karuppariyalurar, the Karaveerattar, the beloved immortals, day and night, praised and worshipped at Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. The Maraikattar, the Valivalattar, the Vaimur Meyar, the Valkozhi Putturar, the Magazhattar, the Karai Kattu Kandanaar, the Kapaliyar, the Karkudiyar, the Virkudiyar, the Kaanapperar, the Parai Kattu Kuzhi Vizhiya Pal Peychuzha Pazhaiyanur Alangattu Adigal, who once showed fear, the cruel Yama, fled.

They worshipped at Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. The Anjai Kalaththullar, the Aiyarrullar, the Arurar. The Perurars, the Azhundur Ullar, the Thanjai Thali Kuluththar, the Thakkalurars, the Santhai Ayavanthi Thanginar Tham, the Nanjai Thamakk Amudavunda Nambar, the Nageshwaraththullar, the Naraiyurars, who rescued me from the prison of harsh words, worshipped at Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. The Kondal Ullar, the Kondichcharaththinnullar, the Kovalur Veerattam Koyil Kondar, the Thandalaiyar, the Thalaiyalangattu Ullar, the Thalaichchangai Perungoyil Thanginar Tham, the Vandalodu Manarkonarum Ponni Nannir Valanjoliyar, the Vaigalin Men Madaththullar, the Venthalai Man Kai Konda Vigithavedar, worshipped at Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. The Harichchandraththullar, the Ambarullar, who are rare even to Hari, Brahma, and Indra, the Purichchandraththullar, the Bogaththullar, who with the daughter of Porupparaiyan, became desirous, and the fire. The Sandhi Vetk Idaththar, the Emakkudaththar, the Padaththen Isaiyar Keethar, the Virichchangai Erik Kondu Ang Aadum Vedhar, worshipped at Thiru-Veezhimizhalai.

The Punkurar, the Purambayaththar, the Putturullar, the Poovanaththar, the Pulivalaththar, who, thinking of his great strength, tried to lift the mountain, whose heads and shoulders were lowered, and who, with a finger, pressed down the golden mountain-like ocean, and then graciously released it, the Vananathar with lightning-like matted locks, the rider of the bull, worshipped at Thiru-Veezhimizhalai.

Now, the seventh Thiru-Pathigam, the fifty-second Thiru-Pathigam of the sixth Thiru-Murai, the Thiru-Thandaga Thiru-Pathigam, composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Veezhimizhalai.

Kannavan Kan Kan Kannozhiseyr Kaatchiyan Kan Kanthiruvum Paattisai. He is the one who shows the melody, He is the essence of those melodies, He is the fruit that ripens and yields taste. He is the king, He is the fire, He is the water. He is the one who comes to destroy, He is the one who resides in the sky with rain clouds, He is superior to the celestials, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is the one whose name is sweet like the juice of sugarcane, He is the one who resides in the minds of devotees of good conduct, He is the one who burned the three cities with His bow.

He is the one who bathed in milk, curd, and pure ghee, He is the hunter of the Pandaranga, He is the one who seeks alms, He is the one who swallowed the poison of the ocean, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is the one who is both gentle and fierce, He is the one who bestowed the discus upon Pushpaka, He is the one with the eye. He is the Kapali with three eyes, He is the one whose eye burned Kama’s body. He is the one who removed countless sins and enslaved me, He is the one who appeared as fire to the two. He is the one who is worshipped by the celestials, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is the one with the conch earring, He is the one whose form is like a golden mountain.

He is the one who tested the great penance of the goddess, He is the one adorned with the white tusk of a wild boar. He is the primordial one, He is beyond the universe, He is the one who made the five-headed serpent His ornament. He is the Vedic scholar, He is the one who showed the Vedic rituals, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is the one who bathed in ghee, milk, and tender coconut water, He is the one who stands as the eternal bridegroom. He is the one who holds the axe, the deer, and the spear in His hand. He is the one who kicked Yama to death.

He is the one whose sacred body is adorned with white ash, He is the one who placed the white moon on His red matted locks. He is the one who played with fierce fire, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is the one who, when the dark-eyed Vishnu sought the discus, plucked out His eye and offered it, and was graciously seen. He is the great Lord who holds the honey-laden Konrai, Vanni, and Datura flowers, and the celestial Ganga in His matted locks. He is the one who has the ancient-tongued goddess as His half, He is the Supreme Being, He is the one who became the Supreme Lord. He is the one who placed the white moon and the serpent on His red matted locks, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai.

He is the compassionate one who bestowed the discus upon the dark Vishnu, who tore apart the stone-like Salandhara. He is the one who tested the path of the victorious Arjuna, He is the hunter. He showed the battle. He is the Supreme Being, He is the Sadasiva, He is the one without equals. He is the beloved of the mountain king’s daughter, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is the true ascetic, He is the one who is truthful to those who stand in true penance, He is the one who is always false to those with a mind full of desires.

He is the one who made the Buddha’s forgotten and burning ashes into fresh flowers. He is the one who saves, He is the one who makes those who contemplate on the highest path, and all the worlds, shine and be saved. He is the wise one, He is the one whom the wise desire and praise, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is the one who weakened the moon with His sacred foot, He is the one who, angered by Daksha, took his head. He is the one who broke Indra’s shoulders and then blessed him, He is the Lord. He is the beloved, He is the one who became all thoughts, mantras, and secret meanings.

He is the one who rose as a bright flame of white fire, whose top and bottom were unknown to Vishnu and Brahma. He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is the one who resides in the cremation ground, He is our Lord, He is the one who wore the skin of the wild elephant. He is the one who stood as one with the daughter of the great mountain king, He is the Omkara. He is the one adorned with the garland of Kongu flowers and Konrai, He is the one who hoisted the bull on His banner. He is the one whose upper garment is the skin of a striped tiger, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai.

Now, the eighth Thiru-Pathigam, the fifty-third Thiru-Pathigam of the sixth Thiru-Murai, the Thiru-Thandaga Thiru-Pathigam, composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar for Thiru-Veezhimizhalai.

The one with the deer in His hand. He is like the giver of boons, He is like the one who bent the great mountain as a bow. He is like the one who flayed the elephant when it roared, He is like the one who holds the skull and drum. He is like the one adorned with the honey-laden Thiru-Idazhi, He is like the Lord residing in Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is like the beautiful one who rides the bull, He is the Lord who owns me, His servant.

He is like the one who, when the fierce Salandhara sought battle, tore him with the discus. He is like the Lord who once cut off Yama’s leg, He is like the one who embraced Narayana on His left side. He is like the one who has Kumaran as His son, He is like the beautiful one residing in cool Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is like the one who drank poison for the sake of the immortals, He is the Lord who owns me, His servant. He is like the pure one whose sacred body is adorned with water, He is like the one who blessed the great Vishnu with the discus. He is like our Lord with the beautiful banner, He is like the one whose arrow burned the three cities.

He is like the one who created the beautiful hunter. He is like the one who resides in the vast Thiru-Veezhimizhalai as the giver. He is like the beautiful one with the garlanded matted crown, He is the Lord who owns me, His servant. He is like the one who created the elephant-faced one, He is like the one who had Gayasura killed by him. He is like the one who once destroyed Daksha’s sacrifice, He is like the one who destroyed one of Brahma’s heads. He is like the one who cut off the head of the true sacrifice, He is like the one who made the vast Thiru-Veezhimizhalai His abode.

He is like the one who became the five sacrifices, He is the Lord who owns me, His servant. He is like the one who wears a loincloth, He is like the pure one who is the three lights and the flame. He is like the pure one with a golden body, He is like the one who comes surrounded by the host of Bhootas. He is like the one with lightning-like red matted locks and a white crescent moon, He is the pure one residing in the vast Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is like the Lord whose feet are worshipped by Brahma on the swan, He is the Lord who owns me, His servant. He is like the giver of boons, unknown even to Vishnu, He is like the one who can sever the cycle of birth for those who do not forget Him.

He is like the Lord of the ancient Vedas, He is like the Lord of the five letters. He is like the one who once created the powerful Viyari, He is like the giver residing in the vast Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is like the one who suppressed and destroyed the poison in His throat, He is the Lord who owns me, His servant. He is like the one with the soft finger of cotton, He is like the Supreme Being who tied the serpent around His waist. He is like the blue-throated one adorned with clouds, He is like the Lord of the northern Kailash mountain. He is like the one who adorned His red matted locks with a white crescent moon, He is like Lord Shiva residing in Thiru-Veezhimizhalai.

He is like the one who is close to devotees who control their five senses, He is the Lord who owns me, His servant. He is like the one who enslaved Kundaru and Prithanai, He is like the one who made Kudamookku His abode. He is like the one whose throne is a fresh lotus flower, He is like the one who killed the wicked king. He is like the one who killed and then restored life. He is like the giver who received alms in a white skull, He is like the Lord of the vast city of Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is like the one who is beyond the universe, He is the Lord who owns me, His servant.

He is like the one with a pearl-like budding smile, He is like the one whose matted locks are like a coral creeper. He is like the one who is sweet to those who show any devotion, He is like the one who became the eight forms. He is like the beloved of Mitra and Vajra, He is like the giver residing in the vast Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is like the one who became both father and mother, He is the Lord who owns me, His servant. He is like the one who flayed the elephant and made Uma tremble, He is like the one who held the Ganga in His red matted locks. He is like the Lord who held the burning axe in His hand, He is like the one who wore the tusk of a boar.

He is like the one who once angered the two suns, He is the pure one residing in the vast Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is like the one who destroyed when Hari and Brahma praised Him. He is like the one who, when the one who lifted Kailash mountain cried out, pressed him down with His toe and blessed him. He is like the beautiful one who can dance when looked at with soft words like a cuckoo. He is like the one who became the lamp of the sun-like light, He is the giver residing in the vast Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is like the one who wields the sharp trident, He is the Lord who owns me, His servant.

Thus, we have contemplated the eight Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. We shall continue our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 419, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We have seen the sacred deeds performed by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar at Thiru-Veezhimizhalai.

There, we contemplated the eight Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman.

Thus, these two great saints, after worshipping the Lord at Thiru-Veezhimizhalai and singing Thiru-Pathigams, developed a desire to visit other sacred places where the Lord resides. They worshipped Lord Shiva, the great jewel of Thiru-Veezhimizhalai, took leave from the Lord, and departed from there to continue their pilgrimage. These two great saints, having departed from Thiru-Veezhimizhalai, reached Thiru-Vanchiyam and worshipped the Lord there. And Lord Shiva. They visit and worship other sacred places where the Lord resides.

There, they compose Thiru-Pathigams as garlands of Tamil. The Peruman states that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman departed from Thiru-Vanchiyam, visited many sacred places, and reached Thiru-Maraikkadu, also known as Vedaranyam. They visited many sacred places in between and sang Thevaram Thiru-Pathigams.

Therefore, the many sacred places in between Thiru-Vanchiyam that these two great saints visited include Thiru-Thalaiyalangadu, Thiru-Peruvelur, Thiru-Chaththangudi, Thiru-Karaveeram, Thiru-Vilamar, Thiru-Arur, Thiru-Karayil, Thiru-Thevur, Thiru-Nellikka, Thiru-Kaichchinam, Thiru-Thengur, Thiru-Kollikkadu. Pottur, Thiru-Ven Thurai, and many other sacred places exist. Sekkizhar Peruman mentions in the Puranam of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman that Thiru-Thandalai Nizhneri, Thiru-Kalaru, and other sacred places were also visited. Although many such places were visited, the Thiru-Pathigams sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for these places are not available to us due to our lack of merit. Among these, the Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Peruman for Thiru-Thalaiyalangadu and Thiru-Peruvelur are not available.

Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman, without elaborating on these places, generally states that they visited many places and composed garlands of Tamil, thus implicitly referring to these.

Therefore, let us briefly contemplate the Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Thalaiyalangadu and Thiru-Peruvelur among these sacred places, and the special features of these places.

First, the sacred place Thiru-Thalaiyalangadu is the ninety-third sacred place on the south bank of the Kaveri. The history of this place is that Lord Shiva danced on Muyalagan, who was sent by the sage Tharuka. The Lord’s sacred name here is Nataneswarar, Adal Vallanathar. The Mother’s sacred name is Thirumadanthai Balambigai. The sacred tree is the Jackfruit tree and the Banyan tree. The sacred water is the Shankhu Theertham and the Kaduvai River.

In the Sangam period, this village was known as Thalaiyalanganam. This is the place where Lord Shiva subdued Muyalagan, who was sent by the Rishis of Tharukavanam, who, filled with arrogance, performed an Abhichara Yagna, and Lord Shiva danced on him. This is the place where he danced on him.

Therefore, the Lord is known by the sacred names Narthanapurishwarar and Adalvallanathar. In the Kritha Yuga, Sage Kapila came here, performed puja, and received the Chintamani on the Thai Amavasya day. This is the place where the Lord appeared as a Jyotirlingam to Goddess Saraswati and blessed her. It is still the unwavering belief of the people that by bathing in the tank in front of the temple and offering lamps to the Lord with determination, one can be cured of leprosy. Every year, during the last two days of the Panguni month and the first two days of the Chithirai month, at sunrise, when the sun’s rays fall on the Lord, a Surya Puja is performed. The Bhairava here is a very powerful deity who resolves intractable enmities and problems.

There are also inscriptions in this temple. On the occasion of Thai Amavasya. For two days, the Lord’s procession takes place, and the Theerthavari is performed in the Shankhu Theertham. One can reach the temple by going near Thalaiyalangadu on the Thiruvarur-Kumbakonam road. These are the special features of the sacred place Thiru-Thalaiyalangadu.

Here, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman came and composed a Thiru-Pathigam. This is a Thiru-Thandaga Thiru-Pathigam. It is compiled as the seventy-ninth Thiru-Pathigam in the sixth Thiru-Murai.

Thondarkku Thooneriyay Ninran Thannai Soozhnarakil Vizhame Kappan Thannai Andaththukku Appalaikku Appalanai Athirai Nal Athariththa Amman Thannai Mundaththin Mulaiththozhundha Thiyayanai Muruvaththu Oruruvay Muthalay Ninra Thandaththil Thalaiyalangadan Thannai Sarathe Sala Nal Pokkinene Akkirantha. He is the one who is the Lord of the chamber, He is the one who burned the three cities of the Asuras in an instant. He is our dancer with the crown adorned with a cuckoo, He is the one with the earring in His ear, He is the pure one who entered the minds of those who waver and does not leave. He is the virtuous one, He is the one who is all the immeasurable joys, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu who remained. I have wasted many days without seeking Him.

He is the true ascetic, the Veda, the essence of the Veda, the one who wears the bright young moon, the giver. He is the one who gave me the axe, the poor one, He is the one who lifted me up from the ocean of suffering. He is the one who stands in the path unknown to false ascetics, He is the one who, with the water, stands as one half with Uma, He is the essence, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu. I have wasted many days without seeking Him. He is Shiva, He is Brahma, He is Vishnu, He is the bright light, He is fire, He is water. He is the world, He is all the worlds, He is gold, He is jewel, He is pearl.

He is the wind, He is all the winds, He is the one who wanders as a cow, He is the one who stands as a wind. He is the ascetic, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu. I have wasted many days without seeking Him. He is the one who held the Ganga and the fierce water, He is the Lord of Kanchi, the one who broke Kama. He is the one who holds a deer in His hand, He is the Lord of Aiyaru, He is the Lord of Arur. He is the one who is compassionate to His faultless devotees, He is the Lord of Parithiniyamam, He is the Lord of Pasur.

He is Shankara, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu. I have wasted many days without seeking Him. He is the one who tied the poison on the serpent, He is the one whose measure is unknown even to the celestials. He is the one who makes those who seek Him rule the celestial world, He is the golden one, the one who fought the elephant. He is the one who placed the flowing water and the living serpent and the moon on the matted locks of the one with the goddess as half, He is the great ocean, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu. I have wasted.

I have wasted many days. He is the one who rides the bull and collects alms from every house, He is the Lord of Veerattam, He is the one with white ash. He is the one who dances in the foul-smelling cremation ground, He is the one who is before, He is the one who is after, He is the one who is that day. He is the one who delights in wearing the skin of an animal as His garment, He is the one who has Uma as His half. He is the one with matted locks, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu. I have wasted many days without seeking Him.

He is the sugarcane, the lump of sugar, the fruit, the honey, the calf, the middle pillar, the black one. He is the one who holds the three-pronged spear of iron, He is the one who is eight, He is the one who is ten, He is the one who protects. He is the one who wears the Konrai flowers where bees hum, He is the pure one, He is the mother, He is the one who gives all things to the world, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu. I have wasted many days without seeking Him. He is the sound of the ancient string, the fruit, the milk, the fruit of the milk, the fierce void, the fire, the wind. He is the one who is easy for those who rejoice at the sight, He is the cause, He is Narayana, He is the one on the lotus.

He is the one who, when contemplated. He is our Lord who resides in my heart, He is the one who cherishes the skin of the wild elephant, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu. I have wasted many days without seeking Him. He is the one who, when the twenty-armed Rakshasa king, without considering Kailash mountain, lifted it, and his pearl-like crowns shook and his bracelets struck, and he hastened, and He placed one sacred toe on him, and heard his song from his ten mouths, and out of compassion, bestowed upon him the name Ravana. He is the essence, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu. I have wasted many days without seeking Him.

This is the Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman at Thiru-Thalaiyalangadu. Next to Thiru-Thalaiyalangadu, we have also received a Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman after visiting Thiru-Peruvelur. Thiru-Peruvelur is the ninety-second sacred place on the south bank of the Kaveri. It is currently known as Manakkal Aiyan. Pettai.

The Lord’s name is Piriyathanathar, Abhimuktheeswarar, Piriyayeeswarar. The Goddess’s sacred name is Abhinambigai, Yelavar Kuzhali. The sacred tree is the Vanni tree. The sacred water is Saravanappoigai. It is the ninety-second sacred place on the south bank of the Kaveri. In old texts, this place is referred to as Kattur Aiyampettai.

It is said that this place is called Velur because Murugan worshipped here, and Peruvelur because Peruvel, a great hunter, lived here. It is said that this is one of the Kailash peaks that fell during the competition between Vayu and Adisesha. This is the place where Vishnu, in the form of Mohini, after fulfilling the purpose of His avatar, worshipped the Lord here and regained His male form. This sacred place is a Madakoyil, built by Kochchengan Chozha Nayanar. The Moolavar (presiding deity) is a Swayambhu Murthi (self-manifested idol) with a square Avudaiyar (pedestal). One Thiru-pathikam (hymn) by Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and one by Appar Swamigal are available for this Thiru-sthalam.

The Thiru-pathikam by Appar Swamigal is compiled as the sixty-sixth Thiru-pathikam in the Fourth Thiru-murai, a Thiru-nerisai Thiru-pathikam.

“Maranai nava nava marappilar manathullaanai Karaiyani kandanthannai kanalerri aadinanai Piraiyani sadaiyinanai Peruveloor peninanai Naraiyani malargal thoovi nalthorum vananguvene Nadhanai ulagamellam nambiran enavum nindra Padhanai paramayogi pala pala thiraththinallum Pedhanai thondrinanai Peruveloor peninanai Odha navudaiyanagi uraikkumaru uraikkindrene Kuravithol manandha selva Kumaravel” “Thathaiyendru naravizha naru menkoondhal nangaiyor bhagathaanai Piraviyai maatruvaanai Peruveloor peninanai Uravinaal vallanagi unarumaru unarththuvene Maingavil kandanthannai valangaiyin mazhu ondru endhi Kaingavil maninodum kanalerri aadinanai Pingagan thannai andhan Peruveloor peninanai Poignaga ninaiyamatta poriyilaa arivilene Odaiser netriyanaai urivaiyai moodinanai Veedadhe kattuvaanai Vedha nangu aayinanai Pedaiser puravaneenga Peruveloor peninanai Koodanan vallamattrang kurugumaar arugilene Kachchai sernagathaanai kadal vidam kandathaanai Kachchiye kamban thannai kanalerri aaduvaanai Pichchai serndhuzhalvinanai Peruveloor peninanai Ichchai serndhu amaranana” “Irainjumaru irainjuvene Siththarai vandhu thannai Thiruvadi vananguvargal Mutthanai moorthiyay mudhalvanai muzhudhumay Pitthanai pirarum etha Peruveloor peninanai Meththane avanai nallum virumbumaru arugilene Mundame thanginanai mutriya gnanathaanai Vandulang kondrai malai valarmathi kanniyanai Pindame aayinanai Peruveloor peninanai Andamaam adhiyanai ariyumaru arugilene Virivilaa arivinargal veroru samayam seidhu Erivinar sonnarenum embirarkku etradhagum Paruvinaal periyor etthum Peruveloor patrinanai Marivinan vazhththivuyyum vagaiyadhu ninaikkindrene Perukkadal ilangai mannan udal keda poruththi nalla Karugiya kandathaanai kadhirilankozhundhu soodum Perugiya sadaiyinanai Peruveloor peninanai Urugiya adiyar etthum ullaththa” “Thaal ulguvene Thiruchitrambalam” Thus, after visiting many sthalams, Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-navukkarasu Swamigal arrive at the sthalam known as Thiru-maraikkadu, or Vedaranyam.

Our contemplation of this shall continue. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 420, Thiru-nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-navukkarasu Swamigal and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman arrive at the sthalam known as Vedaranyam, which is called Thiru-maraikkadu in Tamil.

Here, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman sings a pathikam and opens the sacred doors that were worshipped and sealed by the Vedas. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman then sings a pathikam and causes the opened doors to be sealed again. Vedaranyam is the sthalam where this wondrous sacred history unfolded. Before contemplating this sacred history, let us briefly consider the sthala puranam (legend of the place) and special features of Vedaranyam. This Thiru-sthalam, Vedaranyam, is located on the south bank of the Kaveri. It is the one hundred and twenty-fifth sthalam.

This Thiru-sthalam is situated on the seashore. This Thiru-sthalam, Vedaranyam, possesses unique greatness due to its natural and man-made features, including the sea, sand dunes, forests, temples, and gopurams. One can reach this Thiru-sthalam from cities such as Mayuram, Kumbakonam, and Nagapattinam. The land is good, sandy soil. It is a sthalam surrounded on all four sides by screwpine hedges, water-thorn forests, small reservoirs, and salt marshes. This sthalam is located in the Neythal region, which is a coastal area.

In the Thiru-murais, it is referred to as Maraivanam, Maraikkadu, Vedavanam, and Vedaranyam. In the Puranas, it is called Vedavanam and Satyagiri. This sthalam also bears the sacred name Adisethu. It is commonly known as Vedaranyam. In inscriptions, this sthalam is referred to as Thiru-maraikkadu in Umbalanadu, Kunnoornadu. All these names are based on the history of the Vedas worshipping the Lord here.

Satyagiri means an imperishable mountain. This is the name of the sand hill at Kodiakkarai. History states that there was once a mountain here, from which a river called Satya Nadi originated and merged with the sea, and later merged with the Veda Nadi. It is called Adisethu because it was here that Adi Rama first built a bridge to go to Lanka. This sthalam is also known as Then Kailayam and Dakshina Kailasam. This Thiru-sthalam is one of the Sapta Vidanga sthalams.

Therefore, it is structured like the Thiru-varur Poongoyil. It has an east-facing sanctum. Inside the temple, there are two circumambulatory paths (prakarams), and adjacent to the temple wall is a matha complex, beyond which are streets for chariots on all four sides. The Rajagopuram (main tower) on the east has five tiers and nine kalasams (finials) at the top. Adjacent to the gopuram, in the southeast corner, is the Manikkarnikai Theertham (sacred pond) inside. There are the Navakannikai Mandapam, Viswamithra well, Madappalli (kitchen), and Nandavanam (flower garden).

On the upper side, there are Shiva Linga temples established and worshipped by the Pandiyas, the Melagopuram (upper tower), and adjacent to it, the Brahmagathi Medai and the shrines of Veeragathi Vinayagar and Melakumarar. On the north side, at the head of the prakaram, the Amman (Goddess) temple stands separately. Inside the Amman temple, in the prakaram, there are temples for Vinayagar in the Kanni Moolai and Kumarar in the Vayu Moolai. Temples are located. To the north of the Vedavaneswarar temple, there are the Kasi Viswanathar shrine, a sixteen-pillared mandapam, a swing mandapam, and yagasalas (sacrificial halls). In the inner prakaram, Sundarar, Pichadanar, and Ardhanareeswarar are enshrined respectively.

There are also the sixty-three Nayanmar idols and their processional idols, Kanni Vinayagar, Vedavana Pillaiyar, Murugan, Lakshmi, Saneesar, Saraswati, Annapoorani, Durga, and other shrines. This place is one of the Kozhili sthalams, so the Navagrahas (nine planets) are arranged in a row without being in retrograde motion. In the central mandapam, Tyagarajar, Vedaranyeswarar, and other deities are enshrined. Behind the Moolattanam (main sanctum) of Udayar, Uma Maheswar appears in a bridal form. Annually, on the Saptami day of the Purvapaksha in the month of Chithirai, sandalwood paste is applied to the bridal deity. It is applied.

The sthala Vinayagar here is Veeragathi Pillaiyar. He got this name because he removed the sin of Veeragathi that followed Rama. The Kshetra Kovai Pillai Tamil states this as “Veeragathi Theertharul seyyum Vinayagan, Thiru-maraikkattinil Ramar pinne thodarnthu varum.” He is located in the outer prakaram opposite the Melagopuram. In this Thiru-koyil, the Moolavar is Vedaranyeswarar, a Shiva Linga form.

The Lord has sacred names such as Vedanayagar, Vedavaneswarar, and Maraikkattisar. The Thiru-murais and Puranas have worshipped the Lord. Inscriptions refer to the Lord by the names Vedavanamudaiya Nayagar and Vedavanamudaiyar. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman has sung, “Vedangal potri malaraal vazhipadu sey Ma Maraikkadar.” Behind Vedavaneswarar in the Moolasthanam, the enshrined Lord is Maraikkattu Uraiyum Manalar, the Lord who appeared in a bridal form as Ammaiyappar to Agastya. Appar Swamigal has sung, “Malaiyartham magalodum Madhevan serum Maraikkadu.” The sacred name of the Goddess in this sthalam is Veenavatha Vidushini. This is a Sanskrit name.

In Tamil, the Thiru-murais refer to the Mother’s sacred name as “Yaazhai pazhitha mozhi Umaiyal.” Sundaramoorthy Swamigal has sung, “Yaazhai pazhithathanna mozhi mangaiyodu pangan.” Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman has sung about the Mother as “Pannin ner mozhiyal.” Next, the Tyagarajar here is one of the Tyagamurthis bestowed by Indra to Musukunda Chakravarthi. The dance he performs here is called Hamsa Natanam. Hamsa Natanam means a dance where one moves slowly, taking steps like a swan. It is a dance that moves slowly, taking steps like a swan. Next is Bhuvani Vidangar, an emerald Shiva Linga form enshrined in a casket within the Tyagaraja shrine. This deity is bathed twice daily.

This idol is made of green gemstone. Next is Durga, a highly worshipped deity here. She is enshrined in the first prakaram of the Lord’s temple, facing south on the north side. Durga serves as the family deity for many. Next is the Nataraja idol in the Thiru-koyil. The Vedaranyam Sthala Puranam states that this deity is one of the eighteen dances.

Next is Kaatchi Koduthavar (the one who gave darshan). This is a processional idol. This deity is named Rishabantaka Murthi, one of the twenty-five Maheswara forms. One cannot help but be captivated by the beauty of this form, with a smile, the right hand resting on the head of the bull, and the left hand on the thigh. No one’s heart can remain untouched by the beauty upon seeing this form. The next deity is Chandrasekhara Murthi.

This is also a Utsava Thiru-meni (processional idol). During festivals, on days when Tyagesar does not go out, it is customary to crown this deity. This is known as Chandrasekhara Pattabhishekam.

Now, regarding the Theerthams (sacred waters) in this sthalam, there are ninety-six Theerthams here. There are Theerthams such as Manikkarnikai, Viswamithra Theertham, Vedamrita Theertham, Vedanadi, and Kotti Theertham. It is an ancient tradition to divide these ninety-six Theerthams into six pilgrimages and bathe in them. These six pilgrimages are Vishnu Yatra, Sethu Yatra, Dakshinamana Brahma Yatra, and Uttaramana. The methods of bathing in these are described in the Sthala Puranam. Vedaranyam is a Thiru-sthalam that is special in all three aspects: Murthi (deity), Sthalam (place), and Theertham (sacred water).

This Thiru-sthalam, Vedaranyam, was worshipped by the Vedas. It removed the Veeragathi (sin of killing a warrior) from Rama. It showed the bridal form to Agastya. It made a rat that kindled a lamp into a Mahabali (great sacrifice). It was worshipped by Musukunda Chakravarthi. It is praised by the proverb “Vedaranyam vilakku azhagu” (The lamp of Vedaranyam is beautiful).

It was worshipped by Nachikethas, Ketu, Gautama, Manu, Mandhata, Dasaratha, Viswamithra, Vasishta, and others. It was praised and glorified by the Thiru-murai scholars and other poets. The sacred doors, which were closed by the Vedas, were opened and closed by Thiru-navukkarasu Swamigal and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman here, a glory sung about. The sculptural excellence of the Vedaranyam temple, with its rich corbels, potikas, yalis, stone chains hanging from the mouths of yalis, The stone balls rolling in the mouths of the yalis, and the creeper carvings on the pillars, are all exceptionally fine and beautiful. On the ceiling slab of the front mandapam of the sanctum, the twelve zodiac signs are carved. The twenty-seven constellations are arranged according to their respective Dhyana Slokas.

The bridal form of the Lord, enshrined behind the Moolattanam, is exceedingly beautiful. All the Utsava Murthis (processional deities) of this Thiru-sthalam are very ancient and beautiful.

Now, regarding the Sthala Vriksha (sacred tree) here, the Vanni tree in front of the Lord’s temple is the Sthala Vriksha. Mostly, Sthala Vrikshas are associated with historical events. In that sense, originally, the Sthala Vriksha was a dense forest.

In this context, the Vanni tree here is the place where Agastya performed penance, desiring to see the bridal form, and attained Siddhi (spiritual perfection).

Therefore, it has a connection to Puranic history. The Punnai tree opposite the Amman shrine is also considered a Sthala Vriksha. Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar sings in his Thiru-kurunthogai, “Surakkum punnaigal soozh Maraikkadaro.” In both prakarams, there are mandapams such as the Rajanarayana Mandapam, Sixteen-Pillared Mandapam, Vanniyadi Mandapam, Chettiyar Mandapam, Purana Mandapam, Mahamandapam, and Ardha Mandapam. Around Manikkarnikai, there are tiled mandapams suitable for performing Shiva Puja and Japa. There are also the Vasanta Mandapam and Sethupathi Mandapam. The hall where Nataraja Peruman is enshrined is in the inner prakaram.

This is also known as Devar Thozhu Mandram and Devabhakta Sabai.

Now, let us briefly contemplate the Puranic history of the Vedaranyam sthalam. Thirumal, incarnated as Adi Rama, intended to go to Lanka and destroy Ravana. He investigated which place would be easy to cross the sea. He concluded that Vedaranyam was the best place and arrived here. With the help of the Vanara warriors who accompanied him, he built a bridge. He went to Lanka, killed Ravana, rescued Sita Piratti, and returned to Ayodhya.

On his way back over the bridge, the sin of Brahmagathi (killing a Brahmin), incurred by killing Ravana, afflicted Rama as a Brahma Rakshasa. Due to this, Rama became disheartened. The sages witnessed this state. The sages requested Rama, saying that if he meditated on Shiva Peruman by chanting the Sri Panchaksharam at the very place where he built the bridge, this sin would be removed. Rama Peruman, following the advice of the sages, broke the bridge in three places with his bow, turning it into a sea. He then sought to know which place was suitable for performing penance with sixty-eight thousand sages to attain Siddhi.

At that time, Jabali Muni, the chief of the sages, addressed Rama Peruman, saying, “To the north of this Sethu, there is a mountain called Satyagiri. A river called Satya Nadi flows there. During the time you built the Sethu Bandhanam, that river merged with the sea. That river is now flowing northwards into the sea as Uttarakami. If you bathe there and perform penance on that mountain, the Lord will appear, grant your wishes, and remove this blemish.” Rama Peruman, following the sage’s words, performed penance. Shiva Peruman, pleased with his penance, appeared in the form of a Shiva Lingam with the Manikkarnikai Theertham at noon on a auspicious day in the month of Panguni, when it was a full moon and Uttara Nakshatra.

Along with that, he appeared as a luminous form, bearing a snake and the Ganga river on his sacred head, shining like a thousand suns, holding a deer and a battle-axe, adorned with a Kondrai garland, He revealed his complete sacred form. Rama Peruman, seeing the sacred form of Shiva Peruman, worshipped him with tears of joy in his eyes. Shiva Peruman addressed Rama, saying, “Rama, the sins like Brahmagathi that you committed have been removed. We have come here with the Manikkarnikai Theertham to remove your blemish. All the sins of those who bathe in it will be removed.” In response to Rama Peruman’s request, Shiva Peruman continues to bless devotees even today as a Shiva Linga form, facing east, to the west of the Veda Nadi.

Thus, this sthalam became known as Adi Sethu, worshipped by Adi Rama. It is imperishable even during the Brahma Yuga. The sound world of Vedas and Agamas, and the material universes, both animate and inanimate, merge into it. When the world is recreated, Shiva Peruman will emerge from this Linga form and instruct Brahma on the principles of Vedas and Agamas. Just like the Manikkarnika Ghat in Kasi, the Theertham blessed by the Lord in Thiru-maraikkadu is Manikkarnikai. This pond, like the Lord’s right eye, shines along the outer wall.

Since Shiva Peruman appeared here at noon for Rama Peruman, bathing in this pond at noon is considered special. Bathing in Kasi Manikkarnikai in the morning and in this sthalam’s Manikkarnikai at noon yields equal Shiva Punya (merit). Shiva Peruman blessed the Vedas, the six Angas, Agamas, and Puranas so that all people might live disciplined and within bounds. The great Brahmins, free from faults like the desire to hoard wealth for the next day, would recite these Vedas and, by living according to their teachings, served as guides for others. As time passed, those Brahmins deviated from their observances and They attempted to recite the Vedas for their livelihood. As a result, the Vedic mantras lost their power.

Realizing this, the four Vedas took human form and worshipped the Lord, desiring to regain their lost power. They reached this sthalam, Vedaranyam, which had the ancient name Satyagiri. They began to worship Sambhu, who resides in Satyagiri. To the north of Vedanathan, at a distance of a hundred bow-lengths, they created a large lake named Vedamritham after themselves. Daily, they bathed in it, immersed themselves in Manikkarnikai, and during the times suitable for bathing in the sea, they immersed themselves in the Satya Nadi, which is the sea, and worshipped Shiva Peruman without deviating from the Sivagama path. Shiva Peruman, pleased by the worship of the four Vedas, appeared as Vedavana Peruman in a Shiva Linga form at dawn during the auspicious Vyatipata Punyakalam in the month of Margazhi.

He appeared in form and addressed the Vedas, saying, “Vedas, you have worshipped me with sincere devotion for many years.

“Therefore, I am pleased. I have come here to grant all the desired boons to anyone who worships me as you have. Ask for the boons you wish.” The Vedas, addressing Shiva Peruman, said, “Oh Lord of Grace, who is moved by love, we have no shortcomings by your divine grace.

“However, Lord, we wish to ask for some boons according to your will. We have a desire: we wish to remain here forever, worshipping you like this. Even if many Brahma Kalpas pass, we wish to live in this sthalam, taking all births as grass, shrubs, and trees. Whatever birth we take, our duty should be to behold, worship, and praise you.

“Therefore, this sthalam Should be known by our names as Vedavanam, Vedaranyam, and Maraikkadu. The river here should be called Veda Nadi, the pond Vedamritham, the Lord Vedaranyeswar, and the Mother Vedanayaki.” Thus, they requested that everything in this sthalam should have the prefix “Veda.” They also requested, “Annually, whoever bathes in Vedamritham and Veda Nadi during this Mahavyapata Yoga and beholds you, should attain worldly happiness and liberation in the afterlife. Please grant such boons.” Shiva Peruman, considering the selfless and generous nature of the Veda Purushas, said to the Vedas, “We appreciate your quality of wishing for the well-being of all, with the underlying desire that your name should spread everywhere. You We have granted the boons you requested. May you, who are virtuous, from a good lineage, and unwavering in your observances, always live with the abundant power of mantras in the mouths of Brahmins. Whoever recites you, the Vedas, along with your Angas, will also attain the positions granted by us.” Thus, Shiva Peruman spoke and then merged into the Shiva Lingam.

“The Satya Nadi, which originated from the Satyagiri mountain at Kodiakkarai, merges with the Veda Nadi, which is the sea of the sanctum, for a distance of ten yojanas. Those who remember, touch, or bathe in that river become Jeevan Muktas (liberated while living). Those who bathe in the Veda Nadi and worship Vedavaneswarar will attain long life, Shiva Gnanam (divine knowledge), and all desired objects. If the Vedas themselves bathe in this river, it means that sacred rivers like the Ganga also bathe to cleanse their sins. The meaning of this is that since Kodi Theertham is the southeastern corner of the ocean, and because the tip of the bow of the primordial Rama was immersed in it, and because it removes countless sins of devotees who bathe in it, granting them countless blessings, it is named Kodi Theertham. Those who immerse themselves in this Theertham at any time will attain liberation.

“However, it is most excellent to bathe during the auspicious periods of Vyathipatha Yoga, Dakshinayana, Uttarayana, the beginning of the month, Amavasya, Pournami, and Vishu. At this Thalam, on a Sunday, during the seventh Thithi of the waxing moon in the month of Chithirai, at noon, Lord Shiva revealed to Sage Agathiyar, who had come south, the wedding form of Lord Shiva and Parvathi that took place in Kailash. Another important historical event took place at the Thiru-Vedaranyam temple, the Thiru-Vedavaneswarar temple.

“One day, the lamp burning in the sanctum sanctorum where the Lord resides dimmed slightly. Lord Shiva, addressing Uma Devi, said, “Whoever rekindles this lamp, we will grant them kingship in this world and Shiva-gathi in the next.” Uma Devi smiled and submitted, “The Ardha Jama puja is over, and the doors are closed.

“After this, when the Devas are in solitude, who will come inside and rekindle the lamp? The boon you speak of is wondrous.” The Lord said, “Wait and see.” At that moment, a mouse climbed onto the lamp to drink the ghee in it. As it did, the lamp was rekindled and burned brightly with clear light.

“Lord Shiva blessed that mouse to attain kingship, filled with all riches. That mouse was born as the son of a king named Virochana, and ruled the three worlds under the name Mahabali. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman has sung this history in his Thiru-Pathigam.

“Moreover, this history is also found in the Sthala Puranam. Emperor Mahabali, by the merit of having rekindled the lamp as a mouse, became a king.

“Therefore, kings have had faith and conviction in lighting lamps.

“Thus, inscriptions show that most kings donated gold, land, and cattle for the lamps of Thiru-Vedaranyam.

“Therefore, the proverb “Vedaranyam lamp is beautiful” also originated from this. All these are facts and Puranic histories about this sacred place called Thiru-Vedaranyam. To this glorious Thalam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman arrive. The Vedas worshipped Thiru- The miraculous act of these two great personages singing Pathigams to open the closed doors and then to close them again is about to take place here. Let us contemplate on that.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 421. Thiru-Nindra Charukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman arrive at the sacred Thiru-Marai-Kadu, known as Vedaranyam. Vedaranyam is a coastal Thalam belonging to the Neythal Thinai.

Therefore, the land and primary elements appropriate to that Thinai flourish there. Punnai trees and pearls brought by the sea are the primary elements of the Neythal Thinai.

Additionally, there are salt pans in Vedaranyam that produce salt. There are groves where fragrant Punnai flowers bloom. Salt, which adds taste to food, is produced there.

Thus, providing sweetness to the mind and body, guiding people’s minds towards the path of liberation and helping them, Such an environment exists in Thiru-Marai-Kadu. Here arrive the Lord of Southern Pukali and Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal. This Thalam is close to the sea and its sandy shores. The Vedas worshipped Lord Shiva, who resides in this Thalam as a Brahmin.

Lord Shiva is a Brahmin, so the Vedas worshipped Him. The worship by the Vedas means that the presiding deities of the Vedic mantras took form and worshipped the Shiva Lingam.

In this way, the Vedas worshipped the Lord and then closed the doors. Closing the doors with appropriate rituals, actions, and mantras after opening them for worship and before the next worship is the meaning of “Thiru-Kaappu Seythal.” The meaning of “Thiru-Kaappu Seythal” is to close and lock the doors with appropriate rituals, actions, and mantras after opening them for worship and before the next worship. The Vedas once worshipped the Shiva Lingam here and then departed.

From that day until now, when the Nayanmars arrived, those doors have remained closed. It is a rule of Shiva temple darshan that those who go to the temple should worship the temple entrances and the temple tower before entering. According to this, both Nayanmars worship the sacred entrance of this temple. This ancient sacred entrance, closed by the Vedas, remains locked. No devotees capable of opening these locked doors have come yet, so it remains locked.

Therefore, everyone goes through another entrance next to that entrance and worship Lord Shiva. These entrances are locked with mantra-bound latches.

Therefore, no one with the spiritual power to recite similar mantras and perform actions to undo the mantra-power of the Vedas has come here yet.

Thus, those entrances remain closed.

Therefore, Shiva devotees and people go through another adjacent entrance to perform worship. The point here is that a door closed by the Vedas can only be opened by something similar.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman sing the Thevara Thiru-Pathigams, which are Tamil Vedas, to open the closed door and then again to lock that door. This is about to happen now. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman hear from the devotees there about the closed temple doors and their history. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, having heard this history and background information, addresses Appar Swamigal, saying, “Appare, please sing so that the sacred doors in front of the temple, which the exalted Vedas worshipped, may open, allowing us both to enter and worship the Lord, the God of Gods, without hindrance.” Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman thus speaks to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. Having understood the situation, the Lord of Thoni-Puram, who is the ocean, “Appar, sing so that the sacred doors in front, which the exalted Vedas worshipped, may open, allowing us to enter and worship the Lord without hindrance.” Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasar, in his profound nature, was addressed by Pillaiyar.

Therefore, he began to sing, taking the words “Pannin Ner Mozhiyal.” As a result, the sacred doors, which were closed, opened. The Lord, who wears the southern cool garland, removed the sacred lock. The Thiru-Kadaikkappu was sung, “Enneer Irakkamonrilir.” As he sang and worshipped, by the grace of the true essence of Vedavanam, the jeweled doors, which were locked, opened in front of the loving devotees.

The Lord of the arts, along with the sage of wisdom, bowed down. The sound of the ocean and the roar of the Devas, along with the sound of the Vedas, resounded. Sekkizhar Peruman now describes the events that transpired in these three verses. The main direct doors of the temple are locked.

Therefore, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman asks Appar Swamigal, “Appare, please sing so that these doors may open.” All the people worship the Lord by going through the adjacent entrance, not through the main direct entrance. But Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman asks, “You and I must go through this main direct entrance to worship the Lord.

“Therefore, please sing so that the door may open.” He addresses him as “Appare.” When Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman first met Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman in Sirkazhi, he addressed him as “Appare.” He uses the same address here to make this request. The implication here is that since he is Appar, he should be the one to sing to open the door. While Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman was present, Appar Swamigal did not initially intend to sing a Pathigam.

“Therefore, knowing this intention of Appar Swamigal, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman thus addressed Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, who is Aludaiya Pillaiyar, spoke thus out of love.

“Therefore, as Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman requested, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal began a Thevara Thiru-Pathigam with the words “Pannin Ner Mozhiyal.” “Pannin Ner Mozhiyal” are the opening lines of the Thiru-Pathigam composed by Appar Swamigal for the opening of the temple doors. “Pan” refers to a musical arrangement that is unique to Tamil and naturally aligns with the vocal sound of women.

“Therefore, “Pannin Ner Mozhiyal” is the meaning expounded by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar for the Ambika residing in Thiru-Marai-Kadu, Vedaranyam. We know that the sacred name of the Ambika here is Veena Vatha Vithushini. In Tamil, this is referred to as “Yazhai Pazhitha Mozhiyal.” Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman also sang in his Thiru-Pathigam, “Yazhai Pazhithanna Mozhi Mangai Oru Pangan.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings this very name as “Pannin Ner Mozhiyal.” The name “Yazhai Pazhitha Mozhi Ammai” has a negative connotation. If “Yazhai Pazhitha Mozhi” means that which surpasses the Yazh, then the question arises, what does it equal? It equals “Pan.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman explains it in an affirmative way as “Pannin Ner Mozhiyal,” meaning that which is equal to “Pan.” Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman begins his Thiru-Pathigam with “Pannin Ner Mozhiyal Umaipangaro” and composes it for the opening of the closed sacred doors. At the end of this, in the Thiru-Kadaikkappu, he sings, “Enneer Irakkamonrilir.” This Thiru-Pathigam consists of eleven verses.

“In ten of these verses, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman makes a plea to the Lord to open the door. “Kanni-nal umai kaana kathavinai thinnamaaga thirantharul seymine.” “Remove the strength of the long, great door; open the door. Open the great heavenly door; remove the distant door’s support. Open the door to be seen. Remove the affliction of the great door; remove the strength of the door; open the door.

“Open it firmly.” Thus, in ten verses, he pleads, “Open the door, O Lord!” In the eleventh verse, he pleads, “You have no compassion, O my Lord!” This Pathigam, sung with the plea to open the door, is the tenth Thiru-Pathigam in the fifth Thiru-Murai. Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathigam.

““Pannin Ner Mozhiyal Umaipangaro, Manninar” “O Lord, who resides in the sacred forest worshipped by those who endure! Open the door firmly so that we may see You with our eyes. O Lord, who resides in the red matted locks! O Lord, who is like the dark clouds!

“You who have taken us into Your fold, grant Your grace. Remove the strength of the long, great door. O Appar, who is the eight-formed one! O Lord, who burned the great city with a touch! O Lord, who wears the crown,” “O supreme Lord, who wears the crown!

“Open this door firmly. O Lord, who recited the rare four Vedas! O Lord, who burned the great city with a touch! O Lord, who wears the spreading loincloth! Open the great heavenly door. O Lord, who resides in the sacred forest on the mountain!

“O Lord, whose feet are worshipped by the arts! O Lord, whose form is like a priceless great gem! Remove the support of the distant door.” “O Lord, who resides in the sacred forest surrounded by blooming Thazhai and fragrant Arugam grass! O Lord, who is difficult for anyone to see! O Lord, open the door so that we may see You.

“O Lord, who smears the sacred white ash! O Lord, who resides in the endless, beautiful sacred forest! O Lord, remove the affliction of this great door so that Your devotees may come and worship You. O Lord, who wears the Ganga and resides in the beautiful sacred forest! O Lord, who shares half with the Mother,” “O Lord, who rides the bull!

“O my Lord, remove the strength of this incomparable door. O Lord, who smears the white ash! O Lord, who is the supreme one, who knows the beauty of the Pan! O Lord, who is the primordial one, who resides in the beautiful sacred forest! Open the firm door. O Lord, whom the celestials desire to meet!

“O Lord, whom the earthly beings worship, who resides in the sacred forest! Open the door firmly so that we may see You with our eyes.” “You who crushed the Rakshasa with your finger, you have no compassion, O my Lord! O Lord, who resides in the sacred forest surrounded by abundant Punnai trees! Open the door quickly.”

“Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal sings this Thiru-Pathigam. “Pannin Ner Mozhiyal Pangare,” meaning, “O Lord, who shares half with the one whose language is like the Pan! Remove the great affliction of this door and open it so that we may see You directly with our eyes and so that devotees may come and worship You.” With this sentiment, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal sings this Thiru-Pathigam. “Pannin” Sekkizhar Peruman states that because Lord Shiva, who shares half with the one whose language is like the Pan, enjoyed the benefit of this, He delayed opening the door. Even though we perceive the Lord with our inner eye, he pleads that we should also see the Lord directly with our outer eyes through this entrance.

“These doors are very firmly and strongly locked because the Vedas came here, worshipped, and then closed these doors.

“Therefore, these are doors protected by mantras. That is why Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, throughout this Pathigam, sings about the strength of the door and the strength of its closure, referring to it as “Ma Kathavu,” “Periya Vaan Kathavam,” “Tholaivilaa Kathavam,” “Ma Kathavam,” “Maarilaa Kathavam,” and “Vali.” In the third verse, the word “Suvandar” appears, meaning one who possesses special marks. “Suvandu” means a mark or sign. “Suvadu” might have become “Suvandu.” The crescent moon, Ganga, and Nagasiram on the Lord’s head illustrate His supreme nature. This door is the direct path.

“Its closure has caused sorrow in the hearts of devotees.

“Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings, “Open this door to relieve that sorrow.” Thus, in ten verses, he sings to open the door. In the eleventh verse, he sings, addressing the Lord, “You have no compassion.” Even after Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman pleaded in ten verses for the door to open, the Lord did not grant His grace.

“Therefore, he sings, “You have no compassion,” in the eleventh verse. As soon as Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sang thus, the sacred doors, which had been locked by the Vedas, opened. By the divine grace of the Lord, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, and other devotees, as these doors opened, entered directly and worshipped the Lord. Their hair stood on end; they danced in ecstasy. Tears of joy flowed as they contemplated the Lord’s divine grace.

“Here, the Vedas of the Lord had locked the door, and the Thiru-Pathigam of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, the Tamil Veda, caused it to open.

“The Lord demonstrated this divine grace here so that everyone might realize that the Sanskrit Veda and the Tamil Veda proclaim the same ultimate truth. By the divine grace of the Lord, the true essence shining in Vedaranyam, the luminous jeweled door was opened, and the loving devotees, along with Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, entered through this opened entrance, praised and worshipped the Lord, prostrated themselves, bowed down, and rose. The shouts of the Devas and the sound of the Vedas resounded more loudly than the roar of the ocean. The assembly of devotees experienced great joy. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, the sovereign of the devotees, and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, the child-saint, immersed themselves in joy, entered, bowed down to the Lord, praised Him, sang Thiru-Pathigams, and with their bones melting and hearts overflowing, they worshipped the Lord.

“At this time, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman Many Tamil garlands of hymns are sung.

“At this time, it is most appropriate, as Sivakavimani Aiyya writes, that the Thiru-Kurunthokai hymn, “Othamaal Kadal,” composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, should have been revealed before the Lord. This sacred hymn is the ninth Thiru-Pathikam of the fifth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Kurunthokai Thiru-Pathikam.

“Othamaal Kadal. The world is filled with women who worship the Lord of Marai-Kadu, who is loved and desired. By praising His feet, sins will vanish.

“The Lord of Marai-Kadu, who is difficult for all to see, looks upon His devotees. If we do not perform His service, we will not see Him.

“The Lord of Marai-Kadu, whose feet are worshipped by those who live in the world, has a beautiful form.

“The Lord of Marai-Kadu, who has a beautiful form, has a beautiful form. He is the wealth that delights in a small form, with a part of the body as a woman. He wears eight great flowers and has a round, matted, reddish-brown hair. He is the Lord of Marai-Kadu. He dances and sings the four Vedas. This is the place where He is lovingly present.

“The Lord of Marai-Kadu, surrounded by fields full of water lilies and lotuses, is the one who has taken a woman as a part of His body. He keeps a young white crescent moon and a snake in His matted hair. Those who praise Him without sleep even in their sleep are the Lord of Marai-Kadu, who has a beautiful form. The soft-footed maiden brought a tiger, and the five-headed serpent stood in fear.

“The Lord of Marai-Kadu, who is adorned with wealth and festivities, has taken Uma, the beautiful maiden, as a part of His body. He has placed the Ganga on His head.

“The Lord of Marai-Kadu, where conches wash up on the shore, keeps fire in His hand, not just the Ganga in His red matted hair. How beautiful it is! The ninth verse of this hymn is not available to us.

“Now, the tenth verse: The chariot of the one who showed no fault, the great mountain, the one who took the ten heads, the one who showed no fault, the one who made the Lord speak out, the one who showed no fault, our Lord, to praise you.

“Let us go on contemplating.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 422. Thiru-Nindra-Charukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings a Thiru-Pathikam. The sacred door, which was locked by the Vedas, opens by the grace of the Lord.

Through that open door, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, and other devotees enter the temple and worship the Lord. After worshipping, they come out through the same door. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, and other devotees come out of the temple. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman says to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, the Kaundinya of Pukali, who partook of the nectar of wisdom that flowed from the breast of the mountain goddess, “Please sing so that the open door may close again.”

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman says to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. Because, just as the previously closed doors remained closed, now the open doors should not remain open.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman tells Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, “Please sing so that the open doors may close again.” The power of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman’s sacred wisdom, the sacred words of the Lord, is such that just as the Vedas locked the door, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman’s sacred words also have the power to lock the doors. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman tells Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, “Just as you asked me to sing to open the door, now I ask you...” I request you to sing again so that these doors may close. Because the doors that were closed have now opened. If the opened doors are closed again, then these doors can be opened and closed for worship continuously. That is why the Peruman makes this request.

In response to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s request, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, the Lord of Sirkazhi and the Tamil poet, hearing Thiru-Navukkarasu’s polite words, begins to sing a Thiru-Pathikam. As soon as Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman began to sing the Thiru-Kadavu, the doors of the sacred temple closed with the very first verse. The doors closed with the very first song. By the grace of Shiva Peruman, who has a beautiful forehead with eyes. By the grace of Shiva Peruman, as soon as Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman began to sing, the sacred doors closed again with the very first song. They were locked.

Earlier, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman had requested in ten songs that the door be opened. But when the Peruman delayed, he pleaded with great sorrow in the eleventh song, “You are without mercy,” and then the door opened.

But now, with the very first song sung by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, the sacred doors closed.

Thus, the Lord bestowed His grace upon both Nayanmars in different ways.

Here, Sekkizhar Peruman describes the Lord who bestowed such grace as having beautiful eyes that are responsible. “The ornament of the eye is compassion,” says the Thiru-Kural.

But here, Shiva Peruman bestows grace in different ways upon the two Nayanmars. When Shiva Peruman, who has a beautiful forehead adorned with compassionate eyes, is present, why does Sekkizhar Peruman sing about Him in this way? It is to illustrate that the greatness of the Lord’s compassionate gaze lies in His ability to bestow grace according to each individual’s capacity.
