Similarly, in Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, the Lord’s grace provided coins with interest to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, but to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, He provided coins without interest, as we saw there in Thiru-Vizhimizhalai.

Now, the Thiru-Pathikam that begins with “Ippozhuthu Paadiya Thiru-Pathikam Enbadhu” (This Thiru-Pathikam that was sung now) is about the sacred doors that were previously locked by the Vedas.

Therefore, to lock those sacred doors again, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman begins this Thiru-Pathikam by starting with “Chathuram Marai Than” (The four Vedas) and then with “Marai” (Vedas).

Thus, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman begins this Thiru-Pathikam by placing the Vedas first. By the grace of the Lord, the doors closed with the very first verse. Seeing this, Aludaiya Pillaiyar and Aludaiya Arasu rejoiced, saying, “We have received this grace from our Lord,” and worshipped Him there. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman also completed the Thiru-Pathikam he had begun, sang it, and worshipped.

Thus, seeing these gracious acts performed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, where doors locked by the Vedas opened and then opened doors closed again, all the devotees were amazed. Their hair stood on end, tears of love flowed from their eyes, and they worshipped the feet of these two great ones, who were incomparable in every way.

Then, Sirkazhi Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal went to the sacred monastery. We saw earlier that in Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, both great ones stayed in separate monasteries.

But here, in Vedaranyam, we learn that both great ones are staying in the same sacred monastery. After reaching the sacred monastery, a worry comes to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s mind. He had sung ten songs, requesting the Lord to open the door, and then in the eleventh song, he sang, “You are without mercy.” After that, the Lord delayed and then opened the sacred door.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is now worried because the Lord opened the door after a long delay.

Therefore, opening the door was not Shiva Peruman’s sacred will. It seems that we have strongly urged the Lord by singing. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman thinks that he has achieved the act of opening the door by singing eleven songs and even forcefully saying to the Lord, “You are without mercy.” The Nayanar considers the act of closing the door with the very first song sung by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman to be easy.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman thinks, “I was unaware of the Lord’s sacred will.” “Ayarthal” means to desire. He worries, “It seems that opening the door was not Shiva Peruman’s sacred will. Without realizing this, I requested and desired to open the door.” The Lord’s sacred will, when desired, is easily achieved. What the Lord does not will, It is achieved only with great difficulty and effort.

Therefore, this desire to open the door was achieved after much fervent prayer and many efforts.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman grieves, thinking that this act was not in accordance with the Lord’s sacred will.

Furthermore, he thinks, “When there was no intention in the Lord’s sacred will to open the door, I dared to do it.” And he thinks, “The Lord is greatly compassionate, the embodiment of grace, and does nothing but grace. How could I have forcefully reproached such a Lord, saying, ‘You are without mercy,’ in the Thiru-Pathikam of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman?” Therefore, he worries, considering this to be a mistake he made.

Moreover, he thinks, “We sang, ‘You are without mercy,’ to the Lord, who is the embodiment of compassion and does nothing but grace.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman fears that this has resulted in an offense against the Lord.

Thus, because he has offended the Lord, he feels that he is not fit to be with other devotees and should not join them. He worries that he does not have the qualification to be with other devotees because he has offended the Lord, and he withdraws to a corner of the sacred monastery. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman closes his eyes with worry, but he is not sleeping. He is not sleeping, but only closing his eyes, remaining in a state of alertness.

Thus, grieving, he keeps the sacred feet of Shiva Peruman, the Lord of Thiru-Marai-Kadu, in his mind and meditates on them without his thoughts wavering, and he closes his eyes. He falls into a state of conscious sleep, which is called ‘arithuyil’. While Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is in this state of conscious sleep, Shiva Peruman appears before him with a golden sacred body, adorned with sacred ashes, and blesses Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, saying, “We will be in Thiru-Vaimoor. Will you follow?” Shiva Peruman blesses him, saying, “We will be in Thiru-Vaimoor. Come and follow us there.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman comes out of the state of conscious sleep into a state of alertness. He composes the Thiru-Kurunthokai Thiru-Pathikam with the idea that the Lord went away after telling him to come there.

The Lord, having said, “I am in Thiru-Vaimoor, follow me,” has gone. This is the Lord’s command.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, determined to follow that command, rises and quickly departs from Thiru-Marai-Kadu. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, the primordial Lord, goes before Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar in the same form He had shown before. It is now a state of full consciousness for Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, free from dreams. The Lord, with the same form he saw in his dream, goes ahead, saying, “Follow me.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman now sees the Lord and follows Him. Sekkizhar Peruman says that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sang the Thiru-Kurunthokai Thiru-Pathikam with the idea, “He went there telling me to come, what is that?” That Thiru-Pathikam is the Thiru-Pathikam belonging to the sacred place of Thiru-Vaimoor, the fiftieth Thiru-Pathikam in the fifth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Kurunthokai Thiru-Pathikam.

“Where did He go, searching for me, and there He revealed Himself.

“The Lord of Thiru-Vaimoor, who appears in the south, went away saying, ‘Come there,’ what is that?” “The Lord of Marai-Kadu, who is worshipped by the earth, when I was thinking and thinking and sleeping, the Lord of Thiru-Vaimoor said, ‘I am the Lord,’ and went away saying, ‘Come to me,’ what is that?” “I saw Him in Thanjai, I said, ‘You are not proud.’ He said, ‘Do not fear, I have come to call you.’” I rejoiced and rose, and came running.

“The Lord of Vaimoor is indeed powerful. I did not see Him in a dream, I saw Him before my eyes. I did not go away, I came along with Him. I did not see Him on the way, what is it that I am caught in the whirlpool of the Lord of Vaimoor? “These are the bright ones, there is no other,” I thought and thought and rejoiced. “These are the clear ones, like Thiru-Vaimoor.

“Like the cunning ones, what did they do to me?” “If you are not in me, then you are of immeasurable greatness.

“The Lord of Vaimoor, who is the great God, is it false that He entered?” “The old coin, the reward obtained by singing, like those who remove sorrow and weariness, searching for me, saying, ‘Come to Thiru-Vaimoor,’ what is it that He has left me here?” He who sang to open, and then closed by singing a more refined Tamil verse, is He not the Lord of Thiru-Vaimoor, whose red matted hair bears the crescent moon? He is mad. Even if I pray to avoid what is not suitable for me, I thought, “He is the pure one who performs false grace.” “He came to me, saying, ‘Come to Thiru-Vaimoor,’ is it false that He entered the golden temple again?” “With one sacred foot, which is difficult to touch, He kicked the Rakshasa to return. I prayed to the light of Thiru-Vaimoor. When I said, ‘I will light it,’ He appeared.”

“Thus, the Lord, in the same form He appeared in Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s dream, went ahead, and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman followed the Lord from Thiru-Marai-Kadu. Even though he received the nectar of boundless love in his hand, it was like not being able to eat it in his mouth.

“The Lord with the Ganga-laden matted hair went ahead, and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman followed Him for a long distance. The great Shiva Peruman went ahead, and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman tried to go near Him quickly.

“However, even though the Peruman went ahead quickly, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, unable to go near Him, also followed very quickly. Just like the proverb, “What is within reach of the hand is not within reach of the mouth,” even though the Nayanar followed the Shiva Peruman, who appeared in front as a disguise, and went quickly to reach Him, he could not reach Him. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman grieved as if he had received nectar in his hand but could not eat it in his mouth.

“Thus, the Lord who went ahead, as if to appear nearby, created a golden temple before him. He created a golden temple before Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, and then entered that golden temple and disappeared. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who had been following the Lord, quickly followed Him and went near that golden temple.

“At the same time, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, who had heard the news that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman had left the sacred monastery in Thiru-Marai-Kadu, now arrived at the place where this golden temple was located. He came near Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. Earlier, the Lord had shown a golden temple to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and then disappeared into that temple. At this same time, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, who had left Thiru-Marai-Kadu, arrived at this place. He came very close to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman.

“At that time, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman requested the Lord. O Lord, you called me, saying, “Come,” and showed as if you were coming near, but now you have disappeared. You are not showing yourself to me, who made you open the sacred door without knowing your sacred will. That is very right.

“But Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, who sang to close the door, making the power of sacred devotion clear, is now here. How will you show yourself to him now?” Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings.

“Therefore, the worry that he had sung to open the door without knowing the Lord’s sacred will is still in Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s sacred heart, which we can understand.

“Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman requests, “You can hide and bless me, who made a mistake, but can you not reveal yourself to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, who made no mistake?” Thus, as Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman requested, Shiva Peruman, who is still unseen by Vishnu and Brahma, reveals Himself directly to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, the king of our Sirkazhi. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman sees that sacred dance, the Lord’s sacred dance, and bows down and praises Him. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman shows that sacred vision of Shiva Peruman to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman so that he can also see it. Earlier, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman had requested Appar Swamigal to sing to open the sacred door.

“Accordingly, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sang.

“Now, Shiva Peruman appears to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. When Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman said, “See our Lord,” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman saw Him. When Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman requested, “How can you hide and bless Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman? How can you not appear? How can you not show yourself?” as a result, the Lord appeared and blessed Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman.

“Thus, as Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman showed, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman saw the sacred vision of Shiva Peruman, the Lord.

“At that time, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman composed a Thiru-Pathikam beginning with “Paada Adiyaar” (Devotees to sing). Throughout this Thiru-Pathikam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings about seeing the Lord of Thiru-Vaimoor. “I saw the devotees singing, I saw the multitude of devotees, I saw the way He desires the true devotees who stand and speak of the devotion He created, I saw the understanding that kept the mind within.” All these I saw. These are the gifts, he sings in this Thiru-Pathikam. It is the seventy-seventh Thiru-Pathikam in the sixth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Thandaka Thiru-Pathikam.

““I saw the devotees singing and praising, I saw the multitude of devotees, I saw the bustling ghosts dancing and the drums resounding, I saw the fire in His hand, I saw the Ganga in His matted hair that does not dry up, I saw the kokku flower, I saw the konrai flower, I saw a withered skull in His hand, I saw the Lord of Vaimoor as I saw Him.” “I saw a part of Him with a milky voice, I saw the eighteen ganas practicing, I saw the blue-throated neck, I saw the forehead, I saw the bull, I saw the morning sun and moon, I saw the karandai flower appearing on His sacred head, I saw the garland and the matted hair, I saw the Lord of Vaimoor as I saw Him.” “I saw the feet that dance gloriously on the earth, with anklets jingling, I saw the feet that shine in the sky.” Muṭiyum kaṇṭēṉ Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 423. Thiru-Nindra-Charukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. When the Lord, having said “Come to Thiru-Vaimoor,” showed His dance vision, His Thiru-Katchi, near Thiru-Vaimoor to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman in turn showed that vision to Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, both beheld the Lord’s darshan and sang Tamil garlands of hymns. Earlier, when the Lord had gone ahead and disappeared, saying “Come to Thiru-Vaimoor,” we saw that Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar sang the Thiru-Kurunthogai, a Thiru-Pathigam, beginning with “Where, what?” Now, having seen the Lord’s vision, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman bestows the Pathigam set to the Nattaraga tune, “Thalirilavalarana Umaipadam.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, having seen the Lord’s vision, sings the Thiru-Thandagam Pathigam, “Paada Adiyar Paravak Kanden.” Thus, three Thiru-Pathigams are dedicated to Thiru-Vaimoor. Having sung thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman worship Lord Shiva, who is enshrined in the Thiru-Vaimoor temple.

This is not the golden temple that the Lord showed and then disappeared from earlier; this is the Thiru-Vaimoor temple. The temple that these two great saints now worshipped is one of the Sapta Vidanga Sthalams located in Thiru-Vaimoor.

Here, the Lord’s sacred name is Vaimoornathar, Vaimoor Adigal. The Goddess’s sacred name is Paalin Nanmozhiyal. The Sthala Vriksham is the Balamaram. The Theertham is Surya Theertham. This is one of the seven Thyagesa Vidanga Sthalams established by Muchukunda Chakravarthy.

Here, Thyagesar, as Neela Vidangar, His dance is the Kamala Nadanam. The Papamega Prachanda Theertham, located opposite the temple, is capable of removing all sins. Brahma and other deities, fearing Tarakaasuran, took the form of birds and wandered. They came to this place, bathed in this Theertham, worshipped the Lord, and were blessed with the removal of their sins. This Theertham holds that glory. In this Sthalam too, in the central mandapam, the Navagrahas are arranged in a single line.

Eight Ashtabhairavas, equivalent to those in Kasi, are said to have been present in this Sthalam: Ananda Bhairavar, Aghora Bhairavar, Utthanda Bhairavar, Bala Bhairavar, Pathala Bhairavar, Eeswara Bhairavar, Kala Bhairavar, and Swarna Bhairavar. However, currently, only four forms are present: Aghora Bhairavar, Ananda Bhairavar, Utthanda Bhairavar, and Bala Bhairavar. In place of the other four Bhairava forms, four Andas have been invoked and installed. Jayantan, the son of Indra, whose curse was removed by Bhairava’s grace, prayed to the Lord of this Sthalam, asking that whoever worships Him on the first Friday of the Chithirai month should have their wishes fulfilled and be granted good grace and progeny.

The Lord granted his wish. Accordingly, every year on the first Friday of the Chithirai month, Jayantan Puja is performed for Bhairava. A Rajagopuram with three tiers faces east. It is built with one prakaram. In front of the Rajagopuram entrance are the Kodi Maram, Bali Peetam, and Nandi Mandapam. Thiru-Vaimoor Sthalam is the third of the Sapta Vidanga Sthalams dedicated to Thyagarajar.

The Thyagarajar shrine is located to the right, on the south side, of the Moolavar Vaimoornathar shrine. To the left of the Moolavar shrine, the Thiru-Maraikkadu Vedharanyeswarar shrine is located. At the entrance of the Moolavar shrine, Dvarapalakas are seen on both sides. The Moolavar Vaimoornathar is enshrined facing east in the sanctum sanctorum. On the birth of the Aippasi month, special Abhishekam and Aradhanas are performed for Neela Vidanga Peruman. To the west of the village is the Surya Theertham, believed to have been created by the sun.

Thus, both great saints have sung and praised the Vaimoor Nathar of this Sthalam and bestowed Pathigams. However, not all of those Pathigams are available to us. As we saw earlier, three Thiru-Pathigams for this Sthalam have been found. These include the Pathigams sung when they saw the golden temple shown by the Lord, and the Pathigam sung before that.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, having worshipped the Lord, stay together in Thiru-Vaimoor. The two great saints, who were deeply devoted and constantly contemplated the grace of Lord Shiva, had previously stayed together in a Thiru-Madam in Thiru-Maraikkadu.

At that time, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, not knowing the Lord’s divine will, felt that he had erred by making a request contrary to Lord Shiva’s divine will and singing a Pathigam, and thus considered himself alienated from divine grace.

Therefore, he withdrew and stayed apart from the devotees, as we saw.

Now, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman has received divine indications and experienced a vision of grace. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who were embraced by the Lord’s grace in Thiru-Vaimoor, are now with Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. Realizing this, and having now received divine indications and a vision of grace, he is freed from the fear that his previous thought was an error. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s love for the Lord grows ever stronger, and he sings more Pathigams. Currently, he is staying in the same Thiru-Madam with Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman in Thiru-Vaimoor for some time. After staying together in the same Thiru-Madam in Thiru-Vaimoor for some time, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman praise the Lord by worshipping the feet of Thiru-Vaimoor Peruman and offering garlands of hymns.

Then, both great saints return to Thiru-Maraikkadu. They humbly worship the Lord of Thiru-Maraikkadu, the Primal Being, and perform sacred services there. They are seated there.

At that time, messengers sent by the faultless and virtuous Pandimadeviyar Mangaiyarkkarasi Perumatti, the daughter of the Chola king and queen of the Pandya king, and by Kulachiraiyar, the great minister who served before Pandimadevi, come to Vedharanyam to see Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. They arrive at the Thiru-Madam where Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman is staying. “Adhi Muthalvar Thamai Panindhu Angu Aana Pani Seidhu Amaru Naal Seethamathi Venkudai Valavar Magalaar Thennan Theviyaar Kothil Gunathu Pandimadeviyaar Mun Kulachiraiyaar Pothavittar Silar” Vandhar Pugazhi Vendhar Thamai Kaana, thus the Peruman composes the song. In this song, the Cholas are referred to by the epithet “Seethamathi Venkudai Valavar.” This means the Cholas who possess the white umbrella, which cools and removes fear from this world, signifying their reign. They are those who do not deviate from righteous rule and possess compassion.

That compassionate rule is honored as the white royal umbrella. Such are the glorious Cholas, whom Sekkizhar Peruman refers to as “Valavar” in this sacred song. “Valavar” means those who possess the wealth of a country that does not need to depend on other nations. Such is the glory of the Cholas, and as their daughter, Mangaiyarkkarasiyar, Pandimadeviyar, was born and lives. She is the daughter of the Cholas and the queen of the Pandya king, Thennan. She is the faultless and virtuous Pandimadeviyar.

This is the first time in the Periya Puranam that Mangaiyarkkarasi Ammaiyar is mentioned. Mangaiyarkkarasi Deviyar is one of the sixty-three Nayanmars. This is the first place in the Periya Puranam where she is mentioned.

Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman praises Mangaiyarkkarasiyar, saying, “Valavar Magalaar Thennan Theviyaar Kothil Gunathu Pandimadeviyar.” Thus, Sekkizhar Peruman’s praise of Mangaiyarkkarasi Ammaiyar here reminds us of Mangaiyarkkarasi. The Thevaram composed by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, “Valavarkon Paavai Varivalai Kaimada Maani Pankayach Chelvi Pandimadevi,” is recalled here. Pandimadeviyar, Mangaiyarkkarasiyar, is the Queen of the Pandya kingdom. Kulachiraiyar, the great minister who serves before her, is also one of the sixty-three Nayanmars. Messengers sent by these two great individuals arrive at Vedharanyam to meet Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, the King of Pugazhi. These messengers, who have arrived, possess the qualities of those who have mastered the art of diplomacy.

We will see their character, words, and deeds in detail in the Puranam of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, in this very place.

Now, even though Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman are staying together in the same Thiru-Madam in Vedharanyam, Pandimadeviyar and Kulachirai Nayanar have sent messengers to meet Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman.

Therefore, the messengers have come to see Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. Having arrived at the Thiru-Madam of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman in Thiru-Maraikkadu, they convey their message to the gatekeepers. The gatekeepers take the message, go inside the Thiru-Madam, and inform Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, hearing the news, graciously and joyfully instructs them to invite the messengers inside.

Accordingly, the messengers enter and stand before Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman inquires of the messengers, “Are you free from harm?” That is, he asks if they are without any evil. Generally, people inquire about well-being, asking if one is well.

However, being free from evil is essential for being well.

Therefore, those who ask about well-being will inquire if one is free from evil. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman inquires in this manner. Upon hearing this, the messengers say to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, “Theedhum Ulaamo Indha Ulagam Uyya Vandheer Iruthaal Ninaivu.” They say, “O Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, no harm will ever come to those who meditate upon your sacred feet, anywhere, at any time.” They further state to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, “You have come for the salvation of this world.” The purpose of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman’s avatar is the refutation of other religions and the establishment of the true one. This is what the messengers convey. They say, “You have come for the salvation of this world, and therefore, no harm will come to those who meditate upon your sacred feet.” The implication of this is that even if we have experienced harm until now, we have meditated upon your sacred feet.

Therefore, any harm that may have existed will no longer remain. Your Holiness must grace our country with your presence. This is what we request and submit to you. The messengers convey this, implying that our Queen, Pandimadeviyar, and the great minister, Kulachiraiyar, are constantly meditating upon your sacred feet. The point here is that meditating upon the sacred feet of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman is the means, and freedom from harm is the benefit.

Our reflection on this continues. Thiru- We pray that you will come to our country. We make this request to you. The messengers convey this, implying that our Queen, Pandimadeviyar, and the great minister, Kulachiraiyar, are constantly meditating upon your sacred feet. The point here is that meditating upon the sacred feet of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman is the means, and freedom from harm is the benefit.

Let us resume our reflection on this. Thiru- Thiruchitrambalam Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 424. Thiru-Nindra-Charukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Messengers sent from the Pandya kingdom by Pandimadeviyar Mangaiyarkkarasi Ammaiyar and Kulachirai Nayanar arrive at Vedharanyam and stand before Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. They convey the message given by Pandimadeviyar and Kulachirai Nayanar, requesting him to grace the Pandya kingdom with his presence. The messengers further state that they cannot tolerate the cruel actions of the Jains, who are skilled in falsehood and proclaim their erroneous path as the true path, while the Shaivite path, as expounded in the Vedas, stands firm and unblemished in the world.

They say, the messengers state. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman inquires of the messengers about their well-being, asking if there is any harm or evil. Even though Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman asked, it would not be auspicious to immediately say, “Yes, we have harm.” Therefore, they begin by asking Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, “Is there any harm to those who meditate on your two sacred feet?” and then proceed to explain the harm they are experiencing.

Thus, these messengers, instead of immediately stating inauspicious news, begin auspiciously and then convey the true message. This is the act of wise people. This is the action of wise people.

Similarly, later, when Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman arrived in Madurai, Kulachirai Nayanar, upon greeting and worshipping Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman at the border of Madurai, was asked by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, “Is the grace and goodness for the Queen and for you abundant?” To which Kulachirai Nayanar replied, “By the great grace of your arrival today, we are eternally blessed with divine grace.” We can recall this incident here as well. We will examine this history in detail in the Puranam of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman.

Therefore, the message conveyed by the messengers was that the Shaivite path, as expounded in the Vedas, should flourish in the Pandya kingdom, and the erroneous Jain path should be eradicated from the Pandya kingdom. They were experiencing immense suffering due to the Jains. This was the request the messengers made to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. The Shaivite path is mentioned in the Vedas. The Jain path is a path contrary to the Vedas, an erroneous path. The Vaidika Shaivite path is faultless.

The Jain path, however, is full of faults. The Jain path was considered a high penance, characterized by faults such as plucking hair, torturing the body by lying on hot rocks, and daring to commit murder disguised under the principle of non-violence.

Thus, the messengers made their request to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, asking for the eternal flourishing of the ancient Shaivite path and the removal of the cruelties of the Jains, through the divine sacred ash. the Pandya kingdom should be rid of the Jain path. We are suffering greatly due to the Jains. This was the request the messengers made to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. The Shaivite path is that which is mentioned in the Vedas. The Jain path is a path contrary to the Vedas, an erroneous path. The Vaidika Shaivite path is faultless.

The Jain path, however, is full of faults. The Jain path was considered a high penance, characterized by faults such as plucking hair, torturing the body by lying on hot rocks, and daring to commit murder disguised under the principle of non-violence.

Thus, the messengers made their request to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, asking for the eternal flourishing of the ancient Shaivite path and the removal of the cruelties of the Jains, through the divine sacred ash. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman arose, relying on the strength of the sacred ash. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman arose, believing that this sacred ash would cause the conversion of Jainism and the flourishing of Shaivism. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman arose with mental resolve, thinking that the sacred ash would accomplish these deeds. He sang in the Thiru-Pathikam, “Veyuru Thozhibangan,” that the sacred ash of the Lord, who defeats the Jains and Buddhists in debate, is indeed righteous and firm. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman now made this resolve in his sacred heart.

Similarly, through the Thiru-Neetru Pathikam, Jainism was eradicated in the Pandya kingdom, and Shaivism flourished.

Thus, the messengers’ When Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, listening to the appeal, resolved to go to the Pandya kingdom, remove Jainism, and establish Shaivism, Vageesa Peruman, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, conveyed a message to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman said to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, “The Jains are very cruel and evil. They are skilled in deceit, not washing the dirt from their bodies, and have done many evil deeds to me in the past.

“Therefore, my child, I will not consent to your going there.” Thus spoke Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. He says that Jains accumulate dirt on their bodies. Jain gurus do not bathe or wash their bodies.

“Therefore, they wander in the sun, sweating, and do not brush their teeth, fearing that worms might die. They follow many such practices, allowing dirt to accumulate on their bodies. They are evil-natured, cruel enough to commit murder, deceitful, and follow wicked deeds, portraying falsehood as truth. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman says all this, adding that these Jains have previously harmed him.

“However, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is not saying all this out of anger or He did not speak out of astonishment. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman did not say these things out of anger, astonishment, or other evil qualities. “It is good to forget what is not good immediately” is a Kural, and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman was an embodiment of it. The Jains had inflicted many harms upon Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. They put him in a burning hot chamber, made an elephant trample him, gave him poisoned food, tied him to a stone, and threw him into the sea. Even when the Jains inflicted such harms upon Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, he remained a compassionate being.

“Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman was a being of grace, never showing the slightest anger towards the Jains. But those harms, Why does he mention all those harms to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman here? It is due to the immense affection and love that Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar had for Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. He recounts these incidents out of love, so that such harms should not befall Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman.

“Therefore, we must clearly understand that Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar did not say all this based on evil qualities like anger or astonishment.

“Furthermore, when Appar Swamigal says, “I will not consent to your going to a country where such cruel Jains reside,” it is a command of grace, born of the right that Appar Swamigal felt over Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman addresses Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar as “Appar” (father) and considers him as such.

“Accordingly, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, out of love for Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman whom he considers his child, says, “I will not consent to your going to the Pandya kingdom, that country filled with Jains.” This incident occurred at Thiru-Maraikkadu. When Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, having conveyed the message from the people of the Pandya kingdom to Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal from within the great gopuram, was about to take leave, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman spoke these words to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. This event is elaborated in the Puranam of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman. We are about to see this. When Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman said that he would not consent to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman going to the Pandya kingdom, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman replied, “I have the intention to go and see the two great souls who praise the boundless sacred ash. I will do nothing but destroy the state of the evil Jains there and spread the Shaiva path.

“This is my oath to you.” Thus, Peruman composes the song here. He says to Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, “I intend to go to the Pandya kingdom and see the two great souls, Pandi Maadeviyar and Kulachirai Nayanar, who praise the boundless sacred ash.

“There, I will destroy the evil Jains and their ways. He says, “I will destroy the state of the Jains who commit evil deeds and foster the Shaiva path. I will do no other deed. This is my oath to you,” says Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman to Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal. He says he will destroy the state of the Jains and promote the Shaiva religion. The purpose of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman’s incarnation is to refute other religions and make the glory of the sacred ash manifest.

“He places both these objectives here and replies to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. He says, “Devotees who recite the garland of sacred words will rule in heaven. This is our command,” as he declares with an oath in the eleventh verse of the Kol-Aru Pathikam. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman sings with an oath in the Thiru-Nanippalli Thevaram, “Thinking of Thiru-Nanippalli, karma will be destroyed; this is our command.” We can see such declarations with an oath in the sacred utterances of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman.

“Here, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, who sings with such oaths, says to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, “This is your command.” This is because Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar had commanded, “My child, I will not consent to your going.” Therefore, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman’s reply implies, “I will not go by contradicting you. I will go according to your command. My going is for this sacred service, to change the state of Jainism and make Shaivism flourish. May your command support this.” Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman replies, implying that he seeks support. When Appar Swamigal, standing in the position of Appar, said he would not consent, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, standing in the position of a child, replied to Appar Peruman as a child.

“This is the point here.

“Furthermore, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman continues to tell Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, “You need not come with me. You stay here. I alone will go to the Pandya kingdom, change the state of the Jains, and establish Shaivism.” He takes leave of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, implying that after eradicating the state of Jainism and establishing Shaivism, he will return here to see him again. From Thiru-Pukalur, these two great souls began their pilgrimage and have, until now, journeyed together for a long time through many sacred places. They have traveled together, visiting sacred sites and composing sacred hymns for the world’s well-being.

“Now, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, who is about to embark on the pilgrimage to the Pandya kingdom, states that Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar need not accompany him, and that Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar should remain at Thiru-Maraikkadu, while he alone will go to the Pandya kingdom to remove the evil of the Jains and make Shaivism flourish. Why does he say this? These two, who have journeyed together from Thiru-Pukalur until now, could continue to the Pandya kingdom. Why does Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman tell Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, “You stay here”? Sivakavimani Aiyya explains Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman’s sacred intention as follows: Pandi Maadeviyar and Kulachiraiyar sent messengers to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, conveying their message.

“Therefore, it would be most appropriate for Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman alone to go to the Pandya kingdom, in accordance with their request. This is because Pandi Maadeviyar and Kulachirai Nayanar had sent messengers specifically requesting Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman to come to the Pandya kingdom.

“Next, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman’s journey to the Pandya kingdom is for the purpose of eradicating the arrogance of the alien religion, Jainism, and for the flourishing of Vaidika Shaiva Siddhanta. These two objectives are the very purpose of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman’s sacred incarnation.

“Therefore, it is fitting that Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman alone should perform these deeds, which are the very essence of his incarnation.

“Now, thirdly, when an evil arises, one way is to internalize it, remain calm, and do nothing against it, allowing its power to diminish. The second way is to confront that evil, attack it, and remove it. During this period, when Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman incarnated and lived, the evils of alien religions like Jainism and Buddhism were widespread throughout the Tamil country at that time. They afflicted and prevented the flourishing of Shaiva enlightenment. It was the Lord’s sacred will to remove these evils by both the methods mentioned above and to show it to the world.

“The Lord demonstrates, through Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, the method of doing nothing against evil and allowing its power to diminish. He is about to demonstrate, through Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, the method of confronting evil, attacking it, and destroying it. We can recall here how Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman endured all the evils committed by the Jains, overcame them, and converted the Pallava king to the Shaiva religion.

“Now, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman goes to the Pandya kingdom, debates with the Jains, opposes them, and removes them. This is the second method of confronting and destroying evil, which Lord Shiva demonstrates. We can see this. From the upcoming history, that is, from the upcoming history of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, and further from the history of Pazhaiyarai Vadathali that will occur later, Lord Shiva, who desired to show it to the world, thus willed to send only Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman to the Pandya kingdom.

“Now, fourthly, if Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar had also gone to the Pandya kingdom with Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and removed the evil deeds committed by the Jains, then the history would record that two Shaiva acharyas came to remove the evils of Jainism. This would lead to the accusation that the Shaiva religion needed two acharyas to remove the evils of Jainism. This would diminish the glory of both these great acharyas.

“Therefore, to demonstrate that Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman alone is sufficient to remove the evils of the Jains, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman goes to the Pandya kingdom.

“Next, fifthly, if both great souls had gone together and eradicated the Jain evil there, the world would not have been able to clearly understand and follow who eradicated the Jain evil, and would have been confused. To avoid this, Peruman acts in this manner, performing this sacred play.

“Now, sixthly, even if Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman had been invited, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, who had spoken about the deceptive cunning and evils of the Jains and refused to let Pillaiyar go there, would have preferred to stay away from the place where those evil Jains resided, in accordance with the rule that “seeing evil people is also evil.” This is the sixth reason.

“Now, seventhly, even if Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman wished to avoid approaching the Jains, he would have agreed to accompany Peruman when he went.

“Therefore, to clarify this, Pillaiyar resolved to go to the Pandya kingdom alone.

“Thus, in seven ways, Siva- Kavimani Aiyya explains the seven reasons why Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman alone went to the Pandya kingdom.

“Thus, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, having said this and taken leave of Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, proceeds to the Tamil country, the Pandya kingdom. Sekkizhar Peruman refers to the Pandya kingdom as Tamil Nadu in this verse, speaking of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, the leader of wisdom. Although Tamil Nadu can be understood as the country where Tamil-speaking people reside, our sages have referred to the Pandya kingdom as Tamil Nadu. There were many countries where Tamil was spoken, such as Thondai Nadu, Nadu Nadu, Chola Nadu, Kongu Nadu, Chera Nadu, etc. Nevertheless, due to the special significance of the Pandya kingdom, if Tamil Nadu is used as a proper noun, it refers to the Pandya kingdom. This is because Lord Shiva, the primordial God, presided over the Sangam and fostered Tamil.

“The Pandya kingdom possesses the Podhigai Hills, where the Tamil sage Agathiyar still resides. Due to these many reasons, if Tamil Nadu is used as a proper noun, it refers to the Pandya kingdom.

“Therefore, all our sages have referred to the Pandya kingdom as Tamil Nadu. Tamil Nadu refers to the Pandya kingdom. We have extensively contemplated the connection between the Pandya kingdom and Tamil in the Puranam of Murthi Nayanar, in the sacred verses ranging from 68 to 974. Sekkizhar Peruman sang in the 974th verse, “If the Sangam that removes our sins and bestows the true meaning of the truthful Tamil texts existed in Thiru-Alavai, we can recall that message here.

“Thus, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, the leader of wisdom, proceeds to the Tamil country, the Pandya kingdom, to fulfill his incarnational purpose of refuting alien religions and establishing Shaivism. While he goes there, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman remains at Thiru-Maraikkadu, worshipping the Lord and performing sacred service.

“Our contemplation continues.””” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 425. Thiru-Nindra-Charukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. When Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, the king of Pukali, proceeded to the Pandya kingdom, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman stayed at Thiru-Maraikkadu for some time, performing sacred service. Appar Swamigal composed five Thiru-Pathikams for the sacred place of Thiru-Maraikkadu.

Among them, the Pathikam beginning “Pannin Ner Mozhiyal” was sung by Appar Swamigal to open the sacred doors. When he entered and worshipped the Lord after the doors opened, he sang the Thiru-Pathikam beginning “Odamal Kadal Pavi.” Now, the other three Thiru-Pathikams are those that we can consider to have been composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal. We will look at each of those Thiru-Pathikams one by one. The third Thiru-Pathikam is for Thiru-Marai- The third Thiru-Pathikam for Thiru-Maraikkadu is the thirty-third Thiru-Pathikam in the fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Ner-Isai Thiru-Pathikam.

“Indiranodu Devar Irudigal Ethukindra Sundaramanaar Polum Thuthikkalan Sothi Polum Chandiranodum Gangai Aravaiyum Sadaiyul Vaithu Mandiramanar Polum Mamaraikkadanare Theyana Nadaragi Devarhal Devar Polum Payana Nadarukkum Paththargal Paniyammin Kayana Nadu Kandangu Adanular Kalakandar Mayana Nadar Polum Mamaraikkadanare Arumai Ivvulagu Thannai Yamenak Karuthi Nindru Verumaiyin Manaigal Vazhndu Vinaigalal Nazhivunathe Sirumathi Aravu Kondrai Thigazhdaru Sadaiyul Vaithu Marumaiyum Immaiyavar Mamaraikkadanare Kalkodu Thirugaiyetri Kalinirai Thiraichi Meyndu” Tholpaduthu Uthira Neeral Suvaredu Thiru Irandu Vasal Ezhvudai Thavamaitthang Ezhu Salokam Panni Malkoduthu Avi Vaithar Mamaraikkadanare Vinninar Vinnin Mikkar Vedangal Virumbiyodha Panninar Kinnarangal Paththargal Padiyada Kanninar Kanninulle Jothiyay Nindra Enthai Manninar Valamkondu Ethum Mamaraikkadanare Angaiyul Analum Vaithar Aruvagai Samayam Vaithar Thangaiyil Vinai Vaithar Tham Adi Parava Vaithar Thingalai Gangaiyodu Thigazhdaru Sadaiyul Vaithar Mangaiyai Bhagam Vaithar Mamaraikkadanare Geetharay Geetham Kettu Kinnaran Thannai Vaithar Vedaray Vedam Odhi Vilangiya Jothi Vaithar Etharay Nattamadi Ittamay Gangaiyodu Madhaiyor Bhagam Vaithar Mamaraikkadanare Kanathinar Valiudaiya Kadimathil Aranam Munrum Sinathinul Sinamay Nindru Theeyezha Setrarpolum Thanathinai Thavirndu Nindru Tham Adi Paravuvarkku Manathinul Masu Theerppar Mamaraikkadanare Thesanai Thesan Thannai Devarhal Potrisaippar Vasanaiseithu Nindru Vaigalum Vananguminhal Kasanai Kanalai Endrum Karuthinil Vaithavarkku Masinai Theerppar Polum Mamaraikkadanare Pinniudai Yakai Thannai Pirapparuthuyya Vendil Paniudai Thozhilgal Poondhu Paththargal Patrinale Thunivuudai Arakkanodi Eduthalum Thogai Anja Mani Mudi Paththiruthar Mamaraikkadanare Thiruchitrambalam. The fourth Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for the sacred place of Thiru-Maraikkadu. The thirty-fourth Thiru-Pathikam in the fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Ner-Isai Thiru-Pathikam.

He drove his chariot high and looked with firm resolve, not knowing anyone above him, a man of great strength. He, whose matted hair spread out, making the earth and sky tremble, and whose beautiful form made people say, “Fear not!” is Thiru-Maraikkadanar. He, who, with a roar, lifted the mountain, the king of the rakshasas with matted hair, my Lord, who placed the moon on his head, adorned with the beauty of a serpent, by his will, the waves of the southern sea crash upon Thiru-Maraikkadanar. He drove a chariot of immense profit, and the rakshasa, mighty in strength, lifted the mountain, but when he pressed it down, he laughed and said, “I am Thiru-Maraikkadu.” He drove his chariot into the sky and, saying, “Who is this?” pushed the great mountain. When he pressed it down, the rakshasa, with his ten heads and mouths, cried out in agony, and he thought.

Thiru-Maraikkadanar. He, who, with irresistible strength, drove a chariot and, with what he held in his hands, said, “I will take whatever I want!” and lifted it, is capable of making him groan. He is Thiru-Maraikkadu, the beautiful one. He, who, with his glorious matted hair, trembled and did not go up, the one with the hand that seized and roared, the cruel and mighty one, tried to lift the mountain where the long-haired ascetics reside. He placed his toenail firmly on it. He is Thiru-Maraikkadanar, the ancient one.

He, who had ten mouths and twenty hands, the mighty one, the rakshasa of great strength, who committed evil with his mouth, when he cried out, he pressed his toenail on him. He is Thiru-Maraikkadanar, the ancient one, where the pearl-like waves crash. He, who, with his hands, left his side, and with an unwise mind, entered beneath the great mountain, unable to change his ways. His great wisdom was lost, and his valor was gone. The bhutas were naked. Thiru-Maraikkadanar.

He, who, with five hands and ten good heads, lost his wisdom, not knowing the long five, and lifted it, then made seven hands. He is Thiru-Maraikkadanar, the beautiful one. When he saw that he had placed the Ganga water in his matted hair, the maiden became angry. He drove his chariot with his hand and went and lifted the mountain. He cut the great nerve of his hand and sang songs. He, who granted grace with his hand, is Thiru-Maraikkadu, the beautiful one.

This Thiru-Pathikam is a special Thiru-Pathikam. Generally, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, in all his Thiru-Pathikams, in the tenth verse, sings about Ravana’s attempt to lift Mount Kailash, and how Lord Shiva punished Ravana, subdued his arrogance, and then, when he sang, granted him grace. This is a custom that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman follows in his Thiru-Pathikams, singing about that sacred history in the tenth verse of each Thiru-Pathikam.

Here, in this Thiru-Pathikam, in all ten verses, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar has sung about Ravana’s actions and the nature of Lord Shiva who granted him grace. This is the greatness of this Pathikam.

Now, the fifth Thiru-Pathikam, the twenty-third Thiru-Pathikam of the sixth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Thandaka Thiru-Pathikam, composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Maraikkadu.

He is the light that kindles the unextinguished flame, he is the jewel that surrounds the ancient immortals, he is the God difficult to behold, he is easy for those who contemplate him, he grants whatever those who desire him wish, he is the true path, he is the husband of those with purified minds, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. Hand. He is the one who plays the resounding Veena, he is Kapali, he is the lamp of knowledge that shines with true light, he is the seed in the hearts of true devotees, he is the one who wears the shedding serpent, he is the Supreme Being, he is the one of Thiru-Pasur, he is the one with the sharp, shining sword, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. He is the one who formerly granted grace to the spider, he is the one who set fire to the three cities, he is the one who became earth, water, and fire, he is the one who stands as both formless and with form, he is the one with the matted hair on his head where the water flows, he is the one who is Brahma and the red-eyed Vishnu, he is the one who rides a great bull, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. He is the one who danced in the cremation ground with thorny bushes, he is the one who conquered Yama with his foot, he is the one with the spotted deer skin, he is the one whose garment is the tiger skin, the pure one.

He is the one who wears the shining crescent moon on his head, he is the one with sacred ash, he is the father of the bridegroom of Valli, who resides in our Thiru-Sentil, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. He is the one who became the roaring, surging water, he is the primordial one whose body is like a complete fire, he is the wealthy one who ascended and filled, he is the one who brings joy to his sweet devotees, he is the Aryan, he is the Tamilian, he is the Lord who resides in Thiru-Annamalai, he is like the rutting elephant, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. He is the one who flayed the mighty elephant, he is the one who resides in Thiru-Agathiyanpalli, he is the one of Thiru-Kodi, he is the one of noble lineage, he is the one who made Thiru-Arur his temple, he is the desired good things, he is the one who removes the weariness of this world and the next, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. He is the one with the poison in his throat that joins the sea, he is the Lord of the flowery Kailash mountain that touches the sky, he is the one who destroyed the sacrifices that were performed, he is the Lord whom the immortals praise, he is the one who bathed in the five products of the cow mixed with milk and ghee, he is the one of the mountain, he is the son who has a part of Vishnu, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. He is the nectar that brings forth the mother, he is the clear honey, he is the Lord who brings forth this world, he is the one sweeter than you in my heart, he is the lamp of true knowledge, he is the one of Thiru-Venkaadu, he is the medicine for those whose minds are confused so that their karmas may depart, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. He is the primordial one who cures the root disease, he is the one who is the three Tamils and the four Vedas, he is the one who taught dharma to the four under the tree.

He is the beginning and the end, he is the eternal youth, he is like a coral mountain, he is adorned with the Konrai flowers, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. He is the Lord who stood as a pillar of fire, so that Brahma and Vishnu could not know him, he is the one who, with his radiant toe, pressed down the king of sorrowful Lanka, he is the one who granted great grace to those who praised him, he is the one who gave names and great armies, he is the one who cures the disease of powerful karma, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu.

Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman thus stayed in Thiru-Maraikkadu for some time and sang Thiru-Pathikams.

Now, he again wishes to go to Thiru-Vizhimizhalai and worship the Lord’s feet. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman wishes to do so because, until now, he had been on a pilgrimage with Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman for a long time, and that pilgrimage extended up to Thiru-Maraikkadu. From Thiru-Maraikkadu, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman had departed for the Pandya country. Currently, only Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman remains in Thiru-Maraikkadu.

Therefore, the memory of Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, where he had stayed with Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman for a long time, comes to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. Previously, Thiru-Vizhimizhalai was the sacred place where he had stayed with Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman for a long time and received grace.

Therefore, immediately after parting from Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, he thinks of going to Thiru-Vizhimizhalai to worship.

Thus, having received the grace of Lord Shiva, who resides as a light in Thiru-Maraikkadu with love, he departs from Thiru-Maraikkadu for Thiru-Vizhimizhalai with the thought, “When will I reach Thiru-Vizhimizhalai?” On the way, he visits Thiru-Nagaikkaronam and other sacred places, sings Thiru-Pathikams, and reaches Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. Sekkizhar Swamigal composes this verse, saying, “Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having received the grace of the light that resides in the groves of Thiru-Maraikkadu, departed and, thinking, ‘I will return to Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, where the Lord who consumed the poison of the sea resides,’ worshipped Thiru-Nagaikkaronam and other places that exist in the world, and singing powerful Tamil songs, reached Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, the abode of the Lord.” Therefore, on his way to Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, he visited Thiru-Nagaikkaronam and other sacred places. He sings Thiru-Pathikams as he goes. The other sacred places that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman visited after departing from Thiru-Maraikkadu are Thiru-Nellikka, Thiru-Nattiyathankudi, Thiru-Arur, Nannilam, and other sacred places.

However, the Thiru-Pathikams sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for these other places are not available to us now. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman worshipped the Lord in Thiru-Nagaikkaronam.

At that time, we have four Thiru-Pathikams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for the sacred place of Thiru-Nagaikkaronam. Let us go on contemplating. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 426, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman reaches the sacred place of Thiru-Nagaikkaronam. This place, referred to as Thiru-Nagaikkaronam in the Thiru-Murais, is currently known as Nagapattinam. The Lord’s name here is Kayarohanesvarar, Adhipuranar. The Goddess’s name is Nilayatakshi, Karuntadankanni.

The Sthala Vriksham is the mango tree. The Theertham is Devatheertham, Pundarika Theertham. Adiseshan, Pundarika Munivar, Agathiyar, Ambigai, Murugan, Thirumal, Vasishtar, Musukundan, Arasakesari, Vichitra Kavachan, Viruragan, Pathirasenan, Bhaskaran, Mithiran, Kalakandan, Chandadharuman, etc., worshipped in this place and received the grace of the Lord. Nagapattinam. We can learn from literature and inscriptions that Nagapattinam was one of the most important ports in the Chola country. The Pattu-Pattu, one of the Sangam literatures, states that Ilanthiraiyan, who ruled Thondai Nadu, was the son of a Chola king from Nagapattinam who went to Nagalokam through a tunnel and united with a Naga maiden.

This is a place worshipped by Adiseshan, one of the eight Nagas, and hence it is called Nagai. Karonam is the name of the temple. There are three temples named Karonam in Tamil Nadu. One is Nagaikkaronam, another is Kulandaikkaronam, and the third is Kachchikkaronam. Kayarohanam itself is called Karonam. Thiru-Nagaikkaronam is the place where the Lord accepted Pundarika Munivar into his sacred body.

Pundarika. This is the place where the Lord accepted the sage Pundarika into his sacred body, along with his physical body.

Therefore, it is called Kayarohana Sthalam. Thiru M. Balasubramanian Mudaliar states that this name was given because the Lord made Pundarika Munivar ascend to the celestial world with his physical body. Thiru-Onam is the star associated with Thirumal. Thiru Muthu Manickavasagam Mudaliar, in the Tharumaiyatheena Thiru-Murai publication, states that it received the name Karonam because Thirumal, who is dark-skinned, worshipped here. Thiru-Nagaikkaronam also has other names such as Adhipuranam, Sivarajadhani, Parpatheeswaram, and Aravanagaram.

This place has received the Thevara Thiru-Pathikams of the three, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. It is the eighty-second sacred place among the sacred places on the south bank of the Kaveri in the Chola country. Adiseshan, the king of serpents, worshipped here and established his name. It is one of the Sapthavidanga Sthalams. This is also one of the sacred places where the Goddess is named after her sacred eyes, meaning that just as Madurai Meenakshi, Kanchi Kamakshi, and Kasi Visalakshi are named after the Goddess’s eyes, the Goddess of this place is known as Nagai Nilayatakshi. Like Kailash and Kasi, this place also has a Mukthi Mandapam.

It has the glory of being the birthplace of Adhipattha Nayanar.

The Lord appeared from the Moolalingam to the seven sages and gave darshan as Somaskandar. He showed the wedding form to Agasthya Munivar. To King Salisuka, the wedding temple. The Panchakrosa Yatra, which shows the wedding, and the Sapthasthana festival take place. Dasaratha worshipped here by installing Shani. The temple is located in the middle of the town, facing east.

There are two prakarams. At the entrance, there is a small gopuram adorned with stucco sculptures of the Panchamurthis. After passing through that entrance, one first sees Nagaabharana Pillaiyar in a separate shrine.

Next, there is a large Nandi made of stucco. To the north, there is a pandal darshan mandapam and a cow mandapam, and to the south, there is a mukthi mandapam and Devatheertham. After passing through the front entrance of the temple, there is a Chola gopuram with five tiers. After passing through that entrance, in the second prakaram, there is a Rajadhani mandapam in the middle. To the east, there are shrines for Vinayagar, Pazhaniyandavar, Idumban, and the temple of Adhipathar. To the south, there is a Mani Mandapam, a Nandavanam, a well, and to the west, there are temples for Vallamai Ganapathi, Kali, a mango tree, and Veerabhadra.

To the north, there are the shrine of Athmanathar, the Vasantha Mandapam, and the Yagasalai. Adjacent to the Rajadhani Mandapam are the flagstaffs for the Lord and the Goddess, and to the north, facing south, is the Goddess’s temple.

Next, there is a second gopuram entrance with three tiers. In that entrance, there are Sengazhineer Vinayagar and Arumugapperuman. We circumambulate the first prakaram after worshipping Adhikaranandi and Vinayagar. To the south of the entrance are Surya and Chandra, and to the south, in the Thiru-Maligai Pathi, are the sixty-three Nayanmars and the Samayacharyars. To the west, the deities such as Mavadi Pillaiyar, Karmukeesar, Murugapperuman, and Gajalakshmi shine. To the north, there are Shani Bhagavan, installed by Dasaratha, and the Navagrahas.

Next, there is the Natarajar Mandapam. To the east, there are Bhairavar and Chandra. In front of the Sangu Mandapam, on the pillars, there are bas-reliefs of Pundarika Munivar and King Salisuka. In the Sangu Mandapam, Lord Natarajar gave darshan. Bhikshatanar and Adhipathar’s Utsava Vigrahas are present. In the niches surrounding the Moolavar’s Vimanam, to the south is Dakshinamurthy, to the west is Lingodbhavar, and to the north are Brahma, Ardhanareeswarar, Durga, and Bhikshatanar.

The temple is divided into two parts: to the south, the Thyagesar shrine, and to the north, the Kayarohanar shrine, both facing east. Adjacent to the Sangu Mandapam is the Maha Mandapam, and next to it is the Ardha Mandapam. At the entrance of the sanctum sanctorum, the Dvarapalakas shine with Chola artistic style. Kayarohana Peruman, in the form of a Shiva Lingam, captivates our hearts as a wonderful deity. Behind, in a separate niche, Peruman appears as Somaskandar, in a form that grants grace to devotees as both male and female. In the Maha Mandapam, after worshipping Panchamukha Vinayagar, Villendhiya Murugan, Pundarika Munivar, and the processional deities, we reach the Goddess’s shrine.

The Goddess’s temple shines with unique splendor. Mother Nilayatakshi shines as a creeper whose beauty is unmatched by anyone. Nearby, there is a shrine for Adipooramman. Around this sacred place, there are other sacred Shiva temples that have been sung about, such as Sikkal, Keezhvelur, Devur, Ettukudi, Thirumarugal, and Thirusaththamangai.

Here, the Vidangar in the Thyagaraja Peruman shrine is named Sundara Vidangar. The dance of Thyagaraja here is the Tharanga Natanam.

Now, the Theerthams: the Pundarika Theertham to the west of the temple, the Deva Theertham near the Mukthi Mandapam, the Uppanaru, also called Devanadi, flowing to the west of the town, and the sea. The sea is considered the most important Theertham of this place. On the days of Adi and Thai Amavasai, and Masi Magam, and Adhipathar festival, the Lord grants Theertham in the sea. Six daily pujas are performed in this place every day. Vaikasi. The Brahmotsavam takes place.

In the month of Ani, on Krishna Ashtami, the Sapthasthana festival takes place.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal came to Thiru-Nagaikkaronam, worshipped, and sang a Pathikam, praying to the Lord to grant him all the wealth, such as pearl necklaces, diamond necklaces, musk paste, gold ingots, and horses, which are royal possessions, so that he could live a great life with two wives and worship alongside the three kings. He received all of them. The Nagaikkaronam Puranam, composed by Mahavidvan Meenakshi Sundaram Pillai, exists for this place. There is also a Sthala Varalaru written by Panchanatham Pillai. There are individual songs about Nagai sung by Kalamegha Pulavar. There are Nanmani Malai written by Karunthittaigudi Saminatha Pillai and Meykandavelar Thiruppugal sung by Azhagumuthu Pillai.

Arunagirinathar’s Thiruppugal are dedicated to Lord Muruga of this place. Nagai is also one of the Saptha Vidanga Sthalams. We know that King Muchukunda received seven Thyagesar idols and Vidanga Shiva Linga Murtis from Indra and installed and worshipped them in seven places, including Thiruvarur. Among them, Thiruvarur is the foremost and most glorious. Thiru-Nagai is one of these seven Vidanga Sthalams. The Thyagaraja Peruman here is called Sundara Vidangar, and his dance is called Paravara Tharanga Natanam.

The Vidangar of this place is made of honey-colored Gomedakam. The Thyagesar dance is also called Sukshma Panchakshara Natanam and Uravu Poli Natanam. In the Adhipattha Nayanar Puranam, Sekkizhar Peruman has sung about the glory of this city and the greatness of Adhipathar. The festival where the Lord granted grace to Adhipathar takes place annually in the month of Avani. Adiseshan, distressed by not having children, came here as advised by Vasishta Munivar and worshipped the Lord in Kudanthai in the morning, in Nageswaram at noon, in Pambaram in the evening, and in Nagai at midnight. By the grace of the Lord, a female child was born.

He was saddened to know that she had three breasts. The Lord, as an ethereal voice, blessed him, saying, “One breast will disappear when she sees her husband.” The daughter grew up and reached puberty.

King Salisuka, born in the Chola dynasty, saw her. One of the Naga maiden’s breasts disappeared. As blessed by the Lord, Salisuka married the Naga maiden. Adiseshan also worshipped the Lord with gratitude and received the boon that this town should be known by his name.

Thus, this city came to be known as Nagai. Pundarika Munivar, born as the greatly ascetic son of Karuthamar Munivar in Vedapuram on the banks of the Yamuna, and Vamadevar. As per the words of Kanvar and others, he came to Nagaikkaronam and worshipped the Lord and the Goddess, and performed penance to attain the Lord with this body and be blissful.

Lord Shiva appeared to him and, taking the sage with his body, ascended him to Thiru-Kailash. During the time of deluge, twelve suns united and caused heat in the world. The world was disturbed, and living beings suffered. Thirumal, Brahma, and the seven sages, Markandeyar, Gautamar, Vasishtar, Kashyapar, Pulastiyar, Agasthiyar, and Angirasar, came to this place and worshipped the Lord.

The Lord appeared from the Moolalingam and protected Brahma at the base of the Lingam, Thirumal in the middle, and the sages at the top.

After the deluge, everyone came out and lived by performing their respective duties. Since all the gods resided here, this city is called Sivarajadhani, and because it is very ancient, it is called. Adhipuranam.

The Lord is called Adhipuranar. Dasaratha, the king of Ayodhya, learned from astrologers that the world would suffer from lack of rain if Shani entered the Rohini star. As per the sun’s advice, he worshipped the Lord of this place, installed Shani, and saved the living beings of the world. There are many inscriptions in this place. These are the Sthala Viseshams and Puranic stories about Thiru-Nagaikkaronam. We saw that Appar Swamigal came here on his way from Thiru-Maraikkadu to Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, worshipped the Lord of this place, and sang Thiru-Pathikams.

There are four Thiru-Pathikams composed by Appar Swamigal for this place. The first of them is the seventy-first Thiru-Pathikam of the fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Nerishai Thiru-Pathikam.

Wife, mother, father, children. kaḷ maṟṟuḷḷa cuṟṟameṉṉum viyuḷē viḻuntaḻunti vētaṉaikku iṭamākātē kaṉaiyumā kaṭalcūḻ nākai maṇṇu kāṟōṇattaṉai niṉaiyumāvalliṟākil uyyalām neñciṉīrē vaiyaṉai vaiyammuṇṭa māl aṅkaṅtōṉ mēṟkoṇṭa ceyyaṉai ceyya pōtir ticaimukaṉ ciramoṉṟu ēntum kaiyaṉai kaṭalcūḻ nākaikkāṟōṇam kōyil koṇṭa aiyyaṉai niṉainta neñcē ammaṉām uyntavārē niṟuttaṉai nimalantaṉṉai nīḻnilam veṇṇiṉmikka viruttaṉai vētatvittai viḷai poruḷ mūlamāṉa karuttaṉai kaṭalcūḻ nākaikkāṟōṇam kōyil koṇṭa oruttaṉai uṇartalāl nām uyntavā neñciṉīrē maṇṭaṉai iṟantu koṇṭa māyaṉōṭacurarvāṉōr teṇṭirai kaṭaiya vanta tīviṭam taṉṉai uṇṭa kaṇṭaṉai kaṭalcūḷ nākaikkāṟōṇam kōyil koṇṭa aṇṭaṉai niṉainta neñcē We are saved, O mind! He whose head is adorned with abundant waters, who wears the crescent moon and the serpent, who delights in the cremation ground with the sound of the Vedas, the Lord enshrined in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, if we praise Him daily, our suffering will turn into joy. He who wears the skin of a fierce, dark-trunked elephant, who burnt Kāma, who is praised by the world, the Lord of the celestials, the golden one enshrined in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, if we remember Him, we are surely saved. He who went as a hunter with the poor woman in the fierce forest, and bestowed the sharp arrow upon Pārtha after a battle, the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, where maidens’ dances never cease, we have been blessed to see Him day and night. He who, with one arrow, burnt the three cities of the deceitful ones, those who do not enter the minds of the wicked, the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, where the learned reside and praise Him, Those who have attained Him are born, and those who are born have not yet attained Him.

The ninth verse of this decad is not available to us.

Now, the tenth verse: The Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, whose lotus feet, when pressed by one toe, did not allow the demon Rāvaṇa to stand, with His two consorts, our Lord, the red-bodied serpent, stood with His sacred feet. Surely, we are saved.

Let us press on in meditation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Purāṇam, Part 427. Thiru-Nīṇṭa-Chāṟu-Kam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Purāṇam. We are meditating on the Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for the Thiru-Sthalam of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam. The second Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is the 103rd Thiru-Pathigam in the Fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Viruttam Thiru-Pathigam.

O Lord, who shares a form with the great mountain maiden, whose matted locks hold the Ganges, who resides in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by fragrant groves and the sea! What is this, that you ride a great white bull with a thunderous roar, while an elephant and a horse stand by? O Lord, whose eye is on the forehead, in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, where the learned reside! Your hand that held the bow, the hand of the long-eyed maiden, my good hand that wielded the great bow, your hand that destroyed the cities of your enemies, Tell me, what is it? O our Shankara, who burnt Kāma to ashes, who strung the soft flower-arrows and performed the fire sacrifice, who resides in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea, you bestow the five-letter mantra, “Namashivaya,” to those who praise your name.

You saved me from ending my life by following the path of the wicked, the bald-headed ascetics who follow the path of sin. O our Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea where the waves recede, grant that my lineage may be blessed. O Lord, whose dark eyes, red lips, and white teeth are praised by honey-tongued maidens who circumambulate and dance, who resides in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by fragrant groves and the sea, those who meditate on Him will not be separated from the divine prosperity. O Lord, the supreme light, who flayed the elephant with a trunk like a palm tree, who resides in Thiru-Nāgai, surrounded by the roaring sea, O Lord with an eye on your forehead, in Thiru-Kāṟōṇam! You removed my delusion from the ascetics and the bald-headed ones who abandoned their homes and ate no food. What more can I desire now?

O Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea and groves, rich in wealth and golden mountains! Is it not a wonder that you go begging for alms from maidens with full, soft breasts, and eat the alms you receive in the town? O our Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, where ships abound in the sea! We have a request for you, our Lord. You held the Ganges in your matted locks, and you gently hid the deceit from Umā, the maiden. You are not evil, our Lord.

The ninth verse of this decad is missing.

Now, the tenth verse: The Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, with the dark-eyed maiden, resided on the sacred mountain. He tried to lift it, but He did not do anything else, but only caused the ten heads and twenty arms to be crushed.

The third Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for the Thiru-Sthalam of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, the eighty-third Thiru-Pathigam in the Fifth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Kuṟunthogai Thiru-Pathigam.

Our karma will cease when we know Him who burnt the three cities with a bow, who wears the serpent as an ornament, who is pleasant to see, the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea. When we see the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, whose matted locks are adorned with buzzing bees, whom the celestials worship and praise, our karma will vanish. When we meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the roaring sea, who wears fresh, fragrant flowers on His matted locks, all our karma will disappear.

The Lord who rides the great bull, who dances at night, When we speak of the Lord who dances, the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by stone walls, our karma will vanish. There is no suffering for those who worship the true one, who rides the bull, who holds the white axe, the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, whose throat is dark, the Lord of the celestials. Those who circumambulate the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the turbulent sea, who is the ancient one with flowing matted locks, who desires the soft maiden as a part of Himself, their karma will disappear. Those who embrace the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by great walls, who is the fierce elephant, the excellent bull, the Lord praised by the celestials, their karma will disappear. The sorrows of those who meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by fragrant groves, who is praised by maidens of endless fame as ‘Our Lord,’ will surely cease.

The Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea, the Lord whom the two could not comprehend, those who do not understand the one, When we worship the warrior who shot the three cities, evil karma will be removed.

The Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea, whose foot pressed down on the demon who tried to lift the northern mountain, the fear of suffering will not approach.

Now, the fourth Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for the Thiru-Sthalam of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, the twenty-second Thiru-Pathigam in the Sixth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Thāṇṭakam Thiru-Pathigam.

He who is in Pazhanam, praised by the world, who is the mountain, who is the green parrot, who is the beautiful coral mountain, who wears the moon on His glorious crown, the Lord with a thousand names, who cannot be seen by others, He can always be seen in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by dark seas.

The Lord of the celestials, the hero, whose body is adorned with white ash, the female, He who is the male, who is the hermaphrodite, who resides in Thiru-Puli-Yūr, who is in Thiru-Aṇṇāmalai, who dances with the bull, the Lord who resides in Thiru-Ārūr, He can always be seen in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea.

The Lord of Thiru-Maṟaikkāṭu, Shiva-Lōkaṉ, where the bees sing, He who resides in Thiru-Vāymūr, Kīḻ-Vēḷūr, Vali-Valam, and Thiru-Vūr, the supreme one who resides in Thiru-Oṭṭiyūr, the supreme one who is attached to it, He can always be seen in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea. He who is the swan in the pond, who is in Thiru-Āchchirāmam, who made Thiru-Āṉaikkā His temple long ago, who is the form that became the three worlds, who wears small, many flowers and the white moon on His red matted locks, He who is in Thiru-Puṉṉai, surrounded by the virgin, He can always be seen in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea. He who rides a good bull, who is the great ocean of wisdom, who resides in Thiru-Nallūr, who holds the axe, who speaks only of goodness, the Lord with the blue throat, who resides in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, where the plantains grow in the ponds, He can always be seen. He who is the Lord of Thiru-Pukazhi, where the bees hum, who is the Kalpaka tree of Thiru-Pūmpukār, who resides in Thiru-Puṉkūr, who desired the Ganges on His matted locks, who wears a garland of skulls and a serpent as a belt, He can always be seen in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the turbulent sea. He who wears a garland of golden flowers and Konrai, who is the virtuous one, who smears white ash, who holds the trident, He who is in Thiru-Chirāppaḷḷi, Shiva-Lōkaṉ, who is the gem of the earth, who rides the bull, who is skilled in the Vedas, who resides in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by white waves, He can always be seen. He who holds the white skull and the white axe, who smears white ash, who flayed the fierce elephant, who is the golden one, who wears white ash, who can dance with fire in the eight directions, who resides in Thiru-Ēkampam, our Lord, He can always be seen in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by fertile fields.

He who is in Thiru-Chōṟṟuttuṟai, who removes ancient hell through the good path, who is the archer, who resides in Thiru-Mīyachchūr, who taught the Vedas to the four Vedic scholars, who wears the serpent on His chest, who is under the Banyan tree, He can always be seen in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by joy. O mind, do not consider as truth the lies of the ascetics who abandoned their homes, the lies of the bald-headed ones who speak of greatness, and the lies of those who wear the saffron robe. Only by clinging to the Lord who wears the elephant skin on His body can one see Him in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the southern sea. He can always be seen. The tall one and the lotus-born one searched, but could not find His true form. He who is the serpent, who loves the serpent, who dances with the serpent, who went begging for alms with a skull, who resides in Thiru-Nīṇṭiyūr, He can always be seen in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by fragrant groves.

Thus, we have meditated on the four Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for the Thiru-Sthalam of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having visited many shrines on his way, reaches Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. Let us go on meditating. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Purāṇam, Part 428. Thiru-Nīṇṭa-Chāṟu-Kam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Purāṇam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having returned to Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, worships the Lord of Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, performs sacred service, and sings Thiru-Pathigams.

During this time, the Nayanar’s desire to worship other shrines grew.

Therefore, he set out from Thiru-Vizhimizhalai and traveled along the banks of the Cauvery to worship the shrines. He went to worship the Thiru-Sthalams located on both banks of the Cauvery.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having set out, arrives at Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai. This is the shrine where the Lord, having accepted the worship performed by the Mother in the form of a cow, bestowed His grace upon her. Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai is the place where Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman, at the request of his father, Sivapāda Hṛdayar, for performing yagnas, prayed to the Lord, who then bestowed upon him a never-ending purse containing a thousand gold coins. We will discuss this in detail in the Purāṇam of Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having come to this glorious Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai, worships the Lord there and sings a Thiru-Pathigam. The Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai begins with “Māyiru Gnālamellām.” There are a total of five Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai.

We have already seen that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman had visited Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai during his pilgrimage and had composed four Thiru-Pathigams then.

Now, this Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar is the fifth Thiru-Pathigam composed for Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai. This Thiru-Pathigam is compiled as the fifty-sixth Thiru-Pathigam in the Fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Nērisai Thiru-Pathigam.

The entire great world worships His lotus feet, it seems. He keeps the great Ganges in His matted locks, it seems. He bestows a thousand gold coins to the people of Kaḻumalam, surrounded by dense groves, it seems. He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai. He is a part of the maiden, it seems.

He holds the deer in His hand, it seems. He is the Lord of Kuṭantai, it seems. He wears the tiger skin, it seems. He drank the poison that was churned, it seems. He burnt Kālan, it seems. He is loving to those who approach Him, it seems.

He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai. He cures diseases, it seems. He is the only support, it seems. He fought and burnt the three cities of His enemies, it seems. He is loving to those who are learned, who praise Him, who mingle with Him, who measure Him, and who sing. He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai.

He holds the axe in His hand, it seems. He is a part of the great maiden, He is the Lord who holds the sharp spear, it seems. He is adorned with bones, it seems. He is loving to those who worship, weep, dance, sing, and utter many praises. He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai. He is adorned with ash on His body, it seems.

He wears the sacred white thread, it seems. He rides a fierce bull, it seems. He burnt Kāma, it seems. He holds a skull, it seems. He measures the devotion of His devotees who praise Him with desire, it seems. He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai.

He bestowed the discus to Vishnu, who worshipped Him with His eye, it seems. He is the Lord of the demons, it seems. He casts the ignorant into sorrow, it seems. He is the Lord of the river bank, it seems. He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai. He has the bull as His banner, it seems.

He wears the white sacred thread, it seems. He holds the axe, it seems. He wears the leaping tiger skin, it seems. He wears the elephant skin, it seems. He is the world, it seems. He removes the sufferings of those who approach Him.

He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai. The ancient celestials came and worshipped Him in due order. Nandi and Mahākāla stood in the middle.
