He burnt the three cities of those who did not think, He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai, who wears the crescent moon on His evening sky. He who became a boar and dug the earth, Vishnu, and the lotus-born Brahma, who rides the swan, the Lord who has the sacred form to burn the wicked, He who rides the bull, He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai. He bestows grace upon Arjuna, it seems.

He has matted locks, it seems. He bestows joys to those who praise Him and removes their sufferings, it seems. He who dances and sings, who made the fierce demon cry out, He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai.

Thus, having worshipped Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai, he visits Thiru-Iṭaimarutūr, Thiru-Nāgēsuram, Thiru-Kuṭantai, Thiru-Valañchuḻi, and other shrines.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman arrives at the shrine called Thiru-Paḻaiyāṟai. He arrives at the Thiru-Kōyil of Paḻaiyāṟai Vaṭataḻi. There is a Shiva temple in Paḻaiyāṟai Vaṭataḻi. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman worships that temple with folded hands.

However, the Jains had hidden that temple and converted it into their Pāḻi (Jain temple).

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman stood firm, declaring that he would see the Lord’s form, remove the Jain Pāḻi, and worship the Lord’s temple when it became visible, and only then would he proceed further. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman made a request at the sacred feet of the Lord, saying, “Destroy this power of the Jains and reveal yourselves so that we may see you.” He sat down near the temple that the Jains had converted into their Pāḻi, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman observes a fast without partaking of any food. As Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman was fasting, Lord Shiva appeared in the dream of the king of that country and revealed that the Jains had hidden the temple. He also revealed the signs of the hidden Shiva temple and the signs of His presence to the king in his dream.

Therefore, Lord Shiva instructed the king in his dream to remove the encroachment of the Jains and enable Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to worship Lord Shiva. The king, understanding this, followed the signs revealed by Lord Shiva in his dream, removed the Jain Pāḻi, discovered the temple, purified it, and consecrated it. He then bowed at the sacred feet of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and informed him. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman went there, worshipped, and sang the Thiru-Pathigam, “Can it be hidden even if the Jains hide it?” and worshipped the Lord. This act of grace is to take place here at the sacred shrine of Paḻaiyāṟai Vaṭataḻi. The sacred shrine of Paḻaiyāṟai Vaṭataḻi is a unique shrine.

Paḻaiyāṟai is to its south-southwest. Paḻaiyāṟai Mēṟṟaḻi is another shrine to the northwest of Paḻaiyāṟai. We have meditated on this history in the Purāṇam of Amar-Nīti Nayanar.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having come to Paḻaiyāṟai Vaṭataḻi, worships the Vimana, the gross form of the Shiva temple, as Lord Shiva Himself, with folded hands.

At that time, the devotees present there said that the Jains had encroached upon the Lord’s temple and They say that they have converted it into their Jain Pāḻis.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, from a distance, worshipped Lord Shiva and the Shiva temple. Since it was encroached upon by the Jains, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman worshipped the Lord from outside without entering.

Thus, he made a request at the sacred feet of Lord Shiva to destroy the power of these Jains who had encroached upon the temple.

Here, we must note that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman requested to eliminate the deception of the Jains, not to eliminate or destroy the Jains themselves. Shaivism, as it is said, “Shaivism is a religion that encompasses all religions,” accepts and accommodates all other religions in a hierarchical order. It is an inner religion, an outer-inner religion, and an outer religion. Shaivism is a religion that embraces all other religions as progressive steps, and therefore, Shaivism does not spontaneously engage in conflict with any religion to destroy it. That is why Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman here states that the deception of the Jains should be destroyed, but he does not appeal to Shiva Peruman to destroy the Jains.

However, here, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and the Buddhists in Thiru-Alavai, Madurai, caused harm and suffering, attempting to corrupt the Vedic path. To prevent this, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman performed these sacred deeds. The Jains Here, they had concealed the Thiru-Koyil (temple), the Shiva-Alayam, and transformed it into a Jain school. Nevertheless, the Lord remained within, consenting to this. Not only that, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar was able to perceive and worship the Lord within with his mind’s eye. Even though he worshipped in this manner, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman appealed to the Lord, stating that the deception of these Jains, who had concealed the temple, must be eradicated.

This is because the people of the world would not know that the Lord was within and that the Jains had occupied it.

Therefore, for the Shaiva path to flourish undiminished in the world, and for him to be able to worship the Lord whom he had worshipped with his mind’s eye, with his physical eyes—for these two reasons, he desired that the Thiru-Koyil should be revealed, and the Lord within the Thiru-Koyil should be revealed. He prayed to the Lord, saying, “I will leave this place only after I have seen and worshipped You. I will not leave this place without seeing and worshipping You directly. I will proceed to the next Thalam only if I behold Your sacred form with my eyes. Otherwise, I will not depart from here.” Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having made this firm resolve to the Lord, achieved his desired outcome. He remained without food, fasting there.

It is a long-standing tradition and a noble path for us to fast, praying to the Lord for the fulfillment of our intentions and the completion of our desired actions.

Therefore, some believe that fasting is a new phenomenon that has emerged recently. Some people think that this method is new, but we realize through the sacred history of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman that it is a practice that has been with us for ages. Where is the beginning, where is the seed of this fasting that we undertake until our desired action is fulfilled? It is there when young children stubbornly refuse to eat to get what they want from their parents. The fasts observed by devotees who seek boons from God, by remaining hungry, are also based on this same concept. The subtlety of this is that the compassionate Primeval Lord, unable to bear the suffering of His fasting devotees, will fulfill their requests.

Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, being such a noble soul, Understanding this, he observes a fast here. At this juncture, Shiva Peruman appears in the dream of the king of that land and reveals that the Jains have concealed our temple, and that He is within, despite their concealment. Shiva Peruman reveals all the identifying marks of the Thiru-Koyil to the king in his dream.

Therefore, Shiva Peruman instructs the king in his dream, saying, “Go and remove the occupation of the Jains, and make arrangements for Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to enter and worship the Lord.” Shiva Peruman even accepts the concealment, revealing to the king in his dream that “concealment is also our state.” The Lord commands the king in his dream to destroy and remove the Jains who are without proper conduct. The Jains, who are without proper conduct, They are those who, not adhering to the bounds of their own path, harbor evil intentions to go against and destroy other religions.

Therefore, Shiva Peruman commands, “Remove such unrighteous Jains from this land.” The king, realizing the wondrous scene he saw in his dream, awakens. He explains it to his ministers. He understood the truth revealed by the Lord in his dream, through the signs the Lord had shown.

Thus, the king goes to the place occupied by the Jains. There, a thousand Jains had gathered together. Knowing that the king had arrived, a thousand Jains gathered there. Generally, there would be a thousand Jain gurus, and each Jain school would have a thousand gurus. It is customary for Jains to gather in thousands. In Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, the Jains had deceitfully occupied the Thiru-Koyil of Lord Shiva Peruman and established a Jain school there.

In that Jain school, similarly, a thousand Jain gurus were present. As the king arrived at this place, all those thousand Jains stood together. The king had his servants remove all those Jains from the place, driving them away. He removed the Vimanam (temple tower) of the Jain school, which the Jains had falsely established, and all their encroachments.

At that time, the Thiru-Koyil and the Vimanam of the Lord became visible.

Furthermore, he renovated, cleaned, and reconstructed the Thiru-Koyil. He reinstated the worship that had ceased there according to the Agamas. He established endowments for the performance of sacred ablutions, sacred offerings, daily rituals, and festivals. Shiva Peruman had revealed to the king in his dream, “Our government will worship, and remove the Jains.” Accordingly, the king, in order for Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to worship the Lord, removed the Jains, established the Vimanam for the Lord, and arranged for worship and offerings. Following the Lord’s command, he then went to Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, prostrated at his sacred feet, and offered special reverence. He informed Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman that the Lord had revealed Himself after the removal of the Jains.

At that time, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sang a Thiru-Pathikam (sacred hymn) with the meaning, “Even if the Jains, who pluck their hair and eat, conceal Him, can those who are unstable in their nature conceal Him?” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings a sacred hymn. Even if the Jains, who pluck all their hair and eat, conceal Him, can those who are unstable in their nature, with their limited intellect, conceal my Lord? This sacred hymn is the fifty-eighth Thiru-Pathikam in the fifth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam dedicated to Pazhaiyarai Vadathali.

“Thalaiyellam parikkum saman kaiyal nilaiyinan maraithan maraikkonnumae alaiyināru pozhil ārai vaḍathali nilaiyinān aḍiyē ninainthu uymminē” (Even if the Jains, who pluck all their hair, conceal Him, can those who are unstable conceal Him? O you who dwell in the beautiful groves of Arai Vadathali, remember His feet and be saved!) “Mūkkinal muran rōthiya kuṇṭikai thūkkinaar kulanthūr aṟuththē thanakkākkinān aṇi ārai vaḍathali” (He who carried the water pot with his nose, he who cut off the lineage of the wicked for himself, he who is in the beautiful Arai Vadathali) “Nōkkinārkku illai ālaru nōykalē” (Those who behold Him have no suffering.) “Kuṇṭarai guṇamillaraik kūraiyil miṇṭarai thuṟantha vimalan thannai aṇṭarai pazhaiyāṟai vaḍathazhi kaṇṭarai thozhuthuvaynthaṇa kaikaḷē” (My hands, having worshipped the pure one who abandoned the wicked, the immoral, and the quarrelsome, and who is in Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, are saved.) “Muḍaiyaṟai thalaimuṇṭikkum moṭṭarai kaḍaiyaṟai kaḍinthārkaṇal veṇmazhu paḍaiyaṟai pazhaiyāṟai vaḍathali uḍaiyaṟai kuḷirnthu uḷkum en uḷḷamē” (My heart, cooled and embraced, belongs to the Lord of Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, who wields the fiery white axe, who punished those who shaved their heads and were base.) “Oḷḷarikkaṇār munna maṇ ṇiṉṟuṇum kallarai kaḍintha karuppūralai aḷḷalam puṉal ārai vaḍathali vallalai pugazhath thuyar vāḍumē” (Praising the mighty one of Arai Vadathali, who punished the stony-hearted who ate before women, my sorrow will wither.) “Nīthiyai keḍa niṉṟamaṉēyuṇañcāthiyai keḍumā ceytha caṅkaran āthiyai pazhaiyāzhai vaḍathazhiccōthiyai thozhuvār thuyarthīrumē” (Those who worship the primordial light of Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, Shankaran, who destroyed the caste that stood to destroy justice, their sorrows will cease.) “Thiraṭṭiṟaikka vaḷanthiṇikkum camaṇ piraṭṭaṟai piriththa perumān thanai aruṭṭiṟa thaniyāṟai vaḍathali the” (The Lord who separated the deceitful Jains who gathered wealth, the unique one of Arai Vadathali, the divine one) “Iruṭṭaṟai thozha thīviṉai thīrumē” (Worshipping in the dark chamber, evil deeds will cease.) “Ōthiṉa theḻuththañcuṇarā camaṉ vēthiṉai paḍuththāṉai veṅkūṟṟu uthai pāthaṉai paḻaiyārai vaḍathali nāthaṉai thozha nam viṉai nācamē” (Worshipping the Lord of Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, who caused suffering to the Jains who did not understand the five letters, and whose foot kicked the fierce Yama, our karma will be destroyed.) “Vāyirunthamiḻē pāḍi thāḷu āyirañcamaṉum aḻivākkiṉāṉ pāyirum puṉal ārai vaḍathalimēyavaṉ eṉa valviṉai vīḍumē” (Singing in sweet Tamil, he destroyed a thousand Jains. Saying that he is the one who resides in Arai Vadathali with flowing waters, strong karma will cease.) “Ceruththaṉai ceyyum cē narakaṉ uḍal eruththira viralāl iṟai ūṉṟiya aruththaṉai paḻaiyārai vaḍathali thiruththaṉai thozhuvār thirucciṟṟampalam” (Those who worship the Lord of Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, who pressed down the body of the demon who caused war with his toe, will attain Thiruchitrambalam.) Thus, after the concealed Thiru-Koyil in Pazhaiyarai Vadathali was revealed, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman went there, sang, and worshipped the Lord.

He then continued his pilgrimage to many Thalam where Shiva Peruman resides on both banks of the Kaveri, offering Tamil garlands of praise and worshipping the Lord. He continues his pilgrimage, worshipping the Thalam on both banks of the Kaveri.

Let us go on reflecting. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 429, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having departed from Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, journeyed westward, visiting the Thalam on the northern and southern banks of the Kaveri. Sekkizhar Peruman sings, “He entered the places where the Lord of the bull resides, on both banks of the Kaveri, filled with abundant waters, worshipped, offered Tamil garlands, and then, with his fame spread everywhere, he was met by countless devotees and reached Thiru-Anaikka, the abode of the Lord with the red-eyed bull.” As we mentioned earlier, Sekkizhar Peruman states in this verse that he departed westward from Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, visited the Thalam on both sides of the Kaveri, and reached the Thalam called Thiru-Anaikka.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman visits many Thalam from Pazhaiyarai Vadathali to Thiru-Anaikka. These Thalam include Thiru-Pattiswaram, Arai Metrali, Thiru-Valanjuzhi, Thiru-Poonthuruthi, Thiru-Kandiyur, Thiru-Sotrutthurai, Thiru-Vethikudi, Thenkudi Thittai, Thiru-Pullamangai, Thiru-Chakkarappalli, Thiru-Vaiyaaru, Thiru-Nethanam, Thiru-Alampozhil, Thiru-Perumpuliyur, Thiru-Mazhapadi, Thiru-Pazhuvur, Thiru-Kanoor, Thiru-Anbil Alanthurai, Thiru-Manthurai, Thiru-Palathurai, and so on.

However, the Pathikam (hymns) sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar for all these Thalam are not available to us. However, we have received Pathikam by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for some of these sacred Thalam. These Thalam are Thiru-Alampozhil, Thiru-Kanoor, Thiru-Anbil Alanthurai, Thiru-Vethikudi, Thiru-Kandiyur, Melai Thiru-Kattuppalli, These are the Thalam for which Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s Thiru-Pathikam are available.

Therefore, let us examine them one by one. The first Thalam is Thiru-Alampozhil. For this Thalam, one Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathikam sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is available. This sacred Thalam, Thiru-Alampozhil, is located near Thiru-Poonthuruthi in Thanjavur district. It is the tenth Thalam on the southern bank of the Kaveri. It is a Thalam where the Vasus worshipped and attained blessings.

The sanctum faces west. The Lord’s sacred name is Athmanathar. The Goddess’s sacred name is Gnanaambikai. The sacred water is the Kaveri Theertham. The sacred tree is the Banyan tree. This Thiru-Koyil is known as Arulmigu Vadamooleswarar Koyil.

Opposite the temple is a sacred tank. There is a five-tiered gopuram. Upon entering, one can worship the Thala Vinayagar and Murugan, then the Durga in the northern prakaram, and In the southern prakaram, one can worship Dakshinamurthy Peruman and then reach the Lord’s sanctum.

First, there is the Maha Mandapam, where the Navagrahas are located. One can worship the Ambāl’s sanctum here. After worshipping Vinayagar and reaching the Ardha Mandapam, one can worship the Nalvar. The Lord’s sanctum faces west. Swami is enshrined here as Arulmigu Vada Mooleswarar and Athmanathar. After worshipping Swami and Gnanaambikai, one can return.

This sacred Thalam, Thiru-Alampozhil, is mentioned in Thevaram as belonging to Then Parambaikkudi. Pirambai is now known as Pirambur. This Pirambur, where Vellalars reside, is called Vellamparambur. A short distance south of Alampozhil is a place called Sambandar Medu. We will discuss this in detail in the Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman Puranam. Kashyapar, Nagar, and the Ashtavasus worshipped the Lord here and attained blessings.

These are notes about the Thiru-Alampozhil Thalam. Here is the Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, the eighty-sixth Thiru-Pathikam of the sixth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathikam.

“Karuvāki kaṇṇuthalāy niṉṟāṉ taṉṉai kamalaththōṉ thalaiyariṉtha kāpāliyai uruvārntha malaimakaḷūr pākaththāṉai uṇarvellām āṉāṉai ōcaiyāki varuvāṉai valañcozhiyam perumān taṉṉai maṟaikkāḍum āvaḍu thaṉ thuṟaiyum mēya thiruvāṉai theṉ parampaikkuḍiyiṉ mēya thiru ālampozhilāṉai cinthi neñcē” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who resides in Then Parambaikkudi, who is the embryo, who has an eye on his forehead, who is the Kapali who cut off the head of Brahma, who has the beautiful mountain daughter as a part of himself, who is all consciousness, who comes as sound, who is the Lord of Valanjuzhi, who resides in Maraikkadu and Avaduthurai.) “Uritthāṉai kaḷirathaṉ thōl pōrvaiyāka uḍaiyāṉai uḍaippuliyiṉathalēyāka thariththāṉai caḍaiyathaṉmēl kaṅkai aṅkai thaḻal uruvai viḍam amuthā uṇḍi ithallām pariththāṉai pavaḷamāl varaiyanāṉai pāmpaṉaiyāṉ thaṉakkaṉṟaṅ” (He who wore the elephant’s skin as a covering, who wore the tiger’s skin as a garment, who bore the Ganga on his matted locks, who consumed poison as nectar, who is the coral mountain, who is the one for the serpent-bedecked one.) “Kaḷi nalki ciriththāṉai theṉparampaik kuḍiyiṉmēya thiruvālampozhilāṉai cinthi neñcē” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who resides in Then Parambaikkudi, who laughed with joy.) “Uru mūṉṟāy uṇarviṉ kaṇ oṉṟu āṉāṉai ōṅkāra meypporuḷai uḍampiṉ uḷḷāl karu īṉṟa veṅkaḷavai aṟivāṉ taṉṉai kālaṉai thaṉ kaḻal aḍiyāl kāynthu māṇikku aruḷ īṉṟa ār amuthai amararkōṉai aḷḷūri emperumān eṉpārkku eṉṟum thiruvīṉṟa theṉparampai kuḍiyiṉmēya thiruvālampozhilāṉai cinthi neñcē” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who resides in Then Parambaikkudi, who is the three forms, who is one in consciousness, who is the true meaning of Om, who knows the fierce deceit born within the body, who kicked Yama with his sacred foot, who bestowed grace upon Markandeya, who is the rare nectar, who is the Lord of the celestials, who is our Lord in Allur, who always bestows prosperity.) “Pārmuzhuthāy vicumpāki pāthāḷamām paramparaṉai curumpamarum kuzhalāl pākaththār amuthām aṇi thillai kūththaṉ taṉṉai vāṭpōkki ammāṉai emmāṉ eṉṟu vāramathām aḍiyārkku vāramāki vañcaṉai ceyvārkku eṉṟum vañcaṉākum cīraracai theṉ parampaikkuḍiyiṉmēya thiruvālam pozhilāṉai cinthi neñcē” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who resides in Then Parambaikkudi, who is the whole earth, the sky, and the netherworld, who is the Supreme Being, who has the honey-like tresses as a part of himself, who is the beautiful Thillai dancer, who is our Lord of Vatpokki, who is always dear to his devotees, and who is always deceitful to those who deceive, who is the glorious king.) “Varaiyārntha maḍamaṅkai paṅkaṉ taṉṉai vāṉavarkkum vāṉavaṉai maṇiyai” (He who has the mountain maiden as his half, who is the Lord of the celestials, who is a gem.) “Muṭṭai aṟaiyārntha puliththōl mēl aṟavam mārththa ammāṉai thammāṉai aḍiyārkku eṉṟum puṟaiyārntha kōvaṇaththu em puṉithaṉtaṉṉai pūnthurutthi mēyāṉai pukalūrāṉai thiraiyārntha theṉparampai kuḍiyiṉmēya thiruvālampozhilāṉai cinthi neñcē” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who resides in Then Parambaikkudi, who is our Lord, who wore the serpent over the tiger skin, who is our pure one with the sacred loincloth, who resides in Poonthuruthi, who is the Lord of Pukalur, who is in the wave-filled Then Parambaikkudi.) “Virinthāṉai kuvinthāṉai vēthaviththai viyaṉ piṟappōḍu iṟappāki niṉṟāṉ taṉṉai aṟinthāṉai calantharaṉ thaṉ uḍalam vēṟā āḻkaḍal nañcuṇḍu imaiyōrellām uyya parinthāṉai pallasurar puṟaṅkaḷ mūṉṟum pāḻpaḍuppāṉ cilai malai nāṇēṟṟi ambu therinthāṉai theṉparampaik kuḍiyiṉmēya thiruvālampozhilāṉai cinthi neñcē” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who resides in Then Parambaikkudi, who expanded and contracted, who is the seed of the Vedas, who stands as vast birth and death, who knew, who consumed the poison of the deep sea to save all the celestials, who destroyed the body of Salandhara, who strung the bow of the mountain and chose the arrow to destroy the three cities of the many asuras.) “Pollātha eṉ aḻukkil pukuwāṉ eṉṉai puṟam puṟamē cōthiththa puṉithaṉ taṉṉai ellārum taṉṉaiyē ikaḻa annāḷ iḍupali eṉṟu akaṇṭiriyum emperumāṉai collāthār avarthamai collāthāṉai thoḍarnthu taṉ poṉṉaḍiyē pēṇuvārai cellātha neṟi celuththa vallāṉ taṉṉai thiruvālam pozhilāṉai” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who is the pure one who entered my evil filth and tested me outwardly, who is our Lord who wandered begging for alms on that day when everyone reviled him, who does not speak of those who do not speak of him, who is capable of leading those who follow and cherish his golden feet on the path that cannot be traversed.) “Ainthalaiththa nākaṉai kiḍantha māḷōḍu ayaṉthēḍi nāḍariya ammāṉ taṉṉai panthaṇavu melviralāḷ pākaththāṉai parāyththuṟaiyum veṇkāḍum payiṉṟāṉ taṉṉai poṇthudaiya veṇthalaiyil palikoḷvāṉai pūvaṇamum puṟampayamum porunthiṉāṉai cinthiya veṇthīviṉaikaḷ thīrppāṉ taṉṉai thiruvālampozhilāṉai cinthi neñcē” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who is the Lord whom Vishnu, lying on the five-headed serpent, and Brahma searched for but could not find, who has the soft-fingered maiden as his half, who frequented Paraythurai and Venkadu, who receives alms in a skull with a hole, who is in Poovanam and Purambayam, who removes the white evil deeds that are thought of.) “Kaiyil uṇḍu uḻalvārum cākkiyarum kallātha vaṉmūṭkallāthāṉai poyyilāthavarkkeṉṟum poyyilāṉai pūṇākam nāṉāka poṟuppuvillā kaiyiṉār ambeṟik kāl īrkkum kōlā kaḍunthavaththōr neḍum puṟaṅkaḷ kaṉalvāy vīḻththa ceyyiṉār theṉ parampai kuḍiyiṉmēya thiruvālampozhilāṉai cinthi neñcē” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who resides in Then Parambaikkudi, who is not for those who wander eating with their hands, nor for the Sakyas, nor for the ignorant, who is always truthful to the truthful, who made the serpent his ornament, who held the bow without a mountain, who shot arrows with his hand, who caused the long cities of the severe ascetics to fall into the fiery mouth.) The tenth verse in this Thiru-Pathikam is not available to us.

Next, the Thiru-Pathikam for the sacred Thalam called Thiru-Kanoor. Thiru-Kanoor is the fifty-sixth Thalam among the northern bank Thalam of the Kaveri in the Chola country.

Here, when the Goddess was in Shiva-Yoga, the Lord appeared as a blazing flame and granted His vision.

Therefore, Swami is known as Semmeninathar, and the Goddess is known as Shivayoga Nayaki. Thiru-Kanoor is a very small village. The temple is located on the southern bank of the Kollidam river. It is said that at one time, the temple was covered by an earthen mound, and later, the temple kalasam (finial) was struck by boys playing with cows, leading to the discovery of the temple. In recent times, new renovation works have been carried out, and the temple looks beautiful. The sanctum faces east, and there is a three-tiered Raja Gopuram.

Inside, the Ambāl’s sanctum faces south. There is one prakaram, a sacred kitchen, a well, and Nandavanams (flower gardens). In the western prakaram, there are temples for Vinayagar and Murugan, and in the northern prakaram, There are temples for Durga and Chandeesar. After passing the Nandi and Balipeetam, upon entering the Swami temple, there are shrines for the Nalvar, Bhairavar, Sastha, and others. Swami is known as Arulmigu Arumbeswarar. In Thevaram, he is referred to as Kanoor Mulai.

We have received one Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for this Thalam. The sacred trees are Vanni, Vilvam, and Sugarcane. The Kollidam is the sacred water. The Vimanam is a single-tiered, round-shaped Vimanam. The Ambāl’s idol is said to be a Salagrama idol. The Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for this sacred Thalam is the seventy-sixth Thiru-Pathikam of the fifth Thiru-Murai.

“Thiruvin nāthaṉum cemmalar mēlurai oruvaṉāy ulakaththiṉ uyirkkellām karuvaṉāki muḷaiththavaṉ kāṉūril paramaṉāy parañca” (The Lord of prosperity, the unique one residing on the red lotus, who became the embryo for all living beings in the world, who sprouted in Kanoor, who is the Supreme Being, the Supreme Light.) “Suḍar kāṇamiṉē” (Behold the light!) “Peṇḍir makkaḷ perunthuṇai naṉṉithi uṇḍiṉṟē eṉṟu ukavaṉmiṉ ēḻaikāḷ kaṇḍu koṇmiṉ nīr kāṇūr muḷaiyiṉai puṇḍarīkap pothumpil othukkiyē” (O ignorant ones, do not rejoice saying, “Wives, children, great help, wealth, food are here.” Behold the sprout of Kanoor, hidden in the lotus pond.) “Thāyaththār thamar naṉṉithi eṉṉum immāyaththē kiḍanthiṭṭu mayaṅkiḍēl kāyaththēyuḷaṉ kāṇūr muḷaiyiṉai vāyaththāl vaṇaṅkīr viṉai māyavē” (Do not be deluded by this illusion called relatives, kinsmen, and good wealth. The sprout of Kanoor is within the body. Worship it with your mouth for karma to vanish.) “Kuṟiyil niṉṟuṇḍu kūṟaiyilā camaṉ neṟiyai viṭṭu niṟai kaḻal paṟṟiṉēṉ aṟiyaluṟṟirēl kāṇūr muḷaiyavaṉ ceṟivu ceythiṭṭu iruppathu eṉ cinthayē” (I have abandoned the path of the Jains who eat without clothes and have grasped the full feet. If you wish to know, the sprout of Kanoor is firmly established in my mind.) “Poththal maṇcuvar pollā kuṟampaiyai meythaṉeṉṟu viyaṅkiḍēl ēḻaikāḷ ciththar paththarkaḷ cēr thiru kāṇūril aththaṉ pātham aḍaithal karumamē” (O ignorant ones, do not marvel at this leaky mud wall, this evil hut, thinking it is real.

It is indeed a duty to attain the feet of the Lord in Thiru-Kanoor, where Siddhas and devotees gather.) “Kalvi ñāṉa kalaiporuḷāy avaṉ celvamalku thiru kāṇūr īcaṉai elliyum pakal” (The Lord of Thiru-Kanoor, who is the essence of education, knowledge, and arts, who is full of wealth, day and night.) “Icaivāṉava colliḍīr nuṇ thuyaraṅkaḷ thīravē” (Speak of him who is agreeable, so that subtle sorrows may cease.) “Nīrum pāṟum neruppum aṟukkaṇuṅ kāru māṟuthaṅ kāṇōr muḷaiththavaṉ cērvum oṉṟaṟiyāthu thicai thicai ōrvum oṉṟila rōḍi thirivarē” (They wander in all directions, not knowing the union of water, earth, fire, and air, nor the sprout that appeared, nor any thought.) “Ōmaththōḍaya mālaṟiyāvaṉam vīmappēroḻiyāy viḻupporuḷ kāmaṟkāynthavaṉ kāṇōr muḷaiththavaṉ cēmaththāl iruppu āvathu eṉ cinthayē” (My mind is a safe abode for the sprout that appeared in Kanoor, who is the noble substance, the great light, unknown to Brahma and Vishnu, who burnt Kama.) The ninth verse in this Thiru-Pathikam is not available.

Now, the tenth verse: “Vaṉṉi koṉṟai erukku aṇinthāṉ malai uṉṉiyē ceṉṟeḍuththavaṉ oṉ thiral taṉṉai vīḻa taṉi viral vaiththavaṉ kaṇṇimā mathil kāṇōr karuththaṉē” (He who adorned himself with Vanni, Konrai, and Erukku, who placed his single toe to make the one who went to lift the mountain fall, he is the Lord of Kanoor with the beautiful great walls.)

Now, the next Thalam is Thiru-Anbil Alan Thurai. This sacred Thalam is the fifty-seventh Thalam on the northern bank of the Kaveri. It is known as Anbil. Lower Anbil, Anbil, Ambil, Anbil Alan. The Lord’s sacred names are Sathiyavakeeswarar, Brahmapureeswarar, and Alanthuraiyar. The Goddess’s sacred name is Soundaryanayaki.

The sthala tree is the Banyan, and the sacred water is Chandra Pushkarani. The village is Anbil, and the temple is Alanthurai. The Vinayagar here is known as Sevisaaitha Vinayagar (the listening Vinayagar). He is called so because he listened attentively to the sacred hymns of Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, sung from the south bank of the Kollidam river. Parantaka Chola settled 108 Agnihotris in this sthalam. Because he blessed their Jaimini Sama Veda recitation, this Vinayagar is also known as Samagana Ketta Vinayagar (the Vinayagar who heard the Sama Veda).

Later, he adopted the name Sevisaaitha Vinayagar, having listened to the songs of Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman’s sacred hymn: one. Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal’s sacred hymn: one.

Thus, there are two sacred hymns for this sthalam. Beside the Dvarapalakas, there is a sculpture of Brahma worshipping. The Moolavar (presiding deity) is a Shiva Lingam, a Swayambhu Murthy (self-manifested idol) with a square pedestal. The sacred hymn by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal for this sthalam is the 80th hymn of the Fifth Thirumurai, a Thirukkurunthogai hymn.

“Vaananjer mathi soodiya mainthanai nee nenje keduvai ninaikkirkilai aananjaadiyai anbil alanthurai kon en selvanai kooridagittriye kaaranaththar karuththar kapaaliyar vaaranaththuri poorththa manaalanar aaranapporul anbil alanthurai naaranarkku ariyaan oru nambiye anbinna nanjamainthuda naadiya enbin aanaiyuriththuk kalainthavan anbilanai ammaanai allooriy anbinnaal ninainthaar arinthaargale.” Gloss: “Oh heart, you will perish if you do not remember the Lord who wears the moon, who danced with the elephant, the king of Anbil Alanthurai, my Lord. He is the cause, the thought, the skull-bearer, the groom who wears the elephant hide. He is the essence of the Vedas, unknown even to Narayana in Anbil Alanthurai, a trustworthy one. Those who remembered with love the Lord who removed the poison with love and wore the elephant hide, they understood.” “Sankaiyullathum saavathum meyyumai panganaar adipaaviyen naan uyya angann enthai anbil alanthurai sengkannaaradi seravum vallane kokkiragar kulirmathi senniyar mikkarakkar purameri seythavar akkarainar anbil alanthurai nakkuruvarum nammai arivare vellamulla virisadai nanthiyai kallamulla manaththavar kaankilaar allalaar vayal anbil alanthurai ullavaaru ariyaar silar oomare piravi maaya pinakkil aluthinum uravellam sinthiththu unni ugavaathe aravan embiraan anbil alanthurai maravaathe tholuthu eththi vanangume nunangu noolaiyan maalum iruvarum pinangiyengum thirinthu eyththung kaankila anangan embiraan anbil alanthurai vanangum numvinai maaintharum vanname poyyellam uraikkum saman saakkiya kaiyan.” Gloss: “I, a sinner at the feet of the Lord who shares His body with the Truth, can I reach the red-eyed feet of my Lord in Anbil Alanthurai to be saved?

“The Lord with the cool moon on His head, who destroyed the cities of the mighty Rakshasas, the Lord of Anbil Alanthurai, will also know us. Those with deceitful hearts cannot see Nandi with the flowing matted locks. Some in Anbil Alanthurai, with its fertile fields, are mute, not knowing the truth. Even if entangled in the illusory bonds of birth, do not think of all relations and rejoice. Worship and praise our Lord, the righteous one, in Anbil Alanthurai, without forgetting. The subtle-threaded Brahma and Vishnu, though they wandered everywhere in conflict and grew weary, could not see the formless Lord in Anbil Alanthurai.

“Worship Him, and your karma will be destroyed. The deceitful Jain and Buddhist who speak all falsehoods.” “Maarurai kelaathu eluminno aiyan embiraan anbil alanthurai meiyan sevadi etruvaar meyyare ilangai venthan irupathu thol itru malanga maamalai mel viral vaiththavan alangal embiraan anbil alanthurai valangolvaarai vaanor valangolvare Thiruchitrambalam thodarnthu sinthippom Thiruchitrambalam.” Gloss: “Rise up, do not listen to opposing words! Those who accept the true sacred feet of our Lord in Anbil Alanthurai are indeed true.

“The Lord who placed His finger on the great mountain, causing the twenty shoulders of the king of Lanka to wither and fall, our garlanded Lord in Anbil Alanthurai. Those who circumambulate Him will be circumambulated by the celestials.

“We shall continue our meditation.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 430. We are contemplating the sacred hymns available to us from the sthalams visited by Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman on his way to Thiru-anaikka. In that sequence, the next sacred sthalam is Thiru-vedikudi. It is located in Thanjavur district, near Thiru-kandiyur, on the way from Thanjavur to Thiru-vaiyaru. This sthalam is called Vedikudi because Brahma worshipped here.

It is also called Vedikudi because the Vedas worshipped here.

The Lord is known as Vedapureeswarar. He also bears the sacred name Aara Amudhunathar. The Goddess shines with the sacred name Mangaiyarkarasi. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman each sang one sacred hymn, making a total of two Thevara sacred hymns for this sacred sthalam. Thiru-vaiyaru, Aiyaru. This is the fourth of the seven sthalams in the Sapthasthana festival that takes place in the month of Chithirai.

At the Lord’s shrine, Vinayagar, who listens attentively to the Vedas expounded by the Lord with His four sacred faces, is known as Veda Vinayagar. The sacred water, Veda Theertham, is located opposite the temple. The sthala tree, the Vilva tree, is in the northern prakaram. The temple faces east. Opposite the temple, across the street, is the Veda Theertham. At one time, the current structure had two prakarams, but now there is only one.

The Goddess’s temple is in the second outer prakaram. Adjacent to the Nandi and Balipitam, the Goddess’s temple faces south. Next to the Goddess’s temple is the Vasantha Mandapam. After worshipping these, one can enter the temple. Passing through the small Rajagopuram with three tiers, one enters the temple to find the Maha Mandapam. The Natarajar Sabai is located here.

As one circumambulates the temple, 108 Shiva Lingams are consecrated in rows in the Thiru-maligai sections. In the Garbhagriha Koshtams, Dakshinamurthy is to the south, Ardhanareeswarar to the west, and Brahma to the north. In the western prakaram, one can worship Durga, Vinayagar, Murugan, and Mahalakshmi before reaching the Lord’s shrine. At the entrance to the Snapana Mandapam, Vinayagar and Murugan are visible. Entering the Ardha Mandapam, we are at the shrine. At the shrine, we can behold Vinayagar as Sevisaaitha Vinayagar, with his left leg raised.

It is believed that Vinayagar is listening to the Vedas, which the Lord expounds in this sthalam.

The Lord has a large form. Utsava Murthies (processional deities) are in the Ardha Mandapam, near the Natarajar shrine. The ancient and beautiful idol of the Goddess is located here. The sacred hymn by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal for this sthalam is the 90th hymn of the Fourth Thirumurai, a Thiruviruttha sacred hymn.

“Kaiyathu kaalari naagam kanalvidu soolamathu veyyathu velai nanjunda virisadai vinnnavarkon seyyinil neela manang kamalun thiruvedikkudi ayyanai aara amuthinai naam adainthaaduthume kaiththala maan mari enthia kaiyan kanal malu van poyththalai enthi narpoodhiy aninthu palithirivaan seylaikal paainthu ukalu thiruvedikkudi aththanai aara amuthinai naam adainthu aaduthume munpin muthalvan munivan em melai vinai kaliththaan anbin nilaiyil avunar puram podiyaana seyyum semponai nanmalar melavan ser thiruvedikkudi anbanai nammai udaiyanai.” Gloss: “With a snake in His hand, a fiery trident, He who consumed the terrible ocean poison, the Lord of the celestials with matted locks, the Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, where blue lotuses bloom in the fields, that inexhaustible nectar, let us reach and dance in praise of Him. He who holds a deer in His hand, with a fiery axe, who wanders for alms carrying a skull and adorned with sacred ash, whose deeds are leaping, that Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, that inexhaustible nectar, let us reach and dance in praise of Him. The first and last, the sage, who removed our past karma, the golden one who destroys the cities of demons with love, the Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, where Brahma on the good lotus resides, our loving Lord, our master.” “Naam adainthu aaduthume baktharkal naalum maravaar piraviyai ondru aruthaan muththarkal munnam pani seythu paaridam munnuyarththaan koththana kondrai manang kamalum thiruvedikkudi aththanai aara amuthinai naam adainthu aaduthume aananainthu erum kuri gunamaar arivaar avar ka maananainthu aadum mathiyum punalum sadaimudiyan thenanainthaadiya vandupayil thiruvedikkudi aananainthaadum maluvanai naam adainthu aaduthume ennum eluththum kuriyum aripavar thaam oliya pannin isai moli paadiyavaanavar thaam panivaar thinnen vinaikalai theerkkum piraan thiruvedikkudi nanna ariya amuthinai naam adainthu aaduthume oorntha vidai ukanthu eriya selvanai naam ariyom aarntha madamolli mangaiyor paa.” Gloss: “Let us reach and dance in praise of Him. Devotees never forget Him daily, who cuts off rebirth, who was worshipped by the liberated ones before, who uplifted the earth.

“That Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, where clusters of Konrai flowers spread fragrance, that inexhaustible nectar, let us reach and dance in praise of Him. Those who know the nature of the bull He rides, they know Him. He with the moon and water in His matted locks, who dances with the deer. That Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, where bees hum, that axe-wielding Lord who dances with the bull, let us reach and dance in praise of Him. Those who know numbers, letters, and symbols, they speak. The celestials who sang songs of musical language, they worship Him.

“That Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, who removes strong karmas, that rare nectar, let us reach and dance in praise of Him. We do not know the wealthy one who gladly rides the bull. A modest maiden on one side.” “Aagam makilnthu udaiyan serntha punal sadai selvappiraan thiruvedikkudi saarntha vayal ani than amuthai adainthu aaduthume eriyum maluvinan enniyum matroruvan thalaiyul thiriyum paliyinan theyamum naadum ellam udaiyan viriyum polil ani seru thikal thiruvedikkudi ariya amuthinai anbarkalodu adainthu aaduthume maiyani kandan maraiviri naavan mathiththukandha meyyani neetran vilumiyavenmalu vaalpadaiyan seyya kamalam manang kamalum thiruvedikkudi ayyanai aara amuthinai naam adainthu aaduthume varuththanai vaalarakkanmudi tholodu patthiruttha poruththanai poyya arulani poothappadaiyudaiya thiruththanai thevarapiraan thiruvedikkudaiyaru ththanai aara amuthinai naam adainthu aaduthume Thiruchitrambalam.” Gloss: “The wealthy Lord with matted locks, who delights in His body and has water in His hair, the Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, adorned with fields, that nectar, let us reach and dance in praise of Him. He with the fiery axe, who wanders for alms with another’s skull, who owns all lands and nations, the Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, where beautiful groves spread, that rare nectar, let us reach and dance in praise of Him with devotees. He with the dark throat, whose tongue expounds the Vedas, who delights in sacred ash on His body, who wields the excellent white axe, the Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, where red lotuses spread fragrance, that inexhaustible nectar, let us reach and dance in praise of Him.

“He who crushed the ten heads of the powerful Rakshasa, the truthful bestower of grace, who has an army of Bhootas, the Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, the Lord of the Devas, that inexhaustible nectar, let us reach and dance in praise of Him.

“” The next sacred sthalam is Thiru-kandiyur. This is one of the Ashta Veeratta Sthalams. The Lord’s sacred names are Brahmasirakandeeswarar, Veeratteswarar, Brahmanathar, and Adhivillvanathar. The Goddess’s sacred name is Mangalanayaki. The sthala tree is the Vilvam.

“The sacred waters are Kapala Theertham, Nandi Theertham, Daksha Theertham, Brahma Theertham, and the Kudamurutti River. This place was named Kandana Puram or Kandiyur because the Lord severed one of Brahma’s five heads with His trident. After severing Brahma’s head, the Lord blessed him when he pleaded. Sadathapa Muni used to visit and worship during Pradosham. One time, when he came to Kandiyur, he could not reach the temple in time.

“At that moment, the Lord granted him the Darshan of Kalathi in this very sthalam.

“Furthermore, for Sadathapa Muni, the Vilva tree was brought from Kailash by the Lord and planted in this sthalam.

“Therefore, this place is also known as Adhivillvaranyam. This sthalam is said to remove the sin of Brahmagathi. Just as it is one of the Ashta Veeratta Sthalams, it is also one of the Sapthasthana Sthalams of Thiru-vaiyaru. During the Sapthasthana festival, the Lord comes here, rests for a while, and then proceeds. Since Sadathapa Muni was the elder brother of Silatha Muni, there is a tradition here that when the Lord rests, he is given a packed meal (kattuchoru) as an elder father-in-law. It is customary to send the Lord off with a packed meal of curd rice and puliyodarai.

“In the Navagraha shrine, Surya is seen with his two consorts. The Moolavar here is a Swayambhu Murthy, and the pedestal is somewhat tall. Brahma Deva is depicted holding a Japamala and praying to the Lord with both hands. There is a separate shrine for Brahma. The Vadugakolam (form of Bhairava) taken by the Lord to sever Brahma’s head is depicted as a small stone sculpture by the door of the entrance to Brahma’s shrine. Two Thevara sacred hymns are available for this sthalam.

“One is by Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, and one is by Appar Swamigal. Among them, the Thevaram sung by Appar Swamigal is the 93rd hymn of the Fourth Thirumurai, a Thiruviruttha sacred hymn.

““Vaanavar thaanavar vaikal malarkonarnthittu irainji thaanavar maal biraman ariyaatha thagaimaiyinaan aanavan aathipuraanan andru odiya panriyeytha kaanavani kandiyoor andavaanar tholukinrathe vaanamathiyamum vaalaravum punalodu sadai thaanamathuvana vaiththulal vaan thalal pol oruvan kaanamariyondru kaiyudaiya.” Gloss: “The celestials and demons, bringing flowers daily, worshipped Him. He whose nature is unknown to Vishnu and Brahma, the ancient primordial one, who shot the boar that fled that day. The celestials worship the Lord of Kandiyur. He who wanders with the moon and the fierce snake and water in His matted locks, like a fiery one, holding a deer in one hand.” “Yaan kandiyoor iruntha oonamil vedamudaiyaanai naam adi olukuvathe pandangkaruththathor kaiyudaiyaan padaiththaan thalaiyai undangu aruththum oorodu naadavaiththaan ariyum kandangkaruththamidarudaiyaan kandiyoor iruntha thondarpiraanai kandeer andavaana tholukinrathe mudiyin mutraathathondrillai ellamudan thaanudaiyan kodiyum mutravidaiyeriyor kootrorupaaludaiyan kadiyamutravinai noy kalaivaan kandiyoor iruntha adiyumutraar thondar illai kandeer andavaanavare patriyoraanaiyuriththapiraan pavalaththiral pol mutrum aninthathor neerudaiyan munname koduththa katrangudaiyavan thaan ariyaan kandiyoor iruntha kutramilvedamudaiyaanai yaam andar kooruvathe porpanai yaanaiyuriththapira.” Gloss: “Let us follow the feet of the Lord of Kandiyur, who possesses the flawless Vedas.

“He who holds a skull in His hand, who severed the head of Brahma and consumed it, and who knows all towns and nations. Behold the Lord of the devotees in Kandiyur, who has a dark throat, worshipped by the celestials. There is nothing incomplete in His crown; He possesses everything. He who rides the bull with a flag, who has a part of Yama. He who removes severe karma diseases, the Lord in Kandiyur. Behold, there are no devotees who have not reached His feet, O celestials.

“The Lord who flayed the elephant, who is adorned with sacred ash like a coral heap, who gave the stone before, He does not know. We, the celestials, speak of the flawless Lord of Kandiyur, who possesses the Vedas.

“The Lord who flayed the elephant in battle.” “Porivaay aravan serppathu vaanaththiraikadal sool ulagam ithanai kaappathu kaaranamaaga kondaana kandiyoor iruntha koorppudai ol vaalmaluvanai yaam andar kooruvathe attathu kaalanai aaynthatu vedam aaru angam andru suttathu kaamanai kannathanaale thodarnthu eriya kattavai moondrum eriththa piraan kandiyoor iruntha kutta mun vedappadaiyanai yaamandar kooruvathe attum oli neer ani mathiyum malaraana vellam ittu pothiyum sadaimudiyan indai maalai angai kattum aravathu thaanudaiyan kandiyoor iruntha kottum paraiyudai kooththanai yaamandar kooruvathe maainthana theevinai mangina noykal marukivila theynthanapaavam serukilla nammai setra nangai kaainthapiraan kandiyoor embiraan angam aarinaiyum aayntha piraan allano.” Gloss: “The Lord with the fiery mouth, who protects this world surrounded by the wavy ocean, the Lord in Kandiyur with the sharp, bright axe, we, the celestials, speak of Him. He who kicked Yama, who studied the Vedas and the six Angas, who burned Kama with His eye, who burned the three cities that followed, the Lord in Kandiyur, who has the ancient Vedic army, we, the celestials, speak of Him. He with matted locks adorned with the moon and flowers, who binds the garland of flowers in His hand, who has the snake, the Lord in Kandiyur, the dancer with drum and cymbal, we, the celestials, speak of Him. Evil deeds perished, diseases vanished, sins diminished, our pride disappeared. Is He not the Lord of Kandiyur, our Lord, who burned the woman who angered us, who studied the six Angas?”

“Adiyenai aatkondavane mandi malaiyai eduththu maththaakki avvaasukiyai thandi amarar kadaintha kadal vidam kandaruli undapiraan nanjoliththa piraan anjiyodi nannakkanda piraanallano kandiyooranda vaanavane Thiruchitrambalam ini aduththa thiruththalam melai thirukkaattu palli iraivan uraiyum thirukkoilkalai palli endru kuriththirukkinranar nammudiya munnavarkal iththakaiya palli endra peyaruudaiya thalangal palavatrai thoguththu uraikkinraar thirunavukkarasasamikal poruppalli varaiyilla puram moondru eythu pulanthaliya salanthiranai pilanthaan porchakkara palli thirukkaattu palli kallar kamal kolliyarai palli kalavanjjaaral sirappalli sivappalli semban palli selunanippalli thavappalli seeraar parappalli endrendru.” Gloss: “He who enslaved me, who took the Mandara mountain as a churning rod, and with Vasuki, the celestials churned the ocean, and He consumed the poison that appeared. Is He not the Lord who removed the poison, the Lord who saw the celestials flee in fear and then approached them, the Lord of Kandiyur, O celestial?

“Now, the next sacred sthalam is Melai Thiru-kattu Palli. Our ancestors referred to temples where the Lord resides as ‘Palli’. Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal compiles and describes many such sthalams with the name ‘Palli’: ‘Poruppalli, Varaiyilla, Puram Moondru Eythu, Pulanthaliya, Salanthiranai Pilanthaan, Porchakkara Palli, Thiru-kattu Palli, Kallar Kamal, Kolliyarai Palli, Kalavanjjaaral, Sirappalli, Sivappalli, Semban Palli, Selunanippalli, Thavappalli, Seeraar Parappalli,’ and so on.” “Pagarkor ellam paralokaththai inithaaga paalippaare endru paadukinraar aththakaiya palli endru valangappadum thalangalil sola vala naattil kaattu palli endra peyaruudaiya paadal petra thalangal irandu irukkinrana kaaviriyin vadakarai thiruvengkaattukku arugil ulla thalam keelaith thirukkaattu palli endrum inge melai thirukkaattu palli endra thalam ondrum irukkinrathu thiruvaiyaarukku arugile irukkinra thalam intha melai thirukkaattu palli endra thalam iththalaththirku thirugnana sambandha peruman paadiya thiruppathikam ondrum appar swamikal paadiya thiruppathikam ondrum aaga irandu thiruppathikangal irukkinrana swamiyin peyar arulmigu theeyaadi appar vadamoliyil agneeswarar ambikai peyar alakamar nayaki vadamoliyil soundarya nayaki theertham agni theertham matrum kaaviri sthalavirukkam vanni vilvam palangkaalaththil kottai koththalangalodu koodiya periya nagaramaaga.” Gloss: “He sings that all who utter these names will joyfully attain the heavenly abode. Among such sthalams known as ‘Palli’ in the Chola country, there are two sthalams named ‘Kattu Palli’ that have received hymns. One is Keelai Thiru-kattu Palli, located on the north bank of the Kaveri, near Thiru-venkadu, and the other is Melai Thiru-kattu Palli, located here.

“This Melai Thiru-kattu Palli is near Thiru-vaiyaru. For this sthalam, there is one sacred hymn sung by Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and one sacred hymn sung by Appar Swamigal, making a total of two sacred hymns. The Lord’s name is Arulmigu Theeyaadi Appar, and in Sanskrit, Agneeswarar. The Goddess’s name is Alagamar Nayaki, and in Sanskrit, Soundarya Nayaki. The sacred waters are Agni Theertham and Kaveri. The sthala trees are Vanni and Vilvam.

“In ancient times, this town was a large city with forts and ramparts.” This temple is located in the center of the village, facing east. Upon entering through the Rajagopuram with seven tiers, Vinayagar is visible. After worshipping the flagstaff, Balipitam, and Nandi, one proceeds to the Lord’s shrine, which faces east, and the Goddess’s shrine, which is in the first prakaram, facing south. Opposite the Amman shrine, facing north, shines Narthana Vinayagar. Passing through the second gopuram and reaching the inner mandapam, to the right is the Natarajar Sabhamandapam.

“On the lower platform of the mandapam are the idols of Bhairavar and the Samayacharyas. Passing through the front mandapam, one can reach the Lord’s shrine. The place where the Lord is enshrined is very low. In the Mahamandapam are the Utsava Vigrahas (processional deities). In the inner prakaram are Valampuri Vinayagar, Thirumal, Lakshmi, Dakshinamurthy, Lingodbhavar, Murugan, Durga, and Chandeswarar. Thirumal, Brahma, Surya, Agni.

“Bhageerathan and the elder queen of Uraiyur Chola worshipped the Lord here and received His grace.

“Once, Indra and other Devas came to this sthalam and worshipped the Lord and Goddess.

“At that time, Agni Deva, who was like the face of the Devas, worshipped the Lord of this sthalam with many pujas to absolve himself of the sins incurred by destroying all things in the world.

“The Lord appeared to Agni Bhagavan and blessed him, saying, “Create a sacred water in your name, bathe in it, and continue to worship Me.” Agni Deva worshipped accordingly.

“The Lord granted His divine vision and blessed Agni Deva. The temple worshipped by Agni is named Agneeswaram. Those who bathe in Agni Theertham and worship on Karthigai Sunday, Masimagam, Panguni Uthiram, and Vaikasi Visakam will receive all blessings.

“The King gave the Chrysanthemum flowers, brought by a servant from the Uraiyur Nandavanam belonging to Lord Shiva, to his wives. The elder queen offered those flowers to Lord Shiva and worshipped Him, while the younger one adorned herself with them and rejoiced. When Uraiyur was destroyed by a sandstorm, only Thiru-kattu Palli, where the elder queen who worshipped Lord Shiva resided, survived without being destroyed, it is said here. The Panguni Uthiram festival is celebrated grandly. On Panguni Uthiram, the Lord grants sacred water in the Kaveri. There is one Thirukkurunthogai sacred hymn by Appar Swamigal for this sthalam.

“It is the 84th hymn of the Fifth Thirumurai.

““Maattuppalli makilnthurai veerarkellam kettuppalli kandeer keduvithu ottuppalli vittu odal uraa munam kaattuppalliyulaan kalal sermine maattai thedi makilnthu neer nummule naattu poyyellam pesidu naanileer koottai.” Gloss: “To all the heroes who reside joyfully in Maattuppalli, behold the school of hearing, this is destruction. Before the school of running away and fleeing, reach the feet of the Lord in Kattu Palli. You shameless ones, who search for wealth and speak all falsehoods among yourselves, before the body leaves the soul.” “Vittu uyir povathan munname kaattuppalliyulaan kalal sermine thenai ventra sollaalu selvamum oonai vittu uyir povathan munname kaanavedar karuthungaattuppalli gnananaayakanai sendru nannnume aruththa mummanaiyalodu makkalum poruththamillai pollaathathu pokkidum karuththan kannuthal annal kaattuppalli thiruththan sevadiyai sendru sermine sutramum thunaiyum manai vaalkkaiyum atra pothanaiyaar avar endrendre katravarkal karuthum kaattuppalli petram erum piraan adi sermine adumbum kondraiyum vanniyum maththamum thudumbal seyda thoomani chothiyaan kadamban thaathai karuthum kaattuppalli udambinaarkkor uruthunaiyaagume meyyin maasudaiyaar udal mooduvaar poyyai meyyendru pukkudan.” Gloss: “Before life leaves the body, reach the feet of the Lord in Kattu Palli. The wealth of the woman whose words conquered honey, before life leaves the body, the Lord of knowledge in Kattu Palli, whom the hunters seek, go and reach Him.

“There is no compatibility with the three wives and children who have been cut off.

“The Lord with the eye on His forehead, who removes evil thoughts, the righteous one in Kattu Palli, go and reach His sacred feet. When relatives, companions, and married life are gone, who are they?

“The Lord who rides the bull in Kattu Palli, whom the learned consider, reach His feet. The pure jewel-like light who wears Adumbu, Konrai, Vanni, and Maththam, the father of Kadamban, the Lord in Kattu Palli, will be a strong support for those with bodies. Those with impurities in their bodies, who cover themselves, do not enter and fall into falsehood, thinking it is truth.” “Veelanmin kaiyin maanudaiyan kaattuppalli em aiyan thannadiye adainthu uymine velai ventra kannaarai virumbi neer seelam kettuth thikaiyan min pedaikaal kaalaiye tholung kaattuppalliyurai neelakandanai nitthal ninamminne indrullaar naalai illai enum porul ondrum oraath tholitarum oomarkal andru vaanavarkkaaga vidamunda kandanar kaattuppalli kandu uymine ennilaa arakkan malai enthida enni neenmudi patthum eruththavan kannullaar karuthungaattuppalliyai nannuvaar avar tham vinai naasame Thiruchitrambalam thodarnthu sinthippom Thiruchitrambalam.” Gloss: “Do not fall! Reach the feet of our Lord in Kattu Palli, who holds a deer in His hand, and be saved. You foolish ones, who desire women whose eyes conquered the ocean, do not lose your virtue and be bewildered.

“Worship the blue-throated Lord residing in Kattu Palli every morning and remember Him daily. You mute ones, who do not understand the meaning that those who are here today will not be tomorrow, behold the Lord with the throat who consumed poison for the celestials that day in Kattu Palli and be saved. Those who thought of lifting the countless Rakshasa’s mountain, and whose ten long crowns were crushed, those with eyes who seek Kattu Palli, their karma will be destroyed.

“Let us meditate further.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 431. Thirunindracharukkam. The Puranam of Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, who had been visiting the sthalams on both banks of the Kaveri, arrived at the sacred sthalam of Thiru-anaikka. Thiru-anaikka is a very famous sthalam known to everyone.

It is a sthalam located on an island between the Kaveri and Kollidam rivers, near Trichy. It is a sthalam on the north bank of the Kaveri. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, who came to this sacred sthalam, composed three sacred hymns. Before looking at those hymns, let us briefly contemplate the history and mythological accounts of Thiru-anaikka sthalam. The sthalam is Thiru-anaikka. The deity is Sri Jambukeswarar.

The Goddess is Sri Akilandeswari. The sacred waters are Brahma Theertham, Chandra Theertham, Jambu Theertham, Rama Theertham, and Srimath Theertham. The nine sacred bathing places (Thirthams) such as Agni Thirtham, Surya Thirtham, Indra Thirtham, and Agasthiya Thirtham, the processional deity Sri Somasakandar, the sthala-tree (sacred tree) Naval Maram, and the five circumambulatory paths (Pancha Prakaram) are the special features of this holy place. This sacred sthalam, known as Thiru-Aanaikka, also bears various other sacred names such as Thiru-Aanaikkaval, Gajaranyam, Jambukeswaram, Jambuveeswaram, Ven Naval Vanam, Jambuvana, Gnana Kshethram, Gnana Sthalam, Gnana Bhoomi, Kavai, Thanthi Pukaa Vaayil, Amutheeswaram, Thanthivanam, and Ibavanam. It is called Thiru-Aanaikka and Thiru-Aanaikkaval because the Peruman bestowed grace upon an elephant. It is known as Gajaranyam, Ibavanam, and Thanthivanam, meaning ‘forest where elephants resided’.

Since the Peruman is seated here beneath a white Naval tree, it is called Jambukeswaram, Jambuveeswaram, Ven Naval Vanam, and Jambu. It is also called Poovanam. Because the Ambikai received spiritual instruction (Gnana Upadesam) from the Lord, it is known as Gnana Kshethram, Gnana Sthalam, and Gnana Bhoomi. Due to its beautiful groves, it is called Kavai. It is named Thanthi Pukaa Vaayil because it was built in such a way that elephants could not enter. Since the deity, formed from the ambrosial water, is enshrined here, it is called Amutheeswaram.

This sthalam is one of the Panchabhootha Sthalams (five elemental shrines) representing water, hence it is also known as Appu Sthalam. This sthalam is beautifully situated amidst groves. The Swami Sannidhi faces west, and the Amman Sannidhi faces east. There are two prakarams in the Amman temple. This sacred temple has five prakarams from the inside to the outer street. During the Pancha Prakaram festival, the processional deities appear in all five prakarams.

The fourth and fifth prakarams contain houses. In the fourth prakaram, during festival seasons, processional deities are taken out, and chariot processions (Therottam) take place. Among the many walls surrounding this sthalam, the fourth wall is the largest; it is called Thiruneetru Mathil (sacred ash wall). Inside the temple, there are many thirthams, sannidhis, multi-tiered mandapams, large mandapams, and coconut groves. The Gajaranya Kshethra Mahatmyam states that Sri Ranganathar resides in Srirangam solely to worship the Peruman of this sthalam. Confirming this history, it is customary for the Perumal to come out from a grove here once a year, stay overnight, and return with special decorations that night, just as he would appear.

In later times, due to religious disputes between the two factions, this custom appears to have ceased.

The Lord enshrined in this sthalam is named Jambukeswarar. Other sacred names include Jambunathar, Jambunayagar, Vennavaleesar, Jambulingam, Appulingam, Amutalingam, Amutheeswarar, Brahmalingam, Brahmeesar, Gajaranyanathar, Pachathathapeswarar, Aadhi Perunjelvar, and Sangareswarar. Appar Swamigal praises the Peruman as ‘Sezhuneerthiral’ (abundance of rich water). In inscriptions, the names Thiru-Aanaikka Udaiyar, Thiru-Aanaikkavudaiya Nayanar, and Mahadevapattar are attributed to the Swami. The Goddess is known by the sacred names Akilandeswari, Akilanda Nayaki, and Akilandavalli, which mean ‘Mistress of all worlds’. To the north of this sthalam is the Kollidam River, and to the south is the Thirumanjana Kaveri.

Water for ablutions is brought from both the Kollidam and Thirumanjana Kaveri rivers. Not only this, but there are also nine Thirthams belonging to the temple. They are as follows: Brahma Thirtham, which is located in the south of the fourth prakaram, to the south of the road. Indra Thirtham, which is located in the southwest of the third prakaram, next to the Kasi Viswanathar Sannidhi.

Thirdly, Jambu Thirtham, which is located to the east of the third prakaram, near the old Jambukeswarar temple.

Fourthly, Rama Thirtham, which is the temple tank outside the fifth prakaram, to the west of the Sannidhi. The Theppa Thiruvizha (float festival) takes place in the month of Thai on Punarpoosam.

Fifthly, Srimath Thirtham, which is a small spring near the Moolalingam.

Sixthly, Agni Thirtham, which is a large well located in the third prakaram, in the southeast, next to the Vasantha Mandapam.

Seventhly, Agathiya Thirtham, which is a Sannidhi in the first prakaram of the Amman temple. It is a small well located opposite the Sannidhi, next to the Palliyarai (bedchamber).

Eighthly, Soma Thirtham, which is said to be the Chandra Pushkarani in Srirangam.

Ninthly, Surya Thirtham, which is the temple tank located in the fourth prakaram, in the southwest corner, opposite the Aayiram Kaal Mandapam (thousand-pillared hall). Surrounding it is a two-tiered mandapam with approximately one hundred pillars. The Theppa Thiruvizha takes place here in the month of Aadi on Pooram Nakshathiram.

Next, the glories of the sthalam: This sthalam possesses special significance in terms of Moorthy (deity), Sthalam (place), and Thirtham (sacred water). Among the Panchabhootha Sthalams, this is the Appu Sthalam (water element shrine). Among the Aaru Aadhara Sthalams (six energy centers), this is the Swathishtana Thirthalam. It is a temple where the Ambikai formed the deity from water. Even today, water can be seen seeping from the Moolalingam. It is a temple where an elephant and a spider competed to worship.

This sacred temple is foremost among the Maadak Kovils (elevated temples) built to prevent elephants from entering.

The Lord himself, appearing as a Siddhar, came and gave sacred ash as wages. It possesses the excellent wall known as Thiruneetru Mathil, which was built with sacred ash. When a Chola king was bathing in the Kaveri River, a pearl necklace he wore fell into the Kaveri. This necklace came to rest on the Lord’s neck through a sacred water pot (Thirumanjana Kudam). In front of the Swami Sannidhi, there is a balcony with nine openings. By worshipping the Lord through these openings, one receives the benefits of bathing in all nine Thirthams.

The Brahmotsavam is particularly suited to this sthalam. It is a Mandalotsavam (forty-day festival) conducted by Brahma. It features the excellent festival called Panchaprakaram. The Thirukkalyana Mahotsavam (sacred marriage festival) that occurs in other temples does not take place here. Daily cow worship (Go Pooja) is performed. The Swami receives daily Annabhishekam (rice anointing).

Besides the flagstaff in the Sannidhi, there are eight flagstaffs surrounding the third prakaram. Unlike other sacred temples, here on the sixth day of the festival, a grand procession (Perottam) takes place. On Margazhi Thiruvathirai, Nataraja Moorthy proceeds with the sixty-three Nayanmars. During the Uchchikala Pooja (midday worship), the Amman temple priest, dressed as a woman, worships the Lord. In the third prakaram, there is a Sannidhi for Jyeshtadevi. Kalamega Pulavar is renowned for having received the grace of the Ambikai.

The Naval tree is the sthala-vriksham (sacred tree). It contains many inscriptions. It is distinguished by having hymns sung by the Samayak Kuravargal (four great Shaivite saints). The temples surrounding this sacred temple are: The Rajarajeswarar Temple, which is located on the north street in the fourth prakaram. The Moolalingam in this temple has five faces and is known as Panchamukalingam. Next is the Neelavinteeswarar Temple, which is located to the west of the temple, to the west of Rama Thirtham, and was consecrated by Rama.

It is named thus because it was worshipped by Rama, who is Vishnu with a blue complexion. Next is the Sangareswarar Temple, which is in the third prakaram, at Jambu Thirtham. Besides these, within the main temple itself, apart from the Swami Sannidhi and Amman Sannidhis, there are also sub-temples such as the Mummoorthy Temple, Kasi Viswanathar Temple, Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple, Balathandayuthapani Temple, Saneeswarar Temple, and Vinayagar Temple. Inside the temple, there are many mandapams adorned with sculptures, including the Oonjal Mandapam, Noorrukaal Mandapam (hundred-pillared hall), Aayiram Kaal Mandapam (thousand-pillared hall), Vasantha Mandapam, Navarathri Mandapam, Dhwajastambha Mandapam, Somasakandar Mandapam, Natarajar Mandapam, and Mummoorthy Mandapam. There are two mandapams with one hundred and eight pillars. In the Aayiram Kaal Mandapam, the central mandapam is designed like a chariot, with many sculptures, chariot wheels, and horses.

Among these mandapams, the Somasakandar Mandapam stands out, showcasing ancient sculptural artistry. It is said to have been built by Rama. The stone corbels within it are crafted with bands, resembling wooden work. In this sthalam, the sanctum sanctorum (garbhagriham) of the Moolalingam is built small to prevent elephants from entering. The vimanas (towers) of the Moolamoorthies are constructed entirely of stone. The large Dhwajastambha Mandapam (flagstaff hall) in front of the Swami Sannidhi is prominent.

It is built upon four large pillars, with eight lions supporting each pillar. There is an ancient text called ‘Thiru-Aanaikka Thiruppani Maalai’. Through this, it is known that the walls, gopurams, and mandapams of this temple were renovated from time to time by the Cholas, Pandyas, Nayak kings, and other devotees. The names of kings such as Kochchengan Chozhan, Vijayabalan, Thiruneetru Chozhan, Vikrama Chozhan, Sundara Pandiyan, Kulasekara Pandiyan, Varaguna Pandiyan, Thirumalai Nayakkar, and various devotees are mentioned in this book. Those who worshipped the Lord in this sthalam include Brahma, Vishnu, Dikpalakas, Ashta Vasus, Jambu Muni, Ambikai, the spider, the elephant, Rama, Parachara, Chola Kochchengan Chozhan, Gautama, Kubera, Agathiyar, Surya, Chandra, Indra, Agni, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, Arunagirinathar, Aiyadigal Kadavar Kon, Kachiyappa Munivar, Kalamega Pulavar, and Mahavidwan Meenakshi Sundaram Pillai. In this temple, ablutions and worship (Abhisheka Aradhanai) are performed daily during the four periods: morning, midday, evening, and night.

There is no Abhishekam at Ardha Jamam (midnight). During the Uchchikala Pooja (midday worship), the Amman temple priest, dressed as a woman, circumambulates the Swami temple with attendants and performs worship. It is believed that the Ambikai herself performs the worship. Daily at midday, a cow is brought and worshipped in front of the Sannidhi as a custom. Festivals in this sthalam are conducted according to the Sakalagama Sangiraham. The Brahmotsavam begins annually in the month of Maasi and continues for forty days until Panguni.

During these days, festivals are held for all deities, including Vinayagar, Subramaniyar, Nalvar, Somasakandar, and Chandikeswarar. On the first day, earth is collected. Festivals for Vinayagar and Subramaniyar last five days, for Nalvar three days, for Kalyana Sundarar three days, for Chandrasekarar six days, for Somasakandar ten days, for Pallakku Chokkar three days, a silent festival for three days, for Chandikeswarar one day, Panchaprakaram one day, Vidayatri Utsavam one day, and Mandalabhishekam one day, totaling forty days of festivities. In the month of Maasi, the flag-hoisting (Kodiyetram) occurs on Mirugasirisa Nakshathiram, the chariot procession (Therottam) on Panguni Revathi, the sacred bath (Thirtham) on Rohini, and in the month of Panguni, Panchaprakaram takes place on Chithirai. The Panchaprakaram festival is celebrated with great grandeur. On that day, the Peruman, adorned in female attire, and the Ambikai, in male attire, parade through the five streets, granting their divine vision.

To witness this sacred sight, one would need a thousand eyes. Before the Brahmotsavam, a five-day festival for Pidari Amman takes place.

Additionally, in Vaikasi, the Vasanthotsavam (spring festival) is held for ten days in the Vasantha Mandapam. On Aani Pournami, the Swami receives Mupazha Abhishekam (anointing with three fruits), and on Aani Thirumanjanam, Natarajar proceeds in procession. In Aadi, on Karthigai day, the flag is hoisted, and the ten-day Aadi Pooram festival takes place. On Pooram, the last day, the Theppa Vizha (float festival) is held in the Surya Thirtham, which is an inner tank. In Aavani Moolam, the legend of carrying earth for Puttu (sweet dish) is enacted. In Purattasi, the Navarathri festival is celebrated for ten days in the Navarathri Mandapam within the Amman Sannidhi.

In Aippasi Kanda Sashti, the Soorasamharam Utsavam (festival of slaying the demon Soora) takes place, and in the month of Karthigai, on every Somavaram (Monday), Sangabhishekam (conch anointing) and on Periya Karthigai, Sudalai Deepam (cemetery lamp) takes place. In Margazhi, on Thiruvathirai day, Natarajar from the second prakaram proceeds with the sixty-three Nayanmars. The Moola Natarajar in the first prakaram does not proceed. In the month of Thai, a forty-day festival takes place, and on the last day, the Theppa Thiruvizha (float festival) is held in Rama Thirtham. On Thai Poosam, the Swami goes to the Kollidam riverbank and on Maasi Magam to the Kaveri riverbank, performs Thirtham (sacred bath), and returns at night. On Chithirai Vishu Punyakalam (auspicious time), at night, the Rishabha Vahana Purappadu (procession on bull mount) and the reading of the new Panchangam take place.

On Pournami, Marukkozhundus Moolam Abhishekam. On Vaikasi Pournami, Eka Vasantham. Before this, on the tenth day, the Vasanthotsavam begins. On Pournami Vaikasi Pournami, Annabhishekam. On Vaikasi Visaka Nakshathiram, Paal Maangai Abhishekam (milk and mango anointing). On Aani Uthira Nakshathiram, Aani Thirumanjanam.

The next day, Natarajar proceeds in procession. On Pournami, Muppal Abhishekam. On Aadi Dakshinayana Punyakalam, Thirthavari in the daytime, and Rishabha Vahana Purappadu at night. On Aadi Bharani Nakshathiram, Aadi Pooram Utsava Dhwaja Arohanam (flag hoisting). On the first day, Aadi Pooram Nakshathiram Thirtham. On the twelfth day, Thiruvadi Pooram Theppakulam Theppotsavam (float festival).

On Aadi Amavasai, Rishabha Vahanam Purappadu at night. On Pournami, Pattu Pavithram. On Aavani Moola Nakshathiram, Aavani Moolam Swami Pittu Man Sumandha Utsavam (festival of the Lord carrying earth for Puttu). On Aavani Pournami, Thilabhishekam. On Purattasi Krishna Chathurthi, Navarathri Utsava Aarambam (beginning of Navarathri festival). On Saraswathi Vijayadasami, Ambu Eythal (shooting arrow) and Paalabhishekam.

On Aippasi Deepavali, Abhishekam. On Aippasi Pournami, Vibhuthi Abhishekam. Skanda Sashti Utsavam. On Karthigai Pournami, Kiruthappadam. On Margazhi Dhanurmasa Pooja Aarambam. On Thiruvathirai, Arudra Darisanam.

On the first day of Margazhi, Thiruppavai Manikkavasagar Utsavam. On Margazhi Pournami, Aryabhishekam. On Margazhi Maha Vyapatha Dinam, Udaya Vyapthi Pavadai. In the month of Thai, Uttarayana Punyakalam, Makar Sankranti, Thirtham in the morning, Rishabha Vahanam at night. On Thai Amavasai, Rishabha Vahanam at night. On Thai Sathayam Nakshathiram, Thai Theppotsavam.

On Thai Poosam, Thirthavari in Kollidam, Rishabha Vahanam at night. On the last Tuesday of Thai month, Pidariyar Utsavam, first Kaappu. On Thai Pournami, Madhu Abhishekam. In the month of Maasi, Maha Shivaratri Abhisheka Aradhanai, Rishabha Vahanam. On Maasi Pournami, Kiruthappadam. In Panguni, as we have already seen, the Mandala Brahmotsavam.

In this festival, Thervadaichan Rishabha Vahanam, Rathotsavam, Panchaprakara Mahotsavam, etc., are celebrated grandly. Panguni Pournami Kandabhishekam will take place. These are all the special features of the Thiru-Aanaikka sthalam. The Thiru-Aanaikka Thirthalam is a sacred place with a very rich mythological history. Many saints have worshipped the Lord here.

We will continue to reflect on all those mythological histories. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 432. Thirunindrachcharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We are contemplating the special features of the Thiru-Aanaikka sthalam. Let us briefly reflect on the mythological history of Thiru-Aanaikka.

First, the mythological history of the elephant and the spider’s worship. On Mount Kailash, there are many Gananathas. Among them are two, Maliyavan and Pushpadanthan. Both were preeminent in their devotion to Shiva. They competed with each other in Shiva devotion, each believing himself to be superior. Due to this rivalry in Shiva devotion, they became envious of each other and harbored enmity.

One day, Maliyavan cursed Pushpadanthan to become an elephant. Pushpadanthan, in turn, cursed Maliyavan to become a spider. Both appealed to the Peruman. The Peruman, in His divine grace, instructed them to go to the Gnana Sthalam in the Chola country, worship Him there, and thus be freed from their curses.

Accordingly, the two Gananathas were born as an elephant and a spider in the Thiru-Aanaikka sthalam. Born here as an elephant and a spider, they desired to worship the Peruman residing here and attain liberation. The elephant bathed in many Thirthams.

Then, filling its trunk with water and gathering many flowers, it entered the Sannidhi of the Peruman. It removed the dry leaves and other debris lying there, performed sacred ablution (Thiru Abhishekam) on the Peruman’s sacred head with the water brought in its trunk, and then lovingly offered the many flowers it had gathered to the Peruman, worshipped Him, and returned to its dwelling. While the elephant was thus worshipping, the spider resided in a Naval tree. From the tree’s hollow, it wove a canopy with its silk threads to prevent dust and leaves from falling on Lord Shiva, and thus worshipped Him. The next morning, the elephant, as usual, bathed, gathered flowers, and came to the Sannidhi. It became enraged upon seeing the canopy woven with threads above the Peruman’s head.

Believing the presence of threads there to be an offense, it destroyed the silk canopy made by the spider, purified the spot, bathed again, and again worshipped the Peruman.

Thus, the spider and the elephant worshipped the Peruman alternately. The spider would weave a silk canopy, and the next day the elephant would destroy it. This continued until one day the spider hid on one side of the tree to discover how its silk canopy was being destroyed. The elephant arrived as usual, destroyed the silk canopy made by the spider, and worshipped as before. The hidden spider, seeing its silk canopy destroyed by the elephant, became enraged. It entered the elephant’s trunk, swiftly climbed up, reached the elephant’s skull, and bit it.

The elephant trumpeted like thunder, fell down, rolled here and there, suffered various torments, and died. As the elephant died, the spider, having entered it, also died, unable to find a way out.

At that moment, both, freed from their enmity, appeared in divine form. The Peruman, granting them His vision, said, “Because you worshipped Us with love, you have attained a glory worthy of being worshipped by the Devas. The one who was freed from the elephant form will shine as a Gananatha in Our world as before. This sthalam will be known by the name of him who worshipped in the form of an elephant. You, freed from the spider form, will be born as a king in the Chola dynasty, perform many righteous deeds, and attain liberation.” Thus, Lord Shiva bestowed His grace upon the elephant and the spider and disappeared.

Therefore, this sthalam came to be known as Thiru-Aanaikka because grace was bestowed upon an elephant. The Gananatha who was freed from the elephant form returned to Kailash. The Gananatha who was freed from the spider form was born as the son of Subadeva and Kamalavathi in the Chola dynasty and ruled for a long time with the name Kochchengan Chozhan, due to his red eyes. He built many sacred temples for Lord Shiva to reside in. Thirumangai Azhwar sang about Kochchengan Chozha Nayanar: “He built seventy beautiful elevated temples for the eight-shouldered Lord and ruled the world, the Chola who flourished in the sacred lineage.” Kochchengan Chozha Nayanar was the one who built seventy elevated temples that elephants could not enter. This is the story of the elephant and the spider’s worship in this sthalam.

Secondly, the history of Jambu Muni’s penance. In this sthalam, which was once a Jambu Vanam (forest of Naval trees) filled with Naval trees, a sage once performed severe penance, controlling his senses.

One day, a white Naval fruit fell from a Naval tree before the sage. It was very luminous and had a sweet taste. The sage picked up the fruit and was astonished by its greatness. Thinking that he should not eat it himself but offer it to the Lord, he went to Mount Kailash and offered the precious fruit he had brought to the Peruman. The fruit, having been eaten, began to sprout within the sage’s stomach and grew into a large tree, causing the sage’s head to burst. The sage, now in the form of a tree, performed an ecstatic dance and praised the Peruman.

He requested that this fruit, now grown into a tree, with its mother tree on the sage’s head, should reside in the shade of that mother tree. The Peruman, bestowing His grace upon the sage, instructed him to return to the place where the fruit had originally fallen, promising to come there Himself. The sage, who had taken the form of a tree, desired to reach this sacred place of knowledge and set out from Kailash, walking. Many were astonished to see the tree walking.

Thus, he came to the very spot where the fruit had fallen, to that Jambu Vanam, and performed severe penance for a long time. The Peruman, moved by his penance, resided in the shade of the Naval tree as the sage desired. This glorious Naval tree serves as the sthala-vriksham. Since the Peruman is enshrined beneath the Naval, or Jambu, tree, He is known as Jambunathar.

Next, thirdly, the history of Panchaprakaram, Brahma Devan, his At a time when Brahma was very proud of his creative work, he created a woman of exquisite beauty. Upon seeing her, Brahma, driven by fate, conceived an evil desire for her, like a Chataka bird seeing a cloud.

Consequently, the power of his creative work diminished. Those he created deviated from the path of righteousness and followed evil ways. They met untimely and unnatural deaths. Witnessing this, Brahma realized his mistake and trembled with fear. Seeking atonement for his sin, he came to Thiru-Anaikka, a sacred place of wisdom, and began severe penance. Peruman, understanding this, and wishing to purify Brahma’s mind, came here with the Goddess.

At that time, Shiva disguised as the Goddess and the Goddess disguised as Shiva, appeared before Brahma. Brahma, seeing Shiva standing before him in the form of a woman, fell like a uprooted tree. He prostrated at Shiva’s sacred feet and praised Him in many ways. He prayed that his sin, committed out of ignorance, be forgiven and that he be granted the grace to resume his creative work. Shiva, seeing Brahma’s mature state, bestowed His grace and disappeared with the Goddess. Brahma bathed in the Thirtham he had created and circumambulated the five prakarams (corridors), worshipping Peruman.

He grandly conducted a Mandala Brahmotsavam for forty days for Peruman Jambukeswara. On the thirty-seventh day, Peruman, just as He had appeared to Brahma, manifested with the Lord in the form of a woman and the Goddess in the form of a man, and conducted the Panchaprakara Utsavam. This festival continues to be celebrated annually to this day.

Fourthly, the history of the Goddess receiving instruction.

One day, Uma Devi worshipped Paramasivan, the Lord of Kailash, and raised a question about a doubtful matter. Peruman addressed Uma Devi, saying, “Go to a sacred place of wisdom on earth and perform penance. We will come there and instruct you.” Uma Devi was deeply saddened, unwilling to part from Paramasivan. Peruman comforted the Goddess, gave her assurance, and sent her to the sacred place of wisdom.
