Since a king worshipped here, the Lord is known by the sacred name Rajalingamoorthy. It is believed that if snakes bite on this mountain, the venom will not spread. During dry seasons, if Abhishekam is performed for Sagunakundru Vinayagar, it rains. The milk offered as Abhishekam to the Shiva Lingam turns into curd within a few moments.

Every full moon, devotees circumambulate this herb-rich mountain. While circumambulating, if one stands near the Kaattupillaiyar temple and loudly calls out “Manikka Malaiyane,” an echo is heard. These are all the glories of this Sthalam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having departed from Thiru-Kadambanthurai, arrives here. He worships the Lord of this Sthalam and composes a Thiru-Pathigam. It is the eighty-sixth Thiru-Pathigam, a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathigam, in the fifth Thiru-Murai.

Kaala Paasam Pidithezhuth Thoothuvar, Baalagar Viruththar Pazhaiyaarenaar, Aala Neerhal Amarntha Vaatpokkiyar, Seelamaarnthavar Semmaiyul Nirpare. Viduththa Thoothuvar Vanthu Vinaikkuzhi, Paduththapothu Payanilai Paavikaal, Aduththa Kinnarang Ketkum Vaatpokkiyay, Eduththum Eththiyum Inburuminhale. Vanthivaaru Valaiththazhuth Thoothuvar, Unthiyodi Narahaththidaamunam, Anthiyin Oli Thaangum Vaatpokkiyar, Sinthiyaa Ezhvaar Vinai Theerpare. Kootram Vanthu Kumaiththidum Pothinaar, Thetram Vanthu Thelivu Uralaagume. Aatravum Arul Seyyum Vaatpokki Paal, Ettrumin Vilakkai Irul Neengave.

Maarukondu Valaiththazhuth Thoothuvar, Veru Veru Paduppathan Munname, Aaru Senchadai Vaiththa Vaatpokkiyaarkku, Oori Oori Urugum En Ullame. Kaanamodi Kadithazhuth Thoothuvar, Thaanamodu Thalaipidiyamunam, Aananjadiyugandha Vaatpokkiyar, Oonamillavarkku Unmaiyil Nirpare. Paarththu Paasam Pidithezhuth Thoothuvar, Koorththa Velaar Kumaipathan Munname, Aarththa Gangai Adakkum Vaatpokkiyar, Keerththimaigal Kilarndhuraiminhale. Naadivanthu Naman Thamar Nal Irul, Koodivanthu Kumaipathan Munname, Aadal Paadal Ugandha Vaatpokkiyay, Vaadi Eththa Nam Vaattam Thavirame. Kattaruththuk Kadithazhuth Thoothuva, Pottu Nokkip Purappadaame, Attamaama, Malar Soodum Vaatpokkiyaarkku, Ittamaagi Inaiyadi Eththume. Irakkam Munnariyaathu Ezhuthoothuvar, Parakkaliththavar Pattruthan Munname, Arakkanukkarul Seytha Vaatpokkiyar, Karappathum Karappar Avar Thangatkke.

We shall continue to reflect on the Purana of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 439, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having departed from Thiru-Parayathurai, crosses the Kaveri River and ascends its northern bank, after visiting Sthalams on the southern bank of the Kaveri such as Thiru-Alandurai, Thiru-Chendurai, and also Thiru-Kadambanthurai and Thiru-Vaatpokki. Appar Swamigal reaches the Thiru-Sthalam named Thiru-Paingili.

At this time, the gracious event of the Lord providing Appar Swamigal with a packed meal (Kattuchoru, Potichoru) is about to occur. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having crossed the Kaveri and ascended its northern bank, continues his journey towards the Thiru-Sthalam named Thiru-Paingili. As he travels towards Thiru-Paingili, his body becomes extremely exhausted and weary. He becomes thirsty, and along with it, hunger also sets in. These feelings of hunger and thirst are emotions that can make all our physical and mental efforts falter.

However, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is in the state of a Jeevan Mukta.

Therefore, neither this hunger nor thirst disturbed his mind or consciousness in the slightest.

Thus, even with hunger and thirst, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman continues to proceed, determined to reach Thiru-Paingili. Nevertheless, Lord Shiva decides to alleviate Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s hunger and thirst. Brahma Deva, who is difficult to perceive even when flying in the form of a swan in the sky, and Vishnu, who is difficult to perceive even when digging into the earth in the form of a boar, Lord Shiva Himself comes there to be seen by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. He comes on the very road leading to Thiru-Paingili. How does He come? He creates a cool grove along the path.

He creates a beautiful pond filled with water. The water filled in the pond is created by the Peruman to quench thirst and alleviate water-longing. He creates the grove to relieve the weariness of the journey. He comes ahead on the road leading to Thiru-Paingili, anticipating when His devotee, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, will arrive. Even now, Shiva Peruman is seated there in such a manner, before the time of his arrival. He is seated thus on the path he will take.

How is he seated? As a Brahmin adorned with sacred ash. Sacred ash is that which perpetually adheres to the hearts and sacred forms of devotees. Shiva Peruman, as a Brahmin adorned with such sacred ash, created a pond and a grove on the road leading to Thiru-Paingili, and awaits the arrival of his devotee, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman. Even though Thirunavukkarasu Peruman might experience thirst, hunger, and weariness, the groves and ponds here would not captivate his mind, nor could they.

But Peruman is seated as a Brahmin adorned with sacred ash, and that sacred ash ...will indeed captivate the mind of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman.

Therefore, to enchant his devotee and bring him under his sway, the Lord awaits there as a Brahmin smeared with sacred ash.

Furthermore, having created groves and ponds and seated himself as a Brahmin adorned with sacred ash, the Lord also awaits with a bundle of cooked rice (pothichoru) to alleviate Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar’s hunger. Pothichoru refers to rice packed and tied, also known as kattuchoru (packed meal). It is called pothichoru because it contains rice along with its accompanying curries and other provisions.

Thus, with this pothichoru, to quench Thirunavukkarasu Peruman’s hunger, and having created a pond to slake his thirst, and a grove to relieve his weariness ...Peruman is seated as a Brahmin adorned with sacred ash on the path of Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having arrived at this spot on the way to Thiru-Paingili, sees the Brahmin adorned with sacred ash and approaches him. The Lord, who has the bull as his vehicle, seated there in the guise of a Brahmin adorned with sacred ash, beholds Thirunavukkarasu Peruman who has arrived, and graciously says, “You are very weary from walking a long distance. Eat this packed meal I have, drink the water from this pond, and relieve your fatigue.” This divine intention of Shiva Peruman, seated there, towards Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, is a gracious intent aimed at bringing his devotee under his control. Sekkizhar Peruman sings, “You have come a long way and are weary; eat this packed meal from me, drink water from this overflowing pond, relieve your fatigue, and then depart.” Peruman requests him to eat the packed meal he has. The rice here also signifies the ultimate truth of liberation.

“Pathagame soru pattrinava tholnokkam” is from Thiruvachagam. As the Brahmin adorned with sacred ash spoke thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman accepts it as the Lord’s divine grace.

Moreover, the Brahmin spoke with great affection, as if already well-acquainted with Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, urging him to eat.

Therefore, this is the Lord’s divine grace ...thinking thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, without further thought, accepted the packed meal, partook of the sweet food, drank the water, cleansed himself, and relieved his weariness. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman perceives everything as the result of divine grace.

Therefore, he accepted and ate the packed meal given by the Brahmin without refusal, considering it also as the Lord’s divine grace. Having eaten and relieved his fatigue, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar was asked by the Brahmin present there, “Where are you going?” Thirunavukkarasu Peruman replied, “I am going to Thiru-Paingili.” Then, the incomparable Lord, that Brahmin, also said, “I too am going to that place.” Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, having eaten the packed meal and drunk water to relieve his fatigue on the way to Thiru-Paingili, did not think of resting there for a while longer but immediately attempted to proceed towards Thiru-Paingili.

Therefore, the Brahmin there also accompanied Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, saying, “I too am going to Thiru-Paingili.” Sekkizhar Peruman sings here, “When he, who is difficult to describe, said he was going to Thiru-Paingili, the incomparable one said, ‘I am going there,’ and went with him.” Sekkizhar Peruman uses the word ‘udan’ (with) here, indicating that Shiva Peruman, who came as a Brahmin, went along. This word ‘udan’ is unique to Saiva Siddhanta. This word ‘udan’ ...is used by Saiva Siddhanta scholars to explain the three fundamental truths of Saiva Siddhanta. The Siddhantic implication here is that the Lord is eternally present as one with every soul.

Thus, the Brahmin also accompanies Thirunavukkarasu Peruman to Thiru-Paingili. The term ‘Maraiyavanar’ (the one who conceals) suggests that he is hidden within the form of the Brahmin. It also implies that he will soon disappear. This term ‘Maraiyavanar’ conveys that he is praised by the Vedas, and is generally manifest to those who recite the Vedas.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar and that Brahmin reach Thiru-Paingili. As they are about to reach Thiru-Paingili ...very close to it, Shiva Peruman, who had accompanied Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar until then in the guise of a Brahmin, suddenly disappeared. He concealed the form of the Brahmin he had shown until then and returned to his all-pervading state. As the one who had traveled with him suddenly disappeared, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, whose greatness shone through true penance, realized that the one who had come was Shiva Peruman himself. He understood that it was Shiva Peruman who had kept a packed meal on the way for him, created a pond and a grove to relieve his fatigue, waited for him, quenched his hunger, thirst, and weariness, and had accompanied him as a fellow traveler. Realizing this, he praised Peruman, fell down, rose, and shed tears ...raining down, and melting, he immersed himself in divine bliss, exclaiming, “What immense grace is this that the Lord of Dance has bestowed upon me, even me, a humble servant!” Thirunavukkarasu Peruman sings, “Even me, a humble servant.” This ‘adiyen’ (humble servant) implies “even me, who is good for nothing and wanders performing menial service.” With this sentiment, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman melts in devotion.

Now, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman composes a Thiru-Pathigam (sacred hymn) praising the Lord. He sings a Thiru-Pathigam with the theme, “The Lord of Dance bestowed grace upon me, making me worthy.” This Thiru-Pathigam was sung immediately after the Lord disappeared.

However, this Thiru-Pathigam is not currently available to us. Through the words of Sekkizhar Peruman, we learn that Thirunavukkarasu Peruman sang this Thiru-Pathigam. This reference is available to us.

However, a Thiru-Pathigam sung by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman for the Thiru-Sthalam of Thiru-Paingili is currently available. It is the Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathigam titled ‘Udaiyarkovanam’. When was this sung? It was sung after Thirunavukkarasu Peruman went to the temple of Thiru-Paingili Thiru-Sthalam and had a darshan of the Lord. Even that hymn states: “When the Brahmin who came with him disappeared before him at Thiru-Paingili, the great one of true penance, realizing it was the Lord of Dance who had bestowed grace upon him, making him worthy, sang the song, fell, rose, and shed tears. He went to the temple of the Supreme Lord who resides in Paingili, worshipped the Lord with the dark throat, rejoiced greatly, and with true devotion and overflowing love, sang the Tamil garlands of hymns...”

...and performed extensive sacred service with love, remaining there,“ thus Sekkizhar Peruman composes the verses. When he arrived very close to the Thiru-Sthalam of Thiru-Paingili, the Lord who came as a Brahmin disappeared.

At that moment, he sang a hymn, and then, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar now enters the temple of Thiru-Paingili Thiru-Sthalam and has a darshan of Shiva Peruman enshrined there. He worships the Lord, Thiru-Neelakantar, enshrined there, rejoices greatly, and with true devotion and overflowing love, sings the Thevara Thiru-Pathigams, which are garlands of Tamil hymns, performs extensive sacred service, and remains there in Thiru-Paingili with love. The Thiru-Pathigam sung now is the Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathigam pertaining to the Thiru-Sthalam of Thiru-Paingili. Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathigam, Fifth Thirumurai, Forty-first Thiru-Pathigam.

“Udaiyarkovanam ondrum kuraivilar padaigal paridam soozhndha Paingiliyar sadaiyil gangai tharitha saduraraai adaiyavallavarkku illai avalame.” (Those who can reach the clever one who wears a loincloth, has no wants, is surrounded by hosts in Paingili, and holds Ganga in his matted locks, will have no sorrow.) “Mathamamalarsudiya mainthanar sitharaitthirivar vinai theerpparal patharthan thozhuthethu Paingili em athanai thozha vallavar nallare.” (The Lord who wears intoxicating flowers, wanders as a Siddha, removes karma; those who can worship our Father in Paingili, praised by devotees, are good.) “Vizhuthusoozhathan venmazhu vaazhpadai kazhuthu thunjirudkattagaththadalan pazhathonru inri Paingili paramanai thozhuthu selbavar tham vinai thoozhiye.” (The Lord who dances in the dark forest where ghosts sleep, wielding a bright axe; those who worship the Supreme Lord of Paingili without fault, their karma will be destroyed.) “Ondri malum piramanum thammile nindra soozhal arivariyaan idam sendru paridamethum Paingiliyul endrum mevuyirundha adigale.” (The Lord who resides eternally in Paingili, praised by the hosts, whose state Brahma and Vishnu could not comprehend even when united.) “Velaththin uri porththa ...vikirthanar thazhach chenjadai mel pirai vaithavar thazhai than pozhil soozhndha Paingiliyar yazhin paattai ugandha adigale.” (The Lord who wore the elephant’s skin, placed the crescent moon on his red matted locks, resides in Paingili surrounded by screwpine groves, and delights in the music of the lute.) “Kundupattu kuriyariyaa saman mindarodu paduthuyapponthu naan kandangkar vayal soozhndha Paingiliyam andavaanan adiyadainthu uyndhene.” (Having suffered with ignorant Jain fools, I reached the feet of the Lord of the heavens in Paingili, surrounded by dark fields, and was saved.) “Varippai adaravaatti madagari urippai moodiya uthamanar urai Thiruppaingili thisai thozhuvargal poi iruppar vanavarodu inithagave.” (Those who worship the direction of Thiru-Paingili, where the Supreme Lord resides, who wears the striped snake and the skin of the mad elephant, will dwell sweetly with the celestials.) “Kodal kongam puravani mullai mel padal vandisai ketkum Paingiliyar pedu anum pirarariyathathor adunagam asaiththa adigale.” (The Lord of Paingili, where the song of bees is heard over Kodal, Kongam, and wild jasmine, who wears a dancing snake that others do not know whether it is male or female.) “Karula malar kondraiyan tharinan varula mulai mangaiyor panginan therulam pozhil soozhndha Paingiliyam argila amuthai adainthu uymine.” (Attain salvation by reaching the insatiable nectar, the Lord of Paingili, surrounded by groves where chariots roam, who wears a garland of dark Konrai flowers and has a maiden with full breasts as one half.) “Tharukka ...sendru thadavarai pattralum nerukkiyoondra ninainthu sivanaiye arakkan paada arulum emmanidam irukkai Neeli enbarkku idar illaiye.” (When the demon, in his arrogance, tried to lift the great mountain, thinking to crush it, our Lord, who blessed him to sing of Shiva, resides in Neeli; those who say so will have no trouble.) This Thiru-Sthalam of Thiru-Paingili is the sixty-second Thalam on the northern bank of the Kaveri. Neeli is a type of banana tree, a unique species that does not grow elsewhere. Its leaves, unripe fruits, and ripe fruits are all used here for the Lord. This banana tree itself is the Sthala-Vriksham (sacred tree) of this temple.

It is still evident today that if humans consume these offerings after they have been used for the Lord, their ailments are cured. The fruits of this banana tree are offered to the deity and then released into the water in this temple.

Therefore, this Sthala-Vriksham ...the name of this Thalam is derived from the name of the Neeli banana tree.

Here, the Lord’s names are Neelakandeswarar, Neelivananathar, Kadalivasathar, Aranyavidangar. The Goddess’s name is Visalakshi. The Theerthams are Appar Theertham, Sivaganga.

Here, Lord Nataraja granted a vision of his dance to Sage Vasishta. Neelivanam, Kadalivanam, Arambaivanam, Vimalaranyam, Tharalagiri, Svethagiri, Vyagrapuri, Melaichidambaram are other sacred names associated with this Thalam. The walls of this temple are made of a type of stone called Pulvari, which is found only here. Because of this, this Thalam has acquired the name Vyagrapuri. At the second gopuram entrance, there is the temple marking the spot where Appar was given the packed meal and then the Lord disappeared. It is located below ground level.

For this Thalam ...Madurai Meippatha Puranikar has sung the Sthala Puranam. It is very close to Trichy. One can reach this Thalam from Trichy via Manachanallur.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having worshipped in Thiru-Paingili, continues his pilgrimage, his journey towards the northern direction. Let us resume our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part Four Hundred and Forty, Thirunindracharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman continues his journey towards the north from Thiru-Paingili. Sekkizhar Peruman continues to sing: “With great love, Vagisar (Thirunavukkarasu) went and worshipped many sacred mountains and sacred places where the Lord resides, singing melodious Tamil hymns. By the grace of the Lord who shares a part with the Mother, he proceeded north and reached Thiru-Annamalai, where the primordial Lord resides.” Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, departing from Thiru-Paingili, lovingly worshipped the sacred mountains, sacred places, and sacred lands where Shiva Peruman is enshrined, sang Tamil hymns, and by the divine grace of the Lord who shares a part with Uma, proceeded north and reached Thiru-Annamalai. Peruman sings that he reaches Thiru-Annamalai.

From Thiru-Paingili, he visits many sacred mountains, sacred lands, and sacred places. The sacred mountains mentioned here are Thiru-Ingoymalai, Arappalli Nayinar Malai in Kolli Malai, Kanjamalai, Velur in Pachamalai, Theerthamalai, and others. Sekkizhar Peruman sings that he visited many sacred places. Such places include Pulivalam, Thiru-Thalaiyur, Nerkundram, Tholur, Ezhur, and others. He mentions ‘many lands’. Although ‘nadu’ can mean ‘to seek’ or ‘to desire’, if we interpret ‘nadu’ as ‘lands’, we can also include Kongu Nadu, Thiru-Munaippadi Nadu, and other lands here for our contemplation.

This is because there is a Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Pandikodumudi in Kongu Nadu. That Thiru-Pathigam is the Fifth Thirumurai, Eighty-first Thiru-Pathigam, a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathigam.

Therefore, there is reason to believe that Thirunavukkarasu Peruman must have traveled from here to Kongu Nadu, visited Thiru-Pandikodumudi, and composed this Thiru-Pathigam there.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having visited many sacred places and traveling north, reaches the Thiru-Sthalam of Thiru-Annamalai, where Shiva Peruman, the primordial Lord, lovingly resides. Sekkizhar Peruman describes Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar reaching and worshipping Thiru-Annamalai in this verse: “Thirunavukkarasar worshipped Thiru-Annamalai of the Lord with red-eyed bull, circumambulated it, ascended the lofty mountain, worshipped the beautiful Lord who stands before the devotion of devotees, rose, rejoiced, and attained a greatness for his birth that surpassed even liberation.” This verse describes Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar reaching and worshipping Thiru-Annamalai. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar reaches Thiru-Annamalai, the abode of Shiva Peruman. He worships the great mountain of Thiru-Annamalai from a distance.

Then he circumambulates Thiru-Annamalai. The Sthala Puranam of Thiru-Annamalai states that Shiva Peruman, to resolve the dispute between Brahma and Vishnu, stood as a great pillar of fire, and later, yielding to their prayers and out of compassion for earthly beings, manifested as a mountain here, and then as a Linga on it.

Therefore, it is our tradition to worship the mountain itself as Shiva Peruman in Thiru-Annamalai. This sacred mountain, Thiru-Annamalai, is praised as ‘Thungavarai’ – a mountain of greatness. What greatness? It is that which was formerly unknown even to the great deities Brahma and Vishnu, and now is known to people, bestowing abundant grace and the Lord’s divine blessings. That is why Sekkizhar Peruman says in this verse, “Thondar thozhumpukku ethir nirkum” (stands before the devotion of devotees). ‘Thozhumpu’ means servitude. ‘Ethir nirkal’ means to appear openly and bestow grace. “Thondar thozhumpukku ethir nirkum” means the mountain that appears before the servitude of devotees for the sake of their love.

The immense grace that Shiva Peruman, the beautiful Lord, has for all living beings manifests there as Thiru-Annamalai.

Therefore, here Shiva Peruman stands as Thiru-Annamalai, appearing as an inexhaustible nectar to the eyes of living beings. Sekkizhar Peruman uses the name ‘Angan Arasu’ (Beautiful King), which is specifically used for Shiva Peruman, and Manikkavachagar Peruman also sings in the seventeenth verse of Thiru-Vembavai, “Angan Arasai Adiyongatkku Aramuthai” (The Beautiful King, the rare nectar to us, his servants). To such a glorious Thiru-Sthalam of Thiru-Annamalai, Thirunavukkarasar arrives. He worships the mountain from a distance, rises, and circumambulates the mountain. This Thiru-Annamalai is a very famous Sthalam, so famous that one can say there is no one who does not know Thiru-Annamalai. This Thalam is known by many sacred names: Mukthipuri, Thaleswaram, Sivalokam, Suddhanagaram, Gauri Nagaram, Sonachalam, Sonagiri, Sonathri, Arunachalam, Arunagiri, Arunathri, Anargiri, Thiruvarunai, Thiru-Annamalai.

To this ...there is also the special name ‘Gnana Nagaram’ (City of Wisdom). Among the six Adhara Sthalams, Thiru-Annamalai is the Manipooraka Sthalam. Among the Pancha Bhootha Sthalams, it is the central Agni Sthalam. Among the four Mukthi Sthalams, it is the Sthalam that grants liberation merely by thought. Among the twenty-two Shiva Sthalams of Nadu Nadu, it is a special Sthalam. It is a Sthalam distinguished by its Murthi (deity), Sthalam (place), and Theertham (sacred water).

It is also a dwelling place for those of wisdom and penance. This Thiru-Sthalam is the origin of Maha Shivaratri. The granting of the left half to the Goddess is also one of the unique great glories of this Thalam. “The mountain where the primordial great Vishnu and Brahma could not find the end, where the supreme effulgence appeared as a brilliant light, the mountain where Vedas resound, the mountain that grants liberation to those who contemplate it, Annamalai,” and “The mountain that gave a part to Shakti ...the mountain that sprouted as the seed of liberation, the mountain praised by all directions, the mountain that changes the seven births of those who praise it, Annamalai,” thus Guru Namasivayar has sung. This Thiru-Sthalam is glorified in all sacred texts such as Rig Veda, Atharva Veda, Sarabha Upanishad, Sootha Samhita, Rudra Samhita, Bhaskara Samhita, Shiva Maha Puranam, Shiva Rahasyam, Kanda Puranam, Periya Puranam, Arunachala Puranam, Thevaram, Thiruvachagam, Thiruppugazh. The sacred names of the Lord enshrined in this Thalam are Sri Arunachaleswarar, Sri Annamalaiyar.

The sacred names of the Goddess are Sri Abeetha Kuchambal, Sri Unnamulai Ammai. The Sthala-Vriksham is the Magizha tree. Surrounding the mountain in all eight directions are the Ashta Lingams, Ashta Nandis, and over three hundred and sixty Theerthams. Here are the Chakra Theertham, Agni Theertham, Pandava Theertham, Bali Theertham, Simha Theertham, Yama Theertham, Sona Nadi, Unnamulai Theertham, Varuna Theertham, the Adi Annamalai temple, the Manickavasagar Peruman temple, Ashwini Theertham, Sri Ishanya Gnana Desikar Samadhi, Sri Durga temple, and within it, Kadga Theertham and Pavalakundru.

Additionally, there are Patha Theertham, Mulaippal Theertham, and other sacred waters. Twice a year, in the months of Karthigai and Thai, Sri Annamalai Peruman undertakes Girivalam (circumambulation). This temple is a very large and ancient temple. The outer wall, known as the sixth prakaram, is very high. In the middle of the outer wall, on all four sides, stand four tall gopurams. The great one on the eastern side ...The grand Rajagopuram, with eleven tiers, stands two hundred and seventeen feet tall.

The large gopuram on the south side is called Thirumanjana Gopuram, the large gopuram on the west side is called Peigopuram, and the gopuram on the north side is called Ammaniammal Gopuram. This Ammaniammal Gopuram, on the north side, is historically known to have been constructed about two hundred years ago by a female ascetic named Ammaniammal. Inside the Rajagopuram, to the right, is the Thousand-Pillared Mandapam. To the left is the shrine of Kambathu Ilaiyanar. Its Moolasthanam is located at the northeast pillar of the Valaikappu Mandapam. This is the place where Lord Muruga, in response to the prayers of Sri Arunagirinathar Peruman, appeared before Prabuda Deva Marayar in this pillar.

To the south of this shrine ...To the south, surrounded by the Thirumal Pathi Mandapam on all four sides, is the sacred tank known as Sivaganga. To its north is the shrine of Sarvasiddhi Vinayagar. To the east and south of Sivaganga is the fifth prakaram. To the north of Sarvasiddhi Vinayagar shrine, in the southwest direction of the Thousand-Pillared Mandapam, is the Pathalalingeswarar shrine. Opposite the large Nandi is the Vallala Maharaja Gopuram. It was upon this gopuram that Sri Arunagirinathar, in an attempt to cast off his mortal body, was saved by Sri Murugaperuman, who appeared before him and blessed him.

To its north is the Sri Gopurathu Ilaiyanar shrine. This is the very spot where Arunagirinathar attained blissful ecstasy, exclaiming, “I beheld the mighty Aruna’s sacred gopuram, approaching its northern entrance.” To the south of this gopuram ...To the south is the Sri Kalyana Sundareswarar shrine. Inside the Vallala Maharaja Gopuram, to the right, stands the beautiful Sakthi Vilasa Sabha Mandapam. To its west is the Puravi Mandapam. Adjacent to the southern wall of the gopuram is the Kalabhairavar shrine. The deity here is seen radiating an unparalleled fierce energy.

Nearby is the sacred pond known as Brahma Theertham. The fourth prakaram begins above this pond. The main gopuram visible on the eastern side of this prakaram is the Kili Gopuram. The image of a parrot is found on this gopuram and on its first tier. Inside the Kili Gopuram, opposite it, is the sixteen-pillared mandapam, known as the காட்சி மண்டபம் (viewing mandapam), where on the evening of Karthigai Deepam, the Panchamurthis are seated, facing the mountain, and simultaneously, the Deepa Darshanam (sight of the lamp) takes place. Above this mandapam, opposite it, is the Dhwajasthambam ...The Dhwajasthambam and the Akanda Deepa Sthambam, where the Bharani Deepam is placed, are present.

This is the third prakaram. In this prakaram are located the Sri Sambandha Vinayagar shrine, the Magizhamaram (tree), the Thirukalyana Mandapam, the Sri Arunagiri Yogeeswarar shrine, the Devi Unnamulai Amman shrine, the Yagasalai, the Kalathilingeswarar shrine, the Ekambareswarar shrine, the Jambulingeswarar shrine, the Pidari Sapthakanniyar shrine, and the Chidambaralingeswarar shrine. Numerous ancient inscriptions are found on the inner walls of this prakaram. After worshipping Sri Adhikaranandeeswarar at the main entrance of Sri Annamalai Peruman’s shrine and obtaining permission, one enters the second prakaram, where all the Moolavars (main deities), Utsavamurthis (processional deities), Samayacharyars (spiritual preceptors), Nayanmars, and Sri Venugopala Swamy, accompanied by Sri Rukmini and Satyabhama, are seen. In the first prakaram, which is the western corridor, Sri Dakshinamurthy and Chandikeswarar are present. In the sanctum sanctorum, which is considered the heart of the temple, Sri Annamalai Peruman bestows His grace in the form of a Lingam.

After worshipping with the chant, “Annamalaiyam Anna Potri, Kannar Amudak Kadale Potri” (Praise to Annamalai, the Lord; Praise to the ocean of nectar for the eyes), one can proceed to the Devi’s shrine through the Vaikunta Vaayil on the northern side of the second prakaram. In the Dhwajasthambam mandapam in front of the shrine, the Navagraha Murthis are present. On the pillars of the Mahamandapam in the Devi’s shrine, Ashtalakshmis, Rudradurga, Mahashakti, Mahasaraswati, Siddhi Vinayagar, Karthikeyar, Kalantakar, Veeranathar, and Veerabhadrar are seen in their beautiful forms. In the prakaram surrounding the sanctum sanctorum, Sri Parasakthi Amman, Parivaramurthis, and Chandasakthi bestow their grace. In the sanctum sanctorum of the Ambika’s shrine ...Devi Abeetha Kuchambaal, Unnamulai Ammai, shines with immense beauty as a divine and auspicious form. Six daily rituals are regularly performed in this temple.

Every month, the new moon day, Monday, Friday, Saturday, Amavasai, Krithigai, Pournami, Pradosham, Shukla Chaturthi, and Shukla Shashti are observed.

Now, regarding the festivals celebrated in this sacred place: In the month of Chithirai, the Vasanthotsavam begins on the Mrigashirsha star and lasts for ten days. In the month of Aani, the Dakshinayana Brahmotsavam lasts for ten days. In the month of Aadi, the Aadipooram Utsavam lasts for ten days, with the Theemithi Vizha (fire-walking festival) on the last day. In the month of Purattasi, the Navaratri Utsavam lasts for ten days. In the month of Aippasi, the Skanda Shashti Utsavam lasts for six days. In the month of Karthigai, the Brahmotsavam and Deepa ...The Deepa Thiruvizha (festival of lights) lasts for ten days.

In Margazhi, the Manickavasagar Utsavam lasts for ten days. In Thai, the Sankaranthi Utsavam lasts for ten days. In Panguni, the Uthira Thiruvizha lasts for six days. In addition to these, several special festivals are held. In Chithirai, Sri Natarajar Abhishekam is on the Thiruvonam star, and Sri Thirunavukkarasar Utsavam is on the Sadayam star. In Vaikasi, Abhishekam is on the Visakam star, and Sri Thirugnana Sambandar Utsavam is on the Moolam star.

In Aani, Sri Manickavasagar Utsavam is on the Magam star, and Sri Natarajar Thirumanjanam is also in Aani. In Aadi, Ambika’s Nirai Nonbu and Varalakshmi Nonbu are observed. In Aadi, Sri Sundaramoorthy Swamigal Utsavam is on the Swathi star. In Avani, Vinayagar Chaturthi and the Pittu Thiruvizha are on the Moolam star, and Sri Natarajar Abhishekam is on Shukla Chaturthi. In Purattasi ...In the month of Purattasi, Saraswati Puja and Ambika’s Nirayani Utsavam are celebrated. In Purattasi, Sri Natarajar Abhishekam is on Shukla Chaturthi.

In Purattasi, Sri Arunagirinathar’s Thirunakshatram (birth star) is celebrated with a special utsavam on Moolam. In Aippasi, Annabhishekam is on the Ashwini star. In Karthigai, the 1008 Sangabhishekam is on Somavaram (Monday). In Margazhi, Thiruvathirai Vizha and Arudra Darshanam are observed. In Thai, the Thiruvoodal Utsavam takes place. In Thai, the Manalurpettai Theerthavari is held on the fifth day.

The Kalasapakkam Theerthavari is on Ratha Saptami. The Thaipusam Theerthavari is also held. In Masi, the Pallikondapattu Theerthavari takes place. Vallala Maharaja’s Utharakiriyai (post-funeral rites) is on the Magam star. In Masi, Maha Shivaratri is celebrated specially. In Masi, Sri Natarajar Abhishekam is on Shukla Chaturdashi.

The special festival associated with this sacred place ...The Karthigai Deepa Darshana Brahmotsavam is a Brahmotsavam well-known to all devotees. This festival begins on the Moola Uthiradam star in the month of Karthigai, and on the tenth day, Thirukarthigai, the Mahadeepa Darshanam, followed by the Theppa Thiruvizha (float festival) and Giri Pradakshinam (circumambulation of the hill), takes place. On the first day of this festival, the vehicles of Mooshikam (mouse), Mayil (peacock), Adhikaranandi, Annam (swan), and Chinna Rishabam (small bull) are used. On the second day, silver Indravimanams (celestial vehicles) and other vehicles are used. On the third day, Simham (lion) and silver Annam. On the fourth day, silver Karpaga Viruksham (wish-fulfilling tree), silver Kamadhenu (wish-fulfilling cow), and other silver vehicles.

On the fifth day, silver Mooshikam, silver Mayil, and silver Periya Rishabam (large bull). On the sixth day morning, the procession of the Sixty-Three Nayanmars takes place, and in the evening, the silver Ratham (chariot) and silver Indravimanam. On the seventh day, the Panchamurthis’ chariot. On the eighth day evening, the golden Vanna Meru and Bhikshandar Utsavam. In the evening ...The Panchamurthis on horseback are seen on the ninth day, along with the Kailasa Vahanam and Kamadhenu Vahanam. On the tenth day, at dawn, the Bharani Deepam is lit.

In the afternoon, the Theerthavari (sacred bath) at Brahma Theertham. At 6 PM, the Panchamurthis ascend the golden Vanna Vimanam for the Jyotiswaroopa Mahadeepa Darshanam. In the evening, the golden Varna Rishabam and others are seen. On the eleventh day, the Theppa Thiruvizha takes place in the Iyyankulam, also known as Indra Theertham. On the twelfth day, Sri Abeetha Kuchambaal, accompanied by Sri Arunachaleswarar, performs Giri Pradakshinam. On the thirteenth day, the Chandikeswarar Utsavam is celebrated.

Thus, the Karthigai Deepa Thiruvizha is celebrated with great splendor. These are special details about the Thiruvannamalai temple and its sacred site.

Next, we will contemplate the Thiruvannamalai Sthala Puranam and the Thiruppathigams sung by Appar Swamigal, who visited the sacred site of Thiruvannamalai. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 441, Thirunindra Sarukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We are contemplating the special features of the Thiruvannamalai Sthalam. A Purana called Arunachala Puranam is mentioned in the Rudra Samhita of the Skanda Purana. It comprises thirteen chapters. This Arunachala Puranam is structured as a narration by Nandikeswarar to Markandeya Maharishi on Mount Kailash.

First, the story of searching for the head and foot: Brahma, due to his act of creation, became arrogant, believing that all beings originated from him. Vishnu, who performs the act of preservation, also became arrogant, believing himself to be superior.

Thus, as Brahma and Vishnu quarreled amongst themselves, Lord Shiva appeared before them as a column of fire ...Lord Shiva appears. They both cease their quarrel and decide that whoever discovers the foot or the crown of this fiery mountain shall be deemed superior. Vishnu assumed the form of a boar and began to descend, declaring he would find the foot of the fiery column. Brahma transformed into a swan and began to ascend, intending to find the crown. Both searched for a long time. Brahma, flying upwards as a swan, realized that he could not find the crown of this fiery column.

Therefore, he decided to lie, claiming he had seen the crown, and resolved to find a witness to corroborate his falsehood. Just then, a petal of a Thazhampoo (Kewra flower) fell from Lord Paramasivan’s crown and appeared before him. Brahma spoke to that Thazhampoo petal. He explained that he had been flying and striving for a long time to find the crown of this fiery column, but it remained elusive, and he no longer had the strength to fly.

Therefore, he pleaded with the Thazhampoo to bear witness that he had seen the crown of this fiery column.

Thus, by citing various Dharma Shastras, he persuaded the Thazhampoo to lie.

Then, he descended to Earth with it and, seeing Vishnu, declared, “I have seen the crown of Paramasivan and returned.” The Thazhampoo also affirmed that it was true. At that moment, Lord Shiva emerged from that fiery mountain. Seeing this, Brahma was terrified. Vishnu, however, stood worshipping and praising Paramasivan.

Lord Shiva bestowed various boons upon Vishnu, who stood humbly worshipping. Addressing Brahma, He said, “Because you ...Because you lied, you shall have no temples or worship on Earth.” Addressing the Thazhampoo, He angrily declared, “Because you bore false witness for Brahma, from this day forward, I shall not wear you.” Hearing this, Brahma became extremely fearful and worshipped the Lord with various hymns.

Then, Lord Shiva commanded Brahma to continue his work of creation as before.

Thus, the fiery mountain, which stood as a column of fire, contracted and became a small mountain. When Brahma, Vishnu, and the Devas requested that the brilliance of this mountain be reduced, as its radiant light was unbearable for anyone to behold, Lord Shiva complied.

Afterwards, when everyone requested that a light always be visible at the summit of this mountain, Paramasivan replied that on the Karthigai star in the month of Karthigai ...On the Karthigai star in the month of Karthigai, a light would be shown, and He also spoke of the glory of Arunachalam.

Then, all the Devas requested Lord Shiva to remain in the form of a Lingam for their worship. Paramasivan agreed, saying, “So be it,” and disappeared into the mountain, becoming a Lingam there. All the Devas, Vishnu, and Brahma worshipped that Lingam for fourteen thousand years, received their blessings, and returned to their respective abodes.

Once, on Mount Kailash, Sri Parameswaran and Parvati Devi were playing.

At that time, Parvati rose, bowed to the Lord, and asked, “Lord, who are the Sun and the Moon?” The Lord replied, “They are Our eyes.” Playfully, Ambika covered the Lord’s two eyes with her two hands. At that very moment, the universes plunged into darkness. All beings, including Brahma and Vishnu, lost their eyesight. They approached the Lord and complained.

The Lord reassured them, asked Ishwari to remove her hands, and opened His three eyes. A brilliance as if twelve crore suns had risen appeared, and the seven worlds were freed from darkness. Seeing this, Parvati Devi was frightened and said, “Lord, I have become the cause for all these worlds to be plunged into darkness and for the beings within them to suffer. Because I covered Your sacred eyes, these beings are suffering in darkness, and that sin has now come upon me. Where should I go to perform penance to remove this sin?” The Lord replied, “O Uma, sin will never touch you. The sins committed by others will be removed when you perform penance.”

Therefore, if you wish to perform penance, go to Kanchipuram, which is the most excellent of the seven places of liberation, perform Shiva Puja, and do penance,“ said the Lord.

Then, Ambika came to Kanchipuram and performed Shiva Puja. When the Kampa Nadi overflowed, Ambika embraced the Lord. The Lord, who appeared as Thazhuva Kulaintha Nathar (the Lord who melted at the embrace), asked Ambika, “What boon do you desire?” Ambika replied, “Lord, you must grant me your left half.” The Lord then said, “If you perform penance at the Arunachala Sthalam, which is south of Kanchipuram, I will grant you my left half.” Ambika then asked, “You say Kailash, Kasi, Kanchi, but Arunachalam is greater than these.

Therefore, you must tell me its greatness.” Umadevi asked, and the Lord imparted the greatness of Arunachala Sthalam to Ambika.

Then, Ambika, seated in a pearl palanquin, set out with Ganapathi, Murugar, the Saptha Kannigal, Shiva Ganas, and Bhairavar. After traveling two ‘katham’ (a measure of distance), she had a pandal (temporary shelter) made of plantain trees erected and sat there. She then instructed Subramaniyar, “Bring water here with your Velayudham (spear) for our Sandhyavandanam and other rituals.” Lord Muruga threw his Velayudham to the west, and it pierced through the seven rivers, including the main one, and the seven mountains where they resided, reaching the ocean and bringing back water. That is now flowing as the river Seyar. Ambika bathed in that river, performed her Japa, Tapa, and rituals, and while seated in the plantain pandal ...While seated in the plantain pandal, she asked Subramaniyar why the river water was red. Subramaniyar then narrated the story of seven Brahmins who performed penance in Ananthamapuram.

The next day, at sunrise, after performing their bathing, Japa, and Tapa rituals in that river, everyone set out with the Devi and reached the Arunachala Sthalam. There, they joined Gautama’s ashram, and the Devi resolved to perform penance as instructed by Paramasivan. To the east of Thiruvannamalai, she built a hermitage, placed the Sapthamathars and others as guards in the prakarams, and, placing her left foot on a well-heated copper plate, folded her right leg, placed it on her left thigh, and performed fierce and intense penance facing the Lord. While Ambika was thus engaged in penance ...Brahma, Vishnu, and all the Devas came and bowed to Ambika, explaining their suffering at the hands of Mahishasura. Ishwari then instructed Durga Ambika, “Go and destroy Mahishasura.” The origin of this Mahishasura is narrated as follows: Fifty Rishis, including Agastya Muni, went to the ashram of Vara Muni.

There, Vara Muni did not show them due respect. Thereupon, they cursed Vara Muni to be born as Mahishasura, with the face of a buffalo. He was indeed born as Mahishasura and committed atrocities.

Once, while hunting in the forest, he encountered a Rishi named Mannatha, who was performing penance with a crystal lingam in his hand. Mahishasura, ravenously hungry from hunting, seized and devoured Mannatha Rishi. At that moment ...The crystal lingam in Mannatha Rishi’s hand became lodged in Mahishasura’s throat. This is the story of Mahishasura. The Devas appealed to Ambika, who was performing penance, to alleviate the atrocities of this Mahisha. Mahishasura, who was in the Nilgiris, set out for hunting with a hundred Rakshasas for food.

At that time, the hundred Rakshasas who accompanied him surrounded the forest where Ambika was performing penance. The Ashtabhairavas, who were guarding Ambika, slew those hundred Rakshasas. Some of them went and reported this to Mahishasura, who, enraged, mounted a chariot drawn by a hundred green horses, came with his four-fold army, uprooted mountains, and hurled them at the place where Ambika was performing penance. The Ashtabhairavas then went and killed Nikumbhasura. Hearing this, Mahishasura ...Hearing this, Mahishasura mounted a chariot drawn by a hundred elephants and came to the forest where the Mother was performing penance, accompanied by an army of hundreds of thousands of Rakshasas.

There, the Rishi, Rishiswarar, who was performing penance, informed Ambika. Ambika then dispatched Durga. Durga, mounted on a Yaali (mythical lion) vehicle, set out with the Ashtabhairavas, Sapthamathars, and others, engaged in a fierce battle with Mahishasura, and destroyed half of his army.

Then, Mahishasura, enraged, chased Durga’s army, which fled in fear and hid in the forest. Seeing this, Durga meditated on Ambika, who was performing penance.

Then, by Ambika’s command, sixty-four crore Yogini Shaktis arose in the sky and came here. As fire and lightning rained down, Mahishasura’s armies were consumed by fire. The Sapthamathars killed all of Mahishasura’s armies.

Now, Mahishasura and Durga fought directly against each other. Mahishasura came in many forms, such as an elephant face, a horse face, fire, a deluge, darkness, Brahma, and Vishnu, to oppose her. Durga killed all of them. When he still did not die, she meditated on Ambika, who was performing penance.

Then, by Ambika’s command, an ethereal voice from the sky declared that if Mahishasura, who came in a magical disguise, was killed, he would not die. But when he came with a buffalo-demon face, if his head was severed and trampled underfoot, he would die. Hearing this, Durga again fought with Mahishasura. When he came with a buffalo-demon face, Durga severed his head with her sword, threw it under her foot, and trampled him. She takes the crystal lingam from her neck.

Thus, she takes the crystal lingam from his neck, gives it to Ambika, and narrates what happened. Durga receives the crystal lingam given by Durga, but the lingam does not leave Ambika’s hand. This lingam was on the neck of Mahishasura. Gautama Muni narrates this history, and Ambika listens.

Therefore, Gautama Muni tells Durga that the sin of killing one who wears such a lingam will be absolved by bathing in the nine sacred waters.

Thus, the nine sacred waters, namely Ganga, Yamuna, Saraswati, Narmada, Godavari, Kaveri, Sindhu, Sitadevi, and Sonanadi, came forth. Because it was created by Durga’s sword, it is called Kadka Tirtha. It is named so. Ambika bathed and performed penance in it for a month, and then the lingam left her hand. Ambika placed the lingam on the bank of the spring and worshipped it.

Then, she bathed in Brahma Tirtha, circumambulated the temple, and stood before the Lord to worship Him.

The Lord blessed Ambika to circumambulate the mountain. When Ambika circumambulated this mountain, the Lord appeared on His Rishabha mount and united Ambika with His left side. This is the chapter of receiving the left side.

Similarly, in the Arunachala Purana, there are many sub-sections such as the Vajrangada Pandyan chapter, the Tirtha chapter, the Tirumalai Valampuri chapter, the Aditta chapter, the Pradattarajan chapter, the Papam Tirtha chapter, the Pulakasura chapter, and the Vallala Maharaja Purana, which are found in the Arunachala Purana. These are summaries of the book called Arunachala Purana. There are various Sthala Puranas, books, and Stotra books for Arunachala. Arunachaleswara Anubhuti, Sri Arunachalesar Navakarikai Malai, Arunachala Satakam, Arunachala Aksharamaalai, Arunachala Aksharamanimalai, Arunachala Navamani Malai, Arunachala Pathigam, Arunachala Pancharatnam, Arunachala Ashtakam, Arunachaleesar Pathigam, Arunachaleswarar Sara Prabhandam, Arunachalesar Vannam, Arunachala Kirtanaigal Andadi, Thiruvarunai Thani Venba, Pathittruppattu Andadi, Siledai Andadi, Venba Malai, Thiruvarunai Kalivenba, Thiruvarunai Kalambagam, Thiruvarunai Andadi, Arunagiri Puranam, Arunachala Puranam, Arunachala Puranam composed by Saiva Ellappa Navalar, Thiruvarunai Kalambagam, and Thiruvanamalai Thiruvarul Pathigam, Thiruvanamalai. Malai Pathigam composed by Thirukurugoor Srimath Gnanasiddha Swamigal, Thiruvannamalai Arunachaleswarar Pathigam, Thiruvannamalai Karthigai Deepa Venba, Annamalai Satakam, Annamalai Venba, Annamalaiyar Vannam, Annamalai Pancharatnam, Sonasaila Malai, Sonachala Venba, Sonasaila Pathigam, Sonachala Satakam, Rudrasamhita Stotram, Unnamulaiyamman Pathigam, Unnamulaiyamman Varugai Pathigam, Unnamulaiyamman Satakam, Thiruvarunai Unnamulaiyamman Pillaitamil, and many other books. Thirugnanasambandha Peruman has blessed us with two Thiruppathigams.

Appar Swamigal has blessed us with three Thiruppathigams. Besides that, he has also blessed us with a short Lingapurana. Thiruvempavai, composed by Manickavasaga Peruman, was blessed in this Sthalam. Sundaramurthy Swamigal has sung about this Sthalam as a Vaippu Sthalam in other Pathigams. Parana Deva Nayanar has mentioned and sung about this Sthalam. These are all news from the Arunachala Purana, news about the Arunachala Temple.

Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, who came to this Sthalam, blesses us with three Thiruppathigams. We will continue to contemplate on them.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 442, Thirunindracharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman comes to Thiruvannamalai, worships the mountain from afar, circumambulates it, and stands worshipping the Lord. Sekkizhar Swamigal states here that Thirunavukkarasu, having worshipped the Lord and risen, delighted in it, achieved a greatness superior even to liberation in his very birth. That is, Sekkizhar Swamigal states here that he attained a joy superior to the joy of liberation. Gnana Sastras state that liberation is the highest attainment.

They also state that birth is evil. The Gnana Sastras state that birth is evil.

However, it is mentioned here that when Appar Swamigal worshipped Thiruvannamalai, he experienced a joy superior to the bliss of liberation, which is that supreme state.

Furthermore, in this birth, the joy of worshipping the Lord is experienced in the company of devotees.

Therefore, when Thirunavukkarasu Peruman worshipped, rose, and delighted, he attained that experience of joy, and thus, the meaning here is that he realized, at the level of anubhuti, that this very birth is superior to that state of liberation. It is stated here that he achieved a greatness superior to the bliss of liberation. Generally, Gnana texts state that liberation is a goal to be achieved through spiritual practice. The inner meaning of this is that the greatness superior to the bliss of liberation, which is a goal to be achieved through spiritual practice, was attained here through the very act of worshipping Annamalai. Ramana Chettiar writes the following commentary on this passage: “They say that merely thinking of Annamalai brings liberation.

“Here, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman comes to Annamalai, thinks of it, sees it, sings about it, worships it, rises, and delights in it.

“Therefore, he attained a greatness superior even to liberation.” “Nattravathodu Gnanathiruppare” is a Thiruppathigam.

“Furthermore, when Sekkizhar Swamigal sings about the glory of the holy assembly, he says, “They shone with the virtue of not desiring even liberation, but only worshipping with abundant love.” (Verse 143). We can also apply that here. Sivakavimani Ayyavargal, who commented on “Koodum Anbu” (abundant love), writes that it is the love that causes one to unite with God without separation.

“Therefore, devotees are such that this very birth, in which they stand worshipping due to such abundant love, is enough; they do not even desire the bliss of liberation. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman has thus blessed us: “If one can behold the bent brow, the sweet smile on the coral-red lips, the matted locks, the white ash on the coral-like body, and the golden feet that exude sweet fragrance, then even this human birth is desirable in this great world.” Manickavasaga Swamigal has prayed: “Grant me, O Lord, a birth at Your holy feet.” It is these very things that Sekkizhar Swamigal now sings about, describing the state of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman: “He worshipped the Lord, who is the beautiful mountain shining on Annamalai, the nectar for the eyes of devotees with boundless love, who swallowed the deadly poison that arose from the ocean to protect the celestials, with a melting heart, and performed sacred service by singing Tamil Thiruppathigams filled with melody, bowing and praising Him.” Sekkizhar Peruman continues to sing. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman worships the Lord, who is the beautiful mountain shining on Annamalai, who is like nectar enjoyed by the eyes of devotees with boundless love, and who swallowed the poison that arose from the ocean to protect the celestials, with a melting heart.

“Thus, worshipping with a melting heart, With such a thought, he sings Tamil Thiruppathigams full of melody, bows, praises, and performs sacred services.

“Here, Swamigal has used a paradox with great taste by saying “Annamalai mel animmalai” (the beautiful mountain on Annamalai). That is, if Annamalaiyar is the one who resides in the sacred Sthalam of Arunachala, it means that He is inaccessible even to the minds of the Devas and others.

“Thus, the Siva Peruman, who is inaccessible to the Devas and others, is the “animmalai” (close mountain) for whom? For the devotees. “Animmalai” means a mountain that is close.

“Therefore, the Siva Peruman, who is an inaccessible mountain (Annamalai) to the Devas and others, is a close mountain (animmalai) to the devotees. He is presented here with a delightful paradox, as the Siva Peruman who is the beautiful mountain on Annamalai is like nectar for the eyes of the devotees. Siva Peruman is like nectar that devotees can drink to their fill with their eyes. Nectar is a metaphor. Some poisonous creatures inflict poison merely by their gaze. In Sanskrit, this is called Drishti Visham.

“Here, Annamalai Peruman is endless nectar for the eyes of the devotees. The meaning here is that merely seeing Thiru Annamalai is nectar.

“Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman has used “Kannar Amudhu” (nectar for the eyes) here. “Annamalai, our Lord, praise! Ocean of nectar for the eyes, praise!” is Praise, Thiru Agaval, Thiruvasagam. In the eighteenth verse of Thiruvempavai from Thiruvasagam, which begins with “Annamalaiyan Adikkamalam” (the lotus feet of Annamalaiyan), Manickavasaga Swamigal praises Him as “Kannar Amudhumai Nindran” (He who stands as nectar for the eyes).

“Therefore, it is the word of our elders that Thiruvannamalai Peruman is endless nectar for the eyes of devotees. Sekkizhar Peruman mentions that he worshipped Annamalai and sang many Pathigams.

“Thus, Of the many Pathigams sung, we now have three Thiruppathigams and, as a fourth, the Lingapurana Kurunthogai. The first Thiruppathigam is the 63rd Thiruppathigam of the Fourth Thirumurai, Thirunerisai Thiruppathigam.

““Othi ma malargal thoovi umaiyaval pangaa mikka sothiye thulangum endol sudar mazu padaiyinaane aathiye amararkove ani annamalaiyulaane neethiyaal ninnaiyallaal ninaiyuma ninaiyileene.” (O Lord, who shares a part with Uma, scattering great flowers, O brilliant light, with eight shining shoulders and a radiant axe, O Primeval One, Lord of the celestials, residing in beautiful Annamalai, by righteousness, I think of none but You.) “Pandanaivendra insol paiyor panga neela kandane karkol kondrai kadavule kamala paathaa andane amararkove ani anamalaiyulaane thondanene unnaiyallaal solluma sollileene.” (O Lord, who shares a part with the sweet-voiced one who conquered the demon, O blue-throated one, O God with the konrai garland, with lotus feet, O Lord, Lord of the celestials, residing in beautiful Annamalai, as your servant, I speak of none but You.) “Uruvamum uyirumagi oothiya ulagukkellam peruvinai” You are the great Lord who became the form and life for all the worlds, and who stands as the birth and liberation from great karma. O Lord of the celestials, residing in beautiful Annamalai, where great waterfalls pour forth gold, I desire nothing but Your feet. O pure gold, coral mountain, Supreme Being, You with the white ash, O golden-footed one, O jewel of virtue, O Lord residing in beautiful Annamalai, where abundant gold flows, O my gold, I think of nothing but You. O Lord with the crescent moon on Your head, O golden-hued one, O one who shares a part with the Goddess, O master of the Vedas, O Lord, O one with the konrai garland, O Vamadeva, O Lord with anklets, O Lord residing in beautiful Annamalai, O Lord, I think of nothing but You.

“On Your matted hair, You hold the great Ganga river, and You wear the elephant hide as a garment, O Lord who conquered Kala. O Lord residing in Annamalai, where the bee swarms, O Lord with the beautiful feet where bees hum, I will not forget. You are the sun, the moon, the sky, the two earths, water, wind, the eight serpents, and the directions, all in Your form. O Lord residing in beautiful Annamalai, whose light is like a gem that emits virtue, I hold on to nothing but Your feet, O Supreme Being. You bestowed the Pasupata weapon upon Arjuna that day. You placed the Ganga, which is like water and flesh, on Your long matted hair.

“O Lord residing in beautiful Annamalai, where clouds gather and roar, O Holy One, I have no other strength than the strength of Your feet. O Lord who bathes in the five products of the cow, including milk, O Lord who stood in such a way that Vishnu and Brahma could not see You, O Lord residing in beautiful Annamalai, where the ruling waters and clouds gather, O Lord with the bull, I will not forget Your lotus feet. O Lord who crushed Kala, who had no mercy, With one finger, You crushed the demon who tried to lift the mountain with his strength, O Lord residing in Annamalai, O Lord of the celestials, I will not forget Your holy feet, worshipped and praised with the head.

“The second Thiruppathigam blessed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman to Thiruvannamalai is the 4th Thiruppathigam of the 5th Thirumurai, Thirukurunthogai Thiruppathigam.

““Vattanai mathisoodiyai vaanavar sittanai thiruvannamalaiyanai ittanai igazhnthar pura moondraiyum attanai adiyen maranthuyvano.” (O Lord who wears the moon, O Lord of the celestials, O Lord of Thiruvannamalai, O Lord who destroyed the three cities of those who scorned You, will I, Your servant, forget You and be saved?) “Vaananai mathisoodiya mainthanai thenanai thiruvannamalaiyanai enanai igazhnthar pura moondreitha ananai adiyen maranthuyvano.” (O Lord who wears the moon, O son, O honey-like Lord of Thiruvannamalai, O Lord who destroyed the three cities of those who scorned You, will I, Your servant, forget You and be saved?) “Mathanai mathiyanai urithaven siththanai thiruvannamalaiyanai muththanai muninthar pura moondreitha aththanai adiyen maranthuyvano.” (O Lord who flayed the mad elephant, O Lord of Thiruvannamalai, O Lord who destroyed the three cities of those who were angry with You, will I, Your servant, forget You and be saved?) “Kaatranai kalakkum vinai poyara thetranai thiruvannamalaiya” O Lord who dispels the karma that stirs the wind, O Lord of Thiruvannamalai, O Lord who destroyed the three cruel cities, O Lord, will I, Your servant, forget You and be saved? O Lord who dispelled the lightning-like karma, O Lord of Thiruvannamalai, O Lord who destroyed the three cities of those who scorned me, O Lord, will I, Your servant, forget You and be saved? O Lord who went to the sacrifice of those who did not respect the assembly, O Lord of Thiruvannamalai, O Lord who conquered and destroyed the three cities of those who were enraged, O cruel one, will I forget You and be saved? O brave one, O one who swallowed poison, O hero of the celestials, O Lord of Thiruvannamalai, O Lord who destroyed the three cities of those who did not understand, O Lord, will I, Your servant, forget You and be saved?

“O Lord who swallowed the poison from the ocean of karma, O Lord of Thiruvannamalai, O Lord who destroyed the three cities of those who did not understand the form, O Lord, will I, Your servant, forget You and be saved? O Lord who wears the snake as a garland, O Lord of Thiruvannamalai, O Lord who destroyed the three cities of those who were angry, O Lord, will I, Your servant, forget You and be saved? O Lord who crushed the demon to make him cry, O Lord of Thiruvannamalai, who crushed him, O Lord who mercifully removes the diseases of my body, will I, Your servant, forget You and be saved?

“The third Thiruppathigam blessed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman to Thiruvannamalai is the 5th Thiruppathigam of the 5th Thirumurai, Thirukurunthogai Thiruppathigam.

““Pattiyerugantheyri pala ilam ittamaaga iranthundoli tharum attamoorthi annamalai kaithozha kettuppom vinai kedillai kaanmine.” (Worship Annamalai, the eight-formed Lord, who rides the bull, and who gives light by begging for alms from many young ones; your karma will be destroyed, and there will be no harm.) “Petram yeruvar peybalikkendravar sutramaa migu thol pugazhalodum atranthirkkum annamalai kaithozha natravathodu gnana thiruppare.” (Those who ride the bull and go begging for alms, their ancient fame will increase; worship Annamalai, which removes suffering, and you will have good penance and wisdom.) “Pallilodu kaiyenthi pala ilam ollai sendrunngal kavarvaar avar allal thirkkum annamalai kaithozha nallavayin nammai adaiyume.” (Those who hold a skull and go begging for alms from many young ones, their suffering will be removed; worship Annamalai, and good things will come to us.) “Paadichendru bali” What will those do who went singing and stood begging for alms? If we sing and dance and worship Annamalai, our past karma will flee. Go seeking and praise His sacred feet; He who came seeking will also take us as His own. If we sing and dance and worship Annamalai, our inner karma will flee.

“He who is like a piece of sugarcane, who plays the veena, the eight-formed Lord residing in Annamalai, the dancer, will be good. He who once took the form of a woman with a coiled bun, the Supreme Being who dances to the rhythm, if we worship the golden Annamalai, the great karma that stood guard will depart. He whose throat is the thought, the Lord who once kicked Kala with His foot, if we worship Annamalai, which rises to the sky, our past karma will vanish. Go first and worship Him three times a day.

“The Lord of Annamalai, who does not cease at dusk, removes the karma of those who rise thinking of Him, the Lord who wears the fragrant great flower. Brahma and Vishnu could not see Him, who stood in the fullness of water and blessed them. If we worship Annamalai, where He resides in glory, the sins we have committed will vanish.

“These three Thiruppathigams are the Thiruppathigams blessed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman to Thiruvannamalai. In addition to these, Sivakavimani Ayyavargal has mentioned that the Lingapurana Kurunthogai was also blessed to Thiruvannamalai.

“Therefore, the Lingapurana Thirukurunthogai is the 95th Thiruppathigam of the 5th Thirumurai, Thirukurunthogai Thiruppathigam.

““Pukkanainthu purinthalarittilar nakkanainthu narumalar koythilar sokkanaintha sudaruli vannanai mikkuk kaanalutrar angiruvare.” (They did not enter and offer flowers, they did not approach and pluck fragrant flowers. The two of them sought to see the brilliant, radiant Lord, who is the embodiment of beauty.) “Alaru neerum kondaat” They did not celebrate with water and clarify. They did not draw and wander with a tilak. The two of them sought to see the radiant Lord, the embodiment of the world.

“They did not take cow dung and water. They did not gather flowers and carry them in baskets. The two of them sought to see the Lord, who is the protector, the Kapali, in His form. They did not celebrate with ghee and milk and remember Him. They did not cast away falsehood and deceit and praise Him. The two of them sought to see the truth of the Lord, who is the fiery, radiant one.

“They did not gather erukkam flowers and weave garlands. They did not wear a large loincloth. The two of them sought to see the Lord with matted hair, approaching Him with arrogance. They did not climb trees and pluck flowers. They did not carry abundant water and bathe Him. The two of them sought to see the radiant Lord, who is full of strength.

“They did not hold a skull and a staff. They did not prostrate with eight limbs. The two of them sought to see the Lord’s feet, which are difficult to reach. The two of them, having reached the sacred feet of the Lord, who is a small, wise one, experienced great suffering in their quest. They did not adorn themselves with sacred ash. They did not weave garlands of fragrant flowers.

“The two of them sought to see the Lord, who is the fiery-hued one, who rides the bull, but could not find His end. They did not split and weave the dark blue water lily that had bloomed. The two of them sought to see the Lord, who burned Kama, the one with deceitful deeds, but could not find His measure. They did not wear a garland of bones and hold a skull. They did not blow the conch shell that had burst forth from the sky. The two of them sought to see the Lord of the universe, who is the fiery-hued one, by digging, but could not find Him.

“Brahma and Vishnu searched everywhere for Him, but could not find Him. The Lord, the meritorious one with fiery matted locks, appeared in the lingam, saying, “I am here.”

“Thus, while performing sacred services and praising Siva Peruman by singing many Pathigams in Thiruvannamalai, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, who is our Lord Thiruneelakandar, With unceasing love, he resolves to visit all the sacred places where our Lord delights to reside on this earth and perform appropriate sacred services. He then sets out to bless Thondai Nadu, the Thondai country.

“We shall proceed with our contemplation.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 443. Thirunindrachcharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Departing from Thiru-Annamalai, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman worshipped many sacred places and arrived in Thondai Nadu. It is mentioned that he worshipped many sacred places along the way. These sacred places are believed to include Thirukkovalur Veerattam, Thiru-Mundeescharam, Thiru-Aamaththur, and others.

As it is said, “Thondai Valanadu, auspicious to the world,” Thiru-Thondai Nadu shines as an ornament to all these worlds. It possesses that ornament, that beauty, because of the greatness of the Mother Goddess who worshipped Lord Shiva there for the salvation of all these worlds. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman arrives in such a Thondai Nadu, along the way. He crosses many forests, mountains, wild rivers, and cities with cool fields full of mango groves, and reaches Thondai Nadu. Forests, mountains, and wild rivers are mentioned here. These are small forests in the northern part of Nadu Nadu and the adjacent southwestern part of Thondai Nadu.

The mountains mentioned here are Senji Malai, Nedungundram, Venkundram, and others. These are not continuous ranges but small hills scattered here and there.

Therefore, the region of the country that Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar visited is now known as the Eastern Ghats mountain range. It is known to all of us that these are not continuous like the Western Ghats but are small hills with gaps in between.

Here, It is mentioned that he passes through many cities surrounded by fields full of mango trees. It is understood from this that cities like Thindivanam, Arani, Vellore, and the surrounding regions were renowned for their mango groves in those days.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, who arrived in Thondai Nadu, reached the sacred place called Thiru-Oththur. Thiru-Oththur is a city reachable from cities like Vandavasi, Thiru-Annamalai, Polur, and Arani in Tamil Nadu. The sacred name of the Lord is Vedapureeswarar, Vedanathar. The sacred name of the Goddess is Balakujambikai, Ilamulai Nayaki. The Sthala Vriksham is the palm tree. The Theertham is the well in the temple and Seyaru, which is now known as Cheyyaru.

It is also called Thiru-Vaththipuram, Thiru-Vaththur, etc. The area where the sacred temple is located is now called Thiru-Vaththipuram. Thiru-Oththur is the sacred name of this place. Oththu means Veda. This is the place where the Lord explained the meaning of the Vedas, hence Oththur. With the prefix Thiru-, it is called Thiru-Oththur.

This is a great sacred place where Thirugnanasambandha Peruman sang a Pathigam and transformed a male palm tree into a female palm tree.

Here, Nandi faces not the Lord but the front gopuram. Thondaiman, who had lost his strength and wandered in the forest, worshipped Vedapureeswarar.

The Lord appeared and blessed him with great strength and armies, instructing him to fight Viswavassu and regain his kingdom. When the king, hearing this, feared, “How will I fight?”

Lord Shiva blessed him, saying, “Nandi will come as your military aid. Before that, you shall go and fight with the armies I have given you.” Accordingly, Nandi Devar is facing east.

Thus, the king’s fear was dispelled upon seeing Nandi Devar, who had been facing west, now turned to face east.

The Lord made Nandi the commander, and the Shiva Ganas as horses, elephants, and chariots as the army, and sent Thondaiman to war. He went and defeated the enemy and ascended the throne again. In the outer prakaram of this temple, there are palm trees, the Sthala Vriksham. Opposite the Ambika shrine, there is a stone sculpture of a palm tree, the Sthala Aitheegam, along with the idol of Thirugnanasambandha Peruman and a Shiva Lingam. The Panchabhootha Shrines are arranged as separate Shiva Linga forms, reminiscent of the Panchabhootha Sthalams: Thiruchitrambalavan, Thiru-Kalaththiyar, Thiru-Aanaikkavular, Thiru-Annamalaiyar, and Thiru-Ekamban. Chandeeswarar is depicted with one leg folded and the other hanging, holding a battle-axe in one hand and resting the other hand on the thigh of the folded leg.

There are separate temples for Dakshinamurthy Peruman and Durga. In inscriptions, the Lord of this place is referred to as Oththur Udaiya Nayanar. There is a Thiru-Oththur Sthala Puranam composed by Karunagara Kavirayar. In the month of Thai, Rathasapthami is celebrated as a ten-day chariot festival. There is a book called Thiru-Oththur Ilamulai Ambikai Anthathi composed by Swaminatha Pillai. We saw that there is a Thiru-Oththur Sthala Puranam for this sacred place.

It contains the Thiru-Nagara Charukkam, Vairavar Uthpava Charukkam, Aarumugan Sakthi Petra Charukkam, Veeranattana Charukkam, Thirumal Neri Petra Charukkam, Vedamothi Vaiththa Charukkam, Ammai Thavam Purintha Charukkam, Thirumana Charukkam, Suriyan Peru Petra Charukkam, Vinayagar Angusa Pasam Petra Charukkam, Harisabam Theerththa Charukkam, Bramman Pavam Theerththa Charukkam, Chandran Peru Petra Charukkam, Manmatha Thagana Charukkam, Arunan Pavam Theerththa Charukkam, Indiran Pavam Theerththa Charukkam, Raghavan Pavam Theerththa Charukkam, Parachcharar Velvichcharukkam, Alamunda Charukkam, Gandharuvan Sabam Theerththa Charukkam, Parkkunan Poojai Seytha Charukkam, Virarkkada Mahamuni Mukthi Petra Charukkam, Tharukavanachcharukkam, Vallavan Santhanam Petra Charukkam, Thondaimanukku Padai Thunai Pona Charukkam, Thala Mahimai Charukkam, Samanar Kazhuveriya Charukkam, thus comprising twenty-seven Charukkams. For this sacred place, there is a Thirupathigam by Thirugnanasambandha Peruman. Appar Swamigal’s Thirumurai, 33rd Pathigam, 9th song; 6th Thirumurai, 70th Pathigam, 8th song; 6th Thirumurai, 82nd Pathigam, 5th song, he has sung about this place as a Vaippu Sthalam. Pattinaththu Pillaiyar has sung about this place in Thiru-Ekambamudaiyar Thiruvanthathi. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, who came to this place, has composed Thirupathigams. It is clearly understood from the sacred songs composed by Peruman that he has sung many Thiruthandagams for this sacred place.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having praised and worshipped Lord Shiva in Thiru-Oththur, departs from there and continues his pilgrimage, worshipping many sacred places. The sacred places that Thirunavukkarasu Peruman visited and sang about are Ilaiyanar Velur, Thiruvan Parththan, Panangattur, Thiru-Magaral, Thiru-Kuranganil Muttram, and other sacred places.

However, the Pathigams composed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman for all these places are not available to us.

Thus, having visited many sacred places, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar arrives in Kanchipuram. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman approaches Kanchipuram, where Ekambaranathar, whose sacred body was embraced and disfigured by the Mother Goddess, resides. Hearing the news that Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, the sacred devotee whom Lord Shiva of Thiru-Adigai graciously enslaved by afflicting him with the colic disease for the salvation of the world, is arriving in Kanchipuram, the Shiva devotees in Kanchi, all rejoice greatly and go forth to welcome Thirunavukkarasu Peruman. Just as lotus flowers bloom upon seeing the arrival of the sun, the faces of the Shiva devotees in Kanchi city bloom upon seeing the arrival of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman. Along the streets of Kanchipuram, beautiful gateways are adorned with festoons, banana trees, and areca nut trees arranged in rows. Full pots and lamps are set up.

Fragrant pandals decorated with garlands are erected.

Thus, the Shiva devotees adorn the beautiful, long city of Kanchi in various ways. Shiva devotees always wear sacred ash and rudraksha and are adorned in sacred attire. Such Shiva devotees go forth to welcome Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, with even greater splendor in their sacred attire. It is customary to welcome elders by carrying festive items such as umbrellas, flags, and ceremonial fans.

Similarly, here, along with those auspicious items, they also carry the sacred broom to welcome Thirunavukkarasu Peruman. The streets of Kanchi city are the streets where Thiru-Ekambanathar’s grand procession takes place.

Therefore, the sacred broom is also special for performing service in this sacred street. Hence, they also rush there with the sacred broom to welcome him.

Furthermore, it is noted here that for Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, who made it a rule to sweep with the sacred broom, the sacred broom is an auspicious item for that sacred service. This sacred broom is very rare for even the Devas to know.

Thus, when Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar arrived at the city limits of Kanchipuram, the Shiva devotees went forth and worshipped him, and he, in turn, worshipped those devotees. The special significance of worshipping devotees before worshipping the Lord is indicated here.

Thus, having worshipped the special devotees of Kanchipuram, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman entered the beautiful walled city of Kanchi. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, having entered the streets of Kanchipuram, arrived before the sacred temple where Thiru-Ekambanathar resides and bestows grace. He bowed at the sacred entrance, rose, approached the sacred courtyard, and saw the Lord of Kachi, Ekambar, whose sacred body, adorned with golden jewels, was embraced by the golden mountain goddess, and he was filled with immense love and worshipped Him, as Sekkizhar Peruman describes in his sacred song. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman approaches the sacred temple where Kachi Ekambanathar resides, prostrates at the gopuram entrance, and rises.

Then he approaches the sacred courtyard and circumambulates the sacred edifice.

Thus, having circumambulated, he approaches the presence of Kachi Ekambar and worships Him. He worships Karuvar Kachi Ekambar residing there. Karuvar means Ekambanathar, who is the abode of the Mother Goddess who holds the essence of grace within all beings. The idea here is that this place is the Prithvi Sthalam, the cause for the creation and growth of the worlds. Upon seeing Thiru-Ekambanathar, a great flood of tears gushes forth. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman’s sacred body is filled with goosebumps all over.

His mind melts with love. As Thirunavukkarasu Peruman sang in Thiru-Angamalai, “O eyes, behold!” the purpose of having eyes is to behold the Lord.

Therefore, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having seen Thiru-Ekamba Peruman, is immersed in joy, having attained the benefit of seeing with his eyes. “My eyes have attained the vision of Kambar, my Lord,” is the sacred saying of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal’s Thevaram.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, immersed in such joy, praises Thiru-Ekambanathar, and sings many Pathigams. We shall continue our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 444. Thirunindrachcharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. In Kanchipuram, before Thiru-Ekamba Peruman, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman’s love overflows, and he is immersed in the flood of Shiva-Ananda.

At that time, he begins a Thirupathigam with the words “Karavadum Vannencharkku Ariyanai.” Thirunavukkarasu Peruman composed a total of seven Thirupathigams for the sacred place of Kanchipuram Thiru-Ekambanathar. He now composes the first of these Thirupathigams. This Thirupathigam is the 7th Pathigam of the 4th Thirumurai, set in the Gandhara Pann.

Karavadum Vannencharkku Ariyanai, Karavarbal Viravadum Perumanai, Vidayerum Viththaganai, Aravada Chadai Thazha Angaiyinil Anal Enthi Iravada Padum Perumanai En Manathe Vaithene. Thenokkum Kili Mazhalai Umaikezhvan Sezhumpavala Thanokkum Thirumeni Thazhaloruvaam Sankaranai Vanorkkum Valarmathiser Sadaiyanai Vanorkkum Enorkkum Perumanai En Manathe Vaithene. Kaippodu Malarthoovi Kathaliththu Vanorkal Muppodum Mudisayththu Thozha Ninra Muthalvanai Appodum Malarthoovi Aimppulanum Agaththadakki Eppodum Iniyanai En Manathe Vaithene. Andamai Adiyai Arumaraiyodu Aimpputha Pindamai Ulakukkor Peyporulam Pinjanai Thondartham Malarthoovi Sonmalai Punaikinra Indai Ser Sadaiyanai En Manathe Vaithene. Aareru Sadaiyanai Ayiram Per Ammanai Pareru Paduthalaiyil Palikollum Paramparanai Neereru Thirumeni Ninmalanai Nedunthoovi E Ererum Perumanai En Manathe Vaithene.

Thesanai Thesangal Thozha Ninra Thirumalal Poosanai Poosanigal Ugappanai Poovin Kan Vasanaimalai Nila Neer Theevazhi Akasamam Isanai Emmanai En Manathe Vaithene. Nallanai Nallanai Nanmaraiyodu Arangam Vallanai Vallarkal Manaththuraiyum Mainthanai Sollanai Sollarntha Porulanai Thukalethum Illanai Emmanai En Manathe Vaithene. Viriththanai Nalvarkku Veruveru Vedangal Poriththanai Pathanjathi Porul Uruvam Punniyanai Thariththanai Gangai Neer Thazhsadai Mel Mathil Moonrum Eriththanai Emmanai En Manathe Vaithene. Akampaththaravanaiyan Ayan Aritharkku Ariyanai Pagam Pennan Pagamai Ninra Pasupathiyai Makampam Maraiyodum Irayanai Mathir Katchi Ekamba Meyanai En Manathe Vaithene. Aduththanai Oriththanai Aruchchunarkku Pasupatham Koduththanai Kula Varaiye Silaiyaka Kurambu Thoduththanai Purameriya Sunai Malku Kayilayam Eduththanai Thaduththanai En Manathe Vaithene.

Thus, after singing this Thirupathigam, beginning with “Karavadum Vannencharkku Ariyanai,” Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar arrives at the front of the Katchi temple. He performs the Uzhavaara sacred service with his hands, both by clasping them and by sweeping.

Thus, having performed the Uzhavaara sacred service, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar now composes various types of Pathigams, such as Kurunthogai, Nerisai, Viruttham, and Thandagam. Among the Pathigams composed by Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, he now composes Pathigams belonging to the Gandhara Pann type. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman now composes Pathigams that fall under the Gandhara Pann category.

Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman refers to them comprehensively as “all the beautiful Tamil garlands.” Thus, the Thirupathigams now sung are the Thirunerisai Thirupathigam beginning with “Nambanai,” the Thiruviruttha Thirupathigam beginning with “Othuviththay,” the Thirukkurunthogai Thirupathigam beginning with “Pandu Seytha,” and the Thirukkurunthogai Thirupathigam beginning with “Poomelanum.” Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar now bestows four Thirupathigams, one of each type.

Therefore, including these four Thirupathigams with the “Karavadum Vannencharkku” Pathigam we just saw, there are a total of five Thirupathigams. The other two Thirupathigams are Thiruthandaga Thirupathigams, which he sings later. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman said.

Thus, he bestows a total of seven Thirupathigams. Of these, three Thirupathigams are in the Fourth Thirumurai, two Thirupathigams in the Fifth Thirumurai, and two Thirupathigams in the Sixth Thirumurai.

Thus, the sacred place of Kanchipuram Thiru-Ekambanathar is included in the three Thirumurais sung by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman. Not only this, but the first, second, and third Thirumurais sung by Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, and the Thirupathigam beginning with “Uganthu Amuthu Seytha” by Moorthy Swamigal in the Seventh Thirumurai, thus Kanchipuram is a sacred place that has been sung about in all seven Thirumurais composed by the three saints.
