Similarly, Thiruvarur also has this special distinction. In this, we will now contemplate the four Thirupathigams sung by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman. We have already seen the Thirupathigam “Karavadum.” Now, the second Thirupathigam, the 44th Thirupathigam of the Fourth Thirumurai, is the Thirunerisai Thirupathigam.

Nambanai Nagaram Moonrum Eriyuna Veruva Nokkum Ambanai Amuthai Aatru Ani Pozhil Katchiyulle Kambanai Kathir Ven Thingal Senchadai Kadavul Thannai Sempana Pavala Thoonai Sinthiyayezhukinrene. Oru Muzham Ulla Kuttam Onpathu Tholayudaitthay Arai Muzham Athana Agalam Athanil Vazh Muthalai Aintha Perumulai Vaithal Patri Kidanthu Nan Pithatrukinren Karumugil Thavizhum Madak Katchi Ekamba Neere. Malaiyinar Magaloru Pagamayanthana Mazhuvondrendi Silaiyinal Mathilgal Moonrum Theeyezha Setra Selvar Ilaiyinar Soolam Enthi Ekambam Mevinarai Thalaiyinal Vanangavallar Thalaivarkkunthalaivar Thame. Pooththa Porkkondrai Malai Purisadaikka Anintha Selvar Theerththamangaiyalai Thirumudi Thigazha Vaiththu Eththuvar Eththaninra Ekambam Mevinarai Vazhththumar Ariyamatten Malkodu Mayanginene. Maiyinar Malar Nedungkan Mangaiyor Pangarakki Kaiyil Or Kapalam Enthi Kadaithorum Palikolvartham Eyvathor Enam Otti Ekambam Mevinarai Kaiyinal Thozhavallarkku Kaduvinai Kalaiyalame.

Tharuvinai Maruvum Gangai Thangiya Sadaiyan Engal Aruvinai Agala Nalkum Annanai Amarar Potrum Thiruvinai Thiruvekambam Seppida Uraiyavalla Uruvinai Urugi Ange Ullaththal Ugakkinrene. Kondathor Kolamagi Kolakka Udaiya Kooththan Undathor Nanjamagil Ulakalam That I may serve the Ekamban, who stands adored by the eight directions, I wander, contemplating. He who wears the moon on His matted locks, adorned with a serpent, and covered in the hide of an elephant, making onlookers tremble. He who resides in the spacious Kachi, in Ekambam. The world was saved by witnessing His dancing gait. My heart gently enters the grace of the Lord with the long chest adorned with a golden Konrai garland.

He whose body is like a mountain, with a dark blue throat, our Ekamban, is sweet to those who see Him today. To those who serve with devotion the Ekamban, who rides the bull and is praised by many devotees in Thuruthi and Pazhanam, bestowing grace upon them, their strong karma will vanish.

Now, the next Thiru-pathikam, the ninety-ninth of the Fourth Thiru-murai. The ninth Thiru-pathikam, Thiru-virutham Thiru-pathikam.

You taught me, showing the path of righteousness, and defeated the Jains. You healed my painful diseases, and mingled with me. If I err in Your service, You will strike me with a tamarind whip, You will be pleased, You will be angry, O Ekamban of Kachi! What did You do to me, to make me associate with such a foolish Jain, and lead me astray like a dumb person? O Ekamban of Kachi, whose beautiful grove is like a cluster of pearls and the light in the ripe fruit, and a cluster of red corals!

You shot a true arrow with Arjuna, and then shot a false arrow, showing Your grace. You shot an arrow to burn the three cities. You hid in the hearts of the wicked who do not praise Your feet, O Ekamban of Kachi, surrounded by great walls! Having resolved to offer a thousand red lotuses for many days, to adorn the garland properly, to destroy the shore, You, who saw the shore, made one flower less and made the eye suffer. O Lord with the crescent moon on Your matted locks, O great Kanchi Ekamban! We can only worship You, saying that You are beyond words and understanding, and that You remove the karma of those who meditate on You.

All the suns, Brahma, Vishnu, the Vasus, the Ekadasas, and the Devas, O Ekamban, our Lord, who is the nectar for them! From the day I was conceived, my heart melted to see Your feet, and I have suffered and wasted away. O Thiru-otriyura, O Thiru-alavaya, O Thiru-varura! Seeing my helplessness, why do You not show mercy, O Ekamban of Kachi! Brahma, Vishnu, Indra, the moon, the sun, and all the Devas, who are at the head of Your victorious gate, lay there without food. The matted locks of the ascetics who are devoted to You, the ascetics with matted locks are lamenting.

O Ekamban with fiery red matted locks, what is Your sacred intention? O Lord, who wears a serpent on Your waist and has matted locks, and whose hands are folded in worship, the devotees, having smeared ashes and rolled on the ground for many days, cried out, “Refuge!” You showed mercy to them, O Ekamban of Kachi! You accepted me, my Lord, and there is no one else but You. You saw this whole world as a witness, and You kept those who stood firm by me, saying I am alone.

Then You, O Ekamban of Kachi, the Lord of radiant color, accepted all. Those who stood there, holding the gates of Your assembly hall, and the ancient Devas, came to worship You, O Kachi, the Lord of Brahma and Vishnu! We stand here now, how shall we come and worship You?

Now, the fourth Thiru-pathikam, the forty-seventh Thiru-pathikam of the fifth Thiru-murai, Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathikam.

O my heart, even after seeing and experiencing the fruits of past karma, do not be disheartened. Wander as a devotee of Ekamban, whose red matted locks are adorned with bees and flowers, so that your sorrow may vanish. Worship the Ekamban of Kachi, whose beautiful groves are filled with fragrant flowers, where Uma, the daughter of the mountain, worships with desire, and where the short ones gather. Even if they move their souls in the body and wander all over the world, they dance in the fierce forest where the heavenly music resounds, they are the Ekamban of Kachi. The three-eyed Lord, who does not blink, is in my heart.

No one knows His nature. The Ekamban, who sat there for the Devas to praise, worship Him who rules us. With medicine, good relatives, and children, O my Lord, Ekamban of Kachi, You sat there for Uma to worship with her dark, wide eyes, You who are the burning good deed. Go to the Ekambam of Kachi, the Lord with the coiled red matted locks, who gave good relatives and wealth, and worship Him, so that darkness may vanish. The Ekamban of Kachi is the Lord who protects us from diseases, who unties the knots of the five senses that come as nose, mouth, ear, eye, and body, and who looks at us with grace. The Ekamban of Kachi is the jewel in the eye, who is the sound in music, the sweet taste in fruit, who cannot be described as male or female, who has no color, and whose form is different.

The Ekamban of Kachi is the Lord who is the origin, who is the consciousness, who is beyond consciousness, who is the Lord of the womb, who is the bright light that Brahma and Vishnu could not find, who is the red lotus on the head of Vishnu. Do not desire the nature of women with slender waists and soft breasts.

The Lord with the ash-smeared body, in the beautiful groves of Kachi, our Lord, will remove our great sorrow. When Ravana, the king of Lanka, went to lift the mountain, and when the Lord pressed His toe, Ravana cried out, “O Ekamban of Kachi!” Our Lord, who has grace, then released him.

Now, the fifth Thiru-pathikam, the forty-eighth Thiru-pathikam of the fifth Thiru-murai, Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathikam.

O Ekamban of Thiru-ekambam, whose form is fiery, when Brahma and Vishnu, the consort of Lakshmi, said, “We are the Devas,” and trembled, are we not Your servants? The beautiful Ekambam of Kachi, where the powerful Devas, Brahma, and Vishnu, stood and worshipped with the Goddess, is suitable for us.

Thus, it is written and praised.

The Lord with the dark throat, with eight shoulders, and three eyes, whose tongue recites the Vedas, who is the Lord of the Devas, resides in the beautiful groves of Kachi Ekambam. Go and worship Him in due order. The Ekambam, where the Lord is the nectar that fills the minds of those who control their senses and meditate on Him, go and worship Him with intention. The Ekambam of our Lord, who is Shiva in the mind, who is the evening, fire, water, sky, and intellect, and who fills the heart, praise and worship Him. Do not go to the side of the unfortunate ones who are Sakyas and Jains. Praise and worship the Ekambam of Kachi, whose feet are like flowers, with your tongue.

Before old age and anger afflict us, let us go and attain the Ekambam, which is the protection of the Devas, and be saved. The Ekambam of the grove, let us go and reach it and be saved. O my heart, abandon the company of beautiful women who are like peacocks, and worship the beautiful lotus feet of Ekamban, the Lord with the dark blue throat. There is no suffering for those who worship the Lord, the Ekamban of Kachi, who holds the bright white axe, who is the truth in the minds of those who abandon all falsehood. When the demon Ravana, thinking of his strength, went to lift Kailash, and when the Lord pressed His toe, his crowns were crushed, and he cried out. Let us go and worship that Ekamban.

Thus, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman sang four Thiru-pathikams at this place and visited the Thiru-mayanam of Kachi. We shall go on meditating. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 445, Thiru-nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Having worshipped and sung about Kachi Ekambam, and having performed the Ulavara Thiru-pani there, and having visited the Thiru-mayanam of Kachi, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman then visited various Thiru-koils located in the great city of Kachi. He visited Thiru-metrali of Kachi and other Thiru-sthalams. We have extensively meditated on the history of Kanchipuram, the history of Thiru-ekambam, and the various Thiru-sthalams in Kanchi in the Thiru-kurippu Thonda Nayanar Puranam.

Therefore, when the names of those Thiru-koils come up here, we can connect and meditate on the histories of those Thiru-sthalams.

Here, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman comes to the Thiru-metrali of Kachi and sings a Thiru-pathikam. Thiru-metrali of Kachi. Thiru-metrali is a unique sthalam within the city limits of Kanchipuram. This temple is located in the Pillaiyar Palayam area of Kanchi.

Therefore, this street is called Thiru-metrali Thiru. It is a sthalam where Vishnu worshipped the Lord to attain the state of Shiva-sarupyam. When the Lord appeared, Vishnu desired the state of Shiva-sarupyam, and the Lord blessed him, saying that Gnanasambandar would come here and sing a pathikam, and that he should perform penance here until then.

Accordingly, when Gnanasambandar came here and sang, Vishnu attained Shiva-sarupyam, which is the history of the sthalam. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, having arrived at this sthalam, sings a Thiru-pathikam. It is the forty-third pathikam of the fourth Thiru-murai, the Thiru-pathikam for Kachi Metrali, Thiru-nerisai Thiru-pathikam.

He who lives by singing the Vedas and begging for alms, He who wears the crescent moon on His matted locks, with His consort, the one with bangles, He who has a dark throat, the Lord of the shining Metrali in the great city of Kanchi, whose songs and dances are praised. He who is the ancient one, who is pleased with Vishnu, who is the child, who is Pasupathi, who smears white ash, who kicked Yama with His foot, the Lord of the shining Metrali in the great city of Kanchi, who is the father of Murugan. The Devas in heaven come and worship Him with desire, and He listens to the songs that are sweeter than music. He is like the jewel in the eye, the Lord of the shining Metrali in the great city of Kanchi, who is the number and the letter. He who wears the moon and the serpent, and the Ganga, the Vamana, whom the Devas worship, He who burned Kama with His eye, the Lord of the shining Metrali in the great city of Kanchi, my Father who dances with Yama.

He who is the body and the soul, and the worlds for ages, He who is the wealth, He who is the wealth, and who roared with Arjuna, He who has a dark throat, the Lord of the shining Metrali in the great city of Kanchi, who wears the tusks of a boar. He who is Vishnu, who is Narayana, who is Brahma, who is the earth, who is the eight directions, who is the sacred water, who is the body that wanders, the Lord of the shining Metrali in the great city of Kanchi, who is the partner of the beautiful woman. He who took a part of Vishnu, who swallowed the earth, He who holds the hearts of devotees who sing and dance, He who has three eyes, the Lord of the shining Metrali in the great city of Kanchi, who made us think. He who took Lakshmi as a part, He who took Murugan as His son, He who wears jasmine garlands and great Konrai flowers, the Lord of the shining Metrali in the great city of Kanchi, who stands clearly at the boundary of endless knowledge. He who is without root and shines forever, He who placed the sharp part, He who placed the crescent moon, He who placed the Ganga in His matted locks, our Lord who rides the bull, the shining Metrali in the beautiful Kachi. When the Southern King lifted the mountain, and the beautiful woman trembled, and when the king pressed his toe, and his jeweled crowns were crushed, and he sang sweet music, the Lord in Kanchi, the shining Metrali, showed His grace.

Thus, when Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman worshipped various Thiru-koils in the city of Kanchi, he went to Thiru-malperu, a sthalam near Kanchipuram, and sang a Thiru-pathikam. Thiru-malperu is called Thiru-malpur. The Lord’s names are Manikanth-eswarar, Dhayanidhi-eswarar, Prabala-eswarar, Sadarupar, Pavalamalaiyar, Vattam Thavirthar, Malvanangeesar. The Goddess’s names are Anjanakshi, Karunambikai. It is very close to Kanchipuram. We have meditated on the glories of this sthalam in the Thiru-kurippu Thonda Nayanar Puranam.

Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, who came from Kanchipuram to this sthalam, worshipped it and bestowed four Thiru-pathikams. The first Thiru-pathikam is the one hundred and eighth Thiru-pathikam of the fourth Thiru-murai, Thiru-virutham Thiru-pathikam. In this Thiru-pathikam, only two verses, the third and fourth, are available to us. The other songs are not available.

The lotus feet of the Lord of Malperu, who kicked Yama to save the life of the boy, who is difficult to see for those who are not devoted, who is worshipped by devotees who cherish Him, who is like a ruby. The lotus feet of the Lord of Malperu, who is difficult to see for Garuda, who is in the hearts of the blind who love Him, who is beautiful, The lotus feet of the Lord of Malperu, which turn red when touched by the red lotus hands of the goddess of wealth, who is like a fresh flower.

The second Thiru-pathikam, the fifty-ninth Thiru-pathikam of the fifth Thiru-murai, Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathikam.

If you worship the beautiful Malperu, where the Lord, who granted grace to the dark Kinnaras who worshipped Him with flowers from the great river, resides, your karma will vanish. There is no suffering for those who worship the Lord of Malperu, who taught the four sages under the Banyan tree, who granted grace to Vishnu, who is faultless.

The Lord of Malperu, who granted grace to the beautiful Vishnu, who holds the discus, and who worshipped His feet with beautiful flowers, there is no sin for those who serve Him. Do not commit evil deeds and fall into bad karma. Love and meditate on Him. Come and worship the Lord of Malperu, where good ascetics reside, and your karma will vanish. Those who worship the Lord of Malperu, who has a beautiful woman as a part, who has good drums, who has beautiful groves, will reside in the golden world. Listen, I will tell you how to remove old strong karma.

If you see and worship the beautiful Malperu, surrounded by groves where shining bees gather, your worries will vanish. There is no sorrow for those who worship the Lord of Malperu, who granted grace to those who love and rejoice in His holy name, and who are not strong.

The Lord of Malperu, who is the first, the full jewel of the world, who is golden, who is pearls and pleasure, those who worship Him are our masters.

The Lord of Malperu, who is the three-eyed one, who hunted with Arjuna as a hunter in the fierce forest, and who danced, The Lord of Thiru-malperu, who is tall and great, those who sing about Him will attain the supreme world. There is no suffering for those who worship the Lord of Malperu, who granted grace to Ravana, who lifted Mount Kailash with arrogance, and who was tormented.

The third Thiru-pathikam, the sixtieth Thiru-pathikam of the fifth Thiru-murai, Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathikam.

Even if they know nothing, if they read and worship with folded hands, the Lord of Malperu will rejoice in their hearts without any difference. O heart, do not fear, always remember the righteous names, so that karma may vanish.

The Lord of Malperu is the hidden treasure, who swallowed the fierce poison. What will you do with lineage and caste, O foolish ones who speak many scriptures? If you worship Shiva as the vessel, the Lord of Malperu will grant grace in an instant. Listen to what I say, Listen, O foolish ones! If you recite the five letters given by the great ascetic, it will be a medicine to cure diseases and sorrows, and the Lord of Malperu will remain. Listen, I will tell you, O people of the earth!

If you praise the feet of the one who comes on the bull, He will remove Yama and grant you what you desire, the Lord of Malperu, who is like pure gold. Even if you lose much wealth, and even if Yama calls you quickly, if you say, “O Lord who dances in the forest!” the Lord of Malperu is capable of removing your sorrow. If you cry out, “O Lord, O righteous one!” you can be saved, and the people of the world will cherish you.

The Lord of Malperu will make you rule the world if you meditate on His two red feet. When Ravana, who went and lifted the mountain, was pressed down by His toe, the Lord of Malperu, surrounded by groves where monkeys jump, will grant endless joy.

In this Thiru-pathikam, the eighth and ninth songs are not available to us.

Now, the fourth Thiru-pathikam, the eightieth Thiru-pathikam of the sixth Thiru-murai, Thiru-thandakam Thiru-pathikam, bestowed by Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman on the Thiru-malperu sthalam.

I have reached the red coral mountain of Thiru-malperu, the Lord who is the earth, who is the benefit of the earth, who is the creator, who is compassionate to all living beings, who is the endless nectar, who is all the worlds for His devotees, who is the Lord of the Devas, who has a dark throat, who is the king of Kailash, who is in the minds of those who meditate on Him, who kicked Yama with His foot, who is righteous, who is wealthy. I have reached the red coral mountain of Thiru-malperu, the Lord who is the water that creates, who is the seed, who is the sky and the earth, who is the shining pure gold, who is the hole that pierces, who is the light, who is the unlit lamp, who is the moon and the sun that rise in the unwavering sky, who has the Ganga in His matted locks, and who is eternal. I have reached the red coral mountain of Thiru-malperu, the Lord who is the king of the mountain daughter, who is the beautiful pearl, the emerald, the great jewel, who has the moon in His hand, who is the Ekamban, who is the beautiful shining light, who is the golden mountain, who has a body smeared with great white ash, who grants whatever His true devotees desire, who has a bow in His hand. I have reached the red coral mountain of Thiru-malperu, the Lord who is close, who is the soul to the body, who is the one Omkara, who has Uma as a part, who is the Ekamban, who is unborn, who is great and rare, who has learned everything before, who is everything that is to be learned, who kicked Yama to fall, who is the shining light. I have reached the red coral mountain of Thiru-malperu, the Lord who is water, who emits water, who is fire, who is thought, who is the mountain daughter in thought, who is Yama, who is the planet, who is the quality, who has endless tears of joy.

I have reached the red coral mountain of Thiru-malperu, the Lord who forgives the sins committed by His devotees in joy, and who is always the great Lord. I have reached the red coral mountain of Thiru-malperu, the Lord who is the beautiful fragrant thing, who is the one who shows the Vedas, who is the one who has a wooden body, who has the moon in His matted locks, who is the one shining light, who is the Lord of the Devas, who is the one who has performed penance, who is the seed of the world, who has a dark throat, who is the Lord of Kalathi, who is in the minds of those who meditate on Him, who is knowledge, who has a battle-ready weapon. I have reached the red coral mountain of Thiru-malperu, the Lord who is birth, who is the greatness of being unborn, who is great, who is unknown, who is the one who is in the form of a woman, who is pure, who does not think of those who do not think of Him, who thinks of those who think of Him, who is righteous, who is the righteous one, who is the Lord, who is the master, who is praised by the Devas in the good way, who is the shining light. In the sky, I have reached the red coral mountain of Thiru-malperu, the Lord who is the growing cloud, who is the moon, who is in the minds of those who worship Him, who is the beautiful gold, who is the inner support of the body, who is eternal, who is the perfect one of Ottiyur, who is the calf of the ages, who is the dark elephant in the forest, who is the Lord of Kalathi, who is in the minds of those who meditate on Him, who is the origin, who is the sweet taste in the nail. I have reached the red coral mountain of Thiru-malperu, the Lord who is the incomplete full origin, who is the bud, who is the flower, who is the form, who is always without anger, who is the attachment, who is compassionate to all living beings, who is the supreme, who is the supreme light, who is in the hearts of those who know Him, who is the one with the high black bow, who looked at the fire to burn the three cities, who destroyed them. I have reached the red coral mountain of Thiru-malperu, the Lord who expounded the four Vedas and the six Angas, who pressed down Ravana who lifted the mountain with His toe, who is pure, who is the master, who wears the Ganga in His moon-lit red matted locks, who is Shankara, who is Shambu.

I have reached the red coral mountain of Thiru-malperu, the Lord who laughed when the three cities of the enemies burned in the fire, who is the shining light.

Thus, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman worshipped the sthalam called Thiru-malperu and sang four Thiru-pathikams.

Then, he again wished to worship Thiru-ekambaperuman, who resides in Kachi, and so he again visited the nearby sthalams and returned to Kanchipuram. The nearby sthalams mentioned here are Thiru-ural, Thiru-virkolam, Koom, Ilambaiyangattur, and others.

However, the pathikams sung by Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar for these sthalams are not available to us now. Nayanar, who started from Kanchi and visited Thiru-malperu and other sthalams, returned to Kanchipuram to worship the Lord whom he held in his heart in Kanchipuram. That great love is the reason.

Similarly, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, who worshipped in Thiruchitrambalam, visits the nearby sthalams and returns to Thiruchitrambalam. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, who worshipped from Thiruvarur, visits the nearby holy places and returns to Thiruvarur.

In the same way, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, who visited all the nearby places from Thirunallur, returns to Thirunallur and worships.

Similarly, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, who has now visited the nearby sthalams from Kanchipuram, returns to Kanchipuram. Our contemplation continues. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 446, Thirunindra Sarukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having visited many sthalams in Thiru Kanchipuram and the nearby sthalams, returns to Kanchipuram and worships Thiru Ekamba Peruman. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman now praises the Lord, singing Thiru Pathigams, saying, “He is Kachi Ekamban, He is in my thoughts.” We have seen that Thirunavukkarasu Peruman has bestowed a total of seven Thiru Pathigams for the Thiru Ekambaranathar Temple in Kanchipuram. Of these, we have already seen five Thiru Pathigams.

Therefore, according to this song, he now bestows two Thiru Thandagams: one beginning with “Kootruvan Kaan Kootruvanai Kumaittha Kon Kaan” and another beginning with “Uritthavan Kaan.” Thus, a total of seven Thiru Pathigams for the Thiru Ekambanathar Temple in Kanchipuram by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman. are the sacred hymns. The sixth sacred hymn is the 64th sacred hymn of the sixth Thirumurai, a Thiruthandagam.

Kootruvan kaan kootruvanai kumaittha kon kaan kuvalaiyan kaan kuvalaiyaththin neeraanaan kaan kaatravan kaan kanalavan kaan kalikkum min kaan kanapavala semmeni kalandha vellai neetravan kaan nilaavoorum senniyaan kaan niraiyaarntha punalkangai nimirchadaimel etravan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaar kachchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane. Paranthavan kaan palluyirgal aagi engum paninthezhuvaar paavamum vinaiyum poga thuranthavan kaan thoomalarang kanniyaan kaan thotra nilai iruthi porulaay vantha marunthavan kaan vaiyangal poraiththeerppaan kaan malarththoovi ninainthezhuvaar ullam neengaathu irunthavan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaar kachchi ekamban. Kaan avan en ennatthaane. Neetravan kaan neeraagi theeyaanan kaan nirai mazhuvum thamarugamum eriyum kaiyil thotravan kaan thotrakkedillaath kaan thunaiyili kaan thunaiyendru thozhuvaarvullam potravan kaan pugazhgal thamai padaiththaan kaan poriyaravum virisadaimel punalum gangai etravan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaar kachchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane. Thaayavan kaan ulagirku thannoppillaa thaththuvan kaan malai mangai pangaa enbaar vaayavan kaan varum piravi nooyth theerppaan kaan vaanavarukkum thaanavarukkum mannullorkkum seyavan kaan ninaivaarkkuch chiththam aara thiruvadiye ulkai ninainthezhuvaar ullam eyavan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaar kachchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane.

The fifth verse in this sacred hymn is not available to us. Azhith. Thavan kaan eyil moonrum ayilvaay ambaal aiyaarum idaimaruthum aazhvaan thaan kaan pazhiththavan kaan adaiyaarai adaivaarththangal patravan kaan putrarava naaninaan kaan suzhiththavan kaan mudigangai adiye potrum thooyamaa munivarkaa paarmel nirka izhiththavan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaar kachchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane. Asainthavan kaan nadamaadi paadal peni azal vannaththil adiyum mudiyum theda pasainthavan kaan peyganangal paraviyeththum paanmaiyan kaan paravi ninainthazhuvaarththampaal kasinthavan kaan kariyin uri porththaan thaan kaan kadalil vida mundha amararkku amutham meeya isainthavan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaar kachchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane. Mudiththavan kaan avan kootrai seetraththeeyaal valiyaarththam pura moonrum vevach chaapam pidiththavan kaan pingyaga naam vedaththaan kaan. Pinaiyal veri kamal kondrai aravu senni mudiththavan kaan moovilainal velinaan kaan muzhangiyurum enath thonrum mazhaiyaay minni idiththavan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaarkatchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane.

Varunthavan kaan manamurugi ninaiyaathaarku vanchagan kaan anjezhuththu ninaivaarkku endrum marunthavan kaan vaan pinigal theerum vannam vaanagamum mannagumum matrum aagi paranthavan kaan padarsadai etrudaiyaan thaan kaan pangayaththon than siraththai endhi oorur iranthavan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaarkatchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane. Vemmana uzhuvai athaluri porththaan kaan vedaththin porulaan kaan endriyambi vimmaa nindru azhuvaarkatku alippaan thaan kaan vida eri thirivaan kaan nadanjai poothaththu ammaan kaan agalidangal thaanginaan kaan arputhan. Kaan sorpathamum kadanthu nindra emmaan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaarkatchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane. Aruththaan kaan ayan siraththai amarar venda aazhkadalil nanjudengu annirgangai seruththaan kaan devarkkum devan thaan kaan thisaiyanaiththum thozhuthu ettha kalaimaan kaiyil poruththaan kaan pugalidaththai naliyavantha poru kaiyilai eduththavan than mudiththol naalanjiruththaan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaarkatchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane.

Now, the seventh sacred hymn, the 65th sacred hymn of the sixth Thirumurai, a Thiruthandagam.

Uritthavan kaan urakkazhitrai umaiyaal ulka ongaraththu oruvan kaan unar meijnjanam viriththavan kaan viriththa naal vedaththaan kaan viya nulagil palluyirai vidiyinaale theriththavan kaan silluruvaay thondriyengum thirandavan kaan thiripuraththai. Vevavillaal eriththavan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaarkatchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane. Nesan kaan nesarku nesan than paal illatha nenjaththu neesar thammai koosan kaan koosathaar nenjuththanje kudikonda kuzhagan kaan azhagaarkondrai vaasan kaan malaimangai pangan thaan kaan vaanavargal eppozhuthum vanangiyeththum eesan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaarkatchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane. Poraiyavan kaan bhoomi el thaangi yongum punniyan kaan nanniya pundarigap pothin maraiyavan kaan maraiyavanai payanthoon thaan kaan vaarsadai maasunam aninthu valarum pillai piraiyavan kaan pirai thigazhum eyitru pelvaay peyodu angu idukaattil elliyaadum iraiyavan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaar katchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane. Paaravan kaan visumbavan kaan pavvan thaan kaan pani.

Varigal iravinodu pagalaay nindra seeravan kaan thisaiyavan kaan thisaigalettum serinthavan kaan siranthadiyaar sinthai seyyum peravan kaan peraayirangal eththum periyavan kaan ariyavan kaan petram oorndha eravan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaar katchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane. Perunthavaththu em pingyagan kaan piraisoodi kaan pedaiyen vaathaiyuru piniyai theerkkum marunthavan kaan manthirangal aayinaan kaan vaanavargal thaam vanangum maadevan kaan arunthavaththaal aayizhaiyaal umaiyaazhpaagam amarnthavan kaan amarargal thaam archiththu ettha irunthavan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaar katchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane. Aaynthavan kaan arumaraiyodu angam aarum aninthavan kaan aadaravodu enbum aamai kaaynthavan kaan kan nalalaar kaaman aagam ganandrezhuntha kaalan udal podiyaay veezha paaynthavan kaan. pandu pala sarugaal panthal payinra nool silanthikku paaraal selvam eenthavaan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaar kachchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane. Umaiyavalai orupaagam serththinaan kaan ugantholi neer gangai sadai ozhukkinaan kaan imaya vadakayilai selvan thaan kaan ilbalikkuch sendruzhalum nalkoornthaan kaan samayamavai aarinukkum thalaivan thaan kaan thaththuvan kaan uththaman kaan thaaneyaaya imaiyavan kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaar kachchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane. Thondubadu thondar thuyar theerppaan thaan kaan thoomalar sevadiyinaiyam sothiyaan kaan undubadu vidangandaththu odukkinaan kaan olikadalil amutham amararkku uthavinaan kaan vandubadu malarkondrai maalaiyaan kaan vaanmathiyaay naanmeenum aayinaan kaan en thisaiyum ezhilaarum pozhilaar kachchi ekamban. Kaan avan en ennatthaane.

Munthaikkaan moovarilum muthal aanan kaan moovilay vel moorthi kaan murugavetku thanthai kaan than kadama mugaththinaarku thaathaikkaan thaazhnthadiye vananguvaarku sinthaikkaan sinthaatha siththaththaarku sivanavan kaan sengannmaal vidai ondru erum enthai kaan ezhilaarum pozhilaar kachchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane. Ponnisaiyum porisadai em punithan thaan kaan poothagananaathan kaan puliththol aadai thannisaiya vaiththa ezhil aravinaan kaan sangaven kolaikkaathil sathuran thaan kaan minnisaiyum vellaiyitron vegundu verpai edukka adi adarppa meendavan than vaayil innisai ketu ilangozhivaal eenthoon kachchi ekamban kaan avan en ennatthaane.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having praised and worshipped Thiru Kachi Ekambam, singing “Avan En Ennatthaan,” worships the holy city of Kanchipuram, its temple, and Ekambareswarar enshrined there. Remembering these memories of Kanchi, he decides to proceed to other holy places and continues his pilgrimage. The honey flowing from the ripe pulp of jackfruits reaches the paddy fields, making them fertile. In such a fertile land, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman approaches the holy place called Thirukazhukundram. He arrives at the holy place of Thirukazhukundram, worships the sacred feet of Lord Shiva there, and sings hymns. Among the hymns bestowed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman for the holy place of Thirukazhukundram, we now have one Thiruthandagam.

We have contemplated all the historical glories of Thirukazhukundram in the Thirukurippu Thonda Nayanar Puranam.

Therefore, we shall now contemplate the sacred hymn bestowed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal for this sthalam. This is the 92nd sacred hymn of the sixth Thirumurai, structured as a Thiruthandagam.

Moovilay vel kaiyaanai moorththi thannai muthu pinakkaadudaiyaanai muthal aananai aavinil ainthu uganthaanai amararkonai aalaalam undugantha vaiyan thannai poovinin mel naan muganum maalum potra punarvariya perumaanai punithan thannai kaavalanai kazhukkundram amarnthaan thannai karpagaththai kannaara kanden naane. Pallaadu thalai sadai mel udaiyaan thannai paay puliththol udaiyaanai pagavan thannai sollodu porul anaiththum aanan thannai sudar. Uruvil enbara kolaththaanai allaatha kaalanai mun adarththaan thannai aalin keezh irunthaanai amuthaanaanai kallaadai punaintharulum kapaaliyai karpagaththai kannaara kanden naane.

In this sacred hymn, only the first two verses are available to us; the other eight verses are not.

Afterwards, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman visits many nearby holy places from Thirukazhukundram and sings hymns. The many nearby holy places mentioned here are Thiruvanaiparthan Panangattur, Thirumagaral, Thiruvaidaichuram, Thirukachur Alakkoil, and other such sthalams.

However, none of the hymns for these sthalams are currently available to us.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having worshipped Thirukazhukundram and all the nearby sthalams, arrives at the holy place of Thiruvanmiyur, which is surrounded by the sea. He worships Marundeesar of Thiruvanmiyur and lovingly sings the sacred Tamil hymn of great truth. The sacred name of the Lord of Thiruvanmiyur is Marundeesar. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having seen and worshipped Lord Shiva, the Marundeesar who cures the disease of birth, here in Thiruvanmiyur, sings the sacred Tamil hymn of great truth. “Great truth” signifies the ultimate truth of gnana (wisdom). The ultimate truth is for souls to attain Shiva, shed their bonds, and experience bliss.

Throughout this Thirukurunthogai hymn for this sthalam, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman emphasizes this very idea. The essence of this sacred hymn is the reference to “those who sever birth.” We have extensively contemplated the sthala puranam and special features of Thiruvanmiyur in the Thirukurippu Thonda Nayanar Puranam.

Therefore, we shall now contemplate the sacred hymn bestowed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman for the holy place of Thiruvanmiyur. This is the eighty-second sacred hymn in the fifth Thirumurai, structured as a Thirukurunthogai hymn.

Vindamaamalar kondu virainthu neer andanaayakan than adisoozhmingal pandu neer seytha paavam parainthidum vanduseru pozhil vaanmiyur eesane. Porulum sutramum poymaiyum vittu neer marulum maantharai maatru mayakkaruthu arulumaavalla aathiyaay endralum marul aruththidum vaanmiyur eesane. Manthamaagiya sinthai mayakkaruthu anthamil gunaththaanai adainthu nindru enthai eesan endru eththida vallirel vanthu nindridum vaanmiyur eesane. Ullam ulkalanthu eththavallaarkku alaal kallamulla vazhi kasivaanalan vellamum maravum viravum sadai. Vallalaagiya vaanmiyur eesane.

Padangol paambarai paan mathisoodiyai vadangol menmulai maathorukooranai thodarnthu nindru thozhuthu ezhuvaarvinai madanga nindridum vaanmiyur eesane. Nenjil aivar ninaikka ninaikkuraar panjinmelladiyaal umai panga endri naanmalar thoovi ezuthirel vanjam theerththidum vaanmiyur eesane. Nunangu noolayan maalum arugilaa gunangal thaam paravi kurainthukkavar sunangu poonmulai thoomuzhiyaar avar vananga nindridum vaanmiyur eesane. Aathiyum amaran aay ayan maalum aay paathi pennuruvay paraman endru othi ul kuzhaintheththavallaar avar vaathai theerththidum vaanmiyur eesane. Ottai maadathil onpathu vaasalum kaattil vevathan munnang kalaladi naatti naan. Malar thoovi valamseyil vaattan theerththidum vaanmiyur eesane.

Vaaramaaga malaiyeduththaan thanai seeramaaga thiru viral oondrinaan aarvamaaga azhaiththavan eththalum vaaramaayinan vaanmiyur eesane.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped Marundeesar Peruman of Thiruvanmiyur, visits the nearby holy places such as Nedungundram, Kundrathur, Thirunindravur, Thiruverkadu, Nerkundram, and Thiruvalithayam. However, the hymns sung by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman for these sthalams are not available. Having visited these nearby sthalams, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman arrives at Mylapore, a place of beautiful gardens and peacocks. Mylapore is a town filled with mansions, where clouds drift over the mansions, just as peacocks dance on mountains. Over the mansions in Mylapore, clouds drift. In such a glorious Thirumayilai, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman worships the sacred feet of Sankaranar, Lord Shiva, enshrined there.

He sings sacred Tamil hymns there.

Here, the reference to the Lord of Mylapore as Sankaranar appears. Sankaranar means “one who brings happiness.” Here, the Lord’s name is Kapaleeswarar. Kapali, who eats by begging, does so to make His devotees reach His feet.

Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Kapaleeswarar Peruman as Sankaranar in this sacred verse.

Once upon a time, Uma Devi, Parvati, who grew up in the Himalayas, performed penance there.

Similarly, she came to Mylapore and performed penance in the form of a peacock, worshipping Lord Shiva. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having come to such a special Thirumayilai, worships and sings hymns.

However, none of those hymns are currently available to us.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having worshipped Thirumayilai, walks along the seashore and reaches the holy place called Thiruottriyur. During the time of Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, Thiruvanmiyur, Mylapore, and Thiruottriyur must have been coastal areas with sandy expanses and small villages.

Therefore, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman travels from Thirumayilai to Thiruottriyur along the seashore. Let us go on contemplating. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 447, Thirunindra Sarukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman departs from Mylapore, also known as Thirumayilai, and arrives at the holy place called Thiruottriyur. Thiruottriyur is also a coastal sthalam. Hearing the news of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman’s arrival in the city of Thiruottriyur, the Shiva devotees living in Thiruottriyur beautifully decorate the city’s streets. They arrange beautiful flags, garlands, areca nuts, and plantain trees in rows, adorning the city.

They place golden kalasams, incense burners, and lamps, and welcome Vagisa Peruman, leading him into the city of Thiruottriyur. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar also proceeds to the temple of Lord Shiva, who is lovingly enshrined in Thiruottriyur.

There, he worships the temple tower, enters, and with a unified mind of wisdom, along with those devotees, his heart melting, he circumambulates the temple. He then bows down before the Lord, who removes the name of birth for devotees, and prostrates himself before the sacred presence. It is mentioned here that the Lord of Thiruottriyur is the Lord who removes the name of birth, and the Lord who explains that name to devotees. “Namam” here means “name.” Sekkizhar Peruman has described the Lord of Thiruottriyur as “Karunamam Thavirppar,” meaning “one who removes the name of the embryo.” This refers to the name that living beings acquire when they enter the womb. That is, living beings come into this world through the womb, and the name that comes to the soul as a result is “Jeevan.” That “Jeevan” is the name of the soul. It is the Lord Shiva who removes that name of “Jeevan” from living beings.

This means that He destroys the state of being a “Jeevan” and bestows the Shiva principle.

Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman describes the Lord of Thiruottriyur as “Karunamam Thavirppar” here. Before such a Lord, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar bows down with folded hands and prostrates himself. He worships the Lord of Thiruottriyur, the “Ezhuthaatha Marai Aliththa Ezhuththariyum Peruman,” the Lord who bestowed the unwritten Vedas and knows the letters. “Ezhuthaatha Marai” refers to the Vedas, and “Ezhuththariyum Peruman” is the sacred name of the Lord of Thiruottriyur.

The Lord here bears the sacred name “Ezhuththariyum Peruman.” There is a history to this, which we discussed earlier in the Thirukurippu Thonda Nayanar Puranam, regarding Thiruottriyur. This means that He destroys the state of being a “Jeevan” and bestows the Shiva principle.

As we contemplate the Sthala Purana, we have seen how Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, having worshipped such a Lord who knows writing, prostrates himself on the ground with overflowing love, rising again. His entire being is suffused with ecstatic love, his body covered in goosebumps, and tears stream from his eyes like a downpour as he worships the Lord. He begins a Thiru-pathikam with ‘Vandongu Sengamalam’ and performs sacred services in the Thiru-mutram. According to his vow, he performs the Ulavara Thiru-pani (clearing with a hoe). Among the four great Shaivite Acharyas, only Thirunavukkarasu Peruman performs this manual service of Ulavara Thiru-pani.

He performs it in every temple he visits, as Sekkizhar Peruman states. He continuously mentions it everywhere without fail. While performing these sacred services, he sings Thiru-pathikams known as Thiru-viruththams, Thiru-kurunthogais, and Thiru-nerisais. Sekkizhar Peruman sang earlier that he began with ‘Vandongu Sengamalam’; that is a Thiru-thandaka Thiru-pathikam. Now it is mentioned that he sings Thiru-viruththams. Of such Thiru-viruththam Thiru-pathikams, only one Thiru-pathikam has been found.

Similarly, it is mentioned that he sings Thiru-pathikams, but only one pathikam has been found. It is mentioned that he sings Thiru-nerisai Thiru-pathikams. For this Sthalam, two Thiru-nerisai Thiru-pathikams bestowed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman have been found.

Thus, a total of five Thiru- Thiru-pathikams, bestowed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-vottriyur Sthalam, are currently available. Let us contemplate these five Thiru-pathikams. The first Thiru-pathikam, which Sekkizhar Peruman sang by taking its opening line as ‘Vandongu Sengamalam’, we shall contemplate first. This is the 45th Thiru-pathikam of the Sixth Thirumurai, a Thiru-thandaka Thiru-pathikam.

yavumallai Pennallai anallai pedumallai pirithallai yanayum periyay neeye Unnallai nalla Thiyai allai unarvariya Ottriyur udaiya kove Maruvutra malarkuzhali madavalancha malai thuzhanga thisai nadunga seruththu nokki Seruvutra vazharakkan valithan mazha thiruvadiyin viralvondral alara undri Uruvottriyiruvarodi kana ongina vauvol azhalar inge vanthu Thiru-vottriyur nam ur endru ponar serivalaigal ondondras sendravaru Thiruchitrambalam.

Now, the second Thiru-pathikam, the 45th Thiru-pathikam of the Fourth Thirumurai, a Thiru-pathikam set in Kollippan.

Vellaththaich sadaivil vaiththa vedageethan than padam Mellaththan adaiya vendin meyitharu gnana thiyyal Kallaththaik kazhiya nindrar kayaththuk kalanthu nindru Ullaththul oliyumagum Ottriyur udaiya kove Vasippenum vazhkai venda vanavar iraivan nindru Pusippathor pollal akka Adanudum punarvundil asirpenum arunthavaththal anmavinidamaagi Usirpenum unarvumullar Ottriyur udaiya kove Thanaththai seythu vazhvan salaththulai azhundugindrir Vanaththai vananga vendil vammingal valliragil Gnanaththai vilakkai etri nadiyul viravavallar Unaththai olippar polum Ottriyur udaiya kove Kamaththul azhundhi nindru kandaral oru punnathe Samaththu vedamagi nindrathor sayambuthannai Emaththum idaiyiravum ekantam iyambuvarkku Omaththul ozhiyathagum Ottriyur udaiya kove Samayame larumagi thanoru sayambuvagi Imayavar paraviyeththa inithinangiruntha isan Kamaiyinai udaiyaragi kalaladi paravuvarkku Umai oru pagar polum Ottriyur udaiya kove Oruththithan thalai sendralai karanthittan ulagam eththa Oruththikku nallanagi maruppeduththu ozhiththu minde Oruththiyai pagam vaiththan unarvinal aiyam unni Oruththikku nallanallan Ottriyur udaiya kove Pinamudai udalukkaga piththarai thirinthu ningal Punarvenum bogam venda pokkalam poyyai ninga Ninamudai nenjin ullal ninaikkuma ninaikkindrarkku Unarvinodu iruppar polum Ottriyur udaiya kove Pinnuvar sadaiyan thannai pithatrilap pedaimargal Thunnuvar naraganthannul tholvinai thiravendin Mannuvar maraigalothi manaththinul vilakkondretri Unnuvar ullaththullar Ottriyur udaiya kove Muzhguvar bogam vendin muyarchiyal idargal vanthal Ezhuguvar ezhugi nindrangu ithuvoru mayam enbar Palkuvar paththaragi padiyum adi nindru Ulguvar ullaththullar Ottriyur udaiya kove Veruththugap pulangalainthum venditru vendu nenje Maru Arvachchatra krodangalan maya poruththugap pushpaga ther udaiyanai adaravundri Oru thugan tharugal seithar Ottriyur udaiya kove Thiruchitrambalam.

Now, the next Thiru-pathikam, the third Thiru-pathikam, the 46th Thiru-pathikam of the Fourth Thirumurai, a Thiru-nerisai Thiru-pathikam.

Ompinen koottai vazha ullaththor kodumai vaiththu Kampila mulai pola karuththitre mugakkamaten Pambin vay therai pola pala pala ninaikkindrenai Ompini uyya kollay Ottriyur udaiya kove Manamenum thozhi patti mathiyanum kolai undri Sinamenum sarakkai etri serikadal odum podu Mathanenam parai thakki mariyum podu ariya onna Thunaiyunum unarvai nalkay Ottriyur udaiya kove. The other verses of this Thiru-pathikam are not available to us.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 448, Thirunindrachcharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having worshipped at Thiru-vottriyur, departed from there and visited and worshipped at several adjacent Shiva temples. The nearby Shiva temples mentioned here are Vadathirumullaivayil, Thiru-kallil Punniyakotteeswarar Temple, Gnayiru, and other sacred places. The note here indicates that Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar visited and worshipped at these Sthalams from Thiru-vottriyur and then returned to Thiru-vottriyur to worship again. Having worshipped at many such places, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman arrives at the sacred Sthalam called Thiru-pasur.

In Thiru-pasur, the Lord manifested Himself, residing in a bamboo grove. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman approaches and worships such a Lord with love and devotion welling up in his heart. Overflowing with devotion, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman comes and worships. Sekkizhar Peruman here sings, quoting a verse from the Thiru-kurunthagai pathikam, ‘Sinthippar Vinai Thirththidum Selvanar’. In this song, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, having come and worshipped at Thiru-pasur Sthalam, bestowed two Thiru-pathikams for this Sthalam. Thiru-pasur is the seventeenth of the celebrated Sthalams in Thondai Nadu.

The Sthala Vriksham here is the bamboo tree; the Lord manifested Himself beneath it. For this reason, the Sthalam received this name. ‘Pasu’ means bamboo; therefore, as the Lord manifested beneath the bamboo, it is called Thiru-pasur. This is the Sthalam where the Lord bestowed grace upon Chandra. The history of this Sthalam states that the Lord took the snake sent by the Jains on behalf of the Kurumbar king against Karikala Chola and danced with it, bestowing grace. The Goddess is seated on the right side. The Sodasa Ganapathi is a special Ganapathi of this Sthalam.

The Lord’s sacred names are Pasurnathar, Vasiswarar, Pasupatheeswarar. The Goddess’s sacred names are Pasupathi Nayaki, Moganambal. The Theerthams are Soma Theertham, Mangala Theertham, Chola Theertham. The Sthala Purana states that it is auspicious to have darshan of this Sthalam at noon. It is located in Tamil Nadu, very close to Thiruvallur, north of Thiruvallur near Chennai. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, who graced this Sthalam, bestowed two Thiru-pathikams.

The first Thiru-pathikam is the 25th Thiru-pathikam of the Fifth Thirumurai, a Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathikam.

kollum kutr Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having worshipped Thiru-Pasur and sung Thiru-Pathigams, departed from this holy place and visited many nearby shrines. These nearby shrines include Thiru-Vallur, Thiru-Venpakkam, and others. Having worshipped at many such shrines, he proceeded to Thiru-Alangadu, also known as Thiru-Alavanam, near Pazhayanur. He arrived at the sacred site of Thiru-Alangadu, also known as Thiru-Alavanam.

There, he bowed and worshipped the Lord, singing many Tamil garlands, beginning with the great Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathigam, which concludes with the refrain “Thiru-Alangadu Uraiyum Selvar Thame” (He who resides in Thiru-Alangadu is indeed the wealthy one), possessing an enduring glory. Thiru-Alangadu is a very special sacred site. The Lord’s holy name is Vattaranyeswarar, Devar Singa Peruman, Alangattu Appar. The Goddess’s holy name is Brahmarakambal, Vandarkuzhali. The Sthala Vriksham (sacred tree) is the Palmyra tree. We will extensively discuss the history and Puranic accounts of this sacred site, particularly those related to Karaikkal Ammaiyar.

Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who came to this sacred site, bestowed two Thiru-Pathigams. The Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathigam, which ends with “Thiru-Alangadu Uraiyum Selvar Thame” in each verse, he bestowed. Sekkizhar Peruman sings of it as “Thiru-Alangadu Uraiyum Selvar Thame” as a unique and undiminished great Thiru-Thandagam, and as “many garlands of exalted Tamil truth.” Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman states that he sang this Thiru-Pathigam and other Pathigams. Sekkizhar Peruman praises this Thiru-Pathigam as “Periya Thiru-Thandagam” (Great Thiru-Thandagam). Sekkizhar Peruman also referred to the Thillai Thiru-Thandagam, which begins “Ariyanaai Andhanardham Sindhaiyanaai,” as “Periya Thiru-Thandagam.” Similarly, Sekkizhar Peruman refers to the Thiru-Alangattu Thiru-Thandaga Thiru-Pathigam, which concludes with “Thiru-Alangadu Uraiyum Selvar Thame,” as Thandagam. Of these two Thiru-Pathigams, the first Thiru-Pathigam is the sixty-eighth Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Nerisaith Thiru-Pathigam.

“Vella Neer Sadaiyar Polum Virumbuvarkku Eliyar Polum Ullule Urugi Ninrangku Ugappavarkku Anbar Polum Kal” He is like the one who removes all karmic impurities, like the Lord of Alangadu, who resides in the fertile Pazhanai. He is like the one with a fiery form, like the one with a fierce bull. He is like the one who adorns himself with sacred white ash. He is like the generous one who abounds in the fertile groves of Pazhanai.

He is like the endless Lord, the Lord of Alangadu. He is like the one who burned Kama with his eye. He is like the one who laughed when the three cities of the countless ones burned. He is like the Lord of Alangadu, who rules us, residing in the fertile groves of Pazhanai, where the drum’s sound never ceases. He is like the one with a throat that swallowed the dark poison, like the one with eight shoulders. He is like the one who smears white ash from the cremation ground.

He is like the one who speaks. He is like the one with matted locks, residing in the cool groves of Pazhanai, the Lord of Alangadu. He is like the one who fought with Arjuna and showed his devotion. He is like the one who strings sharp arrows and knows the qualities. He is like the one who gave the quiver with arrows. He is like the Lord of Thiru-Alangadu, who resides in the sacred Pazhanai.

He is like the one who smears sacred white ash on his body. He is like the one who desires to dance in the forest. He is like the Lord of Alangadu, who danced the dharma, residing in the fertile groves of Pazhanai, where the drum’s sound never ceases. He is like the one with lotus-like feet. He is like the Lord who kicked Yama to his demise. He is like the one who removes the cycle of birth, the Lord of Alangadu, who resides in the cool groves of Pazhanai.

He is like the one who united with Uma, taking on a significant form. He is like the one who wears Ganga in his matted locks. He is like the Lord of Alangadu, who sang the Sama Veda, residing in the fertile groves of Pazhanai, and danced for Kali to witness. He is like the one who does not accept the words of the naked Jains who wear tattered clothes, but cherishes their good qualities. He is like the one who delights in riding the bull. He is like the one who knows the shortcomings, the Lord of Alangadu.

He is like the one who, with his sacred finger, pressed down the demon who, in his madness, lifted the mountain, and bestowed grace. He is like the Lord of Alangadu, our master, who resides in the fertile Pazhanai and removes the sins of his devotees.

Now, the great Thiru-Thandagam, referred to by Sekkizhar Peruman as “Periya Thiru-Thandagam,” is the seventy-eighth Thiru-Pathigam of the Sixth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathigam.

“Onra Ulakanaitthum Anar Thame Oozhithoru Oozhi Uyarnthar Thame Ninraki Engum Nimirthar Thame Neer Vazhi Thee Akasam Anar Thame Konradum Kootrai Uthaitharthame Kolap Pazhanai Udaiyar Thame Senradu Theerthangal Anar Thame Thiruvalang Kaduraiyum Selvar Thame Malaimakalai Pakam Amarntharthame Vanor Vanangappaduvar Thame Salamakalai Senjadai Mel Vaithar Thame Saraninri Iruppar” He is the beloved of those who are like stones. He is the one who took on many forms. He is the one who owns Pazhanai as his city. He is the one who destroyed the three cities with the mountain as his bow.

He is the wealthy one who resides in Thiru-Alangadu. He is the one who has five faces. He is the one who possesses immeasurable greatness. He is the one who stands as the fragrance in flowers. He is the one who stands as the sacred essence. He is the one who delights in songs.

He is the one who owns Pazhanai as his city. He is the one who stands to be worshipped by the gods. He is the wealthy one who resides in Thiru-Alangadu. He is the one who wears fragrant Konrai flowers on his head. He is the one who spoke the four Vedas and their six angas. He is the one with an incomparable form.

He is the one who placed the great moon on his red matted locks. He is the one who ate from a broken skull. He is the one who owns Pazhanai as his city. He is the one whose mind is clear and pure. He is the wealthy one who resides in Thiru-Alangadu. He is the one who stands as both night and day.

He is the one who became both dawn and dusk. He is the one who became all words and meanings. He is the one who became both hymns and scriptures. He is the one who became all the verses that are spoken. He is the one who owns Pazhanai as his city. He is the one who is capable of showing the path to salvation.

He is the wealthy one who resides in Thiru-Alangadu. He is close to those who serve him as devotees. He is the pure one who adorns himself with sacred water. He is the one who rose and stood as a pillar of fire when Brahma and Vishnu searched for him. He is the one who stood singing ancient music. He is the one who owns Pazhanai as his city.

He is the one who has eight strong shoulders. He is the wealthy one who resides in Thiru-Alangadu. He is the one with a dark throat. He is the one who delights in dancing in the cremation ground. He is the one who made Aiyaru, Arur, Anaika, and Ambalam his temples. He is the one who tied a snake with a hood.

He is the one who owns Pazhanai as his city. He is the one who stood to be worshipped by Lakshmi. He is the wealthy one who resides in Thiru-Alangadu. He is the one who became the entire sky and the entire earth. He is the one with qualities praised by the great ones. He is the one who burned Kama with his eye.

He is the one who transcended ages and eons. He is the one who delights in songs set to music. He is the one who owns Pazhanai as his city. He is the one who holds a sharp axe in his hand. He is the wealthy one who resides in Thiru-Alangadu. He is the one who swallowed the poison from the dark ocean.

He is the one who owns Mount Kailash. He is the one who delights in Ekambam, the city without a dwelling. He is the one who resided in Ottrur. He is the one who is praised by many. He is the one who owns Pazhanai as his city. He is the one who cures incurable karmic diseases.

He is the wealthy one who resides in Thiru-Alangadu. He is the one who placed the crescent moon on his head. He is the one who, with his finger, crushed the king of Lanka, surrounded by the blue ocean, who did not worship the great mountain of Kailash. He is the one with a body the color of milk. He is the one who owns Pazhanai as his city. He is the one whose greatness is praised by the virtuous.

He is the wealthy one who resides in Thiru-Alangadu.

Thus, having worshipped the beautiful and special sacred site of Thiru-Alangadu and sung Pathigams, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman departed from Thiru-Alangadu, heading north. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman travels through many villages, tall mountains, and dense forests. These sacred sites include Thiru-Thanigai, Valaikulam, and others. Sekkizhar Peruman refers to these as “Palpathiyum” (many shrines) and “Nedungiri” (tall mountains), meaning lofty mountains. These include Nagari Malai, Kundravardhanam, Rajigundamalai, and other mountains. He mentions that he travels through dense forests, which are areas with vast forests between mountains.

He visits and worships the Lord at these sacred sites. This Thiru-Karikkari is one of the Thevara Vaippu Sthalams.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal has sung about it as a Vaippu Sthalam, referring to “Kadangaluru Thiru-Karikkari Kailayam.” Thiru-Alangadu Thiru-Pathigam Thirugnanasambandha Peruman also visited and worshipped at Thiru-Karikkari after worshipping at sites like Thiru-Alangadu.

Similarly, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman also worshipped at Thiru-Karikkari. This sacred site of Thiru-Karikkari is located on the north bank of the Arani River, after crossing it, on the way to Oothukottai, after alighting at Puthur on the Arakkonam-Renigunta route.

However, the Pathigams sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for this site are not available to us.

Thus, departing from Thiru-Alangadu, and traversing many shrines, mountains, and forests, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman reaches the sacred site of Thiru-Kalahasti. We shall continue our reflection. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 449, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman reaches the sacred site of Thiru-Kalahasti.

There, the sacred river Ponmugali flows. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman bathes in the holy waters of this sacred Ponmugali river. The Ponmugali Theertham is a sacred and ancient water. The pure holy ablution poured over the Lord’s head through Kannappa Nayanar’s sacred mouth became this Ponmugali sacred river’s water.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman bathes in this water. Although it is a general rule and custom to begin worship by immersing oneself in water, here, specifically, immersing oneself in the waters of this sacred river became a part of the worship, as Sekkizhar Peruman sings, “immersing in the sacred and ancient waters of the Ponmugali sacred river.” Worshipping and immersing oneself in it became part of the worship, as Sekkizhar Peruman sings, “immersing in the sacred and ancient waters of the Ponmugali sacred river.” Thiru-Kalahasti Hill is part of a large, continuous mountain range. He reaches such a Thiru-Kalahasti Hill, crossing the Ponmugali River, and arrives at the foothills of Thiru-Kalahasti Hill. He bows and worships in the valley. He bows and worships the mountain itself.

He reaches the temple at the top of the mountain and circumambulates and worships there. He worships Lord Shiva, who is seated like the pinnacle of the mountain on the summit of Thiru-Kalahasti Hill, Lord Shiva who exists through the Vedic chants. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s love for Thiru-Kalahasti Appar grows immensely. When he thought of Thiru-Kalahasti Appar, his mind His mind rejoiced. As his mind rejoiced, his eyes, which beheld Kalahasti Appar, were filled with bliss.

Thus, having worshipped Thiru-Kalahasti Appar, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sang a Thiru-Pathigam with the theme “En Kannullan” (He is within my eyes). In the Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathigam bestowed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for the sacred site of Thiru-Kalahasti, “En Kannullan” serves as the refrain in each verse.

Therefore, he now sings this Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathigam with such a theme. The Thiru-Pathigam now sung is the eighth Thiru-Pathigam of the Sixth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathigam. This is the Thiru-Pathigam bestowed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for the sacred site of Thiru-Kalahasti.

“Vitrun Onrillatha Nalkoornthan Kan Viyan Kachi Kampan Kan Pichaiyallal Matrun Onrillatha” He is the clever one who has nothing but alms for food, the Lord of the cremation ground, the pure golden pillar, the great jewel, like a mountain, the unyielding stone pillar that supports the seven worlds, the Lord of Kalahasti, the leader of the Ganas, He is within my eyes. He is the one who destroys my karma, the Lord of Ekambam, the one adorned with bones, the one who completes everything, the one who became the three worlds, the one who, by rule, cut off the head of Brahma to prevent the five senses from becoming strong, the Pasupatha, the Lord of Paraitthurai, the Lord of Pazhanam, the Lord of Paingili, the one who wears the fragrant Konrai flower, the Lord of Kalahasti, He is within my eyes. He is Narayanan, He is Brahma, He is the four Vedas, He is the boat across the great ocean of knowledge, He is Annapurani, He is the virtuous one, He is the ancient one, He is the pure one who received the Ganga on his matted locks, He is the guide, He is the moon, He is the sun, He is the one who is the very nature of things, He is the cause of all good people, He is the Lord of Kalahasti, the leader of the Ganas, He is within my eyes. He is the one who destroyed my karma, He is the fire-dancer, He is the Lord of Thiru-Ottrur, He is the one who is close to those who contemplate Him, He is the one who resides in Ekambam, He is the good husband of Uma, He is the word praised by the celestials, He is the one who resides in Thiru-Sottrutthurai, He is the one who learned to nullify the command of the fish-bannered god, He is the Lord of Kalahasti, the leader of the Ganas, He is within my eyes.

He is within the mind, He is on the head, He is within the words, He is within the devotees who sing His praises with full voice, He is above the refuge of the celestials, He is beyond the seven worlds, He is within this earth, He is within the fragrant Konrai flowers, He is within the mountains, He is within the fire, He is within the wind, He is within the Ganas, He is on the summit of Kailash, He is the Lord of Kalahasti, He is within my eyes. Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman worshipped the Lord of Thiru-Kalahasti and bestowed the Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathigam. We have extensively discussed the history and glories of the sacred site of Thiru-Kalahasti in the Kannappa Nayanar Puranam.

There, at the sacred site of Thiru-Kalahasti, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman worshipped the sacred feet of Thiru-Kannappa Devar, who is seated beside the Lord with a bow in his hand. When the Lord appeared to Kannappa Deva Nayanar, He commanded, “Stand on my right, incomparable.” Accordingly, from that day onwards, Thiru-Kannappa Devar He is enshrined with a bow in his sacred hand beside the Lord. In his previous birth as Arjuna, the Lord bestowed the Pasupatham. That very Pasupatham, when he incarnated as Kannappa Deva Nayanar in this birth, became the bow in Kannappa Deva Nayanar’s sacred hand and offered ambrosia to the Lord. When the Lord bestowed grace upon Kannappa Deva Nayanar, Kannappa Deva Nayanar received the Lord’s grace while holding that bow.

Therefore, in that very form, he is eternally enshrined on the right side of the Lord, bestowing grace upon us.

Thus, having worshipped Kalahasti Appar, the Lord, and Gnana Poongodai Ammai, and Kannappa Deva Nayanar, who is enshrined near them, and because of this, With tears flowing like a waterfall over Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s sacred body, he came out of the temple with folded hands above his head and performed Uzhavara Thiru-Pani (sacred service of clearing) there. He performed Thiru-Pani on the high Thiru-Kalahasti mountain. Thiru-Kalahasti mountain is indeed Thiru-Malai (sacred mountain), meaning it is Mount Kailash itself. This Thiru-Kalahasti is the Southern Kailash mountain.

Therefore, when he performed Thiru-Pani and worshipped the Lord at Thiru-Kalahasti, this Thiru-Kalahasti mountain reminded him of Mount Kailash. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal also had the same divine intuition. That is, when they beheld Thiru-Kalahasti mountain, the memory of Mount Kailash arose because Thiru-Kalahasti mountain is the Southern Kailash mountain, the sacred mountain. It is Mount Kailash itself.

Therefore, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, while at Thiru-Kalahasti mountain, sang Pathigams from there for the northern sacred sites such as Thiru-Kedaram and Vada-Kailash. We can recall those historical accounts here.

Furthermore, with the tradition that Thiru-Kalahasti mountain is the Southern Kailash mountain, Nakkiradeva Nayanar has bestowed the sacred work “Kailai Pathi Kalahasti Pathi Andhadhi.” Thus, Thiru-Kalahasti mountain reminded Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman of Mount Kailash.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman developed a great desire to behold the magnificent form of the Lord enshrined on Mount Kailash. While other Acharyas, from Thiru-Kalahasti mountain, praised Mount Kailash and sang Pathigams, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, with the desire to behold the form in which the Lord is enshrined on Mount Kailash, began his pilgrimage from Thiru-Kalahasti to Mount Kailash. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman set out on a pilgrimage to Kailash.

Following this, devotees, according to this tradition, have been undertaking the great Kailash pilgrimage generation after generation to this day. In this verse where Sekkizhar Peruman mentions Kailash mountain, he has gracefully composed the verse by placing the letter ‘Ka’ in the last four words of the line “Kailai Malai Veetrirundha Perum Kolam Kanumadhu Kathalithar Kalaivaimai Kavalanar” (The guardian of the arts desired to behold the magnificent form enshrined on Kailash mountain), thereby achieving an alliterative effect with ‘Ka’. Previously, when it was mentioned that Thirunavukkarasu Peruman arrived at Mayilai, Thirumayilai, Mayilappur, the poem used the alliteration ‘maruvaaru malarcholai Mayilappur’.

Similarly, here, when referring to Thiru-Kailai, he has used the alliteration ‘kakarumutru’.

Furthermore, this poem reminds us of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman’s previous service as Vakkisa Munivar in Thiru-Kailai, and his earlier sacred service.

Therefore, with a great desire to worship the Lord who resides as medicine on Thiru-Kalathi mountain and to behold the Lord’s divine form in Thiru-Kailai, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, with his heart full, journeys towards the northern direction, known as Uthara Thisai.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having received the abundant grace of the Lord of Thiru-Kalathi and journeying northward, traverses lands with various great mountains and wild rivers. As he proceeds north, the mountains, rivers, and the lands beyond them become increasingly vast and extensive. This is a sprawling region characterized by sparsely populated mountains, wild rivers, and vast plains. This area is now the Telugu country, comprising the states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

In this manner, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having crossed many mountains, forests, lands, and rivers, arrives at the sacred sthalam of Thiruparuppatham, also known as Srisailam. “Senganmal Vidai Annanmevu Thiruparuppatham.” Sekkizhar Peruman sings, “He reached,” meaning he arrived at Thiruparuppatham, where Lord Shiva, seated on a bull with red eyes, resides. The reason Nandi Peruman is specifically mentioned here, and Shiva is described as seated on Nandi, is because Nandi Devar performed penance here, and this mountain formed as a result, supporting the Lord in the form of the mountain. This is the history of the Srisailam sthalam.

Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman sang in this manner to specifically convey this.

Furthermore, there is a path to reach this sthalam from the town of Nandyal. Nandyal is also a name associated with the history of this sthalam. Thiruparuppatham is also called Sri Parvatam and Srisailam in Sanskrit. This Srisailam is It is located in the Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh, near the Nandyal River. It is one of the twelve Jyotirlinga sthalams. It holds the distinction of having received sacred hymns (Thiruppathigam) from the three great saints: Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal refers to this sthalam as Seebarpatham. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman arrives at this sacred sthalam of such greatness.

We shall proceed with our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 450, Thirunindracharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, on his northern pilgrimage towards Thiru-Kailai, arrives at the sthalam of Thiruparuppatham, also known as Srisailam. Thiruparuppatham is one of the five celebrated Shiva sthalams in North India. Although located in Andhra Pradesh, it has been referred to as a North Indian Shiva sthalam in Tamil Nadu. This sacred sthalam of Srisailam is the crown jewel of all Telugu-speaking regions.

The language spoken here is called Telugu. The name Telugu for this language originated because this region is called Thrilinkethram, meaning the sthalam of Kaleswaram, Kalesh The sacred name of Lord Shiva here is Muktheeswara Swamy. This sacred sthalam is currently located in the state of Telangana. The second sacred sthalam is Bhimeswaram, where the sacred name of Lord Shiva is Bhimeswara Swamy. This is located in the East Godavari district of coastal Andhra. Next is Srisailam, where the Lord’s sacred name is Mallikarjuna Swamy.

This is located in the Kurnool district, in the Rayalaseema region of Andhra Pradesh.

Thus, the region situated between these three Linga Kshethras – Kaleswaram, Bhimeswaram, and Srisailam – is called Thrilinka Kshethra.

Therefore, the language spoken in Thrilinka Kshethra came to be known as Telugu. Srisailam is the crown jewel of this sacred land situated between these three Linga Kshethras. The sacred sthalam of Srisailam is located at the summit of a mountain, amidst a dense forest and a thick mountain range. This sacred sthalam has many names, such as Mallikarjunam, Seebarpatham, and Srisailam. Arjunam is a type of tree, which in Tamil is called Marutha Maram. There are three very famous sthalams that have such Arjuna trees (Marutha Maram) as their Sthala Viruksham (sacred tree).

Among these three Arjuna sthalams, Srisailam is considered the first. Mathiyar, which is praised in Tamil as Idaimaruthu, is Thiruvidaimaruthur, located in the Chola country. This is called Mathiyarjunam or Idaimaruthu Thiruvidaimaruthur.

Now, the third sthalam located in the south, the Arjuna tree The third sthalam that has the Arutha Maram as its Sthala Viruksham is called Thiruppudaimaruthur or Pudharjunam. It is located in the south, in the Pandya country, on the banks of the Thamirabarani River, very close to Ambasamudram in the Tirunelveli region. Among such Arjuna Kshethrams, Mallikarjunam, or Srisailam, is the foremost. As we have already seen, this sthalam has received Thevaram hymns from the three Samayacharyas: Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal refers to this sthalam as Seebarpatham. The other two Acharyas praise it as Paruppatham. Sekkizhar Swamigal, when referring to this sthalam, calls it Thiruparuppatham and Thiruchilambu. The history of this sacred sthalam is found in the Vazhinadai Padalam of the Kanda Puranam. The history states that Thiru-Nandi Devar, the son of Silatha Munivar, performed penance and became this mountain, supporting the Lord. This history is found in the Vazhinadai Padalam of the Kanda Puranam, composed by Kacchiyappa Sivachariyar Swamigal.

Sri Arunagirinatha Swamigal refers to Srisailam as Thirumalai in his Thiruppugal. Kanchipuram Chidambaranatha Munivar, one of the twelve disciples of Sri Madhava Sivagnana Yogigal, the author of Dravida Mappadi, referred to this sthalam as Thiruchailam in his Kshethrakovai Pillai Tamil. The passage mentions “Thiruchaila Malai Vaazh Arul Tharum Nayaga” and “Thenmaruthil Idaimaruthil Vadamaruthil Vaazh Muruga.” Here, Vadamaruthu refers to Thiruparuppatham, which is Srisailam. It is also called Hemakoodam. Because Silatha Munivar performed penance here, this mountain is named Srisailam. The greatness of this sthalam is also mentioned in the Shiva Mahapuranam.

Sri Rama, to be absolved of the sin of Brahmahatya incurred by killing Ravana, circumambulated this sthalam with Sita Pirattiyar and worshipped Lord Shiva, thereby being freed from the sin. The Pandavas stayed in this sthalam and worshipped Srisailanatha. The place where Bhima performed penance is called Bhimakundam or Bhimankulam. A princess named Chandravathi worshipped Lord Shiva in this sthalam with flowers and attained blessings.

Therefore, the Lord’s sacred name is Mallikarjunar, and the Goddess’s sacred name is Bhramarambikai. This is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas. On the way to Srisailam, the Sakshi Vinayagar The temple is located. To the north of the sanctum sanctorum resides Lord Shiva in the form of a Lingam, named Adimallikarjunar. It is believed that this is the Lord worshipped by Chandravathi. A little to the north of this, Sahasralingeswarar is located, and behind his temple are the Balipeedam and Veerapathrar.

Nearby, there is a Mallikai Poigai (jasmine pond) with a Vasantha Mandapam (spring pavilion) in its center. The Theppotsavam (float festival) takes place here. To the west of the sanctum sanctorum are the deities of Panchapandavar, Sridevi, Kumaraswamy, Panchanandeeswarar, Rajarajeswarar, and others. The Ambikai temple is found on a high ground to the west. Near it, there is also a temple with a thousand Lingams. In a cave near Pathala Gangai, Narasimha Murthy is enshrined.

The Thirtham called Pathala Gangai is located a short distance from Srisailam. This sacred sthalam is situated on a mountain range, part of the Eastern Ghats, at an altitude of approximately 1,500 feet above sea level. It is a very important Kshethram for the Lingayat Shaivites, who are known as Veera Shaivas. A festival takes place during the Maha Shivaratri period. The Krishna River, along with its tributaries Tungabhadra and Moosi, encircles the mountain like a garland, curving in the east, north, and west directions. A waterfall to the south flows near Bhimakundam.

One must bathe there and carry the sacred water for the Abhishekam of Sri Mallikarjuneswarar.

Here, along with the Marutha Maram (Arjuna tree) as the Sthala Viruksham, the Thripala tree is also present. Theertham Parvatha Theertham, Palali, and many other Theerthams of Srisailam Many texts praise Srisailam. The Srisaila Kandam in the Skanda Mahapuranam speaks extensively about this sthalam.

Furthermore, the Mahabharata Vanaparvam, Padma Purana Uttara Kandam, Markandeya Purana, Shivapurana Rudra Samhita, Bhagavata Dasama Skandam, Aditya Purana Suta Samhita, Rasaratnakara Rasayana Kandam, Adi Shankara’s Sivananda Lahari, Someswara’s Kathacharithra Sagaram, Malathi Madhavam, Banabhatta’s Kadambari, and Ratnavali are texts that describe the glory of this sthalam. This sthalam is where the history of Akkamahadevi, a great devotee of Shiva, unfolded. Akkamahadevi, a great devotee of Shiva, followed the Veera Shaiva tradition prevalent in Karnataka and worshipped Lord Shiva. Akkamahadevi was a devotee who created devotional literature in Kannada. Akkamahadevi worshipped Lord Shiva as her husband. In the Vaishnava tradition, there are many female devotees who considered Vishnu as their husband and lover and practiced devotion.

However, in the Shaiva tradition, Akkamahadevi, belonging to the Veera Shaiva sect, is the only one who worshipped Lord Shiva as her husband and attained blessings. She is affectionately called Akka, Mahadeviyakka, and Akkamahadevi by the people of Karnataka. It is said that Akkamahadevi, of such greatness, came to Srisailam and merged completely with Lord Shiva. Akkamahadevi’s works belong to the genre of Vachana literature. Her Yogangathrivar, comprising three hundred and sixteen Vachanas, Akkamahadevi composed Vachana literature about Srisailam Mallikarjuneswarar in this manner. “The beauty of the eye is to see the Guru and elders.

“The beauty of the ear is to hear the praise songs of elders. The beauty of speech is to speak the truth. The beauty of conversation is to speak the words of good devotees. The beauty of living life is to live in association with good people. What is the use of a life without these, O Chenna Mallikarjuna?” This is one of the Vachanas composed by Akkamahadevi.

“Thus, Akkamahadevi sang about the Lord of this sthalam in each Vachana.

“Therefore, a statue of Akkamahadevi has been installed in Srisailam and is worshipped by devotees. Mallamma, a great devotee of Shiva, This sthalam is where she merged with Lord Shiva. In Solapur, Maharashtra, a couple resided. They were childless. Their family guru, Revana Siddhar, gave them a Nartham fruit and blessed them to perform Shiva Puja.

“Accordingly, the couple had a son. Since the child was born by the grace of Siddhar Revana Siddhar, they named him Siddappa. When the boy was six years old, an old man appeared before him, said his name was Mallayya, and that he was very hungry. Siddappa ran and brought food and payasam to satisfy his hunger.

“But the old man was not there. So, calling out “Mallayya, Mallayya,” the boy joined the devotees going to Srisailam, searching for the old man without eating anything. The boy Siddappa arrived at Srisailam and asked the devotees if they had seen an old man named Mallayya. They pointed to the Mallikarjuneswara Lingam and said, “This is Mallayya.” But he was a boy, so he didn’t believe it and continued searching. At one point, he slipped and fell into a pit with the payasam in his hand.

“At that moment, the Lord appeared before him and saved him. Today, that pit is called Siddaramappa Kulam.

“Later, Siddappa returned to his village and built a Shiva temple there. He paid the workers with mud from the pond, which turned into gold dust, astonishing everyone.

“Later, he attained Jeevasamadhi in the very pond he had dug.

“Now, a Shiva temple named Siddarameswarar has been built there. A sculptor from Uma Maheswaram, belonging to Srisailam, He made two Nandi idols. He worried about how to transport them across the Krishna River to Srisailam.

“The Lord appeared in his dream, gave him a rope, and commanded him to drag the Nandis with it, and to do so without looking back. Waking from his sleep, the sculptor found a rope as the Lord had described. He tied both Nandis with it and began to drag them. When one Nandi got stuck between rocks, the sculptor looked back. Because of this, that Nandi remained there. It is said that he only brought the other Nandi to Srisailam.

“Thus, the Nandi that stood in the middle of the river, giving darshan to devotees as Uppili Basavanna, is now submerged deep in the Srisailam dam. When the water level in the dam decreases, They say it will emerge. For this Srisailam Kshethram, Tripurantakam in Prakasam district serves as the eastern gateway, Siddavatam in Kadapa district as the southern gateway, Alampur in Mahabubnagar as the western gateway, and Uma Maheswarapuram as the northern gateway. To its southeast is Pushpagiri Kshethram, to its southwest is Somasila Kshethram, to its northwest is Sangameswara Kshethram, and to its northeast is Elleswara Kshethram.
