Angilamangaiyaraadum Aiyaaradaigindra podhu Paingili pedaiyodaadi parandhu varuvana kanden avar thiruppaadham kandariyaadhana kanden Kandenavar thiruppaadham kandariyaadhana kanden Valarmathi kanniyanai vaar kuzhalaalodum paadi Kalavu padaadhadhor kaalang kaanbaan kadai kanikkindren Alavu padaadhadhor anbodum Aiyaaradaigindra podhu Ilamanaagudazhuveeru varuvana kanden Kanden avar thiruppaadham Kandariyaadhana kanden Kande navthiruppaadham kandariyaadhana kande Thiruchitrambalam. Thiru-Navukkarasar Peruman, when he reached Thiru-Aiyaaru without leaving any trace from the slopes of Thiru-Kailash, saw all living beings appearing as Shiva and Shakti with their respective consorts. He mentions this in every verse of this Thiru-Pathigam. In that state, he sings that he also saw the sacred feet of the Lord.

“Accordingly, in this first verse, he says he saw a male elephant coming with a female elephant, and in the second verse, he saw a male fowl and a female fowl coming together joyfully. In the third verse, He saw a male cuckoo mingling with a female cuckoo, staying in one place, and then coming together as a pair. In the fourth verse, he saw a male swan coming with a female swan as a pair. In the fifth verse, he saw a male peacock mingling with a female peacock, that is, a peahen, and both coming together as a pair. In the sixth verse, he saw a male Anril bird with a female Anril bird, that is, a pair of Anril birds, coming together. In the seventh verse, he saw a male wild boar coming with a female wild boar.

“In the eighth verse, he saw a male deer coming with a female deer. In the ninth verse, he saw male storks coming with their consorts, the female storks. In the tenth verse, he saw a green parrot flying together with its mate, the female parrot, in joy. In the eleventh verse, he saw a cow and a bull coming together. And having seen all these as Shiva and Shakti, Thiru-Navukkarasar Peruman beautifully composes this Thiru-Pathigam, saying that he saw the Shiva-Anandam, which is the sacred feet.

“Our reflection now resumes.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 456, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasar Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasar Peruman, who sang the Thiru-Pathigam “Matharpiraikkanniyanai,” stayed for some time in the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Aiyaatru and sang many Thiru-Pathigams in praise of Aiyaarappar. He sang many Thiru-Thandagams, Thiru-Kurunthogais, Thiru-Nerisais, and loving Thiru-Viruththams, and other Thiru-Pathigams, and remained engaged in sacred service at Thiru-Aiyaaru. There are a total of twelve Thiru-Pathigams composed by Appar Swamigal for the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Aiyaaru. Among them, we have already reflected on the Thiru-Pathigam “Matharpiraikkanniyanai.” Therefore, as mentioned in this passage, there are a total of eleven Thiru-Pathigams sung by Thiru-Navukkarasar Peruman at this time.

Among them, there are two Thiru-Thandagams, two Thiru-Kurunthogais, and three Thiru-Nerisai Thiru-Pathigams. Three Thiru-Viruththa Thiru-Pathigams and one Thiru-Pathigam set in Pazhanthakkaragam, making a total of eleven Thiru-Pathigams. Among these, we have already reflected on the first Thiru-Pathigam, that is, the first of the twelve Thiru-Pathigams, “Matharpirai Kanniyane.” Now, the second Thiru-Pathigam, which begins with “Aaraar Thiruppurangal,” is a Thiru-Thandaga Thiru-Pathigam, the thirty-seventh Thiru-Pathigam in the sixth Thiru-Murai.

endren naane Aaraa vamudhe en Aiyaarane endrendre naan aratri naygindrene Theevaayin muppurangal neera nokkum theerthaa puraanane endren naan” Moova mathisoodi endren naane Mudhalvaa mukkanane endren endren naane Anna Aiyaarane endren naane Endrendre naan aratri naygindrene Avanendru naan unnai anjaathenai Allal aruppaane endren naane Sivanendru naan unnai ellam solla Selvan tharuvaane endren naane Pavanaagi en ullaththu ulle nindru Pandai vinai aruppaay endren naane Avanendre aadhiye Aiyaarane endrendre naan aratri naygindrene Kachchi Ekambane endren naane Kailaya kaaronaa endren naane endre naane Allaavinai theerkkum Aiyaarane endrendre naan aratri naygindrene Thiruchitrambalam.

Now, the third Thiru-Pathigam, the thirty-eighth Thiru-Pathigam in the sixth Thiru-Murai, is a Thiru-Thandaga Thiru-Pathigam.

“Osai oliyalaam aanaay neeye Ulakukku oruvanaay nindraay neeye Vaasamalaralaam aanaay neeye Malaiyaan maruganaay nindraay neeye Pesap perithum iniyaay neeye Piranaay adi enmel vaiththaay neeye Thesa sembar Pennaan pirappiliyaay nindraay nee E Periyaarkkarkkellam periyaay neeye Unnaa varu nanjam undaay neeye Oozhi mudhalvanaay nindraay neeye Kannaay ulagelam kaaththaay neeye Kalarchchevadivanmel “Now, the fourth Thiru-Pathigam, the twenty-eighth Thiru-Pathigam in the fifth Thiru-Murai, is a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathigam.

““Sindhai vannaththaraay thirampaavanam Mundhi vannaththaraay muzhuneerani Sandhi vannaththaraay thazhal polvadhor Andhi vannamumaavar Aiyaarare Moolavannaththaraay mudhalaagiya Kolavannaththaraagi kozhunjudar Neelavannaththaraagi nedumpalingkaala Vannaththaraavar Aiyaarare Sindhai vannamum theeyadhor vannamum Andhippodhazhaagiya vannamum Pandhik kaalanai paainthadhor vannamum Andhivannamuvavar Aiyaarare Irulin”

“The Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru is the color of the seven notes, the color of the scroll, the color of light, the color of grace, the color of the four-faced Brahma and Vishnu, and the color of compassion. He is the color of the rising flames, the color of the crushing flames, the color of the rain-laden clouds, and the color of the calling. He is the color of the garland, the color of the seven notes, the color of the devotees, the color of light, the color of the seen, the color of the fiery great gem, and the color of the universe. He is the color of desire, the color of the Vedas, the color of the sweet words of a sugarcane-like maiden, the color that removes the karma of those who desire Him, and the color of the bud. He is the color of the eons, the color of the single flame, the color of the elephant’s hide, the color of the living fire, and the color of the ocean. He is the color of the sacred ash worn by the doer, the color that is difficult to perceive, the color of the unseen hand, and the color of subtlety.

“The Thiru- of the demon king who lifted the mountain The Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru is the color of darkness, the color of great troubles, the color of the music from the tightened sinews, and the color of proximity.

“Now, the fifth Thiru-padhigam, the fifth Thiru-murai, the twenty-seventh Thiru-padhigam, Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-padhigam.

“He who is in the mind’s mouth, the noble one, the one with the skull in his hand, holding a three-pronged spear, and wearing a snake at dusk, is the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. He who delights in the garland of parts, the one who wears the hide of the elephant, the one with the garland of water lilies and konrai, and the one who dances with the five elements, is the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. In the deep pond of my heart, when I am about to die, let the five sacred letters of your name appear to me, O Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. He who is in the minds of those who remember Him, the one who burned the great city with fire, is the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. He who wore the hide of the elephant, the one who is in all mouths, is the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru.

“He is vast and subtle, difficult to perceive, a great singer and dancer, and also the one with the dark throat, whose vision is not for others, but easy for devotees, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. He is the golden light that does not fade at dawn, the one whom flowers worship, the one who is not absent even at dusk, and the one who adorns himself even at blooming, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. He is the one with the garland of water lilies, the one with the white-colored Ganga, the one who showed affection, the one who wears the garland of the maiden, the moon, and the kanthali, and the one who adorns his body, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. O foolish ones, the six rivers that tried to rise before, and the six rivers that will separate later, the six rivers that merged with the earth, to worship the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru is penance. He dances as if he is the Lord of the command, see his form, I entered Thiru-Aiyaru, his sweet grace It is like opening a river of honey. He is the one with the body of the demon, the one with the tender body, the one who said, “Fear not,” when the demon’s feet were deep, and the one who made the demon’s ten mouths wail, the one who crushed the demon with his foot, is the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru.

“Now, the sixth Thiru-padhigam, the fourth Thiru-murai, the thirty-eighth Thiru-padhigam, Thiru-nerisai Thiru-padhigam.

“He placed Ganga in his matted hair, he placed the radiant light, he placed the moon to shine, he placed the directions to worship. He placed the maiden as a part, he placed the deer and the battle-axe, he placed fire in his hand, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. He applied sacred ash, he wore the white sacred thread, he placed the fierce snake, he kicked Yama. He placed the beautiful maiden as a part of his chest, he placed his feet to be worshipped, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. He wore the loincloth, he placed all the worlds, he placed the battle-axe, he wore the tiger skin, he placed the bull banner, he placed the white He placed the sacred thread, he placed grace to approach, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru.

“He placed devotees to worship, he placed the pure moon in his matted hair, he placed the eight directions to shine, he placed eternal joy for us. He placed the maiden with bee-laden hair as a part, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, whom the celestial beings praise. He placed the celestials to worship, he removed fierce karma, he placed the dance in the forest, he burned Kama. He placed the five products of the cow, he granted grace to those who worship, he wore the elephant’s hide, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. He placed the conch and the garland, he applied sacred ash, he made the fierce sun burn, he placed all the vast groves. He placed night and day, he removed fierce karma, he made the body recite, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru.

“He granted grace to devotees, he rode the leaping bull, he unified the mind, he made one think of Shiva. He granted liberation, he established righteous paths, he wore the elephant’s hide, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. He made the bull strong, he placed Thiru-Idaimaruthur, he placed the fragrant konrai, he placed the snake on his waist. He placed the maiden as a part, he wore the tiger skin, he placed the six rivers in his matted hair, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. He placed many bhoothas, he placed the surging water, he made songs be sung, he placed Kinnara. He made his feet be praised, he made devotees worship, he placed the beginning and the end, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru.

“He gave to the dying, he granted grace to the givers, he placed severe hells for those who conceal. He placed the vast Ganga in his matted hair, he granted grace to the demon, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru.

“We continue to contemplate the Thiru-padhigams of Thiru-Aiyaru.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 457, Thiru-nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We are contemplating the Thiru-padhigams sung by Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman at Thiru-Aiyaru. In that regard, among the twelve Thiru-padhigams belonging to Thiru-Aiyaru, this is the seventh Thiru-padhigam, from the fourth Thiru-murai, the thirty-ninth Thiru-padhigam, a Thiru-padhigam set in Kollippan.

“As a base person, I joined the Jains, and the garland I wore, O Lord, who is the pure path of the radiant light, the Lord of the universe, the honey of Thiru-Aiyaru, I, your devotee, worship your feet and wander.” “Thinking that wearing peacock feathers and performing great penance daily was noble, I became like a senseless person, O Lord, the honey of Thiru-Aiyaru, whom the noble ones worship. My heart, which rose up, rose beautifully.” “O Jains who argue, I thought it was penance, but what can I do to you, O Lord, the honey of Thiru-Aiyaru, who is in the lotus pond? I have loved you with all my heart.” What can I do to you, O Lord, the honey of Thiru-Aiyaru, who is in the lotus pond? I have loved you with all my heart.

I cannot remove the heart that was attached to the Jains, who are full of moss and dirt, and are powerless. Those who can worship with fragrance the Lord, the honey of Thiru-Aiyaru, whom the people of the world praise, will have their fierce karma destroyed. Thinking that applying ash to the body was penance, O heart that was attached to the wounds, what happened to your wisdom? O heart that eats the Lord, the honey of Thiru-Aiyaru, where bananas flow in the ponds, you have performed great penance. I did not know that renunciation was penance, I spent my time speaking, and I was ignorant with the Jains, without any understanding. O heart without a tree, you have attained good wisdom, O Lord, the honey of Thiru-Aiyaru, surrounded by fragrant groves.

I spent many years with the Jains, speaking many words. I spent my time speaking, and when I remembered, O Lord, the honey of Thiru-Aiyaru, where jasmine flowers bloom in the groves, all day and night, when I remembered, it was sweet. The people of the earth and the heavens worship, and to remove sin, O foolish heart, you were with countless Jains. O Lord, the honey of Thiru-Aiyaru, with a head that burns in the south, I was able to see you with my eyes, and my desire was fulfilled.

The Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, whom Brahma and Vishnu, who are in the lotus, cannot see his sacred feet and sacred head, whom the great ascetics praise, O heart that worships him, your false karma will be destroyed. The ignorant demon, who tried to lift the mountain, saw the Lord’s anger, and the wise one, looking at him, pressed him down with his little finger, and he fell to the ground.

The Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, who showed grace with wisdom.

Now, the eighth Thiru-padhigam, the fourth Thiru-murai, the fortieth Thiru-padhigam. Thiru-nerisai Thiru-padhigam.

There is no world without the Lord, no servitude without the world. There is no dance to be seen, no grace for those who contemplate. He does not ride without the long-haired maiden, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. There is no sitting without the deep, no sacred thread for the great ascetics. There is no breaking without the scripture, contemplating the subtle meaning.

When Vishnu and Brahma joined together to worship his lotus feet, there was no nectar without the deep, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. In the cremation ground where jackals roam, there is no dance without him. There is no being without the curly-haired maiden as his companion. There is no grace without clarity for those with discerning minds. There is no one who praises with flowers, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. There is no companion for the devotees, no clothing without skin.

There is no grace without seeing, no separation after joining. Thinking that he is the one whom the ancient four Vedas see, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, whom the celestial beings praise. There is no form without fire, no riding without the bull. There is no covering without darkness, for the radiant light. The inseparable celestials gather and praise him as the great Lord. There is no goddess without knowledge, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru.

There are no bones as ornaments, no riding without the bull. In the cremation ground that smells of flesh, there is no ash without powder. For the devotees who cry and dance without sorrow, there is no wealth without love, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. There is no clothing without the lower garment, no fierce snake with a bright hood. There is no companion without the tender creeper, no warrior who was wounded by the spear of the spring. There is no one who does not return from the deep, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru.

There is no servitude without the world, no one without himself. For the devotees who worship with flowers, with tears in their eyes, and bow down, there is no temple without their hearts, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. Uma There is no form without Uma, no world without his possession. He is the one who possesses us, there is no good or evil. For the devotees who are patient and worship his feet, he grants boundless grace, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. There is no dwelling without the mountain, he did not crush the head of the demon who did not respect him.

He did not spread fire without the great mountain, when the six sides were burning.

The Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, where the Ponni river flows with waves.

Now, the ninth Thiru-padhigam, the fourth Thiru-murai, the ninety-second Thiru-padhigam, Thiru-virutham Thiru-padhigam.

The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that are contemplated by those who contemplate, that pour forth sweet honey, that grant liberation, that remove the ancient karma that has accumulated, and that dance with a snake wrapped around them at dusk. They removed the seven births, they removed the mind’s attachment, they kicked the fierce Yama, they destroyed the great sacrifice of Daksha. The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that destroyed the great sacrifice of Daksha, that are like the color of gems, that are like the color of gold, that are like lightning, that are like the mountain of Kailash, that are loved by those who are pure and devoted, that are near to them, and far from the celestials. The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that remove the darkness of suffering, that give the eye of true knowledge, that give a helping hand to the blind who have lost their way and are in the pit of hell, and that lift them up. The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that remove the diseases of the eyes, that are unfailing medicine, that save those who fall into the pit of hell, and that are seen by those who cry out in distress.

The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that are like a boat in the ocean of sorrow for the devotees. The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that ferry the devotees to the shore of joy, that are like gold flowing, that perform great deeds, that are dear to the devotees who are not attached to falsehood. The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that remove the sins of those who bathe in the Kaveri river with love and devotion, and worship Him, that pour forth sweet honey, that feed them with nectar, that seat them among the celestials, and that grant them great wealth. The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that correct the mind, that establish it firmly, that torment the body, that offer fresh flowers, that are seen by those who are devoted, and that are praised by ascetics. The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that dance in the cremation ground, where owls and bats fly, where many ghosts gather, where drums beat, where jackals howl, where the earth shakes, and where the long hair of the Lord moves. The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that are worshipped by celestials who bow their long crowns, that are like coral, that are like the leaves and buds that I, a humble person, have plucked, and that accept them as offerings.

The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that are married to the mountain maiden, that are eternally present in the crowns of celestials, that are respected by those who stand, that remove the evil of the earth, and that are surrounded by the waves of the Ponni river. The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that are like fresh lotus flowers, that are a companion to those who praise them and cry, that are like gold, that are adorned with anklets, bracelets, and clusters of tiny bells. The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that are a refuge for the friendless, that are praised by those who have learned the good scriptures, that grant grace to those who love them, and that give precious wealth to the poor. The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that transcend the sky and the universe, that grant grace to those who rejoice in the flesh, that are a luminous light in the middle for the virtuous, and that wore the elephant’s hide. The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that are loved by the beautiful women, that are the great earth, that are the celestials, that are the soft anklets on the crown, that tighten the fierce belt, that drive away the messengers of Yama, and that are a refuge for those who suffer in servitude. The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that are like a ladder to liberation for those who worship them with grace, that are like a ruby on the crowns of celestials, that are like an emerald, that are like a diamond, and that are like pure gold.

The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that are the knowledge and the meaning of knowledge, that are the Vedas and the sacrifices of the learned Brahmins, that are the sky and the earth, that are the light and the red sun, and that are the beginning and the end with the pure moon. The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that are like the lotus, that are worshipped by the maiden with bee-laden hair, who bows with her bangled hands, and that are like the beautiful kanthal flower when she worships and caresses. The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that are a shade for the devotees who are caught in the cycle of suffering, that remove the endless cycle of birth, that remove the karma that does not leave, that are beyond Yama, and that are a fiery light. The sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru are those that crushed the demon’s ten heads when he cried out, that kicked the powerful Yama, that were seen by the celestials, that were praised by many, and that stand firm without pity.

This Thiru-padhigam has twenty verses. This Thiru-padhigam praises the sacred feet of Thiru-Aiyaru. This Thiru-padhigam praises the sacred feet of the Lord and their gracious qualities.

Now, the tenth Thiru-padhigam, the fourth Thiru-murai, the ninety-first Thiru-padhigam, Thiru-virutham Thiru-padhigam.

He who showed the disease of karma, and removed the disease, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, who graciously revealed himself, made me, his devotee, join his golden feet. He who showed the disease of karma, and removed the disease, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, who graciously revealed himself, made me, his devotee, join his golden feet. He who showed the disease of karma, and punished me, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, who graciously remembered me, removed the disease, and made me, his devotee, join his golden feet. He who looked at me, He, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, made me, his devotee, join his golden feet. He, who was arrogant, and due to my ignorance, was afflicted with disease, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, who graciously remembered me, melted me, and made me, his devotee, join his golden feet.

He, who showed the disease of karma, and caused suffering, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, who graciously joined me, removed the disease, and made me, his devotee, worship his golden feet. He, who showed the disease of karma, and caused suffering, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, who graciously remembered me, removed the disease, and made me, his devotee, follow his golden feet. He, who showed the disease of karma, and caused suffering for many days, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, who graciously removed the disease, and also removed all sins and evils, made me, his devotee, join his golden feet. He, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, made me, his devotee, join his golden feet. He, who showed the disease of karma, and caused forgetfulness, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, who graciously removed the disease, and caused death, made me, his devotee, glorify his golden feet. He, who showed the disease of karma, and caused suffering, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, who graciously agreed, removed the disease, and caused confusion, made me, his devotee, join his golden feet.

He, who held the Ganga in his matted hair, and cut off the twenty heads of the king of Lanka, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, who graciously endured me, his devotee, made me join his golden feet.

Now, the eleventh Thiru-padhigam, the fourth Thiru-murai, the ninety-eighth Thiru-padhigam, Thiru-virutham Thiru-padhigam.

The Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, who has the moon as a garland at dusk, The Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, who entered my heart and stood there, how can I say he is false? He, whose matted hair is adorned with the slightly bloomed konrai, is the Lord.

The Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, whose dancing feet are like the sun, who danced before the maiden, who followed the boar, whose feet are worshipped by the forest maiden, is the Lord.

Now, the next Thiru-padhigam, the fourth Thiru-murai, the thirteenth Thiru-padhigam, Pazhanthakkaraga Thiru-padhigam.

I, your humble servant, cannot leave you. I cannot give anything, I was confused by the words of the Jains. I follow your pure lotus feet, I take refuge in Thiru-Aiyaru, and I am saved. He, whose sacred form is like red coral, whose light shines, who has the maiden with bangles as a part, who wears the blooming konrai on his matted hair, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, I am saved by becoming his servant. He is near, he is far, he is our Lord, he is the pure gold, he is the skin, he is the sacred ash.

He is the gem, he is the medicine for the celestials, he removes diseases, he is the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, I am saved by becoming his servant. You stood as the fire of the eons, you are in the hearts of those who meditate, you stood as the living fire, you are the mouth of those who praise. You stood as the great fire, you have the cool moon on your matted hair, I am saved by becoming the servant of the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru. You are the one with the matted hair, you are the one who rides the bull, you are the one who destroyed the cities, you are the one who wanders from village to village with a skull for alms, you are the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, I am saved by becoming his servant. You are water, you are fire, you are the path, you are liberation, you are the village, you are the world, you are the body, you are the soul, you are the name, you are the great one. He is the great Lord who removes suffering, the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, I am saved by becoming his servant.

You are the eye, you are the gem, you are the thought, you are the meaning, you are the number, you are the letter, you are the nature of the letter, you are the sky, you are the Brahmin who destroyed the cities in the sky, you are the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, I am saved by becoming his servant. You are lightning, you are thunder, you are the meaning of the Vedas, you are gold, you are a gem, you are a pearl in the ocean, you are the radiant light that Brahma and Vishnu cannot see, you are the Lord of Thiru-Aiyaru, I am saved by becoming his servant.

The devotees who bathe in the Ponni river, which grants liberation, and worship him many times, the celestials who praise him as our Lord, in that direction is Thiru-Aiyaru, I am saved by becoming his servant.

The Lord who crushed the king of Lanka with his sacred finger, the one who is praised by the people of the great mountain as Thiru-Nandi, in that direction is Thiru-Aiyaru, I am saved by becoming his servant.

Thus, Thiru-navukkarasu We have contemplated the Thiru-padhigams sung by Peruman at Thiru-Aiyaru. We will continue to contemplate them. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 458. Thirunindracharukam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We have contemplated the Thiru-pathikams of Thiruvaiyaru.

Now, let us briefly contemplate the special features and historical accounts of the Thiruvaiyaru sthalam. This sacred place, Thiruvaiyaru, is very close to Trichy and Thanjavur in Tamil Nadu. The Lord’s sacred names are Panchanadeeswarar, Aiyattru Eesar, Sembar Sotheeswarar, Pranarthikaran. The Goddess’s sacred names are Dharmasambarthini, Aramvalartha Nayaki. The sthala-viruksham is Vilvam. The thirthams are Surya Pushkarani, Kaveri, and many others.

This sthalam has many names such as Aiyaru, Panchanadam, Jappeeswaram, Bhooloka Kailayam, Kaveri Kottam. The temple is a very large temple, including its sacred streets. It has five large circumambulatory paths. There are separate temples for the Lord and the Goddess. Both are facing east. The Dakshinamurthy Swami, enshrined in the first prakaram of the Lord’s temple, is very special.

In this circuit, all the parivara murthams, Uma Maheswarar, Sankaranarayanar, Brahmadevar, Thiripura Sundari, Sapthamathargal, and other deities are enshrined. In the second prakaram, there is a separate temple for Somaskandar. Near this, to the west, is the Jappeeswara Mandapam.

Here, the Panchabhootha Lingams, Aadhi Vinayagar, and Navagrahams are enshrined. The Navagrahams are consecrated here according to Agamic rules. On the sacred walls of this circuit, ancient paintings with Puranic legends are depicted. In this circuit, there are also Vinayagar, Subramaniyar, Natarajar, and Sapthasthala Murthams. The third prakaram houses the Yagasalai, Madappalli, and other structures. In this prakaram, there are two gopurams, one in the east and one in the south.

Just as the Lord in Sri Kailayam grants grace through the southern entrance, so too in this Bhooloka Kailayam, during festival times, the Lord proceeds in procession through the southern gopuram entrance. In this sacred circuit, if one goes to the western end of the southern prakaram and stands facing north, or goes to the western end of the northern prakaram and stands facing south, and calls out “Aiyara,” it will echo seven times.

Therefore, this is called the Saptha Oli Prakaram. In the fourth sacred circuit, in the southern prakaram, there is the sacred tank called Surya Pushkarani, and the Lokamadeveeswaram, also known as Dakshina Kailayam, where Appar saw and worshipped Kailayam. In this circuit, gopurams are located in the east, south, and west. At the southern gopuram entrance, there is the Aatkonda sanctum. The temple of the Goddess is located in the northeast direction of the Lord’s temple. This also has two prakarams.

There are separate Rajagopurams for the Lord’s sanctum and the Goddess’s sanctum.

Here, the Lord is a Swayambu Murtham.

The Lord has many sacred names such as Aiyarappar, Sembar Sothiyar, Jappiyesar, Kailayanathar, Pranarthikaran. The Goddess has sacred names such as Aramvalartha Nayaki, Thiripurasundari, Dharmambikai, Dharmasambarthini. The Goddess is enshrined in a standing posture. There are many Ganapathi Murthams such as Olamitta Vinayagar, Aadhi Vinayagar, Vallabha Vinayagar. Lord Muruga here is known as Dhanusu Subramaniam, adorned with bow, spear, and arrow. The sacred name for Dakshinamurthy here is Sri Hari Guru Sivayoga Dakshinamurthy.

This is one of the eighteen forms of Dakshinamurthy. One of the eighteen forms.

The Lord enshrined here, Dakshinamurthy Peruman, holds a skull in his upper right hand, a trident in his left hand, the Chinmudra in his lower right hand, and the Sivagnana Bodham in his left hand, with a tortoise at his feet, bestowing grace. Among the Lord’s Dvarapalakas, Aatkondar is enshrined in a posture of subduing Yama under his foot.

Now, regarding the thirthams: there are many thirthams such as Kaveri river, Surya Pushkarani (also known as Ayanari Thirtham), Samudra Thirtham, Devamrita Thirtham, Nandi Thirtham. Among them, Surya Pushkarani and Kaveri are very important. Bathing in Kaveri here for one day yields more benefit than bathing throughout the month of Thulam in other places. A beautiful mandapam called Poosamandapathurai, with steps leading to the river, is located on the bank of the Kaveri. The sthala-viruksham is the Vilva tree.

Now, let us learn about the Puranic history of this temple. Let us learn the Puranic history of this temple. The story of the Lord worshipping Himself in Thiruvaiyaru is as follows: One of the twenty-four Aadi Saivars who worshipped Aiyarappar went on a pilgrimage to Kashi. When he did not return for a long time, others seized his land and other rights. His wife and son fell at the feet of Aiyarappar and pleaded. The Lord, in the form of an old man, a Siva-vediyar, and then in the form of the Aadi Saivar, entered the house of the vediyar and lived as the Aadi Saivar who had gone to Kashi.

During this time, Lord Shiva, in the form of the Aadi Saivar, regularly worshipped Aiyarappar and stayed in a math.

At this time, the Aadi Saivar who had gone to bathe in the Ganga in Kashi returned to Thiruvaiyaru. Everyone was confused, wondering if there were two people with the same form. They were confused, wondering if there were two people with the same form. The Lord, who had come in the form of a Brahmin, asked the Aadi Saivar, “Who are you?” He replied, “I am one of the twenty-four Brahmins who worship this Shiva.” Both showed their respective documents. Many in the assembly compared the signatures of both and found that the document of the Brahmin who came from Kashi was genuine. While the Aadi Saivar stood jubilantly, the Lord appeared in the sky in His true form.

In accordance with this legend, a crystal lingam and the idol of the Goddess in the Somaskanda Mandapam are worshipped even today.

Now, the history of Thiru-Nandi Devar: Siladha Muni, distressed by childlessness, worshipped Aiyarappar and performed penance. Aiyarappar blessed Siladha, saying, “You must perform a Putrakameshti Yagam. After performing the yagam, when you plough the yaga-bhumi, a box will appear. In it, a son will be found. He will be sixteen years old. Take him.” Siladha Muni accordingly performed the Putrakameshti Yagam, and at the end of the yagam, when he ploughed the earth, he found a box.

He opened it and saw a deity with four arms, three eyes, and a crown adorned with the moon, and worshipped him. Aiyarappar commanded in an ethereal voice, “Close the box and open it again.” When he did so, the deity’s previous form disappeared, and he appeared as a beautiful child. The parents named the child Seppesan and raised him. By the age of fourteen, Seppesar became proficient in all arts, including the Vedas and Agamas. Seeing his parents lamenting that they would lose this intelligent son in two more years, Seppesar went to Aiyarappan’s temple, worshipped, bathed in the Ayanari Thirtham, and performed severe penance by placing one foot over the other. The sacred body of Seppesar was gnawed by water creatures like snakes and fish.

After many days, his parents and others became distressed when he did not emerge. The Lord, pleased by Seppesar’s unwavering devotion, appeared and granted him all his wishes and sixteen boons.

Furthermore, the Lord desired to restore Seppesar’s skeletal body, that is, the body that had been gnawed by various insects.

Therefore, Lord Shiva Himself performed abhishekam with five waters: Ganga water, Brahma’s kamandalu water, the milk from the Goddess’s breast, cloud water, and the foam from Nandi’s mouth.

Thus, Seppesar’s body was restored and shone like the sun. Siladha Muni, the grandson of Vasishta Muni, and the daughter of Vyagrapada Muni, Upamanyu’s sister, Swayamprabha Ammaiyar, was married to his son on the Punarpoosam star in the month of Panguni.

Thereafter, Seppesar received initiation from Aiyattru Annal and attained the position of chief of the Siva Ganas in Kailayam, the right to guard the first sacred entrance, and the status of the first guru among the Saiva Acharyas. This is the sacred history of Thiru-Nandi Devar, which took place in Thiruvaiyaru. In connection with this, the Thiru-Nandi Devar festival takes place every year. This festival is associated with the seven villages surrounding Thiruvaiyaru. These seven villages are called Sapthasthanams. They are Thiruvaiyaru, Thirupazhanam, Thiruchotruthurai, Thiruvedikudi, Thirukandiyur, Thirupoonduruthi, Thiru Neithanam.

These are the seven sthalams. On the auspicious day of Chithirai Pournami and Visaka Nakshatram, Sri Nandikeswarar, in wedding attire, will visit each of these sthalams in a Vetiver palanquin, accompanied by Swayambikai Ammaiyar. Sri Aiyarappar, along with Sri Aram Valartha Nayaki, will also set out in a wondrous glass palanquin and visit each sthalam in turn. After performing Shodasha Upacharam and other rituals with the deities of those villages, the deities of those villages will accompany them in palanquins and return to Aiyattru the next morning. People call this festival the wedding procession of Thiru-Nandi Devar. This festival has a unique specialty not found in any other sthalam and is called the Sapthasthana festival.

The second sthalam in this is Thirupazhanam. It is very close to Thiruvaiyaru on the road to Kumbakonam. The Lord’s sacred name is Apath Sahayar. The Goddess’s name is Periya Nayaki. We have already contemplated the special features of Thirupazhanam sthalam.

Next is Thiruchotruthurai, the third sthalam among the Sapthasthana sthalams. This is where Gautama Muni’s ashram was located. Indra, Surya, and others worshipped here. It is where the Akshaya Patra was given to the Brahmin devotee named Arulalar. The Lord’s sacred names are Othanavaneswarar, Tholayaachelvar. The Goddess’s names are Oppila Ammai, Annapoorani.

We have also contemplated the sthala puranam of Thiruchotruthurai before. The next sacred place among the Sapthasthana sthalams is Thiruvedikudi. It is one of the sthalams where the Vedas worshipped. Vinayagar is also called here. The Lord’s sacred name is Vedapureeswarar. The Goddess’s name is Mangaiyarkarasiyar.

We have already contemplated the sthala puranam of Thiruvedikudi. Next is Thirukandiyur. This is one of the eight Veeratta sthalams, where Lord Shiva severed Brahma’s head. This is the sthalam where Sadanandar worshipped.

Here, there is a separate shrine for Brahma. The Lord’s sacred name is Veeratteswarar. The Goddess’s name is Mangala Nayaki.

Now, the next sacred place is Thirupoonduruthi. Indra, Kashyapar, Cholan, and others worshipped here.

Here, there is a history of Nandi moving aside to allow Thirugnanasambandha Swamigal to have darshan. This is the sthalam where Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal built a sacred math and resided. It was here that Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal carried the palanquin of Thirugnanasambandha Murthy Swamigal, who had returned from Pandya Nadu.

We will now contemplate this history. The sacred name of the Lord in this sthalam is Pushpavanathar. The Goddess’s name is Azhagarndha Nayaki. The seventh is Thirunaithanam. This was worshipped by Saraswati. It is located west of Thiruvaiyaru.

The Lord’s sacred name is Neyyadiyar. The Goddess’s name is Valambikai. It is now called Thillaistanam. Saptha During the Utsavam, Aiyarappar finally proceeds to this sthalam and then returns to Aiyaru. These are the notes about the Sapthasthana Sthalams. In this sacred sthalam of Thiruvaiyaru, the Lord Panchanadeesan, the universal master who creates, protects, and blesses all living beings with immense grace, gave two measures of paddy to the Goddess so that the people of the world could witness and rejoice in the great divine play of His spiritual consort, Aramvalartha Nayakiyar, in performing acts of dharma.

Lord Shiva gave the paddy to the Goddess. The Goddess received it and, with her wondrous power, nurtured thirty-two acts of dharma.

Thus, because the Goddess received two measures of paddy from Lord Shiva and nurtured thirty-two acts of dharma, the Goddess here is known as Sri Dharmasamvardhini and Sri Aram Valartha Nayakiyar. And other sacred names. This sthalam is sung by the three great saints: Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. After visiting Thirukandiyur, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, along with Cheraman Peruman, was on his way to visit Aiyattru. Seeing the Kaveri overflowing and boats unable to cross, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal sang the Thiru-pathikam “Paravum Parisu Ondru Ariyen.” By the grace of the Lord, the Kaveri water stood like a mountain on the western side, and on the eastern side, the water receded, revealing a sandy expanse.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal and Cheraman Perumal Nayanar went this way and had darshan of Aiyarappar. When Sundaramoorthy Swamigal sang the pathikam from the other bank of the river, the Vinayagar Murthy enshrined on this bank cried out “Olam Abayam” (Help! Refuge!).

Therefore, he is known as Olamitta Vinayagar. Those who came to the sacred sthalam of Thiruvaiyaru and praised the Lord Those who received grace are Thirumal, Brahma, Indra, Surya, and other deities; Agasthiyar, Dattisi, Virasan, Gautamar, Kashyapar, Angirasar, Kurshar, Attri, Brahuhu, Vasishtar, Sadanandar, Siladhar, and other great sages; Sivadarshan, Dushpravarthi, Dushpragnyan, Sivapriyan, Surathan, Dharmarasan, Nathasanma, Valiyar, Sucharithan, Karikalan, and other great personalities.

Now, the mandapams: here, like in Kashi, there is a Mukthi Mandapam. This mandapam is now called Sabesa Mandapam.

Now, the Nootrukkal Mandapam (Hundred-Pillared Hall): this is the Dandapani temple. The Utsava Mandapam (Festival Hall) is separately located in the Lord’s temple and the Goddess’s temple. Besides these, the Asthana Mandapam and Prasanga Sabhamandapam are in the third prakaram. The Chokkattan Mandapam is in the Aiyarappar sanctum.

Now, the subsidiary temples belonging to the Thiruvaiyaru temple.

First, Daksha Dakshina Kailayam, which is inside the temple to the south. Uttara Kailayam, also known as Lokamadeveeswaram, is inside the temple to the north. Dandapani temple, which is the Nootrukkal Mandapam (Hundred-Pillared Hall) next to the Rajagopuram in the outer prakaram.

Now, daily pujas and festivals: The deities in this sacred temple receive six daily pujas: Ushatkalam, Kalasandhi, Uchikalam, Sayarakshai, Irundam Kalam, and Ardha Jamam, performed according to the Kamika Agama and Karana Agama Sastra rules. The Mahotsavam takes place in the month of Chithirai. This festival concludes on the day of Chithra Pournami and Chithra Nakshatram, which is considered the Thirtham day. This is a twelve-day festival. The fifth day of the festival is very special. On that day, the Lord, as a Saiva in Aiyaru, worships Himself.

On that day, Maheswara Puja will be performed for the deities and Swamis coming from Thirunaithanam and the other six villages, and for the great Saiva Acharyas. Vasanthotsavam, Aadipooram Utsavam, Appar Kailai Kaatchi on Aadi Amavasai, Seppootsavam on Aavani Moolam day, Navaratri in Purattasi, Thiruvambavai and other festivals in Margazhi are all celebrated. The Thiruvaiyaru Sri Aiyarappar Temple is a temple under the administration of the Dharmapuram Adheenam. We saw that the sacred name of this sacred place is Thiru Aiyaru, which means ‘five rivers’. We saw that Nandi Devar performed Rudra Japam seven crore times in this region and was blessed with holy water by the Lord. We saw that the Lord performed abhishekam for Nandi Devar.

Because of these five thirthams, it is called Thiru Aiyaru. There are twelve Thiru-pathikams composed by Appar Swamigal, five Thiru-pathikams composed by Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal’s one Thiru-pathikam, making a total of eighteen Thiru-pathikams for the sacred sthalam of Thiruvaiyaru. Manikkavasaga Peruman has sung in Thiruvachagam, in Keerthi Thiru Agaval, “Aiyaru adhanil Saivanagiyum.” Aiyadigal Kadavarkon Nayanar has sung about this sthalam. Sekkizhar Swamigal has sung about it. There are sthala purana books such as Sri Panchanathamanmiyam, also known as Thiruvaiyattrumiyam, which is a prose account of the Thiruvaiyaru Puranam.

All these are the sthala puranam and news about the sacred sthalam of Thiruvaiyaru. We shall continue our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 459. Thirunindracharukam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having sung Thiru-pathikams and performed sacred service in Thiruvaiyaru, proceeds to visit nearby sthalams. From Thiruvaiyaru, he goes to Thiruneithanam, a nearby sthalam.

We have contemplated that Thiruneithanam is one of the Sapthasthana sthalams of Thiruvaiyaru. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman proceeds to this sthalam. This sthalam is currently called Thillaistanam. The Lord’s sacred names are Neyyadiyappar, Krithapureeswarar. The Goddess’s sacred name is Balambikai. The sthala-viruksham is Vilvam.

The thirtham is Kaveri. For this sthalam, there is one Thiru-pathikam sung by Thirugnanasambandha Peruman and five Thiru-pathikams composed by Appar Swamigal.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal has sung about it in other pathikams, mentioning it as a Vaippu Sthalam.

Here, the anointing of the Lord with cow’s ghee is special. The sacred name of the Goddess in the Thevaram pathikams is mentioned as Ilamangaiyammai. This sthalam is very close to Thiruvaiyaru. Saraswati, Kamadhenu, Gautama Muni, and others have worshipped here. Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, who visited this sthalam, has composed five Thiru-pathikams. Among them, the first Thiru-pathikam is the thirty-seventh Thiru-pathikam of the Fourth Thirumurai, a Thirunerisai Thiru-pathikam.

Kālanai vīḻac ceṟṟa kaḻalaṭi iraṇṭum vandin Mēlavā irukkap peṟṟēṉ mētakat tōṉṟukiṉṟa Kōla neytāṉameṉṉum kuḷir poḻil kōyil mēya Nīlam vaittanaiya kaṇṭa niṉaikkumā niṉaikkiṉṟēṉē Gloss: I have been blessed to have the two anklet-adorned feet that struck down Yama, come and reside above me. I contemplate the Lord with the blue-throated neck, who resides in the beautiful, cool grove temple called Neythanam, appearing majestically. Kāmaṉai aṉṟu kaṇṇā Kaṇalariyāka nōkki tūpamum tīpam kāṭṭi toḻum avarkku aruḷkaḷ ceytu Cēma neyttāṉameṉṉum ceṟippoḻil kōyil mēya vāmaṉai niṉainta neñcam vāḻvuṟa niṉaintavārē Piṟaitaru caṭaiyiṉmēlē peyppuṇar kaṅkai taṉṉai uraitara vaittayaṅkaḷ uttamaṉ ūḻiyāya Niṟaitaru poḻilkaḷ cūḻa niṉṟa neyttāṉameṉṟu kuṟaitarum aṭiyavarkku kuḻakaṉai kūṭalāmē Vaṭitaru maḻuvoṉṟēnti vārcaṭai matiyam vaittu poṭitaru mēṉi mēlē puritaru nūlar pōlum Neṭitaru poḻilkaḷ cūḻa niṉṟa neyttāṉam mēvi aṭitaru kaḻalkaḷ ārppa āṭum em aṇṇalārē Kāṭiṭamāka niṉṟu kaṇalari kaiyilēnti pāṭiya pūtañcūḻa paṇṇuṭaṉ palavuñcolli āṭiya kaḻalar cīrār antaṉ neyttāṉam eṉṟum kūṭiya kuḻakaṉārai kūṭumār arukileṉē Gloss: Having seen Kama as a fiery flame with his eye that day, and bestowing grace upon those who worship Him with incense and lamps, my heart, contemplating the Vamana who resides in the dense grove temple called Chema Neythanam, has contemplated for a prosperous life.

The supreme Lord, who placed the flowing Ganga on His crescent-moon-adorned matted locks, stands surrounded by abundant groves in Neythanam; can we not attain that youthful Lord who grants boons to His devotees? Our Lord, holding a sharp axe, with the moon in His long matted locks, adorned with sacred thread over His ash-smeared body, resides in Neythanam, surrounded by vast groves, dancing with His anklets resounding. Standing in the cremation ground, holding fire in His hand, surrounded by singing bhoothas, speaking many things with melody, the anklet-adorned, glorious Lord, the ancient one of Neythanam, how can I not approach that youthful Lord? Āṇavar vaṇaṅkiyētti vaikaḷum malarkaḷ tūva tāṉavarkku aruḷkaḷ ceyyum caṅkaraṉ ceṅkaṉ ēṟṟaṉ Tēṉamar poḻilkaḷ cūḻa tikaḻu neyttāṉē kūṇila matiyiṉāṉai kūṭumārikileṉē Kālatiṟ kaḻalkaḷārpa kaṇaleṟik kaiyil vīci ñālamum kuḻiya niṉṟu naṭṭamatu āṭukiṉṟa Mēlavar mukaṭutōya viricaṭai ticaikaḷ pāya māloru pākamāka makiḻnta neyttāṉē Paṉtitta caṭaiyiṉmēlē pāyppuṇal ataṉai vaittu aṉtippōtaṉum āṭi aṭikaḷ aiyāṟu pukkar Vaṉtippār vaṇaṅki niṉṟu vāḻttuvār vāyiṉ uḷḷār ciṉtippār ciṉtaiyuḷḷār tiruntu neyttāṉaṉārē Cōtiyāy cuṭarumāṉār cuṇṇaviṉ cāntu pūci ōtivāy ulakam ētta ukantu tām aruḷkaḷ ceyvār Ātiyāy antamāṉār yāvarum iṟaiñci ētta nītiyāy niyamamāki niṉṟa neyttāṉaṉārē Iḷaiyuṭai paṭaikai Gloss: The Lord Sankaran, with a red-eyed bull, who bestows grace upon the demons, worshipped and praised by men, who daily scatter flowers, shines in Neythanam, surrounded by honey-filled groves. How can I not approach the Lord with the crescent moon? With anklets resounding at His feet, scattering fire from His hand, standing in the world and dancing, His matted locks spread in all directions, touching the sky above, the Lord of Neythanam, who delights with Vishnu as one half of His body.

Placing the flowing water on His matted locks, the Lord danced at dusk and entered Aiyaru. Those who worship, stand and praise, are in their mouths; those who contemplate, are in their hearts; He is the Lord of Thiruneythanam. He who is light and radiance, smeared with fragrant ash, gladly bestows grace as the world praises Him with Vedic chants. He who is the beginning and the end, worshipped by all, stands as justice and rule, the Lord of Thiruneythanam. With a leaf-shaped weapon in hand. He is like the steadfast Lord who crushed the king of Lanka with his head, then performed many miracles for the celestials, and with his bow and arrow, burned the three cities.

He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam.

Now, the second Thiru-Pathikam by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for Thiru-Neythanam, the eighty-ninth Thiru-Pathikam of the fourth Thiru-Murai, the Thiru-Virutham Thiru-Pathikam.

He who danced among all living beings, granting grace to the celestials, and consumed the poison from the ocean as ambrosia. We do not know that he goes from town to town, begging for alms. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, standing on the riverbank. O Lord, whose crescent moon shines on your holy matted locks, from which the Ganga flows in many streams, O Lord with the shining axe and spear, tell me, your humble servant, you and the young maiden are in Thiru-Neythanam. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, who, when Yama, the god of death, came to seize lives, danced and crushed him.

He is the Lord who, with his bow, destroyed the three cities of the Asuras, whose fame is known throughout the world. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, who resides on the cool, verdant banks of the Kaveri, where devotees come to cleanse their sins. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, who dances to the sound of drums and various instruments, with a serpent tied around his waist, the Lord with the bow who burned the three cities of the wicked. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, who delights with the goddess, adorned with fresh Konrai flowers, Thulasi, Vanni, Datura, and Vilvam, whose matted locks are adorned with fragrant flowers, the Lord of the celestials, whose dark blue throat is stained with poison, the pure one, the Lord of the dance, the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam. He took the fragrant Konrai garland, adorned his matted locks, mounted the sharp-horned bull, and amidst the host of Bhootas, he came forth, listening to their songs and dances. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, who resides with Uma.

He is the Lord who wears a serpent and a tiger skin, who burned the three strong cities. He is the Lord with the host of Bhootas, with the trident and axe, who destroys evil deeds. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam. He is the Lord with flowing matted locks, the Lord of the celestials, who consumed poison, who flayed the elephant and wore its skin, who burned the three cities of the enemies with his bow, who, without diminishing, enslaved me. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, who resides with Uma. He is the Lord who is unwavering, who adorns his thick red matted locks with Thulasi, Konrai, the crescent moon, and the Ganga.

He is the Lord who, with great compassion, burned the three cities, and who resides with Uma in Thiru-Neythanam. He is the Lord who stood firm, who burned the cities with his fiery arrow, who caused the enemies to perish, who showed the celestials his matted locks from which the mighty Ganga flowed. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, who stood firm.

Now, the third Thiru-Pathikam by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for Thiru-Neythanam, the thirty-fourth Thiru-Pathikam of the fifth Thiru-Murai, the Thiru-Kurunthakai Thiru-Pathikam.

He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, who resides in Kuttralam, where the cool breeze blows, who burned the three cities of the enemies. Those who praise him with truth are shining celestials. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, who holds the skull of the night, who has the three cities as his weapon. Those who worship him are glorious celestials. They dance with the five elements of the cow, they dance in the dark cremation ground, behold!

He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, where honey flows from flowers. Those who worship him with words are powerful celestials. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, who burned the three cities of the enemies to ashes, who consumed the deadly poison, the luminous one. Those who worship him as devotees are shining celestials. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, who consumed the poison from the ocean without hesitation, while others were churning it, their forearms aching. He is with the goddess.

Those who worship him are supreme celestials. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, who smears himself with ashes, who dances in the cremation ground with good ghosts. Those who worship him with love are joyful celestials. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, who dances in the thorny forest, holding a fiery torch and a cruel skin. Those who worship him with a clear and discerning mind are celestial beings. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, who has the young crescent moon on his head, whose matted locks are adorned with a serpent, who has a fiery eye on his forehead.

Those who worship him are shining celestials. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, whom Vishnu and Brahma, who recited the Vedas, could not find his feet or crown. Those who worship him with Vishnu, their sins will perish. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, who crushed the mighty demon Ravana, who lived by the strength of his skin, by pressing him under the mountain. When Ravana sang with the nerves of his hand, those who worship him with devotion, their sins will perish.

Now, the fourth Thiru-Pathikam by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for Thiru-Neythanam, the forty-first Thiru-Pathikam of the sixth Thiru-Murai, the Thiru-Thandakam Thiru-Pathikam.

You are the one with the unique form, you are the one who resides in Kailash, you are the one who is beyond all, you are the one who resides in Thiru-Venkaadu. You are the one who ended enmity and ruled, you are the one who resides in Thiru-Paasoor. You are the one who goes to be worshipped by all, O Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you are in my heart. You are the one who is the father of Brahma, you are the primordial Lord of Kailash, you are the one who dances with intensity, you are the one who is the protector of the world. You are the one who blessed Arjuna, You are the one with the nature residing in Pazhaiyanoor.

You are the pure one, the Lord of Shiva’s world, O Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you are in my heart. You are the night, you are the day, you are the primordial Lord of Kailash, you are the one who resides under the stone, you are the Kalpaka tree of Kaalathi. You are the word, you are the meaning, you are the one who resides in Thiru-Sotrutthurai. You are the one who goes to Thiru-Aana, O Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you are in my heart. You are the one with the waist like lightning, you are the one who resides in Kailash, you are the one with golden matted locks, you are the Lord of the Bhoota Ganas. You are the one who is beyond all vows, you are the Lord of Thiru-Ekambam.

You are the one who resides in the southern city, O Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you are in my heart. You are the one who existed before all, you are the one who resided in Kailash, you are the one who blessed Nandi, you are the good dancer. You are the one who is bound by nothing, you are the one who resides in Thiru-Paingili. You are the one who is beyond thought, O Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you are in my heart. You are the one who is for the worthy devotees, you are the Lord of Kailash. You are the one who wears bones, you are the self-manifested one in Thiru-Aakkoor.

You are the one who entered the seven worlds, you are the one who is the Lord of Thiru-Pollil Veloor. You are the one who is the Lord of Thiru-Maakonam, O Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you are in my heart. You are the one with fame and greatness, you are the one who resides in Kailash. You are the one who holds the skull, you are the Lord of Thiru-Rameswaram. You are the one with the deep moat, you are the one who resides in Thiru-Aalavaai. You are the one who wears the shining moon, O Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you are in my heart.

You are the one who is the jewel for the celestials, you are the Lord of Kailash. You are the one who dances to be seen, you are the Lord of Thiru-Veerattam in Kadavoor. You are the one who cut off the head of Brahma, you are the one who is the Lord of Thiru-Ottrriyur. You are the honey, you are the ambrosia, O Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you are in my heart. You are the one without father or mother, you are the Lord of Kailash. You are my father, my Lord, you are my Lord in Thiru-Ekambam.

You are the primordial three-eyed one, you are the one who resides in Thiru-Moovaloor. You are the one in my thoughts, the Lord of Thiru-Thennoor, O Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you are in my heart. You are the one who crushed the strength of Ravana, you are the one who resides in Kailash. You are the one who removes rebirth for those who renounce, you are the one who is the Lord of Thiru-Vizhimilalai. You are the one who is righteousness, who gave ambrosia, who consumed the poison that no one could bear, who controlled the five senses, O Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you are in my heart.

Now, the fifth Thiru-Pathikam by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for Thiru-Neythanam, the forty-second Thiru-Pathikam of the sixth Thiru-Murai. Thiru-Thandakam Thiru-Pathikam.

O foolish heart, listen to this: the five senses stand in this body, fulfilling their desires, and karma accumulates. This body is not eternal, it will perish. Do not say that there is a way to escape this. He is the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, whose consort has long, dark eyes, whose throat is stained with the poison from the ocean. If you think of him, you can be saved.

This body, which is not eternal, is a vessel for endless births. Do not say that there is a way to escape this, O heart, listen to me. He is the Lord of the celestials, who enslaved me on earth, who burned the three cities of the enemies, whom Brahma and Vishnu could not see. If you think of him as the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you can be saved. You who wander, seeking many things, and lie in this decaying body, thinking of this life as a home, O heart, abandon this thought and listen to me. The celestials, led by the sun god, countless crores of them, worship him.

If you think of him as the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you can be saved. O heart, do not fear, caught in this body, a vessel of endless karma, entangled in the bonds of desire, sinking into a life of degradation. He is the Lord who adorned his matted locks with the crescent moon, the cool Konrai flowers, and the Ganga. He is the steadfast one, praised by the celestials. If you think of him as the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you can be saved. O heart, abandon your arrogance, thinking that this body, which is as insignificant as a speck of dust, is a treasure, and that you can rule all these worlds.

He is the compassionate one who, for the sake of the celestials, bent his mighty bow and burned the three cities of the enemies with fire. If you think of him as the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you can be saved. O heart, do not be deluded by this fleeting life, thinking it is real, and sink into karma. He is the Lord who resides in the hearts of the humble, the father of Kumara, the one with the nature of a dancer, who holds a spear in his hand, whose anklets and bells on his holy feet resound as he dances. If you think of him as the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you can be saved. O heart, do not fall into the trap of worldly pleasures, thinking this birth is great, desiring the fragrant-haired maidens.

Come, he is the one who flayed the elephant, who smears himself with ashes, who wears the sacred thread, whom the wicked cannot approach. If you think of him as the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you can be saved. O heart, do not consider this body, which is afflicted by the five senses, a source of disease, as a refuge. O heart, do not fall, thinking of yourself as separate from him. He is the Lord with the blue throat, whom the deceitful cannot see, the Lord of the celestials. If you think of him as the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you can be saved.

O heart, do not desire this fleeting life, knowing that the soul will depart from this incompatible body. He is the Lord of the Himalayas, who, on that day, with his third eye, burned Kama, who came to disturb him, and destroyed the sacrifice of Daksha. If you think of him as the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, you can be saved. O heart, I have told you the truth about this body, which is not yours. Do not live without performing penance and austerities. He is the one who burned the three cities, the one with fire, the one with eight shoulders, our Lord.

If you think of him as the Lord of Thiru-Neythanam, who crushed the king of Lanka, If you think of him, you can be saved.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped Thiru-Neythanam, visited nearby Thiru-Perumpuliyoor and other sthalams, and sang Thiru-Pathikams. However, the Thiru-Pathikams sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for these sthalams are not available to us.

Thus, having worshipped many sthalams, he worshipped Thiru-Mazhapadi. Thiru-Mazhapadi is a sthalam very close to Thiru-Aiyaaru. The Lord’s holy name is Vairaththoonnathar, Vajrasthambeswarar, Vaidyanathar, Mazhuvaadeeswarar. The Goddess’s holy name is Sundarambikai, Azhagamai. The sthala-viruksham is the palm tree. The Theerthams are Kollidam, Lakshmi Theertham, Sivaganga Theertham, etc.

This is the sthalam where the Lord danced with an axe for Markandeya.

Therefore, the holy name Thiru-Mazhapadi came to this sthalam. This is the sthalam where the marriage of Nandi Devar and Suyasampikai Ammaiyar was performed. Purushamriga Rishi brought the Shiva Lingam from Brahmaloka and installed it here. When Brahma tried to remove it again, he could not, and he wondered if it was a diamond pillar.

Therefore, the Lord is known as Vairaththoonnathar and Vajrasthambeswarar. This is the sthalam where the Lord called Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, asking if he had forgotten to come to Mazhapadi.

Here, the holy marriage festival of Thiru-Nandiyemperuman is celebrated with great splendor every year on the Punarpoosam star day in the month of Panguni. The Kollidam river flows from south to north in this sthalam, as Uttaravahini. This sthalam has a mythological connection with the Sapthasthana sthalams surrounding Thiru-Aiyaaru. There is a sthala-puranam called Thiru-Mazhapadi Puranam, composed by Kamala Gnana- Kasara. When Sundaramoorthy Swamigal was residing in Thiru-Aalampozhil without visiting this sthalam, the Lord appeared in his dream at night and reminded him, asking if he had forgotten to come to Mazhapadi.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal then sang the Thiru-Pathikam “Ponnar Meniyane” and praised him, saying, “Whom else can I think of but you?” This is the sthalam where he came and worshipped. This sthalam has the glory of being sung by the three great saints. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, who visited this sthalam, has sung two Thiru-Pathikams. The first Thiru-Pathikam is the thirty-ninth Thiru-Pathikam of the sixth Thiru-Murai, the Thiru-Thandakam Thiru-Pathikam.

He is the one with the body adorned with water, behold! He is the one with a single eye on his forehead, who has taken Uma as half of his body, behold! He is the one with the throat stained by consuming deadly poison, behold! He is the one who rides the bull and wanders everywhere, behold! He is the one who became the seven worlds and the seven mountains, behold!

He is the one who destroyed the death of Markandeya, behold! He is the bridegroom who resides in Mazhapadi. He is the one with the skull of a crane, behold! He is the dancer who rides the bull, behold! He is the one who dances on the cremation ground, behold! He is the primordial one who holds fire in his hand, behold!

He is the one who wears the great serpent, behold! He is the ambrosia for his devotees, behold! He is the one with the Ganga in his matted locks, behold! He is the bridegroom who resides in Mazhapadi. He is the one with a single eye on his forehead, behold! He is the one who stands as half of the beautiful maiden, behold!

He is the one who dances with the serpent, behold! He is the supreme one who begs for alms in many towns, behold! He is the one who destroyed the three small cities, behold! He is the one who placed the beautiful moon on his head, behold! He is the one who is without any fault, behold! He is the bridegroom who resides in Mazhapadi.

He is the one with the Ganga in his matted locks, behold! He is the one who stands beyond the universe, behold! He is the one who crushed the cruel Yama, behold! He is the one who wears the skin of a fierce tiger, behold! He is the one who destroyed the cities with his bow, behold! He is the one who placed the beautiful moon on his head, behold!

He is the bridegroom of the mountain maiden, behold! He is the bridegroom who resides in Mazhapadi. He is the one who wears the bones of the deceased, behold! He is the one who performed many miracles with joy, behold! He is the one with the Konrai flowers in his matted locks, behold! He is the one who became the four Vedas and the six Angas, behold!

He is the one who holds the skull as a vessel, behold! He is the Lord of the celestials, behold! He is the bridegroom who resides in Mazhapadi, who placed his holy feet on the heads of those who blossomed. He is the one who cut off the head of Brahma, behold! He is the one who resides in the hearts of the virtuous, behold! He is the one praised by Brahma, behold!

He is the one who stands as the essence of union, behold! He is the one who holds a powerful bow, behold! He is the Lord with the dark throat, behold! He is the one who holds a deer in his hand, behold! He is the bridegroom who resides in Mazhapadi. He is the one who became water and the great mountains, behold!

He is the one who became the shadow and the vast sky, behold! He is the one who became the earth and the seven oceans, behold! He is the one who became day and the sky, behold! He is the one who is the father of his devotees, behold! He is the one who became the atom and the primordial one, behold! He is the one with the breasted maiden as half, behold!

He is the bridegroom who resides in Mazhapadi. He is the one with a golden body, behold! He is the one who wears a garland of Konrai flowers, behold! He is the Lord with shining matted locks, behold! He is the one who desired and wore the skin of the elephant, behold! He is the one who has no equal, behold!

He is the one who stands as Shiva, whom no one can know, behold! He is the one with the steadfast maiden as half, behold! He is the bridegroom who resides in Mazhapadi. He is the one who consumed the deadly poison with joy, He is the primordial one, behold! He is the one who shot the three cities of the enemies, behold! He is the one who kicked Yama with his foot, behold!

He is the youth who blessed Kannappar, behold! He is the one with the sweet-speaking maiden as half, behold! He is the one who rides the bull and wanders, behold! He is the mighty one whom Vishnu could not know, behold! He is the bridegroom who resides in Mazhapadi. He is the one who became a single light and the seven worlds, behold!

He is the one who stands as the inner meaning of Omkara, behold! He is the one who became the spreading light and the shining sound, behold! He is the one who became the sound of festivals and sacrifices, behold! He is the one who crushed the twenty shoulders of the king of Lanka, who was beyond the two lights, behold! He is the ruby mountain that shines again, behold! He is the bridegroom who resides in Mazhapadi.

The second Thiru-Pathikam by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for Thiru-Mazhapadi, the fortieth Thiru-Pathikam of the sixth Thiru-Murai, the Thiru-Thandakam Thiru-Pathikam.

He is the Lord who consumed the poison from the vast ocean as ambrosia and protected the celestials, He is like the wealthy one who took a golden bow, strung it with fire, and burned the three cities. I cry out, saying, “O Diamond Pillar of Mazhapadi, which stands firm with gold, pearls, and diamonds!” The celestials praise him in the sky with the sound of the lute and the lyre. He is the one who, with the Vedas, sacred water, and mantras, granted them the celestial world. I cry out, saying, “O Diamond Pillar of Mazhapadi, which is like a mighty diamond pillar in Kacchi, surrounded by groves, and in the city of Mazhapadi, surrounded by tall mansions!” He is the one who, having destroyed the wicked, the ignorant, the evil-mouthed Jains, and having enslaved me, is like a coral pillar, a golden pearl. He is the one who, having destroyed the wicked, and having made the evil Kama serpent his banner, grants boons to those who worship him.

I cry out, saying, “O Diamond Pillar of Mazhapadi!” He is the one who, having taken the flesh-eating, naked, evil-mouthed Jains as his relatives, and having enslaved me, a dog, as his possession, is the king who wears the white water of the ocean, the Lord of the celestials. I cry out, saying, “O Diamond Pillar of Mazhapadi, which is like a cloud in the sky!” He is the one who destroyed the head of Brahma and the head of Vishnu, who crushed the teeth of the sun, who restored the shining arts of the moon, who rides the bull, who wears the serpent, the one praised by the four Vedas. I cry out, saying, “O Diamond Pillar of Mazhapadi, who grants boons!” He is the one who, though angry, is small and great. I fell into the evil deeds of the wicked Jains, who have corrupt minds. I, who am without senses, who am like a wild pig, who am without a body, he enslaved me as his possession, and gave me the path of compassion, abandoning their ways. I cry out, saying, “O Diamond Pillar of Mazhapadi, which is fragrant!” He is the Lord with matted locks, who removes the sorrow of rebirth, who is pure.

He is my Lord, my master, whom Brahma and Vishnu could not see, the sun, the fruit of the Vedas. I cry out, saying, “O Diamond Pillar of Mazhapadi, who is the companion on the path!” In this Thiru-Pathikam, the eighth, ninth, and tenth verses are not available to us.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped Thiru-Mazhapadi, reaches Thiru-Poondurutthi, a sthalam where Shiva resides. Let us proceed with our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 460. Thirunindracharukkam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman proceeds to the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Poonthuruthi. This sthalam, Thiru-Poonthuruthi, is a very important sthalam in the sacred history of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman.

Appar Swamigal, who would sing praises of the Lord of each sthalam he visited, perform sacred service, and then immediately proceed to another sthalam, established a sacred monastery in Thiru-Poonthuruthi and stayed there for a long time. Such a special sthalam is Thiru-Poonthuruthi, located very close to the Thiru-Vaiyaaru sthalam in Tamil Nadu. This is one of the Sapthasthana sthalams of Thiru-Vaiyaaru. The sacred names of the Lord are Pushpavaneswarar, Adhipuranar, Poiyiliyar. The sacred name of the Goddess is Soundarya Nayaki. The sthala-vrikshams are the Bilva tree, Banyan tree, and Vanni tree.

The sacred waters are Kashyapa Theertham and Surya Theertham. In common parlance, it is currently called Thiruppanthuruthi. Villages located in riverine islands, that is, between two rivers, are named Thuruthi. This sthalam is named Thiru-Poonthuruthi because it is located between the Kaveri River and the Kudamurutti River. This is the sacred birthplace of Poonthuruthi Kadava Nambi, one of the authors of the Ninth Thirumurai. In this sthalam, the Nandi is displaced.

This is the sacred sthalam where Appar Peruman carried the palanquin of Thirugnanasambandha Peruman on his shoulder. We are about to witness this history. The sacred monastery established by Appar Swamigal is here. The Durga idol, standing on one leg performing penance to absolve the sin of slaying Mahishasura, is a very special idol, in a seated posture. Appar Peruman grants darshan. The sacred form of Poonthuruthi Kadava Nambi is also very specially arranged.

Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having reached this sacred place, entered it with great desire, and approaching the temple where the Lord is graciously present, performing the divine dance, circumambulated and worshipped. He bowed low before his Lord, and with an overflowing, unceasing love, tears rained down, and he reached a state of self-forgetfulness. He then composed a Thiruthandakam, filled with devotion, stating, “I saw Poiyili, the Lord with the red matted locks, who graciously resides in Thiru-Poonthuruthi, the Lord who comes upon the great mountain, Anneroy.” He also composed a Thiruppathikam with the sentiment, “Let us be at the sacred feet.” Thus, at this point, Sekkizhar Swamigal mentions two Thiruppathikams sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman with notes. Of the total three Thiruppathikams composed by Appar Swamigal for the Thiru-Poonthuruthi sthalam, Sekkizhar Swamigal mentions two Thiruppathikams in this sacred verse. Sekkizhar Swamigal first mentions the Thiruthandakam Thiruppathikam, which has the concluding phrase “I myself saw Poiyili in Poonthuruthi” in every verse.

Next, Sekkizhar Swamigal mentions the Thiruppathikam beginning with “Kodi Kol.” In this Thiruppathikam, Appar Swamigal has sung with the concluding phrase in every verse, “Let us be at the sacred feet of the Lord residing in Thiru-Poonthuruthi.” Of these two Thiruppathikams, the first Thiruppathikam is the 43rd Thiruppathikam of the Sixth Thirumurai, a Thiruthandaka Thiruppathikam.

aalaakkondu pollaaven noytheerththa punithan thannai punniyanai poonthuruththik kanden naane Kutraalam kokaranam mevinanai kodungai kadungutrai paainthaa thannai utraala nanjudodukkinanai unara ven punithan thannai poiyiliyai poonthuruththi kande naane aarththaanai vaasugiyai araikkor kachchaa asaiththaanai azhagaaya ponnaarmenai pooththaanaththaan mudiyai porunthaavannam punarnthaanai viththaanai venditru ondru eevaan thannai vinnavartham perumaanai vinaigal poga uythaanai olikangai sadaimelthaangi ozhiththaanai oru paagathu umaiyodu aange poiththaanai punniyanai punithan thannai poiyiliyai poonthuruththi kanden naane aandaanai vaanorulagamellaam annaal ariyaatha thakkan velvi meendaanai vinnavargalodum koodi virai malarmel naanmuganum maalum theda neendaanai neruppuruvamaan Now, the next Thiruppathikam is the 32nd Thiruppathikam of the Fifth Thirumurai, a Thirukkurunthogai Thiruppathikam.

Kodigol selva vizha gunalaiyaraa kadigol poompozhil kachchi ekampanaar podigal poosiya poonthuruththin nagar adigal sevadi keezh naam iruppathe aarththa tholudai kattiyor vedanaay paarththanodu padaithodumaagilum pooththa neezh pozhil poonthuruththin nagar theerththan sevadi keezh naam iruppathe maathinai mathiththaanor paagamaaga kaathalaar karanthaan sadai kangaiyai poothanaayakan poonthuruththin nagar kaathi sevadi keezh naam iruppathe moovanaay muthalaay ivvulagalaam kaavanaay kadungaalanai kaaynthaavan poovinaayakan poonthuruththin nagar devan sevadi keezh naam iruppathe semponne okkum meniyan thesaththil umpar aar avarodu angu irukkalum pon ponnaar selva poonthuruththin nagar nampan sevadi keezh naam iruppathe vallampeesi valisai moonruri moonrurinai kollampeesi kodunjjaram noorinaan pullampeesiyum poonthuruththin nagar selvan sevadi keezh naam iruppathe oruththanaay ula thozhanindru paruththa paampodu paanmathi kangaiyum poruththanagilum poonthuruththin nagar thiruththan sevadi keezh naam iruppathe athirar thevar iyakkara vichchaaththar karutha nindravar kaanparithaayinaan poruthaneervaru poonthuruththin nagar sathuran sevadi keezh naam iruppathe sethugaraa manaththaar purang kurinum kothugaraa kanninonpigal kurinum pothuvin naayakan poonthuruththin nagar athivan sevadi keezh naam iruppathe thudiththa tholvazhi vaazharakkanthanai pidiththa kaingerinthutrana kannellaam podikka oondriya poonthuruththin nagar padigol sevadi keezh naam iruppathe Thiruchitrambalam.

Thus, Sekkizhar Swamigal mentions that these two Thiruppathikams were sung.

Furthermore, the third Thiruppathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for the Thiru-Poonthuruthi sthalam is the 88th Thiruppathikam of the Fourth Thirumurai, a Thiru-Virutham Thiruppathikam.

maalinai maalura nindraan malaimagal thannudaiya paalanai paanmathisoodiyai panpunaraar mathin merpolanai porvidai eriyai poonthuruththi magizhum aalanai aathi puraananai naan adi potruvathae maruththavar mummadil maayavor venjil koththor ampaal aruththanai aalathankeezhanai aazhvidamundathanai poruththanai poothappadaiyanai poonthuruththi uraiyum niraththanai neelamidatranai yaan adi potruvathae uruvinai oozhi muthalvanai othi niraintha nindra thiruvinai thesamadaiththanai sendradainththudaiya poruvinai ellaamthoranththanai poonthuruththi uraiyum karuvinai kanmoonru udaiyanai yaan adi potruvathae thakkan than velvi thagarththavan saara mathuvandru kol mikkanam mummadil veeyavor venjilai koththor ampaal pukkanan pon thigazhntha annathor poonthuruththi uraiyum nakkanai nangal piraan thanai naan adi potruvathae arugadai maalaiyum thaanudaiyaan azhagaal amaintha uruvudai mangaiyum thannor paal ulagaayu nindraan porupadai velinan villinan poonthuruththi uraiyum thiruvudai thesamathiyanai yaan adi potruvathae mandriyun nindra mathilarai maaya vagaikkedukka kandriyum nindru kadunjilai vaangi kanal ampinnaal pondriyum poga purattinan poonthuruththi uraiyum andriyum seytha piraan thanai yaan adi potruvathae min niramikka idai umai nangaiyorpaan magizhnthaan en niram endru amarar periyaarin nanthamaariyaar ponniramikka sadaiyavan poonthuruththi uraiyum en nira enthai piraan thannai yaan adi potru vathae anthiyai nalla mathiyinai yaarukkum arivariya senthiyai vaattum semponninai sendradainththudaiya punthiyai pukka arivinai poonthuruththi uraiyum nanthiyai nangal piraanthannai naan adi potruvathae pai kaiyum paanthi velikkaiyum paampu sadaiyidaiye vaikkaiyum vaanili gangaiyum mangai nadungurave moikai arakkanai oondrina poonthuruththi uraiyum mikka nalveda vigithanai naan adi potruvathae Thiruchitrambalam. Our contemplation continues. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 461. Thirunindracharukkam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We saw that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman worshipped the Lord in Thiru-Poonthuruthi and composed three Thiruppathikams. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, when visiting other sthalams, would have darshan of those sthalams and then proceed to the next sthalam.

But here, in Thiru-Poonthuruthi, he stayed for a long time and performed sacred service. He praised the Lord with the Thiruppathikam, “Let us be at the sacred feet.” Therefore, the Lord also blessed him accordingly.

Lord Shiva granted grace for Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to establish a sacred monastery in Thiru-Poonthuruthi and reside there. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, a fully detached ascetic, requested the Lord for the ability to establish a sacred monastery in Thiru-Poonthuruthi and reside there.

Therefore, the note here is that he established the sacred monastery only after receiving divine grace that the attachment arising from residing in such a monastery would not affect him.

Furthermore, in accordance with the Thiruvachakam, “If there is anything more to be desired, that too is not your wish,” the very thought of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to establish a sacred monastery in Thiru-Poonthuruthi was also due to divine grace. This is also the meaning here.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman establishes a sacred monastery in Thiru-Poonthuruthi. He establishes the sacred monastery and resides there, performing sacred service.
