This is an act that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman did not perform in any other sacred sthalam. Sekkizhar Peruman sings, “Desiring to reside there, he composed the Thiru-Virutham, a song of rich Tamil, praising ‘Let us be at the sacred feet,’ and stayed there, performing sacred service, having received the grace of the Lord.” Sekkizhar Peruman sings, “He built a sacred monastery there, where the moon and sun touch.” Sekkizhar Swamigal sings of the sacred monastery established by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman as a sacred monastery touched by the moon and sun. This indicates the greatness of that sacred monastery.

Sekkizhar Peruman sings that there is a spacious sacred courtyard in that monastery, where at night the moon and during the day the sun spread their light and warmth, performing service. Sekkizhar Swamigal mentions that it is the sacred monastery where Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman resided. In Saiva tradition, a sacred monastery is called a Thirumadam, a place where acharyas reside. Sekkizhar Swamigal sings, “He built a sacred monastery there.” Here, “one” does not refer to a number, but rather signifies “unique.” This sacred monastery established by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is a unique sacred monastery. This sacred monastery possesses a special greatness, having been established by our Saiva Paramacharya.

We do not hear of similar monasteries established and resided in by religious acharyas in any other religion. We see that monasteries named after them were established by later generations in memory of those acharyas.

However, in this sacred monastery, our Acharya Murthigal, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, resided for a long time and performed Shiva Puja, Shiva Gnana Yoga, and other penances. Even today, the places where Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman performed puja and sat in yoga can be identified in Thiru-Poonthuruthi. If one visits Thiru-Poonthuruthi, one can have darshan of this and receive divine grace.

Furthermore, this sacred monastery has another special feature. The third meeting of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman is about to take place in Thiru-Poonthuruthi. After such a meeting, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman resided in this sacred monastery for many days, sitting together and conversing. The special experience of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman establishing Saivism in the southern land of Tamil Nadu, and the special experience of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman traveling to the northern land of Thondai Nadu and beyond to the northern regions, and later having darshan of Thiru-Kailai, these two Nayanmars shared their divine experiences with each other while residing in this sacred monastery. This is a unique specialty of this sacred monastery.

Thus, as they shared their experiences of divine grace, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman begins his pilgrimage to Thondai Nadu. It is during this journey to Thondai Nadu that the divine events of resurrecting the girl Angampoombai and later proceeding to the wedding in Achchal are about to unfold in the sacred history.

Similarly, when Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman recounted the experiences of divine grace in Pandya Nadu to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman while residing in this sacred monastery, the desire to visit Pandya Nadu, the land of Tamil Nadu, arose in the heart of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. The pilgrimage of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to Pandya Nadu is now about to take place.

Thus, this sacred monastery serves as an important place in the Periya Puranam. The meeting of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is yet to happen.

However, this event will take place after a very long time, that is, about a year after Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman arrived in Thiru-Poonthuruthi and established the sacred monastery, the arrival of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and the meeting of these two great personalities will occur.

Therefore, our Saiva elders believe that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman must have resided in the sacred monastery in Thiru-Poonthuruthi for at least one year, performing sacred service.

Thus, for such a long period, in no other sthalam did Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman reside, and this is also a point to note here. During this period of residence, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman composed many Thiruppathikams. Sekkizhar Peruman describes them as follows: “He composed various Thandakams, unique Thandakams, Adaippu Thiruthandakams that describe the places where the Lord, who removes suffering, graciously resides, and Thiru-Angamalai that praises to show the path to salvation, and countless other collections of hymns, and praised.” Here, Sekkizhar Swamigal mentions the Thiruppathikams of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. He states that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman composed various Thandakams, unique Thandakams that praise the Lord, Adaippu Thiruthandakams that describe the places where Lord Shiva, who removes the suffering of birth, graciously resides, and Thiru-Angamalai that praises to show the path to salvation for living beings. And also, Sekkizhar Swamigal mentions that he composed countless other collections of hymns.

Thus, during the times he resided in the sacred monastery in Thiru-Poonthuruthi, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman composed many Thiruppathikams for the salvation of this world. Sekkizhar Swamigal has mentioned the names of these Thiruppathikams as various Thiruthandakam, Thanithandakam, Adaippu Thiruthandakam, Thiru-Angamalai, and also states that he composed many more such hymns. The signs of the small room where Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar sat in Shivayoga in that sacred monastery are still visible today.

Thus, the Thiruppathikams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman are generally general Thiruppathikams and many other Thiruppathikams, as written by Sivakavimani Ayyavargal. In that regard, the Thiruppathikams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman are various Thiruthandaka Thiruppathikams, Thani Thiruthandaka Thiruppathikams, Adaippu Thiruthandaka Thiruppathikams, and Thiru-Angamalai Thiruppathikams. These are the Thiruthandaka Thiruppathikams found in the Sixth Thirumurai.

Now, similarly, Thirukkurunthogai Thiruppathikams, Thani Kurunthogai Thiruppathikams, Podhu Thani Thirukkurunthogai Thiruppathikam, Kaalapaasa Thirukkurunthogai, Marakkirpanae enum Thirukkurunthogai Thiruppathikam, Thozhirpaalathae enum Thirukkurunthogai Thiruppathikam, Linga Purana Thirukkurunthogai Thiruppathikam, Manathogai Thirukkurunthogai Thiruppathikam, Siththathogai Thirukkurunthogai Thiruppathikam, Ullathogai Thirukkurunthogai Thiruppathikam, Adhi Purana Thirukkurunthogai Thiruppathikam, these are the Thiruppathikams. We will look at these Thiruppathikams one by one.

First, the Thiruppathikam named Palavagai Thiruthandakam. This Thiruppathikam contains the note that by meditating on the Sapthasthana sthalams, which are the seven great sthalams including Thiru-Vaiyaaru, and some other sthalams, and by chanting their sacred names as mantras, one can overcome the suffering of birth and attain liberation. It speaks of the sacred name as a great mantra. This Thiruppathikam is called a general Thiruppathikam and a Palavagai Thiruthandaka Thiruppathikam because it does not cling to any one sthalam and generally preaches many ideas. Such a Thiruppathikam. The Sixth Thiru-murai, ninety-third Thiru-pathikam, Thiru-thandaka Thiru-pathikam.

Having seen the Lord with a woman as half of His body, and seeing Him with a thousand faces, His stability wavered. Seeing Him with a serpent on His matted locks, and the crescent moon, the Lord who possesses these, the Thiru-thondar who purified their minds and protected them, before their single staff faltered. If you say “Poonthuruthi, Poonthuruthi,” there, if you enter, no one will give you anything. You who live happily in the illusory household life with women of dark eyes, and the ancient moon with a hood. The serpent and water on His matted locks, the Lord who delights in this, if you say “Neythanam, Neythanam,” can you not remove the fleshly impurity?

You who live thinking of yourselves as those who have hands and senses, who speak falsely and rise in the morning seeking wealth. The blue-throated Lord who bathed in ghee, with a third eye on His forehead, and matted locks, if you say “Aiyaare, Aiyaare,” you can rule the heavenly world. If one does not gain anything, the mother, father, wife, and children who gave birth to them, are not a refuge. You who live thinking of yourselves as those who have abandoned the chariot. If you say “Pazhanam, Pazhanam,” the Lord who removes our sins, makes us righteous, and rules the heavenly world, can remove the diseases of old karma that have arisen. You who are in the nine-holed body, you will not realize when it is closed.

Before the other path opens, you who live happily in the illusory household life. If you say “Sotrutthurai, Sotrutthurai,” the Lord who caused the three cities of those who performed other deeds to fall into the fierce fire, you can be freed from sorrow and attain the pure path. In the black ocean that churns the world, O mind, do not drown in the deceitful ocean and waste away. If you desire bliss, if you praise the feet of the Lord, the Lord who is the essence of the Vedas and their branches, who is in the temple of the Lord who removes sorrow, if you say “Valanjuzhiye, Valanjuzhiye,” your strong karmas will be removed, and you can rule the heavens. Thandi, Kundotharan, Pingirudi, the renowned Nandi, Sanku, Kannan, the one who created the ancient world, and the one who was immersed in the rock, all sing praises. The small ghost with a big belly sings some songs, and the one who rides the red-eyed bull, if you say “Kandiyoor, Kandiyoor,” you can quickly remove your strong karmas.

O mind, do not think of the poisonous serpent, but of the white bull. When you see the Lord’s sacred feet, like the great sages of the north, go and worship Him.

The Lord who is in the minds of the great ascetics, the Lord with the axe, the Lord who is like a serpent with a hood, and Brahma on the lotus, cannot see Him. If you say “Kudamookke, Kudamookke,” your evil karmas will be removed, and you can approach the Lord.

The Lord who resides in Thiru-venkadu, where the pure water is like a dark womb, where the beautiful women of Kanchi with dark peacock-like complexions gather and see Him, where He dances in the night, emitting fire, standing in the forest that cannot be seen. Who are born, who are wives, who are children, who are they? What is this illusion? Do not rejoice in this. Listen to what I tell you. Those who weep saying “Whose Thiru-namam is this?” with the shining moon and life in their heads, can remain.

In the first nine verses of this Thiru-pathikam, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman sings about the names of nine Thiru-sthalams, and how great the benefits are if one merely utters the sacred names of those Thiru-sthalams. If you say “Poonthuruthi, Poonthuruthi,” you can remove the evil. He says, “You can remove the fleshly bag.” He sings that if we merely utter the name of that Thalam, Thiru-poonthuruthi, Thiru-poonthuruthi, we can shed this body that is like a bag filled with air and flesh. He sings, “If you say Neythanam, Neythanam, you can remove the fleshly impurity.” He sings that if we merely utter the name of that Thalam, Thiru-neythanam, Thiru-neythanam, we can shed this body made of flesh. In the third verse, he sings, “You can rule the heavenly world.” He says that by doing so, the suffering of birth will end, and one can go to the world of Shiva.

In the fourth verse, he says, “If you say Pazhanam, Pazhanam, you can remove the diseases of old karma that have arisen.” He says that merely by saying Thiru-pazhanam, all our old karmas will be removed. He sings, “If you say Sotrutthurai, Sotrutthurai, you can be freed from sorrow and attain the pure path.” He says that merely by saying Thiru-sotrutthurai, Thiru-sotrutthurai, you can be freed from the sorrow of birth and attain the pure path of liberation. He sings, “If you say Valanjuzhiye, Valanjuzhiye, your strong karmas will be removed, and you can rule the heavens.” He says that merely by saying Thiru-valanjuzhi, Thiru-valanjuzhi, all strong karmas will be removed, and you can rule the heavenly world. He sings, “If you say Kandiyoor, Kandiyoor, you can quickly remove your strong karmas.” He says that merely by saying Thiru-kandiyoor, Thiru-kandiyoor, you can quickly remove your karmas. He says, “If you say Kudamookke, Kudamookke, your evil karmas will be removed, and you can approach the Lord.”

He says that if you utter the sacred name of Thiru-kudamookku, Thiru-kumbakonam, you can be united with Shiva, who is a refuge. He sings, “If you say Venkade, Venkade, Venkade, you can remove the diseases of strong karmas that do not leave.” He says that merely by saying Thiru-venkadu, Thiru-venkadu, the diseases of strong karmas will be destroyed. After saying all this, in the tenth verse, he speaks of the greatness of the Thiru-mantram “Namashivaya.” Who is one’s father, who is one’s mother, who are one’s siblings, who is one’s wife, who are one’s children? Were we united with these relatives? We were not. Even after we leave this world, will we be united with them?

We will not.

Therefore, O people of the world, do not rejoice in this false connection. Do not be elated. I will tell you a certainty, listen. Chant the sacred name of Shiva, “Namashivaya,” the Sri Panchaksharam. Chant it day and night. For those who sleep while chanting the Sri Panchaksharam, and those who wake up while chanting it, a great world of liberation awaits.

You can remain established in that world of liberation.

Therefore, do that, he preaches in the tenth sacred verse. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman.

Now, let us continue to contemplate the other Thiru-pathikams. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 462, Thiru-nindra-cherukkam, Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We are contemplating the general Thiru-pathikams sung by Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar in Thiru-poonthuruthi. In that context, the second general Thiru-pathikam is the ninety-fifth Thiru-pathikam in the Sixth Thiru-murai. Many of the verses in this Thiru-pathikam are known to everyone. This Thiru-pathikam, which begins with “Appan Nee Ammai Nee,” is a Thiru-thandaka Thiru-pathikam.

“Appan Nee Ammai Nee Anbudaiya Mamamum Mamiyum Nee Oppudaiya Madharum Onporulum Nee Oru Kulamum Sutramum Oorum Nee Thuyppanavum Uyppanavum Thotruvai.” You are the one who creates what is enjoyed and what is saved. You are the one who dwells in the heart as a helper. You are this gold, this earth, and the pearl. You are the Lord.

You are the wealthy one who rides the bull. Death will not come near us. The fierce karmas and enemies will not approach us. We are free from ignorance. We have no equals. We are not those who rise with the sun.

The Lord with the red coral-like matted locks, who wears the Ganges, who dances with fire, who delights in bathing with the five products of the cow, the Lord of red coral color, the Lord of red mountain color, the Lord of red sky color, is in my thoughts. Who will not dance if He makes them dance? Who will not be subdued if He subdues them? Who will not run if He makes them run? Who will not melt if He makes them melt? Who will not sing if He makes them sing?

Who will not bow if He makes them bow? Who will not see if He makes them see? Who can see, O Lord with the eye on your forehead, if you do not show? The good ones, the good path, the form of knowledge, the bright light, the one who stands beyond the words of the four Vedas, the one who stands beyond the words, the one who is difficult to describe, this is your nature. The wish-fulfilling tree that entered and remained in the unstable mind, in the unstable fleshly body, I will not leave you, O Lord of golden and precious gem-like color. O Lord, without a temple, without wearing sacred ash, without a great devotion, without singing, without many temples, without blowing the white conch with desire, without banners and white flags, without plucking flowers and offering them, all those places are not towns, but wild forests.

If they do not utter the five-letter sacred name, if they do not speak of the Lord of fire even once, if they never circumambulate the temple, if they do not pluck flowers and offer them before eating, if they do not wear sacred ash to remove great diseases, why were those wretched ones born? Why were they born? Great diseases afflict them greatly, and they are born to die, and they die. You became yourself, without anyone else. You became a seed in the minds of those who think of you. You became the king, you became the nectar for kings.

You became the four Vedas, you became the six angas. You became gold, you became a gem, you became bliss. You are the worthy object on earth. What did you become for me? What did I become? What else can I, a poor one, say but you?

O Father, you embraced your servant with love, you bathed me in the holy water of your merciful gaze. You are so rare, yet you became simple and accepted me. You accepted me. I am mad, foolish, a ghost, a dog. You forgave all my mistakes. Is all this for us?

Alas, alas, how great is the grace of our Lord! My lineage is bad, my character is bad, my aim is bad. I have many faults. My beauty is bad, I am bad, I am not a sage. I do not associate with good people. I am not a good person, nor am I not a good person.

I can speak many hateful things. I am bad at giving, I cannot give. Why was I born, a poor one? If you give the two treasures of Sankhanidhi and Padmanidhi, and the earth and the sky, We will not value the wealth of those who perish, if they are not lovers of the great Lord. Even if they are untouchables who are afflicted with leprosy, whose limbs are decaying, who skin cows and eat them, if they are devotees of the Lord who hides the Ganges in His matted locks, they are the gods whom we worship.

This is that unique Thiru-thandakam. The note on this Thiru-pathikam is as follows: All living beings are under the control of Shiva and are moved by Him. The towns where people do not wear sacred ash and do not sing praises to Shiva with devotion are all cremation grounds. If one asks why those who do not wear sacred ash and do not worship Shiva were born, it is because great diseases afflict them, and they are born to die and die. They were born to die and be born again.

Those who do not associate with good people, who are Shiva’s devotees, and who do not speak Shiva’s sacred words, why were they born? No matter how wealthy they are, if they are not Shiva’s devotees, we will not consider them as anything. If they are lovers of Shiva, we will worship them as God. O Shiva, you are our father, mother, uncle, aunt, and all precious things. O wish-fulfilling tree, I will not leave you. O Lord, you are always in my thoughts.

O worthy object on earth, you became gold, gems, earth, and everything for me. What else do I, a poor one, know but to praise you in this way? What else can I say to praise you? You embraced me, a dog-like servant, with love, and bathed me in the holy water of your merciful gaze. You came to us as a very simple one, showed mercy, and accepted us. You forgave all the mistakes I, a dog, made.

Is all this for us? Alas, alas, how great is your divine grace! Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman sings with melting devotion in this Thiru-pathikam.

Now, the next Thiru-pathikam is the Thiru-pathikam known as Adaivu Thiru-thandaka Thiru-pathikam. This is the seventy-first Thiru-pathikam in the Sixth Thiru-murai. It is given the special name Adaivu Thiru-thandakam. Adaivu means fame, a place worthy of refuge. The suffering of birth, The places where souls, fearing suffering, come to take refuge are the sacred places where Shiva has manifested. This pathikam is called Adaivu Thiru-thandakam because it compiles and categorizes all these sacred places.

Therefore, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman has woven together the sacred names of all the sacred places where Shiva has manifested in this pathikam.

Now, that pathikam.

“Poruppalli Varaivilla Puramoonru Eythu Pulanthaliya Salantharanai Pilanthan Porchakkarappalli Thiru-kattuppalli Kallar Kamal Kolli Araippalli Kalavanjara Sirappalli Sivappalli Semponpalli Sezhunanippalli Thavappalli Seerar Parappalli” — all those who utter these names will happily reside in the heavenly world. “Kaviri-yin Karai Kandi Veerattanam Kadavur Veerattanam.” The beautiful Thiru-athikai-meya Veerattanam, Vazhuvai Veerattanam, the vast Pariyala Veerattanam, Kovalanagar Veerattanam, the abode of the bull-rider, Kurukkai Veerattanam, Kothittaikkudi Veerattanam – if you utter these names with your tongue, when the messengers of Yama come near, they will retreat, saying, “These are Shiva’s devotees.” The Lord who raised the bull on the good banner, Sembankudi, Nallakkudi, Nalinattiyathankudi, Karkkudi, Thenkalakkudi, Sengattankudi, Karunthittaikkudi, Kadaiyakkudi – when you see them, Virkudi, Velvikudi, Nalvettakkudi, Vedikudi, Manikkudi, Vidaippaykudi, Purkudi, Madithevan Kudi, Nilakkudi, Pudukkudi – if you praise them, your troubles will surely go away.

The Lord with the crescent moon on His matted locks, Arur, Perumparrappuliyur, Peravur, Naraiyur, Nallur, Ur, Nallatrur, Nalur, Sottrur, Naraiyur, Uraiyur, Ottur, Uttrattur, Alappur, Omampuliyur, Ottriyur, Turaiyur, Tuvaiyur, Tolur, Tudaiyur – if you worship these, troubles will not follow you.

The Lord who adorned His matted locks with the great river, the great temples, seventy-eight of them, and also Karakkoil, the temples surrounded by beautiful groves, Karuppariyal, the temples like mountains, Kokudikkoyil, the temples where the Brahmins worship by chanting the Vedas, Ilankoyil, Manikkoyil, Alakkoyil, Thiru-koyil – if you circumambulate and bow down to Shiva’s temples, your evil karmas will surely be removed.

The Lord who resides with the daughter of the mountain, Maraikkadu, the beautiful groves surrounding Talaichankadu, Talaiyalankadu, the vast ocean surrounding Anthan Saikkadu, the clear water of Kollikkadu, the much-praised Pazhaiyanur, Alankadu, Panangadu, Kadu, Venkadu, where women play and dive in the pond to remove their sins, if you approach these, your karmas will be different.

The Lord with the eye on His forehead, who removed the cruel ones and accepted me, His abode is Annalvayil, Neduvayil, Neythalvayil surrounded by many fields, the manifested Mullaippayil, and Ngalilvayil. Maduvar Then Madurai Nagar Alavayil, the ocean-surrounded Punalvayil, the tall Kudavayil, Kunavayil – all those who enter these will not be afflicted by evil karmas. Nanthikeswaram, Mahakaleswaram, Nageswaram, Nagaleswaram, the good Koteeswaram, Kondiswaram, Tindiswaram, Kukkudeswaram, Makkiswaram – when we speak of them, Adakeswaram, Mahatheeswaram, Amayaneeswaram, Agatheeswaram, Sittheeswaram, the beautiful Kaanal, the great Rameswaram with its waves – by praising and worshipping these, We will speak of many sacred places. Kanthamathanam, Kailasa Malai, Ketharam, Kalathi, Kazhukkundram, Kannar Anna, the beautiful groves of Vadaparpatham, Mahendra Malai, Neelam, Hemakoodam, Vindha Malai, the great Podhigai Malai made by Brahma, Meru, Udayamatham, and other mountains where the moon-crested Lord resides – we will praise them, and praise them from the midst of our troubles. Nallar, Pazhaiyar, Kottatrodu, Nalanthigalum, Nalarum, Thiru-vaiyaru, Thellarum, Valaikkulam, Thalikkulam, Nalidaikkulam, Thiru-kkulathodu, Anjaikkalam, Villatha Nedunkalam, Vetkalam, Nellikka, Kolakka, Anaika, Viyan Kodikka, the Lord with the Konrai flower on His matted locks, the rivers and ponds where He resides – we will speak of all these. The one who lifted Kailasa Malai, with his hands and heads, the path of his fingers.

We worship all the Thiru-thurais (sacred river banks) where the Lord resides: Thiru-paraitthurai, Thiru-then-palaitthurai, Thiru-pandazhuvar, Thiru-thavaththurai, Thiru-ven-thurai, Thiru-paimbozhil, Thiru-kuyil-aalan-thurai, Thiru-sotru-thurai, Thiru-poon-thurai, Thiru-perun-thurai, Thiru-kurangaadu-thurai, Thiru-mayilaadu-thurai, Thiru-kadamban-thurai, and Thiru-aavaduthurai.

Let us continue to contemplate the other general Thiru-pathigams (sacred hymns) composed by Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 463, Thiru-nindra-charukkam, Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We are contemplating the general Thiru-pathigams composed by Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman at Thiru-poonthuruthi. In that vein, the next Thiru-pathigam is the Thiru-angamaalai Thiru-pathigam, which begins with “Thalaiyae Nee Vanangaay” (O Head, you worship). This Thiru-pathigam is so highly regarded among Shiva’s devotees that it is said there are no devotees who have not recited or studied it. It teaches that all the external and internal organs of the human body were given to living beings for the purpose of worshipping Lord Shiva and attaining well-being.

Therefore, this Thiru-pathigam illustrates how each of these organs should worship to gain strength. This is the essence of this Thiru-pathigam. This is what is meant by: He refers to it as the “Thiru-angamaalai that praises and shows the path to salvation for the great Lord within.” He specifically explains this Thiru-pathigam as the “Thiru-angamaalai that praises and shows the path to salvation.” Such is the Thiru-angamaalai Thiru-pathigam, the ninth Thiru-pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-murai, set to the tune of Sadhaari.

“Thalaiyae nee vanangaay, thalaivanai; kankaaL kaaNmin kaLoo, kadal nanjuNda kaNdan thannai; eNdoL” “Veesi nindraadum piraan thannai, kankaaL kaaNmin kaLoo; sevi kaaL keLmin kaLoo, sivan niyam iRai sembavaLa eri pOl maeni piraan thiram eppOdhum sevi kaaL keLmin kaLoo; mookkae nee muraLaay, mudu kaaduRai mukkaNanai; vaakkae nOkkiya mangai maNaaLanai muraLaa; vaayae vaazhthu kaNdaay, matha yaanaiyuri pOrththu pey vaazh kaattakaththaaL” “Peraan thannai vaayae vaazhthukaN; nenjae nee ninaiyaay, neemi punsadai nirmalanai; manjaadum malai mangai maNaaLanai nenjae nee ninaiyaa; kai kaaL kooppith thozheer, kadi maamalar thoovi nindru; paivaay paambarai aarththa paramanai kai kaaL kooppith thozhi; aa kaiyaal payan eN, aran kOyil valam vandhu; pookkaiyaal atti pOthriyan” “Naathavivaakkaal payan en? KaalkaLaal payan en?

“Karai kaNdan oorai kOyil kOla kOpurak kOkaraN soozhaa kaalkaLaal payan en? Utraar yaaruLarO uyir koNdu pOmpOzhuthu? Kutraala thuRai kooththanallaal namakkutraar aaruLarO? Irumaanthiruppan kolO eesan palkkaNath thennappattu? SiRumaan endhithan sEvaDi keezh sendraNgu iru maanthiruppan kol?” “ThEdi kaNdu koNdEn, Thiru-maalodu naanmuganum thEdi thEdOnaa thEvanai ennuLLE thEdi kaNdu koNdEn.”

“Thus is this Thiru-pathigam structured. In each verse of this Thiru-pathigam, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman instructs the body’s organs to worship Lord Shiva. “O Head, you worship Lord Shiva! O Head, you worship Lord Shiva, who wears a garland of skulls on His head and wanders, begging for alms in a skull!” “O Eyes, you behold Lord Shiva! You behold Lord Shiva, the blue-throated one who consumed the poison from the ocean, and who dances, wielding His eight arms!” “O Ears, you always listen to the qualities and deeds of Lord Shiva!

“Our Lord Shiva has a divine form like red coral and fire. O Ears, you always listen to the qualities and deeds of such a great Lord!” “O Nose, you always praise and make sounds for the three-eyed Lord who resides in the cremation ground, the husband of Parvati who is the embodiment of words! Murazhuthal means to make a sound with the nose. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman commands the nose to praise the Lord with the soft sound that comes through it.” “O Mouth, you always praise Lord Shiva! O Mouth, you always praise Lord Shiva, who flayed the hide of a mad elephant and performs His dance in the cremation ground where ghouls reside!” “O Mouth, you always praise Lord Shiva, who performs His dance in the cremation ground where ghouls reside!” “O Heart, you always meditate on Lord Shiva!

“O Heart, you always meditate on Lord Shiva, the pure one with upward-pointing red matted locks, the husband of Parvati, the daughter of the Himalayas where clouds play!” “O Hands, you always worship Lord Shiva with folded palms! O Hands, you always worship Lord Shiva with folded palms, offering fragrant, excellent flowers to the Lord, who has a hooded serpent tightly bound around His waist!” “What is the use of this body if it does not circumambulate Lord Shiva’s temple, offer flowers with its hands, and pay homage to the Lord? What is the use of the feet? What is the use of these feet that do not circumambulate the sacred temple of our Lord, the blue-throated one, the Thiru-kOyil called Thiru-kOkarnam, which has beautiful gopurams?” The Thiru-kOkarnam mentioned here is the sacred place called Thiru-kOkarnam. The Shiva lingam here is shaped like a cow’s ear, hence the name of this place.

“This is a Shiva sthalam in Thuluva Nadu, sung about in hymns, and is currently located in the state of Karnataka.

“Thus, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, who commanded the body’s organs to worship Lord Shiva in nine verses, continues to sing. “When Yama, the god of death, takes our life, who will be our support? There is no one to support us except the Lord of Dance who lovingly resides in Thiru-kutraalam.” “Shall I remain in joyful intoxication, being one of the Shiva ganas of the Lord who controls and rules everyone, and go beneath the sacred feet of that Lord who holds a small deer?” He then sings, “Shall I remain in joyful intoxication beneath the sacred feet of that Lord who holds a small deer?” In the twelfth verse, he concludes the hymn by singing, “I have found the Lord Shiva, whom Thiru-maal and Brahma searched for but could not find; I have realized that He resides within my heart.” This Thiru-pathigam contains a total of twelve sacred verses.

“Now, the next Thiru-pathigam is a Thani Kurunthogai Thiru-pathigam, which begins with “OnRu VeNpiRai.” It is the eighty-ninth Thiru-pathigam of the Fifth Thiru-murai, a Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathigam. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman has composed verses from one to ten, starting with the number one and progressing numerically up to ten, in an ornamental fashion. This Thiru-pathigam has a structure similar to the Thiru-pathigam that cured the poison, which began with “OnRu Kolam.” In this Thiru-pathigam, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman has composed ten verses, placing the number one in the first verse, the number two in the second verse, and so on. Its specialty is that it systematically describes the divine qualities of the Lord in a numerical sequence.

“Now, that Thiru-pathigam.

““OnRu veNpiRai kaNNiyOr kOvanam onRu keezhumaiyOdu muduththathu onRu veNthalaiyEndhi em uLLaththE onRi nindrangku uRaiyum oruvanE. IraNdumaam avarkku uLLana seythoL iraNdumaam avarkku uLLana kOlangkaL iraNdu millamaan emmai aaLukanthu iraNdu pOdhum en sindhaiyuL vaikumE. MoonRu moorththiyuL nindriyalum thoL moonRumaayina moovilai soolaththan moonRu kaNNinan theeththoL moonRinan moonRu pOdhum en sindhaiyuL moolkumE. NaaLin mEn mukam” “Setrathu manniLal naalu nankkuNarndhu ittathu minpamaam naalu vEtham sariththathu nannari naalu pOl em akaththuRai naathanE.

“Anjum anjumOr aadi araimisai anju pOlaRai aarththathin thaththuvam anjum anjumOr Or ainjum aayavan anjumaam em akaththuRai aathiyE. AaRu kaalvaNdu moosiya konRaiyan aaRu soodiya aNda muthalvanar aaRu koormaiyarkku achchamayap poruL aaRu pOl em akaththuRai aathiyE. Ezhu maamalai Ezhu pozhil soozhkadal Ezhu pOttrumiraavaNan kai narambu Ezhu kEttaruL seythavan poRkadal Ezhum sooL adiyEn manaththuLLavE. Ettu moorththiyaay nindriyalum thoL ettuvAn kuNaththu eesan emmaan thanai ettum moorththiyum em iRai emmuLLE ettum moorththiyum” “EmmuL oDungumE. Onpathu onpathiyaanai yolikaLironpathu onpathu palkkaNanjooLavE onpathaam avai thee thoLilin urai onpathu oththu nindru eNNuL oDungumE.

“Paththu nooRavan veNkaN veLLaeRRu aNNal paththu nooRavan palsadai thOnmisai paththiyaamilamaathalin gnaanaththaal paththiyaan iDam koNdathu paLLiyE.”

“Thus, this Thiru-pathigam is structured with numerical ornamentation, one, two, three, and so on.

“Now, the next Thiru-pathigam is the ninety-first Thiru-pathigam of the Fifth Thiru-murai, a Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathigam.

““Eiyilaanai en ichchai akampaDik kOyil aanai kuNapperungkunRinai vaayilaanai manONmaNiyaip petra thaayilaanai thazhuvum en aaviyE. Munnai gnaana muthal thani viththu” “Thinai pinnai gnaana piRangkuchchadaiyanai ennai gnaanaththu iruLaRuththu aaNdavan thannai gnaana thalaiyittu vaippanE. GnaanaththaaRRuvaar sila gnaanikaL gnaanaththaal thozhuvEn unai naanalaen gnaanaththaal thozhuvaarkaL thozhakkaNdu gnaanaththaay unai naanum thozhuvanE. PazhuvukkungkuNam naankaNakkummathE puzhuvukkingkenakkuLLa pollaangkillai puzhuvinum kadaiyEn punithan thamar kuzhuvukkevvidahtthEn sendru kooDavE.

“Malaiyae vandhu vizhinum manitharkaLaal nilaiyinindru kalangka peRudhirael thalaivanAkiya eesan thamarkaLai kolai seyyaanai thaan konRidiRkiumE. Katrukkolvana vaayuLa naavuLa ittukkolvana poovuLa neeruLa katrai senchadaiyaan uLan naamuLOm etrukkO” “Namanaal munivuNpathE. ManitharkaL ingkE vam onRu sollukEn kaniththandaar kaniyuNNavum vallEerE punithan poRkaLal eesan enum kani ithu saalavum EsatravarkkE. Ennai Ethum aRindhilan empiraan thannai naanum unEthum aRindhilEn ennai thannadiyaan endru aRithalum thannai naanum piraan endru aRindhanE. TheLLaththEri theLindhuththippathOr uLLaththEral amutha oLiviLi kaLLaththEn kadiyEn kavalai kadal veLLaththEnukku evvaaru viLainthathE.”

“This Thiru-pathigam.

“Now, the next Thiru-pathigam is the Kaalapaasa Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathigam. This Thiru-pathigam is about Yama commanding his messengers not to approach Shiva’s devotees. This Thiru-pathigam Recitation of this Thiru-pathigam is capable of removing any difficulties. It is the ninety-second Thiru-pathigam of the Fifth Thiru-murai, a Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathigam.

““KaNdu kol aRiyaanai kaniviththu paNdu naan seytha paazhimai kEttirael koNda paaNi kodu kotti thaaLangai koNda thoNdarai thuNNilum soozhalE. NaDukkaththuLLum nakaiyuLum nampaRku kaDukka kalla vaDam iDuvaarkkaRku koDukka koLka ena uraippaarkaLai iDukkaN seyya peReer ingku neengumE. KaarkkoL konRai kaDimalar kaNNiyaan seerkkaL naamam sivan endru aRatruvaar aarkaLaakilumaak avarkaLai neerkkaL saara peReer ingku neengumE. SaaRinEn sadai neeNmuDi sangkaran seetram kaaman kaN vaiththavan sEvaDi aaRaththavum kaLi patta maNaththaraay pOtru endru uraippaar puDippOgalE. IRaiyan son maRavE”

“Naman thoodhuveer piRaiyum paampumudai perumaan thamar naravam naariya nannoruNjaanthilum niRaiya neeraNivaar ethir sellalE. VaamathEvan vaLanagar vaikaLum kaamom onRilaRaay kaivilaikkodu thaaman thoopamum thannaruNjaanthamum Emamum punaiyaar ethir sellalE. PaDaiyum paasamum pattriya kaiyineer aDaiyanmin namatheesan aDiyarai viDaikaLooRththiyaan aDiyaarkuzaam paDaippukaadhu neer pOtthriyE pOminE. Vichchaiyaavathum vEtkamaiyaavathum nichchal neeraNivaarai ninaippathE achcham eiththi arukaNaiyaadhu neer pichchai pukkavan anparai pENumE. Innam kENmin iLampirai sooDiya mannan paatham manaththudan Eththuvaar maNNum anjaliththaakiya manthiran thaNNil onRu vallaaraiyum saar” “Matrum kELmin manapparipponRinRi sutrum poosiya neetrodu kOvanam ottrayaeRuDaiyaan aDiyE allaal patronRu illikaL mEl paDai pOgalE.

“Arakkan eerainthu thalaiyumOr thaaLinaal nerukkiyoonRiyittaan thamar niRkilum surukkenaadhu angku pErmin kaN matra neer surukkaniRa suDaraan kazhal sooDumE.”

“Now, the next Thiru-pathigam is the MarakkiRpanE Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathigam. In each verse of this hymn, the refrain “Naan marakkiRpanE” (Shall I forget?) appears, hence this Thiru-pathigam is called MarakkiRpanE Thiru-pathigam. It is the ninety-third Thiru-pathigam of the Fifth Thiru-murai.

““Kaasanai kaNalai kathirmaa maNi thEsanai pukazhaar silar thennarkaL maasinai kazhiththaaTkoLa,” “Valla em eesanai ini naan marakkiRpanE. Punthikku viLakkaay puraaNanai santhikkaN naDamaadum sathuranai anthivaNNanai aaRaral moorththiyai vandhennuLLam koNdaanai marappanE. Eesan eesan endrendrum aRatruvan eesandraan en manaththiR pirivilan eesandraannaiyum en manaththu koNdu eesandraannaiyum yaan marakkiRpanE. Eesan ennai aRinthathu aRinthanan eesan sEvaDi Etra peRathalaal eesan sEvaDi Etra petrEn ini eesan thannaiyum yaan marakkiRpanE.

“ThEnai paalinai thingaLai gnaayiRai vaanveNmathi sooDiya mainthanai vENilaanai melivu seyyazhal gnaanamoorththiyai naan marakkiRpanE. KaNNalai karumpooriya thEralai minnanai minnaNaiya oruvanai ponnanai maNikkunRu piRangiya,” “Ennanai ini yaan marakkiRpanE. Karumpinai kattiyai kantha maamalar surumpinai suDar sOthiyuL sOthiyai arumpiniR perum pOdhu koNdaay malar virumbum eesanai naan marakkiRpanE. Thunjum pOdhum suDarviDu sOthiyai nenjuL nindru ninaippukku neethiyai nanju kaNdaththu aDakkiya nampanai vanjanEn ini yaan marakkiRpanE. Puthiya poovinai puNNiya naathanai nithiyai neethiyai niththila kunRinai kathiyai kaNdangkaruththa kaDavulai mathiyai mainthanai naan marakkiRpanE.

“Karugu kaarmukil pOlvadOr kaNdanai uruva nOkkiyE oozhi muthalvanai parugu paalanai paanmathi sooDiyai maRuvu mainthanai naan marakkiRpanE.” Let us continue to contemplate the general Thiru-pathigams composed by Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 464, Thiru-nindra-cherukkam, Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We are contemplating the general Thiru-pathigams composed by Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman while he was staying at Thiru-poonthuruthi. In that vein, the next Thiru-pathigam is the Thani Kurunthogai Thiru-pathigam, “Enbathu ThozhiRpaalathE.” Because the refrain “ThozhiRpaalathE, ThozhiRpaalathE” (It is worthy of worship, it is worthy of worship) appears at the end of each verse in this Thiru-pathigam, it is named “ThozhiRpaalathE” Thiru-pathigam. It is the ninety-fourth Thiru-pathigam of the Fifth Thiru-murai.

“Aṇḍaththāṉai amarar thozhappadum paṇḍaththāṉai paviththiramār thirumuṇḍaththāṉai muṟṟātha iḷampirai thuṇḍaththāṉai kaṇḍīr thozhaṟpālathē. Muththoppāṉai muḷaiththezhu kaṟpaka viththoppāṉai viḷakkiḍai nēroḷi oththoppāṉai oḷipavaḷa thiral thoththop” “Pāṉai kaṇḍīr thozhaṟpālathē. Paṇṇaththāṉai pavaḷaththiraṇḍathōr vaṇṇaththāṉai vakaiyuṇarvāṉ thanai eṇṇaththāṉai iḷampirai pōl veḷḷai suṇṇaththāṉai kaṇḍīr thozhaṟpālathē. Viḍalaiyāṉai virai kamazh thēṉkoṉṟai paḍalaiyāṉai pali thirivāṉ sellum naḍalaiyāṉai nari piriyāthathōr suḍalaiyāṉai kaṇḍīr thozhaṟpālathē.

“Parithiyāṉai palvēṟu samayaṅkaḷ karuthiyāṉai kaṇḍār maṉam mēviya pirithiyāṉai piṟar aṟiyāthathōr suruthiyāṉai kaṇḍīr thozhaṟpālathē. Āthiyāṉai amarar thozhappadum nīthiyāṉai niyamaneṟikaḷai ōthiyāṉai uṇarathaṟku aṟiyathōr sōthiyāṉai kaṇḍīr thozhaṟpālathē. Ñālaththāṉai nallāṉai vallārth thozhuṅkōlaththāṉai kuṇapperuṅkunṟinai mūlaththāṉai muthalvanai mūvilai”

“Now, the next general Thiru-pathikam, the Linga Purana Thiru-kurunthokai Thiru-pathikam. This Linga Purana Thiru-kurunthokai Thiru-pathikam, we have seen it when we contemplated on the Thiru-annamalai Thiru-sthalam.

“Therefore, the next Thiru-pathikam is the general Thiru-pathikam, Manathokai Thiru-pathikam.

“Similarly, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman has composed three Thiru-pathikams based on the inner instruments (anthakaranas) of mind, intellect, and consciousness, namely Ullathokai and Siththathokai. Among them, the first Thiru-pathikam is Manathokai Thiru-pathikam. It is the ninety-sixth Thiru-pathikam in the Fifth Thiru-murai, a Thiru-kurunthokai Thiru-pathikam. “Ponnulla thiral punsadaiyin puram minnulla thiral venpiraiyaayirai ninnulla tharul kondirul neenguthal ennulullathu enthai piranire mukkanum mudaiyaay munigal palar thokkenung kadalaay oru tholinodakkanum maraiyaay arulleyalaa thekkanum ilan enthai piranire paniyaa” You are the one who is seen, worthy of worship. You are the primordial, the eight-formed, the one who transforms the five elements, the one who burns away our karmic bonds, the one who tests the changes in penance.

“You are the one who is seen, worthy of worship. You are the one with sacred ash, the incomparable white-bodied one, the one with a crescent moon, the one with a flowing red matted hair, the one who created the precious lives of the celestials. You are the one who is seen, worthy of worship. You are the one who abandoned, the one who bound the true essence in true knowledge, the one who was filled with love for the multitude, the one who encircled the three cities of his enemies. You are the one who is seen, worthy of worship. You are the one who completed, the one who pressed down the long crown of Ravana with one finger, the one who held a white skull, the one who wore a snake as a belt.

“You are the one who is seen, worthy of worship.

“Now, the next general Thiru-pathikam, the Linga Purana Thiru-kurunthokai Thiru-pathikam. This Linga Purana Thiru-kurunthokai Thiru-pathikam, we have seen it when we contemplated on the Thiru-annamalai Thiru-sthalam.

“Therefore, the next Thiru-pathikam is the general Thiru-pathikam, Manathokai Thiru-pathikam.

“Similarly, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman has composed three Thiru-pathikams based on the inner instruments (anthakaranas) of mind, intellect, and consciousness, namely Ullathokai and Siththathokai. Among them, the first Thiru-pathikam is Manathokai Thiru-pathikam. It is the ninety-sixth Thiru-pathikam in the Fifth Thiru-murai, a Thiru-kurunthokai Thiru-pathikam. “Ponnulla thiral punsadaiyin puram minnulla thiral venpiraiyaayirai ninnulla tharul kondirul neenguthal ennulullathu enthai piranire mukkanum mudaiyaay munigal palar thokkenung kadalaay oru tholinodakkanum maraiyaay arulleyalaa thekkanum ilan enthai piranire paniyaa” You are the ascetic with fierce rays in your matted hair, even if you rule the entire world, you are unique, you are the one who is beyond, you are the one who is greatly sweet to me, my Father, my Lord. You sing the Vedas, you are the one who is less than the great ascetics, you wear a crescent moon, and nothing else is said about you, my Father, my Lord.

“You are adorned with blooming Konrai, you wear the skin of a tiger, you dance with a fierce snake and fire, your devotees do not praise you enough, my Father, my Lord. You are the supreme one, who is not forgotten by the deluded, you are the one who rides the bull, my Lord, other than that Lord, there is no other refuge for this dog-like servant, my Father, my Lord. You are the one who cleanses the impurities of the mind with heat, the one who is called Shiva by the righteous. You are the one who removes evil deeds, the one who is incomparable, for those who are not, there is no other refuge, my Father, my Lord. You are the one who shines brightly, who is always present in the sky, who is the righteous one, who is the object of praise, I will not despise your golden feet, my Father, my Lord. You are the one whom Thiru-mal and Brahma could not grasp, you are the one who is difficult to know, you are the one who is grace, other than that grace, this dog-like servant has no other refuge, my Father, my Lord.

“Those who say “My Lord, my Lord” with a mind full of devotion, those who worship with reverence, those who praise your feet saying “My Father, my Lord,” they will reach your feet, saying “My Lord, my Lord.”

“Now, the next Thiru-pathikam is the general Thiru-kurunthokai Thiru-pathikam, Siththathokai Thiru-pathikam. This Thiru-pathikam is a uniquely special Thiru-pathikam. It is a Thiru-pathikam consisting of thirty Thiru-paadalgal. This is the only Thiru-pathikam among the Thevara Thiru-muraigal that contains thirty Thiru-paadalgal. It begins with “Sinthippar Manaththan.” Therefore, this Thiru-pathikam describes the ways of contemplating Shiva within the mind.

“Hence, it is named Siththathokai Thiru-pathikam. This is its second special feature.

“Now, a third unique special feature is found in this Thiru-pathikam. In this Thiru-pathikam, if we look at the first letters of the verses from the second verse to the twenty-eighth verse, they possess a unique characteristic. That is, the verses from the second Thiru-paadal to the twelfth Thiru-paadal have the first letter from ‘A’ to ‘Au’. The thirteenth Thiru-paadal has the Ayutha Ezhuththu ‘Ah’ as its first letter.

“Then, the next fourteen verses are arranged according to the consonant letters from ‘Ka’ onwards. Fourteen verses have fourteen consonant letters as their initial letters.

“Thus, twelve Thiru-paadalgal have the vowels from ‘A’ to ‘Au’ as their initial letters, one Thiru-paadal has the Ayutha Ezhuththu ‘Ah’ as its initial letter, and fourteen Thiru-paadalgal begin with the fourteen consonant letters from ‘Ka’ onwards.

“Thus, from the second Thiru-paadal to the twenty-eighth Thiru-paadal, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman has composed them with these Tamil letters as their initial letters. This Thiru-pathikam possesses such great Tamil excellence. Not only that, but this Thiru-pathikam also contains numerous subtle concepts. It is the ninety-seventh Thiru-pathikam of the Fifth Thiru-murai, the Siththathokai Thiru-kurunthokai Thiru-pathikam.

“Sinthippar Manaththan Sivan Senchudar Anthi va niraththan aniyar mathimunthichoodiya mukkaninaan adivanthippar avar vaanulakaazhvare Andam aariruloodu kadanthumbar undu polum or on sudaracchudar kandhingaar arivaar arivaarellaam vendhingatkanni vedhiyan enbare Aathiyaay avan aarumizhaathavan pothu serpunai neenmudi punniyan paathi pennuruvaki paranjudar sothiyuthiyaay nindra sothiye Ittathittathor erukantheyiyoor pattithuttangkanayp pali thervathor katta vaazhkaiyanakilum vaanavar attamoorthi arulenru adaivare Eeril kooraiyanaki erinthaven neeru poosi nilaamathi soodilum veerilaathana seiyinum vinnavaar ooralaay arulaayenruraippare Uth Even if he wears the white crescent moon on his head, he is not of flesh, he carries a green skull and begs for alms, even if he is a beggar, the celestials will approach him saying, “O Father, grant us grace.” He is the one who is called ‘Oorilaay’ (one without a place), he is the one without a name, he is the one who wears the crescent moon, the one with a dark throat, those who do not reach his feet will suffer evil, O my Father, my Lord. Those who contemplate on him saying “O my Father, my Lord,” their evil deeds will be removed. The one who is a Brahmin, who smears sacred ash, those who reached his boundless wealth. He wears the white tusk of a boar and bones, he wears the skin of an elephant, he dances with fire, even if he is of that form, the celestials will worship him always. The Lord, the Brahmin, who is male and female, the true one, who smears sacred white ash, the one with a dark throat, the one with a deer in his hand, the one who wears a snake as a belt, The Supreme One stood alone.

“He is not near those who stood as two in this world. Those who praise the one who wore the mountain as a bow, their sins will fly away. The one who is the color of the ocean and the son of the mountain, the Lord, those who lovingly contemplate him daily saying “Grant grace,” their sins will fly away. Do not say that he is of that nature, he is of a fierce nature. He is the one who is on the long lotus flower, the one who is with the ocean, they will worship him. He wears bones and a tortoise shell, he carries fire, he begs for alms in houses, do not enter hell, O you who are pure, the celestials will rule.

“The one with the red matted hair where Ganga resides, the one who wears the young moon, the one with the fiery color, the celestials worship him beautifully, he is of that nature. O my good heart, if you do not enjoy the one who has the banner of a fish, and if you do not take him as your own, then the one who burnt the god of love, his flawless feet will be your praise. Will not others know the way to refuge? After removing the senses and abandoning life, after death, who will remove those things? Is he not the one who shot the three cities? The one who is called Yama for those in hell, and Shiva for us, the one with the deer in his hand, the one who rides the swift bull, even if he is called a relative, confusion will be removed.

“The one who rides the bull and begs for alms in houses, the one who loves the forest and dances, the one who wears a five-headed snake as a belt, go and worship him with folded hands. The one with matted hair adorned with Konrai flowers, a fierce snake, and the moon, his feet, Those who understand with a clear mind will understand. Dharma is penance, penance brings karma, the one with the deer in his hand, reach his rare and resounding feet, O you who are afflicted by evil deeds. If there are those who say “Namassivaya,” their suffering will cease, they will reach the path of penance. Even if one has a settled life, it is very difficult to remain still. For many years, practice devotion to the Supreme One, praise him for many years, just as the morning sun appearing on the mountain removes the dew.

“The one with a dark throat, the one with a deer in his hand, the one who is in the form of a hunter, they protect. Those who are capable of performing tasks, they will remove the bonds of their bodies, O you fools. The Yakshas, Indra, the Asuras, the one whom they desire, the four-faced Brahma, the one with the discus, the one who is deluded, the one who is difficult to know, He became. He is the one who is admired, our Lord, the one who danced the righteous dance, the one who is praised, their sins will be removed. The one who wears a garland of skulls, and the one on the cool lotus, the flawless four-faced Brahma, and the dark one, are they not? The one with fire in his hand, who rose in the sky, who burnt the three cities with bright fire, the one who flew with the lotus-born and the one who flew, his feet and head are difficult to see.

“As youth leaves and old age comes, and wealth goes and diseases come, his mind became light and wisdom, I will think of his kinship as my own.

“The Lord who knows me within himself, if I know myself within him, I will attain him. If I do not know myself within him, I will not be able to reach myself within him. The king of Lanka, the one with ten heads, the one with the beautiful feet that pressed him down, those who worship him daily by circumambulating him, they will attain the celestial world.

“Now, the next is Ullathokai Thiru-kurunthokai Thiru-pathikam, the ninety-eighth Thiru-pathikam of the Fifth Thiru-murai.

“My heart found the Lord who is like the water that washes away, who dances in the flowing river, who is the nectar, who is clear and pure, who is like a flowing river. My heart found my Father, who is like fire, who enters and removes the impurities, who is the clarity of thought, who is pure. My heart found the light within, the Lord who is worshipped by the celestials, who holds the Ganga in his matted hair, who is free from deceit. My heart found my Lord, who is like the red color, who is worshipped by devotees as the nectar, the supreme one. My heart found my Father, who is like the sharp spear, who is half of Uma, who wears the crescent moon on his matted hair where the river flows, He carries a skull and begs for alms in many houses, my heart found my Father, who is like a rising bull.

“Those who die without a mind, those who do not lose their own mind, if you are able to remove that hard heart, my heart found the Lord within me. My heart found the one who conquered the five senses, who destroyed my evil deeds, who is worshipped with good qualities, who is the one knowledge, who is the one. My heart found the form of Shiva, who is within the mind, who removes the evil deeds, who is worshipped with good qualities, who is the wealth. My heart found the Lord, who is the light, who is worshipped by Thiru-mal and Brahma, who is the one who is always present in the mind. My heart found the one who despised the five senses, who cut off the head of Brahma, who is in the hand of the demon, My heart found the one who is the thought, who is the one with a single toe.

“Now, the next Thiru-pathikam is Aathipurana Thiru-kurunthokai Thiru-pathikam. This Thiru-pathikam elaborates on the primary nature of Shiva Peruman.

“Therefore, it is named Aathipurana Thiru-kurunthokai Thiru-pathikam. It is the hundredth Thiru-pathikam of the Fifth Thiru-murai.

“He is the Lord of the Vedas, the Lord of the Brahmins, the Lord of the Mother, the Lord of the ascetics, the primordial Lord, the Lord of Thiru-athirai, the Lord of the Bhoothas, the embodiment of virtue. “Seththu seththu pirappathe thevenru pathisai manappaaraikarku erumo aththan enrodu piramanum thutthiyanjeya nindranar sothiye nooru kodi piramarkal nondhinaar aaru kodi narayanar angene erukangai manal ennil indhirar eerillaathavan”

“The Lord is the only one. Those who are confused and argue, O foolish ones, whatever you say, there is no other God than Maha-deva for all those who are called gods. Is a well-frog equal to a sea-frog? Just as a well is not equal to the ocean, so too, sinners will not see the greatness of Shiva, the God of gods. Those who pray to the one who dwells in the cremation ground, he grants boons, he bows his head at the feet of the celestials, he is the life of the bodies of the ascetics, they do not contemplate Shiva. They will burn, they do not know that fire is the form of the Lord.

“They forget the one who is difficult to reach for Hari, and become like foxes, they are not of the country. They worship the feet of the sun, is not the sun the form of righteousness? They do not contemplate the mind that worships the Lord of the four Vedas. They do not receive the nectar of love in their hearts for Shankara, who is better than a mother. They are like ghosts, those who drank the milk of ghosts and lost their lives, those who are caught in the illusion of Maya. The greatness of the Lord who granted grace to the demon who was destroyed, they do not understand with love, those who are foolish and without thought.

“Thus, Thiru-navukkarasu Swamigal, who was staying in Thiru-poonthuruthi, composed many such general Thiru-pathikams. Let us go on contemplating.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 465. Thiru-nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. While Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman was staying in Thiru-poonthuruthi Thiru-sthalam for a long time, establishing a Thiru-madam, performing service to the Lord, and composing Thiru-pathikams, Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, having eradicated Jainism in Pandya Nadu and re-established Shaivism, is now proceeding to Chola Nadu. Earlier, when Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman were together in Thiru-marai Kadu, also known as Vedaranyam, messengers from Mangaiyarkkarasiyar and Minister Kulachchiraiyar from Pandya Nadu in the south met Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and conveyed the atrocities of Jainism in Pandya Nadu, requesting him to remove Jainism from Pandya Nadu and make Shaivism flourish. The message from the Queen of Madurai, Mangaiyarkkarasiyar, and Minister Kulachchiraiyar was conveyed to Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman.

Accordingly, Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman proceeded to Pandya Nadu, as we have seen.

At the same time, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman continued his pilgrimage, visiting many Thiru-sthalams, traveling north, then arriving at Thiru-vaiyaru, and is currently staying in Thiru-poonthuruthi.

At this time, Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, who had proceeded to Pandya Nadu, defeated the Jains in debate, eradicated Jainism from Pandya Nadu, established Shaivism, visited all the Thiru-sthalams in Pandya Nadu, sang Thiru-pathikams, and is now proceeding to Kaveri Nadu.

At this time, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman is staying in Thiru-poonthuruthi, having established a Thiru-madam and performing service.

Thus, Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, departing from the pleasant Tamil land of Pandya Nadu, arrives in Chola Nadu, which yields many riches due to the abundance of the fertile Kaveri river. When he arrived in Chola Nadu, he heard the news that Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar was staying in Thiru-poonthuruthi, having established a Thiru-madam. Upon hearing this, Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, intending to quickly reach Thiru-poonthuruthi, arrived at a place surrounded by fields outside the village of Thiru-poonthuruthi.

Thus, the place where Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman arrived is an area surrounded by fields outside Thiru-poonthuruthi.

Here, the wonderful event of the reunion of Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman is about to take place. The Tamil scholar who appeared in Seerkazhi, Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman has arrived outside Thiru-poonthuruthi. Hearing this good news, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman’s heart rejoiced, and his joy at seeing Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman with his own eyes increased. With a strong desire in his heart to meet and worship Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman in person, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman went to welcome Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman.

Thus, the place where these two Nayanmars met is the area with fields outside the village of Thiru-poonthuruthi. This place is still called Sambandar Medu (Sambandar’s Mound). Surrounded by fields, this place is slightly elevated. This place is located about two ‘naligai’ (a measure of time, approximately 48 minutes) southwest of Thiru-poonthuruthi, It is on the way from Vellamparambur to Thiru-poonthuruthi. That is, this place is on the way from the Thiru-sthalam called Thiru-valampozhil, which is praised in Thevara hymns, to Thiru-poonthuruthi. Along with this information, Sivakavimani Ayyavargal has specifically provided another historical account.

He has mentioned that this account was written and sent by a devotee from Thiru-poonthuruthi. This is a traditional story prevalent in that region. What is that story? It is that Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman used to perform Thiru-uzhavara pani (service of cleaning) in this Thiru-sthalam called Thiru-valampozhil.

During that time, Vaishnavites caused trouble to Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman. Knowing this, Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman decided to remove that trouble for Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman.

Therefore, the Kudamurutti river overflowed, carrying away the houses of the Vaishnavites and the Vishnu temple in that village, and deposited them at the present location of Sundaraperumal Temple. And from that day until now, there is a tradition that Vaishnava families should not stay overnight in Thiru-valampozhil. Sivakavimani Ayyavargal has mentioned this traditional historical account as a supplementary piece of information at this point.

Now, we continue to contemplate the history of Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman.

Thus, the meeting of these two great Nayanmars is about to take place at the place now called Sambandar Medu. When Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, the leader of Seerkazhi, who was born in Seerkazhi, travels on pilgrimage, he is always accompanied by a large retinue. Even now, when Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman arrived at this place in Thiru-poonthuruthi, a huge crowd surrounded him. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, who arrived with the desire to join this dense crowd, joined the crowd and, unseen, bowed down and rose, then carried the palanquin of Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, who was being carried in the pearl palanquin. This pearl palanquin was bestowed upon Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman by the Lord Himself.

Thus, Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, ascending this pearl palanquin, travels on pilgrimage. As he approaches this place, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman carries Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman’s palanquin and accompanies him. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman carries it, thinking, “With this humble body, I too shall bear Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman’s sacred palanquin.” Sekkizhar Swamigal sings, “As Kaliyarkon approached the boundary, he lovingly mingled with the throng, and without being seen, he worshipped. ‘With this humble body, I shall bear the gem-studded palanquin that carries him,’ he resolved.” Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman carries the palanquin without Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman’s knowledge. For if Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman were to know this, he would immediately descend from the palanquin.

Therefore, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman carries his sacred palanquin without his knowledge, thinking, “With this humble body, I shall bear it.” This body is prone to decay, afflicted by diseases and other ailments. Yet, I shall bear this palanquin. Unlike other virtuous devotees who bear it with a good body to attain blessings, I shall bear it to alleviate the lowliness of my body. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman carries that palanquin.

Furthermore, Sekkizhar Swamigal sings, “With a hidden form, so that no one might recognize him, he joined those who bore the gem-studded palanquin upon which the Brahmin of Pukali, Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, was gracefully seated. His mind filled with immense joy, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman proceeded.” Thus, as Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman carried this palanquin, no one accompanying Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman could discern or recognize him.

Now, the next verse: “The great sage Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, having arrived near Thiru-ppunthuruthi where Appar resided, asked with melting heart, ‘Where is Appar?’ And Appar replied, ‘Your servant has attained the great blessing of bearing your sacred feet, and I am here.’” This is the next beautiful verse composed by Sekkizhar Swamigal. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, the great sage, approaches Thiru-ppunthuruthi. Realizing that he had arrived near Thiru-ppunthuruthi while still in the palanquin, Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, seated in the palanquin, asks, “Where is Appar here in Thiru-ppunthuruthi?” To this, Appar Swamigal, who had been carrying Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman’s sacred palanquin, replies with a melting heart. Appar Swamigal, deeply moved, replies, “Your servant is here, having received the great blessing of bearing your sacred feet,” and he gives this answer while still carrying the palanquin.

Now, the next verse: “Upon hearing this, Pillaiyar, with great haste and a trembling heart, rose and bowed to the King. Before the generous Vagisar could bow, he bowed. All the Thiru-thondar, whose hands hold the leaping deer, worshipped and rejoiced.” As I replied while carrying the palanquin, Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, upon hearing those words, immediately and with great haste, rose and descended from the palanquin. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, in his sacred heart, With a heart filled with fear and trepidation, bowed to Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman. Before the generous Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman could bow to Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, he himself bowed to him. All the devotees of Lord Shiva, who were blessed to witness this divine event, worshipped both these great Acharyas and raised the cry of “Hara Hara Hara Hara!” “The Lord of Kazhumalam, Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, united with Thiru-navukkarasu, resided there, worshipping and melting with joy at the lotus feet of the Lord, whose sacred hands hold the axe and the deer, in the sacred city of Thiru-ppunthuruthi, amidst groves where the crescent moon shines.” This is the next sacred verse composed by Sekkizhar Swamigal.

Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, the leader of Sirkazhi, united with Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar, resided in the sacred city of Thiru-ppunthuruthi, where the crescent moon shines. In Thiru-ppunthuruthi, surrounded by fertile groves, they worshipped the lotus feet of the Lord, whose sacred hands hold the deer and the axe, melting with devotion and attaining bliss, praising the Peruman. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman also resided there in Thiru-ppunthuruthi with Appar Swamigal. During this stay, Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman shared news about his visit to the Pandya country. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman recounted to Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman how he had vanquished the cruel Jains in the Pandya country. He spoke of how the Pandya king, formerly the hunchbacked Koon Pandya, a follower of Jainism, had his hunchback straightened, was anointed with sacred ash by the grace of Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, received spiritual instruction, and attained liberation from bonds and the grace of Shiva, becoming Nedumaran of enduring fame.

Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, of great penance, recounts to Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman how he caused the path of the boundless sacred ash to flourish in the Pandya country, watered by the cool Vaigai River. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, of pure fame, listened to all these histories and rejoiced in his heart.

Here, Sekkizhar Swamigal sings of the Pandya country as “Thann Porundha Punar Nadu” (the land of the cool river). Sivakavimani notes that “Porundham” refers to the Thamirabarani River. The meaning is the Pandya country. In the Chola country, the Kaveri River flows and enriches it, but the Kaveri originates in another country and flows through the Chola country to enrich it. Unlike that, the Porunai River, the Thamirabarani River, The river is born in the Pandya country and enriches that very country, which is the note here.

Thus, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman rejoices upon hearing the sacred history of Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman. Earlier, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman had requested at Thiru-vedaranyam not to go to the Pandya country, fearing the illusions and evils of the Jains. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman has now returned victorious from the Pandya country, having overcome all the fears that Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman had.

Therefore, he is greatly pleased to hear this. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, with great fondness, recounts to Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman the loving nature of the Empress Mangaiyarkkarasi, who possessed chastity and devotion, and the greatness of Kulachirai Nayanar, the minister who lived with great friendship towards the devotees.

Thus, as Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman recounted the glories of the Pandya country and the greatness of the devotees there to Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman desired to visit the Pandya country. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman requested Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman to worship all the sacred places in the glorious Thondai country where Lord Shiva graciously resides. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, having heard this, departs from Thiru-ppunthuruthi, bowing, to go to the Thondai country, to visit the Shiva temples where Lord Shiva resides in the Thondai country. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, who desired to visit the Pandya country, departs from Thiru-ppunthuruthi, bowing and taking leave, to go to the Pandya country.

Thus, the Lord Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, having been graced by the Lord, and having received the grace of Lord Shiva, departs from the sacred sthalam of Thiru-ppunthuruthi, with a desire to go to the Pandya country, and journeys southward. Let us continue to contemplate the pilgrimage of Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar to the Pandya country. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 466. Thiru-nindrachcharukkam. Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. From Thiru-ppunthuruthi, he journeys southward towards the Pandya country, which is Tamil Nadu, to undertake a pilgrimage to its sacred sites. Generally, there are many regions in this land where Tamil-speaking people live, such as Thondai Nadu, Chola Nadu, Chera Nadu, and Nadu Nadu.

In all these regions, only Tamil-speaking people reside. All these regions are Tamil lands.

However, the Pandya country is generally referred to by the special name “Tamil Nadu.” In terms of etymology, if one says “Tamil Nadu,” it refers only to the Pandya country. In Sanskrit, “Pankajam” refers to a lotus flower. This is called “Yoga Roodi.” “Pankajam” literally means “born in mud.” In mud, not only lotuses but also other flowers, fish, and other creatures are born. Nevertheless, in the sense of “born in mud,” “Pankajam” refers only to the lotus flower, according to the grammar of Yoga Roodi.

Similarly, in the Tamil language, Yoga Roodi is called “Karana Idikuri” (a name that is both descriptive and conventional). In that sense, although “Tamil Nadu” generally refers to the Chera, Chola, Pandya, and other Tamil-speaking regions, as a Karana Idikuri, it refers only to the Pandya country. This is because Lord Shiva presided over the Sangam, As the leader, he researched Tamil and also composed grammar for Tamil. The Pandya country is a special land. That is why the Pandya country is given the name “Tamil Nadu” because of this specialty. Sekkizhar Peruman refers to this as “Mankulavu Tamil Nadu.” We can interpret “Mankulavu Tamil” and “Mankulavu Nadu” together.

“Mankulavu Tamil” means that Tamil illuminates this world. For those who learn the Tamil language, it bestows the fruit of birth, because a person who learns the Tamil language gets the opportunity to study the devotional and spiritual texts in the Tamil language. Through this, it serves as a basis for them to attain the ultimate liberation, which is salvation.

Therefore, the Tamil language is such that it can bestow the fruit of birth upon those who learn it. This is the meaning. To such a special Tamil Nadu, the Pandya country, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman proceeds. He travels along the main route that existed in those days from the Chola country to the Pandya country. As he comes thus, he reaches Thiru-ppuththur, the first sthalam in the Pandya country, and there he praises the Lord and sings Thiru-varams, which are Tamil garlands. Sekkizhar Swamigal sings this: “The Lord, who received the grace of the beautiful-eyed one, departed from the sacred place and proceeded southward to the Pandya country.

“He worshipped and praised the beautiful Thiru-ppuththur and reached Thiru-valavai in Madurai, with its moon-touching flag-bearing walls.” Thus, in the Pandya country, The sacred site of Thiru-ppuththur serves as the entrance, the first sacred site for those coming from the Chola country to the Pandya country. This sacred site is located in Tamil Nadu, between Madurai and the town of Karaikudi, in the region known as Chettinad. Near Thiru-ppuththur are various other sacred sites such as Pillaiyarpatti, Kunrakkudi, and Piranmalai. Thiru-ppuththur is one of the fourteen Thiru-varam-sung sites in the Pandya country.

“Here, the Lord’s sacred name is Sri Thaleeswarar, Sri Thalinathar, Thiru-thali-nathar. The Goddess’s sacred name is Sivakamasundari. The sthala-viruksham (sacred tree) is Sarakkonrai. The Theertham (sacred water) is Sri Thali Theertham, Sivagangai Theertham. The Peruman Here, the Lord performs the Gowri Thandavam, which Mahalakshmi witnessed, worshipped, and received blessings. This is a very important Bhairava sthalam.

“It is a long-standing tradition that after the priest rings the bell for the Ardha Jama worship, no devotees should go to the Bhairava shrine. In this temple, the Lord bestows grace as a Swayambhu Lingam. This is one of the Ashta Bhairava sthalams. In this region, the name of the presiding Ganesha is Polla Pillaiyar. The form of the place where Sage Valmiki performed penance is behind the sanctum sanctorum. This is a sthalam worshipped by Jayantan, the son of Indra.

“Lord Mahavishnu also worshipped Thiru-thali-nathar in this sthalam. He also appears in a separate shrine behind the Swami in a yogic posture. He is He is known as Yoga Narayanan, accompanied by Sri Devi and Bhu Devi.

“Here, the Dakshinamurthy idol is without disciples. In the Navagraha mandapam, the Navagrahas are seated.

“Thus, this temple possesses numerous unique features. Hiranyaksha, a devotee of Shiva, had two sons, Andhakasuran and Sambasuran. Although they were great devotees of Shiva, they tormented the Devas. When the Devas prayed to Lord Shiva, he manifested as a cosmic form of himself. He vanquished Andhakasuran and Sambasuran. He is the deity who took the form of Bhairava.

“Such a Bhairava appears here as Yoga Bhairava. During the Sampaka Sashti festival in the month of Karthigai, For six days, a yagam is performed here for Bhairava. When Sage Valmiki was performing penance, an anthill formed around him. Lord Shiva, the deity of this sthalam, appeared to Valmiki who was inside the anthill.

“Therefore, he is called Putreeswarar. Because he appeared before the anthill, this sthalam was called Puththur, and with the prefix “Thiru,” it became Thiru-ppuththur. Among the eighteen Mahapurana, the Skanda Mahapurana is the greatest. In the Shankara Samhita, one of its six Samhitas, the sthala puranam of this place is found as Sri Thalamanam Navapuri Manmiyam. The inscription here states that the Thiru-ppuththur Sthala Puranam in Tamil was composed by Maraijnana Sambandha Peruman, who belonged to the Meykanda Deva Nayanar lineage.

“Thus, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, having come to such a sacred sthalam, here bestows a Thiru-thandakam Thiru-ppathikam. It is the seventy-sixth Thiru-ppathikam of the Sixth Thiru-murai.

““He is the one praised by the celestials who worship, the one who is worthy of fame, the one who is part of the bull-riding Lord, the one who expanded into all three worlds and became many lives, the one who wears a garland of fragrant Konrai, the one who created the four Vedas and held them on his head, the pure one, the one who is part of Thiru-mal, the one who resides in Thiru-thali in Thiru-ppuththur, surrounded by fertile fields. He is in my thoughts.” “He is the one who is part of the goddess with breasts like a river, the one who is the great Vedas, the one who is the earth and the sky, the one who is the fierce white fire, the wind, the water, and the mountains. He is the one with a dark throat who swallowed the deadly poison, the one with eight shoulders, the one who bears Mount Kailash, the one who always resides with love in Thiru-thali in Thiru-ppuththur, with its wide streets where chariots roll. He is in my thoughts. He is the one who always loves Uma, whose waist is like a lightning-flash creeper, the one who holds the mountain as a bow in his hand, the one who, as a good poet, gave the golden purse to the poor.

“He is the one who, seeing the fragrant Konrai blooming golden, and the bees buzzing in the rich groves of Thiru-ppuththur, resides in Thiru-thali. He is in my thoughts. He is the one who resides, worshipped and praised by Brahma, who sits on a lotus, and Vishnu, and Indra. He is the one with matted red locks adorned with blooming Kadukkai, Vanni, and Datura flowers, the one who is free from blemish, the one who is in the assembly. He is the great gem of Maraikkadu, surrounded by fertile fields where buffaloes graze and dive into the water, the one who resides in Thiru-thali in Thiru-ppuththur. He is in my thoughts.

“He is the one who removed the disease of dark, strong karma, the one who is Ekambam in the beautiful Kanchi, the one who dances in the hall of Thillai, the great Puththiyoor, who cures diseases in the vast world. He is the one who is the companion of the generous and mighty Kulachirai, the unique one in Thiru-varur. He is the one who resides in Thiru-thali in Thiru-ppuththur, surrounded by beautiful groves. He is in my thoughts. He is the one who danced with Uma, whose shoulders are like bamboo, to be seen, the one who receives alms from those with matted hair, with a fierce snake in his hand, the one whose form is like a coral mountain, the one who is Shankara, who has a bull as his mount, which roars. He is the one with a fierce snake as his waist-band, the one who resides in Thiru-thali in Thiru-ppuththur, surrounded by fields where taro grows.

“He is in my thoughts. He is the one who adorned his matted locks with fragrant Konrai flowers, the shining moon, and Vanni, the one who wears a fierce snake with fire, the one who wears a tiger skin, the one who is subtle and unknowable, the one with a thousand names, the one who resides in Thiru-thali in Thiru-ppuththur, with its rich groves and gem-studded mansions where Brahmins reside. He is in my thoughts. He is the virtuous one who kicked Yama for the Brahmin who sought refuge, the one who flayed the elephant, making it flee in terror from the white-toothed, white-bangle-wearing goddess, the strong one who adorned the crescent moon, the lord of Thiru-varur, with its dense groves of sugarcane and Punnai trees, the one who resides in Thiru-thali in Thiru-ppuththur, where the southern breeze blows. He is in my thoughts. He is the attachment, the supreme one for others and for the celestials, the victorious one who destroyed Daksha’s sacrifice, the one who conquered fierce anger and chose to increase knowledge, the one who is our Pingakan in Kazhukkundram with its flowing waterfalls, the one who destroyed the beautiful Kama.

“He is the one who resides in Thiru-thali in the glorious Thiru-ppuththur. He is in my thoughts. He is the one who tore the body of the arrogant Jalandhara, the one who created the discus, the one who plucked the teeth of the sun, who circles the world, the mighty one who crushed the shoulders of the king of the celestials, the one who adorned himself with golden ornaments, the one whose sacred foot crushed the heads of the king of Lanka, surrounded by the roaring sea, the one who resides in Thiru-thali in Thiru-ppuththur. He is in my thoughts.

“Thus, having worshipped at Thirupputhur, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman took leave of the Lord from Thirupputhur and proceeded to the great city of Madurai, also known as Thiruvalavai, the capital of the Pandya kingdom. Let us persist in our reflection.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 467. Thirunindrachcharukkam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. During his pilgrimage to the holy sites of the Pandya country, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman arrived at the great city of Madurai, known as Thiruvalavai. Madurai is the sacred place where Lord Somaskandar, as Thiruvalavai Peruman, presided over the Tamil Sangam as its chief poet and fostered the growth of Tamil.

Sekkizhar Peruman highlights this unique glory here. Not only here, but wherever he mentions Madurai and Lord Sokkanatha, who resides there, Sekkizhar Peruman praises Lord Sokkanatha as the leader who researched Tamil and the first head of the Tamil Sangam. This is because this history, where the Lord Himself established a Sangam here and, as its head, nurtured Tamil, is a unique and supreme distinction not found in any other language.

Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman praises Madurai based on this glory. In the southern Pandya country, on the Podhigai mountain, Agathiyar Muni performed penance and nurtured Tamil. The cool breeze emanating from the Podhigai mountain brings cool air, alleviating the heat of this world and providing coolness to humans.

Similarly, the Tamil nurtured by Agathiyar Peruman on the Podhigai mountain, spreading throughout the southern Pandya country, is capable of dispelling the heat of birth and providing coolness to living beings. As stated in ‘Than Nizhalam Pathi’ (His own shadow-like abode), Shivagnana Bodham, accordingly, the Tamil emanating from the Podhigai mountain, the Tamil nurtured by Agathiyar Peruman, is like a cool breeze that dispels the heat of birth from living beings. Not only that, but Lord Muruga also researched and nurtured Tamil here.

Therefore, we can observe here the manner in which Sekkizhar Peruman makes us understand Lord Sokkanatha, the Lord of Alavai, as the poet of the Tamil Sangam. Sekkizhar Peruman states, “Having approached and entered Madurai, he circumambulated the courtyard of the temple of the Lord with a beautiful neck, who once presided over the refined literary Sangam and researched Tamil, and having bowed before Him, he entered and rejoiced in worshipping the Lord with the strong bull.” In this verse, as we have seen, Lord Sokkanatha is referred to as the Lord who once presided over the refined literary Sangam in Madurai and researched Tamil.
