Similarly, in the Purana of Murthi Nayanar, Sekkizhar Peruman sings the same idea, that Lord Sokkanatha is the Lord who presided over the Sangam and researched Tamil. He sings in the Purana of Murthi Nayanar, “If the Sangam existed for the Lord who dispels our sins at Thiruvalavai, who is the essence of truth in Tamil literature, which is superior to the three worlds, and who bestows righteousness and truth.” Madurai is the city where Tamil Sangams existed, serving as a place for the excellent staging of Tamil literary works, poems, and songs. The Potramarai Kulam (Golden Lotus Pond) within the Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple in Madurai is where works like Thirukkural were staged.

Therefore, Madurai is the place where Tamil literary works, encompassing the three forms of Tamil—Iyal (literature), Isai (music), and Nadagam (drama)—arose, proclaiming the glory of the Lord and the greatness of Shaivism. Lord Sokkanatha presided as the chief poet of the first of these Tamil Sangams, bestowing grace. Just as Thirunavukkarasu Peruman sings, “He who arose before all others,” this ancient city of Madurai is an ancient city that appeared before all other holy places. In this ancient city, works explaining the essence of Shaivism, which is righteousness, have emerged. Not only works that determine the truth and righteousness, but also works that bestow the state of liberation, which can be attained through experience, have emerged in Tamil. The experiential state of this righteousness The experiential state of this righteousness is well explained by the commentaries on Thirukkovaiyar and Iraiyanar Agapporul, which are Tamil Akapporul (love poetry) texts.

That the Lord of Thiruvalavai explained the true nature of Tamil literature can be understood from Iraiyanar Agapporul and from historical accounts in the Thiruvilaiyadal Puranam, such as the Lord resolving the disputes of the Sangam poets. Did the Lord, as a poet in the temple of Thiruvalavai, only bestow texts on the experiential state of this righteousness? Did the Lord only bestow texts that provide the experiential state of liberation, which is the state of righteousness? He also bestowed texts that provide worldly pleasures and objects for worldly enjoyment, as is understood without explicit mention. In accordance with “He who bestows gold and truth, and unites enjoyment and prosperity,” the Lord here, having researched Tamil, has bestowed not only texts on liberation but also texts that provide enjoyment and worldly objects. The Agamas refer to these two pleasures as Bhoga and Apavarga.

Many historical accounts, including the story of the Lord singing the song “Kongu Ther Vazhkai” and bestowing a golden purse upon Tharumi, illustrate that the Lord has given both enjoyment and worldly possessions.

Therefore, Lord Sokkanatha not only bestows worldly possessions but also dispels sins. That is why Sekkizhar Peruman mentions there, “If the Sangam existed for the Lord who dispels our sins.” Thus, having researched and bestowed Tamil, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, having reached the courtyard of the temple of Lord Somasundara, circumambulated the temple, prostrated before the Lord outside, entered the temple, worshipped Lord Sokkanatha, and was immersed in joy, reveling in a great flood of bliss.

Thus, immersed in that blissful experience, he praised the Lord with the Thiruththāndagam Tamil Pathigam beginning with “Mulaiththanai.” Sekkizhar Swamigal states that Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, who possessed great penance, worshipped with folded hands, praised, and attained great joy in his heart.

Therefore, the Thiruppathigam composed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman at this moment is the Thiruvalavai Thiruppathigam, the Thiruththāndagam Thiruppathigam beginning with “Mulaiththanai Ellaarkkum Munne Thondri.” It is the sixth The sixth Thirumurai, nineteenth Thiruppathigam, Thiruvalavai Thiruppathigam, Thiruththāndagam Thiruppathigam.

Mulaiththanai ellaarkkum munne thondri muthirum sadai mudimel mugizhven thingal valaiththanai valla surarpurangal moonrum varai silaiyaava sugima naana kooththu thulaiththanai sudusaraththaal thuvazhththumuththa venmuruvazh umaiyodaadi thanai thenkoodal thiruvalavai sivanadiye sindhikka petre naane. (He who appeared before all, with the crescent moon on his mature matted hair, who destroyed the three cities of the mighty Asuras with a mountain as his bow, who pierced with a fiery arrow, who danced with Uma of the pearl-like smile, I have been blessed to contemplate the feet of Shiva at Thiruvalavai, the southern Koodal.) Vinnulagin melaargal melaan thannai melaadu puram moonrum podi seythaanai pannilavu paimpozil suzh pazhanthanai. (He who is superior to the celestials, who reduced the three flying cities to dust, who is ancient, surrounded by melodious green groves.) Pasum ponnin niraththanai paal neetranai unnillavu sadai kattrai gangaiyaalai karanthumaiyodudanaagiyirunthan thannai thennillavu thenkoodal thiruvalavai sivanadiye sindhikka petre naane. (He who is the color of pure gold, who has milk-white sacred ash, who hid Ganga in his matted locks and remained with Uma, I have been blessed to contemplate the feet of Shiva at Thiruvalavai, the southern Koodal.) Neer thirazhai neel sadai mel niraiviththanai nilamaruvineeroda kandan thannai paattrirazhai payinraada vallan thannai pagai thezhuntha vengootrai paainthan thannai kaattrirazhaay megaththin ullae nindru kadunguralaayidippaanai kannor netri thee thirazhai thenkoodal thiruvalavai sivanadiye sindhi. (He who filled his long matted locks with water, who saw the water flow on the earth, who is skilled in dancing with the serpent, who leaped upon the fierce Yama who rose as an enemy, who stands within the clouds as a mass of wind and thunders with a harsh voice, who has a fiery eye on his forehead, I have been blessed to contemplate the feet of Shiva at Thiruvalavai, the southern Koodal.) Petre naane. Vaanamithu vellaamooda yaan thannai variyarava kachchaanai vanpesuzh kaanamathil nadamaada vallan thannai kadai kannaal mangaiyumai nokkaayanmel oonamathu vellaam ozhiththan thannai unarvaagiyadiyenathullae nindra thenamuthai thenkoodal thiruvalavai sivanadiye sindhikka petre naane. (I have been blessed. He who is the sky, who is covered by it, who has a striped serpent as his waist-belt, who is skilled in dancing in the forest surrounded by strong ghosts, who removed all imperfections from me when Uma looked at me with her side glance, who is the honeyed nectar residing within me as consciousness, I have been blessed to contemplate the feet of Shiva at Thiruvalavai, the southern Koodal.) Ooraanai ulagezhaay nindran thannai ottrai ven piraiyaanai umaiyodendrum peraanai pirarkendrum ariyaan thannai pinakkaattil nadamaadal peyodendrum. (He who is the town, who stands as the seven worlds, who has a single white crescent moon, who is always with Uma, who is unknown to others, who always dances in the cremation ground with ghosts.)

Aaraanai amarargalukku amuthinthanai arumaraiyaan muganum maalum potrum seeraanai thenkoodal thiruvalavai sivanadiye sindhikka petre naane. (He who is the river, who gave nectar to the celestials, whose glory is praised by Brahma and Vishnu, I have been blessed to contemplate the feet of Shiva at Thiruvalavai, the southern Koodal.) Moovanai moorththiyai moovaame nee udaiyaanai moovulagum thaane engum paavanai paava maruppaan thannai padiyezhuthalaagaatha mangaiyodum mevanai vinnor nadunga kandu virikadalin nanjunda moodam eentha devanai thenkoodal thiruvalavai sivanadiye sindhikka petre naane. (He who is the ancient one, the form, who possesses you without aging, who is the three worlds everywhere, who removes sins through contemplation, who is united with the maiden whose beauty cannot be written, who, seeing the celestials tremble, consumed the poison from the vast ocean and bestowed immortality, I have been blessed to contemplate the feet of Shiva at Thiruvalavai, the southern Koodal.) Thuranthaarku thoo neriya. Nindran thannai thunbam thoodai thaazha vallan thannai iranthaargal enpeya nindran thannai elli nadamaada vallan thannai maranthaar maathin moonrum maayththan thannai mattru oru patttrilla adiyerkkindrum siranthanai thenkoodal thiruvalavai sivanadiye sindhikka petre naane. (He who stands as the pure path for renunciates, who is capable of removing sorrow, who stands as the bones of the deceased, who is skilled in dancing in the night, who destroyed the three cities of those who forgot, who is always superior to me, who has no other refuge, I have been blessed to contemplate the feet of Shiva at Thiruvalavai, the southern Koodal.) Vaayaanai manaththanai manaththul nindra karuththanai karuththarinthu mudippaan thannai thooyaanai thoovellai yetran thannai suda thingal sadaiyaanai thodarnthu nindren thaayaanai thavamaay thanmai yaanai thala. Yaay devaathi devarkendrum seyanaai thenkoodal thiruvalavai sivanadiye sindhikka petre naane. (He who is the mouth, the mind, the thought residing in the mind, who completes thoughts after knowing them, who is pure, who has a pure white bull, who has a fiery moon in his matted hair, who stands as my mother, who is of the nature of penance, who is always distant from the gods of gods, I have been blessed to contemplate the feet of Shiva at Thiruvalavai, the southern Koodal.) Pagai sudaraay paavam aaruppaan thannai pazhiyizhiyaay nanjam andaamuthinthanai vagai sudaraay valla surar puramattanai valaiviliyaay ellaarkkum arul seyvaanai migai sudarai vinnargal melappaalai melaay devaathi devar kendrum thigai sudarai thenkoodal thiruvalavai sivanadiye sindhikka petre naane. (He who is the fiery light that removes sins, who consumed the poison without blemish, who destroyed the cities of the mighty Asuras with various lights, who is the bow-less one who bestows grace upon all, who is the supreme light, superior to the celestials, who is the god of gods, who is the directional light, I have been blessed to contemplate the feet of Shiva at Thiruvalavai, the southern Koodal.) Malaiyaanai maameru manni naanai valarppunjsadaiyaanai vaanorththangal. Thalaiyaanai en thalaiyin uchchi endrum thaapiththirunthaanai thaane engum thulaiyaaga oruvaraiyum illaathaanai thondraathaar mathin moonrum thuvala veytha silaiyaanai thenkoodal thiruvalavai sivanadiye sindhikka petre naane. (He who is the mountain, who is Mount Meru, who has growing matted hair, who is the head of the celestials, who is always established at the crown of my head, who is everywhere, who has no equal, who is the archer who shot down the three cities of those who did not appear, I have been blessed to contemplate the feet of Shiva at Thiruvalavai, the southern Koodal.) Thooraththanai thol mudi patthiruththan thannai thonnarambin innisai kettarul seythaanai paarththanai pani kandu parinthan thannai parinthavarkku paasupatham eenthan thannai aaththanai adiyenu ganpan thannai alavilaa palloozhi kandu nindru theerththanai thenkoodal thiruvala. Vaay sivanadiye sindhikka petre naane.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman composed the Thiruththāndagam in praise of Lord Thiruvalavai. Hearing the news of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman’s arrival in Madurai, King Ninra Seer Nedumaranar Nayanar, Mangaiyarkkarasiyar, and their minister Kulachchirai Nayanar came and praised the sacred feet of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman.

The King of Madurai, Ninra Seer Nedumaranar Nayanar, was formerly of the Jain faith. Due to the influence of the sacred ash bestowed by Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, the Pandya king, who was formerly the hunchbacked Pandya, became Ninra Seer Nedumaranar due to the influence of the sacred ash bestowed by Thirugnanasambandha Peruman. He embraced Shaivism and attained the glory of being one of the sixty-three Nayanmars, becoming instrumental in the flourishing of Shaivism in the Pandya country. The queen of that Pandya king, Mangaiyarkkarasi Perumatti, and the minister Kulachchirai Nayanar, who resided there, were instrumental in such a historical event.

Therefore, these three great personalities came and praised the sacred feet of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman. As they praised, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar sat there and bestowed his grace. Sekkizhar Peruman continues to sing: “He reached Thiru Poovanam, having sung Tamil hymns of great truth, such as Thiru Nerisai and Thandagam, praising the red flame residing in Thiruvalavai, who bestowed the rich literary texts, and having performed sacred service, he burned the cities of his enemies.”

Thus sings Sekkizhar Peruman. He states that Thirunavukkarasu Peruman praised Lord Shiva, the red flame residing in Thiruvalavai, who bestowed the rich Akapporul (love poetry) texts, by singing Tamil hymns such as Thiru Nerisai and Thiruththāndagam.

Here, Sekkizhar Peruman praises Lord Shiva as the bestower of Akapporul texts. The Akapporul text bestowed by the Lord is the Iraiyanar Kalaviyal. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman praises such a Lord by composing many hymns, including Thiru Nerisai and Thiruththāndagam. Although Sekkizhar Peruman mentioned this, the hymn we currently have is the Thiru Nerisai Thiruppathigam, which begins with “Vedhiya Veda Geetha.” This Thiruppathigam is the sixty-second in the fourth Thirumurai. The Thirunerisai Thiruppathigam is located in the sixty-second chapter.

Vedhiya Veda Geetha Vinnavar Annaay Nandrothiya Malargal Thoovi Orungingalulgal Kaana Paathiyor Pennai Vaiththaay Padarsadai Mathiyam Soodum Aathiyae Aalavaayil Appanae Arul Seyyaayae. (O Lord, the Vedic song, the elder of the celestials, who placed half a woman in your spreading matted hair, adorned with the moon, O Primordial One, O Father of Aalavaay, bestow your grace upon me.) Nambanae Naan Mugaththaay Naathanae Gnana Moorththi En Ponnae Eesaayandrea Thinaanae Esattrandrum Pinbinae Thirinthu Naayaen Paerththinae Piravannam Anbanae Aalavaayil Appanae. (O Trustworthy One, O Four-faced One, O Lord, O Embodiment of Wisdom, O my Gold, O Lord, I, a dog, have wandered after you without fault, O Beloved One, O Father of Aalavaay, bestow your grace upon me.) Arul Seyyaayae. Oru Marunthu Aagiyullaay Umbarodu Ulakukkellaam Peru Marunthu Aagi Nindraay Paeramoothin Suvaiyaay Karumarunthu Aagiyullaay Aalum Val Vinaigal Theerkkum Arumarunthu Aalavaayil Appanae Arul Seyyaayae. (O You who are a single medicine, who stand as a great medicine for the celestials and all worlds, who are the taste of great nectar, who are the black medicine, who are the rare medicine that removes ruling strong karmas, O Father of Aalavaay, bestow your grace upon me.) Seyyanin Kamala Paatham Serumaa Devar Devae Maiyani Kanda Thaanae Maanmari Mazhuvaenthum Seyvanae Saala Gnanam Katrari Vee Laathanayaen Aiyanae Aalavaayil Appanae Arul Seyyaayae. (O Lord of Lords, how can I reach your red lotus feet? O Lord with the dark throat, who holds the deer and the axe, O Lord, I am ignorant, having not learned much wisdom, O Master, O Father of Aalavaay, bestow your grace upon me.) Vendalai Kaiyae. (O Lord with the white skull in hand.) Migavum Moor Bali Kondendrum Undathum Illai Sollil Undathu Nanjuthannai Pandunai Ninaiyamaattaa Pazhaganen Ulamathaara Andanae Aalavaayil Appanae Arul Seyyaayae. (You who always take abundant offerings, if I speak of what you ate, you ate poison.

I, an old sinner, could not remember you before, O Lord, O Father of Aalavaay, bestow your grace upon me.) Enjalil Pugazhithendrea Thinaanae Esattrandrum Vanjakam Ondrumindri Malaradi Kaanum Vannam Nanjinai Midattril Vaiththa Narpuru Pathamae Naayar Kanjalendru Aalavaayil Appanae Arul Seyyaayae. (O Lord, whose fame is endless, I, a dog, have always praised you without deceit, so that I may see your lotus feet, O Good One, who held poison in your throat, O Father of Aalavaay, bestow your grace upon me.) Valuvilaathu Vaazhththi Vazhipadum Thondanaen Un Sezhumalar. Paatham Kaana Thindirai Nanjamunda Kuzhaganae Kolavilli Kooththanae Maaththaayulla Azhaganae Aalavaayil Appanae Arul Seyyaayae. (O Youth who consumed the strong ocean poison, O Dancer with the beautiful bow, O Beautiful One who is within me, O Father of Aalavaay, bestow your grace upon me, so that I, your servant, who praises and worships without fault, may see your rich lotus feet.) Narumalar Neerum Kondu Naadorum Eththi Vaazhththi Serivana Siththam Vaiththu Thiruvadi Serum Vannam Marikadal Vannan Paagaa Maamarai Anga Maarum Arivanae Aalavaayil Appanae Arul Seyyaayae. (O Lord, who is the color of the receding ocean, O Lord of the great Vedas and their six ancillaries, O Father of Aalavaay, bestow your grace upon me, so that I may place my concentrated mind and reach your sacred feet, praising and worshipping daily with fragrant flowers and water.) Nalanthigal Vaayin Noolaara Sarugilai Panthar Seytha Silanthiyai Arasathaala Arulinaay Endru Thin. Kalanthudan Vanthu Nindraal Karuthinaan Kaanpathaaga Alantha Nan Aalavaayil Appanae Aarul Seyyaayae. (O Father of Aalavaay, who bestowed grace upon the spider that built a canopy of dry leaves in the mouth of the good one, so that it might rule as a king, if I, who am weary, come and stand with you, thinking to see you, bestow your grace upon me.) Podi Kodu Poosi Pollaa Kurambayir Punthiyondri Pidiththu Nindru Aalgal Endrum Pithattrinaan Irukka Maattaen Eduppunindru Ilangai Kon Vandeththum Irupathu Thol Adarththanae Aalavaayil Appanae Arul Seyyaayae. (O Father of Aalavaay, who crushed the twenty shoulders of the King of Lanka who came to lift Mount Kailash, I cannot remain, having smeared myself with sacred ash, holding onto this evil body with a united mind, always babbling. Bestow your grace upon me.)

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, having composed the Thiruppathigams in Thiruvalavai, then proceeds to the holy site of Thiruppoovanam. Let us resume our reflection. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 468. Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having worshipped Thiru-Alavai Chokkanatha Peruman and sung hymns, reaches the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Poovanam. This sacred sthalam is one of the fourteen Devaram-sung temples in the Pandya country.

It is located near Madurai on the road to Rameswaram. It is a wonderful sacred sthalam situated on the southern bank of the Vaigai River. This is the only sthalam in the Pandya country sung by the Three Saints (Moovar Devaram). Although it is referred to as Thiru-Poovanam in the Devarams, it is currently known as Thiru-Bhuvanam. This sacred sthalam, Thiru-Poovanam, possesses countless glories. The sacred name of the Lord is Pushpavaneswarar, Poovananathar.

The sacred name of the Goddess is Soundarya Nayaki, Min Anaiyal. The sthala-vriksham is the jackfruit tree. The Theertham is the Vaigai Theertham. As we have already seen, this is the only sacred sthalam in the Pandya country sung by the Three Saints: Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, Appar Swamigal, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal.

Furthermore, Karuvoor Devar has sung about this sthalam in the Ninth Thirumurai. Manikkavasaga Swamigal has sung in Thiruvasagam, Keerthi Thiru Agaval, “Polindhu irundhu aruli.” In Thiruvasagam, Potri Thiru Agaval, he has sung, “Poruppu amar Poovanathu Arane Potri.” To dispel the darkness of Jainism in the Pandya country and to make Saivism flourish, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, before proceeding to Thiru-Alavai, arrives at Thiru-Poovanam, which serves as the eastern boundary of Madurai. This temple is situated on the bank of the Vaigai River. From this bank of the Vaigai River, he worships Thiru-Poovananathar on the opposite bank.

At that moment, all the sands of the Vaigai River appear as Shiva Lingams.

Therefore, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, fearing to tread on the river sands, sings and worships the Lord from that bank. Lord Shiva, hearing the song, asks Nandi to move aside and grants darshan to Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, who is singing from the opposite bank of the river. Even today, Nandi is situated in a displaced position at Thiru-Poovanam. Goddess Parvati, to atone for sins committed knowingly, came to this sacred sthalam, cultivated a Parijatha tree, and performed penance beneath it.

At that time, Lord Shiva, manifested as a Shiva Lingam beneath that tree and graciously absolved the sins of Umaiyamai. Surya worshipped this Shiva Lingam and received the boon of being the leader of all Navagrahas. This is the sacred sthalam where Brahma Devan’s knowingly committed sins were absolved. This is the sacred sthalam where Maha Vishnu obtained the Chakra-ayudham to slay Salandharan. This is the sacred sthalam where Kali Devi installed and worshipped a Shiva Lingam. This is the sacred sthalam where Thiranasanan attained liberation.

This is the sacred sthalam where the great sinner Thunmanjyan attained a good destiny. This is the sacred sthalam where the bones in the ash-urn brought by the Brahmin Dharmagnan all transformed into flowers. This is the sacred sthalam where the woman Utpalangi received the boon of obtaining a good husband and living as a long-married woman. This is the sacred sthalam that removes sins committed knowingly. This is the sacred sthalam that absolved the curse of Thiru-Magal. This is the sacred sthalam where the ancestors of King Suchchothi came in person, received the Pindam, and blessed him.

This is a sacred sthalam with many Theerthams. This is the sacred sthalam where Salandharan, a frog, was granted the boon of being an emperor. This is the sacred sthalam that removed the suffering of Kaliyuga from King Nala and granted him peace of mind. This is the place where Lord Shiva imparted the auspicious Upadesam of Thiruchitrambalam to the sages Manthiyanthina and Dhyana Katta. This is the sacred sthalam where Thazhambu worshipped Lord Shiva to be absolved of the sin of falsehood. This is the sacred sthalam where the Three Kings came together, worshipped, and paid tribute.

This is the sacred sthalam where Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal worshipped and sang Devaram. This is the sacred sthalam sung by Manikkavasaga Peruman. This is the sacred sthalam where Karuvoor Devar’s Thiruvisaippa was sung. This is the sacred sthalam where Arunagirinathar’s Thiruppugazh was sung. This is the sacred sthalam where Lord Shiva of Madurai, Chokkalinga Peruman, came in the form of a Siddhar, performed alchemy, and enacted divine plays. This is the sthalam where he came and bestowed grace upon Pon Anaiyal.

Thus, Thiru-Poovanam sthalam shines forth, ancient and possessing great glories. Based on the principles of Vastu Shastra related to geographical location, Thiru-Poovanam sthalam serves as the Vastu Mukha Mandalam of the Pandya country. The Theerthams here are called Papanasa Theertham, Vaigai River, Manikkarnikai or Devi Kundam, Brahma Theertham, Lakshmi Theertham, Markandeya Theertham, Nala Theertham, Vasishta Theertham, Chandra Theertham, and others. As for the sthala-vrikshams, in the first Yuga, it was the Parijatha tree; in the second Yuga, the Vilva tree; in the third Yuga, the Vanni tree; and in this Kali Yuga, it is the jackfruit tree. The Lord, who manifests as a Swayambhu Lingam, is known here by the sacred names Poovananathar, Pushpavananathar, Pushpavaneswarar, Bhaskarapuriy Eesar, Pithur Moksha Pureesar, Brahmapureesar, Rahasya Chidambara, Thiru-Poovaneswarar, and Adaivarvinai Theerppavar. The Utsavamoorthy has the sacred names Soundarya Nayagar, Azhagiya Nayagar, and Ponnanaiyan.

The sacred names of the Goddess are Soundarya Nayaki, Thadithambai, Swarnavalli, Annapoorani, Azhagiya Nayaki, Azhagiya Minnanaiyal, and Minnamai.

Here, the Lord, as a Swayambhu Lingam, is made of Parijatha flowers. Similar to the Madurai temple structure, the Goddess’s shrine is located to the right of the Lord’s sanctum. Thiru-Poovanam serves as the eastern gateway to Madurai.

Therefore, it is considered auspicious to worship Madurai Meenakshi Sundareswarar after worshipping Thiru-Poovananathar. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman worshipped Thiru-Poovananathar, received grace, and then went to Madurai to defeat the Jains. There is an Aadithapasu Mandapam at the place where the Goddess performed penance in the month of Aadi. For this sthalam, there is a Sthala Puranam in Sanskrit, which was translated into Tamil and sung by a poet named Kandasamy Pulavar. The glories of Thiru-Poovanam sthalam are also extensively sung in Kadambavana Puranam and Thiruvilaiyadal Puranam. Thiru-Poovanam has other names such as Devipuram, Pushpavanam, Lakshmipuram, Brahmapuram, Bhaskarapuram, Anandavanam, Muthiyashramam, Rahasya Thiruchitrambalam, Dakshina Kasi, Chathurvedapuram, and Pithirmukthipuram.

To such a sacred sthalam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman arrives. Sekkizhar Peruman sings: “He worshipped the Lord residing in Thiru-Poovanam, adorned with lofty mansions and flags, who is beyond the comprehension of even the great Vishnu, and praised Him with the ‘Vadiveru Thirusoolam Thandakam’, then bowed to the sacred place where the holy body is covered in ash.” Thus, the Lord residing in Thiru-Poovanam, adorned with flags and mansions, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman worships Lord Shiva.

At that time, Lord Shiva manifests and bestows grace upon Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman.

Here, the Lord stood directly before Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman inside the temple and revealed His sacred form, granting darshan. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, seeing this vision part by part, worshipped each part individually and firmly praised it by repeating “Thondrum Thondrum” (appears, appears) through his Thiruthandaga Thiruppathigam.

Thus, the Thiruppathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman upon the Lord’s direct manifestation is the Thiru-Poovanam Thiruppathigam, which begins with “Vadiveru Thirusoolam Thondrum Thondrum.” This Thiruppathigam is the eighteenth Thiruppathigam of the Sixth Thirumurai, a Thiruthandaga Thiruppathigam.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped Thiru-Poovanam, visited many other sacred places and reached the sacred sthalam of Rameswaram. We shall continue our reflection. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 469. Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having worshipped Thiru-Poovanam, visited many sacred places and reached Rameswaram. Thiru-Rameswaram is a very famous Kshetram in Bharat.

It is the aim of every person born in Bharat to undertake a pilgrimage to Kashi and Rameswaram at least once. Everyone born in Bharat Desam would have thought of, visited, and worshipped these sacred places. Such is the glorious sthalam known as Rameswaram, or Thiru-Rameswaram.

The Lord is known as Rama Nathar, Rameswarar, and Ramalinga Swamy. The sacred name of the Goddess is Parvathavar, Malai Valar Kathali. The sthala-vriksham is the Vilva tree. Rameswaram is a famous sthalam for performing Theertham.

Therefore, we can reflect on the Theerthams located in Rameswaram, along with the Sthala Purana stories and special features of the sthalam, in detail. The Rameswaram Sthala Puranam is a well-known Sthala Puranam. To absolve the sin of killing Ravana, Sri Rama Peruman, along with Sita and Lakshmana, installed a Shiva Lingam and worshipped it; he performed Shiva Puja. This Rameswaram is one of the fourteen Devaram-sung temples in the Pandya country. This sthalam has hymns sung by Appar Swamigal and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal visited this sacred sthalam, but the Thiruppathigam he composed is not available to us.

Furthermore, Rameswaram is one of the twelve Jyotirlingams. Rameswaram stands as the southern boundary of Bharat. “A Sethu Himachalam” is a famous saying, meaning that the land from Sethu to Himachal is Bharat Khandam, Bharat Desam. It is our country’s tradition for those who undertake Kashi Yatra to come to Rameswaram and complete their Kashi Yatra. It is our country’s tradition to perform Abhishekam to Ramanatha Swamy with the Ganga Prayagai Theerthams brought from Kashi. The island of Rameswaram is located in the southeastern corner of Ramanathapuram district in Tamil Nadu.

One can reach the island of Rameswaram by crossing the Pamban Canal. Rameswaram also has the names Devanagaram and Devai. The island of Rameswaram resembles the shape of Vishnu’s Valampuri conch. Rama Peruman, after slaying Ravana and other Rakshasas in Lanka, rescued Sita Devi and came to reside on Gandhamadhana Parvatham on the island of Rameswaram. He desired to install a Shiva Lingam to absolve the sin of slaying the Rakshasas. He summoned Hanuman and commanded him to go to Kailash and bring a Shiva Lingam.

Hanuman proceeded accordingly. As Hanuman was delayed in returning, Rama Peruman decided that the Shiva Lingam should be installed at an auspicious time. He consecrated and worshipped a Lingam made of sand by Sita Devi. That Lingam came to be known as Ramalingar, Ramanathar, and Rameswarar, and the place as Rameswaram. The Lingam brought by Hanuman, located to the north, is known as Visweswarar, Kashi Lingam, and Hanumalingam. This history associated with Rameswaram is a history known to all of us.

In the shape of a conch, The sacred temple is located near the sea, northeast of Rameswaram Island. Lord Shiva, the master of Rama, is enshrined here with the holy name Rameswarar, the Ishwara of Rama. The Ramanathar shrine faces east. The first thing visitors to the temple see is the west gopuram entrance. There are four chariot-drawing streets surrounding the temple, and entrances on all four sides. To the east, there are two entrances directly facing the Lord’s shrine and the Goddess’s shrine.

The east gopuram of the Ramanatha shrine faces the sea and is of considerable height. Upon entering the temple through the east gopuram entrance, to the right is the Anjaneyar shrine. He faces south, and his sacred form appears reddish. After worshipping Hanuman, proceed through the Anuppu Mandapam. Through the mandapam, one can reach the flagstaff, where there is a large Nandi made of stucco. Before entering the gateway from here, there are shrines for Ganapathi and Murugan on both sides.

After worshipping them, one can enter and reach the first circumambulatory path. In the southeast corner of this path are Surya, Usha, Pratyusha, and Sahasralingam. On the southern wall of the sanctum sanctorum is a depiction of the Lord’s Kailasa scene, with a five-headed serpent above and a tortoise supporting everything below; this is a magnificent sculpture. In the southern circumambulatory path are the shrines of the Nalvar (four great Shaivite saints) and the processional and main idols of the sixty-three Nayanmars. In the western circumambulatory path are Vajreswarar, Manonmani, Kandan, Sankaranarayana, Ardhanareeswarar, Kangalanathar, Chandrasekar, and others. In the northern circumambulatory path are Ekadasarudras, meaning eleven lingams, and Visalakshi.

Jyotirlingam and Natarajar shrines are located here. The eleven lingams consecrated and worshipped by Rama, Lakshmana, Sita, Hanuman, Vibhishana, Sugriva, Angada, Jambavan, Nala, Nila, and Indra are considered important here. The Jyotirlingam is made of crystal and is said to have been consecrated by Vibhishana. In the Natarajar shrine, there are two Natarajar idols. In the northern part of the eastern circumambulatory path, idols of Chandra, Krittika, and Rohini are seen.

Afterwards, one can proceed towards the Ramanatha Swamy shrine. The Ramalingamurthy faces east. To the north of his shrine, facing east, is the Kasi Viswanathar shrine. The lingam here is the one brought by Hanuman. The pujas and other rituals are first performed for this idol brought by Hanuman. In the Ramalingesar shrine, In the southern part of the front mandapam are the idols of Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana.

In front, Sugriva is depicted with his hand near his mouth, bowing his head in supplication. His feet are those of a monkey. Hanuman stands holding two lingams in his two hands. We can admire and worship this beautiful sculpture well. Opposite these figures, facing south, is a separate Anjaneyar. One of the must-see attractions in the Lord’s temple is the Utsava Nandikeswarar, who appears in the form of Hanuman.

He is depicted with two hands clasped in prayer and two hands holding a deer and a battle-axe. After worshipping Ramanatha Swamy, one can proceed to the Goddess’s shrine through the entrance in the first southern circumambulatory path. The shrine faces east. The Goddess’s holy names are Malai Valar Kathali and Parvatavardhini. A form full of beauty and grace. Upon entering the shrine, in the southeast corner of the circumambulatory path, facing east, is Kalyana Sundareswarar.

Beside him, facing north, are beautiful forms of Brahma and Vishnu. In the southern corner of the western circumambulatory path are Soubhagya Ganapathi and Santana Ganapathi. In the same circumambulatory path are the forms of the Sapta Kanniyar (Seven Maidens), including Brahmi, Maheswari, Kaumari, Vaishnavi, Varahi, Mahendri, and Chamundi. In the northwest corner, Pallikonda Perumal grants his service. In the northern circumambulatory path is the Chandikeswari shrine, and in the northeast corner is the Palliyarai (bedchamber). In the Sukravara Mandapam in front of the Ambika shrine, facing east, are the Ashtalakshmi idols.

In the same mandapam, on the eight pillars on the northern side, are the forms of Mahendri, Kaumari, Rajarajeswari, Lakshmi, Kali, Chamundi, and Dvarapalika. On the eight pillars on the southern side are the Dvarapalikas. Dvarapalika, Sivadurga, Manonmani, Vakkiswari, Sethupathi, Kadambathevar, Pradhani, Bhuvaneswari, and Annapoorna are enshrined here. Behind the Ramanatha Swamy shrine is the Perumal shrine named Sethu Madhavar. The circumambulatory paths of this sacred temple are world-renowned. As one circumambulates the third path, one can delight in its immense beauty.

The circumambulatory paths are four thousand feet long, seventeen to twenty-one feet wide, and the upper mandapam is thirty feet high from ground level.

Now, we must examine the sacredness of the Tirthas (holy waters) of this place. It is said that there are about sixty-four Tirthas in and around this sacred place. Some texts mention fifty-six. Although the names of some Tirthas are known, information about their current location is unavailable. In the Sthala Purana, which is the Sethu Purana, and in the Thevai Ula, Twenty-four Tirthas are mentioned as being excellent. They are as follows: Sethu Tirtham.

This is located at the southeastern tip of Rameswaram Island. People refer to it as Punya Sethu, Rama Sethu, and Holy Sethu. It is a tradition that one must bathe in Sethu before proceeding to Rameswaram. In Sanskrit, Sethu means bridge. Since Lord Rama built a bridge here to go to Lanka, it acquired the name Rama Sethu. The Sethu Punya Tirtha Ghat is located at the confluence of the Bay of Bengal and the Indian Ocean, known as Mahodadhi and Ratnakaram.

Rameswaram Island is shaped like a bow. Its southeastern tip is called Dhanushkodi because Lord Rama broke the bridge with the tip of his bow here, hence the name. The first bath in the Ratnakaram of Sethu is taken. They first bathe in this. This is called Malaneeka Mulukku, Malavimochana Snanam (bath for removal of impurities). It is a tradition that thirty-six baths should be taken in this holy tirtha over thirty-six days.

People also perform ancestral rites here. On the new moon days of Aadi and Thai months, and on all new moon days, people bathe here. During auspicious times like Ardhodaya and Mahodaya, Ramanatha Swamy goes with the Panchamurthis to offer tirtha.

At that time, more than a lakh of people bathe and worship the Lord. The Sethu Purana extols its greatness, stating that merely remembering, praising, or seeing the long Dhanushkodi makes it easy to attain liberation. Lord Rama, showing this Sethu Tirtha to Sita Devi, describes its greatness as follows: “O Sita, even the Ganga, residing in Lord Shiva’s matted locks, performs great penance, wishing to attain the blessing of being Sethu.”

Thus, Lord Rama explains the glory of Sethu Tirtha to Sita. The Sthala Purana states that the sin of Ashwatthama for killing those asleep, the madness of Dharmagupta, the crime of Paravasu for killing a Brahmin, and the great sin of Sumathi were all absolved after bathing in this Tirtha. Next is Agni Tirtham. This is the sea to the east of the Ramanathar Temple street. It is customary to bathe here and perform ancestral rites. Dushpunniyan, who suffered from a ghost, got rid of his affliction by bathing in this Tirtha.

Next is Mahalakshmi Tirtham. This is the holy pond south of the Hanuman temple on the East Gopuram street. Dharmaraja bathed here and gained wealth. Next are Gayatri, Savitri, and Saraswati Tirthams. These three are wells north of the East Gopuram. Kashyapa’s curse was removed by bathing here.

Next is Sethu Madhava Tirtham, west of the three. In the first circumambulatory path, south of the Sethu Madhavar temple, is a beautiful holy pond. Those who bathe here will receive the grace of Lakshmi and purity of mind. Next are Kandamadana Tirtham, Gavaksha Tirtham, Gavaya Tirtham, Nala Tirtham, and Nila Tirtham. These five are located around the Sethu Madhavar temple. Those who bathe here will also receive the benefits of yagnas, be relieved of poverty, gain wealth, and attain liberation.

Next is Sanku Tirtham. This is in the northern second circumambulatory path, near the treasury. By bathing here, Vatsanabha Muni removed the sin of ingratitude. Next is Chakra Tirtham or Muni Tirtham, located in the eastern second circumambulatory path. History states that Surya bathed here and obtained golden hands. Next are Brahmakathi Vimochana Tirtham, Surya Tirtham, and Chandra Tirtham.

These are in the northern inner circumambulatory path. Bathing here removes the sin of Brahmakathi and grants knowledge of the three periods of time. Next is Ganga. Yamuna and Gaya Tirthas are also located in the northern inner circumambulatory path of the temple. History states that King Gnanasruthi attained wisdom by bathing here. Next is Shiva Tirtham or Sivaganga, a beautiful small pond south of the large Nandi, between the Lord’s and Goddess’s shrines.

Next is Sathyamirtha Tirtham, a well south of the Sukravara Chowkai in the Goddess’s shrine. Emperor Pururavas removed Thumburu’s curse by bathing here. Next is Sarva Tirtham, a well in the southeast of the first circumambulatory path in the Ramanathar shrine. Sudarshana, who was born blind and suffered from gray hair, wrinkles, and old age, was cured by bathing here. Next is Koti Tirtham, a well near the Visalakshi Amman shrine in the northern first circumambulatory path. No one can directly draw water and bathe here; a Brahmin on duty must draw and pour it for them.

This is considered superior to all other Tirthas. After bathing in this, It is a tradition that no one should stay in Rameswaram. That is why it is called Koti Tirtham, the last Tirtha. People usually carry this water in kalasams. It is a tradition that this water never spoils. Lord Krishna bathed in this Tirtha and absolved himself of the sin of killing Kamsa.

Those who bathe here will attain desired accomplishments and liberation through knowledge. The twenty-two Tirthas mentioned above, from Mahalakshmi Tirtham to Koti Tirtham, are all located within the Rameswaram temple. Their locations can be learned from assistants when visiting the temple, and one can bathe in them according to tradition.

Now, let us systematically look at the Tirthas located in and around the Rameswaram temple and the sacred site of Rameswaram.

First, Uppur Vinayaka Samudram. This is the sea in the village of Uppur, a short distance north of Devipattinam. The deity enshrined here is Veyilugandha Vinayagar. Next is Thirupparkadal Ksheerakundam. This is near Thiruppalakudi on the way from Uppur to Devipattinam. Next is Devipattinam.

This is the place where the Navapashana Navagrahas are located.

Here, the Navagrahas are in the sea water. They were consecrated by Lord Rama. Those who circumambulate and bathe here will be relieved of Navagraha doshas. Next is Chakra Tirtham. This is Dharma Pushkarani, a holy pond in Devipattinam. This is the Tirtha where Chakrathazhwar received liberation from his curse.

Next is Vedala Varada Tirtham. From Mandapam, one goes to the village of Vettilai Mandapam, and from there, a short distance away is a place called Vedala. The Tirtha here is Vedala Varada Tirtham. By bathing here, Sudarshanan, a Gandharva, was freed from his Vedala form. Next is Papa Vinasa Tirtham, near Mandapam. Near the place called Mandapam, if you go to Vettilai Mandapam, this Tirtha is there.

Next are Bhairava Kapi Tirthams. These are also near the place called Pamban. Rambha was freed from her curse by bathing in Kapi Tirtham. Next is Sita Kundam. It is north of the village of Thangachimadam and east of Kapi Tirtham.

Here, Indra removed the sin of Brahmakathi. Next is Mangala Tirtham. This is on the south side of Thangachimadam road. Next is Amrita Vapi. This is a well inside the Ekanta Rama Swamy temple near the village of Thangachimadam. Next is Runa Vimochana Tirtham.

This is north of the road near the Ekanta Rama Swamy temple. Next is Villoorani. This is north of Runa Vimochana Tirtham, near the seashore. Lord Rama created this by piercing the ground with his bow to quench Sita’s thirst. Although near the seashore, it has very good, sweet water. This is it.

Next is Lakshmana Tirtham. This is a holy pond a short distance away on the road west of the Rameswaram temple. This pond was created by Lakshmana for the consecration of a Shiva lingam and for performing ablutions. This Tirtha is where Balarama’s Brahmakathi dosha was removed. Next is Rama Tirtham. This is a holy pond east of Lakshmana Tirtham.

On its upper bank is an ancient Rama temple. Next are Sugriva Tirtham, Angada Tirtham, Jambava Tirtham, Dharma Tirtham, Bhima Tirtham, Arjuna Tirtham, Nakula Tirtham, Sahadeva Tirtham, and Draupadi Tirthams. All these are east of Gandamadanam. Next is Hanumakundam, north of the temple’s outer street. Next is Agastya Tirtham, outside the temple, in the northeast direction, north of Agni Tirtham. Next is Naga Tirtham, in the garden behind the Devasthanam building on Rameswaram East Street.

It is said that all Tirthas, including the Ganga, come here to cleanse themselves of their sins. Next is Jata Makuta Tirtham, also known as Jatayu Tirtham. This is a holy pond on a sand dune near the Kodandaramaswamy temple, on the path to Dhanushkodi, east of Rameswaram. It is said that Rama and Lakshmana washed their matted hair here. There are also Deva Tirtham, Vibhishana Tirtham, Gaja Tirtham, Sarabha Tirtham, Kumuda Tirtham, Hara Tirtham, and Panasa Tirtham. These are all mentioned in the Sthala Puranas, including the Sethu Purana.

Now, other temples in Rameswaram include the Ekanta Rama Temple, Kattuppillaiyar Temple, Gandamadana Parvatam, Nambi Nayaki Amman Temple, Kodandarama Temple, Ujjaini Mahakali Temple. When Tayumanava Swamigal once visited Rameswaram, people were suffering from drought. At their request, he sang a song: “If Saivism is the religion, and the deity of that religion is the crescent-moon-crowned deity, then if attaining liberation is to conquer the five senses and be immersed in a flood of bliss, then let the sky pour rain.”

At that moment, clouds gathered, and heavy rain fell.

Next, he sang a hymn called ‘Malai Valar Kathali Pathigam’ in praise of Parvatavardhini Ambika.

Now, let’s look at the method of Sethu Rameswaram pilgrimage.

First, we should begin our Sethu Rameswaram pilgrimage from Uppur, located northeast of Ramanathapuram. We should start the pilgrimage by worshipping Veyilugandha Vinayagar in Uppur. From there, we should go south to Devipattinam, worship Navapashanam, bathe in all the Tirthas we have already seen in places like Mandapam and Pamban, and then proceed to Dhanushkodi. After bathing in that holy Sethu, we should come to Rameswaram and, as we have already seen, bathe in many Tirthas and worship Ramanatha Swamy. Finally, after bathing in Koti Tirtham, one should leave Rameswaram without staying there. It is stated in the Ananda Ramayana that Lord Rama returned for a Sethu pilgrimage after his coronation in Ayodhya.

After leaving Rameswaram in this manner, one should bathe in the Adi Sethu beach south of Ramanathapuram and then worship Perumal at Darbhasayanam or Thiruppullani, which is north of it. Afterwards, one should come to Ramanathapuram and see the stone inscription in the Ramalinga Vilasam palace, which commemorates Lord Rama crowning Guha, the Adi Sethupathi, as the last part of the pilgrimage. One can complete the Sethu and Rameswaram pilgrimage by visiting and worshipping at Uthirakosamangai, a Shiva temple southwest of Ramanathapuram. The glories of Rameswaram and Sethu are mentioned in many Sanskrit and Tamil texts. The greatness of Rameswaram and Sethu is mentioned in Rig Veda, Taittiriya Samhita, Valmiki Ramayana, Adhyatma Ramayana, Ananda Ramayana, Agneya Purana, Bhagavata Purana, Padma Purana, Brahmanda Purana, Matsya Purana, Manu Smriti, Kalava Smriti, Gautama Smriti, Parashara Smriti, and others. In Kambar Ramayanam, in the Yuddha Kandam, in the Meetchi Padalam, in seven verses, and in the Poosai Padalam, in twenty-one verses, Rama describes the greatness of Sethu to Sita and consecrates and worships the Shiva Lingam.

Two full verses praise this sacred place. The Thiruvilaiyadal Puranam praises Rameswaram. We saw earlier that Tayumanava Swamigal sang a song praying for rain when he came to Rameswaram, and also a song in praise of Ramanathar. Parvatavardhini, enshrined in Rameswaram, Has been graced with the ‘Malai Valar Kathali Pathigam,’ a hymn of eight verses. Nirambu Azhagiya Desikar composed the Sthala Purana called ‘Sethu Purana.’ Palapattadai Sokkanatha Pulavar authored the work ‘Thevai Ula.’ Six daily worship services are grandly performed in this sacred temple. Annually, three major festivals are celebrated with grandeur in the Ramalingam Peruman temple during the months of Aani, Aadi, and Masi.

Besides these, smaller festivals are also held occasionally. When we remember the holy Sethu, we must also remember the Sethupathi kings, its protectors. According to puranic tradition, they belonged to the lineage of Guha. The Sethupathi kings built and protected the Rameswaram temple and performed great renovation works. These are the puranic stories and notes about the sacred site of Rameswaram, and notes about the Tirthas. We find many references to sacred places in the Periya Puranam.

It is our tradition that when a reference or song about a sacred place first appears in the Periya Puranam, we contemplate as much as possible on the purana and details related to that place before continuing. Accordingly, the mention of the sacred place Rameswaram first appears here in the Periya Puranam at this point.

Therefore, we have contemplated a little about this sacred place.

Now, let us continue to contemplate the sacred hymn composed by Appar Swamigal for the sacred place of Thiru Rameswaram. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 470. Thirunindrachirukkam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman proceeds to the sacred site of Rameswaram. Lord Shiva, who absolved Lord Rama of the great sin incurred by felling the ten heads of Ravana of Southern Lanka, is enshrined here in Rameswaram as Ramanatha Swamy.

Thirunavukkarasu Peruman goes and worships this Lord Shiva. The history discussed and spoken of in the Ramayana is known to all of us. Lord Rama was the one who defeated Ravana by severing his ten heads. It was Ramanatha Swamy who absolved Lord Rama of the great sin that came upon him for killing Ravana in this manner. If one asks whether killing Ravana would incur a great sin, Sivakavimani explains it thus: Ravana was learned in the Vedas, a man of penance, a worshipper of Shiva, and a great warrior. He possessed such qualities.

Therefore, killing such a Ravana, who possessed these qualities, was considered a great sin. Not only that, Ravana was guilty of desiring another man’s wife, Sita. Even though Ravana was guilty of desiring another’s wife, the punishment of severing his head is considered excessive. It is considered too much. Besides the sin of killing Ravana, other male and female rakshasas, and children, were also killed there. The entire Lanka was destroyed.

Therefore, due to these actions, it was called a great sin. That is why the great sin that came upon Lord Rama for defeating Ravana was absolved by Lord Shiva, who is enshrined in Rameswaram. The king of words, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, sings, “Remembering to worship the one who absolved Rama, the king who severed the ten heads of Ravana of Southern Lanka, of the great sin that came upon him, he went with great joy, his heart melting, and worshipped.” The entire sacred hymn composed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman for Thiru Rameswaram sings of Rama’s act of killing Ravana and Rama’s act of worshipping Lord Shiva.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman went to Thiru-Rameswaram, stood before the Lord, and sang many Thiru-Nerisaigal and other Tamil hymns in praise. He performed sacred services there and resided there.

Now, among the Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, we have one Thiru-Nerisaigal Thiru-Pathigam. This is the sixty-first Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai.

The Thiru-Rameswaram where the glorious one resided, where the Lord, who destroyed the demons unable to shed their attachments, built a temple with fragrant flowers and wisdom, remember Him with intense love every day. The temple built by the Lord who destroyed the senseless demons with battles, with the intention of ending the days that had come to an end. O heart, praise Thiru-Rameswaram! The temple built by the Lord, who, with His matted locks, blocked the mountains in the sea and completed His task. I, impure, with my tongue, keep Thiru-Rameswaram, the temple built by the Lord, who, with His matted locks, blocked the mountains in the sea and completed His task, in my mind.

I, tormented by the five senses that do not leave my body, am like a mountain. The temple built by the Lord, who, with His matted locks, blocked the mountains in the sea and completed His task, is good. O heart, you have attained goodness. Go and worship Thiru-Rameswaram and be saved. The temple built by the Lord, who, showing His mighty teeth, killed the tall demon and cast him into the sea. Those who gather with great devotion will have their desires fulfilled at Thiru-Rameswaram.

The Lord, who, with great love, gathered those demons and fought. The Lord, who destroyed those who fought fiercely, built the temple of Thiru-Rameswaram. O foolish heart, join the Lord with the red matted locks. Those who do not speak sweet words with their mouths, the Lord, who consumed their lives, built the temple of Thiru-Rameswaram with abundant water. If one looks at it, the diseases and karmas of those who worship will diminish. The Lord, who, after many days of evil, gathered against Parthan and killed the cruel demons, built the temple of Thiru-Rameswaram with His bow.

Those who worship with their heads will not diminish their penance. The Lord, who, after performing great penances and destroying them all with His discus, then with love, built the temple of Thiru-Rameswaram. O heart, seeking life, that is the good path. The life of the cruel demons. The Lord, who, not knowing anything, became sorrowful and fought, built the temple of Thiru-Rameswaram. Those who can reach it with gold will not diminish in the presence of the Lord.

The Lord, who, after destroying the demon with the high crown like mountains, built the temple again. Those who speak of Thiru-Rameswaram, which worships with waves of pearls, with ten words, will be filled with love.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman stayed in Thiru-Rameswaram for many days and received the grace of Lord Shiva.

Then, with the permission of Lord Shiva, he left that place and traveled to the Pandya country, surrounded by fertile Tamil land, visiting and worshipping all the sacred places, including Thiru-Nelveli and Thiru-Kaanapperu.

Here, Sekkizhar Peruman mentions that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman visited and worshipped at Thiru-Nelveli. However, we do not have any Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Nelveli. Sekkizhar Peruman also mentions that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman visited and worshipped at Thiru-Kaanapperu. This Thiru-Kaanapperu is now known as Kaalaiyar Kovil.

Here, the deity is called Kaaleeswarar, and therefore, this place is known as Kaalaiyar Kovil. We do not have any Thiru-Pathigam by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for this place.

Similarly, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman visited and worshipped many other places in the Pandya country. These many places must have included other sacred places in the Pandya country, such as Thiru-Chuzhiyal and Thiru-Kutralam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman mentioned Thiru-Chuzhiyal. In the Kaappu Thiru-Thandagam for Thiru-Adhigai Veerattanam, he sang it as a Vaippu-Thalam.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman must have visited and worshipped many sacred places in the Pandya country, including Thiru-Chuzhiyal. However, those Thiru-Pathigams are not available to us now.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman visited and worshipped many sacred places, sang rich Tamil hymns composed of various word-chains, performed flawless sacred services, and with a melting heart, with eyes always shedding tears, and with a mind constantly embracing the sacred feet of Lord Shiva, he lived in this manner. After visiting and worshipping the Lord in many sacred places in the beautiful Tamil land of Pandya country, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman then proceeded to the Chola country, where the river Kaveri flows.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having arrived in the Chola country, Peruman now visits and worships many of the sacred places he had previously worshipped and rejoiced in. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, the unique ascetic sage, thus visited many sacred places in the Chola country and arrived at Thiru-Poompugaloor, a sacred place in the Chola country. It is in this Thiru-Poompugaloor that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is to attain liberation. The Puranam of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, which has a total of four hundred and twenty-nine verses, mentions in the four hundred and twelfth verse that he arrived at Thiru-Poompugaloor.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, in the final part of his incarnation, at Thiru-Poompugaloor, He arrives at this sacred place in the state of attaining liberation. He stays in this place for some time and performs sacred services.

Then he is about to attain Sayujya Mukti with the Lord. This is the concluding part of the Puranam of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar. He comes to Thiru-Poompugaloor, performs sacred services, and composes various Thiru-Pathigams. After contemplating all those Thiru-Pathigams, we will continue to contemplate the Puranam of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part Four Hundred and Seventy-One, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Having visited many sacred places in the Pandya country and many sacred places in the Chola country, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman arrives at the sacred place called Thiru-Pugalur. It is in this sacred place called Thiru-Pugalur that Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal is to attain liberation. We have contemplated the special features of Thiru-Pugalur, also known as Pugalur, in the history of Muruga Nayanar. Pugalur means a place where souls, fearing rebirth, take refuge as a refuge.

Sekkizhar Swamigal mentions Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s arrival at Thiru-Poompugaloor, Thiru-Pugalur, saying, “He arrived at Poompugaloor to remove false attachments.” He sings that he arrives at Thiru-Pugalur to remove false attachments. False attachments here refer to the continuation of this worldly state. This continuation of the worldly state is about to be severed for Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman here.

Therefore, he mentions, “He will remove false attachments.” On his way to Thiru-Pugalur, when many sacred places he had already visited were along the way, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman visited them again and then came to Thiru-Pugalur.

Therefore, the tradition that when one goes on a pilgrimage, even if the places along the way are ones we have already visited, we should visit them again, is conveyed to us here. Pugalur, Poompugaloor, is surrounded by ponds and has a sacred temple. It has a sacred temple.

There, the pure Lord Shiva resides. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, with a heart melting with love, worships the lotus-like feet of Lord Shiva and stays there, going before the Lord every day to worship. He performs sacred services with his hands. During the days he stayed there with great love, he composed countless rich Tamil garlands of Thevaram Thiru-Pathigams. The Thevaram Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman are hymns that convey to us the essence of the Vedas. They are hymns that teach us the ultimate truths of Saiva Siddhanta and the conclusions of the Vedas.

Such Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman composed many such countless Thiru-Pathigams.

Here, Sekkizhar Peruman sings about the types of Thiru-Pathigams Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman composed during his stay in Thiru-Pugalur: “He composed Nindra Thiru-Thandagam, Needu Thani-Thandagam, Vazhuthu Thiru-Thandagam praising the places where those who speak in the assembly reside, Kuraindhadaindha Nerisai where the Lord with Kondrai flowers in His matted locks came down, and Thundru Thani Nerisai, among others. He sang of the Lord, the ocean of great grace, who composed Aruyirin Thiru-Viruttam, Dasapurana Thadai, Paaparavum Paavanaasa Pathigam, and other Thiru-Pathigams that stood before him and called out.” In these two verses, Sekkizhar Peruman mentions the Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman during his stay in Thiru-Pugalur. Sekkizhar Peruman mentions the Thiru-Pathigams. These Thiru-Pathigams include the Nindra Thiru-Thandagam, which begins with “Irunilanaay,” and is the ninety-fourth Thiru-Pathigam of the Sixth Thiru-Murai. Next is the Thani Thiru-Thandagam, which begins with “Aamayath Theerthu,” and is the ninety-sixth Thiru-Pathigam of the Sixth Thiru-Murai. Next is the Kshethrakkovai Thiru-Thandagam, which begins with “Thillaichchitrambalamum,” and is the seventieth Thiru-Pathigam of the Sixth Thiru-Murai.

Next are the Kuraindha Nerisai Thiru-Pathigams, two of which begin with “Vendrilen,” and are the seventy-eighth Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai, and the seventy-ninth Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai. Next are the Ninaindha Thiru-Nerisaigal Thiru-Pathigams, which begin with “Muththinai,” and are the seventy-fourth Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai.

Sixthly, The Thani Thiru-Nerisaigal Thiru-Pathigams, which are three in number. The first Thani Thiru-Nerisaigal Thiru-Pathigam begins with “Thondanena,” and is the seventy-fifth Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai. The one beginning with “Marulavaam” is the seventy-sixth Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai. The one beginning with “Kadumbagal” is the seventy-seventh Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai. Next is the Aruyir Thiru-Viruttam Thiru-Pathigam, which is the eighty-fourth Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai. Next is the Dasapurana Thadai Thiru-Pathigam, which begins with “Paruvarai,” and is the fourteenth Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai, composed in Pazhampanjuram Pann.

Next is the Paavanaasa Thiru-Pathigam, which begins with “Patrattar Ser,” and is the fifteenth Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai, a Pazhampanjuram Pann Thiru-Pathigam. Next are the Araikkuvum Thiru-Pathigams, which begin with “Sivanenum” Thiru- The Thiru-Pathigam, in the Pann Gandharam, Thiru-Viruttam of Pasupathi, which begins with “Saambalai Poosi,” is the one hundred and tenth Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai. The Thiru-Viruttam of Sarkarai, which begins with “Vidaiyum Vidaipetrum,” is the one hundred and eleventh Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai. Next are the Thani Thiru-Viruttams, which are the one hundred and thirteenth Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai, the Thiru-Pathigam beginning with “Pavala Thadaivarai,” the one hundred and twelfth Thiru-Pathigam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai, and the Thiru-Pathigam beginning with “Vellikkulai,” which is the seventh Thiru-Pathigam of the Sixth Thiru-Murai.

Thus, these mentioned Thiru-Pathigams are known to us through these two verses composed by Sekkizhar Peruman. Besides these, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman composed many other Thiru-Pathigams.

In this way, we will contemplate a little on these Thiru-Pathigams mentioned by Sekkizhar Peruman in these two verses of the Periya Puranam.

First, the Nindra Thiru-Thandagam, a well-known Thiru-Pathigam. This Thiru-Pathigam, which begins with “Irunilanaay Theeyaagi,” is the ninety-fourth Thiru-Pathigam of the Sixth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathigam. This Nindra Thiru-Thandagam, which begins with “Irunilanaay Theeyaagi,” is a Thiru-Pathigam that embodies the essence of Sri Rudram found in the Vedas. Just as Sri Rudram speaks of the Lord’s pervasive presence in all things, animate and inanimate, so too does this Nindra Thiru-Thandagam, which begins with “Irunilanaay Theeyaagi,” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman has composed it with the same meaning embedded within. Where is this mentioned?

In the Sivagnanabodham Sitrurai, in the twelfth sutra, Madhava Sivagnana Munivar illustrates this for us. That section is as follows: “It is appropriate for those with true knowledge to see Parameswaran everywhere without distinction, and it is also stated in Nindra Thiru-Thandagam and others, and in Thiru-Rudram, worship is described by mentioning things without distinction.” In this place, Madhava Sivagnana Swamigal has stated that this Nindra Thiru-Thandagam and Thiru-Rudram (Sri Rudram) illustrate the Lord’s pervasive presence without distinction in all animate and inanimate things. This Thiru-Pathigam also begins with “Irunilanaay Theeyaagi Neerumaagi Iyamaananaay Yeriyum Kaatrumaagi Arunilai Thingalaay Gnaayiraagi Aakaasamaay Attamoorthiyaagi.” This first part shows us that the Lord exists as the Ashtamoorthies, pervading the entire universe. It begins by illustrating the Lord’s pervasive nature as the Ashtamoorthies, consisting of the five elements, the sun, the moon, and the soul.

Furthermore, this Thiru-Pathigam describes in great detail how the Lord resides in all things.

Now, that Thiru-Pathigam.

Irunilanaay theeyaagi neerumaagi iyamaananaay yeriyum kaatrumaagi arunilai thingalaay gnaayiraagi aakaasamaay attamoorthiyaagi perunalamum kutramum pennum aanum piraruruvum thammuruvum thaameyaagi nerunalaiyaayaagi naalaiyaagi nimir punsadaiyadigal nindravaare. Mannagi vinnagi malaiyumaagi vairamumaay maanikkamthaaneyaagi kannagi kannukkor maniyumaagi kalaiyaagi kalai gnanam thaameyaagi pennagi pennukkor aanumaagi pralayathukku appaalor andamaagi ennagi ennukkor ezhuththumaagi ezhunjudaray em adigal nindravaare. Kallaagi kalaraagi kaanumaagi kaaviriyay kaalaraay kazhiyumaagi pullaagi puthalaagi poodumaagi puramaagi purumoonrum kedu. Destroyed. Solli sollukkor porulumaagi sulaavaagi sulaavukkor soozhalaagi nellaagi nilanaagi neerumaagi nedunjudaray nimirndhadigal nindravaare.

Kaatraagi kaarmugilaay kaalam moonraay kanavaagi nanavaagi kankulaagi kootraagi kootruththaiththa kolkalimaagi kuraikadalay kurai kadarkkor komaanumaay neetraanaay neeretra meniyaagi neel visumbaay neelvisumbin uchchiyaagi etraanaay eroorndha selvanaagi ezhunjudaray emmadigal nindravaare. Theeyaagi neeraagi thinmaiyaagi thisaiyaagi aththisaikkor deivamaagi thaayaagi thanthaiyaay saarvumaagi thaarakaiyum gnaayirum than mathiyumaagi kaayaagi pazhamaagi pazhaththil nindra irathangal nugarvaanum thaameyaagi neeyaagi naanaagi nermaiyaagi nedunjudaray. Nimirdhadigal nindravaare. Angamaay aadhiyaay vedamaagi arumaraiyodu aimbootham thaameyaagi pangamaay pala sollum thaameyaagi paanmathiyodu aadhiyaay paanmaiyaagi gangaiyaay kaaviriyay kanniyaagi kadalaagi malaiyaagi kazhiyumaagi engumaay eroorndha selvanaagi ezhunjudaray em adigal nindravaare. Maadhaapithaavaagi makkalaagi marikadalum maal visumbum thaameyaagi godhaaviriyay kumariyaagi kol puliththol aadai kuzhaganagi podhaaya malarkondu potri nindru punai vaara pirapparukkum punithanagi yaadhaanum ena ninaindhaarkku elidheyaagi azalvanna vannardhaam nindravaare. Aavaagi aavinil aindhumaagi arivaagi azhalaagi aviyumaagi naavaagi naavukkor uraiyumaagi naadhanaay vedaththin ulloonaagi poovaagi poovukkor naatram.

Aagi pookkuzhaal vaasamay nindraanaagi dhevaagi dhevar mudhalumaagi sezhunjodaray sendru adigal nindravaare. Neeraagi neel agalam thaameyaagi nizhalaagi neel visumbin uchchiyaagi peraagi perukkor perumaiyaagi perumadhilgal moonrinaiyum eythaanaagi aarenum than adaindhaar thammaiyellam aatkolla valla em eesanaardhaam paaraagi pannaagi paadalaagi paranjodaray sendru adigal nindravaare. Maalaagi naanmuganaay maa boodhamaay marukkamaay arukkamaay magizhuvumaagi paalaagi en thisaikkum ellaiyaagi parappaagi paralogam thaameyaagi boologa buvaloga suvalogamaay boodhangalaay puraanandhaaneyaagi iyalaadhanavellam elvippaanaay ezhunjodaray em adigal nindravaare.

Now, the next. Thiru-Pathigam is the Thani Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathigam. In this Thiru-Pathigam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman praises the grace with which the Lord made him His servant. This is the ninety-sixth Thiru-Pathigam of the Sixth Thiru-Murai.

“Aamayath theerththadiyenai aalaak kondar adhigai veerattaanam aatchi kondar thaamaraiyon siramariththu kaiyir kondar thalaiyadhanir palik kondar niraivaandha thanmai vaamanaar maakaayath thudhiram kondar maanidam kondar valangai mazhu vaazhkondar kaamanaiyum udal kondar kannaal nokki kannappar paniyum kol kapaaliyaare muppuri nool varai maarbil muyangak kondar mudhukelil mulai maruppum kondar poonaa seppuruva mulai malaiyaal paagam kondar semmeni venniru thigazhak kondar thuppuravaar surisangin.” He wore the conch shell, and the gods with shining crowns worshipped Him. He accepted the offerings and the love of young women. He is my Lord who made me His own. He wore the crescent moon and the fierce snake on His head.

He wore anklets on His feet that jingled. He crushed the untamed Muyalagan under His feet. He held the sharp axe in His right hand. He took the left side of the Lord. He held the drum and wore the skeleton. He removed my suffering and made me His own.

He wore the begging bowl and tiger skin on His shoulders. He was surrounded by hosts of ghosts. He wore the snake and the serpent on His waist. He created all worlds and contained them all. He wore the Kokkiragam and the Vilva leaf. He made the fierce demon His prey.

He had a reddish-hued sacred body. He is Shiva who made me, the sinner, His own. He Himself embraced the God of Death with His spear; He made the Vedas His chariot and horses; He made Sundarar wave the fly-whisk of service; He made the cremation ground His dancing stage; He bent the Mandara mountain as a mighty bow; He made Maakaalan His doorkeeper; He bestowed the tantras and mantras; He dispelled my afflictions and enslaved me. He Himself made the Bhoota Ganas practice many instruments; He assumed the coral hue; He held the crystal; He held the moon on His matted locks containing the Ganga; He held the blue hue in His beautiful, full throat; He received alms from women with firm breasts who came to Him in infatuation; He held the bangles; He seized the entire city of Ottriyur; He cured my bodily ailments and enslaved me. He made the beautiful Thillai Ambalam His dancing stage; He made Arunan, the sun god, His servant. He made Amudha His own; He nurtured the fruit; He made the golden Cassia flower fragrant; He held the hearts of countless lovers; He held the serpent’s hood as a bracelet; He rode the great bull through the long streets; He wore the tiger skin as His garment; He held the trident in His hand; He held His devotees.

He created the serpent-bodied Brahma and Vishnu; He made the Keezhkottam in Kudamookku His temple; He saved the Brahmin who was kicked by Yama; He covered Himself with the skin of the elephant in Nedumookku; He expelled the unthinking sinners; He made Idaimarudhu His abode.

The Lord who enslaved me on this day, He Himself took the head of Yajna; He took the eye of Bhaga; He broke the teeth of one of the sun gods. He took the head of the revered Vyathiran; He held the fire in His hand; He protected the sacrifice; He cut off the head of the arrogant Daksha; He destroyed all of Daksha’s sacrifices with fear and bestowed grace; He, the immaculate one, enslaved me. He held the Ganga in one of His matted locks; He played the Veena with the music of the Sama Veda; He wore the spotted deer skin as a garment; He purified the hearts of those who meditate on Him; He received alms at the temple entrance; He held the fire; He assumed the form of a Kapalika; He held the victorious bull on His banner; He dispelled my great sorrow and enslaved me. He held the Kuram flower and the crescent moon on His matted locks; He made Nandi, the drummer, His reciter; He held the poison of Thiru-Siramalai Thanjai. He held the great Thiru-Siramalai Thanjai; He destroyed the chariot-riding god of the south wind; He took the name Paraparan (the Supreme Being); He held the mountain in His hand; He caused fear; He made Ravana utter His name; He dispelled my suffering and enslaved me.

In the eleventh verse of this sacred hymn, in the second line, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings, “He made Nandi, the drummer, His reciter.” About whom does he sing? He sings about Manikkavasagar Peruman. It says, “He made Nandi, the drummer, His reciter.” The reciter mentioned here is Manikkavasagar. The history states that Nandi Peruman later incarnated as Manikkavasagar. Tamil Thatha U.

V. Swaminatha Iyer has written a preface to the Thiruvalavudaiyar Thiru- He wrote a preface to the Thiruvalavudaiyar Thiru-Vilayadal Puranam. In that preface, he states the following: “As Buddhism increased in Tamil Nadu, the clarity of Shaivism diminished. To remove this, that is, for Shaivism to gain clarity by removing Buddhism, everyone, including the Devas, prayed. By the divine command of Lord Shiva, Thiru-Nandi Devar himself incarnated as Manikkavasagar Peruman in Thiru-Vathavur.” This history is mentioned in the Adi Kailasa Mahatmyam, the Sanskrit Purana of Thiru-Perundurai, and in the Sri Manivakya Charitram, which narrates the history of Manikkavasagar Peruman in Sanskrit.

Thus, Tamil Thatha U. V. Swaminatha Iyer writes this note.

Therefore, The statement “He made Nandi with the pot drum His reciter” confirms this history, as Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings that Nandi Peruman, who was Nandi with the pot drum, was made to incarnate as Manikkavasagar and became His reciter.

Therefore, this passage in this sacred hymn is worthy of deep contemplation. We will continue to contemplate the other sacred hymns. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 472. Thiru-Nindrachirukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We are contemplating the general sacred hymns composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman in Thiru-Pugalur. In that sequence, the next sacred hymn is the Kshetra Kovai Thiru-Thandagam.

In this sacred hymn, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman praises all the sthalams where Lord Shiva has manifested. To praise the sacred sthalams means to worship the temples in those sthalams as Lord Shiva Himself. “The temple itself is a refuge to be worshipped” is the twelfth sutra of Siva Gnana Bodham. In accordance with this, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman has mentioned various sacred sthalams in this hymn and concluded it by showing that “if one sees many temples existing in any place, one can see the Lord of Kailash.” That is, in these He has declared that in all these sacred places, one can behold Lord Shiva, the Lord of Kailash.

Now, this sacred hymn is the seventieth hymn in the sixth Thiru-Murai, structured as a Thiru-Thandagam.

Thillai Thiruchitrambalam and Sembponpalli, Thevankudi, Sirappalli, Thengur, Kolli, Kuliraraipalli, Koval Veerattam, Kokaranam, Kodikkavu, Mullaipuravam, Murugan Poondi, Muzhaiyur, Pazhaiyarai, Sakthimuttam, Kallitrigal, Seerar Kalathiyum, one can behold the Lord of Kailash. Arur Moolathanam, Anaikaavu, Akkur Thanthondri Madam, Avur, Perur, Piramapuram, Peravurum, Perundurai, Kampili, Pidavur, Paanum, Kurar Kurukkai Veerattanamum, Kottur, Kudamookku, Kozhambamum, One can behold the Lord of Kailash in Karar Kazhugundrum and Kanapperum. Idaimarudhu, Ingoy, Rameshwaram, Innampar, Eridai Vai, Emaperur, Sadaimudi, Salaikudi, Thakkalur, Thalaiyalangadu, Thalaichangadu, Kodumudi, Kutralam, Kollambuthur, Kothittai, Kottaru, Kottukadu, Kadaimudi, Kanur, Kadambanthurai, one can behold the Lord of Kailash. Echil Ilamar, Emanallur, Ilambaiyangattur, Iraiyancheri, Achirupakkam, Alappur, Ambar, Avadu Thurai, Azhundur, Arai, Kachinangarkudi, Kachur, Alakkoil, Karaveeram, Kattuppalli, Kachi Palathazhiyum Ekambathum, one can behold the Lord of Kailash. Kodungolur, Anjaikkalam, Sengundrur, Konganangundriyur, Kurukkakavu, Nedungalam, Nannilam, Nellikavu, Nindriyur, Needur, Niyamannallur, Idumbavanamum, Ezhumbur, Ezhur, Tholur, Erumbiyur, Erarum, Emakoodam, Kadambai, Ilangoyil Thannullum, one can behold the Lord of Kailash.

Mannai, Padikkarai, Valkozhiputhur, Vakkarai, Mandaram, Varanasi, Vennai, Vilathotti, Velvikudi, Vilamar, Viradapuram, Vetkalathum, Pennai, Arulthurai Than, Pennagadam, Pirambil, Perumpuliyur, Peruvelurum, Kannai, Kalarkarai, Kalippalaiyum, one can behold the Lord of Kailash. Vizhi, Milalai, Venkadu, Vengur, Vedikkudi, Visayamangai, Viyalur, Azhiyagathiyan Palli, Annamalai, Alangadum, Arathai, Perumpali, Pazhanam, Pananthal, Pathalam, Paraythurai, Paingili, Panangattur, Thankazhi, Kadalnaga, Karoonathum, one can behold the Lord of Kailash. Unchenaikkalam, Ural, Oothur, Oruthirakkodi, Maraikkattullum, Manchar, Podiyinmalai, Thanjai, Vazhuvur, Veerattam, Mathanam, Kedarathum, Venjamakkudal, Miyachur, Vaika, Vedichuram, Vivichuram, Ottriyurum, Kanjanur, Kanjara, Panchakkaiyum, one can behold the Lord of Kailash. Thindicharam, Sengalur, Sembpanpalli, Thevur, Sirapuran, Sittemam, Serai, Kondicharam, Kunthalur, Kuzhaiyur, Koodal, Kurukavur, Velladai, Kumari, Kongu, Andar Thozhum Athikai Veerattanam, Aiyaru, Asoganthi, Ammathurum, Kandiyur Veerattam, Karugavurum, one can behold the Lord of Kailash. Naraiyur, Sithicharam, Nallaru, Naraiyur, Nageswaram, Nallur, Nallathuraiyur, Sotrutthurai, Soolamangai, Thonipuram, Thuruthi, Somicharam, Uraiyur, Kadal Ottriyur, Oottrathur, Omampuliyur, Or Edagathum, Karaiyur, Karuppariyal, Kandrapurum, one can behold the Lord of Kailash. Pulivalam, Puthur, Pugalur, Punkur, Purambayam, Poovanam, Poigainallur, Valivalam, Marperu, Vaimur, Vaigal, Valanchuzhi, Vanjiyam, Marugal, Vanni, Nilamali, Neythanathodu, in any place, if you see many great temples, O devotees, you can behold the Lord of Kailash, who crushed the mighty Kali with His toe.

Now, the next sacred hymn is a short Nerisai hymn. There are two such hymns under this title.

First, the seventy-eighth hymn of the fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Nerisai hymn.

“Ventrilen pulangal aindhum ventravar valagathannul sendru” (I have not conquered the five senses; I have gone into the realm of those who have conquered them). Aathalaale sennneri atharkum seyyan nindrule thuzhumbugindren neesanen eesaneyo indrulen naalai yillen en seivan thondrinene. (Therefore, I am far from the righteous path, O Lord, I, the lowly one, am immersed in suffering. I exist today, but not tomorrow; for what purpose was I born?) Kattrilen kalaigal gnanam kattrvar thangalodum uttrilen aathalaale unarvukkum seyananen pettrilen perunthadangann pedhai maaru thamakkum pollan ettrulen iraivane naan en seivan thondrinene. (I have not learned the arts and wisdom; I have not associated with those who have learned them, therefore I am far from understanding. I have not gained the large-eyed, innocent women; I am not good for them. O Lord, what have I gained?

For what purpose was I born?) Maattinen manathai munne marumaiyai unaramatten moottinaan munnai naale muthalvanai vanangamaten paattinaipola nindru pattathaam paavam thannai eettinen kalaiyamatten en seivan thondrinene. (I have bound my mind before; I cannot understand the future. He ignited me on a former day; I cannot worship the First Being. Standing like a song, I have accumulated the sin of attachment; I cannot remove it. For what purpose was I born?) Karaikadanthothamerum kadalvidam mundagandan urai kadanthothu nirmaiyai unarnthilen aathalaale araikkidanthasaiyunagam asaippane inba vazhkai kirai Kiraikidanthurugugindren en seivan thondrinene. (I am melting away in this joyful life, O Lord, for what purpose was I born?) Semmai venniru poosum sivanavan thevathevan vemmai noy vinaigal theerkkum vithithanukku aarvameithi ammai nindradiamai seyya vadivilaa mudivil vazhkai kimmai nindrarugugindren en seivan thondrinene. (I am melting away in this endless life, O Lord, for what purpose was I born? I have not served the Lord, who smears pure white ash, the God of gods, who removes the burning diseases and karmas, with devotion.) Pechchodu pechchukellam pirarthamai purame pesa koochile aathalaale kodumaiyai vidumaroren naacholi naalum murthi nanmaiyai unaramatten echchule nindru meyyee en seivan thondrinene. (I am standing in disgrace, O Lord, for what purpose was I born? I have not been ashamed to speak ill of others in all conversations, therefore I do not know how to abandon cruelty.

I cannot understand the goodness of the Lord, who is spoken of daily.) Thesanai thesamagum thirumalor pangan thannai poosanai punithan thannai punarum pundarikathaanai nesanai neruppan thannai nivanjagathagandra semmai eesanai ariyamatten en seivan thondrinene. (I cannot know the Lord, who is the light of lights, who shares a part with Vishnu, who is worshipped, who is pure, who is the lotus-eyed one, who is love, who is fire, who is the righteous one who has abandoned deceit. For what purpose was I born?) Vilaikkindra vinaiyai nokki vennmayir viravi melum mulaikkindra vinaiyaip poga muyal Iyalagillain iyalavellam thilaikkindra mudiyinaan than thiruvadi paravamattaa thilaikkindren irumiyundri en seivan thondrinene. (I am unable to praise the sacred feet of the Lord, whose head is adorned with all things, and I am immersed in suffering, O Lord, for what purpose was I born?) Vilaivarivilamaiyaalai vedanai kuzhiyil aazhnthu kalaiganumillen enthay kamarangkattrumillen thadaiyavil kodhai nallar thangalodu inbamaiytha ilaiyanumallen enthay en seivan thondrinene. (I am immersed in the pit of suffering due to my lack of understanding of consequences, and I have no one to remove me, O Lord, nor have I learned the arts of love. I am not even young enough to enjoy with beautiful women, O Lord, for what purpose was I born?) Vettana udaiyanagi veerathal malaiyedutha thuttanai thuttu theerthu suvaipada geetham ketta attama murthiyay aathiyai othinallum ettanai ettamaten en seivan thondrinene. (Even if I praise the Primordial Lord, who is the eight-formed one, who removed the evil one who lifted the mountain with valor, and heard the sweet music, I cannot reach Him even a little. For what purpose was I born?)

Now, the next sacred hymn is the seventy-ninth hymn of the fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Nerisai hymn.

“Thammaanam kaappathaagi thaiyalar valaiyul aazhnthu ammanai amuthan thannai aathiyai anthamaaya” (Being a protector of self-respect, immersed in the net of women, the Lord, the immortal one, the beginning and the end).
