Semmaana oligal mene sindhaiyul ondra emmanai ninaiyamatten en seivan thondrinene. (I cannot think of my Lord, whose red light is in my mind. For what purpose was I born?) Makkale manantha tharam avvayitravare yomum sikkule azhunthi eesan thirampaden thavamathu oren koppule polath thondri athanule maraiya kandum ikkale parathai yompa en seivan thondrinene. (I am immersed in the entanglement of protecting the children and the married wife, and I do not know the Lord’s path or penance. Even seeing that it appears like a bubble and disappears within it, I am protecting this body. For what purpose was I born?) Koozhaiye nagamaten koduvinai kozhiyil vizhnthu ezhinin isaiyinalum iraivanai eththamaten mazhaiyon kannin nalla madanthaimar thamakkum pollan ezhaiye naginalum en seivan thondrinene. (I cannot be a servant; I have fallen into the pit of evil karma.

Even with the seven notes of music, I cannot praise the Lord. I am not good even for the beautiful women with dark eyes. Even if I am a poor person, for what purpose was I born?) Munnaiyen vinaiyinale murthiyai ninaiyamatten pinnai naan piththanagi pithatruvan pedhaiyen naan ennulle manni nindra seermayathayinanai ennulle ninaiyamatten en seivan thondrinene. (Due to my past karma, I cannot think of the Lord.

Later, I, the fool, became mad and raved. I cannot think of the glorious one who resides within me. For what purpose was I born?) Karaiyani Kandan thannai kamarangkattrumillen piranuthal pedhai mathar peyvalaiyarkkumallen marainavil navinanai manni nindru irainjinalum iraiyeyum eththamaten en seivan thondrinene. (I have not learned the arts of love for the Lord with the dark throat, nor am I suitable for the beautiful women with bangles. Even if I worship the Lord with the Vedic tongue, I cannot praise Him even a little. For what purpose was I born?) Valaithu nindravar kalvar vanthanai nadukkam seyya thalaithu vaithu ulaiyai etri thalalerri madutha neeril thilaithu nindradugindra aamai pol thelivilathen izhaithu nindradugindren en seivan thondrinene. (Like a turtle that plays in the water heated by a fire, with its head held high, when thieves surround and make one tremble, I, the unclear one, am playing. For what purpose was I born?)

In this second sacred hymn, verses six, seven, eight, and nine are not available to us. Both these sacred hymns conclude with the sentiment, “Ezhaiyen en seivan thondrinene” (What shall I, the poor one, do, for what purpose was I born?).

Therefore, these hymns are named Kuraintha Nerisai (Short Nerisai). The commentator interprets “Kuraintha” as diminished or attained. Diminished To attain means to melt and humbly submit, remembering one’s shortcomings.

Now, the next sacred hymn is the seventy-fifth hymn of the fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Nerisai hymn.

Thondan en pattathenne thuyakaviri nannir kondu irukku othi aatti kungumakkuzhambu saathi indai kondera nokki eesanai embiranai kandanai kandirathai kalathai kazhithavare. (What has happened to me, the devotee? I have spent my time seeing and not seeing the Lord, my Master, who is bathed with pure Kaveri water, worshipped with Vedic hymns, anointed with saffron paste, and adorned with garlands.) Pinnilen munnilen naan pirapparathu arul seyvane ennilay nayinen naan ilangathir payalai thingal sinnila erikkum senni sivapurathu amararere ninnalal kalaigan are niruser agalathane. (I am neither behind nor ahead; I am a dog, a sinner, who has not received grace to end rebirth. O Lord of Sivapuram, whose head is adorned with the crescent moon that shines like a young sun, who else but You can remove my afflictions, O Lord of the vast expanse?) Kallanen kallathondai kalathai kazhithu pokki thelliye nagi nindru thedinen nadikkanden ulguvar ulgittellam udanirunthu aruthi endru. (I, the thief, spent my time in deceitful devotion, then became clear and searched, and found Him. When I thought that all that those who meditate think is with Him and decided it,) Velginen velginanum vilavirach siruthittene. (I was ashamed, and He too was ashamed, and I became small.) Udambenum manaiyagathul ullame thagaliyaga madambadum unar neyyatti uyirenum thiri mayakki idambadu gnanathiyal erikola irunthu nokkil kadambamatr kalai thathai kalaladi kanlame. (If one sits and looks with the fire of knowledge, making the body a house, the mind a lamp, pouring the ghee of understanding, and making the soul a wick, one can see the sacred feet of the Father of the Kadamba youth.) Vanjappen arangu koyil vazhaiyitraravan thunja vanjappen iruntha suzhal vanthaval mathiyam thoyum vanjappen vazhkaiyalan vazhvinai vazhalutru vanjappen urakkamanen vanjanen en seykene. (I, the deceitful one, have become a deceitful woman’s sleep, desiring to live the life of a deceitful woman, in the deceitful woman’s temple, where the deceitful woman sleeps, where the deceitful woman’s surroundings are touched by the moon.

What shall I do, the deceitful one?) Ulguvar ullathane unarvenum perumaiyanai ulginen nanum kanban uruginen uriyuri ezhuginen enthai pemman iruthalai minnugindra kollimel erumben ullam enganam koodumarre. (I meditated on the Lord, who is in the hearts of those who meditate, who is the greatness of consciousness. I too meditated to see Him, I melted, I rose again and again. How can my heart, like an ant on a two-headed glowing coal, reach my Father, the great Lord?) Mothaiyai kanda kakkai polaval vinaigal moythun varthaiyai pesavotta Mayakka naan mayangugindren. Seethaiyai sidambu thannai sedigal noy vadivondrilla uththaiyai kazhikkum vannam unarvutha ulagamurthi. Angathai mannukku akki aarvathai unakke thanthu pangathai poga mattrri pavithen paramaninai. Sangotha meni selva sathal nal nayen unnai engutrray endra potha yangutren en kandaye.

Vellaneer sadaiyanartham vinavuvar pola vanthen ullame pugunthu nindrarkku urangunan pudigal ponthu kallaro pugunthir enna kalanthuthan nokki nakku vellaromendru nindrar vilangilampiraiyanare. Peru viral irai than undra piraiyeyirilang angan tharuvarai anaiya thozhan arakkandru alari vizhnthan iruvarum oruvanay uruvamangudaiyavalla thiruvadi sumanthu kondu Kankanan thiriyumarre. (I, the deluded one, am deluded, unable to speak your words, as my karmas gather like crows seeing a lump of food. O Lord of the world, grant me the understanding to remove this filth, this impurity, this disease-ridden form. I have made my body earth, given my desire to you, removed my imperfections, and meditated on you, the Supreme Being. O Lord with a conch-like body, on the day of my death, when I, a dog, ask you, “Where are you?” what will you see where I am?

The Lord with the white water in his matted locks came as if to inquire. When I, who was sleeping, asked those who had entered my heart, “Are you thieves who have entered?” He looked at me, laughed, and stood there, saying, “We are white ones,” the Lord with the shining crescent moon. When he pressed his great toe, the demon with crescent-like teeth, who was like a mountain, fell down screaming in anger. Carrying the sacred feet of the Lord, who was one with both of them,) Kayamay koyilaga kadimanam adimaiyaga vaymaiye thuymaiyaga manamani lingamaga neyame neyyum pala niraiya nir amaiya vaatti poosanai eesanarkku potravikkattinome. (We offered worship to the Lord, making the body a temple, the firm mind a servant, truthfulness purity, the mind a precious lingam, love ghee and milk, and filling it with water.) Vanjagappulaiyanenai vazhiyarat thondirputti anjalendrandu konday athuvanin perumaiyandre nenjagang kaniyamatten ninnaiyul vaikkamaten nanjidam kondakanda ennanan nanmaithane. (You, who have the poison in your throat, enslaved me, the deceitful wretch, by showing me the path and saying, “Fear not.” Is that not your greatness? I cannot melt my heart, nor can I keep you within me.

What good is it then?) Nayinum kadappattenai nanneri katti anday aayiram aravamartha amuthane amuthamuthu niyumen nenjinulle nilavinay nilavinirka noyavai sarumagil nokkinir arul seyvay. (You, who are sweeter than nectar, who wore a thousand serpents, who are the nectar itself, you reside in my heart. If diseases afflict me, look upon me and grant your grace.) Villathan ondrumatten viruppenum vetkaiyale vallathen pola nunnai vaymaduthundidamay ullathe nitriyenam uyirppule varuthiyenum kallathe nitri amma enga Kaanumarre. (I cannot do anything with a bow; with the desire of longing, I cannot drink you like a cup. Even if you reside in my heart, even if you come into my breath, you reside deceitfully, O Mother. How can I see you?) Aasaivan pasameythi angutren ingutrenay oosalattundu vazha uzhanthu naan olitharame thesanay thesamurthi thirumaraikkadumey eesanay undran patham eththumararul emmane. (I, the deluded one, am here and there, caught in the swing of desire and attachment, struggling to live, unable to shine. O Lord, the light of lights, who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu, grant me the grace to praise your feet, O my Lord.) Niraivilen nesamillen ninaivilen vinaiyin pasa maraivile purappattedrum vagaiyana arulanemman siraiyilen seyvathenne thiruvadi paraviyeththa kuravilen kutram theeray kondrai ser sadaiyinane. (I am imperfect, without love, without memory, caught in the snare of karma. O Lord, who is grace, who can rise above this concealment, what can I, the imprisoned one, do?

Praise your sacred feet. O Lord with the Kondrai flower in your matted locks, remove my imperfections and faults.) Naduvila kalan vanthu nanugumbothariya onna aduvana anju pootham avaithamakku atralagane paduvana palavum kutram pangila manithar vazhkai keduvathi piravi sichi kilaruli sadaiyinire. (When the impartial Yama comes near, I cannot know. I cannot withstand the five elements that dance. Many are the faults that befall human life, which is without order. This birth is a ruin, alas! O Lord with the shining matted locks.)

Now, the next sacred hymn is the seventy-seventh hymn of the fourth Thiru-Murai.

“Kadumbagal nattamadi kaiyilo” (Dancing fiercely at midday, in hand) Kapalamenthi idumbalikkillanthorum muzhitharum iraivanire. Nedumborai malaiyarppai nerilai nerimen kunthar kodungulai pugunthavendrum kovanam araiyatheyo. Kovanam muduthavarum kolaravasaithavarum theevana sambarpusi thiruvurunthavarum poovanakkizhavanarai puliyuri araiyanarai evanachilaiyanarai yavare ezhuthuvare. Vilakkinnal petra inbam mezhukkinnal pattrithiyagum thulakkil nan malarthoduthal thuyavin nerallagum vilakkittar peru sollin meigneri gnanamaagum alappila geetham sonnar kadigal tham arulumarre.

Chandirar sadaiyil vaitha sangaran samavethi antharath thamararvemman an nalvellurthiyan than manthiram namachivaya aganiranip petral ventharum vinaiyum noyum vevazhal viragi.

Then, the five hunters, like thieves, entered the field, leaping and plundering. They caused pure dharma to flourish. Those thorny ones, hidden within the shade of the Three-Eyed Lord’s feet, can be struck down by spiritual wisdom. I, a devotee, born into this world, did not live well, but fell into the pit of ancient karma, carrying this body, and was seized by a great desire. O Lord of the universe, King of the celestials, the Wise One, say ‘Fear not!’ O Lord with the radiant matted locks adorned with the clear-waved Ganga! O sinful heart, if you meditate on the Lord, like a pig in distress, then the path to Shiva will be certain.

You considered beautiful this body, which is a dwelling of aversion, foul odor, and flowing blood, covered by a roof. When the demon, in his arrogance, sought to place his many crowns upon the head of the Lord, who, at the dawn of creation, placed Uma to quell her trembling, then When he placed the crescent moon, like a budding flower, upon the crown of the Lord’s head, he withered and shrank, thinking it would cause pain.

In this sacred decad, the eighth and ninth verses are unavailable to us.

Let us continue to contemplate the other sacred decads. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 473. Thiru-nindra-charukkam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We are contemplating the general sacred decads composed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman in Thiru-pukalur, also known as Poompukalur. In that sequence, the next sacred decad is the Aruyir Thiru-virutha Thiru-padikam.

This is the 84th sacred decad of the Fourth Thiru-murai.

“O Lord of the eight directions and the two directions!” cried the celestials in a fierce battle. “Is it not beneath the shade of the feet of the Lord, who with one arrow destroyed the three cities of the wicked, who are like eyes that do not see?” Thus speaks my precious soul. “O Lord, whose waist is adorned with a wide-mouthed serpent, whose matted locks bear the waning crescent moon, the Lord of the celestials, who is without beginning or end, who is the entire world, earth, and sky, is it not beneath the shade of His feet?”

Thus speaks my precious soul. “Is it not beneath the shade of the feet of the Lord, who, in fierce wrath, destroyed the sacrifice of Daksha, who holds a shining trident of fire, who has three unblinking eyes, who is great, who severs the birth of the great, and whose own birth is unknown?” Thus speaks my precious soul. “Is it not beneath the shade of the feet of the Lord, who joyfully holds Uma, the beautiful one with long eyes, on one side, who is adorned with a serpent and a tiger skin, whose body is covered in sacred ash, and who wears the golden Konrai garland?” Thus speaks my precious soul. “Is it not beneath the shade of the feet of the Lord, who, to protect the celestials, consumed the poison and held it in His throat, who is of dark beauty, who bears the Ganga in His red matted locks, and who severed the chest of Arjuna with one arrow?” Thus speaks my precious soul. “He struck He struck the three fortified cities with a fiery arrow. He pervaded the vast worlds and examined the profound scriptures.

“Is it not beneath the shade of His feet? Thus speaks my precious soul. He, who with one nail, severed the head of the one who was difficult to fight, and filled the great Vishnu’s eyes with blood, then, with one finger, caused him to fall and smeared Himself with white ash. Is it not beneath the shade of His feet?

“Thus speaks my precious soul. All that was caught in the cycle of birth and death, perhaps fearing the wounds inflicted by the rows of kings, my soul sought refuge at the feet of the Lord, who is Nandi, who wears the great Konrai flower, and whose head is adorned with the twilight sky. He, who with a very large tiger skin, closely embraced and within Himself, the pure lady He, who is within, who delights the golden-faced ones who come to Him, who is pleased by those with cool hearts, is it not beneath the shade of His feet?

“Thus speaks my precious soul. He, the three-eyed Lord, who destroyed Kama, the god of love, with His fiery bow, when the two, Brahma and Vishnu, praised Him saying, ‘He is our Lord,’ is it not beneath the shade of His feet?

“Thus speaks my precious soul. He, the beautiful one, who, when the Lord of Lanka, with his twenty shoulders, was crushed by one finger, danced with the sound of flutes and drums, accompanied by the green-eyed goblins. Is it not beneath the shade of His feet?

“Thus speaks my precious soul.

“Now, next is the Dasa Purana Thiru-padikam, a sacred decad set to the tune of Pazhampancharam. In this sacred decad, the glories of Lord Shiva, as described in the Puranas, are recounted. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman declares that the feet of the Lord, who is praised in the Shiva Maha Puranas, are our sole refuge. He sings of the Lord who held poison in His throat, who stood as a pillar of fire, who destroyed Taraka, who burned the three cities, who graced Markandeya, who destroyed Daksha’s sacrifice, who burned Manmatha, and who bestowed the discus upon Vishnu. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, in this decad, recounts these acts of grace of the Lord, praised individually in the Shiva Maha Puranas, and proclaims that the Lord’s sacred feet are our glory and our refuge.

“Therefore, this is named Dasa Purana Thiru-padikam. As each verse of this decad elaborates and praises a story from a Maha Purana, it is called Dasa Purana Thiru-padikam.

“Now, that sacred decad.

“When the celestials, having churned the great mountain with the serpent, abandoned it, and the poison, burning with fear, rose to consume the color of the great Vishnu and scorch the sky, and as it spread, they cried, “O Lord, grant us a remedy!” Then, He, who mercifully consumed the great poison without casting it away, He is the King of the kings of the universe. When the flood of sound and light covered the vast universe, and the earth stood firm, and the divine essence of the supreme being was attained, there is none like Him. When Brahma and Vishnu stood on either side and worshipped, unable to comprehend His crown and feet, He stood as the Great One. He, the primordial Lord, the form of Shiva among the gods, He is our refuge. He, who existed before time, days, and eons were created, as the primal form, and who became the three forms, and who is exceedingly He, the fiery one, who stands as the form of the six great religions, who consumed the earth, the upper heavens, and the seven worlds, and as a child on a banyan leaf, He is the supreme form for them.

“He is our refuge. When the tall earth and sky, the vast ocean, mountains, and the seven worlds were all distressed, and the celestials, with folded hands, praised and worshipped Him, He danced a great dance to quell the unending wrath, splitting the body of the fleeing Taraka. His fiery feet are our refuge. When the earth and sky, without any stable path, were destroyed everywhere, and the three cities, causing distress, fled in fear, and Vishnu and the gods sought refuge, He, by His grace, with the serpent as His bowstring, and fire as His arrow, and water as His outer He, the generous one, who bent the mountain as a bow in His hand, He is our refuge. When the dark-bodied, red-eyed, white-tusked Hiranyakashipu sought Him, and in the morning, with good garlands, worshipped Him, and when Yama came near to seize the child, causing him to flee in fear, He, who destroyed that Yama, the ocean-like Lord, worshipped by the celestials, His feet are our refuge. When the celestials who came to partake in the great sacrifice of the highly ascetic Daksha, saw the fear-stricken Yagna, the moon, and all others, and stood in fear, and Brahma and Vishnu, in our ignorance, worshipped the primordial Lord and departed, He, the fiery-hued Lord, our Father, seeing their victorious state, it is our duty to behold Him as the ocean.

“When the beautiful goddess, playing, ran and covered her eyes with her hands, and the seven worlds were plunged into darkness When darkness enveloped everything, and to dispel that darkness, an eye opened on His forehead, and the goddess, fearing, removed her hands and worshipped, He, the three-eyed Lord, who caused that eye to bloom like the moon, He is our refuge. When the god of love, with his five arrows, approached and praised Him, as the cuckoo sang in the forest, and the cloud-hued Vishnu thought and sent his son, and Manmatha, who touched Him with his flower arrows, was burned to ashes, and the celestials worshipped Him with fire and departed, He, the fiery-hued Lord, our Father, whose single eye on His forehead was red with fire, His feet are our refuge. When Vishnu worshipped Him with a thousand beautiful flowers, and finding one short, offered his own eye, our Father, the Lord, pleased with him, bestowed upon him the discus, which, with its radiant edge, split the heart of the demon. He, who granted him the powerful discus, He is our refuge. When the charioteer said, “Your chariot cannot proceed on Kailash; do not think your valor will be hidden; it is not dharma to hasten,” and the demon, enraged, said, “Let go, let go!” and quickly went to lift the mountain, and his crowns and skin were greatly torn, then my mind remembered His foot that pressed down.

“Now, the next sacred decad is the Pavanasam Thiru-padikam. In this sacred decad, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman describes various sacred places where Lord Shiva resides and then preaches that he has enshrined the Lord, who is praised in these sacred places, within his heart. He worshipped Him with a cool mind, he will never forget Him, his heart was filled by remembering Him, and he embraced Him with love.

“Therefore, he worshipped in this manner, and if you also worship, your sins will be destroyed.

“Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman instructs in this sacred decad.

“Therefore, this is called Pavanasam Thiru-padikam. Thus it is called.

“Now, that sacred decad. This sacred decad is the 15th sacred decad of the Fourth Thiru-murai, set to the tune of Pazhampancharam.

“I have enshrined within my heart our supreme Lord of Ottriyur, who is the ancient city sought by those who have renounced attachments, the coral that shines in the ocean, the radiant fruit of Thiruchitrambalam, the sacred form difficult to touch, the spreading light in Vetriyur, the Lord of the pure ones, surrounded by waves. I will not forget the Lord of Anaikka, the Lord residing in Thiruvarur, the sweet lump of Kanapperur, the sugarcane that sprouted in Kannur, the Lord of Valampuri residing in Vaimur, praised by the celestials, the great elephant of Manakkailai, the moon, the light. I have enshrined within my heart the moon-crested sun, the medicine that dispels delusion, the King of the ancient city of Athigai, the Lord residing in Aiyaru, the destiny, the glory, the light sought by those who desire, the essence, the sprout of wisdom – my heart is filled by remembering Him. I have attained the lion-like Lord of Athigai Veerattam, who is our pearl of Purambayam, the shining gold of Pukalur, the sun that illuminates the world in Uraiyur’s lofty Sirappalli, the eye that sees those who see Him in the embracing Thiru-kazhukundram. I worshipped with a cool heart the Lord of Kolakka, the gem, the poison-consuming sage residing in Kudamukku, the Lord of Alangadu, the flower on the heads of the celestials, the green fruit shining in milk, our fresh gold of Paraythurai, the trident-bearer, the one without equal.

“I have enshrined within my mind our Lord of Thiru-vanjiyam, who is the ruby residing in Marugal, the garland of Valanjuzhi, the Kalpaka tree in Karukavur, the light difficult to behold, our birthless Lord of Peruvelur, who is inseparable from those who cherish Him, our wealth. I embraced with love our Lord of Anbil, who is the beautiful Raja Singam, the beautiful bull of Rameswaram, our dancer of Kutralam, whose broad chest is adorned with garlands of hair, the eternal bridegroom residing in the long mountain of the shady groves, the Lord of Adalvannatham. I eagerly swallowed with desire our Lord of Annamalai, who is the growing moon that appears in the evening, the bridegroom residing in Marai-kadu, the juice of the sugarcane, the radiant parrot residing in the city of Thuruthi in the groves, the Lord of the upper celestials. I worshipped with a cool heart our Lord of Neythanam, who is the light of Thiru-sotruthurai, the pure gem residing in Thuruthi, the Lord of Attruppazhanam, our precious gem of Alavai, whose strong shoulders are adorned with sacred ash, the ocean of creation, the mighty bull. Our pure Lord residing in Putthur, our mighty bull of Poovanam, the seed that sprouted in Mizhalai, the Vedic scholar of Velvikudi, the one who burned the three cities of the liars, the ancient one residing in Pothigai – I have enshrined within my mind the medicine residing in Mathur. He who was before all, who sprouted forth, who rode the mighty white bull, who is the color of the twilight sky, who destroyed the power of the demon – those who bathe their minds in the flood of thought, and offer garlands of pure words at His feet, saying, ‘My Father, my Lord, my Master,’ their sins will be destroyed.

“Now, the next sacred decad is the Sarakkarai Thiru-virutha Thiru-padikam. The author states that this sacred decad is one that directly challenges the Lord many times. This is the 111th sacred decad of the Fourth Thiru-murai.

““O Lord with the bull and the bull-riding charioteer, my plea! O Lord with the fierce axe-weapon, and the many hosts of bhoothas that fill O Lord, whose garment is the tiger skin, whose garland is of skulls, whose matted locks bear the crescent moon, O Sarakkarai, my lonely heart! O Lord of the great mountains, my plea! O Sarakkarai, my heart, where the conch, the sliding serpent, the drum, the twilight moon, and the fiery serpent are all mingled and united! O Lord, who holds a skull as a begging bowl, my plea!

“O Sarakkarai, my heart, where the sacred ash, the pure white ash, the beautiful lotus-like body, the spotted deer skin, and the tiger skin are all present! O Lord, who is the refuge in fierce battles, my plea! O Sarakkarai, my heart, where the deceitful Ganga, the great moon, the poisonous serpent, the garland of laughing skulls, and the laughing white skulls are all present as refuge! O Lord, who consumed the poison of the ocean O Lord, who consumed the poison of the ocean, my plea! O Sarakkarai, my heart, where Kailash, the place where Yama was overcome, and the beautiful Konrai garland, the crescent moon, and the jewel-mouthed serpent are all abundantly present! O Lord, who wears the garland of Konrai flowers, my plea!

“O Sarakkarai, my heart, where the beautiful crown jewel, the ashes of the cremation ground, the seven beautiful bones, the serpent, the bones, and the tortoise shell are all present! O Lord, who pierced the three cities of those who rebelled, my plea! O Sarakkarai, my heart, where the sacred ash of the devotees, the feet worshipped by them, Kailash seen by those who have seen Him, and the garland of Konrai flowers are all present! O Lord, who delights in riding the bull, my plea! O Sarakkarai, my heart, where the Kodukatti, Kokkarai, Thakkai, flute, cymbals, veena, Monthai, the Konrai with its marks, and the Vanni O Sarakkarai, my heart, where the Datura, the serpent, and the dance of the dwarf are all present! O Lord, who conquered the roaring Ganga, my plea!

“O Sarakkarai, my heart, where the rosary, the sacred thread, the skull garland, the water pot, the Kokkarai, the crooked moon, the weapon of sound, and the staff are all arranged! O Lord, who wields the fierce axe, my plea! O Sarakkarai, my heart, where the radiant crown jewel, the ashes of the cremation ground, the half-moon, the severed head, and the tiger skin are all established! O Lord, my Father, whose feet danced, my plea! O Sarakkarai, my heart, where the penance of the one who had ten heads, the tiger skin, the red sacred ash, and the garland of skulls are all present, and where penance itself resides!

“Let us continue to contemplate the other sacred decads.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 474. Thiru-nindra-charukkam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We are contemplating the general sacred decads composed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman in Thiru-pukalur. In that sequence, the next sacred decad is the Pasupathi Thiru-virutha Thiru-padikam, also known as Thiru-virutham.

This is the 110th sacred decad of the Fourth Thiru-murai. In each sacred verse of this decad, the Lord is addressed as “Pasupathi, Pasupathi,” and it is a supplication made by challenging Him.

Therefore, this is the Pasupathi Thiru-virutha Thiru-padikam.

“O Pasupathi, who rules us, whose matted locks are adorned with a serpent that coils around the beautiful, flower-laden breasts of the maiden, who rolls on the ground smeared with ash, and who shows mercy to those who praise Him with longing, O friend with bamboo-like shoulders!” O Pasupathi, who rules us, whose matted locks are adorned with a serpent that coils around the beautiful, flower-laden breasts of the maiden, who rolls on the ground smeared with ash, and who shows mercy to those who praise Him with longing, O friend with bamboo-like shoulders! O Pasupathi, who rules us, whose waist is adorned with a serpent that spits venom, O Lord with the fiery axe that destroys darkness, show mercy to the noble ones who have sacrificed their bodies and placed their heads at Your feet, so that they may not suffer! O Pasupathi, who rules us, whose eye, like a spreading fire, burned Manmatha, the god of love with five flower arrows, on a certain day, dispel the great waves of confusion for Your devotees who are caught in the cycle of birth and death! O Pasupathi, who rules us, who flayed the skin of the great mountain, causing the vast mountains to split and the maiden to fear, dispel the evil relatives for those who worship Your feet, taking no one else as refuge!

O Pasupathi, who rules us, dispel the diseases that afflict those who worship Your feet without any hindrance or deficiency, O Lord with red matted locks adorned with the moon, who holds a trident, and whose bees buzz around! O Pasupathi, who rules us, dispel the suffering of those who have sought Your feet to overcome their pride, O Lord whose radiant crown is adorned with the fragrant Konrai, the moon, the ashes of the cremation ground, and the serpent coiled around the precious gem! O Pasupathi, who rules us, dispel the forgetfulness of those who engage in renunciation and worship Your feet, O Lord who destroyed the flying chariot of the three cities with Your righteous deeds! O Pasupathi, who rules us, who, with a heart melting in devotion, thinking ‘Shiva is our Lord,’ and with a mind filled with overflowing madness, prattles, heal their ailments! O Pasupathi, who rules us, who crushed the twenty shoulders and heads of the mad demon, heal their ailments!

In this sacred decad, the eighth and ninth sacred verses are unavailable to us.

Now, the next Thiru-virutha Thiru-padikam is the 112th sacred decad of the Fourth Thiru-murai.

He is the Vedic scholar who has a skull like a silver-plated cloth, who wears a white sacred thread like silver strands, who adorns his matted locks with a white crescent moon like a silver plate, who is smeared with white ash, and whose coral-like body is covered with silver dust. By renouncing the body and transcending the seven worlds, one can cross the endless ocean of sorrow. O heart, resolve to be a servant of the golden-hued Lord, whose matted locks are like a garland, whose Ganga is like waves, whose crescent moon is cold, and who is the Lord of the cremation ground! If I speak first, it will be flattery. You are the Mother and Father to these three worlds; are You not the Lord of the blazing fire?

My life, which thinks only of You, will pass away. After it passes, do not forget me, my Lord, my Lord. I have only desired You. You never allow me to think of You. If I begin to think of You, You immediately make me forget and seek another name. Is there anyone like me who always forgets You and yet is dear to You, O Lord of the heavens?

The Lord with three-fold form, covered in white ash, the beautiful great light of the golden mountain, our Lord, whom you have scorned, behold! He is worshipped by the gods who are worshipped. After worshipping Him, He causes His devotees to be worshipped by the gods who are worshipped. He is in the heavens, in the vast Vedas, in the king who is girded by the wide waters, in Thiru-Mal, the Lord of the earth, in the one who is beyond dispute. He is within the eye, within the hearts of devotees, within the mind of this ancient servant, within my eye, within my mind, upon my head; He has found my shore. When the great ocean covered the earth, and the deluge came, and Brahma too was submerged and died, and his body, and the body of the dark-ocean-hued one, were taken, and He became a Kankalar, standing amidst the returning ocean, our Lord plays the good Veena.

What if the sky trembles? What if the earth quakes? What if the great mountain trembles and its head reels? What if the fish in the ocean die? What if the bright lights fall? To the excellent ones who are devoted to the One who drank the ocean poison and has no blemish, Shiva is the name that belongs to Him alone, the Lord of the red form.

If He takes me as His servant and protects me, then I will wander, holding the name of ‘Bhavan’, and call out for many days.

Thus, he will not cease calling me for many days, and will meet me. How can those like me see You? Your greatness is not such that those like You can see You. O Vedic one, whose matted locks shine like lightning, who has refined gold and destroyed the red deer, and whose matted locks are like lightning!

Now, the next Thiru-Pathikam, the 113th Thiru-Pathikam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai, the Thiru-Viruttha Thiru-Pathikam.

His strong shoulders are like a coral mountain, and upon His shoulders, coral-like matted locks are bound. Upon those matted locks, a serpent with a coral-like head, like a coral sprout, along with the serpent, and the coral-eyed moon, my Father wears as a garland. The fragrant flowers, rich with honey, are entwined, and the bees hum around them, a great garland. O Lord with matted locks, who has created and sustained this body, this dark cage, which I possess! If I am separated from it, grant me refuge at Your holy feet.

O First One with three eyes and an ageless form, when great suffering comes, I cry, ‘Protect me!’ The sound of the gods shaking the bell with their hands, the sound that changed, O Lord of Thillai, You burned the three cities into ash and dust. The sins bound by mothers in previous births, when they confront me in this birth, what is there to be ashamed of? My good heart, which does not hasten to prostrate before Nandi, who bows his head and worships at Your feet, scattering fresh flowers before the gods. Will I call Him a liar, the one with the crescent moon in the evening, whose red matted locks are adorned with the battle, who has entered and stands within the circle of my thoughts? The matted locks in a circular form, The Lord, adorned with the Nandi-vattam flower, slightly bloomed, and the Konrai flower, wears a garland of skulls on His head, and wanders from door to door, begging for alms, with many skulls. He never leaves my head, day or night.

He is Shankara, who wears a young crescent moon on His head. He wears a loincloth made of a piece of cloth. He holds a begging bowl in His hand. He is the Father whom the Vedas seek. Our Lord, the Supreme One, does what those who speak speak of. If I die, abandoning this body that cannot be abandoned, with the white messengers, I will ascend to the vast sky.

Having ascended, I will be reborn. My heart is troubled, wondering if I will forget the name of the Lord with the crescent moon on His matted locks, the one who is born. The Lord, who wears the fragrant Konrai flower, which is different from this, has entered my mind, which is different from this. The young crescent moon seems to have settled upon His holy head, where the Ganga, full of water, is contained within His matted locks. Even if the eye-long period of heat causes the dark ocean waters to shrink, and for many long years the rain refuses to fall, causing famine, fear not, O heart! I saw a golden mountain with three unblinking eyes, and it flowed into a place of praise.

Neither Brahma, who went above, nor Vishnu, who delved below, knew Him, and they were bewildered. The God of Death, who cast his noose upon the worshipping child, knew Him, the One who is difficult to know, His holy feet.

Now, the next Thiru-Pathikam, the Thiru-Pathikam of the sound ‘Shiva’, the Thiru-Viruttha Thiru-Pathikam, the eighth Thiru-Pathikam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai.

There is a truth that stands in the world, which is nothing but the sound of ‘Shiva’. He is also a mendicant, wearing a tiger skin, and upon it, a dancing serpent. His temple is the cremation ground, where He eats. If one considers His nature and His humility, the gods who are within Him are not the bright sun, nor the moon, nor the Vedic injunctions, nor the sky and earth, nor the wandering wind, nor the small fire, nor the clear water. He comes as the cause of grace, with a part of His body as the one with the fiery eyes.

He is the one with the fiery chest, not the one who blinks, nor the one who is blinked at. He is the one with the white ash, and upon it, a crescent moon as a tilak on His forehead. He is the one with the dark throat, like a blazing sun, for the cremation ground. O friend, who dances with the bamboo, she is bewildered. He wields the axe, and wears the elephant skin. How can she contend with Him?

How can she see Him? This is His nature. The growing fire, He is the one whose chest shines with a growing garland of bones, and a growing sacred thread, and a growing serpent. He delights in the cremation ground. He is the one whose form is like a tender sprout, like a cool, shining maiden. A woman with hair where cool, shining bees hum, like a flock of birds.

His dwelling place is like a forest. He wears a begging bowl and rides a bull. This is the way He lives. The Lord, who is one part, and the maiden with the crescent moon on her forehead, Uma, the goddess, stands beside Him, and the bees hum around her feet. The world of the gods does not cross Him. He is adorned with the honey-laden Konrai flower and the cool moon.

He is the one with the beautiful, shining, white, ash-colored form. He is the one who is one or two, with a shining, jeweled, beautiful maiden, the daughter of the mountain, with the clouds and groves. He is the Lord. His shining form is like hers, and her form is like His. Their forms are like the sweet laughter of a child. He is the one with the growing Konrai flower and the white skull.

He is the one with the cool Ganga in His matted locks. He is the one who is skilled in the Vedic hymns, with their proper methods. He is the one with the jeweled throat. He is the one with the growing garland of flowers, the maiden, who sings and dances in the fire. This is His nature, as He casts the growing serpent and the moon. The shining Ganga, the shining garland, the forehead burned to ashes, the one with the shining, white, ash-colored form.

He is the one who is alone, or two, with a joyful form, wearing the skin of a wild elephant, and a garland of bones. His shining form is like hers, the ancient one, with her as a part. He is the one who recites the beautiful Vedas. He delights with the mountain maiden and the Ganga maiden, the bridegroom. He strives to be a renunciate, wandering alone, with a skull as His begging bowl. He is the one who plays with the sacred ash, saying it is priceless, and applies the fragrant water.

The ocean, full of water, churned the destructive poison. He is the one who drank the poison. He has a new, shining, golden earring in one ear, and a conch shell in the other. The Vedic hymns are chanted on one side, and on the other side, the maiden smiles gently. He comes with the fragrant Konrai flower in His matted locks, and the maiden as a part of Him. This is His form, her form, their beautiful form, their nature.

Now, the next Thiru-Pathikam, the Thiru-Nenaintha Thiru-Nerisai Thiru-Pathikam, the 74th Thiru-Pathikam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai.

My heart, which thought of the Pearl, the Gem, the Gold, the First Cause, the Coral-like One, the Cluster, the Garland, the Sprout, the Seed worshipped by the gods, the Lord who shines as the Vedic sacrifice, is beautiful, just as it thought. My heart, which thought of the First One for all the worlds, the Lord whom the sages praise, the blissful One, the young Light, the Lord, the Knowledge, the One who is not afraid, the generous One, the one who tore the elephant skin, Our beloved, my heart, which thought of Him, is beautiful, just as it thought. My heart, which thought of Him who is sweeter than sugarcane, who is the light of the blazing sun, who is the nectar of the vast ocean, who has no death or birth, who is the great wealth, whom the great ascetic sages praise, the bud, is beautiful, just as it thought. My heart, which thought of Him who cut off the head, who sent the red arrow to the city, who is the dark one, the golden-bodied God, the one who is for the gods, the one who has a part of the maiden, and whose anger is not appeased, is beautiful, just as it thought. My heart, which thought of Him who kicked the God of Death, the beautiful one, the one who rides the white bull, whom the gods praise, the one with the vast matted locks, the one who is the river, the nectar whom the devotees praise, the one with the sacred ash, is beautiful, just as it thought.

My heart, which thought of Him who tore the elephant skin, the one with the dark, strong arm, the one who is hated, the one with the shining light, the one who is the mountain called Kailash, the one who is the mountain, the one who has the maiden as a part, the one who holds the fire in His hand, My heart, which thought of Him, is beautiful, just as it thought. My heart, which thought of Him who is in the mind of those who think of Him with justice, who is in the mind of those who think of Him, who is the caste, the white ash, the light of the gods in the white sky, the unwavering light, the indestructible beginning, is beautiful, just as it thought. My heart, which thought of Him who is the ancient one for all the worlds, the one who is the mountain, the one who gives patience, the one who is the beautiful one, who wore the elephant skin, making the mountain maiden tremble, the one with the young crescent moon, the one with the cool matted locks, the beautiful one, is beautiful, just as it thought. My heart, which thought of Him who is like lightning in the sky, who is the true great substance, who is like the gem in the eye, who is like the fierce light, who is the great one who stood tall, beyond the reach of thought, is beautiful, just as it thought. My heart, which thought of Him who is the relative, who crushed the strong-armed demon, the one with the three colors, the one with the shining light, the one with the long crown, the guru of the gods, the one who holds the cool white moon in His matted locks, the one with the five-headed serpent, is beautiful, just as it thought.

Now, the next Thiru-Pathikam, the Vinaividai Thiru-Thandakam Thiru-Pathikam. In this Thiru-Pathikam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman raises questions in the first five verses. He asks, ‘Is there a trace beyond the universe? Is there a flag with a bull?’ He mentions many holy symbols of the Lord and asks, ‘Are these present? Are these present?’ He asks the devotees if they have seen the Lord who possesses these holy symbols.

Thus, asking questions by mentioning the holy symbols is found in the first five verses. The answers given by the devotees to these questions are found from the sixth to the eleventh verse. In those verses, from the sixth to the eleventh, the answer is ‘I saw, I saw, I saw.’ While the first part asks ‘Is there? Is there?’, the second part answers ‘I saw, I saw, I saw’. This wonderful Thiru-Thandakam, the Vinaividai Thiru-Thandakam, is structured with the first half as questions and the second half as answers. It is the 97th Thiru-Pathikam of the Sixth Thiru-Murai.

Is there a trace beyond the universe? Is there a dance with fire held in the palm? Are there the ancient seven worlds? Did He come surrounded by many Bhoota-Ganas? Is there a dark throat?

Is there an eye above the eye? Is there a retinue surrounded by devotees? Tell me, how did you see our Lord? Is there a body like the blazing young sun, with young relatives? Is there a white bull? Is there a blazing fire with sparks?

Is there a begging bowl? Is there a white sacred thread? Is there a shining, striped, Is there a matted lock? Did He place a young moon on that matted lock? Is there flowing water? Is there a trident?

Tell me, how did you see our Lord? Did He place a garland of the moon on His red matted locks? Is there an eye on His forehead? Did He smear sacred ash? Did He wear white bones that smell of flesh? Are there Bhoota-Ganas surrounding Him?

Is there a great bull? Is there a part with a beautiful-eyed maiden? Is there a garland of Konrai flowers? Is there a garland of dancing serpents on His shoulder? Tell me, how did you see our Lord? Did He play the well-tuned Veena?

Did He come surrounded by many Bhoota-Ganas? Did He drink the un-eatable, great poison? Is there light in the fire of the ages? Did He destroy the beautiful, dark throat? Did He burn Kama with the fire of His eye? Did He shoot the three cities of the enemies?

How did you see our Lord? Is there a part of His body with water? Is there another eye on His forehead? Is there a sharp, fierce axe in His hand? Is there a tiger skin as His garment? Is there a six-part matted lock?

Is there a serpent? Is there a crescent moon near it? Is there a flag with an immeasurable bull? Is there youth? How did you see our Lord? I saw a crown and an earring on one side.

I saw Him come begging for alms from the Bhoota-Ganas. I saw the Bhoota-Ganas dance with joy. I saw the crescent moon on His head, which does not wither. I saw the banner of the skull on His strong shoulder. I saw the axe shining in His right hand. I saw the perfect one in Thiru-Alavai.

I saw the God in my dream. I saw the flowing Ganga in His matted locks. I saw Him adorned with the garland of Konrai flowers. I saw the serpent in the hand of the one who wanders with the tiger skin. I saw Him as the one who enters the fields, the one who is the day. I saw Him residing in Thiru-Kachchi-Metrali.

I saw His dark throat. I saw the fire. I saw the tightly bound deer skin around His waist. I saw the Lord who knows the Vedas. I saw His body shining with water. I saw the full Ganga ascending His long matted locks.

I saw Him holding the sharp, fierce axe. I saw Him holding the Kodukotti and the skull in His hand. I saw the moon adorning His six-part head. I saw Him as the nectar for His devotees. I saw Him coming on the bull, on this path.

Thus, I saw our Lord. He has the fragrant white ash. He has a white skull in His hand. He has a Veena in one hand. He has a gourd. He has a crescent moon that He wears.

He carries a trident and a staff. He has a loincloth. He has a staff and a skin, beautifully. He has a serpent that does not know to bite. What is not present in the Lord of the gods? He is with the kohl-eyed maiden, and He is the Lord of Thiru-Kachchi-Mayanam, the one with matted locks, the one who is beyond thought.

He is not one who has an equal, He is not from any town, He has no comparison. Unless one sees Him with His grace as the eye, one cannot describe Him as ‘He is like this, He is of this color, He is of this form, He is the Lord.’ I saw the ash on His golden body. I saw the tiger skin garment. I saw the maiden with the lightning-like slender waist as a part of Him. I saw a shining serpent around His waist. I saw His feet that crushed the demon who rode the swan.

I saw the garland of small Konrai flowers. I saw Shiva in my thoughts.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, while performing Thiru-Thondu in Thiru-Pukalur, composed countless such Thiru-Pathikams. Let us continue to contemplate the sacred history of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman attaining the holy feet of the Lord in Thiru-Pukalur. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 475, Thiru-Nindra-Charukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman resided in Thiru-Pukalur, performing the sacred Ulavara Thiru-Thondu, praising the Lord in his mind, and composing Thevara Thiru-Pathikams with his holy words, thus living in that holy place called Thiru-Pukalur. Continuing, Sekkizhar Peruman sings: “In that state, while the King performed service, the Lord, to show his good state, caused gold and precious gems to shine forth in the sacred courtyard where the Ulavaram entered.” This is the 416th verse in Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. While Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman was performing this sacred service, Lord Shiva desired to reveal the excellent state of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to the world. The excellent state of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman means that he possessed a mind firmly fixed at the holy feet of the Lord.

A mind firmly fixed at the holy feet of the Lord means a mind that is constantly absorbed in the holy feet of the Lord without interruption. It means a mind that always meditates on the holy feet of the Lord.

Furthermore, this excellent state of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman means a good state where he has no attachment whatsoever to worldly pleasures such as gold. It is a good state of non-attachment. He possesses a mind firmly fixed at the holy feet of the Lord.

Therefore, he has a state of mind that is not attached to anything other than the Lord. The reason for this non-attachment to worldly pleasures is that his mind is always fixed on the holy feet of the Lord. Arunanandi Sivanar states in Sivagnana Siddhiyar that those who have realized the Supreme through Para-Jnana and have loved it will only perceive Shiva and will not see other objects. These worldly pleasures, which are other objects, are things that are subject to the influence of Prarabdha Karma. Such objects, that is, objects subject to the influence of Prarabdha Karma, will not be seen by those who have attained this Para-Jnana. Those who have attained this Para-Jnana are Jivanmuktas.

These Jivanmuktas, who have attained Para-Jnana, will only perceive Shiva and will not be affected by Prarabdha Karma by looking at other objects. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman possesses such an excellent state.

Lord Shiva desired to make this good state of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman known to the world. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is performing the Ulavara Thiru-Thondu in the holy streets surrounding the Thiru-Pukalur temple. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is performing the Ulavara Thiru-Thondu. Ulavara Thiru-Thondu means removing stones, weeds, and other obstacles from the temple and the streets surrounding it, where devotees walk, so that devotees and the Lord can circumambulate the holy streets without any hindrance. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman always carries this Ulavara tool in his hand and performs the Ulavara service. Sekkizhar Peruman unfailingly mentions that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman performed this Ulavara service in all the holy places he visited.

Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is performing the Ulavara Thiru-Thondu. Ulavara Thiru-Thondu means removing stones, weeds, and other obstacles from the temple and the streets surrounding it, where devotees walk, so that devotees and the Lord can circumambulate the holy streets without any hindrance. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman always carries this Ulavara tool in his hand and performs the Ulavara service. Sekkizhar Peruman unfailingly mentions that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman performed this Ulavara service in all the holy places he visited. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman is shown performing the Thiru-Ulavara service. This Ulavara service here indicates that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s hands performed the service naturally, without any effort.

While he was thus performing the Thiru-Ulavara service in Thiru-Pukalur, wherever Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s Ulavaram entered for the Lord’s service, Lord Shiva blessed it so that gold and precious gems appeared and shone forth. This passage in the hymn states that He blessed them to shine forth with gold and precious gems.

Now, the next hymn: “Chembponnum navamaniyum sen vilanga aangavaiyum umbarpiran thirumunril urul parukkaiyudan okka Emperuman Vakkisar” Ulavaraththinil endhi vamppalar men poongamala vaaviyinil puka erindhar enbadhu adutha thiruppadal. While Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman was performing the Ulavara service, Lord Shiva caused gold and precious gems to appear on that street. They shone brightly, their light extending far.

But what did our leader, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, do? He took the gold and precious gems that were before Lord Shiva with his Ulavara tool, removed them, and threw them into a nearby pond. He gathered the gold and precious gems along with the stones on the street and threw them away. This is because this gold, and precious gems are equal to the stones lying on the street. They are not in any way superior or different objects.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman picks up the gold and precious gems along with the stones, throws them into the pond, and cleanses that path. Sekkizhar Peruman states, “Chembponnum navamaniyum sen vilanga aangu evaiyum.” “Evaiyum” means that this gold and these gems, and anything else like them, should be considered equal to pebbles. This is the meaning. The pebbles lying on that street, and the gold and gems there, are all the same. As far as Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is concerned, whether it is a stone, a thorn, gold, or precious gems, they all obstruct the sacred feet of the devotees who walk along that holy street. Along with the stones, the precious gems also cause pain to the sacred feet of the devotees walking on that street.

Therefore, these stones and precious gems cause pain to the devotees’ feet. In this sense, gold, precious gems, and stones are of the same nature. That is why Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman picks up the precious gems along with the stones, throws them into the pond, and performs the Thiru-Ulavara service, cleansing the street.

Therefore, just as stones and thorns are not allowed, Just as stones and thorns should not be in the holy street of the temple, so too gold and precious gems are unsuitable items to be in the holy street before the Lord. Their presence would cause hindrance to the devotees. With this understanding, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, considering stones, gold, and precious gems to be of the same nature, removes them.

At this point, some people interpret it differently. In the eighth sutra, twenty-ninth verse of Sivagnana Siddhiyar, it says: “Mikkathoru pakkuvaththin miga sakthi nipadham mevudhalum gnanam vilaindhor kuruvin arulaal pukkanuttiththe nittai purindhullorgal poothalaththil pugazh jeevan muththaragi thakka piriyap piriyamindri ottil thapaniyaththil samapuththi panna” This refers to the state of mind described as “ottil thapaniyaththil samapuththi panni” (having an equal mind towards potsherds and gold). Some special commentators interpret this passage to mean that because he had such an equal mind, he gathered and threw both stones and precious gems into the pond while performing the Ulavara service.

However, Sivakavimaniyar’s view is that this state is different. The state mentioned in Sivagnana Siddhiyar is that potsherds and gold are not perceived as separate; that is, stones and gold are not perceived as separate. Both are understood to be products of Maya. This is the meaning we should take there. This is what Sekkizhar Peruman sings in Thiru-Kootta Sirappu, “odum semponum” Okkave nokkuvar.

However, in this passage of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s Puranam, gold, precious gems, and pebbles are distinctly perceived. Even though they are thus distinctly perceived by their material nature, gold, stones, and precious gems are all unsuitable to be in the holy street of the Lord’s temple. This is because, in causing hindrance to the devotees’ sacred feet, all of them are of the same nature. It is with this understanding that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman removes all these and performs the Thiru-Ulavara service.

Thus, Sivakavimani Ayya explains here. The pond into which he threw the gold, stones, and gems is the pond surrounding the Thiru-Pukalur temple. “Poigai soozhum poompukalur” is how Sekkizhar Peruman sings about Poombukalur. Generally, this holy place of Thiru-Pukalur is surrounded by ponds. Specifically, this temple is surrounded by a pond. That pond is full of flowers.

Therefore, the temple shines as one surrounded by flowers. In such a temple, in the lotus-filled pond surrounding it, he throws the gems and performs the Ulavara service.

Furthermore, these items are harmful, and therefore should not be touched, he thought. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman removes them with his Ulavara tool. Indeed, precious gems are valuable, but here, because they cause pain to the devotees’ sacred feet, they were considered equivalent to rubbish and removed. Small gems that fell from the crowns of the Devas, which would hurt the devotees’ feet, were therefore removed as rubbish. “Anthiyum pakalum thondar alakidum kuppaiyaakkum” is from Thiru-Vilayadal Puranam. This is because these precious gems and gold are those that fell from the crowns on the heads of the Devas.

Therefore, they are items that were worn by them, used by the Devas, and then fell to the ground.

Thus, they are impure. They are impure items, and therefore they were removed with the intention of removing them. Through this, we also learn another message: when we go to worship in temples, we should not leave behind any item that we have used. The Shiva temple worship rules also inform us that items used by us should not be inside the temple or in the streets surrounding the temple.

Thus, items used by humans, fallen items, and discarded items should be removed by performing the Thiru-Ulavara service. We must remove them so that they do not cause pain to the sacred feet of the devotees. This sacred act of the Chariya path, This sacred act is also conveyed to us here. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who came to show us the path of Chariya in Gnana, conveys this to us.

Therefore, to show the excellent state of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who was completely detached from all worldly possessions and worldly pleasures, and who completely severed and cast away all worldly attachments, the Lord thus bestows His grace, and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman continues to perform the Thiru-Ulavara service. Let us go on reflecting. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 476, Thiru-Nindra Charukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. While Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman was performing the Ulavara service in Thiru-Pukalur, he was also performing the service of throwing the gold, precious gems, and other items created by the Lord, along with stones, into the pond there.

At this time, by the grace of the Lord, celestial maidens descended from the heavens. Women with foreheads whose eyebrows curved and swayed, outdoing bows, these celestial maidens descended there from the heavens. They descended like flashes of lightning coming down from the sky. They sang songs accompanied by beautiful music, and with their eyes and hands, They performed beautiful dances with expressive gestures. With feet like the tender shoots of the Kalpaka tree, they spun in circles, making gestures with their hands, and danced very beautifully. Sekkizhar Peruman sings about this, saying: “Aduvar paduvar alar mari mer pozhivar kooduvar pondru anaivar kuzhal avizha idai nudanga oduvar maravedudan meezhvar oli peruga needuvar thukil asaiya nirpparum ayinar.” There, the women danced, sang beautifully, showered flowers like rain, approached as if to embrace, ran with their hair disheveled and waists swaying.

Thus, these celestial maidens performed various actions. While these women were performing all sorts of actions, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman remained steadfast in his unwavering love, fixed on the sacred feet of Lord Shiva. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman shone as a supreme being, standing in pure penance, whose body melted with such love. Such a Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, possessing pure penance, remained steadfast in his Ulavara service, without deviating even slightly from his inner state. He stood firm in it. Sekkizhar Peruman sings about this, saying: “Iththanmai arambaiyargal evvidhamum seyalpuriya aththanar thiruvadikke ninaivugala anbu urugu meyththanmai unarvudaiya vizhuththavaththu melor tham siththa nilai theriyathu seyniyin thalai nindrar.”

He sings. Even when women came and danced and sang around him, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s mental state remained undisturbed. This is because he possessed profound penance, a very excellent tapas. His mind never strayed from the Lord’s sacred feet. Because he had such love, fixed on the Lord’s sacred feet, his heart melted with that love, leading to true realization, and from the abundance of that realization, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman shone with profound penance.

Therefore, the reason for all this is the unwavering love that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman held for the Lord’s sacred feet. We saw this in the 1405th verse, “Nayagan sevadi thaivaru sinthai.” We saw this in the 1490th verse, “Sempporralle sarbana thirumanamum.” We also saw Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s exalted state in the praise of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman composed by Sivagnana Swamigal in Kanchi Puranam, which states, “Sivaperuman thiruvadikke pathintha nenjum.” The reason for all this is that quality of melting with love. “Anbirkum undo adaikkum thazh” (Is there a lock for love?) is a Kural. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman possessed the state of true realization (meyththanmai unarvu), that is, the stable realization of the imperishable, sat-like Shiva-nature. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman was one who possessed such true realization.

That is why Sivakavimani Ayya also wrote a book titled “Vakkisar allathu Meyyunardhal.” In it, he compared the history of Vakkisa Peruman, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, with the ten Kurals from the chapter on Meyyunardhal in Thirukkural, and explained Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s state of true realization to us. The word “vizhuththavam” (profound penance) that appears in this hymn means exalted penance, which is the act of Sivagnana. Shiva Puja itself is penance. Sekkizhar Peruman continues to sing: “Immaya pavath thodakkam iru vinaigal thamai nokki ummal ingu enna kurai udaiyen yan Thiruvarur ammanukku aalanen alaiye” (What lack do I have here from you, looking at the beginning of this illusory birth and the two karmas? I am a servant of the Lord of Thiruvarur, am I not?) Thus, Sekkizhar sings that he proclaimed the Thiru-Thandagam, “Poymaya perungadalul.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman saw the celestial women surrounding him as embodiments of the two karmas. The two karmas are the two karmas that cause us to fall into this birth, which is a product of Maya.

Therefore, he saw all these women as embodiments of the two karmas. He did not consider those forms to be celestial maidens, or even women, but rather as the very forms of the two karmas. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar saw them as such. The two karmas are the good and bad deeds that bring us merit and sin, good karma and bad karma. Just like bad karma, good karma also leads to birth. If bad karma is considered an iron chain that binds us, then good karma is a golden chain that binds us.

Therefore, both bind us.

Thus, good people who have attained the equivalence of the two karmas will see both karmas as one. Such good people will see worldly experiences and worlds as effects, and will not accept them, but rather see them as Maya, the causal form.

Thus, those who do not see these as Maya and the effects of Maya, but rather succumb to them, will be born and suffer the fruits of the two karmas.

Therefore, good people will withdraw, not setting their minds on the world. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who possessed such a nature and had attained the state of a Jivanmukta, saw all the women who surrounded him as embodiments of the two karmas. Seeing them thus, he addressed them, saying, “What business do I have with you here? Nothing. I am a servant of the Lord of Thiruvarur.

“Therefore, do not wander here in vain.” And he sang a Thiru-Thandagam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings the Thiru-Thandagam, “Aalanen” (I am a servant) of Thiruvarur Amman. He is currently in Thiru-Pukalur, a holy place, but Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman says he is a servant of the Lord of Thiruvarur, not the Lord of Thiru-Pukalur. This is because the women who surrounded him were celestial maidens, all subservient to Indra, the king of the Devas. Indra is the one who waits outside the Devasiriya Mandapam, watching for the right time to serve the assembled devotees, the devotees of Shiva.

“Therefore, your leader is Indra, but my leader is the Lord of Thiruvarur, who is the leader of your leader, Indra. I am one of the holy assembly gathered in that Devasiriya Mandapam, where your leader waits at the entrance.

“Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, referring to the greatness of his Lord, thus composed a Thiru-Thandagam as a reply to those women, saying, “Do not perform your actions with me.” That is the Thiruvarur Thiru-Thandagam. Sekkizhar Peruman states that he composed that Thiru-Thandagam which begins with “Poymaya perungadalil.” This is the Sixth Thiru-Murai, Twenty-Seventh Thiru-Pathigam, Thiruvarur Thiru-Pathigam, Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathigam.

““Poymaya” Perungadalir pulambanindra punniyangal theevinaygal thiruve neengal immaya perungadalai ariththu thinpirku illaiye kidanduthan yanel vanorthammanai thalaimaganai thannal arur thadangadalai thodarnthorai adangach cheyyum emman than adithodarvan olitharukindren idaiyilen keduveergal idaranmine. Aimperuma poothangal oruveer vendil oruveer vendir eendiv avaniyellam umbarame um vasame akkavallirkku illaiye nugar bhogam yanel vanor umbarumay uzhiyumay ulagezhagi ol arur nallamitham vallal vanor tham perumanar nindra aranai kanben thadaippaduvena karuthi tharukken minne silluruvil kuriyirutthi nitthal patri sezhungan. Nal nokkumithu ookkamandru palluruvir sozil poonda panchaputha pazhagirum vasamandre pare ellam solluruvir sudar moondray uruvam moondray thu nayana moondragi anda arur nalluruvir sivanadiye adaiven nummal namaippunnen kamaiththu nir nadamingale unnuruvir suvai oli uru osai natraththu uruppinathu kuripagum aiveer nungal mannuruvaththiyarkkaigalal vaippirkkaiyo vaiyagame pothathey yanel vanor ponnuruvai thennarur mannu kundrai puvikku ezhilan sivakkozhunthai pugundhu en sinthai thannoruvai thanthavanai enthai thannai thalaippaduven thulaippaduppan tharukken minne thuppinai munpatra virale mikka sorvupadu sutchiame sugamE neengal oppinai Paaviththu ivvulagamellam uzhalurumithu kuraimudippirku arithe endran vaippinai ponmathil arur maniyai vaigal manalanai emperumanai vanorthangal appanai seppidavadaiven nummal nanum atrunen ottanthinkalaiyen minne pongumathamanaame arvasettra kurothame ulobame poraiye neengal ungal perumanilathin ellaiyellam uzharumithu kurai mudippirku aritheyanel angamalaththayanodu malagi matrum atharku appal ondragi ariyavonna sengkanaga thani kundrai sivanai arur selvanai servenu ma seluththunene idarpavamenamikka thukka vetkai veruppe endranaiverum ulagaiyodik kudaikundrirku ulagangal kulungi nungal kurinindrathu If I am not, the celestials will not approach; He who burned the three cities of those who did not approach, the Lord of the celestials, Hara, the possessor of Thiruvarur, I will swiftly reach. You cannot restrain me; I will not be hindered.

“O lightning, though you hasten, you will not prosper. O evil joy, joy, hatred, you have spread and devoured the earth; there is no enjoyment. If I am not, I will see the Paramjyoti in Thiruvarur, the Kalpaka who consumed the poison that came when the celestials churned, the Parabrahman. I will not be caught; I will not be boastful, but will run with devotion. O lightning, you will drown in the five senses, the deceitful faces of this world. You will not be able to carry out your foolishness for long.

“If I am not, the celestials will not be able to bear the long sky. I will swiftly reach the Lord of Thiruvarur, who is like a pillar reaching from the netherworld. You cannot restrain me; I will not be hindered. O lightning, you who speak of brevity and expansion, and of renunciation, you have wandered through this world, boasting and performing many deeds. If I am not, I will not be able to do so. He who took on a form to humble the arrogant demon who lifted the mountain, and who, hearing his song, was moved to compassion and bestowed grace upon him, the great Lord, I will not be separated from His feet.

“You will perish, O lightning, you will not be troubled.

“Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman addresses the celestial maidens, saying, “You perceive worldly pleasures as good and evil, and you wander through all the worlds, issuing commands. Is this world not enough for you?” You attempt to command me as well.

“But I am a servant of the Lord of Thiruvarur, and I stand steadfast in His service. There is nothing you can accomplish here.

“Therefore, do not wander here; go!” Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, seeing those maidens as embodiments of the two karmas, offers this good counsel to us, the people of the world, through this Thiru-Pathikam. As Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman thus bestowed his grace, the celestial maidens, unable to sway the great Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, who possessed an unwavering and unified consciousness, from his steadfast position, departed from there. While this was happening, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman continued his sacred service in Thiru-Pukalur. He continues his Thiru-Thondu in Thiru-Pukalur.

“We shall proceed with our reflection.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 477, Thiru-Nindra-Charukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. In Thiru-Pukalur, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman continues his Ulavara Thiru-Pani. Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman as “a great one with an undifferentiated consciousness.” This phrase, “undifferentiated consciousness,” should be understood as “undifferentiated consciousness” and “a single consciousness” separately. Some say that “undifferentiated consciousness” means a consciousness that is not swayed by worldly desires or by the actions of celestial nymphs, etc.

However, the most accurate explanation for “undifferentiated” would be “unwavering.” The state of remaining steadfast in one’s chosen goal, without deviation, We can understand it as consciousness. “A single consciousness” means a consciousness that is united with the Lord’s feet, without going anywhere else.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is a great one with an undifferentiated consciousness. “Great ones perform difficult deeds” is a Kural from the Thiru-Kural. We can reflect on this here in the context of this great one. “Lust, anger, and delusion—when these three names are destroyed, the disease is destroyed” is the ninth Kural in the chapter on “True Knowledge.” Lust means desire, anger means hatred.

Therefore, great ones with true knowledge are those in whom the very names of desire, hatred, and delusion are eradicated. The meaning of this Kural is that the karmic fruits that are yet to come will not affect such great ones who possess true knowledge. Before those who have attained maturity in Jnana Yoga, these faults—namely, lust, anger, and delusion—disappear like cotton before a forest fire.

Therefore, even the names of these faults will not exist for them.

Thus, Thiru-Valluvar mentions “the destruction of names” here. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having renounced the three desires known as Edanathrayam—desire for land, desire for gold, and desire for women—and being free from hatred and other emotions that arise when these desired objects are not attained, and thus free from the great whirlpool of attachment and aversion, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman attained the path from which there is no return. According to the Thiru-Kural, “Birth is caused by the delusion that mistakes non-things for things.” The meaning is that if this delusive consciousness is absent, there is no birth.

Therefore, by conquering the three desires, by eliminating anger, and by dispelling the delusion that perceives impermanent things as permanent, a soul becomes worthy of attaining that imperishable bliss, that ultimate liberation. Such great ones are those who possess true knowledge, those who embody true knowledge. Such a great one, a great one with an undifferentiated consciousness, is our Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. In this state, He continues his Ulavara Thiru-Pani in Thiru-Pukalur. Sekkizhar Peruman then composes the next verse as follows: “In this state, the world, having understood and known, worshipped him. Thiru-Navukkarasu, the embodiment of unwavering love and devotion, the Lord of speech, whose matted locks shine like lightning, remained there for some days, as if that state of attaining the true essence of the Lord was near.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is worthy of worship by all seven worlds.

All seven worlds worship his state. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman shines as the embodiment of such devotion. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman saw no difference between stone and gold. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman saw the celestial nymphs as the beginning of illusory existence and as embodiments of the two karmas. His mind, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is a great ascetic who remains steadfast in the work he undertakes, without losing his mental composure. The people of all these seven worlds, understanding the qualities of such a Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and recognizing his greatness, and adopting the same goal as their own, worship Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman with unwavering love.

He shines as the very embodiment of devotion. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is like devotion itself having taken a form. Such a great Lord of speech, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, realizes that the irreversible state of supreme bliss, which is the result of Shivattva, the enjoyment of Shiva, and the fullness of divine grace, is very near to him. In Thiru-Pukalur, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman realizes that the Shivabhogam, which is the result of Shivattva, and the irreversible state of supreme bliss, which is absorbed in the fullness of divine grace, are now very near to him. Subsequently, the next sacred verse states: “With the effort of foreknowledge arising from the unwavering inner self, he uttered many Thiru-Virutthams, saying, ‘O Lord of Pukalur, place me, your humble servant, under your sacred feet.’” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings Thiru-Virutthams with a combination of knowledge, desire, and action, firmly established at the sacred feet of the Lord. He sings many Thiru-Virutthams with the thought that the Lord of Pukalur will now place him under His sacred feet.

Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings many Thiru-Virutthams with the thought that the Lord of Pukalur will now place him under His sacred feet. Here it says, “with the unwavering inner self, by the power of its turning.” Until now, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s desire, action, and knowledge, which were engaged in the external service of the Lord, perceiving the devotees’ sacred attire and the Shiva temple as the Supreme Lord, are now turned inward, focusing solely on Shivanantha. In this verse, it is stated that the inner instruments are now in this state. Sekkizhar Peruman metaphorically refers to the desire, knowledge, and action that govern the inner instruments as the inner instruments themselves in this verse.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having shed the remnants of attachments, now focuses solely on the sacred feet of the Lord. We can understand this state by learning and comprehending the section of the Sivagnanabodham, “The entrance of the humble one into the heart,” from competent teachers. Realizing that all the shortcomings in this world have been resolved, and that there is no longer any reason to remain here, and with the foreknowledge that the Lord will now keep him forever under His sacred feet, he sings many Thiru-Virutthams with that emotional surge.

At this point, the Thiru-Viruttha Thiru-Pathikam sung now is the 105th Thiru-Pathikam of the Fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Pathikam belonging to the sacred site of Thiru-Pukalur. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman composed it with the foreknowledge that the Lord of Thiru-Pukalur would not keep him in this world, but would keep him permanently under His sacred feet forever. Thiru-Viruttha Thiru-Pathikam.

“I have surrendered to Him, taking refuge in His feet. Hear what the Lord of Pukalur, surrounded by punnai groves, will do! He will cut off my births, sever my karmic bonds, and will not let me lie in the seven hells; He will place me in Shiva’s abode. O Lord whose body is like refined gold, who has a part of the soft-breasted one, who is like a part of her, have mercy on me, the humble one! O King of Pukalur, where bees sleep on the punnai flowers, what can I say about the place where I am placed in this womb of suffering?

“O Lord with matted locks adorned with konrai, O King of Pukalur, O medicine sought by the celestials on earth, O Lord of Valanchuzhi! What can I say about my state, being caught in the middle, having fallen for you? Have no mercy on me, O Lord! O Supreme One! Neither Brahma, the creator, nor Vishnu, the radiant one on the great lotus, could see You, though they sought You. O Lord with four shoulders, who destroyed the strength of the one who bore the burden!

“O Lord of ancient Pukalur, O Lord of Kona, if I approach You, evil deeds will not approach me.

“In this Thiru-Pathikam, the third, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, and ninth verses are not available to us. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who praised the Lord on this earth for eighty-one years, thus sings Thiru-Virutthams in Thiru-Pukalur. He sings many such Thiru-Virutthams with the foreknowledge that the Lord will now graciously place him under His sacred feet. Sekkizhar Peruman continues to sing in the 427th verse of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam: “Having sung the steadfast Thiru-Thandakam, ‘O Virtuous One, I come to Your feet,’ which is praised by all worlds, beginning with the earth, he became the very embodiment of the auspicious Shivanantha Jnana and remained seated at the sacred feet of the Lord.” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman composed this Thiru-Thandaka Thiru-Pathikam, which begins with “How can I think, what can I say to think?” and concludes with “O Virtuous One, I come to Your feet,” so that all living beings in this world may praise, benefit, and attain salvation. This Thiru-Pathikam is a steadfast Thiru-Pathikam that shines forth.

“O Virtuous One, I come to Your feet” is the crown and inner meaning of this Thiru-Pathikam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman thus composed this Thiru-Thandakam. This Thiru-Pathikam is the concluding Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. It is the 99th Thiru-Pathikam in the Sixth Thiru-Murai. This Thiru-Pathikam is a Thiru-Thandaka Thiru-Pathikam belonging to the site of Thiru-Pukalur.

““How can I think, what can I say to think? I have no eyes but for the sacred feet of my Lord. I have no other art but to worship His feet with my hands and see Him. You have placed nine gates in one; when they are all closed, I will not understand. O Virtuous One, I come to Your feet, O Virtuous One residing in Poompukalur.”

“You wear bones as ornaments, You danced with fire, You are Adhirai, You are under the banyan tree, You rode the bull. O Lord with faultless matted locks, You removed the enmity between the snake and the moon. Without any doubt, when the celestials pleaded, You drank the poison from the ocean, You are immortal, You are ageless, O Lion, I come to Your feet, O God of gods residing in Thiru-Pukalur. O Lord with a serpent belt, O Lord with white sacred ash, O Lord with ear-rings of palm leaves, You have a part of the sweet-voiced, dark-eyed maiden. You hold a fawn in Your hand. You have sent the five deceitful thieves upon me; their desires are not here.

“Without speaking falsehood, I come to Your feet, O Virtuous One residing in Poompukalur. O Lord who is not deluded, O God who bent the bow and shot the red arrow to burn the three cities, You remove the distress from the minds of those who are not deluded. You are the medicine, You cure diseases. You are always grace to the celestials, You are the beginning, You are the Vedas. You are the substance that Brahma on the lotus and Vishnu on the water could not find. I come to Your feet, O Virtuous One residing in Poompukalur.
