“O Just One, who lovingly placed the cool moon on Your red matted locks, never to leave. O Lord who takes alms in the great skulls, O Lord who burned Kama, O Destroyer of illusions. O Lord with a throat like a dark cloud, O mighty warrior who tore apart the black elephant, I come to Your feet, O Virtuous One residing in Poompukalur. O Lord with flowing matted locks, O Vedic One, O Singer of Vedas, O Lord of the vast White forest surrounded by groves, O Lord of Meeyachur, O God of gods who burned the three cities, O Lord residing in Thiru-Moolattanam of Thiruvarur, O Lord of Thiru-Magazham with fragrant Tulasi, O Lord of Valanchuzhi, O Lord of Marai-Kadu, O Lord with fiery matted locks, I come to Your feet, O Virtuous One residing in Poompukalur. The celestials, all the gods, searched for the Lord, crying out at His feet, singing the Vedas with their tongues, and dancing. Brahma, Indra, and Vishnu praised Him.

“O Lord of Kaanapper, surrounded by dense groves, O Lord at the summit of Kazhukkundram, O God, I come to Your flower-like golden feet, O Virtuous One residing in Poompukalur. O Lord bathed in ghee, O Pure One, O Blue-throated One, O Complete One, O Knower of Vedas, O Just One, O Lord with the dark-eyed maiden as a part, O Lord wearing a deer skin, You stood rejoicing. I, your servant, offer the intertwined Vilvam and Konrai garland, and standing firm, I come to Your unfailing sacred feet, O Virtuous One residing in Poompukalur. O Lord wearing a stitched loincloth, O Lord with pure sacred ash, O Lord holding a shining white battle-axe in Your hand, O Lord who lovingly placed Yourself, Your intellect, the snake, and the water on Your matted hair. O Lord with the swan-like maiden as a part, O Lord wearing beads, O Primordial One, I come to Your golden feet, O Virtuous One residing in Poompukalur. My heart, which does not know anyone else, is caught in the confusion of consciousness.

“I am unable to send the two and the three upon me, and if You do not trouble me, O Lord, who crushed the king of Lanka, surrounded by dark mountains, so that his mighty chariot could not move, with Your foot, O Peerless One, I come to Your feet, O Virtuous One residing in Poompukalur.

“Thus, having composed this Thiru-Pathikam, he became the very embodiment of the auspicious Shivanantha Jnana and remained seated at the sacred feet of the Lord. He sat at the sacred feet of the Lord, which are difficult to reach, under the Lord’s grace, within the fullness of the Lord’s grace, in that great state where there is no coming and going, no night and day, in that all-pervading and all-encompassing state.

“The King of Thiru-Navu, Thiru-Navukkarasu, sat as the very embodiment of Shivanantha Jnana. He sat as the very embodiment of Shivanantha Jnana. Shiva is Sat, Jnana is Chit.

“Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sat there as the very embodiment of the Lord’s full grace, in that essential state of the Lord, which is Sat-Chit-Ananda. The state in which Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman had been until now was the state of a Jivanmukta, associated with the illusory body and so on.

“Now, from this state of Jivanmukti, he sat there in the pure Advaita Siddhanta of Mukti, where the experience of Shivanantha alone manifests. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman now sits as the very embodiment of Shivanantha at the sacred feet of the Lord. The sacred body of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, which the people of the world had seen until now, dissolved like a camphor flame. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s soul merged with the Sat-Chit-Ananda nature of Shiva and became absorbed within it. It is experiencing the bliss that that exalted consciousness bestows. Although both are of the nature of Sat-Chit-Ananda, the Sat-Chit-Ananda nature of the Lord bestows bliss, and the Sat-Chit-Ananda nature of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s soul, which is seated there, experiences the bliss bestowed by the Lord.

“It became a unified joy, pervading all beings. Sekkizhar Peruman continues to sing in the 28th verse: “The celestials showered flowers, filling the earth, and the five great sounds from the heavens, beginning with Brahma’s...” On the sacred day of Sathayam in the month of Chithirai, when great joy filled all the boats, Sekkizhar Peruman sings.

“Thus, Sekkizhar Peruman states that the day Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sat at the sacred feet of the Lord was the sacred day of Sathayam in the month of Chithirai. As the Devas showered flowers, and the five types of celestial drums resounded in the heavens, all beings born in the seven types of births, beginning with Four-faced Brahma, experienced the great joy that filled them as the very life of their lives. On that sacred day of Sathayam in the month of Chithirai, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who ruled over us as Arasu, became the very form of Shiva-ananda Gnana at the sacred red feet of the Lord. Thiru-Navu- Karasu Peruman’s sacred day of attaining liberation, that Chithirai Sathayam, is forever celebrated by devotees of Shiva as Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s Guru Puja day.

“Thus, Sekkizhar Peruman, who sings the sacred history of Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, continues: The four hundred and twenty-ninth verse, the concluding verse in the history of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar’s Purana: “I have recounted the history of Arasu, who ruled with my devotion, as I understood it.

“Now, having bowed with folded hands to that great sage, I shall speak of the efforts of Kulachiraiyar’s glorious sacred service,” sings Sekkizhar Peruman.

“Thus, the history of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who ruled as Arasu, is recounted by that great sage, whose mind is like a flower, soft and tender. Having bowed with my hands to the sacred red feet, I have recounted his sacred history as I understood it. I have spoken of it within the limits of my understanding. Having bowed with my hands to the soft, flower-like sacred feet of that supreme sage, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, I shall now begin to speak of the boundless greatness and efficacy of Kulachirai Nayanar’s sacred service, says Sekkizhar Peruman, concluding the sacred history of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, who is Appar Swamigal, the sage Vakkisa. He now begins to speak of the sacred history of Kulachirai Nayanar. Let us also, with the aid of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s sacred grace, complete this history and continue with the sacred Purana of Kulachirai Nayanar, through the grace of the Guru and the sacred grace.

“Let us contemplate through the grace of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s sacred feet. Praise be to the sacred feet of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman! Praise be to the sacred feet of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal! Praise be to the sacred feet of Nambiandar Nambigal! Praise be to the sacred feet of Sekkizhar Peruman! Praise be to the sacred feet of Sivakavimani Aiyya, who wrote the commentary on the Periya Puranam!

“Let us go on contemplating.” Thiruchitrambalam.

lines: இங்கு என் செயல் உற்ற பிழைப்பு அதனால்
மை வாச நறும் குழல் மா மலையாள்
அரசு இங்கு அருள் பெற்று உலகு உய்ந்தது
எனாஅடியார் புடை சூழ் அதிகைப் பதி தான்
காவில் களி மயில் மகிழ் உற்று எதிர்
எதிர் ஆடக் கடி கமழ் கமலம் சூழ்
அணைவுற அணி கொம்பரின் மிசை அருகு எங்கும்
தவம் முன் புரிதலில் வரு தொண்டு எனும்
சிவ முன் பயில் மொழி பகர் கின்றன
வளர் சிறை மென் கிளியொடு சிறு பூவை.
கல்வித் துறை பல வரு மா மறை முதல்
செல்வக் குடி நிறை நல் வைப்பு இடை
நவ மின் சுடர் மணி நெடு மாலையும்
பவனன் பணி செய வருணன் புனல் கொடு
எவரும் தொழுது எழும் அடியார் திரு அலகு
வளர் பொன் கனக மணி திரு மாளிகையினை
தொழுது அணை உற்று ஆண்ட அரசு அன்பு
அருள் பெருகு தனிக் கடலும் உலகுக்கு எல்லாம்
பொருள் சமய முதல் சைவ நெறி தான்
பெற்ற புண்ணியக் கண் இரண்டு எனவும் புவனம் உய்ய
இருள் கடு உண்டவர் அருளும் உலகம் எல்லாம்
ஈன்றாள் தன் திரு அருளும் எனவும் கூடித்
தெருள் கலை ஞானக் கன்றும் அரசும் சென்று
செம் சடை வானவர் கோயில் சேர்ந்தார் அன்றே.
பண் பயில் வண்டு அறை சோலை சூழும்
விண் பணிய ஓங்கு பெரு விமானம் தன்னை
கண் பயிலும் புனல் பொழிய அரசும் வாய்மை
கலை பயிலும் மொழி பொழியக் கசிந்து பாடி.
பெரிய பெருமாட்டியுடன் தோணி மீது பேணி வீற்று
அரிய வகை புறம் போந்து பிள்ளையார் தம்
மருவிய நண்புறு கேண்மை அற்றை நாள் போல்
வளர்ந்து ஓங்க உடன் பல நாள் வைகும் நாளில்.
மைத் தழையும் மணி மிடற்றர் பொன்னி நாட்டு
நீண்ட கருப் பறியலூர் புன்கூர் நீடூர் நீடு
மேவு புனல் பொன்னி இரு கரையும் சார்ந்து
விடை உயர்த்தார் திருச் செம் பொன் பள்ளிபாடிக்
ஆவடு தண் துறையாரை அடைந்து உய்ந்தேன் என்ற
தாமம்பல சாத்தி மிக்கு எழுந்த பரிவின் ஓடும்
பூ வலயத்தவர் பரவப் பல நாள் தங்கிப்
எறி புனல் பொன் மணி சிதறும் திரை நீர்ப்
செய்ய மா மணி ஒளி சூழ் திரு முன்றின்முன்
தெய்வ நீறு நினைந்து எழுந்தார் சீர் கொள்
